content.title: Restart an unavailable execution runtime automatically

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Automatically restart an enabled execution runtime after it becomes unavailable, with bounded backoff and one attention item when retries run out.

**Current behavior:**
When an enabled runtime fails while the service runs (for example the Codex App Server exits), the service records it as unavailable. Queued work waits with "runtime unavailable; turn it off and on in Settings → Runtime, or restart the service". Running turns are held for recovery. Only the Settings off/on toggle or a service restart replaces the runtime. The toggle goes through the service's runtime reconciliation, which replaces an unavailable runtime with a fresh one and runs the normal startup checks.

**Desired behavior:**
- After an enabled runtime becomes unavailable, the service retries starting it at **30 s, 2 min, then 10 min**. Each attempt uses the same replacement path as the Settings off/on toggle. No new admission or recovery semantics are added.
- The attempt counter resets only after the runtime has stayed available for **10 minutes**. A runtime that crash-loops therefore exhausts its retries instead of restarting forever.
- When the last attempt fails, the service raises **one** attention item (a problem that needs operator action) for that runtime. The item **resolves automatically** when the runtime becomes available again by any route: the toggle, a service restart or a later successful start. There is one item per exhaustion, not one per attempt.
- A restart replaces only the runtime process. Turns that were running stay held for the existing recovery path. Queued work is admitted only after the new runtime passes the existing startup and admission checks. Nothing is relaunched or resumed implicitly, and nothing is admitted twice.
- This applies to every harness that has an unavailable state (Codex, and Claude where it applies).
- A disabled runtime is never restarted, and disabling it during backoff cancels pending retries. Backoff state is not persisted: a service restart during backoff starts cleanly through normal startup.
- Each attempt and its outcome appears on the runtime page and in diagnostics.

**Key interfaces:**
- The service's per-harness unavailable state and its runtime reconciliation (the toggle's path): retries call this path and don't duplicate it.
- The attention inbox: a new problem item kind for "runtime restart exhausted", resolved by recovery.
- The runtime page and diagnostics payloads: attempt history (time, outcome, next attempt).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Deterministic test: a runtime fails with queued and running work. It restarts after backoff, queued work is then admitted, running work stays held, and there are no duplicate admissions.
- [ ] Deterministic test: persistent failure stops after the third attempt and produces exactly one attention item. Recovery through the toggle resolves the item.
- [ ] Deterministic test: a runtime that recovers and fails again within 10 minutes continues the same attempt count. One that stays available for 10 minutes resets it.
- [ ] Deterministic test: disabling during backoff cancels retries. A service restart during backoff starts cleanly with no leftover retry.
- [ ] The SPEC's runtime enablement and recovery paragraphs, `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` (replacing "Nothing restarts the App Server automatically") and the README describe the restart behaviour. "Retain unresolved holds rather than relaunching work" stays as it is.
- [ ] A bounded live check kills the real App Server process once while idle and once with work queued. It is recorded in `docs/evidence/`.

**Out of scope:**
- Relaunching, resuming or reattaching held turns.
- Making the retry schedule configurable.
- Restarting the service itself (#1144) or notifying outside the inbox (#1145).

content.title: Start the service unattended after a reboot

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Add an opt-in LaunchDaemon install mode that runs as the operator, so the service can start before GUI login, plus the credential path it needs.

**Decisions from triage:**
- Pursue option 2: a LaunchDaemon with `UserName` set to the operator. The per-user LaunchAgent stays the **default**, and the daemon is an **opt-in, privileged** install mode.
- The target host has FileVault on. Planned restarts and OS updates use `fdesetup authrestart`. After a power cut the disk stays locked until someone unlocks it, which remains a **disclosed limit**.
- Known credential facts on the host: the Codex login is file-based (`~/.codex/auth.json`), the gh login is keyring-backed, and the Claude token reference may be `file:`. The login keychain is normally unlocked only by GUI login.
- If the gh login can't be read before GUI login, as expected, add a **`file:` GitHub credential reference** to an operator-owned 0600 token file. Discovery, source reads and `git push` all use it. Don't put tokens in the daemon plist environment, because other local users can read it.

**Current behavior:**
`ensemble service install` renders a LaunchAgent in the operator's GUI domain. Nothing runs after a reboot until the operator logs in. GitHub credential references are `env:NAME` or `gh:github.com`.

**Desired behavior:**
- Probe first and record the result: as the operator, outside a GUI session where you can without sudo, check whether the Codex login, the gh login and a `file:` Claude token are readable. Record each in `docs/evidence/`.
- `ensemble service install` gains an opt-in daemon mode. It renders a LaunchDaemon with `UserName` set to the operator, the same fixed `PATH` and environment rules as the LaunchAgent, and the same data directory. When it can't write the system location, it explains the `sudo` step instead of escalating. Uninstall, and switching back to the LaunchAgent, are supported, and the two modes are never both active.
- A `file:` GitHub credential reference is accepted wherever `env:`/`gh:` references are. The file must be owned by the service user with mode 0600, or startup and Settings report a clear credential failure. Its value never appears in UI payloads, logs or child-process environments, the same rules as existing references.
- Readiness and startup reconciliation are unchanged. Reconciliation still runs before dispatch after any start.

**Key interfaces:**
- The LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon renderer and `ensemble service install`/uninstall commands.
- The credential reference schema (`env:` / `gh:` / new `file:` for GitHub), plus the discovery and source credential consumers and the git credential path used for push.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The probe results are recorded in `docs/evidence/`.
- [ ] Deterministic tests: the daemon plist renders with `UserName`, a fixed `PATH` and no secrets. Install refuses to leave both modes active. Uninstall/switch-back restores the LaunchAgent.
- [ ] Deterministic tests: a `file:` GitHub reference resolves for discovery, source reads and push. A wrong owner or mode, or a missing file, fails clearly. The value is excluded from child environments and payloads.
- [ ] `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`, the SPEC and ADR-1011 record the decision: the daemon mode, `authrestart` for planned restarts, power cuts with FileVault as a disclosed limit, and the `file:` reference.
- [ ] Deterministic coverage for the install itself. The real `sudo` install and reboot qualification belong to #1149.

**Out of scope:**
- Running `sudo`, installing on the real host or rebooting it (#1149).
- Making the daemon the default, or removing the LaunchAgent.
- Unattended recovery from a power cut with FileVault on.

content.title: Notify the operator when an agent needs input

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Deliver a Web Push notification to subscribed operator browsers when a new attention-inbox item needs the operator.

**Decisions from triage:**
- The channel is **Web Push** to the operator UI, using a service worker and VAPID keys generated at install. Outbound HTTPS from the service to the browser vendors' push endpoints is accepted. There is no third-party relay and no macOS-only notification.
- Live validation covers the **host browser only**. Phone delivery and opening the deep link on a phone move to #1150, which qualifies independent-device access. That is not a blocker for this issue.
- Notifications through ChatGPT stay out of scope (#734 / ADR-1006 remain paused).

**Current behavior:**
New questions, approvals and operator-action problems appear only in the attention inbox and task detail. The SPEC says the inbox is the notification source of truth, unchanged alerts are suppressed, and OS/push delivery is optional. No delivery channel exists.

**Desired behavior:**
- A **new** attention-inbox item (question, approval request, or problem needing operator action) produces exactly one push to each subscribed, unrevoked browser. Routine progress and completed work produce none.
- The payload is minimal: the item type, the project and the waiting count (for example "Question in fixture-app: 1 waiting"), and a deep link to that exact inbox item. It contains no question text, instructions, file content or credentials. Opening the link still needs the Ensemble login.
- Unchanged items aren't re-sent. When an item is resolved elsewhere, it gets no further push, and its notification closes where the platform allows.
- Settings has subscribe/unsubscribe for the current browser, a test notification, and a list of subscribed devices the operator can revoke. Muting is explicit, and pausing a project does not mute it.
- Notifications never answer or approve anything. `ensemble inbox` and the inbox UI are unchanged.

**Key interfaces:**
- The attention inbox's item creation and resolution events, as the trigger source.
- New persisted push subscriptions (endpoint, keys, created time, revoked flag) and VAPID key material in the service state, never exposed in payloads.
- Operator API routes for subscribe, unsubscribe, test and revoke, behind the existing operator login.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Deterministic tests: a new question or approval produces one push. An unchanged item produces none. A resolved item produces no further push. The payload contains no private text. Unsubscribed or revoked devices receive nothing.
- [ ] A browser test covers subscribe, the test notification, unsubscribe and opening the deep link.
- [ ] The SPEC and the `answer-question` / `approve-action` user flows describe delivery, payload limits and controls. `design/DESIGN.md` and the design canvas show the Settings controls, reusing the shared `Sidebar`/`TopBar` and existing tokens.
- [ ] A bounded live check on the host browser is recorded in `docs/evidence/`.

**Out of scope:**
- Phone or independent-device delivery qualification (#1150).
- ChatGPT, ntfy, Pushover, email or macOS-native notification channels.
- Answering or approving from a notification.

content.title: S08c: Execute the separately reviewed standalone project cutover
Install in one command and let doctor run before a CLI credential exists

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1080
**Planned against:** `main` at `a83792b2fcfc18e69d6532d8bcef69d780cbc015`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Extend the existing `service install` lifecycle in `src/cli/service.ts` instead of adding a new command. `service install [TARBALL]` keeps every current refusal and its undo-on-failure behaviour. It also unpacks a tarball into `STATE/versions/<version>`, prompts once for the operator password (creating the auth file when it is missing) and, after `/app` answers, signs in over the session API the UI uses. It then issues a `read`, 90-day credential named `install · <hostname>`, stores it as a normal CLI connection, runs `doctor` and prints/opens the URL. Everything after the health stage is best-effort: it never undoes or fails the install, and on any failure it prints the manual login line. The CLI-side work (storing the login, running doctor) stays in `src/cli/main.ts` behind an injected `InstallCli` seam, so `service.ts` keeps loading no operator-CLI state, and tests can fake it. Upgrade is not touched.

### Guardrails

- The recorded decision in #1080 is the contract: install issues the read credential; **doctor gets no credential-free local read**. Do not add any unauthenticated readiness route, a password-from-env/argv/stdin-pipe option, a credential with any scope but `read`, or an expiry other than 90 days. Any of these needs a new decision from Chris: stop and return it.
- `service upgrade` and `service uninstall` behaviour, output and refusals stay unchanged; upgrade never signs in or mints a credential.
- Keep the current install refusals unchanged and still before any launchd change: the release sits directly in `STATE/versions` with a matching `manifest.json`, the label is not loaded, no record or LaunchAgent exists, and the port is free. Keep the plist rendering, lock, lint, record and the undo of render/start/health failures.
- Nothing after a successful health stage may run `leaveStopped` or remove the record. Login, doctor and open failures, a wrong password and Ctrl-C at that point all leave the service installed and exit 0.
- Never print, log or put in argv the password or token (the existing `KeychainCredentialStore` stdin path and the `0600` token file are the only token sinks). Error output keeps the fixed-message `ServiceFailure` convention.
- Tests and live runs must never touch the user's real installation. Do not use the default label `local.ensemble.service`, the real `~/Library/{Application Support/Ensemble,LaunchAgents,Logs/Ensemble}`, the real `~/.config/ensemble`, the user's login Keychain or the browser (see Final validation).
- Out of scope: #1081 (data-directory mode), #1106 (`auth login` defaults/prompt copy), #1105/#1107 (help layout and Fix-line conventions), release signature/quarantine handling, and an upgrade-from-tarball form.
- **Mechanical plan mismatch vs ordinary repairs.** If a seam or repository fact this plan states turns out to be wrong (a named symbol, signature, route contract, file or command does not exist or behave as stated), that is a plan mismatch: make one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles that keep the same requirements, coverage, architecture and authority, record the correction in the delivery record, then stop and report if it still does not fit. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs belong to the implementer and do not use that budget. Investigate unknown overlap with sibling work. Stop for material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Both install forms run the first-run steps.** `service install` with no positional keeps binding to the release it runs from (today's behaviour and the live harness's form). `service install TARBALL` unpacks first and binds to the unpacked `STATE/versions/<version>`. Both then use the same password, login, doctor and open steps. This keeps one install path, and "or equivalent" in the acceptance criteria covers it.
- **Unpack is staged and idempotent.** Create `STATE/versions` (mode `0700`) if it is missing. Extract with `/usr/bin/tar -xzf TARBALL --strip-components 1 -C STAGING` into `mkdtemp(STATE/versions/.staging-)` (bsdtar refuses absolute and `..` member paths by default). Read `STAGING/manifest.json` with the existing `manifestSchema`. If `versions/<version>` is absent, rename the staging directory into place. If it exists with byte-identical `manifest.json` (the manifest carries the tree digest), reuse it and remove the staging directory. Otherwise refuse with "`STATE/versions/<version>` already holds a different release" and change nothing. Always remove the staging directory on failure. A later failure keeps the unpacked version, so a rerun reuses it, just as uninstall keeps versions. `releaseVersion()` then validates the target exactly as today.
- **Order of steps.** (1) Cheap preflight refusals: tarball is a readable regular file; label not loaded; no record or activation; port free; auth file missing with no interactive terminal is refused with "`<authFile>` is missing; run install in an interactive terminal or run `ensemble service init-auth`". (2) Hidden password prompt, once, on stderr: `Ensemble operator password: `, or `New Ensemble operator password: ` when the auth file is missing. (3) Unpack and `releaseVersion`. (4) When the auth file is missing, create `STATE/auth` (`0700`) and call `OperatorAuth.initialize(authFile, password)`. An empty or cancelled password then refuses before render. (5) Run the existing render, start and health stages. (6) Run the best-effort `login`, `doctor` and `open` steps.
  - With the auth file present, a cancelled or non-interactive prompt skips sign-in; it is not an error.
- **Sign-in is the UI's session API, from `service.ts` with `host.fetch`.** Call `GET /api/operator/session` to get the cookie and `csrfToken`. Call `POST /api/operator/login {password}`, which rotates the cookie and CSRF token. Then call `POST /api/operator/credentials {name, scope:"read", expiresInDays:90}` with the `origin: <install origin>`, `x-csrf-token` and `cookie` headers, as in `test/operations/service-lifecycle-qualification/live-service-lifecycle.mjs:313-336`. Parse responses with `sessionSchema` and `operatorCredentialIssuedSchema` from `src/operator/contracts.ts`. Hand the token to the `store` callback. If storing fails, `POST /api/operator/credentials/<id>/revoke {}` so no orphan active credential is left (this is the recovery path for the one irreversible mint). Always `POST /api/operator/logout {}` at the end. A 401 from login is `wrong-password`. Bound each request with `host.timeout(HEALTH_PROBE_MS)` plus the interrupt signal. One login attempt only, which keeps the service's lockout counter at one failure.
- **Credential name** is `install · ${hostname}` with control characters removed and truncated to 64 code points (`operatorCredentialNameSchema`). The hostname comes from a new `ServiceHost.hostname()` (default `os.hostname()`), so tests are deterministic.
- **Connection.** `--connection NAME` is now accepted for install. It defaults to `local`, the name the operations doc already uses with upgrade. `--token-file PATH` writes the token to a new file (`open(..., "wx", 0o600)`, refusing an existing path) and records a `token-file` connection. Without it the token goes to the Keychain through `deps.keychain().set`. The stored connection has exactly the shape `auth login` writes, including the identity-validated `installationId`, so `auth status/logout`, upgrade and Settings → CLI credentials treat it like any other.
- **Output contract.** The single JSON result line stays on stdout so scripted callers keep parsing it. It gains `"connection": NAME | null`, which is null when the CLI was not logged in. Human lines go to stderr in this order: the password prompt; doctor's table and `Fix …` lines (`main(["doctor","--connection",NAME])` with its stdout pointed at stderr); when not logged in, `Log in the CLI with a read credential from Settings → CLI credentials: ensemble auth login --connection NAME --url ORIGIN`, then `Then run: ensemble doctor`; finally `Open ORIGIN/app`. Then `host.open(ORIGIN/app)` runs unless `--no-open` is given; an open failure is ignored. `--no-open` is the one new non-contract flag, needed so scripted and live runs never open a browser.
- **No new security policy is needed.** Every step uses the existing session login, CSRF, credential issue/revoke and CLI storage paths. The trust-boundary paragraph in the issue is documented verbatim in substance.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/cli/service.ts`.
  - `installService` / `installServiceLocked` (lines ~619-698) run preflight → render → start → health and undo on any throw where `stage !== "preflight"`.
  - The `Service` class owns `releaseVersion`, `prepareDirectories`, `activate`, `bootstrap`, `waitForApp`, `checkInterrupt` and `write`.
  - `ServiceHost` (lines 76-91) is the fake-able OS boundary, and `defaultServiceHost()` (line ~897) implements it.
  - `serviceCommand` (line ~1017) parses lifecycle args with `parseLifecycleArgs`/`lifecycleOptions`. It currently requires 0 positionals for install and rejects `--connection` for install.
  - `initAuth` (line ~1075) is the TTY-gated `init-auth`.
  - `SERVICE_USAGE` (line 32) is the help text.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/main.ts`. `main()` dispatches `service` to `serviceCommand(argv, deps, name => operatorConnection(deps, name))` (line 145). `login()` (line ~577) validates a token through `ServiceClient.identity`, then writes the Keychain or token-file reference and `connections.json`. `doctorCommand` lives in `src/cli/doctor.ts`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator.ts:1634-1737` holds the session, login, logout and credential routes. POSTs require `Origin === auth.origin` and `x-csrf-token`. `src/standalone/operator-credentials.ts` `OperatorCredentialStore.issue/revoke` handles credentials. `src/standalone/operator-auth.ts` `OperatorAuth.initialize` and `src/standalone/operator-hidden-password.ts` `readHiddenPassword(input, output, prompt)` handle the password.
- **New:** `src/cli/service.ts`:
  - `export type InstallCli = { interactive: boolean; readPassword(prompt: string): Promise<string>; login(connection: string, origin: string, token: string, tokenFile: string | undefined): Promise<void>; doctor(connection: string): Promise<void> }`.
  - An `issueInstallCredential(host, origin, password, name, store, signal)` returning `"stored" | "wrong-password" | "failed"`.
  - `ServiceHost.extract(tarball, dir): Promise<boolean>`, `ServiceHost.open(url): Promise<void>` and `ServiceHost.hostname(): string`. The defaults are `/usr/bin/tar` (timeout 300 s, not the 20 s `run` default), `/usr/bin/open` and `os.hostname`.
  - `installService(options, release, host, io, first?: { tarball?: string; cli?: InstallCli; connection: string; tokenFile?: string; open: boolean })`. Without `first.cli`, as in existing direct tests, sign-in is skipped and the manual line is printed.
- **New:** `src/cli/main.ts`, `export function installCli(deps: CliDeps): InstallCli`.
  - `login` reuses a `saveLogin(config, deps, name, origin, token, tokenFile)` extracted from `login()`. `login()` then calls it unchanged in behaviour. With a `tokenFile`, `installCli.login` first writes the file exclusively at `0600`.
  - `doctor` calls `main(["doctor", "--connection", name], { ...deps, stdout: deps.stderr })`.
  - `readPassword` wraps `readHiddenPassword(deps.stdin, deps.stderr, prompt)`.
  - `interactive` is `Boolean(deps.stdin.isTTY && deps.stderr.isTTY)`.
  - `main()` passes `defaultServiceHost` and `installCli(deps)` to `serviceCommand`, which gains a fifth parameter `cli?: InstallCli`.
- **Follow:** `test/operations/service-lifecycle.test.ts` `FakeLaunchd.host()`/`setup()`/`release()` for fake-host lifecycle tests. `test/fixtures/operator-cli.ts` `serveCli`/`startCliService` for a real operator HTTP service with real `OperatorAuth` and credentials. Its auth origin is fixed at `http://127.0.0.1:8787`, so tests use a fetch wrapper that rewrites that origin's URLs to the served port while keeping the `Origin` header.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3; acyclic, strictly sequential. T1 and T2 both edit `src/cli/service.ts` and `src/cli/main.ts`, and T3 needs T2's built release behaviour. No tasks run concurrently.

#### 1. Credential issuance and CLI login seam

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/cli/service.ts`: `InstallCli` type and `issueInstallCredential`.
- `src/cli/main.ts`: `saveLogin` extracted from `login()`, and the exported `installCli(deps)`.
- New test file `test/operations/install-credential.test.ts`.

**Test:** In `test/operations/install-credential.test.ts` (non-browser, real service via `startCliService`), with a URL-rewriting fetch as in Implementation context:
- (a) `issueInstallCredential` with `"fixture-password"` and name `install · test-host` returns `stored`. The stored token's `GET /api/operator/cli` bearer identity reports that name, scope `read` and an expiry 90 days after creation. The session cookie is logged out afterwards (`GET /api/operator/session` with it reports `authenticated:false`).
- (b) A wrong password returns `wrong-password`, calls `store` zero times and leaves the `credentials.list()` count unchanged.
- (c) A `store` that throws returns `failed`, and the issued credential is listed `revoked`.
- (d) `installCli(deps).login("local", origin, token, tokenFile)` with a temp `ENSEMBLE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` writes the token file at mode `0600`. `connections.json` then holds `{url, installationId, credential:{kind:"token-file"}}`, and an existing token-file path is refused. With a fake `CredentialStore`, omitting `tokenFile` calls `set("local", token)` once.
- (e) `installCli(deps).doctor("local")` writes doctor's readiness table to the injected stderr and nothing to stdout.

Existing `auth login` tests in `test/operator/operator-cli.test.ts` must still pass unchanged.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions (sign-in sequence, revoke-on-store-failure, logout, name sanitising). `saveLogin` is a pure extraction, so the observable behaviour of `login()` is unchanged.
**Validate:** From the repo root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operations/install-credential.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-cli.test.js`; expect all tests to pass with 0 failures.
**Complete when:** The new contract tests pass against the real operator routes, and `auth login` tests are unchanged and green.

#### 2. One-command install with login, doctor and open; docs

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the working branch.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/cli/service.ts`:
  - `ServiceHost` gains `extract`/`open`/`hostname`, with defaults in `defaultServiceHost`.
  - `installService`/`installServiceLocked` gain the `first` parameter, the new stages `unpack` and `login`, and the post-health best-effort block.
  - `parseLifecycleArgs` gains `token-file` (string) and `no-open` (boolean).
  - In `serviceCommand`, install takes 0 or 1 positional and accepts `--connection`, `--token-file` and `--no-open`. Upgrade and uninstall still reject `--token-file` and `--no-open`, and uninstall still rejects `--connection`.
  - `SERVICE_USAGE` documents `service install [TARBALL] [--connection NAME] [--token-file PATH] [--no-open] [SERVICE_OPTIONS]`.
- `src/cli/main.ts`: pass `defaultServiceHost, installCli(deps)` to `serviceCommand`.
- `test/operations/service-lifecycle.test.ts`.
- `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` (Install section, the first-install block before it, and the "Then log in…" paragraph).
- `docs/user-flows/readiness-check.md` (status line, Entry points).
- `docs/user-flows/first-run.md`: status line only, to say the one-command install is implemented and the budget is not yet asserted.

**Test:** In `test/operations/service-lifecycle.test.ts`, use `FakeLaunchd` extended with:
- a route-aware `fetch` (`/app` → `health`; session, login, credentials, revoke and logout emulate the contract and record method, path, headers and body);
- `extract` running real `/usr/bin/tar` on a tarball built in the test with `tar -czf` from a `release()` tree under a top directory;
- `open` recording URLs;
- `hostname` returning `test-host`;

and a fake `InstallCli` recording calls. Cases:
- **tarball install, auth present.** It unpacks to `versions/0.1.0`, leaves no `.staging-*`, and the plist `ProgramArguments[0]` is the unpacked node. The credential POST body is `{"name":"install · test-host","scope":"read","expiresInDays":90}` with `origin` and `x-csrf-token`. `cli.login("local", origin, token, undefined)` then `cli.doctor("local")` run, `open` gets `ORIGIN/app`, and the stdout JSON has `ok:true` and `connection:"local"`. Exit 0.
- **auth missing, interactive.** It prompts with `New Ensemble operator password: `, the auth file then exists at mode `0600`, and `OperatorAuth.open` accepts that password.
- **auth missing, non-interactive.** It refuses at preflight: no `versions/<v>`, no launchd mutation, no auth file. Exit 1.
- **wrong password (login 401) and store failure.** Each exits 0 with the record and activation present, no `bootout`, `connection:null`, and stderr containing the `ensemble auth login --connection local --url ORIGIN` line. Doctor is not called. Store failure triggers one revoke POST.
- **Interrupt** (abort `io.signal`) during the login stage leaves the service installed (no `bootout`).
- **Existing version directory.** With identical `manifest.json` it is reused. With a different one it is refused, with the existing tree unchanged (`tree()`) and no launchd mutation.
- **The existing refusal test** (`install refusals change nothing and never bootstrap`) still passes for both forms. Add a tarball-form run for loaded label, existing record and busy port, asserting no `versions/<v>` was created for the cheap refusals.
- **`--no-open`** makes no `open` call.
- **`--token-file`** is passed through to `cli.login`.
- **Upgrade never mints.** After a full upgrade test, the fake fetch saw no `/api/operator/login` or `/api/operator/credentials` request.
- **Argument validation.** `install a b` is a usage error. `upgrade … --token-file x`, `upgrade … --no-open`, `uninstall --token-file x` and `uninstall --connection x` return 2.

Existing tests that `JSON.parse` the install stdout must keep passing unmodified, apart from the new `connection` field.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Put the post-health block in its own `try/catch` that only writes stderr lines, so no exception after `health` reaches the undo path. `checkInterrupt` must not be called there. Report `stage:"unpack"` failures with `jobStopped:null`, the same as preflight. The docs replace the hand procedure with the following and keep `init-auth` and the manual login as the documented fallback:

```sh
ensemble-0.1.0-darwin-arm64/bin/ensemble service install ensemble-0.1.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
```

They describe the password prompt, the issued credential (name, `read`, 90 days, Keychain or `--token-file`), doctor, open and the non-fatal failures. They state the trust boundary: whoever runs install as the service user already holds the auth file and data directory, so the issued read credential widens nothing, and it is listed, rotatable and revocable in Settings → CLI credentials. They also state that upgrade never mints a credential and that an expired or revoked one stops upgrade with the existing message.
**Validate:** From the repo root, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operations/service-lifecycle.test.js dist/test/operations/ensemble-local-commands.test.js dist/test/operations/install-credential.test.js`; expect all tests to pass with 0 failures. Then run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run format:check` and expect each to exit 0.
**Complete when:** Every case above is green, and the docs describe the one-command procedure, its fallback and the trust boundary.

#### 3. Bounded live qualification of the one-command install

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 complete. The controller has confirmed the access listed under Final validation.
**Files and symbols:**
- `test/operations/service-lifecycle-qualification/live-service-lifecycle.mjs`.
- A new `docs/evidence/1080-one-command-install-<run date>.md`, linked from the "Not yet proven" or Install text in `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`.

**Implementation:**
- Change the harness so that release A is installed with the new form, run from the build's unpacked `ensemble-<v>-darwin-arm64/bin/ensemble`:

  ```sh
  service install <tarball A> --connection live --token-file <root>/cli/token --no-open --label <throwaway> --state-dir … --log-dir … --launch-agents-dir … --port <free>
  ```

  Do not create the auth file first, so creation is exercised.
- Drive the hidden prompt through a pseudo-terminal with `/usr/bin/script -q /dev/null <ensemble> …`. Write the random password only after the prompt text appears, never write raw pty output to evidence, and pass `HOME`/`ENSEMBLE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` inside the temp root.
- Assert:
  - exit 0, with the JSON `connection:"live"`;
  - `versions/<A>` was created by install;
  - the token file is mode `0600`;
  - `ensemble auth status --connection live` reports scope `read` and a name starting with `install · `;
  - stderr contains doctor's table.
- Then run the existing upgrade to B with `--connection live`, which proves the install-issued credential satisfies upgrade's readiness read, then uninstall and run the existing postflight comparison.
- Keep the harness's refusal without `--live` and its cleanup.

**Validate:** From the repo root on the qualifying Mac, run `node test/operations/service-lifecycle-qualification/live-service-lifecycle.mjs --live`; expect exit 0, every step recorded, the throwaway label absent afterwards (`launchctl print` exit 113) and the temp root removed. Record the identity, steps and limits in the evidence file. If `/usr/bin/script` cannot drive the prompt after one focused diagnosis, stop and report the live gap to the controller. Do not add a non-interactive password path; that is a security-policy decision for Chris.
**Complete when:** One passing live run is recorded in the evidence file. The file states what is still unqualified: the default label and real `~/Library` paths, the Keychain write from install, the browser open, and a quarantined browser-downloaded tarball.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `service install <tarball>` unpacks into the version directory, prompts for the password when the auth file is missing, installs, waits for `/app`, prints and opens the URL | 2, 3 | T2 tarball/auth-missing/open cases; T3 live run |
| Current refusal checks (release location, manifest version, port free, label unloaded) still apply | 2 | T2 existing refusal test plus tarball-form refusals |
| Install issues the read credential and logs the CLI in; trust boundary in the operations doc | 1, 2, 3 | T1 (a)/(d); T2 credential body and `cli.login`; T3 `auth status`; T2 doc edit |
| Install runs doctor and prints its result before opening the URL; a failed check or wrong password leaves the service installed and prints the manual login line | 1, 2 | T1 (e); T2 call order, wrong-password, store-failure and interrupt cases |
| Upgrade is unchanged and never mints a credential | 2, 3 | T2 upgrade-never-mints assertion and unchanged upgrade tests; T3 upgrade via the install credential |
| `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` and `docs/user-flows/readiness-check.md` describe the new procedure | 2 | T2 doc edits and format check |

### Final validation

- From the repo root on Node `24.21.0` (`.node-version`), run `npm ci && npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate, before review and PR. Expect typecheck, lint, format and every test profile to pass. The PR's CI `check` context must be green.
- Live qualification (T3) needs access CI does not have, so the controller must confirm it before T3:
  - a macOS arm64 GUI login session for the implementing agent's user, with real `/bin/launchctl` and `/usr/bin/script`;
  - network access to `nodejs.org` for `scripts/package-release.mjs build`;
  - about 2 GB of temp space;
  - Codex installed. This is optional: doctor's result does not fail install, and upgrade's readiness accepts Not configured, as in #980.
- Exclusive resources:
  - one throwaway launchd label `local.ensemble.validation-<random hex>` in `gui/<uid>`;
  - one free loopback port chosen at run time;
  - a `mkdtemp` root of mode `0700` holding state, logs, LaunchAgents, `HOME` and CLI config.
- Not used: the default label `local.ensemble.service`, port 8787 (unless free and randomly chosen), the user's login Keychain (the run uses `--token-file`), the browser (`--no-open`) and any path under the real `~/Library` or `~/.config/ensemble`.
- Unit and integration tests use the fake launchd host, temp directories, `freePort()`, a fake `CredentialStore` and the fixture service's random port. They need no live access.
- The Keychain write path is covered by the injected fake. The existing opt-in `ENSEMBLE_KEYCHAIN_LIVE=1` test covers the real store with a unique service name and is not required here.

### Review focus

- No exception after `health` reaches the undo path, and no stage reorders the existing refusals behind a side effect.
- Token and password hygiene: no argv, log, JSON output or evidence exposure. The token file is created exclusively at `0600`. Revoke-on-store-failure and logout run on every exit path.
- Staged unpack: the staging directory is cleaned on every failure, a different release under an existing version is refused, and member-path handling follows bsdtar defaults.
- Overlap with sibling tickets:
  - **#1106** edits `login()` and the `auth login` prompt in `src/cli/main.ts`. This plan only extracts `saveLogin` without behaviour change. Whichever lands second rebases and keeps one shared login path. If #1106 has landed and chosen a default connection name or new login-line wording, install's default `--connection` and its printed manual login line must use the same name and wording.
  - **#1105** restructures `USAGE`/`SERVICE_USAGE` and help output, which conflicts textually with T2's `SERVICE_USAGE` line. Its "Next: ensemble doctor" rule applies to `auth login` only.
  - **#1107** adds `Fix:` remedies to `CliError` messages in `src/cli/main.ts`/`connections.ts`. Install's manual login line should follow its Fix/Next wording if it has landed.
  - **#1081** touches `src/standalone/readiness.ts` and data-directory claiming only; there is no file overlap. Install still creates `data` at `0700` as today.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- The real session API cannot issue the credential as specified (for example, the `Origin` check rejects the install origin). Diagnose once under the plan-mismatch budget. If it needs a route or auth-policy change, stop and return it for a decision.
- Any need for a non-interactive password source, a credential-free readiness read, or a scope or expiry other than `read`/90 days stops the work and goes back to Chris.

content.title: Set the data directory mode on first start instead of failing readiness

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1081
**Planned against:** `main` at `a83792b2fcfc18e69d6532d8bcef69d780cbc015`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Set the mode where the claim already happens: in `StandaloneDataDirectory.openExclusive`, inside the existing fresh-claim branch (`!markerIsReady`, after the SQLite owner lock is held and before the marker is written), make the data directory `0700` when the service user owns it. A failed `chmod` does not stop startup; readiness keeps reporting the current rule and fix. Readiness itself is unchanged.

### Guardrails

- `src/standalone/readiness.ts` (`dataPaths`) and its reasons/fixes are unchanged: a directory that is not owned by the service user, or whose mode could not be changed, still fails with "Data directory must not permit group or other access" / "Run chmod 700 on the data directory".
- Only a fresh claim changes the mode: an already marked directory (any mode) is never touched, and a non-empty unmarked directory is still refused by `standaloneMarkerReady` before any change. `createFreshMarker: false` paths (offline operations, restore) never reach the branch.
- No new permission policy: no change to ownership checks, auth-file rules, install/launchd validation (`src/cli/service.ts` `prepareDirectories`/`requireDirectory`, `src/standalone/launchd.ts` `requirePrivateDirectory`) or the marker/owner-file contract.
- Out of scope: `service install`, doctor, the operations runbook (`docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`) — owned by sibling #1080.
- Plan-mismatch vs ordinary repairs: if an approved-plan seam or repository assumption proves factually wrong (for example `openExclusive` is not the first-start claim path, or the fresh-claim branch is not reached for an empty directory), that is a mechanical plan mismatch: one focused diagnosis plus at most two repair cycles, then stop and report. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the implementer and do not consume that budget. Record routine corrections in the delivery record and renew affected evidence; investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Seam: `data-directory.ts`, not `service.ts`.** `StandaloneService.start` (`src/standalone/service.ts:608`) delegates the claim to `StandaloneDataDirectory.openExclusive`; the marker write in its `!markerIsReady` branch is the "claims an empty directory and writes its marker" moment the issue names. Changing it there covers every fresh claim, including recovery of an interrupted first start (empty `.ensemble-owner.sqlite`, partial marker), which is still a first start.
- **Ownership guard.** Change the mode only when `lstatSync(canonical).uid === process.getuid?.()`. Without it, a service running as root would silently alter another user's directory and the readiness message for a foreign-owned directory would change (it would lose the mode rule). This realises AC 2 ("not owned by the service user ... still fails readiness with the current message").
- **Best-effort `chmod`.** Wrap `chmodSync(canonical, 0o700)` in `try/catch` and continue; the existing readiness check is the reporting path for "mode cannot be changed" (AC 2). Startup must not fail on it, since that would replace the readiness Fix line with a startup error.
- **Installed path checked; unchanged.** `ServiceManager.prepareDirectories` (`src/cli/service.ts:378-390`) creates a missing data directory with `0700` and `requireDirectory(..., exclusive=true)` refuses an existing one with any group/other bit, and `launchd.ts` `requirePrivateDirectory` refuses it again at render. `service install` therefore cannot hand the service a `755` data directory; no install change.
- **Test placement.** `test/operations/standalone.test.ts` already owns `openExclusive` claim/ownership behaviour; the new cases go there. Root/foreign-uid and `chmod` failure cannot be produced portably by an unprivileged test without adding an injection option nobody asked for; those branches are covered by the guard's code review plus the unchanged readiness tests (`test/coordination/readiness.test.ts` "the data and auth paths check names the rule, not the path", which asserts the 755 and foreign-uid messages).

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/data-directory.ts` — `StandaloneDataDirectory.openExclusive` creates a missing directory with `mkdirSync(..., { mode: 0o700 })` (umask-dependent), validates canonical path, calls `standaloneMarkerReady` (throws for non-empty unmarked contents), opens the owner DB with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and in `if (!markerIsReady)` writes the marker. An existing empty `755` directory passes all of this unchanged today.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/readiness.ts:509` `Readiness.dataPaths` — `(data.mode & 0o077) !== 0` → fail with the current reason/fix.
- **Existing:** `docs/development.md` (~line 108) — "On first use, the directory must be empty or carry Ensemble's standalone marker…" describes the first-start claim.
- **Follow:** `src/standalone/operations.ts` `reserveDirectory` (`mkdirSync` + `chmodSync(path, 0o700)`) for the sync `chmodSync` style.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Single task `T1`; acyclic. No concurrency within this issue.

#### 1. Fresh claim makes the data directory private

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/standalone/data-directory.ts` — `StandaloneDataDirectory.openExclusive`, fresh-claim branch; add `chmodSync` to the `node:fs` import.
- `test/operations/standalone.test.ts` — new tests next to the existing `openExclusive` cases.
- `docs/development.md` — one sentence in the first-use paragraph.
**Test:** In `test/operations/standalone.test.ts`, using `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), ...))` and `rmSync` cleanup like neighbouring tests:
1. "claiming an empty data directory makes it private": `mkdirSync(data)`; `chmodSync(data, 0o755)`; `StandaloneDataDirectory.openExclusive(data).close()`; assert `statSync(data).mode & 0o777` equals `0o700`.
2. "an already claimed data directory keeps its mode": open and close once (claims), `chmodSync(data, 0o755)`, `openExclusive(data).close()` again; assert mode is still `0o755` (only the claim changes it).
Sensitivity: test 1 fails on the base commit (mode stays `0o755`).
**Implementation:** In `openExclusive`, inside `if (!markerIsReady) { ... }` after the `createFreshMarker === false` throw and before the marker write: if `lstatSync(canonical).uid === process.getuid?.()`, `try { chmodSync(canonical, 0o700); } catch { /* readiness reports a mode that could not be changed */ }`. Add to `docs/development.md` after "On first use, the directory must be empty or carry Ensemble's standalone marker.": "Claiming an empty directory owned by the service user sets its mode to `0700`; an existing marked directory keeps its mode, and readiness reports one that permits group or other access."
**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operations/standalone.test.js dist/test/coordination/readiness.test.js`; expect all tests pass, including the two new ones and the unchanged data-paths readiness test.
**Complete when:** Both new tests pass, the readiness test is unchanged and passing, and the docs sentence is present.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| On first start the service sets mode 0700 on the empty data directory it claims | 1 | New test "claiming an empty data directory makes it private" |
| A non-empty, foreign-owned, or unchangeable-mode directory still fails readiness with the current message | 1 | New test "an already claimed data directory keeps its mode"; existing "Unmarked data directory must be empty" refusal (`test/operations/operations.test.ts`); unchanged `readiness.test.ts` data-paths test (755 and foreign-uid messages); ownership guard + catch reviewed |
| A test covers the first-start case | 1 | New test 1 |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate; expect typecheck, lint, format, build and the full test suite to pass. CI on the PR runs the same profiles (`docs/development.md`).

### Review focus

- The `chmod` sits inside the fresh-claim branch only, after the owner lock, and is skipped for a directory not owned by `process.getuid()`.
- No change to readiness reasons/fixes or to install/launchd validation.

### Coordination (controller)

- **Files touched:** `src/standalone/data-directory.ts`, `test/operations/standalone.test.ts`, `docs/development.md`.
- **Exclusive resources:** none beyond those files; tests use temp directories only. No live runtime, Keychain, launchd, ports or GitHub access needed.
- **Overlap with #1080 (install in one command):** #1080 is sequenced after this issue and changes `src/cli/service.ts`, doctor, `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` and `docs/user-flows/readiness-check.md`. This plan touches none of those. Residual risk: if #1080 edits `docs/development.md` or adds tests in `test/operations/standalone.test.ts`, expect a trivial textual merge only; no shared symbols.

content.title: Flaky operator-comments browser test: source refresh follow-up request times out

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Make the operator-comments browser test's follow-up task `GET` wait independent of Playwright's request/response event ordering.

**Current behavior:**
In the test "approval-mode exact operator review and unknown remote comment retain original intent through viewing and provider read reconciliation", the `settleAction` helper arms its follow-up task `GET` wait before the click, so the wait is not armed late. That wait ignores any task `GET` observed while an `acknowledged` flag is still false. The flag is set only when the action's POST response event is evaluated. If the app's follow-up `GET` request event is delivered before the POST response event (plausible under CI load, since the app refetches as soon as the fetch resolves), that `GET` is skipped permanently. Nothing else sends a task `GET`, so the 5 s `waitForRequest` times out. This is the leading hypothesis, consistent with the evidence in the issue but not reproduced.

The app side is ruled out as a cause: the source-refresh handler always calls the foreground refresh right after the POST resolves, and a foreground load supersedes any in-flight read instead of being coalesced. Only background polls bail out. The `"view"` action goes through the same gate and is exposed the same way. The `"task"` action starts acknowledged and is not.

**Desired behavior:**
`settleAction` for `"source"` and `"view"` finds the first task `GET` that started after the action's POST was sent, regardless of whether the POST response event has been evaluated yet. For example, record candidate task `GET`s since the click and select by "started after the POST request", not by "acknowledged flag". Or wait on `taskRead` and an observable UI outcome instead. A superseded or aborted earlier read must not satisfy the wait. The existing guarantee that a prior view `GET` cannot satisfy a later `"source"` action still holds. The milestone marks and failure evidence stay intact.

**Key interfaces:**
- `settleAction("view" | "source" | "task")` in the operator-comments browser test: the `taskRequest` waiter and its `acknowledged` gate.
- The `acknowledged` flag, set from the POST `waitForResponse` predicate: stop using it as a precondition for observing the task `GET`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Root cause is confirmed with a deterministic reproduction, for example by delaying the POST response event or forcing the `GET` before it. The reproduction fails before the fix and passes after. If the gate is not the cause, record what the evidence shows and fix that instead.
- [ ] No step of `settleAction` depends on the relative order of the POST response event and the follow-up `GET` request event.
- [ ] The test's assertions on original intent and on provider-read reconciliation are unchanged.
- [ ] 20 consecutive runs of the file pass locally.
- [ ] The file passes in the `node24-integrations` CI profile, repeated runs included.
- [ ] Non-browser cases in the file remain independently runnable, and the file keeps its `browserTest`/`browserSuite` registration.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the app's refresh or polling behavior.
- Raising the 5 s timeout as the fix.
- Reworking other browser tests unless they share the same gate pattern. Report any that do instead of changing them here.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1102
**Planned against:** `main` at `a83792b2fcfc18e69d6532d8bcef69d780cbc015`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Settle the root cause first, using the failing CI run's milestone log plus a bounded reproduction. Then change only the test's `settleAction` helper and the test's route setup. The helper must not depend on the order of Playwright events. The follow-up task read must not cross a Playwright route-expiry interception toggle. All assertions stay unchanged.

### Guardrails

- Change test code only, in `test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.ts`. Out of scope: app refresh and polling behaviour (`web/src/task-workspace.tsx`, `web/src/resource.ts`, `web/src/api.ts`), the service, raising the 5 s timeout, and other browser tests. Report other tests that share the pattern; do not change them. `test/workspaces/operator-retention-access-browser.test.ts` also uses `{ times: 1 }` routes.
- Keep the test's assertions on original intent and provider-read reconciliation unchanged. That covers the view receipt `deepEqual`, the source-refresh project assertion, `currentTask.data.task.id`, the held-repeat-view no-receipt check, the source identity and version checks, and every comparison text wait. Keep the milestone marks, `source-segment-final-state`, `source-segment-milestones`, the `browserSuite("operator-comments-browser")` registration, and independent runs of the non-browser cases.
- A prior view `GET` must never satisfy a later `"source"` action. An aborted or superseded read must never satisfy the wait.
- Plan-mismatch rule: a wrong factual assumption in this plan gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before the implementer stops and reports. Examples: `settleAction` or the route setup is not where or shaped as described, the Playwright 1.64 `_onRoute` expiry path differs, or the run commands below do not work. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the implementer under normal repair rules and do not use that allowance. Continue routine corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority, record each correction, and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **The triage hypothesis is refuted by the CI evidence.** Run 38941092604, attempt 1, job 117108958210 (`node24-integrations-1`) logged `source-segment-milestones`. In step `partial-source` it shows `source-route-fulfilled` at 520 ms and `source-post-response` at 521 ms, so `acknowledged` became true. After that there is **no `task-get-started` mark at all**. That mark comes from the ungated `page.on("request", observeRequest)` listener. `source-segment-final-state` was `{"errorCategory":"timeout","unknown":true,...}`. Playwright therefore never emitted a request event for the follow-up `GET`, so the `acknowledged` gate (the agent brief's hypothesis) is not what failed here. In the passing attempt 2 on the same SHA, the same step shows `source-post-response` at 398 ms, then `task-get-started` at 417 ms.
- **The app is ruled out as far as the code shows.** The final state shows "source comparison unknown", not "pending". So `refreshSource()` in `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` passed `owned()`, took the partial branch (`setSourceObservation("unknown")`), and then called `refresh()` without a condition. `refresh()` calls `resource.load(loader)` as a foreground load, which never bails (`web/src/resource.ts`), and `loader` calls `client.read`, which calls `fetch` directly (`web/src/api.ts`). Page-side instrumentation in T1 verifies this, because the evidence cannot prove that the page issued the fetch.
- **The leading remaining hypothesis (H2) is Playwright route expiry.** The source-refresh route is registered with `{ times: 1 }`. In Playwright 1.64 (`node_modules/playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js`, page `_onRoute`), an expiring handler is removed from `_routes`. After `handle(route)` resolves, which is after `fulfill`, Playwright calls `_updateInterceptionPatterns` when `_routes` is empty. That turns request interception off at the moment the app sends its follow-up `GET`, so a `GET` paused under the old patterns can be lost or stalled. At that point no other route is registered, because the held-repeat-view `{ times: 1 }` commands route has already expired. T1 must confirm or refute H2 before T2 applies the H2 fix.
- **Ordering fix.** `settleAction` stops using `acknowledged` as a precondition. It records every task `GET` request event that arrives after the action's originating request (`sent`) is matched. Request events are delivered in issue order, and the app sends the follow-up only after the POST resolves, so a `GET` from before the action can never match. `taskRead` resolves on the first response whose request is in that recorded set. An aborted read never produces a response, so it cannot satisfy the wait. The page polls every 15 s (`setInterval(..., 15000)`) and the segment takes under 1 s, so a background poll does not need its own handling. The `"task"` action keeps using its own request.
- **Interception fix (applies if T1 confirms H2 or leaves it as the only unrefuted candidate).** Before the first `{ times: 1 }` route, register one segment-scoped pass-through route, `page.route("**/api/operator/**", (route) => route.fallback())`. Remove it with `page.unroute` in the existing `finally`/`j.cleanup` path. Playwright tries the most recently registered route first, so the specific `times: 1` handlers still run first. Because `_routes` never empties during an action, an expiring handler no longer switches interception off. Keep the existing `{ times: 1 }` handlers as they are.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.ts` contains:
  - `settleAction` (lines ~639–766), which holds the `post`, `request`, `taskRequest` and `taskRead` waiters and the `acknowledged` gate (lines 641, 647, 682).
  - The `observeRequest`/`observeFailure` milestone listeners (lines ~619–636).
  - The `{ times: 1 }` routes for held-repeat-view (`**/api/operator/commands`, line ~785) and partial-source (`**/api/operator/source-refresh`, line ~830).
  - Failure reporting in the `catch`/`finally` (lines ~888–920).
  - The `"source"` call sites at lines 861 and 885 and the `"view"` call sites at lines 777 and 798.
- **Existing:** `test/fixtures/browser-diagnostics.ts` provides `browserSuite` and `captureBrowserEvidence`. Evidence directories hold only `manifest.json`, sanitized logs and screenshots, with no network trace, so the milestone log is the network evidence.
- **Follow:** the existing `mark(...)` milestones and `source-segment-final-state` for added diagnostics. Keep both bounded the same way (64 events).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3. The graph is acyclic and strictly sequential: all three slices edit or validate the same file, and the T2 interception fix depends on T1's result.

#### 1. Establish the root cause

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** `test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.ts`: add page-side fetch instrumentation. The reproduction harness lives outside the repository (scratch directory, not committed).
**Implementation:**
1. Add permanent page-side evidence. Before navigation, or before the segment if the page is already loaded, use `page.addInitScript`/`page.evaluate` to wrap `window.fetch` so it records the start and settle of fetches to `taskPath` in a bounded window array. Include the counts in `source-segment-final-state`. The wrap must return the original promise unchanged so app behaviour stays the same. This separates three cases: the app never fetched, the app fetched and Playwright saw nothing, and the fetch stalled.
2. Build a deterministic reproduction of H2 in a scratch Playwright script:
   - Serve a trivial page from a local `http.createServer` on port 0.
   - In page code, `fetch("/a")` then, as soon as it resolves, `fetch("/b")`.
   - Register only `page.route("**/a", fulfill, { times: 1 })`.
   - Record `/b` request events with timestamps and whether `/b` resolves within 5 s.
   - Run N=300 iterations, including a variant with a 0–20 ms delay before `fulfill`, and a control variant with an extra persistent `route.fallback()` catch-all.
   - H2 is confirmed when the expiring-route variant misses or stalls `/b` at least once and the control misses none.
   - If it does not reproduce, repeat the real test file under load, for example 4 concurrent loops of 15 runs, using the instrumentation from step 1.
3. Write down the root cause and its evidence, including the CI milestones cited in Planning decisions, for the PR description. If the instrumentation shows the app never called `fetch`, stop: the cause is in the app, which is out of scope, so re-plan.

**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm run build`, run `ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=chromium node --test dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js`. Expect every test to pass, with the new fetch counts in the logged final state on failure. Run the scratch harness with `node <scratch>/repro.mjs`. Expect counts of missed or stalled `/b` for the expiring and control variants.
**Complete when:** The root cause is recorded with evidence: H2 confirmed by the harness, H2 left as the only unrefuted candidate with the reproduction attempts recorded, or a different cause shown by instrumentation. The instrumentation is in place and the file passes.

#### 2. Remove the event-order and interception dependence

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 recorded a cause that is not an app defect.
**Files and symbols:** `test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.ts`: `settleAction`, the held-repeat-view and partial-source route setup, and segment cleanup.
**Implementation:** Apply the Planning decisions ordering fix to `settleAction`:
- Delete `acknowledged`.
- The `taskRequest` predicate accepts task `GET`s only after `sent` is set, and adds each one to a per-action `Set<Request>`. The first one also resolves `taskRequest` and the `task-get-started` milestone flow is unchanged.
- `taskRead` waits for a response whose request is in the set.
- The POST response predicate still marks `view-command-recorded`/`source-post-response`.

Apply the interception fix if T1 confirms H2 or leaves it as the only unrefuted candidate. If T1 showed a different, non-app cause, fix that cause in this file instead and record it.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm run build`:
- Rerun the T1 scratch reproduction against the changed helper pattern. Expect 0 misses where the old pattern missed at least once.
- Run `ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=chromium node --test dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js`. Expect all tests to pass.
- Run `ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=none node --test dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js`. Expect the browser cases to be skipped and every non-browser case to pass.
- Run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run format:check`. Expect a clean result.
- Confirm by diff that no assertion line changed.

**Complete when:** No step of `settleAction` reads state set by a POST response predicate before it observes the task `GET`. If H2 applies, interception stays enabled across every action, and the focused checks pass.

#### 3. Prove stability

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 complete.
**Files and symbols:** none (validation only).
**Validate:**
- From the checkout root, after `npm run build`, run `for i in $(seq 1 20); do ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=chromium node --test dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js || { echo "failed on run $i"; exit 1; }; done`. Expect 20 of 20 passes.
- Repeat under load: 4 concurrent copies of a 5-run loop. Expect no failures. Record both results.
- Run the lane locally with `npm run test:built -- --suite=coordination,sources,delivery,operations,infrastructure --profile=chromium`. Expect it to pass.
- In CI on the PR: the `node24-integrations-1` job must pass. Then rerun that job twice with `gh run rerun <run-id> --job <job-id>`. Expect 3 of 3 green runs. Link them in the PR.

**Complete when:** The local and CI repeat evidence is recorded in the PR.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Root cause identified from the CI evidence or a deterministic reproduction; a reproduction that fails before the fix and passes after, or a recorded alternative cause | 1, 2 | T1 harness and instrumentation; T2 harness rerun |
| No step of `settleAction` depends on the order of the POST response event and the follow-up `GET` request event; no dependence on a request that can race or be lost | 2 | T2 diff review and focused file run |
| Assertions on original intent and provider-read reconciliation unchanged | 2 | T2 assertion-unchanged diff check |
| 20 consecutive local runs pass | 3 | T3 20-run loop |
| Passes in the `node24-integrations` CI profile, including repeated runs | 3 | T3 PR CI plus 2 job reruns |
| Non-browser cases independently runnable; `browserSuite` registration kept | 2 | T2 `ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=none` run |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate. Expect type checking, lint, formatting, build and all tests to pass.
- PR CI `check` must be green, including `node24-integrations-1` and its two reruns from T3.

### Review focus

- A recorded task `GET` set must not let an aborted foreground read or an earlier view read settle a later action.
- The catch-all fallback route must not change routing for the later persistent 503 source route (line ~924) or for `openTaskTab`/sign-out flows. It must be removed before those run, or shown to be harmless.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- Instrumentation shows the app did not issue the follow-up fetch. That is an app defect, and app refresh behaviour is out of scope.
- The only fix that works needs a timeout increase or changes to shared fixtures or other browser tests.

**Exclusive resources:** none. The fixture uses ephemeral ports (`listen(0)`) and the harness uses port 0. Local Chromium from Playwright 1.64 is required. The concurrent-load step in T3 is CPU-heavy, so do not run it alongside other browser-suite stress runs.

nodes.body:
**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1085 **Planned against:** `main` at `a83792b2fcfc18e69d6532d8bcef69d780cbc015` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach The `design/DESIGN.md` half of this issue already landed with #1111/#1113 at the planned base: Interaction notes → Presentation carries the four rules (lines ~1476–1492), and the Overview card note (Implementation status → Overview, task list and Board) says a missing time, age, requester or evidence line is omitted. Frame `01-attention-overview` needed no change. What remains is code: 1. Add one shared presentation module, `web/src/presentation.ts`, holding the clock label, the short identifier and the code-to-sentence helper. Sibling screen tickets import from it. 2. Stop printing "Age unknown" and "Responsibility unknown" on Overview, Inbox (queue row, request pane, approval facts, inspector) and the task attention bar. Drop the field when it is missing. The uncertain-ownership headline ("Execution ownership is uncertain", the intervention reason) stays the only place the unknown is stated. 3. Render the inspector's Evidence block only when it has a link, as links that look like links, and without the duplicate "Reported by …" line. One PR. No server, contract or DESIGN.md change. ### Guardrails - Change only presentation. Keep `InboxItem`, the operator API, `attentionNext` and the wait-reason vocabulary as they are. Honest unknowns that are the message keep their wording: the intervention headline, "Ownership stays held", "Exact details unavailable", "Unavailable task/project", "Exact approval unavailable", and the assignment chain's "Requester unknown" root. These are material a read could not supply, which DESIGN.md Presentation keeps explicit. - Out of scope, owned by the sibling tickets: replacing the raw tokens and identifiers on task detail, Changes, Files, Delivery, imported task and GitHub source screens (#1088, #1093, #1094, #1096, #1097, #1103); removing sub-panel Refresh buttons (#1083, #1084, #1091, #1094, #1097); `web/src/task-inspector.tsx` "state unknown" (#1097); Inbox scaffolding (#1084); List/Board card lines (#1086). Do not migrate other screens' `toLocaleTimeString()` calls or `settings-view.ts` `clock` here. Those tickets adopt the helper. - Do not edit `design/DESIGN.md` or the canvas. The rules and the Overview note are already in the base. If the implementation finds the snapshot contradicts the shipped behaviour, record that as a finding and do not redesign. - **Plan-mismatch budget vs ordinary repairs.** If an approved-plan seam or repository assumption is factually wrong (for example a named symbol, caller, file or test seam does not exist or behaves differently than recorded under Implementation context), that is a mechanical plan mismatch: one focused diagnosis, then at most two repair cycles, and stop and report if it is still unresolved. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, formatting and CI repairs stay with the implementer under normal repair rules and do not use that budget.
