content.title: Persist recovery-continuation resolution state so admission and task reads stay bounded

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Make recovery-continuation checks bounded by persisting resolution state, with decisions identical to today.

**Current behavior and verification:** `CoordinationStore.hasUnresolvedRecoveryContinuation` (`src/core/coordination.ts` ~3399) loads every operator-reconciled continuation for an assignment and calls `hasRecoveryContinuation` per row (proof, event, receipt and delivery queries). `recoveryContinuationCandidates` (~3439) walks every held turn of the lead assignment and runs the reconciled-assignment proof join per turn. These run synchronously on the coordinating event loop for admission, the task read (#998) and the lead-awaits check. Growth is bounded only by the number of manual recoveries/held turns. Validity can change after newer continuations are recorded (covered by the "invalidated recovery continuation keeps the successor waiting" test). Evidence: PR #1012 thread 4277032220.

**Desired behavior:** Persist per-assignment (or per-turn) resolution state, updated in the same transaction wherever continuation validity can change, so all three checks become a bounded number of indexed queries.

**Key interfaces:** `hasUnresolvedRecoveryContinuation`, `hasRecoveryContinuation`, `recoveryContinuationCandidates`, `leadAwaitsRecoveryMessage`, `StandaloneService.recoveryContinuationUnresolved`, coordination schema/migrations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Admission, task-read waits and lead-awaits use a constant number of queries regardless of history size (query-count test).
- [ ] Parity tests show identical decisions to current per-row validation, including invalidation after newer continuations.
- [ ] Migration backfills state for existing data; restart/replay keeps it consistent.
- [ ] Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing recovery semantics, operator recovery UI.

<!-- run-github-project:authority-pause:v1 -->
**Decision needed. Automatic work on #1024 is paused.**

- Repository: `chrisbanes/ensemble` · Issue: #1024 · Project item: `PVTI_lAHOAAN4ns4BatgHzhA6zk8`
- Configuration digest: `sha256:d397f661efe931ee747a5bfa66dcdccf32900dacb662235eea215bb9b7526ff8` · Base: `main` @ `b2d7a2b489444d9e477477d07418c81f7d864086`
- Status: Todo · Assignee: chrisbanes · Plan: none · PR: none · Branch: none
- Blocked operation: implementation planning (`to-plan` returned Blocked, `human-required`).

### Why it is blocked

The accepted contract is AC1 (bounded queries independent of history) plus AC2 (identical decisions to per-row validation) plus AC3 (migration-backed persisted state). The code does not allow all three together:

1. Continuation validity depends on the live `reconciledAssignmentProof` (`src/standalone/state.ts`, about 22 tables, plus JavaScript witness and material checks). Those inputs have about 190 write sites. Task-wide holds invalidate every continuation, and validity can come back after being lost.
2. The proof is suppressed while live callbacks for the work exist in memory (`src/standalone/service.ts:715-719`). No persisted state can reflect that.
3. The required parity test (`test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.ts:479`) invalidates a continuation with raw SQL, outside every write path.
4. Even triggers could only mark state stale. Revalidating after a task-wide change still scales with history.

### Decision needed

Choose one and record it on this issue:

- **A (recommended):** Narrow AC1 to "independent of ordinary held-turn history; bounded by the assignment's recovery receipts and continuations". Filter `recoveryContinuationCandidates` in SQL to held turns that have a recovery receipt, the reconciled reason and intent, and no continuation. Keep AC2 and drop AC3, so there is no migration and no persisted state.
- **B:** Approve SQLite triggers on every proof-input table to mark persisted per-continuation state stale, with JavaScript revalidation. AC1 would still need restating.
- **C:** Rewrite the proof as one set-based SQL predicate with persisted input fingerprints. This carries a high risk of decisions no longer matching.

### Resume condition

A recorded decision on this issue choosing A, B or C (or another stated contract), with AC1 and AC3 updated to match. Nothing has been implemented, so no work is preserved.

## Decision (Chris, from the drain session)

This resolves the decision pause at https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1024#issuecomment-6200274191. **Option A is chosen.**

- **Approach:** narrow `recoveryContinuationCandidates` with a SQL pre-filter to held turns of the lead assignment that have an `execution_recovery_receipts` row, the operator-reconciled reason and intent, and no continuation. The live proof requires all of these anyway, so decisions stay identical by construction. No persisted resolution state.
- **AC1 is restated:** "Admission, task-read waits and the lead-awaits check do work proportional to the assignment's operator recovery receipts and continuations, independent of ordinary held-turn history."
- **AC2 is kept:** the existing recovery-continuation tests, including "an invalidated recovery continuation keeps the successor waiting", pass unchanged.
- **New evidence:** a scaling test that adds many ordinary held turns and asserts that the candidate scan does not visit them (the proof-call or prepared-statement count stays flat).
- **AC3 is dropped:** with no persisted state, there is no migration or backfill.

Options B (triggers plus persisted state) and C (a set-based SQL proof) are rejected. They add coupling across stores and risk decisions no longer matching, and they still can't meet constant cost after task-wide invalidations.

<!-- run-github-project:authority-resume:v1 -->
**Resuming #1024.**

- Pause: https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1024#issuecomment-6200274191 (payload sha256 `818c336ca901963f7c54a67305d99aa289c19d01f69673caa5b8fdd219891ed3`)
- Decision evidence: https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1024#issuecomment-6209719429 (Chris chose option A and restated the acceptance)
- Repository `chrisbanes/ensemble` · Project item `PVTI_lAHOAAN4ns4BatgHzhA6zk8` · configuration digest `sha256:d397f661efe931ee747a5bfa66dcdccf32900dacb662235eea215bb9b7526ff8`
- Base: `main` @ `daf806c096cdf21aa40abd22facfd864b0e04cf5`
- Status: Todo · Assignee: chrisbanes · Plan: none · PR: none · Branch: none
- Next: plan under the recorded decision (a new accepted contract), then implement through the drain.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1024#issuecomment-6209719429

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1024
**Planned against:** `main` at `daf806c096cdf21aa40abd22facfd864b0e04cf5`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

The governing contract is Chris's recorded decision (https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1024#issuecomment-6209719429), which supersedes the issue body's original AC1 and AC3. It chooses option A: a SQL pre-filter, no persisted state, AC1 restated, AC2 kept plus a scaling test, and AC3 dropped.

### Approach

Change only how `CoordinationStore.recoveryContinuationCandidates` (`src/core/coordination.ts`) selects rows. It currently loads every held turn of the task and assignment, then calls the live proof once per turn. It will select only held turns that satisfy SQL conditions the live proof already requires: an `execution_recovery_receipts` row, a `reconciled` execution intent, `kind = 'assignment'`, the operator-reconciled reason, and no `coordination_recovery_continuations` row. The proof, the delivery-batch checks and the insert loop stay exactly as they are and still run per surviving row. `hasUnresolvedRecoveryContinuation`, which admission and the task read use, already joins `coordination_recovery_continuations`, so its proof work is already proportional to continuations. It stays unchanged, and a test locks that behaviour in.

### Guardrails

- Decisions must stay identical. The pre-filter may only add conjuncts that the proof's own SQL requires (`src/standalone/state.ts` `reconciledAssignmentProof`). It must not add a predicate that the proof does not require, such as hold, effect, binding or witness checks, and it must not weaken or reorder the per-row proof, the `proof.taskId`/`proof.assignmentId` checks, the batch checks, or `ORDER BY sequence`.
- Keep `reconciledAssignmentProof` and `deliveryForWork` evaluated lazily, inside the loop, once per surviving row. `recordRecoveryContinuation` interleaves inserts and batch updates with that loop, so do not precompute proofs or batches.
- No persisted resolution state, schema change, index, trigger or migration. The receipt migration in `state.ts` near line 2411 rejects extra indexes or triggers on `execution_recovery_receipts`. The existing `workId UNIQUE` index and the `turn_requests(assignmentId, sequence)` index are enough.
- Out of scope: the original AC3 (migration and backfill), options B and C, changes to recovery semantics or to the operator recovery UI, and changes to `hasRecoveryContinuation`, `reconciledAssignmentProof`, `hasUnresolvedRecoveryContinuation` or the service's callback suppression.
- Existing tests in `test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.ts` and elsewhere must pass unchanged (AC2). Do not edit existing assertions to make them pass. If one fails, that is evidence the pre-filter is not implied by the proof; diagnose it as a plan mismatch.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence.
- Two kinds of repair are budgeted differently. A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping for a replan. Examples: a pre-filter predicate the proof does not actually require, `execution_recovery_receipts` unreachable from the coordination connection, or a test seam that cannot observe proof calls. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget. Examples: SQL syntax, typing, lint or format, test setup, and flaky CI reruns.
- Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **The pre-filter is implied by the live proof, so decisions are identical.** Today's loop keeps a held turn only if it has no continuation row and `reconciledAssignmentProof(workId)` returns a proof whose `taskId` and `assignmentId` match. The production callback (`src/standalone/service.ts` around lines 712-719) returns `state.reconciledAssignmentProof(workId)`, or `undefined` while live callbacks exist. The state proof returns `undefined` unless its single-row query matches. That query joins `execution_recovery_receipts receipt` on `receipt.workId = ?`, joins `execution_intents intent` with `intent.state = 'reconciled'`, and joins `turn_requests request` on the same `workId` with `request.kind = 'assignment'`, `request.state = 'held'` and `request.reason = 'Execution reconciled; no automatic successor'`. Each pre-filter conjunct is therefore a necessary condition for a non-`undefined` proof, read from the same rows. The `NOT EXISTS` continuation conjunct is the loop's existing skip, moved into SQL. Any turn the filter drops would have reached `continue`, so the surviving list, its order (`ORDER BY sequence`) and every later per-row check are unchanged. `awaitsRecoveryContinuation`, and with it `CoordinationView.leadAwaitsRecoveryMessage`, returns the same boolean, and `recordRecoveryContinuation` writes the same rows.
- **The filter cannot see a different snapshot from the proof.** The filter and the proof run synchronously on the same `node:sqlite` connection with no `await` between them. Inside `recordRecoveryContinuation` (called from `src/core/coordination.ts` near line 2229), each iteration inserts a continuation for its own `workId`, which is unique, and may complete that work's own batch. Neither write changes another row's pre-filter conjuncts. Receipts, intents and turn-request reason and state are untouched, and the continuation check for another row is keyed by that row's own `workId`. So evaluating the filter once, before the loop, matches today's per-iteration skip.
- **The store boundary allows this.** `CoordinationStore` and `ExecutionState` share one database. `service.ts` constructs `ExecutionState(db)` at line 687, which creates `execution_recovery_receipts` (`state.ts` line 633), and then `new CoordinationStore(db, …, proof)` on the same `db`. `coordination.ts` already joins standalone-owned tables such as `turn_requests`, `execution_intents`, `task_execution_bindings` and `task_work_revisions`, so precedent exists. `recoveryContinuationCandidates` returns `[]` before any query when no proof callback is configured. That is true for every test and core-only `new CoordinationStore(db)` construction, so the receipts table is only read when `ExecutionState` has created it. The `hasTurnRequests === false` path is unchanged: the existing `turn_requests` query would already fail there. No blocker.
- **Callers.** Lead-awaits (`operator-api.ts` near line 3128) calls `CoordinationView.leadAwaitsRecoveryMessage`, then `awaitsRecoveryContinuation`, then the candidates; that path changes. Operator messages call `recordRecoveryContinuation`, then the candidates; that path changes. Admission (`service.ts` near line 4651) and the task read's waits (`operator-api.ts` near line 2238) call `StandaloneService.recoveryContinuationUnresolved`, then `hasUnresolvedRecoveryContinuation`. That path is already continuation-driven and is unchanged; the existing test at `recovery-continuation.test.ts:479` proves it, and T1's scaling test re-asserts it.
- **Reason literal.** Repeat the literal `'Execution reconciled; no automatic successor'` in the SQL, with a one-line comment naming `reconciledAssignmentProof`, rather than adding a cross-layer constant. If the two copies diverge, the existing recovery tests fail because valid candidates disappear.
- **Bound.** The bound is measured the way the decision's evidence specifies: the number of proof calls stays flat as ordinary held history grows. Inside that one SQL statement, SQLite may still walk the assignment's `turn_requests` index entries. That is accepted under option A, because it runs no per-turn JavaScript or extra statements.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/coordination.ts` — `recoveryContinuationCandidates` (around lines 3439-3482) is called by `awaitsRecoveryContinuation` (around 3435) and `recordRecoveryContinuation` (around 3484). `hasUnresolvedRecoveryContinuation` (around 3399) and `hasRecoveryContinuation` (around 3334) stay unchanged.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `reconciledAssignmentProof` (around 2950) is the source of the required conjuncts. It is read-only for this ticket.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` (lines 712-719) wires the proof callback. `recoveryContinuationUnresolved` (around 4544) is unchanged.
- **Follow:** `test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.ts`, the test "an invalidated recovery continuation keeps the successor waiting without scanning every request" (line 479), for the `heldFixture`/`internals` setup, the 200-row held-history insert, and method wrapping. The service's proof callback looks up `state.reconciledAssignmentProof` at call time, so wrapping that method on the `internals(f.service).state` instance observes every candidate proof call.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** There is one task, `T1`, with no dependencies, so the graph is trivially acyclic. There is no concurrency.

#### 1. Pre-filter recovery continuation candidates in SQL, with a scaling test

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** None.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/coordination.ts` `CoordinationStore.recoveryContinuationCandidates` (query only), and `test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.ts` (one new test).
**Test:** Add `test("lead recovery candidates prove only receipt-backed reconciled turns, not ordinary held history", …)` to `test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.ts`.
  1. Set up with `heldFixture()` and `await f.service.resolveHeldExecution(f.receipt)`. Get `{ db, coordination, state } = internals(f.service)` and `assignmentId = String(f.old.assignmentId)`.
  2. Insert 200 held copies of the old request, using the pattern from line 479 (`'history-' || value`, `state = 'held'`, `reason` NULL). Insert 20 more copies with `reason = 'Execution reconciled; no automatic successor'` and no receipt.
  3. Wrap `state.reconciledAssignmentProof` on the instance to record each `workId`.
  4. Assert `coordination.awaitsRecoveryContinuation(f.taskId, assignmentId) === true` and that the recorded IDs equal `[f.old.workId]`.
  5. Clear the record, then `f.pause(true)` and `await f.service.coordinationView().postOperatorMessage(f.message)`. Assert that `audit(f.service, f.old.workId)` exists, that no `coordination_recovery_continuations` row has a `workId` starting with `history-`, and that every recorded proof call is `f.old.workId`.
  6. Assert `f.service.recoveryContinuationUnresolved(assignmentId, "other-work") === false`, and that it causes no proof calls for `history-*` IDs.

  Sensitivity: on the baseline code, step 4 records 221 IDs and fails, so the test proves the new bound.
**Implementation:** Replace the `SELECT workId FROM turn_requests WHERE taskId = ? AND assignmentId = ? AND state = 'held' ORDER BY sequence` query with a query on `turn_requests request` that keeps those predicates and adds the following:
  - `request.kind = 'assignment'`
  - `request.reason = 'Execution reconciled; no automatic successor'`
  - `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM execution_recovery_receipts receipt WHERE receipt.workId = request.workId)`
  - `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM execution_intents intent WHERE intent.workId = request.workId AND intent.state = 'reconciled')`
  - `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM coordination_recovery_continuations c WHERE c.workId = request.workId)`

  Keep `ORDER BY request.sequence`. Remove the now-redundant per-row continuation `this.one(...)` skip. Leave the early `if (!this.reconciledAssignmentProof) return [];` before the query. Leave the rest of the loop byte-for-byte: the proof call, the proof task and assignment checks, `deliveryForWork`, the batch checks and the push. Update the JSDoc on `awaitsRecoveryContinuation`/`recoveryContinuationCandidates` in one line to say that only receipt-backed, operator-reconciled held turns are proved.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout root, with Node 24.21.0 from `.node-version` and after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.js`. Expect all existing tests plus the new one to pass, with 0 failures; the baseline is 67 passing. Also run `npm run test:built -- --profile=service` and expect 0 failures.
**Complete when:** The candidate query carries the pre-filter, the new scaling test passes and fails on the baseline query, and every existing recovery-continuation test passes unchanged.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Restated AC1: admission, task-read waits and lead-awaits do work proportional to recovery receipts and continuations, independent of ordinary held-turn history | 1 | New scaling test, steps 4-6 (lead-awaits and record path), plus the existing test at line 479 (admission and task-read path) |
| AC2: existing recovery-continuation tests pass unchanged, including "an invalidated recovery continuation keeps the successor waiting" | 1 | `node --test dist/test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.js` with no edits to existing tests, and full `npm run check` |
| Scaling evidence: many ordinary held turns are not visited by the candidate scan (proof-call count stays flat) | 1 | New scaling test, step 4 assertion `[f.old.workId]`, which fails on the baseline |
| Original AC3 (migration and backfill) | — | Dropped by the decision; verify the diff contains no schema or migration changes |

### Final validation

- On the integrated delivery candidate, from the implementation checkout root with Node 24.21.0, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check`. Expect typecheck, lint, format, build and all tests to pass, including both browser engines. PR CI on the candidate must also pass. The base `daf806c0` CI was green (`check`, `quality` and all node24/node26 shards).

### Review focus

- Confirm that each added SQL conjunct appears verbatim among the `reconciledAssignmentProof` join and `WHERE` conditions, and that nothing else was added or removed from the loop.

Decision (Chris): the candidate query in PR #1061 is driven by `execution_recovery_receipts`. Its cost is bounded by recovery receipts across the installation, not by the assignment's held-turn history. That bound is accepted: receipts come only from rare, manual operator recoveries, and bounding per assignment would need a schema change, which was ruled out with AC3.

content.title: Record which readiness rule each task's Ready flag was evaluated under

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Record which readiness rule each task's Ready flag was evaluated under, so explanations and counts know exactly when they reflect the current rule.

**Current behavior and verification:** After #1002/#1018, `readinessByTask` (`src/core/github-source.ts`) reports `not-evaluated` (and selection counts report `matching: null`) when the current rule disagrees with the stored `domain_tasks.ready`. A rule change between two rules that both fail leaves the flags equal, so the new rule's unmet conditions show before the selection is re-read. `updateReadiness` is the only writer of `ready` for imported tasks and reads the same inputs, so this matches what re-evaluation will produce; it's a precision gap. Evidence: PR #1018 thread 4277887078.

**Desired behavior:** Store the rule identity (e.g. source configuration version) used when `ready` was last evaluated; report `not-evaluated`/`matching: null` whenever it differs from the current rule.

**Key interfaces:** `updateReadiness`, `readinessByTask`, `selectionCounts`, readiness text, schema/migration for the stored rule identity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Any rule change (including same-result changes) shows `not-evaluated` until reconciled; counts show unknown.
- [ ] The Ready-agreement test still holds; collection reads keep a constant query count.
- [ ] Migration initialises the stored identity for existing tasks without changing `ready`.
- [ ] Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing when `ready` itself is re-evaluated.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1026
**Planned against:** `main` at `b2d7a2b489444d9e477477d07418c81f7d864086`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Source contract: the issue's Acceptance list and the accepted [Agent Brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1026#issuecomment-6188930037).

### Approach

Stamp each imported task with the exact readiness rule text its Ready flag was last evaluated under, in a new nullable `domain_tasks.readinessRule` column written by `GitHubSourceStore.updateReadiness`. `readinessByTask` and `selectionCounts` report `not-evaluated` / `matching: null` when the stamp differs from the project's current `project_github_sources.readiness` text, in addition to the existing Ready-disagreement check. `DomainStore.migrate()` adds the column with a column-presence guard and backfills existing imported tasks to their project's current rule text without touching `ready`.

### Guardrails

- When `ready` is re-evaluated does not change (brief: out of scope). Reconciliation stays the next selection read, a project transfer, or a configuration change that already calls `updateReadiness`.
- Keep the existing check (`result.satisfied !== ready` → `not-evaluated`) alongside the new stamp check. The two checks together keep the Ready-agreement invariant (an outcome of `matched` iff `ready = 1`), including for backfilled rows.
- Collection reads keep their current prepared-statement counts: `selectionCounts` 3 and `readinessByTask` 3 (`test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts` "selection counts use a fixed number of queries…"). Add columns to existing queries; never query per task.
- A stamp-only change must not bump `domain_tasks.version`. Delivery approval bindings compare task versions (`src/core/delivery.ts` `taskVersion` checks), so a reconcile that leaves Ready unchanged must not make them stale. A Ready change keeps its existing `version = version + 1`.
- Treat the stamp as an opaque persisted value. Only strict equality with the current rule string is "current"; `NULL` or any other value fails closed to `not-evaluated`. The current rule text still goes through `parseRule`.
- Do not bump `domain_schema` (it stays at 3): an older binary rejects unknown schema versions. Local tasks keep `readinessRule` NULL and are never evaluated.
- Out of scope: `web/`, `test/operator/`, docs, `src/operator/readiness-text.ts` wording (the existing stale-match text already describes this state, and `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` already states the target behaviour), the `github.activate` result (#1025), and in-flight UI tickets #1040/#1041/#1042/#1044.
- A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping for a replan. Examples: another `domain_tasks.ready` writer for imported tasks, a project rule that changes without passing through `project_github_sources.readiness`, or the query-count seam being unable to hold. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Rule identity = the exact `project_github_sources.readiness` JSON text, not the source configuration `version`.** Ready depends only on memberships, the observed state and the rule. Memberships and observed state change only through reads, which call `updateReadiness`; the rule is the one input that changes without re-evaluation. `version` also bumps for credential, selection and closed-issue changes, so it would blank explanations and counts after unrelated saves. Version integers also collide across projects on a project transfer. The text changes on every rule change, because `github.configure` rewrites it from the parsed command. A rule changed and then reverted before a read compares as current, which is correct: Ready was evaluated under that same rule against the same stored facts.
- **Store on `domain_tasks`, owned by `DomainStore.migrate()`** (`src/core/domain.ts`), next to `ready`. `github_external_issues` is filled with positional `INSERT … VALUES` in five `test/operator`/`test/fixtures`/`test/workspaces` fixtures, and a new column there would break them while UI tickets are in flight. `domain_tasks` inserts all name their columns.
- **Migration id: `domain_tasks.readinessRule`.** `DomainStore` has no string-id migrations table. Its convention is idempotent `PRAGMA table_info` column-presence guards inside the `migrate()` transaction (for example `project_github_sources.closedIssues`), so this migration is that guarded step. It needs no `domain_schema` bump and no new migrations table.
- **Backfill to the current rule text.** Ready flags are unchanged. The kept disagreement check still marks legacy disagreeing rows `not-evaluated`. Legacy same-result staleness from before the upgrade cannot be known, so legacy rows keep today's precision.
- **Verified writers of `domain_tasks.ready`:**
  - `updateReadiness` (`src/core/github-source.ts`) is the only evaluator for imported tasks.
  - Import inserts `ready = 0` (`github-source.ts` `INSERT INTO domain_tasks … 0`), and the same loop then calls `updateReadiness`, which stamps the row.
  - `task.create` (`domain.ts`) creates local tasks only.
  - `task.configure` rejects `ready` for imported tasks (`preflightTaskConfigure`, "readiness are provider-owned").
  - Project transfer (`domain.ts` around `UPDATE domain_tasks SET projectId`) and `github.configure` selection removal both call `updateReadiness` after the change, so they stamp the new rule.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source.ts`
  - `updateReadiness(taskId, deliveryClosure)` reads the project's `closedIssues`, evaluates `this.readinessRule(projectId)` and writes `ready` only when it differs.
  - `readinessRule(projectId)` returns the parsed rule.
  - `selectionCounts(projectId)` (3 prepares) computes `stale` per open member as `matching(r) !== ready`.
  - `readinessByTask(taskIds)` (3 prepares) returns `notEvaluated` when the outcome disagrees with `t.ready`.
  - Callers: `taskReadiness`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (task list, composer, inbox, task detail), `src/standalone/operator.ts` (HTML fallback), `src/cli/source.ts` via counts.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStore.migrate()` creates `domain_tasks` and `project_github_sources`, applies guarded `ALTER TABLE` steps, and ends with the `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO project_github_sources` backfill.
- **New:** `domain_tasks.readinessRule TEXT` (nullable) — the rule text the task's Ready was last evaluated under; NULL for local tasks.
- **Follow:** `test/sources/github-source-config.test.ts`. Its `closedIssues` upgrade test does `ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN` and then `migrate()` again; reuse that upgrade-test pattern. In `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`, reuse the `readinessFixture` and the "after a rule change and before the next read…" test shape.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2. The graph is acyclic. Both tasks edit `src/core/domain.ts` and `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`, so they run sequentially in one branch and PR. No task is safe to run concurrently.

#### 1. Stamp the evaluated rule and report stale explanations and counts

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/core/domain.ts` `DomainStore.migrate()`: add `readinessRule TEXT` to the `domain_tasks` `CREATE TABLE`, plus a guarded `ALTER TABLE domain_tasks ADD COLUMN readinessRule TEXT` for existing databases (backfill is T2).
- `src/core/github-source.ts`: `updateReadiness`, `selectionCounts`, `readinessByTask`.
- `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`.

**Test:** Add `"a same-result rule change reports not-evaluated until the next read"` to `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`.
1. Use `readinessFixture({ mode: "all", conditions: [{ kind: "label", name: "ready" }] })`.
2. Read `repo` with `I_1` (no labels: unmet, Draft) and `I_2` (labels `["ready","approved"]`: matched, Ready).
3. Configure with `selections: [{ id: "repo", keep: true }]` and the rule label `approved`. This is the same call shape as the existing rule-change test.
4. Assert `ready` is unchanged (`I_1` 0, `I_2` 1).
5. Assert `taskReadiness` is `{ outcome: "not-evaluated", unmet: [] }` for both tasks, and `selectionCounts(projectId).get("repo")?.matching === null`.
6. Activate `repo` and read the same issues again.
7. Assert `I_1` is `{ outcome: "unmet", unmet: [{ kind: "label", name: "approved" }] }` and `I_2` is `matched`.
8. Assert `matching === 1` and the Ready-agreement loop over `f.domain.tasks(projectId)` holds.

Sensitivity check: at baseline, step 5 fails, because `I_1` reports `unmet` (label `approved`) and counts report 1.

The existing tests "task readiness … agrees with the stored Ready flag", "selection counts use a fixed number of queries…" (still 3 and 3 prepares) and "after a rule change and before the next read…" pass unchanged.

**Implementation:**
1. In `updateReadiness`, read `readiness` with the existing `closedIssues` query (`SELECT closedIssues, readiness …`), so it adds no query. Evaluate with `parseRule` of that text instead of a second `readinessRule()` call.
2. In the same function, read `readinessRule` with the existing `SELECT ready, state …` query.
3. Keep the existing `ready` UPDATE (with its version bump) and include `readinessRule = ?` in it. When only the stamp differs, run `UPDATE domain_tasks SET readinessRule = ? WHERE id = ?` with no version bump. Stamp on every branch, including the closed or held branches.
4. In `selectionCounts`, get the raw current rule text from the existing rule query (return or select the raw `readiness` alongside the parsed rule, still one prepare). Add `t.readinessRule` to the member query. Mark `stale` when `r.readinessRule !== currentRuleText || matching(r) !== ready`.
5. In `readinessByTask`, keep the raw `readiness` in the `rules` map and add `t.readinessRule` to the externals query. Return `notEvaluated` when the stamp differs from the task's project rule text, before or alongside the existing disagreement check.

**Validate:** From the repository root, with Node from `.node-version` and `npm ci` done, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.js dist/test/sources/github-readiness-explanation.test.js`; expect all tests pass, including the new one, with 0 failures.
**Complete when:** the new test passes, the existing readiness, query-count and service-level explanation tests pass unchanged, and `npm run typecheck` passes.

#### 2. Initialise the identity for existing tasks on upgrade

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's column and readers are in place and its Validate step passes.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/domain.ts` `DomainStore.migrate()` (the `domain_tasks.readinessRule` guarded step); `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`.
**Test:** Add `"upgrading initialises each imported task's readiness rule identity without changing Ready"` to `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`.
1. Use `readinessFixture` with rule label `ready`, and read `I_1` (labels `["ready"]`) and `I_2` (no labels).
2. Record each task's `ready`, `version`, `taskReadiness` and `selectionCounts(...).get("repo")`.
3. Run `f.db.exec("ALTER TABLE domain_tasks DROP COLUMN readinessRule")`, then `f.domain.migrate()`.
4. Assert `ready` and `version` are unchanged for both tasks.
5. Assert `SELECT readinessRule FROM domain_tasks WHERE id = ?` equals `SELECT readiness FROM project_github_sources WHERE projectId = ?` for both tasks.
6. Assert `taskReadiness` and counts equal the recorded values (`matched` / `unmet` with label `ready`, `matching: 1`), and the Ready-agreement loop holds.
7. Call `f.domain.migrate()` again and assert the values are still unchanged (idempotent).
8. A local task created with `task.create` in the same fixture keeps `readinessRule` NULL.

Sensitivity check: without the backfill, step 6 reports `not-evaluated` and `matching: null`.

**Implementation:** Place the guarded step after the `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO project_github_sources` backfill in `migrate()`. When `PRAGMA table_info(domain_tasks)` lacks `readinessRule`, run `ALTER TABLE domain_tasks ADD COLUMN readinessRule TEXT` and then:

```sql
UPDATE domain_tasks
SET readinessRule = (SELECT c.readiness FROM project_github_sources c
  WHERE c.projectId = domain_tasks.projectId)
WHERE id IN (SELECT taskId FROM github_imported_tasks)
```

Never write `ready` or `version`. The `CREATE TABLE` from T1 already includes the column, so fresh databases skip this step.

**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.js dist/test/sources/github-source-config.test.js`; expect 0 failures, including the new upgrade test.
**Complete when:** the upgrade test passes and is idempotent on a second `migrate()`.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Any rule change, including a same-result change, shows `not-evaluated` until reconciled; counts show unknown | 1 | New same-result rule-change test, plus the existing "after a rule change…" test |
| The Ready-agreement test still holds | 1, 2 | Existing "agrees with the stored Ready flag" test, plus the agreement loops in both new tests |
| Collection reads keep a constant query count | 1 | Existing fixed-query test (3 and 3 prepares), plus the service-level `readinessByTask` call-count assertion in `github-readiness-explanation.test.ts` |
| Migration initialises the stored identity for existing tasks without changing `ready` | 2 | New upgrade test |
| Pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check` | Final | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, using Node from `.node-version` and the pinned npm, run `npm ci && npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate; expect typecheck, lint, format check, build and the full test suite (both browsers) to pass.
- PR CI (`.github/workflows` CI on the PR head) must pass. Baseline CI run 38788855704 on `b2d7a2b4` passed all jobs (`node26-full-compatibility` skipped by design).

### Review focus

- Every `updateReadiness` branch stamps the rule it evaluated under, including the closed-after-import hold, `deliveryClosure` and provider-completion reversal paths. A stamp-only write never bumps `version`.
- The `selectionCounts` stale check still only considers members whose task belongs to this project (`taskProjectId === projectId`).

content.title: Report whether a selection was already active when it's activated

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Let the activation result say whether the selection was already active, so the Sync tab copy is exact under concurrency.

**Current behavior and verification:** After #1004, `activationLine` (`web/src/settings-view.ts`) chooses "Activated S-1…" or "S-1 was already active…" from `activeSelectionIds` captured from the configuration read loaded on the page. The `github.activate` receipt (`src/standalone/operator-api.ts`) carries no prior state because activation is an idempotent upsert, so a concurrent activation from another browser or the CLI reads "Activated". It never claims an import, sync, wrong selection or wrong version. Evidence: PR #1014 thread 4277071034.

**Desired behavior:** The activation command result reports whether the selection was already active at that source version; web (and CLI/HTML where activation is shown) use it instead of the page snapshot.

**Key interfaces:** `github.activate` command/result schema and receipt replay, `activationLine`, `SavedRecord.activeSelectionIds`, CLI activation output.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Result includes prior active state; receipts recorded before the change still replay.
- [ ] Web copy uses it; concurrent activation reads "already active".
- [ ] Tests cover first, repeat and concurrent activation (web and CLI).
- [ ] Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** "Activate and refresh", changes to observation refresh.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1025
**Planned against:** `main` at `b2d7a2b489444d9e477477d07418c81f7d864086`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Source contract: the issue's Acceptance list and the accepted [Agent Brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1025#issuecomment-6188928411).

### Approach

Make the domain command report the prior state and carry it through the public receipt to every reader. `DomainStore.apply` for `github.activate` checks `project_github_active` for a row at the current source version before its upsert and returns `alreadyActive`. The result schema requires the field for newly applied results and treats it as optional for recorded ones, as `github.configure` does for `closedIssues`. The public `github.preview` configuration receipt exposes it as an optional boolean. `activationLine` reads it from the receipt in place of the page snapshot, and `project preview-source` states it in plain words.

### Guardrails

- Activation stays an idempotent upsert: no new refusal, no import, sync or refresh, and no change to observation refresh. "Activate and refresh" and observation refresh are out of scope.
- A recorded receipt keeps the prior state it recorded. Replaying a key returns the original `alreadyActive`, never a recomputed value.
- Receipts recorded before this change must still replay. `parseDomainCommandOutcome` (replay and read) accepts a result without `alreadyActive`; `parseFreshDomainCommandOutcome` (new apply) requires it. A malformed value (not a boolean) is rejected on both. Do not backfill stored receipts and do not bump `domain_schema`.
- An absent `alreadyActive` means "unknown", never "false": the web copy and the CLI make no first-activation claim for it.
- No new HTTP route or command type. The public receipt change is one optional boolean on the existing `github.preview` configuration result; the existing `github.preview` command input is unchanged.
- Out of scope: the in-flight readiness work (#1026), the neutral-badge work (#1044), `design/DESIGN.md` (the copy for known states is unchanged and DESIGN.md already says the line "names the selection (or says it was already active)"), and the legacy HTML operator (`src/standalone/operator.ts`), which shows only active or inactive from the store and redirects without any activation message.
- A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping for a replan. Examples: a second writer of `project_github_active`, a `github.activate` result consumer that cannot accept an optional field, or the receipt read path not going through `parseDomainCommandOutcome`. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **"Already active" means a `project_github_active` row exists for `(projectId, selectionId)` with `configVersion` equal to the current configuration version.** `githubActiveSelectionIds` and `GitHubSourceStore` already define "active" this way (`configVersion = config.version`). A save that keeps a selection leaves its row at the old version (`docs/design/ui06-configuration.md`: kept selections read inactive until previewed again), so the first activation after such a save must report `alreadyActive: false`. The command already requires `expectedVersion === config.version`, so the current version is the source version of the request.
- **The check is a read before the existing upsert inside `apply`.** `DomainStore.executeParsed` runs `replayed`, `apply` and the receipt insert in one synchronous SQLite transaction (`transaction(this.db, …)`) and `node:sqlite` is synchronous, so two commands with different keys serialize: exactly one reads no row and reports `false`, the others report `true`. The same-key duplicate is deduplicated by `DomainCommands.inFlight` or replayed from `command_receipts`. No new locking is needed. The asynchronous provider read in `OperatorApi.previewGitHubSelection` happens before the command, so two previews that both pass the pre-read still serialize in the domain.
- **Field name `alreadyActive`, boolean.** The result keeps `active: z.literal(true)`; it is a separate fact. The optional public field uses a conditional spread in `commandReceipt` because both tsconfigs set `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.
- **Legacy handling follows `legacyGithubConfigurationCommandResultSchema` and `parseUnchanged`.** `parseUnchanged` rejects schemas that alter validated material, so a required field cannot be defaulted. A `legacyGithubActivationCommandResultSchema` with `alreadyActive` optional is used when `fresh` is false; the type map entry for `github.activate` becomes the legacy output type.
- **The web stops keeping a snapshot of active selections in the saved record.** `SavedRecord.activeSelectionIds` exists only to answer this question and is removed. `useLoadedDraft` in `sync-placement.tsx` keeps `activeSelectionIds` in its values: it is part of the signature that re-initialises the form after a preview is recorded and the next read shows the new active set, so only its comment changes.
- **Copy.** `alreadyActive === false` reads `Activated S-1.`; `true` reads `S-1 was already active.`; absent reads `S-1 is active.` (a receipt recorded before this change, replayed by key). The trailing "Tasks aren't imported…" sentence and the "Couldn't confirm that S-1 is active" branch are unchanged.
- **Entry points checked.** Sync tab (web) and `project preview-source` (CLI) show the activation outcome. `operation get` and `GET /api/operator/operations` print the receipt generically (`receiptLines` prints every configuration field), so they gain `alreadyActive` with no edit. The legacy HTML form posts and redirects with no activation message. No notification or deep link shows it.
- **Baseline:** trusted CI run on `b2d7a2b4` passed `check`, `quality`, every `node24` and `node26-service` shard (`node26-full-compatibility` skipped by design). On Node 24.21.0, `npm run build` then `node --test` on `command-results`, `operator-settings-presentation`, `operator-settings-state`, `operator-cli-source-activation` and `operator-configuration` (61 pass) and on the `first source activation` and `repeat activation` browser tests (2 pass) all passed at the base commit, proving the seams and commands below.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStore.apply` `case "github.activate"` (about line 2236) verifies the operator actor, `expectedVersion` and the selection id, then `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` into `project_github_active` and returns `{projectId, selectionId, configVersion, active: true}`. `executeParsed` (about line 960) validates it with `parseFreshDomainCommandOutcome`, stores `JSON.stringify(result.result)` in `command_receipts`, and `replayed` / `recordedResult` re-validate stored JSON with `parseDomainCommandOutcome`.
- **Existing:** `src/core/command-results.ts` — `githubActivationCommandResultSchema` (strict), `parseCommandOutcome(type, value, fresh)` with the `github.activate` case, `DomainCommandResultMap`.
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `configurationReceiptSchema`, its `commandType: "github.preview"` variant (about line 2130, strict). `src/standalone/operator-receipts.ts` — `commandReceipt` `case "github.activate"` projects the domain result into that variant.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `previewGitHubSelection` (about line 5207) replays `recordedCommand`, else reads the selection, runs `executeDomain` and returns `commandReceipt(parseDomainCommandOutcome("github.activate", raw), …)`. `readOperation` (about line 4725) reads by key through `recordedResult`.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/source.ts` — `project preview-source` (about lines 570-690) sends the command through `sendCommand`, then prints `Recorded preview of …`, `keyValues(receiptLines(receipt))` and the live state. `src/cli/operation.ts` `receiptLines` prints all fields of a configuration receipt.
- **Existing:** `web/src/settings-view.ts` — `activationLine` (about line 139) picks the sentence from `saved.activeSelectionIds`; `web/src/settings-state.ts` — `SavedRecord`, `ConfigurationDraft.submit` `onSaved` (about lines 352-362), `ConfigurationDrafts.get`; `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` — `SyncTab` `useLoadedDraft` values and `activationLine({saved, …})`.
- **Follow:** `src/core/command-results.ts` `legacyGithubConfigurationCommandResultSchema` and its use in `parseCommandOutcome` for the optional-on-replay pattern; `test/coordination/command-results.test.ts` "legacy receipt validation preserves only the known migrated omissions"; `test/operator/operator-configuration.test.ts` "profile operation lookup returns an unchanged legacy receipt after SQLite migration" (strip a field from the stored result with `f.seedPersistedState`, `f.reopen()`, replay and `readOperation`).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → {T2, T3}; the graph is acyclic. T1 establishes the persisted-receipt and result boundary, so T2 and T3 start only after T1's Validate step passes. T2 and T3 own disjoint source and test files and can run concurrently. T1 and T2 both edit `test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.ts` (T1 fixes one existing expectation, T2 adds a test), which is why T2 depends on T1. In-flight overlap: T1 edits `src/core/domain.ts` (the `github.activate` hunk about line 2236) beside #1026 (`migrate()` and the `domain_tasks` DDL, a different hunk about 1,500 lines away); T3 edits `web/src/settings-view.ts` (`activationLine`, about lines 139-170) and `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` (the `SyncTab` header, about lines 40-60) beside #1044 (`observationSymbol` after `observationLabel` about line 185, `HoldTone`/`holdPills`, and the badge JSX about line 250 of `sync-placement.tsx`). Hunks do not overlap in either case; a second lander only rebases.

#### 1. Report the prior active state in the activation result and public receipt

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/core/command-results.ts`: `githubActivationCommandResultSchema` gains `alreadyActive: z.boolean()`; new `legacyGithubActivationCommandResultSchema` (`.extend({ alreadyActive: z.boolean().optional() }).strict()`); `parseCommandOutcome` `case "github.activate"` selects fresh or legacy like `github.configure`; the `DomainCommandResultMap["github.activate"]` entry uses the legacy output type.
- `src/core/domain.ts`: `apply` `case "github.activate"`.
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: the `github.preview` configuration receipt variant gains `alreadyActive: z.boolean().optional()`.
- `src/standalone/operator-receipts.ts`: `commandReceipt` `case "github.activate"`.
- Tests: `test/coordination/command-results.test.ts`, `test/sources/github-source-config.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-configuration.test.ts`, `test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.ts` (one expectation).

**Test:**
1. `test/coordination/command-results.test.ts`: add `alreadyActive: false` to the `cases["github.activate"]` entry. In the legacy-validation test, assert that `{projectId, selectionId, configVersion: 1, active: true}` (no `alreadyActive`) parses unchanged with `parseDomainCommandOutcome` and throws with `parseFreshDomainCommandOutcome`; that `alreadyActive: "yes"` throws with both; and that `parseFreshDomainCommandOutcome` with `alreadyActive: true` returns it. The existing "rejects schemas that normalize result identities" activation case must still throw `/changed validated material/`.
2. `test/sources/github-source-config.test.ts`, new test "github.activate reports whether the selection was already active at the source version": use the setup of "a version-matched successful source preview activates only that selection", with selections `repo` and `other`. Execute `github.activate` for `repo` at version 2 with key A: `alreadyActive` is `false`. Execute again with a new key B: `true`. Re-execute key A: the same result as the first (`false`; a replay returns the recorded value). Activate `other` with a new key: `false` (per selection). Save the configuration keeping both selections (version 3), then activate `repo` at version 3: `false` (its row is at version 2); activate again: `true`.
3. `test/operator/operator-configuration.test.ts`, new test "concurrent source previews report exactly one first activation": build the fixture and project as in "preview original activation receipt replays without provider access…", but with a reader whose `readSelection` increments a counter and waits until it reaches 2 (both previews are past the pre-read), then resolves. Run `Promise.all([api.execute(a), api.execute(b)])` with distinct keys, same selection and version. Assert both receipts are `kind: "configuration"`, `commandType: "github.preview"`, that the `alreadyActive` values sorted equal `[false, true]`, that exactly one `project_github_active` row exists (`f.service.domain().githubActiveSelectionIds(projectId)`), that each key's `readOperation` (`scope: projectId`-based `project:<id>`, `type: "github.preview"`) returns its own original receipt, and that a third preview with a new key reports `true`.
4. Same file, new test "preview lookup replays an unchanged receipt recorded before alreadyActive existed": follow the profile legacy test. Execute one preview, read the stored `command_receipts` row for scope `projectId` and that key, delete `alreadyActive` from the JSON through `f.seedPersistedState`, `await f.reopen()`, build a reopened `OperatorApi` with the same reader factory. Assert `execute(command)` and `readOperation` return a receipt equal to the original with the field removed, that `"alreadyActive" in receipt.result` is false, and that the reader count did not change.
5. `test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.ts`: the first-activation `deepEqual` (about line 236) gains `alreadyActive: false`.

Sensitivity check: at baseline tests 2 and 3 fail (no `alreadyActive`), and the stale-version step in test 2 fails if the check ignores `configVersion`.

**Implementation:**
1. In `apply`, after the existing unknown-selection check and before the upsert, read `SELECT 1 AS present FROM project_github_active WHERE projectId = ? AND selectionId = ? AND configVersion = ?` with `command.projectId`, `command.selectionId`, `config.version` (use `this.one`). Return `alreadyActive: Boolean(row)` in the result; the upsert is unchanged.
2. Schemas as listed above. The fresh schema is used for new results; the legacy schema parses replay and read.
3. Public contract and projection as listed above: in `commandReceipt`, spread `alreadyActive` only when `outcome.result.alreadyActive !== undefined`.
4. Update `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` line 19 in T3, not here; no other doc changes in this slice.

**Validate:** From the repository root with `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH` (Node 24.21.0) and `npm ci` done, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/coordination/command-results.test.js dist/test/sources/github-source-config.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-configuration.test.js dist/test/operations/operator-operations.test.js dist/test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.js`; expect type checking to pass and every test to pass, including the four new or extended ones, with 0 failures.
**Complete when:** a newly applied activation reports `alreadyActive` correctly for first, repeat, new-version and concurrent cases, a pre-change stored receipt replays and reads back unchanged, and the focused command passes.

#### 2. Show the prior state in `project preview-source`

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's Validate step passes.
**Files and symbols:** `src/cli/source.ts` (`project preview-source` result handling, about lines 648-680); `src/cli/main.ts` (help text near line 112, only if it describes activation output); `docs/development.md` (the `preview-source` paragraph, about lines 372-378); `test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.ts`.

**Test:** In `test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.ts`, add "preview-source reports whether the selection was already active" using `world(t)` and the `preview` argument helper:
1. First: `w.ok("rw", preview("S-1"))`; `data.receipt.result.alreadyActive === false`. The human run (`w.h.run([...preview("S-1"), "--connection", "rw"])`, a replay) still prints the original and matches `/Activated S-1 at source version/`.
2. Repeat: `preview("S-1")` plus `--request-id <new UUID>` reports `alreadyActive === true` and, in human output, `/S-1 was already active at source version/`.
3. Another actor: activate `S-2` through `w.s.sessionPost("/api/operator/commands", { type: "github.preview", key, projectId, selectionId: "S-2", expectedVersion })` (response `{status, body}`; `body.result.alreadyActive` is `false`), then `preview("S-2")` through the CLI reports `true`.
4. Concurrent: `Promise.all` of a CLI `preview("S-3")` and a `sessionPost` preview of `S-3` at the same version with distinct keys; exactly one of the CLI `data.receipt.result.alreadyActive` and the POST `body.result.alreadyActive` is `false` (order is not asserted).
5. A receipt without the field: strip `alreadyActive` from the stored `command_receipts` result for scope `atlas` and the first request's key with `w.s.f.seedPersistedState` (as T1 test 4 does), rerun the same `preview("S-1")` in human mode, and assert the output matches neither `/Activated S-1 at/` nor `/already active at/` while `data.receipt.result` has no `alreadyActive`.

Sensitivity check: at T1 alone (before this slice), 1, 2 and 3 fail on the human text.

**Implementation:** Extend the existing `result` cast to `{ configVersion: number; alreadyActive?: boolean }`. After the `Recorded preview of …` line and the key-values, add `Activated ${selectionId} at source version ${result.configVersion}.` when `alreadyActive === false` or `${selectionId} was already active at source version ${result.configVersion}.` when `true`; add nothing when absent. JSON output already carries the receipt, so no JSON change. Keep the existing "Now:" and replay lines. Update the `docs/development.md` paragraph to say the receipt and output report whether the selection was already active at the previewed version, and `src/cli/main.ts` help only if it duplicates that sentence.
**Validate:** From the repository root after T1, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.js dist/test/sources/operator-cli-source.test.js`; expect all pass with 0 failures.
**Complete when:** the CLI test file passes with the new test, and `docs/development.md` describes the output.

#### 3. Drive the Sync tab copy from the receipt

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's Validate step passes.
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/settings-view.ts` (`activationLine`); `web/src/settings-state.ts` (`SavedRecord`, the `onSaved` callback type and call in `ConfigurationDraft.submit`, `ConfigurationDrafts.get`); `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` (the `useLoadedDraft` comment only); `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` (line 19, the Sync tab sentence); tests `test/operator/operator-settings-presentation.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-settings-state.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.ts`.

**Test:**
1. `operator-settings-presentation.test.ts`, "the activation line claims only a confirmed preview…": make the `preview` receipt builder take `alreadyActive?: boolean` and drop `activeSelectionIds` from the `saved` records. Assert `false` reads `Activated S-1. <next>`, `true` reads `S-1 was already active. <next>`, absent reads `S-1 is active. <next>`. Assert the page snapshot no longer matters: a `true` receipt with `selections: [{ id: "S-1", active: false }]` and `recorded: true` still reads "already active". Keep the other-version, no-saved-record, other-command and re-read ("Couldn't confirm", refresh flag) assertions.
2. `operator-settings-state.test.ts`, replace "a saved record keeps the active selections of a source preview and no other form value" with "a saved record keeps the receipt of a source preview and no private form value": the stub client returns `alreadyActive: false` for `github.preview`; assert `drafts.saved("github.preview:a")?.receipt` carries it, that the record survives `startOperation`, that a `profile.configure` record contains no `PRIVATE` text, and that `JSON.stringify(record)` has no `activeSelectionIds`.
3. `operator-action-feedback-browser.test.ts`, new test "activation by another client after the page loaded reads as already active": `startSettings` on `/app/projects/:atlas/settings?tab=sync` with `readerFactory: reader`; before clicking, call `fixture.f.service.domain().execute({ type: "github.activate", actor: "operator", key: randomUUID(), projectId: fixture.ids.atlas, selectionId: "S-1", expectedVersion: domain.githubConfiguration(fixture.ids.atlas).version })` with no reload; click `previewButton`, `savedOutcome(page, repeatActivation)`, and assert `message(page)` equals `S-1 was already active. Tasks aren't imported until you refresh source observations.`. The existing first, repeat and "made before a source change" tests stay unchanged.

Sensitivity check: at baseline, browser test 3 reads "Activated S-1" and fails. If the page re-reads on its own before the click so the baseline passes, hold the page's read with `page.route("**/configuration", …)` serving the pre-activation body, as the withheld-selection test in the same file does; that is an ordinary test repair.

**Implementation:** `activationLine` takes `alreadyActive` from `r.result` (the `github.preview` variant) and chooses the sentence as in Planning decisions; the `saved?.activeSelectionIds` read and the `wasActive` constant are deleted. Remove `activeSelectionIds` from `SavedRecord`, from the `onSaved` signature and call, and from `ConfigurationDrafts.get` (the `this.values.activeSelectionIds` read goes with it). In `sync-placement.tsx` keep the `activeSelectionIds` value and replace its comment with one saying it re-initialises the form once a preview is recorded and the next read shows the new active set. Update the `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` sentence to say the Sync tab names the activated or already-active selection from the confirmed receipt's prior-state field, at the loaded source version, and says nothing about prior state for a receipt recorded before the field existed.
**Validate:** From the repository root after T1, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-settings-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-settings-state.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.js`; expect all pass with 0 failures (the browser file uses Chromium and runs as in CI).
**Complete when:** the three test files pass with the updated and new tests, `web` type checking passes, and the doc sentence matches the behaviour.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| The activation result includes prior active state at the source version | 1 | Domain test "github.activate reports whether the selection was already active…" (first, repeat, replay, stale-version) |
| Receipts recorded before the change still replay | 1 | `command-results` legacy assertions; "preview lookup replays an unchanged receipt recorded before alreadyActive existed" |
| Concurrent activation reports exactly one first activation | 1 | "concurrent source previews report exactly one first activation" |
| The web outcome uses the result and a concurrent activation reads "already active" | 3 | Presentation test 1; browser test "activation by another client after the page loaded reads as already active" |
| CLI output uses it (first, repeat, another actor, concurrent) | 2 | "preview-source reports whether the selection was already active" |
| HTML: no activation message is shown, so nothing to change | 1 | Entry-point check in Planning decisions; the legacy HTML preview test in `github-source-config.test.ts` stays green |
| Pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check` | Final | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, using Node 24.21.0 (`.node-version`) and the pinned npm, run `npm ci && npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate (after T1, T2 and T3); expect typecheck, lint, format check, build and the full test suite to pass.
- PR CI on the PR head must pass. Baseline CI on `b2d7a2b4` passed every job (`node26-full-compatibility` skipped by design).

### Review focus

- The prior-state read uses the current configuration version, not mere row existence, and sits in the same transaction as the upsert; replay returns the recorded value.
- Replay and read stay on `parseDomainCommandOutcome` (legacy-tolerant), and only the new apply path uses the fresh parser.
- An absent `alreadyActive` never renders as "Activated" or "already active" on the web or the CLI.
