nodes.body:
**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1042 **Planned against:** `main` at `15e16a300145d760a00f082b92e6e3f231920523` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach Re-lay the existing Board (`TaskBoard` and `TaskCard` in `web/src/task-views.tsx`, the `.board-*` and `.task-card` rules in `web/src/work.css`) on the `04-tasks-board` composition: equal-width columns on one screen at 1366, every empty column collapsed to a narrow labelled rail, drawn cards (title, project and source identity, reason, next actor in amber when it is you, lead and response) and the phone one-column tabs with previous/next. Everything is `web/` presentation over the task-list read the shell already holds and the whole-Inbox read it already passes in as `requests`: no `src/` change, no new read, command or endpoint, and no change to `taskColumn` grouping, filters, URL state, the link bar's behaviour or the Back/scroll restoration. Order: T1 card anatomy, column header and the Ready label (with its pure helpers) → T2 equal-width columns, rails, segmented link bar and phone/tablet polish → T3 DESIGN.md, ui08 row and evidence. ### Guardrails - SPEC.md owns behaviour; the canvas owns presentation (epic #1035 Boundaries). No change to `src/`, contracts, commands or endpoints; `taskColumn` priority and its closure-held rule (Paused with "Held · closed on GitHub", #1031); List and Board showing identical filtered task IDs; no drag-and-drop or status mutation; Stop/Resume and holds. Haze stays untouched. - Keep these DOM and state hooks exactly, because existing tests and the Back/scroll restoration depend on them: `.board-columns` (the one horizontal scroller), `.board-column` with `id="column-"`, `data-empty="true"` and `aria-label=" tasks"`, `.task-card` (a `Card`, `data-slot="card"`) inside `[data-task-id]`, `.task-title`, `.task-reason`, `.task-next[data-operator]`, `.column-navigation` (`role=toolbar`, name "Board columns") with `.column-tab` buttons reading " · " and `aria-pressed`, `.phone-column-controls` with its `Previous column: …` / `Next column: …` names, the `#column- p` empty-state sentences, and `history.state.board.{selected,scrollLeft}`. - Out of scope: Overview (#1039, merged), Inbox (#1040), task detail (#1041), composer (#1043, merged), neutral badges (#1044), the readiness picker (#1032), List restyling, the shell page header (title and subtitle stay the shell's; `web/src/app.tsx` is edited by #1040 and is not touched), `.page`'s 1200px max width, and any identifier, time, count or repair fact that no read model carries (Planning decisions). - Keep every existing test. Update the selectors and assumptions listed per slice rather than deleting; add browser tests for each new behaviour. Non-browser cases stay independently runnable (Node 26 service CI has no browser). - Plan-mismatch vs ordinary repair. A factual plan mismatch (one diagnosis, at most two repair cycles) is only a wrong seam or repository assumption in this plan, namely: (a) seven populated Active columns cannot share one 1366 screen with readable cards using only CSS on the existing `.board-columns` flex scroller and `.board-column` sections (measured below: the board is 1094px wide; seven columns plus six 10px gaps need 140px each); (b) `TaskListSummary` lacks a fact the card, chip or tone rules use (`ready`, `admission.eligible`, `attention.codes`, `execution`, `lead`, `source` are all present); (c) the rail cannot keep the `

` empty-state sentences and `aria-label` names the existing tests read. Ordinary in-scope work stays with the ticket owner and consumes no budget: selector, copy and fixture updates, CSS and responsive tuning (including the Allowed deviations), test setup, lint/format/typecheck, documentation, CI flake and baseline-equivalent path or command corrections. Record such corrections briefly in the delivery record; stop for a material design/contract change, changed authority, or unknown overlap. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption. ### Planning decisions - **Artboards.** `04-tasks-board` governs the all-projects Board (1366); `23-atlas-project-board` shows the same rules on a project route and collapses Ready, Paused and Uncertain to rails; `800f-tablet-all-projects-board` governs 1024 (link bar kept, Stopping and Uncertain reached through it); `25-phone-board-waiting` and `25b-phone-board-uncertain` govern the phone; `ds-domain-components` gives the board-card rule ("amber border only when the next actor is you") and the column-tab specimen. Compose any state a frame does not draw from these, as the sibling plans did. - **One screen at 1366, measured.** On the base, the seeded catalog populates all seven Active columns, `.board-columns` is 1094px wide at 1366×900 and today scrolls to 2592px (360px columns). Seven equal columns plus six 10px gaps give 147px each, so the column floor is `--board-column-min: 140px` (not the frame's 176px, which fits only five populated columns plus rails; the frame draws no Draft column). Populated columns are `flex: 1 1 0` (equal width); seven fit at 1366, and narrower viewports (below about 1310px with the sidebar, about 1080px in the drawer shell) or State "All tasks" (nine columns) scroll inside `.board-columns` only, with the link bar and phone tabs as the reach path. A fixed-minimum scroller is the frame's own `overflow-x: auto` behaviour. - **Every empty column is a rail** (as `23-atlas-project-board` draws and the current build already collapses), 44px wide at 760px and wider: the count on top, then the column name and its existing empty-state sentence set vertically (`writing-mode: vertical-rl`). The `

` sentences ("None ready. Held Ready work is in Waiting.", "No tasks") and `aria-label`s stay. On the phone the selected empty column renders as an ordinary block, so rails are a ≥760px treatment only. - **Card anatomy** (`ds-domain-components`, `04-tasks-board`): title (with a chip, below), project and identity (`repository#number` in mono, source link opens GitHub in a new tab; "Local task"), recorded reasons, next actor (amber through the existing `data-operator`), then a footer row with the lead on the left and the existing request response link on the right. Border tone: `--risk-border` when `isUncertain(task)`, else `--attn-border` when the next actor is you, else `--line-strong`; fill `--raised`; 10px padding, 6px gap. The card stays the `Card` primitive with its 8px radius (the frame's 6px is a 2px difference and `operator-foundation-browser.test.ts` measures the primitive), and the footer drops the avatar and the corner arrow, which the frame does not draw. The lead keeps today's " · accountable lead" wording (accountability stays visible, SPEC; `23` draws it), not 04's "Lead · ". - **The state word leaves the card.** The column heading already names it, so the card's state badge is removed from Board cards (List rows keep theirs). nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Pick GitHub readiness Project-field conditions by name, with node-ID fallback

**Current behavior:**
A GitHub source readiness condition of kind "Project field" takes three typed inputs: Project node ID, field node ID and option node ID. Operator discovery (`/api/operator/discovery/projects`) already lists a repository's linked Projects by id and title using the discovery credential, but nothing discovers a Project's single-select fields or their options for the operator UI.

**Desired behavior:**
- With discovery available, the condition form offers a picker: linked GitHub Project by title, then its single-select fields by name, then that field's options by name. Saved values are the same node IDs as today.
- When discovery is unavailable, unauthorized or truncated (e.g. `hasNextPage`), the typed node-ID inputs remain with the existing "discovery unavailable" note. A previously saved condition whose IDs are not in the discovered list stays editable as typed IDs.
- Field/option discovery is a fixed read-only GraphQL query that uses only the configured discovery credential, never the source or delivery credential, and returns validated data.

**Key interfaces:**
- The discovery reader (`DiscoveryReader` / `GitHubDiscoveryReader`) and its operator API route: add a read for a Project's single-select fields and options
- The readiness condition shape (`projectNodeId`, `fieldNodeId`, `optionNodeId`): unchanged
- `design/DESIGN.md` Interaction notes › Settings and sign-in describes the target picker

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] With discovery, the form lists Projects, single-select fields and options by name and saves the same node IDs as typed entry would
- [ ] Without discovery or on truncation, typed node-ID inputs and the existing note remain
- [ ] Versioned, keyed source save, preview and activation behave exactly as before
- [ ] Field/option discovery uses only the discovery credential (test asserts the credential used)
- [ ] Service tests cover the new discovery read (success, missing credential, truncation); browser tests cover picker and fallback
- [ ] `npm run check` passes

**Out of scope:**
- Label-kind readiness conditions
- Delivery Project-field configuration
- Non-single-select field types

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1032
**Planned against:** `main` at `1da07083a8b826c93d786d5923366930a54d9023`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add one read-only discovery read, a Project's single-select fields and options, behind the existing discovery path (`GitHubDiscoveryReader` -> `OperatorApi.discoveryRead` -> `GET /api/operator/discovery/project-fields?project=<node id>`), then use it in the GitHub source tab's readiness "Project field" condition row. The browser composes the Project list from reads that already exist (repositories, then each linked repository's Projects), reads fields lazily for the chosen Project, and renders three name selects. Row values stay `projectNodeId` / `fieldNodeId` / `optionNodeId`, so `sourceCommand`, the keyed versioned save, preview and activation are untouched. Anything unavailable, unauthorized, truncated, empty or unlisted degrades that row to the existing typed node-ID inputs with a note.

### Guardrails

- The readiness condition shape, `web/src/settings-changes.ts`, `sourceCommand`, `github.configure`, `src/core`, the save/version/preview/activation rules and Label-kind conditions stay unchanged. Out of scope: delivery Project-field configuration and non-single-select field types.
- The new read uses only the configured discovery credential, through `OperatorApi.discoveryRead` / `discoveryToken`. It must never receive the source, delivery or Claude credential, and it stores nothing. Returned data is validated with Zod on the server (GitHub payload) and again by the shared contract schema; failures are reason codes, never a message, token or URL.
- Agent tooling gets no new surface: the route is an authenticated operator GET only (read authority, no POST), and no coordination tool is added.
- No dependencies, no CSS changes (reuse `settings-rows`, `settings-fields`, `metadata muted`, `NativeSelect`).
- Plan-mismatch budget: a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example GitHub rejecting the `node(id:)` + `ProjectV2SingleSelectField` query shape, or linked repositories not resolvable to `owner/name` from the existing reads) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; after that stop and request a replan. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, lint, type and CI repairs (including the known unrelated CI flake in Final validation) stay with the ticket owner, are recorded briefly in the delivery record, and do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap with in-flight #1030/#1039; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews.

### Planning decisions

- **Browser composes the Project list; no new Projects read.** A saved repository link carries only `repositoryId` (a GitHub node ID from guided discovery, or the typed form `github.com/owner/name`, lowercased; the browser-test seed uses `acme/atlas`), but `/discovery/projects` needs `owner/name`. The picker resolves each saved link through `/discovery/repositories` (match on node ID, `typedRepositoryId`, or `owner/name`, case-insensitive), then reads `/discovery/projects?repository=` per resolved repository and lists only `linked` Projects (the issue says "linked"; `owned` is ignored). The server already filters closed Projects, so a condition saved against a closed Project is treated as unlisted and stays typed. Rejected: a Project-keyed server read that resolves repositories itself, which needs a new repository-resolution surface and more shared edits.
- **One new fixed GraphQL query**, following `src/standalone/github-source.ts` `projectFieldsQuery`: `query ($project: ID!) { node(id: $project) { ... on ProjectV2 { id fields(first: 100) { nodes { __typename ... on ProjectV2SingleSelectField { id name options { id name } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage } } } } }`. `project` travels only as a variable; there is no mutation. A null `node`, or a node that is not a `ProjectV2` (no `id`), is `forbidden`. `pageInfo.hasNextPage` on fields is `truncated`; options are not paginated by GitHub. The existing `projects()` GraphQL error/rate-limit mapping moves into a private `graphql()` helper shared by both reads (same behavior, one copy).
- **Fallback is conservative and per row.** Typed inputs replace the selects when: the repositories read, any linked repository's Projects read, or the chosen Project's fields read is unavailable or truncated; no linked Project is found; or the row already holds IDs that are not all in the discovered lists. An unlisted-ID row stays typed (sticky by `rowKey`) for as long as the form is open, so typing never swaps controls under the cursor. A new row or a row whose IDs are all listed uses the selects. Choosing a Project clears field and option; choosing a field clears option.
- **Reads happen only while at least one Project-field row exists** and are re-run when the session CSRF token changes; each Project's fields are read once and cached. Label-only users and existing tests make no new requests.
- **Notes.** Unavailable reasons reuse `discoveryReasonCopy` from `web/src/setup-model.ts` with " Type the node IDs." appended, except `unconfigured`, whose copy is guided-setup specific and gets a condition-specific sentence. Truncated and "no linked Project" have fixed sentences. All start with "GitHub discovery is unavailable" or "No GitHub Project is linked".
- **Design doc.** `design/DESIGN.md` Interaction notes already states the target picker; only the production-difference sentence that names #1032 changes. That is the sole unavoidable shared-file edit (see overlap).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 -> T2, acyclic. T2 needs T1's schema, route and `fakeDiscovery` extension, so there is no safe concurrency between them. Files owned: T1 `src/standalone/github-discovery.ts`, `src/operator/contracts.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-web.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-credentials.ts`, `test/fixtures/setup-home.ts`, `test/sources/github-discovery.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-setup-api.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-cli-http.test.ts`, `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md`. T2 `web/src/readiness-discovery.ts` (new), `web/src/readiness-picker.tsx` (new), `web/src/source-config.tsx`, `test/operator/operator-readiness-picker-model.test.ts` (new), `test/operator/operator-project-config-browser.test.ts`, `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts`, `design/DESIGN.md`. Overlap with in-flight #1030 and #1039: no web file, `contracts.ts`, `operator-web.ts` or `operator-credentials.ts` overlap. Shared with #1030 only: `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (this plan edits the import list near line 58 and adds one method after `readDiscoveryProjects` near line 5413; #1030 edits the `task.stop` branch) and `design/DESIGN.md` (this plan changes one sentence in the "Settings, profiles, routing, runtime and recovery" production-differences list near line 1747-1749; keep that hunk to that sentence). Shared with #1039 only: `design/DESIGN.md` (same sentence). Hunks are disjoint, so a clean rebase is expected; re-check at delivery.

#### 1. Discovery read for a Project's single-select fields

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/github-discovery.ts` (`DiscoveryReader`, `GitHubDiscoveryReader`, new `projectFields`, new private `graphql`); `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`discoveryProjectFieldsSchema`); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`readDiscoveryProjectFields`, new `discoveryProject(query)` parser beside `discoveryRepository`); `src/standalone/operator-web.ts` (route); `src/standalone/operator-credentials.ts` (`operatorRouteAuthority` read list); `test/fixtures/setup-home.ts` (`fakeDiscovery`); `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md`.
**Test:**
- `test/sources/github-discovery.test.ts`: with the existing `fake()` fetcher. Success: a response with a single-select field, a non-single-select node (`__typename` other) and a second single-select field returns only the two single-select fields as `{ fieldNodeId, name, options: [{ optionNodeId, name }] }`, `truncated: false`; assert exactly one POST to `https://api.github.com/graphql`, `authorization` equals `Bearer <token>`, the query starts with `query ` and contains no `mutation`, and `variables` deep-equals `{ project: "PVT_atlas" }`. Truncation: `pageInfo.hasNextPage: true` gives `truncated: true`. Failures through the existing `reason()` helper: `new GitHubDiscoveryReader(undefined, f.fetcher)` gives `missing-credential` with zero calls; 401 `unauthorized`; GraphQL `errors` give `forbidden`; `RATE_LIMITED` error gives `rate-limited`; `node: null` and a node without `id` give `forbidden`; a malformed single-select node gives `unreadable`. The error message never contains the token.
- `test/operator/operator-setup-api.test.ts`: new test beside "discovery reads list through the injected reader". Set `process.env.FIXTURE_DISCOVERY` to a distinct token and `FIXTURE_GITHUB` to a different one (restore both in `t.after`), configure `env:FIXTURE_DISCOVERY`, inject `discovery: (ref, token) => { seen.push({ ref, token }); return reader }`. Assert `readDiscoveryProjectFields(new URLSearchParams({ project: "PVT_atlas" }))` is `ready` with the fake's fields, `seen` deep-equals `[{ ref: "env:FIXTURE_DISCOVERY", token: <discovery token> }]` and never contains the source token (credential used). Unconfigured returns `unavailable`/`unconfigured` without constructing a reader; `DiscoveryFailure("unauthorized")` maps to that reason; `new Error("PRIVATE")` maps to `unreadable` with no echo; `truncated: true` passes through; `command_receipts`, `project_github_sources` and `domain_projects` row counts are unchanged. Bad queries throw `{ status: 400 }`: none, `project=`, two `project` values, an extra key, and `project=a/b`. In the HTTP route test near line 491 add `/api/operator/discovery/project-fields?project=PVT_atlas` to the 401/200/405 loop and the missing/duplicate/invalid forms to the 400 loop.
- `test/operator/operator-cli-http.test.ts`: in "every known API route has an explicit authority" add the new path to the representative list and assert `operatorRouteAuthority("GET", path) === "read"` and `undefined` for POST.
**Implementation:** Extend `DiscoveryReader` with `projectFields(project: string): Promise<{ fields: { fieldNodeId: string; name: string; options: { optionNodeId: string; name: string }[] }[]; truncated: boolean }>`. Extract the GraphQL POST plus error/rate-limit handling from `projects()` into a private `graphql(query, variables)` and use it from both reads; behavior of `projects()` must not change. Implement `projectFields` with the fixed query in Planning decisions, validating single-select nodes strictly with Zod and ignoring other `__typename` values. Add `discoveryProjectFieldsSchema = discoveryRead({ fields: array of strict { fieldNodeId min1 max512, name max512, options: array of strict { optionNodeId min1 max512, name max512 } max 500 } max 100 })`. Add `OperatorApi.readDiscoveryProjectFields(query)`: exactly one key `project` matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_=-]{1,512}$`, otherwise `OperatorApiError(400, "invalid-input")`; then `discoveryRead(discoveryProjectFieldsSchema, r => r.projectFields(id))`. Route `/api/operator/discovery/project-fields` in `operator-web.ts` next to branches/projects (before the empty-query guard) and add it to the read list in `operator-credentials.ts`. Extend `fakeDiscovery`: `projectFields(project)` returns, for `PVT_atlas`, `Status` (`PVTSSF_status`; options `Todo` `PVTSSO_todo`, `Ready` `PVTSSO_ready`) and `Priority` (`PVTSSF_priority`; options `High`, `Low`), and no fields for other Projects, with `truncated: Boolean(state.truncated)` and the same `fail("projectFields")` call recording as the other methods. Document the route in the discovery-read sentence of `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` (line 15) and add Project fields to the "discovery read" table row.

#### 2. Name picker in the readiness Project-field condition

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the working branch (schema, route, `fakeDiscovery.projectFields`).
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/readiness-discovery.ts` (new, pure; no React), `web/src/readiness-picker.tsx` (new), `web/src/source-config.tsx` (`SourceTab` project-field branch only), `test/operator/operator-readiness-picker-model.test.ts` (new), `test/operator/operator-project-config-browser.test.ts`, `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts` (`startSettings` option), `design/DESIGN.md`.

(b) Fallback: with `state.truncated = true`, reload, the typed "Readiness Project node ID" / "field" / "option" inputs and the note "GitHub discovery is unavailable" are shown; typed IDs save as before. (c) A saved condition whose IDs are not discovered (seed one via `github.configure` with `PVT_gone` IDs) renders typed inputs prefilled with those IDs and stays editable and savable. It also exports `ProjectFieldPicker`, which renders three labelled `NativeSelect`s ("Readiness Project", "Readiness field", "Readiness option"; disabled with a "Loading..." option while reads are pending) or, in typed mode, the node passed in by `SourceTab`. In `source-config.tsx` replace only the project-field branch with `ProjectFieldPicker`, passing the existing three `input(...)` calls as the typed fallback and `update("conditions", i, patch)` as the change handler; reuse `rowError` for `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`. > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Label a Closure hold "Held · closed on GitHub", distinct from Project pause

**Current behavior:**
When an imported issue closes on GitHub without Ensemble delivering it, `providerClosure()` reports `"held"` and the task stays open. The task status line and the retained HTML task page read "Paused · closed on GitHub", reusing the Project pause word. The CLI closure suffix already reads "(closed on GitHub; held)".

**Desired behavior:**
- Every operator-facing label for a closure-held task reads "Held · closed on GitHub" (with the active execution state appended where it is today) and uses the neutral badge.
- Project-paused tasks keep "Paused" wording unchanged.
- List/Board keep grouping closure-held tasks in the Paused column; only the reason text changes.
- CLI wording stays consistent with the new label (adjust only if it diverges).

**Key interfaces:**
- The task overview status derivation that branches on `source.closure === "held"`
- The retained operator HTML GitHub source provenance paragraph
- The shared CLI `closureSuffix` helper
- CONTEXT.md **Closure hold** and **Project pause** (terms already settled)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Task status line, List/Board reason, task detail and retained HTML page read "Held · closed on GitHub" for a closure-held task
- [ ] Closure-held badge uses the neutral variant
- [ ] Project-paused tasks still read "Paused"/"project paused"
- [ ] Browser tests cover a closure-held task and a project-paused task side by side
- [ ] `npm run check` passes

**Out of scope:**
- Changing closure-hold domain behaviour, resolution flow or the Paused column grouping

content.title: Offer Stop only on open tasks

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Offer and accept Task stop only on an open task

**Current behavior:**
The operator task header and the retained `/runtime/task/:id` page offer Stop… whenever the task has no Stop hold, including Done and Cancelled tasks. The `task.stop` command (operator API, service `controlTask`, CLI task control) accepts a finished task: it records an `operator-stop` hold and cancels zero executions. CONTEXT.md **Task stop** says stop applies only to an open task.

**Desired behavior:**
- Stop… is offered only while the task is open, on every surface that offers it (React task header, retained runtime task page, CLI help/output where it advertises Stop).
- `task.stop` for a Done or Cancelled task is refused with a plain operator-facing reason through the existing refusal path (HTTP conflict, CLI error, receipted command semantics unchanged for open tasks). If evidence shows refusal would break recovery or receipt replay, ship the UI gate only and document the command behaviour in `docs/SPEC.md`; say which in the PR.
- A Stop hold that already exists on a finished task stays visible ("Stop requested") and remains resumable via `task.resume`.

**Key interfaces:**
- `task.stop` / `task.resume` command handling in the service `controlTask` path and the operator API command dispatch
- The task report's `stop` state used by the task header to decide what to render
- Task open/finished status from the domain task model

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Task header and retained runtime task controls show no Stop… for Done and Cancelled tasks, and still show it for open tasks
- [ ] `task.stop` on a finished task is refused with a plain reason (or the documented UI-only fallback, with justification)
- [ ] A pre-existing Stop hold on a finished task is still displayed and `task.resume` clears it
- [ ] Service tests cover stop on open, Done and Cancelled tasks; browser tests cover the header for all three
- [ ] `npm run check` passes

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Stop semantics on open tasks (hold + best-effort cancellation)
- Project pause, task cancellation or completion flows
- Migrating or clearing existing Stop holds on finished tasks

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1030
**Planned against:** `main` at `c10d9dbc55529935dfed1be09bd7dd6ebce8094a`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Gate Stop on the task being open at the one shared seam, `ExecutionState.holdTask`, so the receipted `task.stop` (operator API, CLI) and the non-receipted retained form/`service.stopTask` all refuse a Done or Cancelled task; surface the refusal as a plain `409 conflict` message; then hide Stop on both UI surfaces (React header, retained `/runtime/task/:id`). Resume, the receipt-replay path and existing Stop holds on finished tasks are untouched. Three disjoint increments (backend, retained page, React header) with their docs and tests.

### Guardrails

- Stop semantics on open tasks (hold plus best-effort cancellation), project pause, task cancellation/completion and migration or clearing of existing Stop holds on finished tasks are out of scope. `task.resume` is unchanged and must keep clearing a pre-existing Stop on a Done or Cancelled task.
- A same-key replay of a stored `task.stop` receipt must still return the stored receipt even if the task is now finished: the finished-task check runs only after the receipt lookup in `ExecutionState.controlTask`.
- No change to `src/standalone/operator.ts`, `web/src/task-overview.ts`, `web/src/tasks.ts`, `web/src/task-views.tsx`, `web/src/work.css`, `web/src/task-attention.tsx`, `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx`, `web/src/app.tsx` (in-flight #1031/#1039 territory). Do not edit `operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts`; new browser coverage goes in a new file.
- Plan-mismatch budget: a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (listed under Planning decisions: the `holdTask` seam, Done/Cancelled tasks having no live execution or writer hold in production, `domain_tasks` readable from `ExecutionState`'s database, the `publicMessage` refusal path) gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; on exhaustion stop and return for replanning. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs (for example a fixture or test that stops a finished task, copy wording, lint/format, snapshot or timing-weight updates) stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap with #1031/#1039; stop for material design or contract changes.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews; use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Command behaviour: refuse `task.stop` for a finished task (no UI-only fallback).** Evidence at base: (1) `controlTask` looks up the stored receipt before any state change (`src/standalone/state.ts` ~L842-852), so a replay of an earlier Stop returns the stored receipt regardless of later task state; the refusal sits after that lookup and does not affect replay. (2) Resume never calls the Stop path (`releaseStop`), so recovery of a pre-existing Stop hold is unaffected. (3) A task becomes Done only through `coordination.ts` completion, which rejects while any `task_writer_holds` row or unfinished bound execution exists (~L4522-4590), or through `completeFromProviderClosure`, gated on `taskExecutionSettled` (`src/standalone/service.ts:2742`); no production code path sets `cancelled` (only fixtures). So a finished task has nothing to cancel, which matches the brief's "Stop on a finished task records an `operator-stop` hold and cancels zero executions". The one exception, a lead turn still finishing the completion it requested (`externalAction`), ends on its own terminal status and is recovered through the existing assignment recovery commands, not `task.stop`. (4) The only callers of `stopTask`/`controlTask` are the operator API command branch, the CLI and the retained form route; no scheduler, supervisor or recovery code stops a task. (5) Allowing the Stop is actively harmful: any `task_writer_holds` row blocks archival (`archiveUnblockedClause`, `state.ts:398`), so a Stop on a Done task creates a hold that needs a Resume.
- **Seam:** `ExecutionState.holdTask` (private, run inside the transaction, shared by `stopTask` and `controlTask`). It reads `SELECT state FROM domain_tasks WHERE id = ?` (the table is in the same database; `controlTask` already reads it) and throws `TaskNotOpenError` when the state is not `open`. The throw rolls the transaction back, so no hold, stop target or receipt row is written.
- **Error type:** `TaskNotOpenError extends DomainConflictError` in `src/core/domain-errors.ts`, carrying `taskState: "done" | "cancelled"`; being a subclass, existing mapping keeps it a 409 on every path.
- **Plain reason:** in `operator-api.ts` the `task.stop` branch converts it to `new OperatorApiError(409, "conflict", undefined, undefined, "Only an open task can be stopped. This task is Done.")` (or `Cancelled`), using the existing `publicMessage` path that `runtimeRefusal` uses. `src/standalone/operator.ts` is untouched; the CLI prints the API message (`src/cli/transport.ts:100`) with exit 4 `conflict`, a definite rejection that does not reuse a journal key. A stale retained Stop POST gets the existing generic 409 "Change conflict" page, because the retained page no longer offers the form.
- **React header:** `taskHeaderReport` adds `stop.open = data.task.state === "open"` (computed in `task-header.tsx`, not `stopConsequences`). Render order: `held` shows the disabled "Stop requested"; else `open` shows the Stop… dialog; else nothing. A Stop hold on a finished task therefore stays visible; its Resume remains on the retained page, CLI and API (the React header has no Resume control for open tasks either, an intentional existing gap not widened here).
- **Retained page:** on a finished task `operator-runtime.ts` omits `stopForm`, keeps `resumeForm`, and uses the sentence "Only an open task can be stopped. Resume clears only the Stop, not any other hold on this task." The open-task copy stays byte-identical because `assertTaskControlsCopy` in `operator-browser.test.ts` asserts it.
- **Entry points:** React task header; retained `GET /runtime/task/:id` plus `POST /runtime/control/stop`; operator API `task.stop`; CLI `task stop`; `service.stopTask`/`controlTask`. No other web surface offers Stop (`rg "Stop…"` finds only `task-header.tsx`); `design/DESIGN.md` L155 already says Stop… only while open.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `ExecutionState.holdTask` (insert hold, collect stop targets, hold intents/turn requests), called by `stopTask` and by `controlTask` after receipt lookup and the optional version check.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `stopTask`/`controlTask` call `this.domain().task(id)` (not-found) then state; no change needed.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` ~L6284 — `task.stop|task.resume` branch calls `this.service.controlTask(c)`; outer catch maps `DomainConflictError` to 409 via `domainApiError` (L359).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` — task page builder around L447-517 (`stopForm`, `resumeForm`, `task.state`), `POST /runtime/control/stop` calls `api.stopTask`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-header.tsx` — `taskHeaderReport`, `TaskHeaderActions`; `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` and `web/src/app.tsx` only forward the report.
- **New:** `src/core/domain-errors.ts` — `TaskNotOpenError`.
- **Follow:** `runtimeRefusal` in `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` for a 409 with fixed public copy; `test/coordination/operator-task-control.test.ts` (`fixture`, `control`, `rows`, direct `INSERT INTO task_writer_holds` seeding) for service tests; `test/coordination/operator-cli-task-control.test.ts` and `startCliOperator` for CLI; `test/execution/operator-runtime.test.ts` (`runtimeOperatorRoutes(service)` handler invocation) for retained page tests; `operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (`browserSuite`, `createOperatorFixture`, `signIn`) for browser tests.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1, T2, T3 all have `Depends on: none`; the graph is acyclic. Their owned files are disjoint (T1: core error, state, operator-api, CLI help, SPEC, operator-cli.md and three test files; T2: operator-runtime plus one new test file; T3: task-header plus ui08/DESIGN docs plus one new browser test file), so all three may run concurrently. Files touched, for overlap checks against #1031 (`web/src/task-overview.ts`, `web/src/tasks.ts`, `src/standalone/operator.ts`, task browser tests) and #1039 (`web/src/task-views.tsx`, `web/src/work.css`, `web/src/task-attention.tsx`, `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx`, `web/src/app.tsx`, work/task browser tests): none of the source or test files is on either list. The one shared surface is `design/DESIGN.md` L1681-1686, where the "It still offers Stop… on finished tasks (#1030)" clause shares a sentence with #1031's closure-hold clause; edit only the #1030 clause and rebase over any #1031 edit.

#### 1. Refuse Stop on a finished task at the shared seam

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/core/domain-errors.ts` (new `TaskNotOpenError`)
- `src/standalone/state.ts` (`holdTask`)
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`task.stop|task.resume` branch)
- `src/cli/main.ts` (task-operations help paragraph, one sentence)
- `docs/SPEC.md` ("Execution and recovery", Stop paragraph ~L254)
- `docs/design/operator-cli.md` (~L410 task.stop/task.resume paragraph)
- Tests: `test/coordination/operator-task-control.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-cli-http.test.ts`, `test/coordination/operator-cli-task-control.test.ts`

**Test:**
- Service (`operator-task-control.test.ts`, new test "Stop applies only to an open task"): use `fixture(t)`, `seedReviewTask` for three tasks; flip two with `f.seedPersistedState((db) => db.prepare("UPDATE domain_tasks SET state=?, version=version+1 WHERE id=?").run(...))`. Assert: open task Stop records a `task-stop` receipt; for `done` and `cancelled`, `control(f, "task.stop", id)` and `f.service.stopTask(id)` reject with `TaskNotOpenError` whose `taskState` matches, and `databaseDigest` (from `test/fixtures/database-digest.js`) is identical before and after (no hold, stop target or receipt). Replay: Stop an open task with key K, flip it to done, call Stop again with K and assert deep-equal to the first receipt. Recovery: on a done task, `INSERT INTO task_writer_holds (taskId, reason, holdKind) VALUES (?, 'Task stopped', 'operator-stop')` (as at the file's existing L511), then `control(f, "task.resume", id)` returns `stopCleared: true` and `f.service.isTaskStopped(id)` becomes false.
- HTTP (`operator-cli-http.test.ts`, new test): with a read-write bearer token POST `task.stop` for a Done task to `/api/operator/commands`; expect 409, `error.code === "conflict"` and `error.message` matching `/Only an open task can be stopped\. This task is Done\./`; repeat for Cancelled; open task still returns 200; resume of a seeded hold on a Done task returns 200 with `stopCleared: true`.
- CLI (`operator-cli-task-control.test.ts`, new test): `cli("rw", ["task","stop", doneTaskId])` exits 4 and its error output contains the same sentence; no hold recorded (`stopped(o, id)` false). With a seeded hold on that Done task, `task get` shows `execution.holds.stop === true` and `task resume` exits 0 with `stopInEffect: false`.
- Sensitivity: temporarily removing the `holdTask` guard must fail the service, HTTP and CLI refusal assertions while the replay and resume assertions still pass.

**Implementation:**
1. Add `TaskNotOpenError` (message "Only an open task can be stopped", field `taskState`).
2. In `holdTask`, first statement: read the task state from `domain_tasks`; if it is not `open`, throw `TaskNotOpenError(state)`. Keep it before any insert so nothing is written. Do not move the receipt lookup; `controlTask` must still return a stored receipt first.
3. In `operator-api.ts`, wrap `this.service.controlTask(c)` for `c.type === "task.stop"` only: catch `TaskNotOpenError` and throw the `OperatorApiError(409, "conflict", ..., "Only an open task can be stopped. This task is <Done|Cancelled>.")`; rethrow everything else unchanged.
4. Docs: SPEC Stop paragraph gets "Stop applies only to an open task; a Done or Cancelled task refuses `task.stop`, and an existing Stop on it stays visible and resumable." `operator-cli.md` states that `task.stop` on a finished task is refused with `409 conflict` and a plain reason, evaluated after receipt replay, and that `task.resume` still clears an existing Stop. `src/cli/main.ts` help adds "Stop applies only to an open task." Do not touch `CONTEXT.md` (**Task stop** already says it).
5. Grep the test tree for stops on finished tasks (`rg "state='(done|cancelled)'" test` against `stopTask`/`task.stop` users) and repair fixtures that relied on the old behaviour; these are ordinary repairs.

**Validate:** From the repo root, after `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 24.21.0` (the `.node-version` release) and `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/coordination/operator-task-control.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-cli-http.test.js dist/test/coordination/operator-cli-task-control.test.js`; expect all tests pass, including the three new ones. Also run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint`; expect no errors.
**Complete when:** the three new tests pass, the replay and resume assertions pass, and docs state the behaviour.

#### 2. Hide Stop on the retained runtime task page

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` (task page builder: `stopForm`, `resumeForm`, Task controls section)
- New test `test/operator/operator-runtime-task-controls.test.ts`

**Test:** service-tier, no browser. `createOperatorFixture`, `seedReviewTask` for an open, a Done and a Cancelled task (finish via `f.seedPersistedState` UPDATE as in T1), `runtimeOperatorRoutes(f.service)`, find `GET /runtime/task/:taskId`, invoke the handler with `{ params: { taskId }, fields: {}, csrfToken: "t" }` (the shape used in `test/execution/operator-runtime.test.ts`). Assert: open page body contains `action="/runtime/control/stop"` and `Best-effort Stop`; Done and Cancelled bodies contain neither, contain `action="/runtime/control/resume"` and the sentence "Only an open task can be stopped." With a seeded Stop hold on the Done task, the body still reports "Operator Stop remains active" (existing `executionHoldSection`) and the Resume form. A `POST /runtime/control/stop` handler call for the Done task rejects with a `DomainConflictError` (T1 behaviour; if T1 has not merged, assert only the page content and add this assertion on integration).
**Implementation:** in the page builder, when `task.state !== "open"` build the Task controls section with the finished-task sentence and `${resumeForm}` only; otherwise unchanged. Do not alter the open-task paragraph (asserted by `assertTaskControlsCopy`).
**Validate:** From the repo root, after `npm run build:service`, run `node --test dist/test/operator/operator-runtime-task-controls.test.js dist/test/execution/operator-runtime.test.js`; expect all pass, and run `node --test --test-name-pattern="Best-effort|Task controls" dist/test/operator/operator-browser.test.js`; expect the open-task copy assertions still pass.
**Complete when:** the new test passes and existing runtime page tests are unchanged.

#### 3. Hide Stop… in the React task header

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/task-header.tsx` (`TaskHeaderReport.stop`, `taskHeaderReport`, `TaskHeaderActions`)
- `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` (the `/app` shell row ~L54 and the `/app/tasks/:id` header row ~L57: Stop… while the task is open)
- `design/DESIGN.md` (~L1681-1693: remove "It still offers Stop… on finished tasks (#1030)" and make the header actions "Execution and, while the task is open, Stop…")
- New test `test/operator/operator-task-stop-browser.test.ts`

**Test:** Chromium via `browserSuite("ui-task-stop")` following `operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (`createOperatorFixture`, `j.start`, `signIn`). Seed three tasks with `seedReviewTask` (distinct project names/titles), finish two via `f.seedPersistedState`. For each task page `/app/tasks/:id` read `.page-header .task-header-actions > *` as `[tag, text]` pairs: open `[["A","Execution"],["BUTTON","Stop…"]]`; Done and Cancelled `[["A","Execution"]]` with zero buttons named "Stop…" or "Stop requested". Then seed an `operator-stop` hold on the Done task (`INSERT INTO task_writer_holds (taskId,reason,holdKind) VALUES (?,'Task stopped','operator-stop')`), reload, and assert the header shows exactly `[["A","Execution"],["BUTTON","Stop requested"]]` with the button disabled.
**Implementation:** add `open: boolean` to `TaskHeaderReport.stop`, set from `data.task.state === "open"` in `taskHeaderReport`; in `TaskHeaderActions` render `held ? <disabled "Stop requested"> : open ? <Dialog…> : null`. Keep the dialog, form and focus handling as they are.
**Validate:** From the repo root, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/operator/operator-task-stop-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js`; expect all pass (the existing open-task header and Stop dialog assertions are unchanged). Also run `npm run typecheck` (includes `web/tsconfig.json`).
**Complete when:** the new browser test passes in Chromium and the docs match.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Task header and retained runtime controls show no Stop… for Done and Cancelled tasks, and still show it for open tasks | 2, 3 | T3 browser test header pairs for all three states; T2 retained page test |
| `task.stop` on a finished task is refused with a plain reason (UI-only fallback not needed; evidence in Planning decisions) | 1 | T1 service, HTTP (409 plus message) and CLI (exit 4 plus message) tests |
| A pre-existing Stop hold on a finished task is still displayed and `task.resume` clears it | 1, 2, 3 | T3 "Stop requested" assertion; T2 retained page shows the hold and Resume form; T1 resume tests at service, HTTP and CLI |
| Service tests cover stop on open, Done and Cancelled; browser tests cover the header for all three | 1, 3 | T1 service test; T3 browser test |
| Receipt replay is unaffected (guardrail) | 1 | T1 replay assertion |
| `npm run check` passes | all | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repo root, with Node 24.21.0 from `.node-version` and `npm ci` done, run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate; expect it to exit 0. CI on the base SHA passed (run 38775102741), so no separate baseline run is needed.
- Before the PR, `rg "task\.stop|stopTask\(" test` against finished-task fixtures to confirm no remaining test or live-qualification script stops a Done or Cancelled task.

### Review focus

- The check order in `controlTask`: replay, then version, then finished-task refusal; confirm the refusal writes nothing.
- No second production path stops a task without passing `holdTask`.
- The open-task retained page copy and Stop dialog are byte-for-byte unchanged.

content.title: W6: Composer prediction panel

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1043
**Planned against:** `main` at `1da07083a8b826c93d786d5923366930a54d9023`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Re-lay out the existing `TaskComposer` as presentation only: no change to `src/`, `composerOptionsSchema`, `ComposerState`, commands or the draft/recovery/receipt lifecycle. Project, Title and Desired outcome lead; Optional settings becomes one bordered panel that shows chips of supplied values (and the error count) when collapsed; the prediction and the inherited facts move into a right-hand column as two panels ("If you create it now" with numbered reasons, "Inherited from <project>"); the sticky bar states what is only on this device and holds Save draft and Create and start. The numbered reasons come from an opt-in `variant="numbered"` of the shared `WaitReasons`, so task detail, getting started and the post-create receipt render exactly as before.

Order: T1 chips and Optional settings panel → T2 right column and field layout → T3 sticky bar → T4 documentation and evidence.

### Guardrails

- SPEC.md owns behaviour; this slice is `web/` presentation (epic #1035 Boundaries). Unchanged: Create and start primary / Save draft secondary; a start-or-wait statement with reasons in `orderWaits` order before submission; every Fix (Resume project confirms then sends only `project.configure {paused:false}`; others link; holds and dependency/approval/source waits have no Fix); drafts (`ready:false`) versus Ready creation; validation (errors open the collapsed group and focus the first invalid control; stale assignee/dependency checks block both actions and send nothing); on-device recovery, frozen unknown-outcome reconciliation, receipt view ("Task created." / "Draft saved.", Open task, Refresh execution, "It will wait: …"); the composer-options read and its scoped refetch. Keep Haze untouched.
- Out of scope: Overview (#1039), Inbox (#1040), task detail (#1041), Board (#1042), neutral badges (#1044), `app.tsx` (page header, breadcrumb, routes), new read models, a `⌘↵` shortcut, rebuilding Optional settings' inner controls, keeping the form on screen after creation.
- Keep every existing test. Update selectors and copy that change (listed per slice) rather than deleting tests; add browser tests for each change. Non-browser cases stay independently runnable (Node 26 service CI has no browser); register browser cases through `browserSuite`, with an explicit engine for WebKit.
- Plan-mismatch versus ordinary repair. A factual plan mismatch (one diagnosis, at most two repair cycles) is only a wrong seam or repository assumption in this plan, namely: (a) the opt-in numbered `WaitReasons` variant cannot be added without changing the default output used by task detail (`task-workspace.tsx`), getting started or the receipt; (b) `ComposerOptions` (`waits`, `assigneeWaits`, `dependencies[].blocking`, `capacity`, `lead`, `routingEnabled`) lacks a fact a panel here is specified to show; (c) moving the aside outside `fieldset.composer-fields` or the outcomes above the bar changes lock, focus or lifecycle behaviour that the existing composer tests prove. Ordinary in-scope work stays with the ticket owner and consumes no budget: selector, copy and fixture updates, CSS and responsive tuning, test setup, lint/format/typecheck, documentation, CI flake and baseline-equivalent path or command corrections. Record such corrections briefly in the delivery record; stop for a material design or contract change, changed authority, or unknown overlap.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Artboards exist; some canvas facts have no read model.** Confirmed on the canvas (version 1792087205-60bd): `05-composer`, `02-composer-optional-expanded`, `34-phone-composer-collapsed`, `35-phone-optional-settings-error`, `35b-phone-collapsed-validation`, `800h-phone-composer-short`, `800e-tablet-composer-validation`, `148-composer-project-paused`, `161-composer-created-project-paused`, `166c-phone-task-created-project-paused`, and the `149c-wait-reasons-specimen`. Compose from them; do not invent contracts. Deliberate differences, recorded in T4: (1) the inherited panel keeps the facts the read carries (lead, lead summary, routing sentence, capacity, "View project instructions"); the canvas "Instructions" and "Repository access" rows stay absent (no read exposes them; already in DESIGN.md Implementation status); (2) no "Project X is enabled · lead is available · capacity" line: `waits` carries blockers, not satisfied conditions, and capacity stays in the inherited panel; (3) no `⌘↵` key on Create and start (no shortcut exists; adding one is a behaviour change); (4) no "Markdown supported" claim; the existing 16,000-character brief note stays; (5) Optional settings keeps its supported controls (one link per line, dependency checklist with search), not the canvas's add/remove link rows and dependency chips, and its count reads "N supplied" at every width (canvas desktop: "N values retained"); (6) after creation the receipt view stays (Task created/Draft saved, Open task, execution, "It will wait: …") instead of 161/166c's locked form with an outcome line in the bar; creation and admission already read as separate lines there; (7) Create and start comes before Save draft in DOM order and visually at every width, so focus order equals visual order (canvas desktop right-aligns Save draft then Create and start); (8) the phone artboards draw no prediction panel (a status line only); production keeps the full prediction, below the fields, and the bar's hint repeats the verdict so it stays in view; (9) the page header keeps "Create a task" and its subtitle, and the label stays "Task title".
- **Opt-in numbered variant, secondary Fix.** `WaitReasons` gains `variant?: "list" | "numbered"` (default `list`, today's output). Numbered renders `ol.wait-numbered` of `li` (the first carries `data-primary="true"`): a mono index (`aria-hidden`), `span.wait-label` (the `waitLabels` text, no "It will wait: " prefix because the panel badge says it), the existing `WaitAction`, and `WaitDetail`; `ResumeOutcome` stays after the list so a Resume outcome remains visible when no wait is left. Every Fix or link in the numbered variant uses the secondary style: the bar's Create and start is the one primary in view (DESIGN.md shape rules; `149c` draws Fix as a secondary button). The first reason is primary by position, not by button colour.
- **Badge tone.** "Will wait" uses the idle tone with a clock symbol (as `05-composer`). "Starts now" uses the accent tone with a distinct symbol, never emerald (emerald means completed or recorded; created is not running). Symbol and word always together.
- **Aside outside the fieldset.** The `aside` leaves `fieldset.composer-fields` (today it sits inside, between Project and Title). Prediction still renders only when options are fresh and the phase is `editable`; the inherited panel renders whenever a project is chosen, as now. In single-column widths (≤1120px, the drawer shell) the aside follows the fields and precedes the bar (DESIGN.md says "under Project" today; T4 corrects it).
- **Bar, status and hint.** The status line is the old `composer-saved` paragraph moved into the bar and extended: "Unfinished input saved on this device · not yet an Ensemble draft". It keeps the existing condition (`state.savedOnDevice && state.phase === "editable"`), so it never appears after a failed write or discard; nothing new is claimed. Hint: with a prediction, "Starts now." or "Will wait: <first reason label>." followed by "Save draft keeps it without starting."; without one, the existing "Creates ready work; waits for dependencies and other holds. Saved drafts are not Ready."; with an optional-settings error, the existing "Check the optional settings to continue. Your input is still here." Failed and unconfirmed outcomes render directly above the bar so the bar stays the form's last element; unknown-outcome focus is unchanged.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/task-composer.tsx` — `TaskComposer` renders the recovery prompt and the recorded receipt as early returns; otherwise one `form` with `fieldset.composer-fields` (Project select, an inherited `aside[aria-label="Inherited from X"]`, Task title, Desired outcome, `details.composer-disclosure` whose `summary` is `optionalSummary().summary`, and `.composer-optional-values` lines when collapsed), then `.composer-actions` (sticky; `.composer-prediction` with `WaitReasons prefix="It will wait: "` or "Starts now."; Create and start; Save draft; hint `p`), then failed/unknown `ActionOutcome`s. `ComposerState` (`composer-state.ts`) owns phase, notice, errors, `savedOnDevice` and storage; do not edit it. The prediction (`orderWaits` over `o.waits` or the assignee's runtime waits, plus a `local-dependency` wait for selected blocking dependencies) stays as computed.

content.title: Show remaining scheduler rejection causes as task wait reasons

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Explain persistent scheduler/admission rejection causes consistently through task wait reasons.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, production `deriveWaits` maps supplied `repository-access-revoked`, `recovery-continuation-unresolved` and `task-revision-changed` reasons to the generic `admission-blocked` wait without a Fix. An isolated real-SQLite `OperatorApi` fixture showed a held assignment has an `assignment-held` wait while its request is queued, loses that wait without a queued request, and exposes no specific wait for a task-revision-only refusal. Static inspection additionally shows repository-access and recovery-continuation checks live in scheduler validation, outside the current domain-only wait projection. This verifies the projection gaps; it did not run live runtime recovery or every scheduler rejection end to end.

**Desired behavior:** Persistent causes that prevent work have a specific wait and an appropriate navigation/recovery entry point. Repository access revocation offers a Fix that opens the operator's repository configuration. Recovery and held execution remain visibly held; their links do not release ownership. Revision-only refusals are either accurately explained or documented as intentionally hidden when transient/already represented elsewhere.

**Key interfaces:** Scheduler rejection facts; `OperatorApi` task/assignment wait projection; shared `WaitCode`, Fix and link schemas; ordered server, CLI and web presentation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Repository-access revocation reaches the task read model with a specific wait and a configuration Fix.
- [ ] Recovery-continuation rejection, revision-only refusal and held assignment after reporting repair each have a tested disposition: visible cause or documented reason for intentional omission.
- [ ] The affected persistent-held case remains explained even when no queued request exists.
- [ ] Server task reads, CLI list/detail, web List/Board/detail and Inbox use the same codes/order and appropriate Fix or link.
- [ ] Unknown causes retain the `admission-blocked` fallback; deduplication and redaction remain intact.
- [ ] Tests cover fact collection as well as mapping, including the no-queued-request and captured-revision cases. Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing admission eligibility, automatically rebinding stale work, granting repository access, releasing recovery holds or adding automatic retries.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/998
**Planned against:** `main` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442` (planned branch `cb/issue-998-scheduler-wait-reasons`)
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Source contract: the issue body's Acceptance and the [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/998#issuecomment-6177413669) acceptance criteria and out-of-scope list. Consistency pattern: #950, #984, #987 (PR #993, `b3188184`).

### Approach

Keep waits a read-side projection (as #993 decided). Move the two scheduler-only checks in `StandaloneService.attemptRequest`'s `validateAssignment` closure into two public service predicates that the closure and `OperatorApi` both call, so the read and the scheduler cannot drift and admission is unchanged. Feed them into `deriveWaits` as new facts, add held assignments as wait candidates, and extend the shared `WaitCode`/Fix/link schema once so server, CLI, task detail and Inbox pick the new codes up in one order.

Dispositions:

| Cause | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `repository-access-revoked` | New wait `repository-access-revoked` ("Repository access revoked"), task-level, Fix `open-repositories` (projectId) → web `/app/projects/<projectId>/settings?tab=github`, CLI `project sources` / `prepare-source` / `apply`. No `detail` (no repository path or name is disclosed). |
| `recovery-continuation-unresolved` | New wait `assignment-recovery-unresolved` ("Assignment recovery unresolved"), no Fix, `detail` = assignment profile name (as #993), one link of new kind `recovery` (assignmentId, label "Open recovery") → web `/app/assignments/<id>/recovery`, CLI `Recovery: ensemble recovery get <id>`. Opening the page or running `recovery get` releases nothing. |
| `assignment-held` without a queued request (failed reporting repair) | Existing `assignment-held` wait; a `held` assignment becomes a wait candidate whatever its last request. |
| Revision-only refusal (e.g. `task-revision-changed`) | Intentionally no wait. The refused request is the assignment's current request in state `held`, so the task read already reports `execution.state: "uncertain"` with reason code `recovery-held`; clearing it is a recovery/fresh-operator-message decision, which a wait Fix must not imply. Documented in SPEC and pinned by a test. |
| Any other reason | Unchanged `admission-blocked` fallback. |

### Guardrails

- Admission eligibility, scheduler outcomes, refusal/hold reasons and their stored text are unchanged: the extracted predicates must return exactly what the closure computed (`recovery-continuation-unresolved` appended before `repository-access-revoked`, same inputs). Existing `test/delivery/github-review-regressions.test.ts` and `test/execution/recovery-continuation.test.ts` scheduler assertions must pass unmodified.
- Out of scope (brief): changing admission eligibility, rebinding stale work, granting repository access, releasing recovery holds, automatic retries. No new Fix sends a command; `open-repositories` and the `recovery` link only navigate. No List/Board change: at `812ecfeb` `taskListSummarySchema` carries no waits (List/Board render admission reasons and attention), so they are untouched; adding waits to list summaries is a contract change outside this ticket.
- Redaction and dedup: profile names only through `OperatorApi.exact` (omitted, never `null`, when excluded); the repository wait has no `detail`; `orderWaits` keeps first-per-code; unmapped reasons still become `admission-blocked`.
- Do not parse the queued request's `Admission waiting: …` reason text as a fact source; read live facts through the shared predicates.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Ordinary implementation defects — integration wiring, test, fixture, documentation, lint/format and CI repairs — stay with the ticket owner and do not consume any plan-mismatch budget. Only a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example: a predicate cannot reproduce the closure's result from stored state, `schedulerStore.current` does not return the refused held request, or the revision-only refusal is not reported as `uncertain`/`recovery-held`) counts as a factual plan mismatch: it allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; then stop and return a replan report. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Shared predicates, not string parsing or duplication.** The scheduler reasons are only persisted as free text on the queued request (`state.begin` writes `Admission waiting: <reasons>`), which is stale until the next attempt and mixes in other text. Extracting the checks keeps one implementation; the scheduler keeps calling them inside `validateAssignment`.
- **Repository revocation is task-level.** The scheduler compares the task's workspace binding repositories with the project's linked repositories for an imported task; it does not depend on the assignment. The read uses the stored binding (`workspaceBindings.get(taskId)`), whose `repositories` are the same rows `workspaces.forExecution` returns. It shows for any open task where the predicate holds, like `power-held`, not gated on execution state.
- **Order.** `repository-access-revoked` sits after `power-held` and before the assignment waits; `assignment-recovery-unresolved` after `assignment-held`, before `local-dependency`.
- **Recovery link, not Fix.** The brief requires recovery to stay visibly held with links that do not release ownership; the existing assignment recovery page and `recovery get` are read entry points. A new link kind is the smallest schema addition that reaches them.
- **Revision-only refusal hidden** — evidence: `StandaloneService.attemptRequest` refuses with `immutableRevisionMismatches` (includes `task-revision-changed`), `StateStore.begin` holds the request; `SchedulerStore.current` returns the latest request for the assignment version (the held one); `OperatorApi.execution` sets `uncertain` + `recovery-held` when a selection's request is `held`. The one-argument `assignmentAdmission` reports no reason for it, so no assignment wait appears.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` — `waitCodes`, `waitFixSchema`, `waitLinkSchema`, `waitLabels`, `fixLabels`, `WaitFacts`, `assignmentReasonWaits`, `deriveWaits`, `cliFix`; the single shared contract used by server, CLI and web (`src/operator/contracts.ts` bounds waits by `waitCodes.length`).

CLI Fix lines: `ensemble project sources <projectId>`, `ensemble project prepare-source <projectId> --out source.json --edit-file EDIT_FILE`, `ensemble project apply --file source.json`. Web `open-repositories` → `/app/projects/<projectId>/settings?tab=github`; `recovery` link → `/app/assignments/<assignmentId>/recovery`.

#### 2. Collect the facts on the task read; pin the revision-only disposition

"")`; `taskWaits` passes `repositoryAccessRevoked: service.repositoryAccessRevoked(taskId)`).

#### 3. Task detail presentation and documentation

### Acceptance coverage
