content.title: Fix remaining frame-callback focus races and stale restart copy

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Move focus after the relevant React commit and make runtime recovery copy match the available controls.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, an isolated Chromium production-bundle fixture aborted a runtime-toggle write. The UI showed an unknown outcome and “Check whether it saved”, disabled the switch, and left `document.activeElement` on BODY after the frame callback. Focus did not reach the reconciliation action. Existing unavailable-runtime browser checks also confirm the restart-only alert. Static inspection found the remaining local-review and auxiliary-request frame callbacks, but adverse frame/React-commit ordering was not reproduced; those races remain unproved and need targeted regression tests.

**Desired behavior:** Deferred focus belongs to the current surface and action. Local-review add/edit/remove/cancel/close and auxiliary-request reconciliation focus their intended mounted, enabled target after the state update commits. An unknown runtime-toggle outcome focuses “Check whether it saved”, preserving the exact original command for reconciliation. Runtime alerts and task wait guidance explain off/on recovery for an unavailable enabled runtime, enabling a disabled runtime, or installing a missing binary as applicable.

**Key interfaces:** Local-review deferred focus/close helpers; post-render draft revision callbacks; task auxiliary-request reconciliation; runtime-toggle outcome control; shared runtime status and recovery copy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] The listed focus paths work when tests force animation-frame callbacks before the React commit.
- [ ] Unknown toggle outcomes focus the reconciliation action; successful/refused outcomes restore a valid target. Reconciliation keeps the same command identity and never sends a second logical change.
- [ ] Unmount, navigation, authentication scope changes or superseding actions cannot focus stale/disconnected controls.
- [ ] Shell, task waits, profile/runtime settings and shared recovery text give cause-appropriate guidance consistent with runtime enablement.
- [ ] Chromium and WebKit coverage protects focus and unknown outcomes, with pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing runtime admission/drain behavior, replacing execution recovery, releasing holds, restyling the UI or a general focus-management rewrite.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/997
**Planned against:** `main` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442` (planned branch `cb/issue-997-focus-races-copy`)
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Requirements: issue body and agent brief [comment 6177512162](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/997#issuecomment-6177512162) (acceptance criteria A1–A5 below are its five checkboxes, in order). Baseline: trusted CI `CI` run on `812ecfeb` passed all jobs (`check`, `quality`, operator/execution/workspaces/integrations/service shards); baseline is not rerun locally.

### Approach

Reuse the #974 pattern (`ConfigurationDraft.revision` / `committed` / `afterRender`, wired by `useDraft`'s `useEffect(() => d.committed(revision))`) instead of focusing on `requestAnimationFrame`:

- Local review: give `LocalReviewState` the same revision/commit gate (small shared class) and move `focusLater` / `closeComposer` focus behind `afterRender`.
- Auxiliary-request replay (`task-workspace.tsx`): request the focus in a ref and apply it in a post-commit `useEffect`, the same ref+effect shape as the file's existing `focusUnconfirmed` / `sent` / `checking` refs.
- Runtime toggle (`recovery.tsx`): an unknown outcome passes `focus` to the existing `ActionOutcome` (autofocus on its action), and every other settled outcome restores the switch from a post-commit effect.
- Copy: change operator-facing text (shell alert, wait guidance, profile note, server-rendered runtime page, docs) to name the cause-specific recovery. The persisted wait-reason string is changed last, in its own separable task.

### Guardrails

- Out of scope (brief): runtime admission/drain behaviour, execution recovery, releasing holds, restyling, a general focus-management rewrite. Do not touch `ConfigurationDraft` / `settings-state.ts` / `settings.tsx` (the precedent stays as is), `web/src/wait-reasons.tsx`, `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts`, `src/cli/task-write.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/user-flows/first-task.md`, `web/src/task-files.tsx`, `web/src/task-detail.css`, and `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (other in-flight tickets).
- Other `requestAnimationFrame` focus sites are not listed in the issue and stay unchanged: `task-workspace.tsx` `ask` (~L1032, `#workspace-reply` is always mounted) and the `showSection` scroll (~L1583), `task-files.tsx`, `search.tsx`, `app.tsx`, `task-detail.tsx`.
- Reconciliation keeps the exact original command/key: never build a new command, key or request in any change here. The runtime toggle's `retry` closure and local review's `check()` replay stay as they are.
- Keep restart advice where restart is the true recovery: Claude token `restart-required` notices (`service.ts` L963/L983, `readiness.ts`, `failureNotice`'s `unauthorized` copy), `readiness.ts` messages and `docs/user-flows/readiness-check.md` rows other than "Runtime harness".
- Mismatch budget. A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example, a symbol/file/call flow named here that does not exist or behaves differently, such as `LocalReviewProvider` not committing together with the focus targets) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; if a third is needed, stop and return for replanning. Ordinary implementation defects (integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs, snapshot/string expectations, flaky waits, formatting) stay with the ticket owner, are recorded briefly in the delivery record, and do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. An integration amendment is only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Seam.** The #974 `afterRender` pattern is the repository precedent; `ConfigurationDraft` cannot be reused directly because `LocalReviewState` is not a draft. A new ~15-line `CommitGate` (`revision`, `changed()`, `committed(n)`, `afterRender(run)`, `discard()`) is copied from that logic rather than extracted from `ConfigurationDraft`, to avoid changing the precedent's public `revision`/`committed` API and its tests (`test/operator/operator-settings-state.test.ts` ~L949).
- **Why `afterRender`, not "after notify".** `settle` calls `state.notify()` and then `focusLater`, but `write()` clears `state.pending` and notifies again afterwards, so the controls are re-enabled only by the later commit. `afterRender` waits for the latest announced revision, which covers that second notify (both run in microtasks before React's scheduled commit).
- **Stale focus.** `LocalReviewState.subscribe`'s unsubscribe discards queued callbacks when the last listener leaves (unmount/navigation). Callbacks re-query the DOM when they run and focus only a connected element, as today. `closeComposer` still returns without effect while `state.unconfirmed`. A superseding action is covered because callbacks read live state/DOM at run time and a new `write()` does not queue stale targets.
- **Aux replay.** Focus is applied in an effect that runs only when `!pending` (the Refresh button is also `disabled={Boolean(unconfirmed)}`; `state.unconfirmed` is already null in state before the DOM updates, which is the observed race). The ref is cleared when consumed and on `taskId` change; the early `if (!scope.current || !current()) return` after the command keeps unmounted/re-authenticated pages from queuing it.
- **Runtime toggle.** Verified at `812ecfeb`: after an unknown outcome the switch is disabled (`Boolean(outcome?.retry)`), so `control.current.focus()` can never succeed and `ActionOutcome focus` (autofocus on the action button, `action-feedback.tsx`) is the correct existing mechanism. `p.reload()`/`p.refresh()` after a recorded outcome can re-render the row, so success/refusal focus also waits for commit.
- **Copy scope and persisted reason.** The runtime wait copy lives in `web/src/execution-runtime.ts` `waitRoute` (guidance) and, for the verbatim reason, `src/standalone/service.ts` `runtimeWaitReason` (L1667); it is **not** in `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts`. The reason is persisted (`execution_intents.reason`, `turn_requests.reason`) and matched exactly by `waitRoute`, so T4 first makes `waitRoute` accept both the legacy and the new string, and T5 (separable, may be dropped or deferred without breaking T1–T4) flips the stored text. The new unavailable wording reuses `readiness.ts` L244/L325: "turn it off and on in Settings → Runtime, or restart the service". Off/on recovery of an unavailable runtime is established by `reconcileRuntime` (`service.ts` ~L1397: an enabled-but-unavailable runtime is replaced by a fresh one) and ADR-1012.
- **Cause mapping.** Unavailable (enabled, failed): turn off and on in Settings → Runtime. Not enabled (`... is not configured`, disabled or binary missing): turn on in Settings → Runtime; if enabling is refused, install `codex`/`claude` on the service PATH first (`executableMissingMessage`, ADR-1012). The wait reason does not distinguish disabled from missing binary, so the guidance states both steps.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/settings-state.ts` — `ConfigurationDraft.revision/committed/afterRender` (precedent); `web/src/settings.tsx` `useDraft` (`useEffect(() => d.committed(revision))`) and `sendDraft` (`d.afterRender(...)`); test precedent `test/operator/operator-setup-browser.test.ts` "Setup moves focus to the rejected path field even when frame callbacks run before the page commits" (replaces `window.requestAnimationFrame` with a microtask runner, restores it in `finally`, uses locator waits because `waitForFunction` polls with the replaced frames).
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace-state.ts` `LocalReviewState` — `notify()` calls listeners; `subscribe()`; `composer`, `pending`, `unconfirmed`. `web/src/local-review.tsx` — `useLocalReviewController` (`focusLater` L391, `closeComposer` L399; callers: `settle` `add` case L481, `edit` case L498/L500, `cancelEdit` L703, `close()` L617), `LocalReviewProvider` (L794; sole instance at `task-workspace.tsx` L1183, wraps the page content up to L2065; its parent's `changed` re-renders it).
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` — `command()` (~L760): unknown path sets `focusUnconfirmed`; replayed non-unknown path focuses `[data-unconfirmed-control="<type>"]` in an rAF (L836–845); controls at L1508 (`review.view`) and L2513 (`delivery.refresh`, `disabled={refreshDisabled}`, L1614 `Boolean(unconfirmed)`).
- **Existing:** `web/src/recovery.tsx` `RuntimeToggle` (L67–): `send()` ends with `setPending(false); requestAnimationFrame(() => control.current?.focus())`; unknown outcome sets `retry`, which disables the switch and renders `ActionOutcome action={{label:"Check whether it saved"}}`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/execution-runtime.ts` — `unavailableAlert` (shell alert; used by `app.tsx` ~L888 and `setup-model.ts` ~L291), `harnessReason`, `harnessNote` (profile settings, `profile-config.tsx`), `waitRoute` (task wait guidance, rendered by `execution-notice.tsx`); `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` L116 server-rendered `/runtime` alert.
- **New:** `web/src/commit-gate.ts` — `export class CommitGate`; owned by `LocalReviewState` as `readonly gate`.
- **Follow:** `web/src/settings-state.ts` `ConfigurationDraft.committed/afterRender`; `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` `focusUnconfirmed` ref reset effect (~L345).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic: T1, T2, T3 are roots; T4 depends on T3 (both edit `test/operator/operator-harness-status-browser.test.ts`); T5 depends on T4. T1, T2 and T3 touch disjoint source and test files and may run concurrently; T4 and T5 are sequential. Shared-file constraints with other tickets: T2 edits `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` only near L345 and L836 (#1005 edits ~L1352 brief rendering; hunks are disjoint but expect a trivial rebase); nothing here touches the #998 files listed in Guardrails. T5 is the only task touching `src/standalone/service.ts` (one line, ~L1667) and can be dropped to avoid that file without invalidating the others.

#### 1. Local review focuses after the commit

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** new `web/src/commit-gate.ts` (`CommitGate`); `web/src/task-workspace-state.ts` (`LocalReviewState.gate`, `notify()` calls `gate.changed()` before the listeners; `subscribe` unsubscribe calls `gate.discard()` when no listener remains; expose `committed(revision)`/`afterRender`/`revision` via `gate`); `web/src/local-review.tsx` (`focusLater`, `closeComposer` bodies; `LocalReviewProvider` adds `const revision = props.state.gate.revision; useEffect(() => props.state.gate.committed(revision))`); test file `test/workspaces/operator-local-review-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `operator-local-review-browser.test.ts` (seam: production bundle through `startReview`/`signIn`/`commentOnLine`, as "local review keeps focus on the selection, the next comment and the heading"), add `test("local review focus survives frame callbacks that run before the page commits", ...)`. After the three comments exist, replace `window.requestAnimationFrame` with the microtask runner from the Setup precedent (restore in `finally`) and, with locator waits only (no `waitForFunction`): (a) Add review comment then Escape/Cancel and Save: assert the origin line control (`[data-review-return]`) has focus; (b) Edit then Escape: `[data-review-edit]` button focused; (c) Edit, change text, Save: the Edit button for that comment focused and enabled; (d) Remove first/middle/last comment: neighbour `[data-comment-id]` focused, then `#local-review-heading`; assert `pageErrors` empty. Sensitivity check: revert `focusLater` to rAF locally and confirm (c)/(d) fail under the override. A second case: queue a focus (remove a comment with the response delayed by `page.route`), navigate client-side away before release, release, and assert focus is not moved to any control and `pageErrors` is empty (discard on unmount).
**Implementation:** `CommitGate`: `revision`, private `shown`, private callback list; `changed()` increments `revision`; `committed(n)` sets `shown = max(shown, n)` and runs/clears the queue only when `shown >= revision`; `afterRender(run)` runs at once when `shown >= revision`, else queues; `discard()` clears the queue. `focusLater(selector, fallback)` becomes `state.gate.afterRender(() => ...same query-and-focus...)`. `closeComposer`: same body inside `state.gate.afterRender`, keeping the `state.unconfirmed` early return and the live-control lookup. `cancelEdit` already notifies before `focusLater`. No behavioural change other than ordering. Check that `TaskFiles`/`Changes` (origin buttons) re-render with the page's `changed()` (no `React.memo` exists in `web/src`; `rg "memo\(" web/src` is empty at the planned SHA); if a child owns its own render path, report from that child instead of the Provider.
**Validate:** From the repo root, with `$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH` and after `npm run build`, run `node --test --test-name-pattern="frame callbacks|keeps focus on the selection" dist/test/workspaces/operator-local-review-browser.test.js`; expect the new test(s) and the existing focus test to pass; then `npm run typecheck`.
**Complete when:** Add/edit/remove/cancel/close focus the intended enabled target under forced frame-before-commit ordering, and unmount queues nothing.

#### 2. Auxiliary-request replay focuses after the commit

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` (`command()` replayed branch L836–845; new `focusReplay` ref beside `focusUnconfirmed` (~L236); a post-commit `useEffect` next to the effect at ~L345); test file `test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** The existing unknown-outcome journey is one long test (`production workspace retains literal history, ...`, ~L22–787; it drops the `review.view` and `delivery.refresh` responses at ~L495–570 and clicks "Check whether it saved"). Add a separate `test("a replayed auxiliary request focuses its control after the page commits", ...)` that reuses the same fixture helpers (`createOperatorFixture`, `seedReviewTask`, the route-drop pattern) and installs the microtask `requestAnimationFrame` override before the replay click and asserts, with locator waits, that after a successful replay `[data-unconfirmed-control="review.view"]` (then `delivery.refresh`) is the active element and enabled; assert the replay body equals the original (same key) and exactly one logical change. Add a case where the page is left (navigate to another route) while the replay response is delayed: no page error and focus does not jump to a control of the new page. Sensitivity check: restore the rAF code and confirm the delivery.refresh case fails (it is disabled until `unconfirmed` renders null).
**Implementation:** Replace the rAF with `focusReplay.current = input.type` (only when `replayed`) — the following `changed()` is already called at the end of the `!reply` branch. New effect (no deps, runs every commit): if `focusReplay.current` and `!pending`, clear it and focus `[data-unconfirmed-control="${type}"]`; also clear it in the existing reset effect when `taskId` changes. The early return `if (!scope.current || !current()) return` already prevents queuing after unmount or authentication-scope change; add no new guards.
**Validate:** From the repo root, after `npm run build`, run `node --test --test-name-pattern="replayed auxiliary|production workspace retains" dist/test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.js`; expect the new test and the existing journey pass; then `npm run typecheck`.

#### 3. Unknown runtime-toggle outcomes focus the check; other outcomes restore the switch

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/recovery.tsx` (`Outcome.focus?: boolean`; `send()`; `RuntimeToggle` effect + `restore` ref; `<ActionOutcome focus={outcome.focus}>`); test file `test/operator/operator-harness-status-browser.test.ts`.

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Make source activation's outcome and import next step visible.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, an isolated Chromium production-bundle fixture showed `Saved.` after both the first source preview/activation and a repeat. Source observations stayed `never`/“Not synced”, with no already-active marker or direct contextual import action. The generic shell Refresh and installation-wide observation request remain available elsewhere. This confirms the ambiguous activation feedback while preserving the existing distinction between activation and import; it used a fake provider rather than live GitHub.

**Desired behavior:** A confirmed activation names its selection and explains that tasks are imported by refreshing source observations. Offer a direct Refresh action or link. Show active state in the selection control and observation rows; reactivating a currently active selection says it was already active. Use the current selection/configuration version and authoritative readback rather than inferring success or activation from a click.

**Key interfaces:** Source preview/activation command receipts and live activation state; `DraftOutcome`/shared action feedback; Sync selection controls and source-observation rows.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] First activation reports the selection and the refresh/import next step with an accessible action/link.
- [ ] Repeat activation reports already-active status for the current version, without claiming that a refresh or import occurred.
- [ ] Selection controls and observation rows consistently identify active selections; configuration changes invalidate old activation markers correctly.
- [ ] Unknown/refused/conflicting outcomes preserve existing drafts, reconciliation and exact-request identity; an old successful receipt does not falsely claim current activation.
- [ ] Browser tests cover first/repeat activation, the refresh entry point and current-version/readback behavior. Preserve server, CLI and fallback activation semantics.
- [ ] Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** The optional combined “Activate and refresh” action, automatic imports, changing readiness rules, or treating activation as proof of successful sync.

**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1004 **Planned against:** `cb/issue-1004-activation-feedback` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null Source contract: the issue body plus [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1004#issuecomment-6177514960) (acceptance criteria AC1-AC6 below follow the brief's checklist in order). CI on the exact base SHA passed (run 38621969701, `CI`/push/main); the focused file `dist/test/operator/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.js` also passed locally at the base (21/21). ### Approach Web-only change; the server, CLI, fallback HTML page and `github.preview` receipt are untouched. The Sync tab already receives authoritative active state: `projectConfigurationSchema.source.selections[].active` is read from `githubActiveSelectionIds(projectId)`, which filters `project_github_active` by the *current* source `configVersion`, so a source save invalidates old markers on the next read. The web UI never uses it on this tab. 1. Snapshot, at save time, whether the selection was already active (read from the loaded configuration) into the session's `SavedRecord`, and add a pure `activationLine` that turns that record plus the current read into the success sentence. 2. Show `active`/`inactive` in the "Selection to preview" options and a badge on each Source observations row, both from the configuration read. 3. Replace the generic "Saved." for `github.preview` with that sentence and put a "Refresh source observations" button inside the same success outcome (one outcome message stays the contract). The button calls the existing `client.refreshSources` then re-reads observations. ### Guardrails - Unchanged: server, CLI (`src/cli/source.ts`), fallback HTML (`src/standalone/operator.ts`), `src/operator/contracts.ts`, command/receipt shapes, `github.preview`->`github.activate` mapping, the `matchesConfigurationReceipt` check, exact-request replay, conflict/refused/unknown handling and draft preservation. Activation never claims a refresh, import or sync occurred, and the activation line never changes on a refresh. - Out of scope: the optional "Activate and refresh" action (decision: **out**. The brief lists it under Out of scope, and combining the two would make the receipt for activation imply a sync it does not prove; the in-outcome Refresh button gives the operator the one-step path without that coupling), automatic imports, readiness rules, project state card "Next step" text, task-detail source lines. - Success copy is only claimed from a confirmed `github.preview` receipt whose `configVersion` equals the currently loaded `source.version`. Never infer activation from the click. - Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. **Plan-seam budget:** a *wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption* (for example `source.selections[].active` not being version-scoped, `SavedRecord` not surviving `startOperation`, `DraftMessage` `children` not rendering in the success branch, `refreshSources` not importing active selections) gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; if still wrong, stop and report for replan. **Ordinary implementation defects** (integration wiring, test, fixture, documentation, formatting, lint and CI repairs, updating the `Saved.` expectations in existing tests) stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants. ### Planning decisions - **Already-active comes from the loaded read, captured at submit.** The receipt does not say whether the selection was active before (activation is an idempotent upsert), so `wasActive` is read from `data.source.selections` when the form is submitted and stored with the save. This is authoritative for the version being activated; the residual gap (another actor activated the same selection at the same version after this page loaded) reads as "Activated" rather than "already active" and is accepted. - **Where it is stored:** `ConfigurationDraft.set` before `submitDraft` (the `github.place` form does the same with `placementTitle`) and a `values` snapshot added to `SavedRecord` in `ConfigurationDrafts.get`'s `onSaved`. Draft values do not survive `startOperation` after a recorded save, but `savedRecords` does and is also what the unknown->Check->recorded path writes, so first/repeat/Check all read one source. `savedLine` and `add-claude` use `SavedRecord.at`/`receipt` only and stay valid. - **Stale claims:** `DraftMessage` already drops the confirmation when a re-read loads another `expectedVersion`; `activationLine` additionally returns `null` when `receipt.configVersion !== source.version` and, after the re-read, requires `selection.active` in the read (otherwise a plain "Couldn't confirm that S-1 is active. Preview it again." line with no Refresh action). `success: null` is the existing way for `DraftMessage` to render nothing. - **Refresh action is a button, not a link.** The brief allows either; a button makes a first-time setup one click from the confirmation. It is a small self-contained component in `sync-placement.tsx` using `client.refreshSources` + `observations.refresh()` and its own pending/status text, deliberately *not* a shared hook with `SourceObservations`, to keep that function's hunks separate from #1002. Duplicated strings can be consolidated after #1002 lands. Its label is "Refresh source observations"; the existing "Request installation-wide source observations" button keeps its exact name (several tests locate it). - **Copy** (from the brief's example; no "recorded/receipt/revision/version", which `savedOutcome` rejects): - first: `Activated S-1. Tasks aren't imported until you refresh source observations.` - repeat: `S-1 was already active. Tasks aren't imported until you refresh source observations.` - Selection is named by its `S-` id. - **Design:** frames 118-121 in `design/DESIGN.md` do not draw an activation success line or an in-outcome action. The brief's copy and "direct Refresh action" are the authority; no `.pen` change is needed. Record it as a production deviation in `design/DESIGN.md` (hand-edited text only; no MCP refresh because no frame changes). - Selection options read `S-1 (GitHub Project) · active` / `· inactive`; the observation row gets a second `StatusBadge` ("Active"/"Inactive") and its existing sentence `{id}: {state}. Newest attempt...` is left unchanged because tests match it. ### Implementation context - **Existing:** `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` — `SyncTab` builds the `github.preview:${projectId}` draft (`useDraft`, `useLoadedDraft`), the "Selection to preview" `DraftField` options, `` with no `success`; `SourceObservations` renders per-selection rows from `p.observations` and the "Request installation-wide source observations" button. - **Existing:** `web/src/settings.tsx` — `DraftMessage` renders `success ?? "Saved."` plus `children` inside `ActionOutcome` only in the recorded/re-read branch; `DraftOutcome` forwards `success` but not `children`. - **Existing:** `web/src/settings-state.ts` — `ConfigurationDraft.send` calls `onSaved(receipt)` then sets `savedAt`; `startOperation(values, true)` keeps `savedAt`/`details` only if `details.version` equals the re-read `expectedVersion`; `ConfigurationDrafts.get` creates drafts with `onSaved` writing `savedRecords`; `SavedRecord { at, receipt }`. - **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` (read only) — `github.preview` receipt `{resourceId, selectionId, configVersion, active: true}`; `projectConfigurationSchema.source.selections[].active`; `sourceObservationSchema` rows keyed by `selectionId`. - **Existing:** `web/src/settings-view.ts` — `selectionLine`, `observationLabel`, `savedLine`, `ProjectConfigurationData` helpers; `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts` — `startSettings(..., { readerFactory })`, `savedOutcome(scope, text)` (asserts exactly one `[data-slot="action-outcome"]` and no service words), `outcomeMessages`. - **New:** `web/src/settings-view.ts` — `activationLine({ receipt, wasActive, sourceVersion, selection, recorded })` returns `string | null` per the table in T1. - **New:** `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` — `RefreshObservations` (button + status text) rendered as the outcome's `children` only when `activationLine` returned a claim. - **Follow:** `sync-placement.tsx` `PlacementConfiguration` (`d.set("placementTitle", ...)` then `submitDraft`, `success={placedLine(d)}`) for the pre-submit capture and custom success line. ### Implementation slices **Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic: T1 (root), T2 (root), T3 depends on T1. T1 and T2 touch different files and may run concurrently. T2 and T3 both edit `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` and `test/operator/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.ts`, so run T2 then T3 (or one owner) even though T3 does not logically need T2. All three share one PR. #### 1. Save-time snapshot and activation sentence **Task ID:** `T1` **Depends on:** `none` **Prerequisites:** none **Files and symbols:** `web/src/settings-state.ts` (`SavedRecord`, `ConfigurationDraft` constructor `onSaved`, the `this.onSaved(this.receipt)` call in `send`, `ConfigurationDrafts.get`); `web/src/settings-view.ts` (new `activationLine`); `test/operator/operator-settings-state.test.ts`; `test/operator/operator-settings-presentation.test.ts`. **Test:** (a) state test next to the existing `drafts.saved(...)` test (~L600-625): set `draft.set("wasActive", true)` before `submit`; after `recorded`, `drafts.saved(key)?.values.wasActive === true` and the snapshot is unchanged after `draft.startOperation({...})`. (b) presentation test for `activationLine` with a hand-built `github.preview` receipt (`configVersion: 3`, `selectionId: "S-1"`): first -> `Activated S-1. Tasks aren't imported until you refresh source observations.`; `wasActive: true` -> `S-1 was already active. ...same sentence...`; `sourceVersion: 4` -> `null`; not `recorded` and selection `active: false` -> `Couldn't confirm that S-1 is active. Preview it again.`; not `recorded` and `active: true` -> claim; receipt of another `commandType` -> `null`. **Implementation:** `onSaved(receipt, values)` is passed `{ ...this.values }` at the call in `send`; `SavedRecord` gains `values: Record`; `ConfigurationDrafts.get` stores it. `activationLine` is pure and only reads its arguments. content.title: Add a per-source setting for closed GitHub issues: skip them or treat closure as Done

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Give each GitHub source an explicit closed-issue policy, keeping provider closure distinguishable from Ensemble-delivered completion.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, a production-service/SQLite fixture imported a first-observed closed issue as a local open, unready task with closed source provenance. The current task-column projection places this in Draft. A ready imported issue that closed stayed open/unready with a `closed` source hold; reopening restored source state/readiness but retained that hold. No closed-issue mode exists. These are fake-provider service observations and static column inspection, not a live provider/browser or active-turn stopping proof.

**Desired behavior:** Implement the issue's two modes: **Skip closed issues** by default; **Treat closure as Done** as an explicit source-level override. Keep completion provenance, task identity and history. Provider state never resolves uncertain execution or releases independent holds.

**Key interfaces:** Versioned GitHub source configuration; stored provider observations and import identity; source closure/readiness reconciliation; task completion origin and safe execution settlement; reopening; web/HTML/CLI source settings and task state views.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Existing and new sources default to Skip closed issues. Changing the mode is a versioned, keyed configuration change.
- [ ] Skip mode creates no task for a first-observed closed issue. A task imported while open remains retained when its issue closes, with a visible closed-source hold rather than Draft/Ready/ordinary Waiting.
- [ ] Done mode imports a first-observed closed issue as Done. For existing work, record provider-origin completion only after admitted execution reaches a proven safe stopping point; retain unresolved writer/capacity/Stop/uncertainty holds.
- [ ] Completion explicitly identifies provider closure rather than successful Ensemble delivery. Do not conflate independent/manual completion or cancellation with provider-origin completion.
- [ ] The next refresh re-evaluates existing imported tasks after a mode change, without deleting tasks/history or treating incomplete provider observations as closure.
- [ ] Reopening restores the normal readiness flow in both modes and reopens provider-completed tasks. Reconcile the closure-specific disposition without clearing independent holds or silently granting readiness.
- [ ] Web source settings, HTML fallback and CLI expose the mode; List, Board, detail and CLI task views agree on state/provenance.
- [ ] Cover first-observed closed, closure after import, safe settlement, reopening, mode switch and incomplete observations. Coordinate stored skipped observations with #1002's counts.
- [ ] Amend SPEC's closure/admission/completion contract and affected design/documentation; run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Deleting imported history, automatic force-unlock, changing native blocker authority, a new generic task workflow state or interpreting closure as verified result delivery.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1006
**Planned against:** `main` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442`
**Planned branch:** `cb/issue-1006-closed-issue-mode`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Requirements: the issue body's acceptance criteria and the [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1006#issuecomment-6177458338). The maintainer decision in the issue body is the accepted contract: two modes per GitHub source, default **Skip closed issues**, and **Treat closure as Done** as an explicit per-source override of SPEC.md:501-502.

### Approach

Add a `closedIssues: "skip" | "done"` field to the versioned GitHub source configuration (`project_github_sources`), next to `readiness`. Apply the mode in the core provider reconciliation (`GitHubSourceStore`):

- Skip mode does not import an issue that is closed when first observed.
- An issue that closes after import puts its open task under a `closed` source hold, in both modes.
- Done mode imports an issue first observed closed directly as Done, with a provider-completion record.
- Reopening reverses a provider completion.

Done mode completes an existing task only through a service-level finalizer. The finalizer runs after each GitHub refresh. It completes the task in one SQLite transaction, and only when the established execution-settlement predicate holds. Expose a single `closure` provenance field (`held | completed | null`) in the task list/read projections. Web List/Board/detail, the HTML fallback and the CLI all render from that field. Expose the mode in the web source settings, the HTML fallback form and the CLI. Amend SPEC and the affected design docs.

### Guardrails

- Provider closure never resolves uncertain execution and never clears writer, ambiguity, archival, operator-Stop, capacity or independent source holds. Provider reopening never grants readiness. Readiness still comes only from the source rule. A `closed` hold still needs the existing operator `source.review` → `resume-source-hold` resolution (SPEC.md:219-221). The only exception remains confirmed own-delivery closure (`DomainStore.hasOwnDeliveryClosure`). Its flows (`recordDeliveryClosure`, `reconcileOwnDeliveryClosures`, completion continuation) stay unchanged and never produce a provider-completion record.
- Never delete tasks, memberships, task history, reviews or holds because of the mode or a mode switch. Manual operator completion/cancellation (`task.configure` state) and Ensemble completion (`coordination.ts` finalization) never write a provider-completion record. Reopening never changes them.
- An absent, partial or unknown provider observation is never closure. A first-observed closed issue from an incomplete selection snapshot is not imported in either mode. Done-mode completion of an existing task requires complete current-version membership evidence.
- Out of scope: a new generic task workflow state, deleting imported history, automatic force-unlock, changing native blocker authority, treating closure as verified result delivery, persisting skipped closed issues, editing `design/design.pen`, and the paused X01–X08 work.
- `src/core` stays host-independent (ADR-1003). Core never queries standalone execution tables. The service injects the settlement predicate.
- Delivery uses `npm ci` and `npm run check` on the pinned Node (`.node-version` 24.21.0). Tests run against real SQLite and the fake runtime/provider fixtures. Name tests by behaviour and place them by the AGENTS.md grouping.
- Plan-mismatch budget versus ordinary repairs:
  - **Plan mismatch:** a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption. Examples: the settlement predicate cannot reach Done because the closure hold leaves a permanently queued intent, a named symbol or file does not own the stated behaviour, or a migration pattern does not apply. This gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles under to-plan's allowance. After that, stop and report for replanning.
  - **Ordinary defects:** integration, test, fixture, documentation, type/lint and CI repairs. These stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.
  - Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record each correction and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Storage:** add the mode as a column, `closedIssues TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'skip' CHECK(closedIssues IN ('skip','done'))`, on `project_github_sources`. Follow the `PRAGMA table_info` + `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` pattern at `src/core/domain.ts:548-588`. Existing rows read as `skip` and no data is rewritten (additive, reversible). Do not fold the mode into the `readiness` JSON. #1001 is changing that default independently.
- **Command contract:** in the stored/result `githubConfigurationSchema` the field is required (`closedIssuesSchema = z.enum(["skip","done"])`). In `githubConfigurationCommandSchema` it is optional, and omitted means "keep the saved mode". This matches the CLI's `edit.readiness ?? source.readiness` keep semantics. Older receipts, replays and clients then cannot silently reset a Done-mode source. Changing only the mode is a normal keyed, versioned `github.configure`: it bumps `version` and invalidates source evidence through the existing handler, exactly like a readiness change. Re-evaluation happens on the next refresh of the reactivated selections under the existing activation flow.
- **Closure hold for any post-import closure:** today `updateReadiness` sets the `closed` hold only when a Ready task loses readiness. An unready task that closes stays in Draft. Set the `closed` hold whenever an imported open task observes `observedState='closed'` without own-delivery closure, whatever its prior readiness. This also covers legacy first-observed-closed tasks that are already imported. They are retained, become `closure: held`, and need the existing operator resolution after a reopen.
  - Precedence follows `recordDeliveryClosure`: set or keep `closed` when no hold is active, or the active hold is `closed`, `withdrawn`, `readiness-lost` or `closure-read-unavailable`.
  - Keep an active `changed-text` hold, because its text review is stricter.
- **Provider completion record:** create a provider-owned table `github_provider_completions(taskId PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES domain_tasks(id), nodeId NOT NULL, completedAt TEXT NOT NULL)` in `GitHubSourceStore.migrate`. A task is provider-completed only while `domain_tasks.state='done'` and this row exists. Any `task.configure` state change deletes the row; guard with the existing `sqlite_master` table-presence pattern. This keeps provenance out of `domain_tasks`, which #1001/#1003 also touch.
- **Reopen semantics:** an issue observed open again behaves as follows:
  - If it has a provider-completion row, it reverts to `open` and the row is deleted.
  - Readiness is recomputed from the rule.
  - Holds are untouched. A task completed by provider closure *after* import keeps its `closed` hold and needs the existing operator resume, exactly as in Skip mode. A Done-mode task imported already-closed never had a hold, so it simply enters the normal readiness flow.
- **Mode switches:** each re-evaluates on the next refresh.
  - Skip→Done: open closure-held tasks complete through the finalizer once settled. Previously skipped issues import as Done on the next complete read.
  - Done→Skip: provider-completed tasks revert to `open` with a `closed` hold, because the SPEC override no longer applies to that source. Their history is retained.
- **Safe stopping point:** the service finalizer uses the existing archival settlement predicate `archiveUnblockedClause` (`src/standalone/state.ts:398`). It requires no writer hold (including operator Stop), no writer-ambiguity hold, and no unrefused bound intent in `ready|capacity-waiting|held|submitting|running`. Expose it as `ExecutionState.taskExecutionSettled(taskId)` and inject it into the core call, so the check and the state change share one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction (`src/core/store.ts:17`, not nestable). The existing `closed` source hold already blocks new admission and drives `emitSourceHoldNotices`, which notifies the lead and assignees to stop safely. Assumption to prove in T3: a hold notice queued for a held task does not leave an unsettleable intent. If T3's test shows it does, that is a plan mismatch under Guardrails.
- **Projection:** add `closure: z.enum(["held","completed"]).nullable()` to `taskSourceSummarySchema` (list) and to the task-read `source` object (`src/operator/contracts.ts`).
  - `completed`: `state='done'` and a provider-completion row exists.
  - `held`: `state='open'`, `observedState='closed'`, and no own-delivery closure.
  - Otherwise null.
  - The existing `hold.reasonCode` stays unchanged.
- **Board placement:** a `held` task goes in **Paused**, so never Draft/Ready/Waiting. A `completed` task goes in **Done** with a "Closed on GitHub" fact.
  - Evidence: DESIGN.md:334 and :392 already draw provider closure without delivery as "provider-closed/Ensemble-paused" (`ALMfc`), and the Paused column precedes Draft in the documented priority (docs/design/ui03-tasks.md:41).
  - This adds one documented exception to ui03's "Source status never determines grouping".
  - Copy: held reason "Closed on GitHub"; completed fact "Closed on GitHub, not delivered by Ensemble"; detail header `Paused · closed on GitHub` and `Done · closed on GitHub`.
  - DESIGN.md has no node for a provider-completed Done card or for the source-settings mode control. Reuse the existing Done mark/fact line and the existing Readiness-panel `<select>` pattern. Do not edit `design.pen`, and leave DESIGN.md unchanged because no design node changes.
- **No skipped-observation store:** skipped closed issues are not persisted, because they are re-read each refresh and import when first seen open (or as Done after a switch). #1002's counts derive from `github_external_issues`, so they count imported issues only. #1002 owns its count labels.

### Implementation context

#### 3. Service finalizer: Done only after a safe stopping point

### Acceptance coverage

### Final validation

### Review focus

- The `completeFromProviderClosure` transaction re-verifies every condition and calls `settled()` inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. No path writes `state='done'` with a held or unfinished execution.

- T3 shows that a held task's queued source-hold notice or intent can never settle, so Done is unreachable. This is the plan-mismatch budget in Guardrails. If a fix would require changing hold-notice or admission semantics, stop for a decision.
