content.title: Stabilise native-input live-harness budgets under CI load

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Make native-input qualification fixtures tolerate CI runner load while keeping deadline enforcement deterministic.

**Current behavior and verification:** The protocol fixture gives ordinary execution 450 ms of its 600 ms total budget; service fixtures also share tight wall-clock budgets with setup and cleanup. The [failed node26-service-1 job](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/actions/runs/38598557210/job/115971897166) confirms three failures: `async-after-confirmed` timed out instead of detecting unsupported async input, and two cleanup-boundary cases failed before reaching their intended boundary, including `provision-deadline`. Later cited runs currently show successful latest attempts. On main `812ecfeb`, the existing native-input harness, power and wait-reason suites passed together with Node 24.21.0. Local passing tests do not reproduce or disprove CI contention; runner load remains the reported cause, rather than a measured causal conclusion from this triage.

**Desired behavior:** Separate tests of protocol/service behavior from tests of deadline semantics. Successful behavior cases must have bounded headroom for fixture startup, provisioning and cleanup under the supported CI profiles. Each budget must retain a deterministic enforcement test whose outcome does not depend on incidental machine speed.

**Key interfaces:** Native-input protocol/service proof budget validation, fixture startup and cleanup deadlines, and CI runtime-profile selection. Production live-proof grants and finite caps retain their authority.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Behavioral cases reach and assert their intended protocol, provisioning or cleanup boundary under runner load.
- [ ] Request, total, provisioning/startup and cleanup budgets retain applicable deterministic enforcement coverage.
- [ ] Invalid/unbounded budgets still fail before execution; uncertain cleanup still retains evidence and ownership.
- [ ] Report a finite repeated CI sample for the affected Node 24 execution and Node 26 service lanes, with run links, repetitions and failures. Do not substitute an indefinite “never flakes” guarantee or hide failures through blanket retries.
- [ ] Run the pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`, plus the affected CI profiles.

**Out of scope:** Raising production live-execution grants, weakening protocol/cleanup assertions, broad test-runner redesign or additional model evaluations.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/996
**Planned against:** `main` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Change only `test/execution/native-input-live-harness.test.ts`. Split its budgets into two kinds:

- **Behaviour budgets.** Cases that assert a protocol, provisioning, replay, settings or cleanup result get one generous but finite budget set. These cases stop as soon as they reach their asserted boundary, so the larger budget only covers slow runners. It does not make a passing case take longer.
- **Enforcement budgets.** Each deadline-semantics case gets its own budget set. The fixture stalls forever at the target boundary, so only the targeted deadline can end the run. Every other budget gets large headroom, so it cannot fire first. Wall-clock assertions measure from the stalled boundary, plus a fixed allowance for timer latency. They do not measure the whole run's speed.

The harness modules, fake fixtures, production live bounds and grant limits stay unchanged.

### Guardrails

- Do not edit `test/execution/native-input-qualification/{runtime-contract,service-contract,fake-app-server,native-runtime-fixture}.mjs`. Their `bounds`/`limits` caps (request ≤ 90 000, total ≤ 240 000, hold ≤ 250, cleanup ≤ 10 000 ms) and live fixed-budget rules stay authoritative. Every budget in this plan is within those caps. Do not change the production live budgets, `package.json` `native-input:live`, or the finite-grant test's limits.
- Keep every existing protocol, receipt, count, privacy, evidence-retention and cleanup-ownership assertion. Do not relax or delete any of them. The only assertions that change are the whole-run wall-clock bounds named in T1 and T2; boundary-relative bounds replace them. Tests may gain extra assertions, such as `failure.stage`.
- Do not use blanket retries, `test.skip`/`todo`, CI `retry` settings, lane moves, env-scaled multipliers, test-runner changes or `scripts/test-timings.json` refreshes. Hidden retries would hide failures. A lane move or multiplier adds machinery that this fix does not need.
- Out of scope: new fixture modes, new dedicated deadlines for the service request or provision stages (see Planning decisions), the paused X01–X08 work, and model or live evaluations.
- **Plan-mismatch budget vs ordinary repairs.** The approved seam is test-only budget separation in the one test file, against the unchanged harness. A wrong seam or a wrong repository assumption counts as a factual plan mismatch: one focused diagnosis, then at most two repair cycles, then stop and request a replan. Examples: a behaviour case still fails at its boundary under the load check even with behaviour budgets; meeting acceptance needs a harness or fixture edit; a cited symbol or behaviour does not exist. Ordinary implementation defects do not use that budget and stay with the ticket owner: integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs. Examples are typos, assertion details, lint or format fixes, test-timeout tuning, and CI infrastructure reruns. Record each routine correction in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and any valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only when a published integration decision changes and needs durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Root cause confirmed locally on the base.** On `812ecfeb` with Node 24.21.0 on a 10-core Mac, the file passes alone (93/93, about 12.4 s). In a stress run of 24 concurrent copies (command in T2), 16 of 24 runs failed. Each failure ended before its asserted boundary:
  - `service preparation secret` / `cleanup-unproved` reached `turns 0` with service `requestMs 200`.
  - `config envelope exception refuses oversized-native/unknown` failed with `native-request-deadline` instead of `oversized-message` (protocol `requestMs 150`).
  - `wrong-question`, `timed` and `a new fixture process…` failed once each.

  This matches the CI symptoms in the issue (`async-after-confirmed` hit the total budget, and the cleanup-boundary cases hit `provision-deadline`). Under that load, passing protocol cases ran at p50 168 ms and p90 294 ms, and service proof cases took up to 1.8 s. CI ran about 8× slower than local.
- **Behaviour budgets:** protocol `{ requestMs: 10_000, totalMs: 30_000, holdMs: 20, cleanupMs: 5_000 }`, service `{ requestMs: 10_000, totalMs: 30_000, cleanupMs: 5_000 }`. These give ≥15× headroom over the slowest loaded local case. They satisfy `requestMs < totalMs − cleanupMs` and `holdMs < requestMs`. They also give SIGTERM exit up to 2.5 s (`min(3000, remaining/2)`), where 75 ms was allowed before.
- **Enforcement isolation.** These cases rely on the fixture stalling forever:
  - Request: `timeout` never sends the native request.
  - Total: `no-resolution` never resolves; `mode-resume-timeout` never answers resume.
  - Startup: `startup-stall` never answers initialize.
  - Cleanup: a verifier or `afterServiceStop` that never settles.

  The targeted deadline is the only way the run can end. Every other budget gets headroom, so the outcome does not depend on runner speed within that headroom.
  - Total enforcement uses `totalMs 6_000, cleanupMs 1_000, requestMs 4_000`. The total timer fires 5 s after spawn, about 17× the loaded-local p90 setup time. This adds about 9 s across the two cases, which is accepted.
- **Coverage mapping.**
  - The protocol request, total and cleanup budgets keep their dedicated enforcement cases.
  - Service startup and provision share one `deadline` (`totalDeadline − cleanupMs`) in `service-contract.mjs:94-95,254,289`. The `startup` boundary case therefore enforces the provisioning/startup budget.
  - Service cleanup is enforced by the `service-stop` and `verification` boundary cases.
  - The base has no service request-deadline enforcement case, so none is "retained". Adding one would need a new fixture mode and is out of scope.
  - `holdMs` is a fixed delay, not a deadline. The existing validation test covers its bound.
  - Invalid-budget rejection is covered for the protocol seam. T2 adds the same pre-execution check for the service seam. `runService` returns failures as evidence rather than rejecting, so a rejection proves validation failed before any work started.
- **CI evidence rule (finite).** The acceptance item about "repeated CI runs" is met by a fixed sample, defined in Final validation, on the delivery PR's branch. It does not mean an open-ended observation window. A later recurrence on another branch is new evidence for a new issue, not unfinished work on this one.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `test/execution/native-input-live-harness.test.ts`:
  - `fixture(t, mode, overrides, source)` at about L519 hard-codes `{150, 600, 20, 150}`. Callers include the protocol-probe loop (`timeout`, `no-resolution` at about L617), the mode-readback loop (`mode-resume-timeout` at about L270), and `an unresponsive cleanup verifier…`, which has `timeout: 2000` and `< 1500` and is at about L662.
  - Direct `runProtocol` callers use `{1000, 3000, 20, 500}` at L60, L454, L485 and L508.
  - Service cases are at L721–L900:
    - Phase cases use `{1000, 3000, 500}`.
    - Preparation cases use `{200, 1500, 500}`.
    - Boundary cases use `{200, 1000, 300}` for `startup` and `{1000, 3000, 300}` for the others, with whole-run checks of `< 1800` and `< 3800` and test timeouts of 3000/5000. Their non-startup cases use an 850 ms delayed-start fixture, which is kept.
  - The CLI refusal test uses `spawnSync` with `timeout: 3000` (L30). It took about 4.7 s in total for five spawns under load.
- **Existing:** `runtime-contract.mjs`:
  - `validateBudgets` (L67) checks the bounds. `runProtocol` (L224) starts the total timer at `totalMs − cleanupMs` before spawn (L617). It starts the request timer at `turn/start` (L687) and clears it when the native request arrives (L703).
  - Cleanup uses `cleanupDeadline`, with SIGTERM and SIGKILL waits of `min(3000, remaining/2)`, then verification bounded by the remaining time, which yields `process-verification-deadline` (L878–L925).
  - `failure.stage` is recorded.
- **Existing:** `service-contract.mjs`:
  - `runService` (L50) validates against `limits` before `mkdtemp`.
  - Startup and provision are bounded by `deadline`. Cleanup operations and verification are bounded by `min(totalDeadline, now + cleanupMs)` (L476–L530).
- **Follow:** `public fixture seam rejects unbounded budgets before spawning` (about L547) for the new service validation case.
- **Base CI:** run 38621969701 on `812ecfeb` passed. The file runs in `node24-execution-1` and `node26-service-1`; confirm this by finding the test name "one exact native callback replay after resume response" in the job logs.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2. The graph is acyclic. Both slices edit the same test file, so they are not independent. Run them in order on one branch.

#### 1. Protocol behaviour/enforcement budget split

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** `npm ci` with Node 24.21.0 (`.node-version`).
**Files and symbols:** `test/execution/native-input-live-harness.test.ts` only. Changes:
- New module constants `protocolBehaviourBudgets` and the protocol enforcement budgets.
- The `fixture()` helper gains an optional trailing `budgets` parameter, defaulting to the behaviour budgets.
- The direct `runProtocol` callers.
- The CLI refusal test.
**Test:**
- Behaviour cases: every `fixture()` caller and every direct `runProtocol` caller with `{1000, 3000, 20, 500}` uses `protocolBehaviourBudgets`. Their assertions do not change.
- Request enforcement: the `timeout` probe uses `{ requestMs: 500, totalMs: 30_000, holdMs: 20, cleanupMs: 5_000 }`. It keeps its existing assertions (`native-request-deadline`, replies 0, retained evidence) and adds `failure.stage === "native-request"`.
- Total enforcement: `no-resolution` and `mode-resume-timeout` use `{ requestMs: 4_000, totalMs: 6_000, holdMs: 20, cleanupMs: 1_000 }`. Each keeps its existing reason, stage and count assertions (`no-resolution` replies 1; `mode-resume-timeout` stage `effective-mode`, requests 1, replies 0).
- Cleanup enforcement: `an unresponsive cleanup verifier cannot exceed the total proof budget` uses `{ requestMs: 4_000, totalMs: 8_000, holdMs: 20, cleanupMs: 2_000 }` and a test `timeout` of 20 000.
  - Record `verifierEnteredAt` inside the stalled `verifyTermination`.
  - Assert `cleanup.verified === false` and `cleanup.verification.reason === "process-verification-deadline"`.
  - Assert `Date.now() - verifierEnteredAt < cleanupMs + 2_000`, and the whole run `< totalMs + 2_000`. These replace `< 1500`.
- CLI refusal test: `spawnSync` `timeout` raised to 30 000. Its status-2 assertions stay.
**Implementation:** Add the constants and a one-line comment explaining why behaviour budgets are large: cases end at their boundary, and the headroom covers runner load. Thread budgets through `fixture()`. In the two parameterised loops, pick enforcement budgets per mode, for example with a mode→budgets lookup; the executor chooses the shape.
**Validate:** From the repository root with Node 24.21.0, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/execution/native-input-live-harness.test.js`. Expect 0 failing and at least 93 passing. The four enforcement cases should report durations consistent with their budgets: about 0.5 s plus cleanup for `timeout`, about 5 s each for `no-resolution` and `mode-resume-timeout`, and under 4 s after the proof for the cleanup verifier case.
**Complete when:** Protocol behaviour cases use behaviour budgets. The request, total and cleanup enforcement cases use isolated budgets, assert boundary-relative timing and pass. The file passes.

#### 2. Service behaviour/enforcement split, service validation and load evidence

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 is complete on the working branch.
**Files and symbols:** `test/execution/native-input-live-harness.test.ts` only. The service-phase, service-preparation and service-boundary cases, plus a new constant `serviceBehaviourBudgets` and a new service validation test.
**Test:**
- `service phase proof|reply-replay` and `service preparation secret|cleanup-unproved` use `serviceBehaviourBudgets`. Their assertions do not change; `turns 1` is now reached under load.
- `startup` boundary: `{ requestMs: 200, totalMs: 2_000, cleanupMs: 500 }` with a test timeout of 15 000. Keep `startup-deadline`, threads 0 and turns 0. Replace `< 1800` with `< totalMs + 2_000`.
- `service-stop` / `verification` boundaries:
  - Use `{ ...serviceBehaviourBudgets, cleanupMs: 3_000 }` with a test timeout of 40 000. This gives the real `service.stop()` room before the stall, so `provision-deadline` and a missed `faultEntered` cannot occur.
  - Record `faultEnteredAt` in `stall`. Replace `< 3800` with `Date.now() - faultEnteredAt < cleanupMs + 2_000`.
  - Keep every existing cleanup, ownership, snapshot-immutability and `faultSettled` assertion.
- New `service fixture seam rejects unbounded budgets before execution`: for each of `{ totalMs: Infinity }`, `{ requestMs: 0 }`, `{ totalMs: 240001 }`, `{ requestMs: -1 }`, `{ cleanupMs: Number.NaN }`, assert `assert.rejects(runService({ fixture: { executable: "/must-not-spawn" }, budgets }), assert.AssertionError)`.
**Implementation:** As specified in Test. The 850 ms delayed-start fixture and the finite-grant test stay unchanged.
**Validate:**
1. From the repository root with Node 24.21.0, after `npm run build`, run `node --test --test-name-pattern="service" dist/test/execution/native-input-live-harness.test.js`. Expect 0 failures, including the new validation case.
2. Load check, from the repository root after `npm run build`:
   ```sh
   d=$(mktemp -d); for i in $(seq 1 24); do node --test dist/test/execution/native-input-live-harness.test.js > "$d/$i.log" 2>&1 & done; wait; grep -h 'ℹ fail' "$d"/*.log | sort | uniq -c
   ```
   Expect `24 ℹ fail 0`.
3. Run the same command on `812ecfeb` on the same machine and record the result. On the planning machine it showed 16 of 24 runs failing.

If the base result does not reproduce, raise the copy count to about 2.4× the CPU count for both runs, and report the counts used.
**Complete when:** All service cases use the split budgets. The service validation test passes. The load check on the candidate shows 0 failing runs, and the base comparison is recorded.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| No `total-budget-exceeded`/`provision-deadline` failures from this file across repeated CI runs | 1, 2 | T2 load check, plus the finite CI sample in Final validation |
| Budget enforcement still covered by deterministic tests | 1, 2 | T1 request/total/cleanup cases; T2 startup (shared provision deadline) and service cleanup cases |
| Behavioural cases reach and assert their intended boundary under runner load (brief) | 1, 2 | T2 load check, 24 runs with 0 failures, with unchanged boundary assertions |
| Request, total, provisioning/startup, cleanup enforcement coverage retained (brief) | 1, 2 | Coverage mapping in Planning decisions; T1 and T2 enforcement cases |
| Invalid/unbounded budgets fail before execution; uncertain cleanup retains evidence and ownership (brief) | 1, 2 | Existing protocol validation test and the new service validation test (T2); unchanged `unreadable cleanup`, `cleanup-unproved`, `service-stop`, `verification` assertions |
| Finite repeated CI sample for the Node 24 execution and Node 26 service lanes (brief) | — | CI sample rule in Final validation |
| Pinned `npm ci`, `npm run check` and the affected CI profiles (brief) | — | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, with Node 24.21.0 and the `packageManager` npm, run `npm ci && npm run check` on the integrated candidate. Expect exit 0.
- Push the branch and open the PR. Expect the PR CI `check` context to pass.
- **CI sample.** On the PR's CI run, find the job IDs that ran this file:
  ```sh
  gh run view <run-id> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[]|"\(.databaseId) \(.name)"'
  gh run view --job <id> --log | grep -c "one exact native callback replay after resume response"
  ```
  Expect one `node24-execution-*` job and one `node26-service-*` job.

  Rerun each of those two jobs with `gh run rerun --job <id>` until each lane has 5 completed attempts, including the original. Wait for each attempt to finish before starting the next. That makes 10 executions in total. Record the run and attempt links, the attempt count per lane, and every failure from this file with its reason in the PR description.
  - Pass: 0 failures from this file across all 10 executions.
  - Infrastructure-only failures, such as a runner loss or a failure in another file, are recorded and replaced by one extra attempt each. They are not counted as file failures.
  - Any `native-input-live-harness` failure counts as a failure. Do not retry it away. Diagnose it under the Guardrails repair rule.

  This finite sample satisfies the "repeated CI runs" criterion.

### Review focus

- Every changed assertion should stay at least as strong as before. Whole-run wall-clock bounds become boundary-relative bounds. No reason, count, receipt or ownership assertion may be weakened.
- Enforcement cases must still stall at the intended boundary. Check that the budget ordering means no other deadline can fire first within its headroom.

content.title: Periodic refreshes cause the UI to flash

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Keep unchanged operator content stable during background polling.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, an isolated Chromium fixture held the 15-second Inbox poll response. The unchanged row remained visible, but a transient “Refreshing. Showing the last fetched data.” status appeared and disappeared on success. A second production-bundle probe seeded real retained assignment text, expanded history, and held the task poll and subsequent assignment-history response. During the poll the retained marker disappeared, previews showed “Recent captured text unavailable”, and open history disclosures fell from three to two. Releasing the history response restored the marker and all three disclosures. This reproduces transient clearing of actual retained assignment history, alongside the refresh alert; it used controlled fake-host reads rather than production traffic.

**Desired behavior:** Distinguish background polling from an operator's explicit Refresh. A successful background read with unchanged business data keeps displayed last-good content, history and layout stable. Manual Refresh can show progress. Failed reads still disclose stale/error state. Preserve generation, task, assignment and authentication ownership when responses overlap or arrive late.

**Key interfaces:** `ResourceController` load/refresh intent and stale/error state; shared `ResourceStatus`; task assignment-history cache/invalidation; task-workspace, Inbox and shell pollers.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Successful unchanged background polls insert no transient refreshing alert or layout shift on task workspace, Inbox or shell.
- [ ] Task retained assignment history stays visible during a poll; refresh/revalidation updates it without losing ownership guards or showing history for the wrong task/assignment.
- [ ] Explicit Refresh still provides appropriate progress; a failed background or manual read exposes stale/error state while retaining last-good content.
- [ ] Overlapping background/manual reads, navigation, authentication changes and late history responses cannot overwrite newer or differently owned data.
- [ ] Browser coverage holds a task poll response and asserts visible history/content remains, then checks unchanged success and failed-read disclosure. Cover shared behavior on Inbox/shell as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve focus, drafts, selections and reading position; run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing polling frequency, adding a streaming transport, hiding refresh errors, #1008's layout redesign or dropping response-ownership protections.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1007
**Planned against:** `cb/issue-1007-quiet-background-refresh` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Authoritative requirements: the issue's acceptance criteria and the [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1007#issuecomment-6177520688) (acceptance list and out-of-scope list). Both are referenced below as **AC1–AC6** (brief order: AC1 no alert/layout shift on unchanged polls; AC2 history stays visible and revalidates with ownership guards; AC3 explicit Refresh progress and failed-read disclosure with last-good content; AC4 overlapping reads, navigation, authentication and late history cannot overwrite newer or differently owned data; AC5 browser coverage of a held task poll, unchanged success and failed read, plus Inbox/shell; AC6 preserve focus, drafts, selections and reading position, and `npm ci` + `npm run check`).

### Approach

Add a **background** load mode to `ResourceController` that publishes nothing until the read settles, and move the three timers and the two poll-derived re-reads onto it. Explicit loads (Refresh, retry, post-command refresh) are unchanged, so they keep their "Refreshing…" progress. In the task workspace, a poll no longer blanks retained assignment history, and its history revalidation replaces what is shown only when it succeeds. Fix the reading-position restore, which currently jumps on a poll because capture and restore pick different elements.

### Guardrails

- Unchanged: polling frequency (15 s), transport, `ResourceStatus` wording and error disclosure, `generation`/`AbortController` ownership in `ResourceController`, `useOperatorResource` scoping by `scope` (CSRF token + route key), the `owned()` guard in `loadHistory` (scope mounted, `captureAuthenticationScope`, per-assignment revision), history hidden when a revalidation fails or `visibilityRevision` changes, and the explicit-Refresh behaviour including its history clearing. Out of scope: #1008's layout redesign, streaming, hiding refresh errors, dropping any ownership protection, new product scope.
- Do not change `sourceObservation` semantics: a failed read must still make source comparison "unknown" (SPEC: a failed refresh cannot establish unchanged requirements).
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Ordinary implementation defects stay with the ticket owner and do **not** consume the plan-mismatch budget: integration, test, fixture, documentation, lint/format, build and CI repairs, and test flake or timing fixes.
- A **wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption** is a distinct case that allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. It means a factual claim in this plan proves false: `ResourceController.load` is not the single publish path that drives `ResourceStatus`, `pending` and `sourceObservation`; the task-workspace history effect or `loadHistory` cannot honour "keep shown" without weakening the `owned()` guard; `capture`/restore element mismatch is not the cause of the scroll shift; or the three timers are not the only background reads. Stop for replanning if two repair cycles do not resolve it, or for any material design/contract change or exhausted grant.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Probe result at `812ecfeb` (scratch copy of the planning checkout, held-response Chromium fixtures on the real production bundle).** Held 15 s task poll: one `.resource-status` alert present; the retained history marker count fell to 0 (preview "Recent captured text unavailable"); open history `<details>` fell from 5 to 2. This confirms both causes named in the issue. Three further causes were found:
  1. `App` passes `observation={workspace.state.data}` to `Inbox`, whose effect calls the explicit `refresh` whenever the shell's poll replaces that object. After the poll itself is silent, the Inbox still shows the "Refreshing…" alert from this chained read (reproduced in the probe). `useInboxTask` (`inbox-detail.tsx`) re-reads its task the same way on every `observedAt` change.
  2. The task workspace derives `sourceObservation` from `resource.state.status !== "fresh"`, so the current "stale" status during every poll flips the source line to "source comparison unknown". Keeping status `fresh` during a poll fixes it, and a failed poll still goes stale with an error.
  3. Reading position: `capture` anchors to the innermost visible `[data-record-id]` element, but the restore effect re-finds it with `querySelectorAll(...).find(id)` (first match in document order). Review contexts render a `<div data-record-id={captureId}>` containing a `Disclosure` with the same id, so the restore picked the outer element and scrolled the page 68 px on every poll (scrollY 2912 → 2844 with no DOM mutation).
  Everything else listed (shell Refresh `disabled={workspace.state.pending}`, `TaskViews pending`) is code-read, not browser-observed; it is covered by the same silent-poll mechanism because a background poll never publishes `pending` or a status change.
- **Silent background mode rather than a new `refreshing` flag.** `status`/`pending` are read by about a dozen components (disabled buttons, `sourceObservation`, `ResourceStatus`). Not publishing at poll start leaves all of them untouched. A poll publishes only when it settles: `fresh` with new data on success, or `stale`+error (same shape as today) on failure, and the error stays until a later read succeeds, so the alert does not flicker between polls. `unauthenticated` still calls `clear()`.
- **Ownership.** A background load is skipped while any read is in flight (`state.pending` or a poll already running), so it never aborts an operator's read or starves behind a slow response. An explicit load supersedes a running poll through the existing `generation`/abort, so a late poll answer is dropped. The history `owned()` guard and `historyRequests` revisions are unchanged.
- **History keeps what is shown only for polls.** The existing focus-restoration test (`test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.ts`, the held explicit-Refresh history case) relies on explicit Refresh clearing history and detaching the focused disclosure, so explicit Refresh keeps that behaviour. A `quietHistory` ref is true while the last task read was a poll: the effect then passes `keepShown` to `loadHistory` (skip the initial delete of `histories[id]`) and `invalidateHistory(false)` on error (supersede in-flight reads without `setHistory({})`). `loadHistory` still deletes the entry on a failed read or a `visibilityRevision` mismatch, so unvalidated history stays hidden. Explicit Refresh sets the ref false before `invalidateHistory()`. The poll sets it only when no read is pending. The task data identity is not deduplicated, because history can change while the task read does not.
- **Poll-derived re-reads use `poll`.** `Inbox` interval and `observation` effect, `useInboxTask`, and the `App` Inbox-route timer (and its initial tasks read) call `poll`. The header Refresh on the Inbox route keeps its progress in the shell's workspace status (`app.tsx` renders `ResourceStatus` for `workspace` when not fresh); the Inbox queue's own alert no longer shows for header-triggered re-reads. This is the one intentional change to explicit-Refresh presentation; it was exercised in the probe.
- **Scroll restore uses the captured element.** Keep the captured `HTMLElement` in a ref; restore with it when still connected and carrying the same record id, else fall back to the existing first-match lookup. `state.historyAnchor` stays `{id, y}` (it is serialised into `history.state`).
- No documentation change is expected: `docs/acceptance.md` UX04 already requires updates to preserve reading position, disclosure and unfinished replies. Confirm that at implementation and edit only if the implemented contract contradicts it.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/resource.ts` — `ResourceController.load` aborts the previous read, bumps `generation`, publishes `{status: data ? "stale" : "loading", error: null, pending: true}`, then publishes `fresh` or `stale`/`error` (`unauthenticated` → `clear()`). `useOperatorResource` returns `{state, refresh}`; `refresh` takes no arguments and is passed directly as `onClick` in many places, so it must stay argument-free.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` — `invalidateHistory` (L253) bumps `historyRequests` and `setHistory({})`; `capture` (L391) and the restore effect (L598) use `[data-record-id]`; `refresh` (L444) = capture + `invalidateHistory` + `resource.refresh`; `refreshRef` (L454) is what the 15 s interval (L477) calls; `loadHistory` (L605) deletes `histories[id]` first, then pages; the effect at L760 invalidates on `pending || error`, otherwise loads history for every assignment. History renders at L1818–1885 (`histories[id]?.items.at(-1)?.text ?? "Recent captured text unavailable"`).
- **Existing:** `web/src/inbox.tsx` L132–152 (`refresh` ref used by the interval and the `observation` effect); `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx` L41 (`useInboxTask`); `web/src/app.tsx` L531–546 (Inbox-route timer for `tasks` and `workspace`), L988 (`observation={workspace.state.data}`).
- **New:** `ResourceController.load(loader, {background?: boolean})` and `useOperatorResource(...).poll`; `test/fixtures/background-refresh.ts` (`holdResponse`, `failResponses`, `watchDom`/`observedDom` helpers); the unit and two browser test files below.
- **Follow:** `test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.ts` for fixture setup (`createOperatorFixture`, `seedReviewTask`, SQL history rows, `page.clock.install()` + `page.clock.runFor(15000)`, `browserSuite`, `page.route` holds) and `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts` for Inbox access.
- **Entry points (UI coverage):** polling — task workspace, Inbox, Inbox-route shell, Inbox detail hold read; explicit — shell header Refresh, "Refresh task", Inbox/question Retry, post-command refreshes. No other timers exist (`setInterval` appears only in `task-workspace.tsx`, `inbox.tsx`, `app.tsx`). All other `refresh` users stay explicit. Reverse operations: none (no state-changing action is added).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 (acyclic). T2 and T3 both use the helper module that T2 creates, and T3 edits `task-workspace.tsx`, so run them sequentially; no ready tasks are safe to run concurrently. T1 is the proof that `ResourceController` can express the contract the other slices depend on.

#### 1. Background load mode in ResourceController

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/resource.ts` (`ResourceController.load`, `clear`, `useOperatorResource`); new `test/operator/operator-resource-polling.test.ts` (imports `ResourceController` from `../../web/src/resource.js`, as other tests import web modules).
**Test:** Plain `node:test`, no browser, deferred promises (build the deferred with an explicit `new Promise` executor that assigns resolvers inside a block; lint forbids assignment-in-expression and `Promise.withResolvers` may not type-check on the pinned ES target). (a) After a successful load, a background load records no publish at start (`state` unchanged, `pending` false, status `fresh`); rejecting with `unavailable` publishes `stale`, `error: "unavailable"`, `data` kept. (b) A second background load while one is in flight does not call its loader; an explicit load during a background load publishes `stale`+`pending: true`; the background answer resolving late leaves the data unchanged and the explicit result wins; a background load while an explicit one is pending does not call its loader. (c) A background `unauthenticated` rejection clears to `empty` with `data: null`.
**Implementation:** Add `private polling: AbortController | undefined`. `load(loader, {background = false} = {})`: return immediately when `background && (this.state.pending || this.polling)`; abort the previous read and bump `generation` as today; set `this.polling = background ? abort : undefined`; publish the `pending` state only when not background; clear `this.polling` once the read settles for the current generation (success, error and the `unauthenticated` path) and in `clear()`. Add `poll: () => resource.load(loader, {background: true})` to the `useOperatorResource` return value, leaving `refresh` argument-free.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-resource-polling.test.js`; expect clean type/lint and 3 passing tests with 0 failures.
**Complete when:** The three unit tests pass and all existing `refresh` call sites compile unchanged.

#### 2. Silent Inbox and shell polling

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 complete (`poll` exists and its unit test passes).
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/inbox.tsx` (`Inbox`: the `refresh` ref L132, interval L135, `observation` effect L148–154); `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx` (`useInboxTask` effect L41); `web/src/app.tsx` (`taskRefresh`/`workspaceRefresh` refs L531–534 and the Inbox-route effect L539–546); new `test/fixtures/background-refresh.ts`; new `test/operator/operator-inbox-background-refresh-browser.test.ts` (`browserSuite("operator-inbox-background-refresh-browser")`).
**Test:** Seed with `seedReviewTask` plus a result and an open question row inserted into `coordination_interactions` (as in the task-workspace test) so `/app/inbox` shows at least one `.inbox-row`; `page.clock.install()` before `goto`, sign in, wait for the row and `networkidle`. Record row count and the first row's `getBoundingClientRect().top`; install `watchDom` (a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` with `childList`, `characterData`, `attributes`, recording every mutation and whether `.resource-status` was ever present). Hold the first `/api/operator/inbox`, `/api/operator/task-list` and `/api/operator/workspace` responses with `holdResponse` (fetch, signal entry, await a gate, then fulfil), `page.clock.runFor(15000)`, await all three entries, and assert: no `.resource-status`, same row count, same row `top`. Release, `networkidle`; assert the observed log has no transient status and zero mutations. Then fail `/api/operator/inbox` with 503, `runFor(15000)`, expect the exact text "Refresh failed. Showing the last fetched data." with the row still present; remove the failure. Then hold the workspace read and click the header "Refresh": expect "Refreshing. Showing the last fetched data." (shell status) with the row still present; release and `page.waitForFunction` that no `.resource-status` remains (the shell's fresh read triggers the Inbox's silent re-read that clears the earlier error). Helpers in `test/fixtures/background-refresh.ts` are shared with T3.
**Implementation:** In `Inbox`, use `resource.poll` for the interval and for the `observation` effect; keep `resource.refresh` wired to the retry/`onRecorded` paths. In `useInboxTask`, call `current.current.poll()` (poll already skips while pending; drop the explicit `pending` check, keep the comment) and leave the user "Retry" on `refresh`. In `App`, point `taskRefresh` and `workspaceRefresh` at `tasks.poll` and `workspace.poll` (including the first call on entering the Inbox route). Do not change `refreshAll`, the header Refresh button or any other call site.
**Validate:** From the repository root run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-background-refresh-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-web-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-shell-browser.test.js`; expect all pass. Sensitivity check, once and not committed: temporarily point the `Inbox` interval back at `resource.refresh`, rebuild, and confirm the new test fails on the transient status; record the result.
**Complete when:** The new Inbox/shell test passes and the existing Inbox and shell browser tests are unchanged and green.

#### 3. Quiet task-workspace poll, history revalidation and stable reading position

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T1 and T2 complete (helper module present).
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` — `invalidateHistory` (L253), the ref list at L260 (new `anchorElement`, `quietHistory`), `capture` (L391), `refresh` (L444), new `poll`, `refreshRef` (L454), the restore branch (L596–604), `loadHistory` (L605, new fourth parameter `keepShown`), the history effect (L760–765); new `test/operator/operator-task-background-refresh-browser.test.ts` (`browserSuite("operator-task-background-refresh-browser")`).
**Test:** Fixture as in `operator-task-workspace-browser.test.ts`: `seedReviewTask`, `delegatedResult`, three `conversation_history_items` rows with text `Retained marker 0..2`, `page.clock.install()`, open `/app/tasks/<id>`, wait for the marker in `#history`, click "Expand all history", record the count of `#history details[open]` (at least 3), the "Refresh task" button `top`, and `scrollY`. (1) Unchanged poll: `watchDom`, hold the first `/api/operator/tasks/<id>` response, `runFor(15000)`; while held assert no `.resource-status`, the marker still present, same open count, same `top`; release the task read, then hold the next `/api/operator/assignments/<assignmentId>/history` response and assert the marker and open count while *that* is held; release, `networkidle`; assert no transient status or "Recent captured text unavailable", zero DOM mutations, the same `top` and `scrollY` (this last assertion fails without the scroll-restore fix). (2) Failed poll: 503 on the task read, `runFor(15000)`, expect "Refresh failed. Showing the last fetched data." with the marker still present. (3) Explicit Refresh: hold the task read, click "Refresh task", expect "Refreshing. Showing the last fetched data." (use `.first()`: the shell workspace read shows its own status too) and the "Latest result" heading still present; release. (4) Late history: hold the next history response, click "Refresh task", wait for the held request, insert a `Retained marker NEW` row, click "Refresh task" again, wait for `Retained marker NEW` in `#history`, release the older response, `networkidle`, and assert `Retained marker NEW` is still shown.
**Implementation:** (a) `quietHistory = useRef(false)`; `invalidateHistory(clear = true)` always bumps `historyRequests` and calls `setHistory({})` only when `clear`. (b) `refresh()` sets `quietHistory.current = false` before `invalidateHistory()`; add `poll()` = `capture()`, `if (!resource.state.pending) quietHistory.current = true`, `resource.poll()`; point `refreshRef` (the interval) at `poll`; `refreshAll` is unchanged. (c) `loadHistory(id, before?, beforeOmission?, keepShown = false)`: skip the initial `setHistory` delete when `keepShown`; leave the failed-read and `visibilityRevision` deletions and all `owned()` checks as they are. (d) In the history effect, call `invalidateHistory(!quietHistory.current)` on `pending || error`, and pass `quietHistory.current` as `keepShown` when loading each assignment's history; the "Refresh captured history" and "Load earlier…" buttons keep the default (clearing) behaviour. (e) `anchorElement = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null)`: `capture` stores the chosen element; the restore step uses it when `isConnected` and its `dataset.recordId === a.id`, else the existing lookup.
**Validate:** From the repository root run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-task-background-refresh-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-task-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-readiness-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-project-config-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-changes-browser.test.js`; expect all pass. Planning evidence: a prototype of T1–T3 passed 87 tests across 15 browser/unit files (these plus the T2 set, search, foundation and integrated browser files) with the baseline failing the new held-poll assertions. Sensitivity check, once and not committed: revert only `refreshRef` to `refresh` and confirm assertion (1) fails.
**Complete when:** The new task test passes in repeated runs (run it three times) and the existing task-workspace focus, draft and history tests are unchanged and green.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| AC1: unchanged successful poll has no alert or layout shift on the task workspace, Inbox and shell | 2, 3 | T2 held Inbox/task-list/workspace poll; T3 assertion (1) |
| AC2: retained history stays visible during a poll and revalidates with ownership guards | 3 | T3 assertions (1) and (4) |
| AC3: explicit Refresh shows progress; failed background or manual read discloses stale/error with last-good content | 1, 2, 3 | T1 test (a); T2 failed read and header Refresh; T3 assertions (2) and (3) |
| AC4: overlapping background/manual reads, navigation, authentication and late history cannot overwrite newer or differently owned data | 1, 3 | T1 tests (b) and (c); T3 assertion (4); existing scope/key tests in the T3 regression set |
| AC5: browser coverage holds a task poll, then checks unchanged success and failed-read disclosure; Inbox/shell as applicable | 2, 3 | T3 assertions (1)–(2); T2 |
| AC6: focus, drafts, selections and reading position preserved; pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check` | 3 | T3 `top`/`scrollY` assertions and the existing focus/draft regression set; Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, using Node 24.21.0 from `.node-version` and the pinned package manager, run `npm ci` then `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate; expect exit 0 (type checking, lint, formatting, build and the full suite, with the three new files discovered exactly once).
- Baseline: trusted CI passed on `812ecfeb` (`check`, `quality`, and the Node 24 and Node 26 test jobs). Do not rerun baseline checks locally.

### Review focus

- Every call site that still passes `refresh` is intentionally explicit; no timer may call `refresh`. Confirm with `rg "setInterval" web/src` and that each interval target is a `poll`.
- `loadHistory` ownership and the privacy rule that unvalidated history is hidden must be unchanged when `keepShown` is true.
- Intentional change: the Inbox queue no longer shows its own "Refreshing" alert for header-triggered re-reads (the shell status shows progress).

### Overlap with in-flight work

Files this plan touches: `web/src/resource.ts`, `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`, `web/src/inbox.tsx`, `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx`, `web/src/app.tsx`, and new `test/fixtures/background-refresh.ts`, `test/operator/operator-resource-polling.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-inbox-background-refresh-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-task-background-refresh-browser.test.ts`. No existing test file is edited.

`task-workspace.tsx` hunks are at about L253–262, L391–420, L444–460, L596–640 and L757–770. They are separable from #1005 (brief rendering near L1352, also open as PR #1010), #997 (near L345 and L836, with `task-workspace-state.ts`, `local-review.tsx`, `recovery.tsx`, `execution-runtime.ts` and the new `commit-gate.ts`, none touched here) and #998/#1004 (no shared files). #1007 has no required landing order relative to #1005, #997, #998 or #1004. The only coupling is semantic: if any of them adds a timer-driven read, it should use `poll`, and a rebase conflict in `task-workspace.tsx` is mechanical.

### Allowed deviations

- Rename helper functions, move the helper module within `test/fixtures/`, and choose the hold/fail helper signatures, provided the asserted behaviours above are kept.
- If another change lands a new timer-driven read, point it at `poll`.

### Re-plan triggers

- Making explicit Refresh retain history, or changing a failed explicit read's history disclosure, would alter the existing focus-restoration test's mechanism and is a contract change.
- Any need to publish `pending` or a status change at background-poll start, or to dedupe task-data identity.

content.title: Task detail screen is too long and complex

nodes.body:
Specifics from the 16 October 2026 UX pass on a seeded fixture world, for when this is picked up:

- The Overview tab repeats Files, Changes, Review, Assignment context & identifiers, Assignment history and Message lead as in-page sections below the brief, duplicating the top tabs (Files, Changes, Review, History). One set should own each section.
- The header has five buttons (Execution, Stop…, Advanced task controls, Requests and coordination, Refresh task) before the status strip; #1087 covers the legacy ones.
- Raw identifiers, literal tokens and GitHub-only controls on local tasks are split out as #1088 so they can land independently of the restructure.

**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1008 **Planned against:** `main` at `c844e21f39cab46ac0206f5978c1883b655ea1e8` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach Restructure task detail in place, without splitting `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` and without new routes, tabs or dependencies: 1. **Overview reading order (T1).** Move the existing Overview cards into the order `design/DESIGN.md` → Interaction notes → Task detail and updates prescribes and frames `46a-task-overview-laptop` / `03-task-detail` draw: decision card → latest result (summary, criterion rows, viewing reference, Result revision) → reply → **Shared brief**, **Evidence** and **Assignments** as collapsed native `
` cards, each with a one-line summary. Then one pointer line. Remove the in-page `EntryLinks` row, which repeats the tabs. Captured context and retained history already live in History, and delivery evidence on Changes. They stay there. 2. **Phone detail header (T2).** Below 760px the shell header becomes one row: an icon-only Back, a one-line title, a mono identity subtitle (`repository#N` or `Local task`) and one outline overflow disclosure, "Task actions", that holds the existing Execution link and Stop… / Stop requested controls (frame `47-phone-task-overview`). From 760px the header keeps Execution and Stop… as today. The responsive matrix then asserts that the decision card is inside the first 390 × 844 viewport. Every deep link keeps its current section id and tab mapping. A link whose target sits inside a closed disclosure opens it first. ### Guardrails - **No API, CLI, URL or persisted-contract change.** `src/`, `src/operator/contracts.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (including Search `href`s and attention `destination`s) and the CLI are untouched. Section ids (`decisions`, `brief`, `review`, `reply`, `assignments`, `files`, `changes`, `local-review`, `context`, `history`), `sectionIds`, `tabSections`, `web/src/task-tabs.ts` (`tabForSection`/`tabForLocation`) and every query parameter (`section`, `record`, `request`, `result`, `evidence`, `source`, `assignment`, `path`, `repository`, `target`, `base`, `review`) keep their current meaning and tab. - Out of scope: the review-result first-screen budget and the other #1098 rows (that flow's `Status: planned` line stays), copy fixes owned by #1088, drill-in phone screens, a sticky bottom bar, the GitHub source / Ensemble phone tab pair (still "not built" per DESIGN.md), Inbox and Board changes, and settings/onboarding work (#1137, #1078, #1140, #1077, #1075, #1076, #1079, #1103). - Keyboard and focus: DOM order equals visual order (no CSS `order`, no `grid-area` reordering of Overview cards), nothing navigates or opens on blur, and existing focus/reading-restoration code paths (`capture`, `readingFocusTarget`, the `useLayoutEffect` restore, `focusReplay`) keep their behaviour. Overview disclosure contents always stay mounted: closing a disclosure never unmounts `RetainedResultEvidence`, `ReviewEvidence`, the brief's `Disclosure` or `AssignmentRows`, so in-flight reads, caches and selections survive. - Overview disclosure state lives in `TaskWorkspaceState`, separate from `state.expanded`. A poll, a manual refresh, an arriving request or "Collapse all history" never opens or closes an Overview disclosure. - The canvas is not edited (see Planning decisions). Any further visual change found necessary must update the canvas (artifact `6JBCAUn25QRBPVnyJNCBxY`) and `design/DESIGN.md` together in this PR. - Continue routine implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. This includes updating the existing tests listed under each slice. These stay with the implementer, consume no repair budget, and are recorded briefly in the delivery record with their evidence renewed. A **wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption** is different: a named symbol, file, call path or behaviour that does not exist or does not behave as stated here, such that the planned increment cannot be built as written. It gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping with the evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or once a grant is exhausted. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants. ### Planning decisions Controller-visible decisions, settled from the frames and DESIGN.md: - **Collapse vs tab.** Shared brief, Evidence and Assignments **collapse** on Overview as native `
` cards. No new tabs are added. Captured context and retained history stay in **History** and delivery evidence stays on **Changes**, where they already live. Basis: DESIGN.md Interaction notes ("the shared brief and assignments as collapsed disclosures with a one-line summary"; captured conversations, earlier results and delivery evidence "live in History, Changes and Review, and the Overview tab does not repeat those tabs as sections") and frames 46a/03 (brief and assignments drawn as disclosure headers below the reply). - **Evidence disclosure.** The latest-result card keeps the summary, `CriteriaRows` (criterion evidence), "Ask lead about result", the viewing-reference block (changes line, Set viewing reference, its unconfirmed check and disclaimer) and the Result revision select. `ReviewEvidence` and `RetainedResultEvidence` move into a new collapsed **Evidence** card after the reply. Basis: frame 47's "Evidence" row and review-result step 3 ("retained evidence are one step away"). The viewing block stays visible so the `review.view` replay focus target (`[data-unconfirmed-control="review.view"]`) is never inside a closed disclosure. DESIGN.md already records that no "Earlier results (2)" button is built. - **Execution/Stop location.** Desktop and tablet (≥760px) keep Execution and Stop… in the header (frame 46a, DESIGN.md "The task header keeps Execution and Stop… only"). Phone (<760px) puts both in the header's single outline overflow (frame 47). It is a native `
`/`` disclosure named "Task actions", not an ARIA menu. It is keyboard-operable natively, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the summary. It does not use the status strip. - **One overflow instance.** `TaskHeaderActions` always renders one `
`. `useMediaQuery("(max-width: 759px)")` (existing `web/src/use-media-query.ts`) forces `open` from 760px, where CSS hides the summary. Because the wrapper element type never changes across a resize, the Stop `Dialog` and its `open`/`sent` state never remount. - **Phone subtitle and outcome.** The phone header subtitle is the mono identity from `taskIdentity(data).label`, carried as a new `identity` field on `TaskHeaderReport` and a new `shortSubtitle` prop on `PageHeader` that mirrors `shortTitle`. The phone hides the outcome subtitle and the strip's `.task-id`, which the subtitle now carries. So that the outcome stays reachable, the strip's "Full desired outcome" disclosure also renders on phone when the outcome is a single line (`data-phone-only`, hidden from 760px). - **Canvas.** No frame changes are required. Frames `46a-task-overview-laptop` and `03-task-detail` already draw decision → latest result → Message lead → collapsed Shared brief → collapsed Assignments → "Captured conversations, earlier results and delivery evidence are in History, Changes and Review." Frame `47-phone-task-overview` draws Back, the title, the mono subtitle `acme/atlas#142`, one outline "Task actions: Execution, Stop" control and the decision card in the first viewport. Production differences (a disclosure instead of an ARIA menu, a collapsed Evidence card instead of drill-in rows or Earlier results / Changes since viewed links, tabs kept on phone) are recorded in DESIGN.md → "Task detail, composer and Stop", following that section's convention. Frame `12b` (#1139) is unaffected. - **Brief/Evidence/Assignments summaries** reuse recorded data only: - Brief: `Requirements · GitHub|Local · supplied criteria`, "None supplied", or the existing gap sentence when there is no source. - Evidence: `R`, plus counts already in the task read for the selected result's review metadata. No async read. - Assignments: `Assignments · `, with each row's short id and known state from `assignmentRow`, clamped to one line, or "No assignments yet." ### Implementation context - **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` - `TaskWorkspace`'s Overview `TabPanel` currently renders, in order: `section#decisions` (decision card, `QuestionResponse` for `?request=`, `QuestionHolds`, `WaitReasons`), `section#brief` (open), `section#review` (Latest result, `CriteriaRows`, `EntryLinks`, viewing block, Result revision, `ReviewEvidence`, `RetainedResultEvidence`), `section#assignments` (`AssignmentRows`), then `{reply}` (`section#reply`), then `TaskInspector`. - Deep links are handled in the `selectedPath` init block (around lines 343–390: `result`, `evidence`, `source`, `assignment`, files and changes params), in `reveal(id)` → `selectTab` + `showSection`, and in the `useLayoutEffect` restore. The restore covers the saved `taskWorkspaceReading`, the in-place link branch (`section` → fragment → default section → `showSection`) and the first-paint `record`/`request`/`section` branch (`showSection` or `target.scrollIntoView()`). - "Collapse all history" calls `state.expanded.clear()`. - **Existing:** `web/src/task-detail.tsx` — `showSection(target)` scrolls and focuses the first `h3,h4`. `EntryLinks` is used only at task-workspace.tsx:1878. Its `.entry-links` CSS is in `web/src/task-detail.css`. `inPage` is also used by `AssignmentRows`. - **Existing:** `web/src/task-header.tsx` — `taskHeaderReport` and `TaskHeaderActions` (Execution link plus the Stop… `Dialog`, rendered by `web/src/app.tsx` in `taskHeaderProps.action`). `TaskStrip` holds the "Full desired outcome" `
`. - **Existing:** `web/src/components.tsx` `PageHeader` (`shortTitle` pattern with `.page-title-full` and `.page-title-short`); the phone header CSS is in `web/src/styles.css` (around lines 880–1000) and `web/src/task-detail.css` (`.page-header[data-desktop-back]`, `.task-header-actions`). - **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace-state.ts` — `TaskWorkspaceState` (per task, kept by `app.tsx` `taskStates` across navigation) holds `expanded`, `tab`, `tabScroll` and others. - **New:** a `TaskWorkspaceState.overview = new Set<"brief" | "evidence" | "assignments">()` field. A `task-detail.tsx` `openDisclosures(target)` helper opens every closed ancestor `details` of the target, and the target's own `:scope > details`. - **Follow:** `task-workspace.tsx:Disclosure` for a controlled `
` whose `onToggle` is the single writer of the set. `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` uses `openFixture`, `seed`, `seedOwnApproval`, `settle`, `selectedTab`, `openTaskTab` and `page.clock.install()` + `clock.runFor(15000)` for deterministic polls. `test/operator/operator-responsive-browser.test.ts` has `firstViewportProblems`. ### Implementation slices **Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3, acyclic. T1 and T2 share `web/src/task-detail.css`, `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` and `design/DESIGN.md`, so they are not concurrent. There is one implementer and one PR. Estimated total is about 900–1,300 changed lines, including test updates: roughly 350 production and CSS, 80 DESIGN.md, and the rest tests. That is reviewable as one PR, so no split is proposed. #### 1. Overview leads with attention, result and reply; secondary detail collapses **Task ID:** `T1` **Depends on:** `none` **Prerequisites:** none **Files and symbols:** - `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`: reorder the Overview JSX; new brief, evidence and assignments disclosure cards; init-block expansion for `source`/`evidence`; `openDisclosures` in the first-paint record branch; remove the `EntryLinks` import and use. - `web/src/task-detail.tsx`: `showSection` and new `openDisclosures`; delete `EntryLinks`. - `web/src/task-workspace-state.ts`: the `overview` set. - `web/src/task-detail.css`: `.overview-disclosure` summary styling (44px summary below 1121px, one-line clamped summary text); delete `.entry-links` rules. - `design/DESIGN.md`: - Core surfaces "Task detail (`03-task-detail`)" line ~156: the Overview order. - "Task detail, composer and Stop": the Tabs/links bullet (disclosures open for their links), the Overview bullet (order, the three disclosures, the pointer line, the inspector after the cards below 1024px), and the "Frame 57's entries … stay" bullet, replaced by "Overview has no in-page entries to other tabs". - Interaction notes → Task detail and updates: one bullet, "A link to a section or record inside a closed disclosure opens it; polls never open or close one." **Test:** in `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (seam: the real web app over `createOperatorFixture`; `openFixture`/`seed` and the existing approval, question and holds seeds). Each new test is a self-contained `test(...)` with its own fixture. - **New "Overview reads decisions, result and reply before the collapsed brief, evidence and assignments".** At 1366 × 900, with `seedOwnApproval` (several decisions: reuse the two-approval seed of "The decision card and inspector list only the other open approvals as holds"): - Bounding boxes and DOM order are `section#decisions` < `section#review` < `section#reply` < `section#brief` < the Evidence card < `section#assignments` < the pointer line. - `compareDocumentPosition` agrees with visual order. - The brief, Evidence and Assignments `details` are closed by default, with summaries showing their labels and counts (`Requirements · Local · N supplied criteria`, `R`, `Assignments · `). - `nav[aria-label="Task material"]` has count 0, and no link on Overview targets `#files`, `#changes`, `#local-review`, `#context` or `#history` except the inspector and the `AssignmentRows` buttons. - Pressing Tab from the last decision-card control reaches a control in `section#review` before any `summary`. - Matrix cases in the same test or sibling tests: - Task with no decisions (`seed`): the card reads "No operator decision needed." and precedes the result. - Task with holds (reuse the "Holds stay listed beneath Fix…" seed): the hold lines are inside `#decisions`, above `#review`. - Running vs finished task: the Overview order is unchanged. - **New "Deep links open collapsed Overview sections and focus them".** Table-driven over: - `?section=brief`, `#brief`, `?source=`, the Search `href` for a brief hit (fetched from `/api/operator/search` as `operator-search-browser.test.ts` does), `?section=review`, `?result=`, `?section=reply`, `?section=decisions`, `?request=`, `?request=#history`, `?assignment=#history`, `?section=context`, and the inspector `R1` link followed in place. - For each: the expected tab is selected (as in "Task deep links open their tab on the first paint"). The target section or record is in the viewport. A disclosure containing it has `open`. For `section` links, `document.activeElement` is that section's `summary` or heading. For `source`, `#retained-source-revision` has that value. - Then close the brief, follow `?section=brief` in place and assert it reopens. - **New "Overview disclosures survive polls, refresh, Collapse all history and leaving the task, and never take focus".** - `page.clock.install()`. content.title: Use the signed-in GitHub CLI login for a new project's GitHub source by default

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Configure a newly created project's GitHub source with the offered usable GitHub CLI login by default.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, a production-service/SQLite fixture with fake gh reported an available signed-in discovery account, but a newly created project's source still had `credentialRef: null`. Creation/backfill deliberately initialise null, and ADR-1009/SPEC prohibit implicit use today. This confirms the current default, using simulated gh detection; it did not use real credentials or exercise invalid overrides and existing/cleared sources.

**Desired behavior:** At new-source setup, use `gh:github.com` when the offered service-host CLI login is usable, and clearly show the account being selected. Persist the default through the supported configuration boundary so sync actually has a credential. An unusable or missing login remains visibly unconfigured. This issue amends the existing explicit-selection contract for new sources only.

**Key interfaces:** New-project/source initialisation; GitHub CLI detection and per-use credential resolution; source configuration/ready check; versioned keyed source saves; CLI source presentation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] A new project's source uses the usable offered gh login and shows the account in setup/source settings.
- [ ] Missing gh, signed-out/unreadable login and invalid `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` override cases receive no automatic default or fallback.
- [ ] Existing sources, explicitly selected environment credentials and explicitly cleared credentials remain unchanged, including migration/restart.
- [ ] Setup's ready check explains a missing source credential before the first refresh. Configuration changes keep their existing versioning, receipts and activation rules.
- [ ] Change, Clear and Cancel still work, and the HTML fallback and CLI report the same persisted choice.
- [ ] Preserve credential exclusion/redaction and per-use resolution; do not copy/cache tokens or grant repository access.
- [ ] Amend ADR-1009, SPEC, the operations guide and Pen design through MCP, refreshing DESIGN.md. Cover fresh setup, missing/invalid login, existing/cleared sources and UI/CLI readback.
- [ ] Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Defaulting discovery/delivery/routing credentials beyond this new-source choice, retroactive changes to existing sources, authentication setup, token storage or additional access grants.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1003
**Planned against:** `main` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442`
**Planned branch:** `cb/issue-1003-default-gh-login`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Guided setup records the default explicitly. The setup form already reads `GET /api/operator/discovery`. That read gains a `sourceGh` field: GitHub CLI detection in the same candidate environment that an explicit `gh:github.com` source selection uses. When `sourceGh` is `signed-in`, setup shows "GitHub source credential: GitHub CLI · @login" and sends a new optional `sourceCredentialRef: "gh:github.com"` with the existing keyed `project.create`. The domain writes that value into the version-1 `project_github_sources` row instead of `NULL`. Otherwise setup says that no source credential will be set, and omits the field. After creation, the ready check reads the project configuration's existing `source.credential` status. It shows the credential being used, or why the source cannot sync, without blocking Resume. Source settings, the HTML fallback and the CLI read back the same persisted reference. ADR-1009, SPEC, the operations guide and the Pen design are amended in place.

### Guardrails

- The default applies only to a new project created through guided setup (`/app/settings/projects/new`), only as `gh:github.com`, and only when setup's last `sourceGh` read was `signed-in`. Discovery credential selection stays explicit (frame 117b offer unchanged). Delivery and routing stay env-only. The HTML-fallback create form (`src/standalone/operator.ts:167`) and the CLI `project.create` change document (`src/cli/configure-project.ts:168`) remain explicit/null: they show no account, so they record no default. Report them as known entry-point gaps; do not add a default there.
- No resolution-time fallback. `resolveGitHubSourceCredential(null, …)` still returns `missing-credential`, so `test/sources/github-source-credential.test.ts:155` must keep passing unchanged. A `NULL` source is never re-defaulted at read, sync, migration or restart. The backfill insert in `DomainStore.migrate()` (`src/core/domain.ts:648`) stays `NULL`. `github.configure` semantics (keep/set/clear) are unchanged.
- The status-only `sourceGh` probe runs `gh auth status` only, never `gh auth token`. It never returns a token, reference name or stderr. Per-use resolution, exclusion/redaction (`credentialReferenceExclusions`, `ghEnvironment`), the 512-byte bound and runtime-limit disclosures are unchanged. No token is copied, cached or persisted, and no repository access is granted.
- `project.create` without `sourceCredentialRef` must keep its exact payload hash and receipt. Never emit the key with an explicit `undefined`, because `legacyDomainPayloadHash` hashes it as `undefined`. Creation stays version 1 with an inactive linked source. Activation, preview, readiness and admission rules are unchanged. The ready-check credential line is informational and never disables Resume.
- Continue routine implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. These stay with the ticket owner, do not consume the plan-mismatch budget, and are recorded briefly in the delivery record with affected evidence renewed. A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example, `sourceGh` cannot distinguish an invalid override, or `project.create` cannot carry the field without changing legacy hashes) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles under to-plan's allowance. After that, stop for a replan. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption, and preserve repair budgets and grants.
- Sequencing: start only after #1006 has merged. Rebase this branch's base onto the then-current `main` and re-verify the shared regions listed under Implementation context. If #1006 has changed the `project.create` insert, `discoveryStatusSchema`, or `readDiscoveryStatus` beyond adding columns or fields, that is unknown overlap: investigate it before continuing.

### Planning decisions

- **Default recorded at setup, not inferred by the service.** The issue allows either setup or a GitHub-tab preselection. A preselection persists nothing, so sync would still skip the project (`src/standalone/github-sync.ts:93-94`). A server-side default inside `project.create` would make the payload hash of a replayed keyed create depend on detection at replay time. The setup-sent explicit field is persisted, replays deterministically, and is the only path that states the account before the credential is recorded.
- **"Usable" means `sourceGh.state === "signed-in"`.** That is `detectGh` (`src/standalone/gh-credential.ts:70`) under `ghEnvironment(domain, { reference: "gh:github.com" })`, the environment `StandaloneService.gitHubSourceCredentialStatus` already uses (`src/standalone/service.ts:2452-2466`). `GH_TOKEN` takes precedence over `GITHUB_TOKEN`, then the stored login, and an invalid override makes `gh auth status` fail, so the state is `unreadable` with no fallback to the stored account. This matches the documented offered-account contract (`docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`, "GitHub source credential") and the AC's negative cases. The fake gh `setAccounts` override path already models these cases.
- **The server does not re-check detection at create.** `project.create` accepts exactly `gh:github.com` without probing, as `github.configure` does today. Per-use resolution fails closed. The ready check and source settings show any reason from a later failure. If detection changes between the setup read and create, the result is a visible unusable credential, never a fallback.
- **`sourceGh` is added to the existing discovery status read, not served from a new route.** Setup already reads that envelope, so this needs no new route, CSRF or authentication classification. The field is named so it cannot be mistaken for the discovery reference: discovery's own `gh` field and `available` keep their current discovery-environment meaning. Share one `GhLoginScope` across both probes so identical environments run `gh` once.
- **The setup form has no opt-out control.** Change and Clear stay in the project's GitHub source settings. The setup line says this.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` holds the `project.create` command schema (~71-81). `DomainStore.apply` case `"project.create"` inserts the `project_github_sources` row with `credentialRef` `NULL` (~1837-1859). `createProject` (~739) replays with `legacyDomainPayloadHash` (~398), and `migrate()` backfills existing projects with `NULL` (~648).
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` holds the operator `project.create` schema (~1751-1763), `sourceCredentialStatusSchema` (~2352) and `discoveryStatusSchema` (~2795). `projectConfigurationSchema.source.credential` (~2443) already carries usability, reason and `gh` for a project.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` `readDiscoveryStatus` (~5191) detects with discovery's `ghEnvironment(domain)`. `readProjectConfigurationOnce` (~4741) fills `credential` via `service.gitHubSourceCredentialStatus`. The `project.create` path (~6109-6146) passes the command through to `executeDomain`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/project-setup.tsx` reads `/api/operator/discovery` only while discovery is unconfigured (~150-166). It offers discovery gh (~585-636) and submits `project.create` through `useDraft(p.drafts, "project.create")`. `web/src/ready-check.tsx` lists recorded facts (~95-117) and wait items from `readyCheckItems` (`web/src/setup-model.ts:249`); it already reads `/api/operator/projects/${projectId}/configuration` on review (~214).
- **Existing readback:** `web/src/source-config.tsx` has the credential panel copy "Choose explicitly for this project…" (~634-730). The `src/standalone/operator.ts` HTML GitHub source paragraph is at ~300 ("Credential reference configured … choosing it is explicit"). `src/cli/source.ts:122-146` prints `Credential` as GitHub CLI / environment variable / not configured, plus the detected account.
- **Follow:** use `test/operator/project-setup.test.ts` `setupWorld`/`create` and the "guided create … replays" case (~94) for domain/API create tests. Use `test/sources/source-credential-exclusion.test.ts` "candidate gh offers match selected identity…" (~1097) with `createFakeGh().setAccounts` for override precedence. Use `test/fixtures/setup-browser.ts` `setupJourney({ ghExecutable })` for setup browser journeys.
- **Shared with #1006 (rebase after it merges):** `src/core/domain.ts` (the project.create insert ~1839 is the same statement #1006 extends with a column: keep its column and bind `credentialRef` to `command.sourceCredentialRef ?? null`); `src/operator/contracts.ts` (different schemas); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`readDiscoveryStatus` only); `web/src/source-config.tsx` (credential panel copy only); `src/standalone/operator.ts` (GitHub source paragraph ~300, adjacent to #1006's form fields); `src/cli/source.ts` (only if a readback row changes; expected test-only). Only #1003 touches `web/src/project-setup.tsx`, `web/src/ready-check.tsx`, `web/src/setup-model.ts`, the docs, `design/design.pen` and `design/DESIGN.md`. #1003 does not touch `githubConfiguration()`, `github.configure`, the table definition or the migration.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 → T5, and the graph is acyclic. T1 and T2 both edit `src/operator/contracts.ts`; T3 needs both contracts; T4 shares `web/` and its readback tests with T3; T5 documents the final behaviour. All slices are sequential on one branch with one owner, and none may run concurrently.

#### 1. `project.create` records an explicit setup source credential

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** #1006 merged; branch rebased per Guardrails.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/domain.ts` (`project.create` schema; `DomainStore.apply` `"project.create"` insert); `src/operator/contracts.ts` (operator `project.create` schema); `test/operator/project-setup.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/operator/project-setup.test.ts` through `OperatorApi.execute`:
(a) `create({ sourceCredentialRef: "gh:github.com" })` gives `githubConfiguration(id).credentialRef === "gh:github.com"`, `version === 1`, and zero `project_github_active` rows (with a linked `githubProject`). After `f.service.stop()/start()` the value is unchanged and the exact replay returns the identical receipt.
(b) A create without the field still records `null`, and the receipt and replay are unchanged. Assert that the command object has no `sourceCredentialRef` key.
(c) Projects that exist before re-running `migrate()` keep an existing `NULL`, a cleared reference (set then `github.configure` with `credentialRef: null`) and an `env:NAME` reference unchanged after restart.
(d) `sourceCredentialRef: "env:X"`, `"gh:other.host"` and `null` are rejected as invalid input, with nothing recorded.
**Implementation:** Add `sourceCredentialRef: z.literal("gh:github.com").optional()` to both `project.create` schemas. Bind the insert's `credentialRef` to `command.sourceCredentialRef ?? null`. Make no other domain changes.
**Validate:** From the repository root, with Node from `.node-version` on PATH, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/project-setup.test.js`; expect every test to pass, including the new cases (a)–(d).
**Complete when:** a setup create persists `gh:github.com` at version 1, legacy creates and existing sources are byte-identical, and the focused file passes.

#### 2. Discovery status reports the candidate source login

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the branch (shared `contracts.ts`).
**Files and symbols:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`discoveryStatusSchema`: add `sourceGh: ghLoginStateSchema`); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`readDiscoveryStatus`); `test/operator/operator-setup-api.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/operator/operator-setup-api.test.ts`, use a fake gh via the service `ghExecutable` and assert `GET /api/operator/discovery` `data.sourceGh` for each case:
- signed-in gives `{ state: "signed-in", login: "octo" }`;
- `set("not-signed-in")` gives `not-signed-in`;
- the missing executable gives `not-installed`;
