`gh.commands()` contains no `token` invocation for these reads, and the response text contains neither token nor `GH_TOKEN`.
**Implementation:** In `readDiscoveryStatus`, add a second detection with `{ executable: this.setup.ghExecutable, environment: ghEnvironment(this.domain(), { reference: "gh:github.com" }) }`. Run it through one request-local `GhLoginScope` together with the existing discovery probe. Leave `configured`/`available`/`source`/`gh` unchanged. #### 3. Guided setup shows and records the default; ready check shows the credential

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T1 and T2 on the branch.
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/project-setup.tsx`: read discovery status regardless of discovery state, keep `ghLogin` gating for the 117b discovery offer, add `sourceGh` state, a "GitHub source credential" line, and the `sourceCredentialRef` field on submit, and rewrite the stale comment/copy "only for discovery"/"never uses a login the operator did not choose". `web/src/ready-check.tsx` gets a recorded-facts credential line from a project configuration read. `web/src/setup-model.ts` gets a new pure `sourceCredentialLine(credential)` returning text plus an optional settings link. Tests: `test/operator/operator-setup-model.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`, `test/fixtures/setup-browser.ts` if its discovery-status stub needs `sourceGh`.
**Test:**
- **Model test:** `sourceCredentialLine` gives these lines:

The recorded `project.create` body (read via the receipt or `/api/operator/projects/:id/configuration`) has `source.credential.source === "gh"`. The ready check lists "GitHub source credential: GitHub CLI · @octo", and Resume enablement is unchanged.

A failed discovery-status read counts as not signed in. The ready check uses `useOperatorResource` on `/api/operator/projects/${projectId}/configuration` with `projectConfigurationSchema` and refreshes with "Check again". The ready check does not change `readyCheckItems`/`blocked`.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npx playwright install chromium` if browsers are absent, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-setup-model.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-setup-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/project-setup.test.js`; expect all tests to pass.
**Complete when:** fresh setup with a usable login persists and shows `gh:github.com`, an unusable login records nothing and is visibly unconfigured in the ready check, and the focused files pass.

#### 4. Source settings, HTML fallback and CLI read back the same choice

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3.
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/source-config.tsx` (credential panel description ~639: say that new projects created in setup start with the detected GitHub CLI login when usable, and that discovery credentials are separate); `src/standalone/operator.ts` (GitHub source paragraph ~300: state the persisted kind as "GitHub CLI"/"environment variable"/"not configured", matching `src/cli/source.ts`, and drop "choosing it is explicit"); `src/cli/source.ts` (no change expected; edit only if readback differs). Tests: `test/sources/operator-source-credential-browser.test.ts`, `test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.ts`, `test/sources/operator-cli-source.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- **Source browser test:** add a case starting from a project created with `sourceCredentialRef: "gh:github.com"`.
  - The GitHub tab shows the configured GitHub CLI account with Change and Clear.
  - Cancel restores the reference.
  - Clear saves version 2 with `credentialRef: null`, and after a reload it stays cleared with no re-default.
  - Change to `env:NAME` saves version 3.
- **HTML and CLI readback:** extend the case at `test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.ts` (~94) or `operator-cli-source.test.ts`. For the setup-created project, `GET /api/operator/projects/:id/configuration` `source.credential.source`, the HTML project page, and the CLI source view all report GitHub CLI / @octo. After Clear, all three report not configured.
- Keep existing assertions such as `/Detected GitHub CLI account @octo/` passing, or update their copy.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/sources/operator-source-credential-browser.test.js dist/test/sources/operator-cli-source-activation.test.js dist/test/sources/operator-cli-source.test.js dist/test/sources/github-source-credential.test.js`; expect all tests to pass, with `github-source-credential.test.js` unchanged.
**Complete when:** Change, Clear and Cancel work on a defaulted source, and the UI, HTML fallback and CLI agree on the persisted choice.

#### 5. Amend ADR-1009, SPEC, the operations guide and the design

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T4`
**Prerequisites:** T4 (final copy settled).
**Files and symbols:**
- `docs/adr/1009-project-setup-discovery.md` ("Discovery" paragraph "Detection only offers the login…", and "Linking a GitHub Project" paragraph "Detection alone chooses nothing").
- `docs/SPEC.md` (~563-575, "The service never uses a login the operator did not choose", and the project GitHub sources paragraph).
- `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` (~226-243, "GitHub source credential").
- `design/design.pen` via Pen MCP only: setup 115 `wk678`/117 `bkNmZ` source credential line; ready check 146 `UdnEc`/146b `PFBIv`/147 `akpq9` credential line; 119 `w0ozf` description.
- `design/DESIGN.md` ("Guided project setup", "Ready check (146, 146b, 147)" and the 119/119b notes).
**Implementation:** Revise each document in place to the new contract, with no dated or amendment sections:
- Discovery stays explicit.
- Guided setup records `gh:github.com` for the new project's source when the candidate login is signed in, and shows the account.
- Otherwise the source starts unconfigured, and the ready check says so.
- No resolution fallback; existing/cleared sources are never changed.
- HTML-fallback and CLI creates record no default.

Edit the design with the Pen MCP server. Make `design/design.pen` the active Pen window, run `osascript scripts/pen-save-all.applescript`, and confirm its modification time or hash changed. Refresh `design/DESIGN.md` through MCP. If the Pen MCP server or the save script is unavailable, stop and report a human-required blocker; never parse or hand-edit the `.pen` file.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run format:check && rg -n "never uses a login the operator did not choose|Detection alone chooses nothing|choosing it is explicit" docs design/DESIGN.md src web`; expect formatting to pass and `rg` to print no matches (exit 1). Confirm the `design/design.pen` hash differs from base with `git diff --stat -- design/design.pen`.
**Complete when:** the ADR, SPEC, guide, Pen design and DESIGN.md describe the shipped behaviour, and the design file is saved and changed.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Usable offered gh login configures a new project's source with `gh:github.com`, and the UI states the account | 1, 2, 3 | T1 (a); T2 signed-in case; T3 signed-in browser journey |
| No default when gh is missing, not signed in or unreadable, or when `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` override with an invalid token; no fallback | 2, 3, 4 | T2 not-installed/not-signed-in/invalid-override cases; T3 not-signed-in journey; `github-source-credential.test.js` unchanged in T4 |
| Existing, env-selected and cleared sources unchanged, including migration/restart | 1, 4 | T1 (b), (c); T4 Clear-and-reload case |
| Ready check shows the source credential, including missing before the first refresh; versioning, receipts and activation unchanged | 1, 3 | T1 (a), (b) receipts/version/inactive; T3 model test and ready-check browser assertions |
| Change, Clear and Cancel work; HTML fallback and CLI report the same persisted choice | 4 | T4 source browser case and HTML/CLI readback case |
| Credential exclusion/redaction and per-use resolution preserved; no token copy/cache; no access grant | 2, 4 | T2 no-`token`-command and no-token-in-body assertions; `source-credential-exclusion.test.js` in T2; final `npm run check` |
| ADR-1009, SPEC, operations guide, Pen design and DESIGN.md amended | 5 | T5 `rg` and `.pen` diff check |
| Pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check` pass | Final | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, with Node from `.node-version` and the pinned npm, on the integrated delivery candidate after rebasing onto `main` with #1006 merged: run `npm ci && npm run check`. Expect typecheck, lint, format check, build and the full test suite (both browsers) to pass.
- PR CI `check` must pass on the PR head; the base `812ecfeb` CI run 38621969701 passed every job.
- Bounded live check on the service host, with no real tokens printed: with gh signed in, create a project through `/app/settings/projects/new`. Confirm setup and the ready check show the account, and that `GET /api/operator/projects/:id/configuration` reports `source.credential.source: "gh"`, `usable: true`. Do not use or reveal a real token. Record the result in the PR description.

### Review focus

- The `sourceGh` probe uses the source candidate environment, never discovery's, and runs no `gh auth token`.
- The `project.create` hash is unchanged when the field is absent. Setup never sends the field after a failed or non-signed-in read.
- The ready-check credential line cannot affect `blocked`/Resume. Copy across setup, source settings, HTML, CLI and docs no longer claims the login is used only for discovery or only after explicit choice.

### Re-plan triggers

- `gh auth status` in the candidate environment reports `signed-in` for an invalid `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` override, so detection alone cannot satisfy the no-default AC. content.title: Power admission stays held because the pmset log header is treated as malformed

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Recognise the macOS pmset preamble without accepting unfamiliar power-history lines.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, the production `parsePmsetPowerLog` returned `complete: true` for the supplied timestamped Start row alone and `complete: false` when preceded by the supplied Time stamp header, separator and `UUID: (null)` rows. An unfamiliar untimestamped row also returned incomplete. A bounded call to the real `MacPowerEventSource.readSince(null)` on this host returned `complete: false, cursor: null` in about 8.9 seconds. The existing power tests passed. The fixture isolates header handling; the live failure is consistent with it, but the full live stream was not independently classified in this triage.

**Desired behavior:** Accept the recognised column header, separator and UUID preamble before timestamped rows. Continue to reject unfamiliar or misplaced records, malformed timestamps, ordering violations and unavailable cursor history. Valid input must allow power supervision to establish its baseline without disabling supervision.

**Key interfaces:** Incremental pmset line parser, `parsePmsetPowerLog`, `MacPowerEventSource.readSince` and persisted power-event cursors.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] The supplied macOS header produces a complete baseline and works with streamed input.
- [ ] Negative tests retain rejection of unfamiliar untimestamped rows and invalid power-event history; recognised preamble handling is limited to the intended position.
- [ ] Baseline/follow-up cursors remain valid, including the line-index contribution of skipped header rows.
- [ ] A bounded read-only live baseline and follow-up on the affected macOS host both return complete, recording host version, duration and cursor/result status.
- [ ] Preserve existing power admission and conservative recovery controls. Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Disabling power supervision, sleep/wake manipulation, physical power qualification, changes to containment guarantees or log-tail/timeout optimisation. Track demonstrated read-margin problems separately.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none
**Semantic payload digest:** sha256:280a60b83b0289f4dfaff5c4dd2eaccd9c58666fa81ac3ba3c303f008e049072

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1000
**Planned against:** `main` at `812ecfeb94cd99bbbb1ae61da3c9f5faff48f442`
**Planned branch:** `cb/issue-1000-pmset-header` (cut from that SHA; does not exist yet)
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Teach the incremental pmset parser (`createPmsetParser`, `src/standalone/power.ts`) to accept the macOS 27 column header, `=====` separator and `UUID:` line as an ordered preamble that is valid only before the first timestamped row. Every other untimestamped line stays malformed. Cover it with parser, streamed-reader and `ExecutionPower` tests in `test/operations/power.test.ts`, then prove the real `MacPowerEventSource` on this macOS 27 host with a read-only script. No production code outside the parser changes.

### Guardrails

- Unchanged: `knownPmsetSummary` and the `Assertion status system-wide:` summary handling; timestamp ordering and malformed-timestamp rejection; sleep/wake-keyword rejection of unknown rows; cursor formats (`pmset-time:<ms>`, `pmset-event:<ms>:<lineIndex>:<hash16>`) and `lineIndex` counting every raw line, including preamble lines; `ExecutionPower` admission, hold and reconciliation logic; `MacPowerEventSource` bounds (10 s timeout, 64 KiB line, default reader `spawnPowerLogReader`).
- Out of scope (issue #1000 brief): disabling power supervision, sleep/wake manipulation, physical power qualification, containment changes, and log-tail or timeout optimisation (see Planning decisions). Do not change `docs/evidence/` records.
- Authority and mutation: the live check must run only `/usr/bin/pmset -g log` through the real reader, plus `sw_vers`. It must not run any `pmset` setter, `pmset schedule`, `sleepnow`, `caffeinate` or service start/stop, and must not touch `~/Library` or service state. No GitHub mutation other than the delivery PR.
- **Plan-mismatch budget (one diagnosis, two repair cycles).** Only a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption consumes it. That means: the preamble is not the only rejected content on this host (the live read or the classifier still fails for a line class other than `Time stamp`, `=====`, `UUID:`); `createPmsetParser` is not the single parse path for `MacPowerEventSource` and `parsePmsetPowerLog`; or acceptance cannot be met without changing cursor format, `lineIndex` semantics or `ExecutionPower`. On that evidence: one focused diagnosis, at most two repair cycles, then stop and request a replan with the evidence.
- **Ordinary implementation defects do not consume that budget.** Test-fixture mistakes, regex or off-by-one repairs in the new code, integration or typecheck/lint/format failures, documentation, CI or flake repairs, and live-script bugs stay with the ticket owner and are fixed in place. Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence.
- Investigate unknown overlap with new work on `power.ts`. Stop for a material design or contract change (for example any change to what counts as complete history beyond the preamble) or an exhausted grant.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. An integration amendment is only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Preamble position and order.** Accept, in order and each at most once, only while no timestamped row has been accepted and the assertion summary has not begun: (0) the column header, (1) the separator, (2) the `UUID:` line. A stage counter in the parser enforces order. A header after a timestamped row, a duplicate, a `UUID:` without the header and separator before it, or any other untimestamped text stays `malformed`. This keeps the brief's "intended position" and fails closed on unfamiliar output. Evidence: on this host (macOS 27.0.1, 26A434) `pmset -g log` is 179,945 lines / 41.2 MB, with exactly one header block at lines 2–4 (0-based), and the production parser returns complete `false`. The same text with lines 2–4 removed returns `true`. The only other untimestamped lines are blank lines and the final `Assertion status system-wide:` summary, which are already accepted.
- **Patterns** (tested against trimmed lines; the real header has tab and space padding): header `^Time stamp\s+Domain\s+Message\b.*\bDuration\s+Delay$`, separator `^=+(?:\s+=+)*$`, UUID `^UUID: (?:\(null\)|<8-4-4-4-12 hex>)$`. Only `(null)` is observed; a well-formed hex UUID is accepted too because it is the same record shape, and anything else is rejected.
- **Cursor validity.** `lineIndex` already increments for every raw line before any classification, so skipping preamble lines keeps whole-output and streamed indices identical. In the fixture the lines are 0 `PM ASL`, 1 blank, 2 header, 3 separator, 4 UUID, 5 the first Assertions row, 6 Sleep, 7 Wake, so the Sleep event cursor carries index 6. A test asserts this and that a cursor with a shifted index is rejected.
- **Tail-read follow-up: out of scope.** The brief lists "log-tail/timeout optimisation" as out of scope and says to track demonstrated read-margin problems separately. A tail read would also have to preserve whole-output line indices in persisted event cursors, which is a cursor-contract change. The margin is real: two planning-time production-default reads took 9.6 s and 9.9 s against the 10 s timeout, and a third `pmset -g log` took 23 s wall time under load. The live check therefore records durations and distinguishes a timeout from a parse failure (T2). The controller should open a separate issue if the margin fails again.
- **Live check is evidence, not a repo change.** Results go in the PR body (macOS version and build, duration, result and cursor status of both reads); no new file in `docs/evidence/`. No user-visible contract changes, and `rg -in "pmset|power-event" docs README.md CONTEXT.md` finds no parser description to update; the implementer re-runs that grep to confirm.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/power.ts` — `createPmsetParser(requested)` (line ~66): `line()` increments `lineIndex`, returns early on `unusable`, the `Assertion status system-wide:` summary and `knownPmsetSummary`, then requires `timestampPrefix`, otherwise sets `malformed`. `finish()` returns `rejected()` when `malformed`. Callers: `parsePmsetPowerLog` (whole text split on `/\r?\n/`) and `MacPowerEventSource.readSince`, which feeds streamed lines from `spawnPowerLogReader`. `ExecutionPower.pollUnlocked` holds with "Power-event history is incomplete or ambiguous" when `batch.complete` is false, and on a complete baseline with no events it calls `setPowerCursorBaseline`.
- **New:** `src/standalone/power.ts` — three module-level preamble patterns (an ordered tuple) and a `preambleStage` counter inside `createPmsetParser`, checked in `line()` after the summary and `knownPmsetSummary` returns and before the `timestampPrefix` match, guarded by `earliestTimestamp === undefined`.
- **Follow:** `test/operations/power.test.ts` — "macOS pmset source accepts ordered sleep/wake rows…" (`readLog` fixture generator, `MacPowerEventSource(readLog, …, () => baselineMs)`), the streamed-parity test using `spawnPowerLogReader` with `printLines` and CRLF/trailing newline variants, and "a complete cursor can establish an idle baseline…" (`powerStore`, `ExecutionPower`, `CaffeinateAssertion(() => new FakeChild())`).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 -> T2 -> final validation; acyclic. Both tasks touch the same two files or the same evidence run, so nothing runs concurrently; one owner does both.

#### 1. Accept the macOS 27 preamble only before the first row

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none. The baseline is green on this exact SHA (trusted CI run 38621969701 on `main`, jobs `quality`, all `node24-*`, `node26-service-*` and `check` succeeded), so do not rerun the full suite before editing.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/power.ts` (`createPmsetParser`, new preamble patterns); `test/operations/power.test.ts` (new tests next to the existing pmset tests, around lines 836–1010).
**Test:** In `test/operations/power.test.ts`:
1. Add `macos27Preamble` and `macos27Rows` fixtures: `PM ASL data store: /var/log/powermanagement`, blank, `Time stamp` + 16 spaces + `Domain` + padding + `\tMessage` + padding + `\tDuration  \tDelay     `, a `==========` line with the same tab layout, `UUID: (null)`, then the existing ordered Assertions/Sleep/Wake rows and the trailing `Assertion status system-wide:` summary.
2. "macOS 27 preamble gives a complete baseline and follow-up": `MacPowerEventSource(readLog, …, () => baselineMs)` over the fixture. Assert baseline `complete` and cursor `pmset-time:<baselineMs>`; the follow-up is `complete` with events `["sleep","wake", …]` and `previousCursor` chaining as in the existing test; the Sleep event cursor's line index is `6` and the Wake's is `7`.
3. Streamed parity: through `spawnPowerLogReader` with `printLines` for `\n` and `\r\n`, with and without a trailing newline, `batch` deep-equals `parsePmsetPowerLog(text.join(eol), baseline.cursor)`. Resuming from `batch.events[0].cursor` returns only later events. A cursor whose index is shifted down by 3 (as if the three preamble lines were uncounted) returns `complete: false`.
4. Negative table, each expected `complete: false` from `parsePmsetPowerLog(…, powerCursor("pmset-time:<ms>"))` and a `null` cursor where relevant: header after a timestamped row; separator after a timestamped row; `UUID: (null)` after a timestamped row; a duplicated header; `UUID:` directly after `PM ASL` (stage skip); separator before header; `UUID: not-a-uuid`; an unfamiliar line such as `Domain: surprise` in the preamble; the macOS 27 preamble followed by an out-of-order timestamp; `UnknownWakeSummary` as in the existing test.
5. `ExecutionPower` baseline: copy the idle-baseline test, with `new MacPowerEventSource(readLogOverMacos27Fixture)` as the event source, `poll()` once, and assert `admissionHeld() === false`. Add the same fixture with the header after the first row and assert `admissionHeld() === true`.
6. Sensitivity: before editing `power.ts`, build and run the new tests and confirm that the positive cases (2, 3, 5) fail and the negative cases pass on the unmodified parser. Record this as the actual testing order.
**Implementation:** In `src/standalone/power.ts` add

```ts
const pmsetPreamble = [
  /^Time stamp\s+Domain\s+Message\b.*\bDuration\s+Delay$/,
  /^=+(?:\s+=+)*$/,
  /^UUID: (?:\(null\)|[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}(?:-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}){3}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{12})$/,
];
```

In `createPmsetParser` add `let preambleStage = 0;`. In `line()`, after `const normalized = trimmed.trim();` and before the `timestampPrefix.exec`, add: if `earliestTimestamp === undefined && pmsetPreamble[preambleStage]?.test(normalized)` then `preambleStage++` and `return`. `lineIndex++` stays at the top of `line()` so skipped lines still count. Do not touch `knownPmsetSummary`, `finish()`, `parsePmsetPowerLog`, `MacPowerEventSource` or `ExecutionPower`. Add a one-line comment saying why the preamble is accepted only once and only before the first row.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, with Node from `.node-version` and `npm ci` done, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operations/power.test.js`; expect `fail 0` and the new tests listed as passing. Then `npx biome lint --error-on-warnings src/standalone/power.ts test/operations/power.test.ts` and `npx biome format src/standalone/power.ts test/operations/power.test.ts` with no diagnostics, and `npm run typecheck` clean.
**Complete when:** the focused power test file passes including all new positive and negative cases, and the sensitivity run shows the positive cases failing before the parser change.

#### 2. Bounded live check of the real reader on macOS 27

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 complete and `npm run build:service` re-run so `dist/src/standalone/power.js` contains the change. The host is macOS 27 with `/usr/bin/pmset`; it was 27.0.1 (26A434) at planning time.
**Files and symbols:** no repo file changes. Runs `MacPowerEventSource` (default reader, `/usr/bin/pmset -g log`) from `dist/src/standalone/power.js`.
**Implementation:** From the checkout root, run exactly this. It reads `pmset -g log` twice (a baseline and a follow-up from the baseline cursor), writes nothing, and each read is killed by the reader's own timeout. The expected wall time is under 30 s.

```sh
sw_vers
node --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { MacPowerEventSource } from "./dist/src/standalone/power.js";
const timeoutMs = Number(process.env.PMSET_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 10_000);
const source = new MacPowerEventSource(undefined, timeoutMs);
const read = async (cursor) => {
  const started = performance.now();
  const batch = await source.readSince(cursor);
  return { batch, result: {
    complete: batch.complete,
    cursor: batch.cursor?.value ?? null,
    events: batch.events.length,
    seconds: Number(((performance.now() - started) / 1000).toFixed(1)),
  } };
};
const baseline = await read(null);
const followUp = await read(baseline.batch.cursor);
console.log(JSON.stringify({ timeoutMs, baseline: baseline.result, followUp: followUp.result }, null, 2));
process.exit(baseline.result.complete && followUp.result.complete ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

Interpretation. Pass: exit 0 with both `complete: true` and the baseline cursor `pmset-time:<ms>`. If a result is incomplete with `seconds` at or above 9.5, suspect the reader timeout, not the parser: rerun once with `PMSET_TIMEOUT_MS=60000` prefixed to `node`, and record both runs. A pass only at 60 s is a recorded read-margin finding to report for a separate issue, and still satisfies this acceptance row. If a result is incomplete in under 9.5 s, treat it as a parse failure: save `/usr/bin/pmset -g log` once to a file in the session scratchpad and run the parser over it line by line to name the first rejected line. If that line is not in the preamble, this is a plan-mismatch (see Guardrails). Do not paste log contents into the PR, only the line class.
**Validate:** The command above exits 0 on macOS 27. Record in the PR body: `sw_vers` version and build, `timeoutMs`, each read's `complete`, `seconds` and cursor status, and the follow-up event count.
**Complete when:** a recorded live run shows both reads `complete: true` on macOS 27, with the host version and durations in the PR body.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| The parser accepts the Time stamp, `=====` and `UUID:` preamble before timestamped rows, and unfamiliar untimestamped lines are still rejected | 1 | T1 tests 2 and 4 |

content.title: Explain why imported GitHub tasks are Draft under the readiness rule

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Explain the effect of each GitHub selection's readiness rule using stored observations.

**Current behavior and verification:** At main `812ecfeb`, an isolated production-service/SQLite fixture imported two open issues, one matching `label ready` and one not. Source observations exposed completeness and timestamps but no item counts; the unready task exposed `task-unready` without naming the missing condition. Reading observations, project and task data kept the fake provider selection-read count at one. A subsequent incomplete refresh remained explicitly `partial`. This confirms the read-model gap; the warnings were not reproduced in a browser.

**Desired behavior:** Show observed/open/readiness-matching counts per selection and explain why an imported open task is unready. When open observed items exist but none match, Sync and the GitHub source tab warn and link to the relevant readiness configuration. Calculate from persisted provider observations/memberships, without fetching additional provider data.

**Key interfaces:** Source-observation and task-read contracts; stored GitHub issue/selection membership observations; readiness all/any label and Project-field evaluation; Sync, GitHub source configuration and task reason presentation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Each selection reports distinct observed, open and readiness-matching item counts with its configured condition, including the zero-match case.
- [ ] Sync and the GitHub source tab show the zero-match warning and a working configuration link.
- [ ] Imported open Draft tasks name unmet conditions accurately for both all/any rules; do not imply that a readiness match satisfies other admission controls.
- [ ] Never/partial/unavailable observations retain truthful completeness and credential/redaction boundaries. Counts do not imply a complete provider total when the observation is incomplete.
- [ ] No extra provider selection/status reads are introduced by the counts or explanations; verify with a counted fake reader.
- [ ] Coordinate with #1006 so skipped closed observations can still contribute to “observed” counts without requiring a task. Preserve membership deduplication.
- [ ] Cover API, affected web surfaces and CLI task/source presentation; run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Choosing #1001's no-rule policy, changing the configured readiness rule, granting readiness, automatic admission or additional provider polling. #1001 settles an absent rule as no readiness filtering; explanations must distinguish unavailable/redacted rule knowledge from a genuinely absent filter.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1002
**Planned against:** `main` at `07d9e553ac12b61598d7b10c76e1f587ae5e1863`
**Planned branch:** `cb/issue-1002-readiness-counts`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Requirements: the issue body's acceptance criteria and the [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1002#issuecomment-6177452757). Sequencing: this ticket lands **after #1006** ([approved plan](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1006#issuecomment-6179258232)); implement on a branch rebased on the merged #1006. #1004 (PR #1014) and #1001 may land before or after; see Planning decisions.

### Approach

Add one read-only projection of stored GitHub observations, shared by every surface. No new provider read, endpoint or table.

- `src/core` gets a pure `evaluateReadiness(rule | null, facts)` that `updateReadiness` also uses, so the counts and the task reason cannot drift from the real readiness predicate. `GitHubSourceStore` gains `selectionCounts(projectId, selectionId)` and `taskReadiness(taskId)`.
- `github_sync_state` gains an integer `skippedClosed` that the (#1006) Skip-mode branch of `reconcileSelection` sets on complete reads. It lets "observed" include closed issues that were skipped and never became tasks.
- The operator API adds `readiness` (the rule as `none | unavailable | rule`) and per-selection `counts` to source observations, and a per-task `source.readiness` (`matched | unmet | not-evaluated` plus the unmet conditions) to the task list summary and task read.
- One text module, `src/operator/readiness-text.ts`, renders counts, the zero-match warning and the unmet reason for the Sync tab, the GitHub source tab, the phone state card, the HTML fallback and the CLI. Task List, Board and detail use the same unmet text.

### Guardrails

- Counts and reasons are read-only projections of persisted `github_external_issues`, `github_memberships`, `github_sync_state` and the stored readiness rule. They add no provider selection/status read, no domain command or receipt, no readiness grant, no admission change and no new task state. "Matches the rule" never means Ready or admissible: activation, completeness, dependencies, holds, repository access and capacity still apply, and no copy may imply otherwise.
- Truthful completeness: counts are shown only for `complete` and `partial` observations; `never` and `unavailable` have `counts: null`. A partial read labels its counts as possibly incomplete and shows no zero-match warning. Counts are per selection and never summed across selections, so one issue in two selections is one task and counts once in each selection.
- Credential/redaction boundary: a readiness rule that the existing exclusion check withholds (`exact(JSON.stringify(rule), excluded) === null`) is `unavailable`, never `none`, and then `matching` is `null` and no condition text is sent. "No rule" (`none`) is only ever derived from a stored `null` rule, never from redaction, an empty condition list or a failed read.
- Out of scope: choosing or changing the no-rule policy or stored representation (#1001), the closed-issue mode and closure states (#1006), the Active/Inactive badge and the activation message (#1004), changing a readiness rule, automatic admission, extra polling, `design/design.pen`, the Settings index list, the CLI `task list` table, and the paused X01–X08 work.
- `src/core` stays host-independent (ADR-1003). Delivery uses `npm ci` and `npm run check` on the pinned Node (`.node-version` 24.21.0). Tests use real SQLite and the fake reader fixtures; name them by behaviour under the AGENTS.md grouping. Register browser-dependent cases through `browserSuite`/`browserTest`.
- Plan-mismatch budget versus ordinary repairs:
  - **Plan mismatch:** a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption. Examples: the #1006 Skip branch in `reconcileSelection` cannot expose the distinct set of skipped node IDs; `evaluateReadiness` cannot reproduce `updateReadiness` results for existing fixtures; `OperatorApi` cannot reach the store methods named here; a named symbol or file does not own the stated behaviour. This gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles under to-plan's allowance. After that, stop and report for replanning.
  - **Ordinary defects:** integration, test, fixture, documentation, type/lint and CI repairs. These stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget. In particular, adding the new required fields to hand-built fixtures, rebasing onto #1006/#1004/#1001, resolving textual conflicts and renewing evidence are ordinary work.
  - Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record each correction and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **What the counts mean (with #1006).** Per selection, from stored data and the latest sync state:
  - `observed` = distinct stored memberships of that selection (open or closed) + `closedSkipped`.
  - `open` = those memberships whose issue has `observedState='open'`. Open issues are never skipped, so on a complete read `open` is exact.
  - `closedSkipped` = distinct closed issues the Skip mode did not import on the latest **complete** read of that selection. #1006's plan persists no skipped observation and says #1002 owns its count labels. The brief requires skipped closed observations to count as observed without a task. A single integer on `github_sync_state` satisfies both with no per-issue data and no task. It is recomputed (set, not incremented) on each complete read, so a reopened issue (imported on that read) leaves it. A partial read leaves it unchanged, exactly as partial reads leave memberships unpruned. Done mode imports closed issues, so it writes 0 and they count through memberships.
  - `matching` = open memberships whose labels/Project fields satisfy the rule (see next decision). `null` when the rule is `unavailable`.
  - `complete` = the sync state's `complete`.
  - Closed issues imported before #1006, or closed after import, stay in `observed` through their membership. If #1006 changed before merge to persist skipped observations, count those instead of adding `skippedClosed`; that is a routine integration, not a plan mismatch.
- **Rule view and the null-rule case (#1001).** The API exposes `readiness: {kind:'none'} | {kind:'unavailable'} | {kind:'rule', mode, conditions}` per project in source observations and per task. `evaluateReadiness(null, …)` is explicitly `satisfied` (no filtering, #1001's decision), and every renderer handles `none` ("no readiness rule: all N open items match", no warning). At `07d9e553` the stored rule is never null, so `none` is produced only by unit and presentation tests until #1001 lands. The server derives the view from the **core** rule (`GitHubSourceStore.readinessRule(projectId): Readiness | null`, a private reader of `project_github_sources.readiness`), not from the project-read `readiness` field, which uses `null` for redaction today. If #1001 has merged first, that reader must delegate to #1001's explicit null handling and `updateReadiness` keeps #1001's branch. Do not re-derive "absent" from an empty condition list.
- **Per-task reason.** `outcome` is `unmet` only when the issue is open, has a membership in the task's project and the rule is not satisfied. `unmet` lists the unsatisfied conditions (all-mode) or every condition (any-mode). `not-evaluated` covers closed, withdrawn (no membership) and `unavailable`. Copy, from the shared module:
  - all-mode: ``Not Ready: missing label `ready` ``; several: `missing label `a`, label `b``; Project field: ``missing Project field <fieldNodeId> = <optionNodeId>``.
  - any-mode: ``Not Ready: needs any of label `a`, label `b` ``.
  - Matched, closed, withdrawn and unavailable tasks keep today's generic "Draft: not Ready" (no rule claim). Local tasks are unchanged. Board placement is unchanged ("Source status never determines grouping", ui03-tasks.md:41), so only the reason text changes.
- **Zero-match warning** = counts present, `complete`, `open > 0`, `matching === 0`, rule kind `rule`. Text: "No open item matches the readiness rule (<rule>); imported tasks stay Draft until one does." Link: `/app/projects/<id>/settings?tab=github#source-readiness` (same-page `#source-readiness` on the GitHub tab). The Readiness `fieldset` gets `id="source-readiness"`; `SourceTab` focuses it on mount when the hash matches, because the content renders after the async read and the browser would not scroll.
- **Where the GitHub tab gets observations.** `ProjectConfiguration` (`web/src/project-config.tsx`) already loads `/api/operator/source-observations`; pass the same `observations` resource to `SourceTab`.
- **Required fields.** The new fields are required on the strict response schemas (repo style); hand-built fixtures are updated. The cost is a few indexed SQLite queries per selection and per imported task, with no network access.
- **Design gap.** `design/DESIGN.md` frames 118–121 draw no counts line, warning or reason text. Reuse the existing `settings-row` body text, `StatusBadge` and `role="status"` patterns. Do not edit `design.pen`. Add a short text note about the production addition beside the existing frame 118–121 notes in DESIGN.md (as #1004's PR does for its deviation), and flag the missing frames in the PR.
- **Shared regions (resolve on rebase; no plan change needed).**
  - #1006: `src/core/github-source.ts` `migrate`, the `reconcileSelection` new-issue branch, the final `github_sync_state` upsert and `updateReadiness`; `src/operator/contracts.ts` `taskSourceSummarySchema` and the task-read `source` (it adds `closure`; add `readiness` beside it); `operator-api.ts` `sourceSummary` and `source()`; `web/src/tasks.ts` `reasonLabels`/`taskReasons`; `web/src/task-overview.ts` `taskStatusLine`; `web/src/source-config.tsx` panel 2; `src/standalone/operator.ts` project form and task page; `src/cli/main.ts` `task get`; `src/cli/source.ts`. A `closure: held | completed` task has `observedState='closed'`, so its readiness is `not-evaluated` and never takes the unmet text; closure labels keep precedence.
  - #1004: `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` `SourceObservations` row header (~L172–197, Active/Inactive badge) and its `RefreshObservations` button, `web/src/settings-view.ts`, `web/src/settings-state.ts`, `web/src/settings.tsx`, `design/DESIGN.md`, `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md`. Add counts as a sibling **after** the `.settings-row-heading` block; do not edit the heading, the badge or the refresh button/notice. Merging #1004's duplicate refresh handler into one is a separate follow-up, not part of this ticket.
  - #1001: the readiness default and `web/src/settings-changes.ts`; this ticket touches neither. The `projectStateSummary` next-step ordering below is the only overlap with its UI copy.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source.ts` `GitHubSourceStore`:
  - `migrate` :183 (`github_sync_state` DDL :197);
  - `reconcileSelection` :567, whose complete branch prunes memberships :712 and whose final `INSERT … github_sync_state … ON CONFLICT` :749 records `complete`, `reason`, `refreshedAt`;
  - `invalidateProviderObservations` :395 (sets `complete=0`);
  - `updateReadiness` :889 (rule parse, `satisfied` per condition, `ready = memberships.length>0 && open && all/any`), called from `reconcileSelection`, `recordDeliveryClosure` and the `github.configure` handler (`src/core/domain.ts`).
- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` `readinessSchema` :49 (`conditionSchema` is module-private), `projectFieldsSchema` :4.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`:
  - `readSourceObservationsOnce` :5038 (state from `syncState`, credential status; `exclusions()` and `safe`/`exact` :683–705);
  - `sourceSummary` :2369 (called at :2478 list summary, :2561 composer dependencies, :2317 and :4267 for url only);
  - `source()` :3941 (task read);
  - project read `readiness` :4801 (null when redacted; leave unchanged).
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` `sourceObservationSchema` :2362, `taskSourceSummarySchema` :805 (used by the task list summary :838 and composer dependencies :888), task-read `source` ~:1050–1115.
- **Existing:** web `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` `SourceObservations` :148; `web/src/project-config.tsx` (observations resource :64–76, `SourceTab` rendered at :134 and defined in `web/src/source-config.tsx` :44 as `SourceTab(p: TabProps)`, `ProjectStateCards`); `web/src/source-config.tsx` ("2 · Readiness matching" panel, `fieldset` :448); `web/src/settings-view.ts` `observationLabel` :138, `projectStateSummary` :178; `web/src/tasks.ts` `reasonLabels` :151, `taskReasons` :169; `web/src/task-overview.ts` `taskStatusLine` :80; list/board render `taskReasons` in `web/src/task-views.tsx` :80.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator.ts` `project()` selection `<li>` :217 and task page :395 (reads `GitHubSourceStore` directly; no API); `src/cli/source.ts` `sourcesCommand` :88 (observations table), `src/cli/main.ts` `task get` :428.
- **New:** `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` exports `readinessConditionSchema`, types `Readiness`/`ReadinessCondition` and `evaluateReadiness`; `GitHubSourceStore.selectionCounts`, `taskReadiness`, private `readinessRule`; `src/operator/readiness-text.ts` (`conditionText`, `ruleText`, `selectionCountsText`, `zeroMatchWarning`, `unmetReason`); `web/src/observation-counts.tsx` (`ObservationCounts`); `test/sources/github-readiness-explanation.test.ts`; `test/operator/operator-readiness-text.test.ts`.
- **Follow:** `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` (a shared pure module imported by web and server); `test/sources/github-service.test.ts:37` (service plus counted fake `GitHubSourceReader`); `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts:26` (direct `reconcileSelection` snapshots); the migration pattern `PRAGMA table_info` + `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` at `src/core/domain.ts:548-588`.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:**

- Acyclic: T1 → T2 → {T3, T4, T5, T6}. Everything is blocked on #1006 being merged into the branch base.
- T3, T4, T5 and T6 touch disjoint files (T3 settings web, T4 task web, T5 CLI, T6 HTML fallback) and may run concurrently only in separate worktrees; one owner, one branch and one PR. They all read the T2 contracts and text module.

#### 1. Core readiness evaluation, counts and the skipped-closed counter

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** #1006 merged; the branch rebased on it. Read the merged `reconcileSelection` Skip branch and `migrate` first. If #1001 is merged, read its null-rule handling and reuse it.
**Files and symbols:**

- `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts`: export `readinessConditionSchema`, `Readiness`, `ReadinessCondition`; add `evaluateReadiness(rule: Readiness | null, facts: {labels: readonly string[]; fields: readonly ProjectField[]}): {satisfied: boolean; unmet: ReadinessCondition[]}`. `null` → `satisfied: true`. All-mode `unmet` = unsatisfied conditions; any-mode `unmet` = every condition when none is satisfied, else `[]`.
- `src/core/github-source.ts`:
  - `migrate`: add `skippedClosed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to `github_sync_state` (DDL for fresh DBs, plus `PRAGMA table_info` + `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` for existing ones).
  - `reconcileSelection`: collect the distinct node IDs the Skip mode leaves unimported in this call. In the final upsert set `skippedClosed = excluded.skippedClosed` only when `excluded.complete = 1`; otherwise keep the stored value (use `CASE`). Done mode writes 0.
  - `updateReadiness`: call `evaluateReadiness` with the rule, labels and the fields of all the node's memberships in the project. Behaviour unchanged.
  - Private `readinessRule(projectId)` and `readinessFacts(nodeId, projectId)` shared by the three readers below.
  - `selectionCounts(projectId, selectionId): {observed, open, closedSkipped, matching, complete} | null` (null when no sync-state row).
  - `taskReadiness(taskId): {outcome: "matched" | "unmet" | "not-evaluated"; unmet: ReadinessCondition[]} | null` (null for a non-imported task).

**Test:** `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`, direct `GitHubSourceStore.reconcileSelection` with real SQLite (fixture as at :26, a project with rule `all [label ready]` and active selections):

1. Counts: one complete snapshot with A open `[ready]`, B open `[]`, C first seen closed `[ready]`. Expect `{observed:3, open:2, closedSkipped:1, matching:1, complete:true}` in the default Skip mode. A later complete snapshot with C open expects `closedSkipped:0`, `observed:3`.
2. Closed after import: A reported closed on a later complete read → `open:1`, `matching:0`, `observed:3` (membership retained).
3. Zero match: rule `label nope`, two open issues → `{open:2, matching:0}`.
4. Partial: after a complete read, a partial snapshot (`complete:false`) keeps `closedSkipped`, keeps memberships, and reports `complete:false`. A never-synced selection returns `null`.
5. Dedup: the same issue in two selections gives each selection `observed:1`, and one task.
6. `taskReadiness`: all-mode with `[label a, project-field F=O]` lacking `a` → `unmet:[label a]`; any-mode lacking both → both conditions; matching task → `matched`, `[]`; closed issue and issue with no membership → `not-evaluated`.
7. Consistency guard: over a mixed fixture, for every imported task `taskReadiness(...).outcome === "matched"` exactly when `domain_tasks.ready = 1`.
8. Pure: `evaluateReadiness(null, anyFacts).satisfied === true` and all/any truth tables.
9. Migration: a DB whose `github_sync_state` lacks `skippedClosed` gains it with value 0 and unchanged rows.

**Implementation:** as Planning decisions (counts, rule view). The counter lives in the same transaction as the sync-state write.
**Validate:** From the repository root (Node from `.node-version` first on `PATH`), run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.js dist/test/sources/github-dependencies.test.js dist/test/sources/github-sync-race.test.js dist/test/sources/github-source-config.test.js`. Expect all pass, including the new cases and the unchanged readiness/closure tests (guarding the `updateReadiness` refactor).
**Complete when:** counts and per-task readiness reproduce the real readiness predicate for the cases above and the migration is additive.

#### 2. Contracts, API projection, shared text and docs

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 evidence (counts, `taskReadiness`, migration) passes.
**Files and symbols:**

- `src/operator/contracts.ts`:
  - `readinessRuleViewSchema` (discriminated union above) and `taskReadinessSchema` `{rule, outcome, unmet}`;
  - `sourceObservationSchema`: per project `readiness: readinessRuleViewSchema`; per selection `counts: {observed, open, closedSkipped, matching: nullable, complete}.nullable()`;

- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`:
  - private `readinessRuleView(projectId, excluded)` (none/unavailable/rule per the redaction rule);

- `src/operator/readiness-text.ts`: new pure module (see Implementation context). Counts format: ``149 observed (141 closed, not imported) · 9 open · 0 match label `ready` ``; the parenthesis only when `closedSkipped > 0`. Partial adds "partial read; counts may be incomplete". `none` → "all 9 open match (no readiness rule)". `unavailable` → "readiness match unknown (rule unavailable)".
- Docs: `docs/SPEC.md` (admission paragraph ~:194–197: read-only counts and unmet reasons from stored observations, never a readiness grant or provider read), `docs/acceptance.md` A20 (counts and warning from stored data; partial never implies a total), `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` (":19 Source observations": counts, warning, link), `design/DESIGN.md` note (see Planning decisions).

**Test:**

- `test/operator/operator-readiness-text.test.ts` (new, pure): every format: single/multiple/any/project-field, `none`, `unavailable`, partial, `closedSkipped` parenthesis, zero-match warning present only for complete + open>0 + matching 0 + rule kind, and `unmetReason` null for matched/not-evaluated.

Project rule `label ready`; one refresh returns 3 open issues without the label and 1 closed issue.
  - `readSourceObservations()` → `readiness.kind='rule'`; the selection's counts are `{observed:4, open:3, closedSkipped:1, matching:0, complete:true}`.
  - `readTaskListPage()` and `readTask(id)` → each imported task has `source.readiness` outcome `unmet` with `unmet:[label ready]`.

**Implementation:** as Planning decisions. The text module is the only place that formats counts, warnings and reasons.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-readiness-text.test.js dist/test/sources/github-readiness-explanation.test.js dist/test/sources/source-credential-exclusion.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-contracts.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-configuration.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-api.test.js`. Expect all pass.
**Complete when:** the API exposes the three-state rule, counts and per-task readiness with the redaction rule, the counted reader proves zero extra provider reads, and the docs describe them.

#### 3. Sync tab, GitHub source tab and phone state card

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 contracts and text module.
**Files and symbols:**

- `web/src/observation-counts.tsx` (new): `ObservationCounts({projectId, rule, selection, sameTab})` renders `selectionCountsText`, and the warning (`StatusBadge tone="warning"` plus the text and a link) from `zeroMatchWarning`.

**Test:**

content.title: Don't default a new GitHub source's readiness rule to label `ready`

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Make GitHub readiness an optional filter; no rule means no readiness filtering.

**Decision:** A readiness rule filters the selected source's open issues. `readiness: null` means the filter accepts all open issues with valid source membership. It does not mean “nothing Ready”. Readiness remains distinct from execution admission: activation, complete source observations, placement, repository access, dependencies, approvals, runtime availability, pauses, capacity and execution/recovery holds still apply.

**Current behavior and evidence:** On checkout `812ecfeb`, project creation and missing-source migration backfill install `all [label ready]`; source settings recreate that condition when readiness is null. Configuration/readiness validation currently requires a non-null rule with at least one condition, and the evaluator parses it unconditionally. The current read model also uses null for an unavailable/redacted rule, so absence and unavailable knowledge must be distinguishable. These are inspected code paths, not a reproduction of the proposed behavior.

**Desired behavior:** New projects and backfilled missing source rows store no filter. Settings show “No readiness rule” and create no condition until the operator adds one. Operators can add a label/Project-field filter and explicitly remove it. Non-null filters retain the supported all/any semantics. Persist and evaluate no-filter semantics explicitly rather than relying on an empty array's `every()` result.

**Key interfaces:** GitHub source configuration and persisted readiness representation; project creation/backfill; readiness evaluation and own-delivery closure reconciliation; source settings/change documents; API/CLI source reads and writes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] New projects and missing-source backfill store `readiness: null`, without a hardcoded label.
- [ ] With no rule, open issues in the selected source satisfy readiness regardless of their labels/Project fields. Closed or withdrawn issues do not become Ready solely because filtering is absent; preserve #1006's separately defined closure policy.
- [ ] Tests demonstrate that no-filter Ready tasks still wait when other admission controls block them, including incomplete source observations and dependencies.
- [ ] Adding a filter applies the existing all/any label and Project-field conditions; removing it returns to no filtering. Preserve versioned saves, activation invalidation, receipts, drafts and existing independent holds.
- [ ] Existing stored non-null filters remain unchanged, including rules using `ready` or `ready-for-agent`. Do not guess which historical rules were explicitly chosen.
- [ ] Web settings, setup, HTML fallback and CLI consistently display and round-trip no-rule state without inventing a condition. Unavailable/redacted readiness is shown as unknown and cannot be treated as proof of an absent filter.
- [ ] Update default-dependent fixtures and tests, and cover persistence/restart, filter add/remove, all/any rules and unavailable-read boundaries.
- [ ] Revise SPEC and affected user/design documentation to describe the optional readiness filter; edit Pen through MCP if its controls change and refresh DESIGN.md.
- [ ] Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing task selection queries, choosing labels automatically, #1002's counts/warnings, source credential defaults, bypassing admission controls, removing holds or reinterpreting existing saved filters.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1001
**Planned against:** `main` at `3e53073e28cec4a5940f93adef147c7ad0de03e9`
**Planned branch:** `cb/issue-1001-no-default-readiness`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Requirements: the issue body's Decision and acceptance criteria, and the [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1001#issuecomment-6177655008) (`readiness: null` means no readiness filtering). The issue's Decision is the accepted contract. Sequencing: implement **after #1006 merges** ([approved plan](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1006#issuecomment-6179258232)). Branch from the then-current `main` and re-verify the shared regions below. #1002 ([plan](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1002#issuecomment-6179873529)) and #1003 ([plan](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1003#issuecomment-6179715732)) may land before or after; see Planning decisions.

### Approach

Make the readiness rule an optional filter with one explicit representation, `null`, from storage to every surface.

- **Core.** The stored `project_github_sources.readiness` text keeps its `NOT NULL` column. The no-rule value is the JSON text `null`, parsed by `readinessSchema.nullable()`. `project.create` and the missing-source backfill write it. `GitHubSourceStore.updateReadiness`, `recordDeliveryClosure` and the agent label/field guard in `DeliveryStore.authorize` each get an explicit `rule === null` branch. `readinessSchema` is unchanged and still rejects an empty condition list.
- **Command.** `github.configure` carries `readiness: rule | null`. It stays required: every configure states the rule, so a null removes the filter explicitly.
- **Read.** The project configuration read changes `source.readiness` from `rule | null` to `{kind:"none"} | {kind:"unavailable"} | {kind:"rule", mode, conditions}`. Today `null` means redacted. The new view makes "no rule" and "unknown" distinct, so redaction can never be shown as an absent filter.
- **Surfaces.** The web settings form, HTML fallback and CLI read and write that shape and invent no condition. Docs describe the optional filter.

### Guardrails

- A rule filters; the absence of a rule filters nothing. With no rule, an issue is Ready when the task is imported, open and has a current membership, regardless of labels or Project fields. A closed or withdrawn issue is never Ready merely because filtering is absent. Readiness never bypasses `DomainStore.admission`: source completeness (`source-unknown`), activation, `source-hold`, imported blockers, local dependencies, placement, repository access and approvals still apply. Do not change those controls, selection queries or Ready-gated holds.
- Do not rewrite stored data. Existing non-null rules stay byte-identical, including `label ready` and `label ready-for-agent`. The migration only inserts a row where a project has none (`INSERT OR IGNORE`). Do not guess which historical rules were chosen. Nothing in this ticket needs a data-change decision beyond the acceptance criteria.
- No-filter must be explicit. Never encode "no filter" as an empty `conditions` array, `every()` on an empty array, a sentinel label or an omitted field. `readinessSchema` keeps `conditions.min(1).max(20)` and still rejects an empty list. In the web form, an empty condition list maps to `null` only in `sourceCommand`, the command-building seam.
- Unavailable (redacted) readiness is never proof of an absent filter: it never maps to `none` and never shows "No readiness rule".
- Out of scope: #1002's counts, warnings and per-task unmet reasons, #1006's closed-issue mode and closure states, #1003's credential default, choosing labels automatically, source credential defaults, removing holds, `design/design.pen`, and the paused X01–X08 work.
- `src/core` stays host-independent (ADR-1003). Delivery uses `npm ci` and `npm run check` on the pinned Node (`.node-version` 24.21.0). Tests use real SQLite and the existing fixtures, are named by behaviour and are placed per AGENTS.md. Browser-dependent cases go through `browserSuite`/`browserTest`.
- Plan-mismatch budget versus ordinary repairs:
  - **Plan mismatch:** a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption. Examples: a named symbol or file does not own the stated behaviour; the stored JSON-`null` text cannot be read by a consumer that needs a different parse path; a core consumer of `project_github_sources.readiness` that this plan does not list; a #1002/#1006 contract that cannot share `readinessRuleViewSchema`. This gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles under to-plan's allowance. After that, stop and report for replanning.
  - **Ordinary defects:** integration, test, fixture, documentation, type/lint and CI repairs. Examples: updating hand-built read fixtures to the new view shape, rebasing onto #1006/#1002/#1003 and resolving textual conflicts, browser-test selectors that assumed a prefilled `ready` condition, formatting. These stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.
  - Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record each correction and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Storage keeps the column, with JSON `null`.** `readiness TEXT NOT NULL` (`src/core/domain.ts:455`) cannot be relaxed in SQLite without a table rebuild. Storing the JSON text `null` needs no DDL or migration of existing rows and is unambiguous: valid rules are always objects. The two default inserts (`domain.ts:648` backfill, `domain.ts:1839` `project.create`) bind `JSON.stringify(null)`. A throwaway probe on this base (in a scratch copy, not the checkout) confirmed that this storage change plus nullable parsing in `githubConfiguration()`, `updateReadiness`, `recordDeliveryClosure` and `DeliveryStore.authorize` is enough: no other core consumer of the column breaks. Across the 81 non-browser source, operator, delivery and related test files, the only failures were the explicit default assertion (`test/operator/project-setup.test.ts:122`) and one compile error at `test/sources/operator-source-credential-browser.test.ts:118`. Those are updated in T1.
- **Existing `label ready` defaults are left alone.** Project creation and backfill are the only writers of the default, and the brief says to keep existing non-null filters and not guess intent. An operator who wants no filter removes the condition in settings or CLI. No migration touches non-null rows, and a test pins that.
- **Command contract.** `githubConfigurationSchema.readiness` becomes `readinessSchema.nullable()` (`src/core/github-source-contracts.ts:115`). `githubConfigurationCommandSchema` inherits it, and the operator `github.configure` schema spreads that shape (`src/operator/contracts.ts:~1826`). The field remains required, so there are no keep semantics, and old receipts and clients (which always send a rule) replay unchanged. The command must reject `{mode, conditions: []}` and the read-view shape `{kind:"rule", …}` (the schema is strict).
- **Read contract compatible with #1002.** Export `readinessRuleViewSchema` from `src/operator/contracts.ts`: a discriminated union on `kind` of `none`, `unavailable` and `rule` (`mode` + `conditions`, strict). This is the same name and shape #1002 plans for its observation and task views. `none` comes only from a stored `null`; `unavailable` comes only from the existing exclusion check (`exact(JSON.stringify(rule), excluded) === null`, `operator-api.ts:~4801`). If #1002 merged first, import its schema and server helper (`readinessRuleView`) instead of defining new ones. If #1001 lands first, #1002 reuses these. Either order is routine integration.
- **Evaluation, with #1002 in mind.** Add a private `GitHubSourceStore.readinessRule(projectId): Readiness | null`, the same name and signature #1002 plans, and use it in `updateReadiness`. `updateReadiness` keeps its structure but computes `filterSatisfied = rule === null || (all/any over conditions)`. Memberships present and `observedState === "open"` are still required, so the closed/withdrawn guarantee holds. #1002's later `evaluateReadiness(null, …)` replaces this body; its plan already says null is `satisfied`.
- **Own-delivery closure.** `recordDeliveryClosure` computes `labelProof` from the rule's label conditions (`github-source.ts:~845`). With a `null` rule readiness cannot be lost, so `labelProof` is true: a confirmed own closure sets the `closed` hold, never `readiness-lost`. The snapshot's labels do not matter.
- **Agent authority guard.** `DeliveryStore.authorize` (`src/core/delivery.ts:~534`) denies agent label and Project-field changes that touch a readiness condition. With no rule nothing is protected, so no denial. After the operator later adds a rule, the guard applies again.
- **Web form.** The form state is a mode plus a list of condition rows. Zero rows means "No readiness rule", shown as helper text in the "2 · Readiness matching" panel; nothing is prefilled. The mode select stays visible, and the helper says it applies once a condition exists, so the layout and the "Readiness matching" label other tests use stay. `sourceCommand` sends `readiness: null` for zero rows, else `{mode, conditions}`. For `kind:"unavailable"`: no rows are loaded, the panel says the saved rule cannot be shown, and Save is blocked until the operator adds at least one condition (the existing "replaces unavailable readiness" change line stays). The UI never clears an unknown rule to none. The CLI can, only through an explicit `"readiness": null`.
- **CLI.** In the edit file, `readiness` is `rule | null | absent`: absent keeps, a rule replaces, `null` removes. `edit.readiness ?? source.readiness` becomes an explicit `!== undefined` check. The current view maps back to the command value: `none` to `null`, `rule` to `{mode, conditions}` (the `kind` key must be stripped, since the command schema is strict), `unavailable` to the existing conflict unless the edit sets `readiness`.
- **HTML fallback.** It reads the core store, so it shows `none` or a rule. The page gets one sentence naming the state ("No readiness rule: open issues in active selections are not filtered by label or Project field" or the rule summary). The existing JSON textarea shows `null` and a POST of `null` removes the rule.
- **Setup.** Guided setup (`web/src/project-setup.tsx`) does not display or send a readiness rule, so it needs no code change. A test pins that a setup-created project reads `none` and its GitHub settings show "No readiness rule".
- **Design.** No control is added or removed: the existing "Add readiness condition" and "Remove condition" controls drive the state, and the empty state is helper text. Do not edit `design/design.pen`. Add a short production-deviation note in `design/DESIGN.md` beside the existing "Settings, profiles, routing…" notes, and flag in the PR that no frame draws the no-rule state.
- **Shared regions (resolve on rebase; no plan change needed).**
  - **#1006:**
    - `src/core/domain.ts` default inserts (backfill ~:648 and `project.create` ~:1839): it adds a `closedIssues` column/value. #1001 changes only the readiness binding in those statements.
    - `web/src/settings-changes.ts` `sourceRowsFrom` (~:169), `sourceChanges` and `sourceCommand`; `web/src/source-config.tsx` initial values and panel 2.
    - `src/operator/contracts.ts` project read `source` (~:2454); `operator-api.ts` project read (~:4801).
    - `src/standalone/operator.ts` project form and `src/cli/source.ts` (`editSchema`, `prepare`, render).
    - `GitHubSourceStore.updateReadiness`, which #1006 changes for the closure hold: keep its closure code and add the `rule === null` branch.
  - **#1003:** the same `project.create` insert (~:1839). Its `credentialRef` binding is separate from the readiness binding. `test/operator/project-setup.test.ts` is shared.
  - **#1002:** `github-source.ts` `updateReadiness` (it extracts `evaluateReadiness`), the private `readinessRule`, `readinessRuleViewSchema` and the project read in `contracts.ts`/`operator-api.ts`, and `source-config.tsx` (it focuses the Readiness fieldset). Keep the names above so that integration is textual only.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` — `readinessSchema` :49 (`conditions.min(1).max(20)`, strict), `githubConfigurationSchema` :104 (`readiness: readinessSchema` :115), `githubConfigurationCommandSchema` :128.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts`:
  - DDL :455.
  - Backfill `INSERT OR IGNORE … SELECT id,1,NULL,'[]',?,'[]' FROM domain_projects` :646-654.
  - `githubConfiguration()` :982-1006, which parses `readinessSchema`. Its return type declares a non-null `readiness`.
  - `project.create` insert :1839-1859.
  - `github.configure` :2050-2133, which does `JSON.stringify(command.readiness)`, bumps `version`, invalidates sync and status, and drops the activations of removed selections.
  - `admission()` :1508, the single place that combines readiness (`task-unready`) with the other controls.
- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source.ts` `GitHubSourceStore`:
  - `reconcileSelection` :567 (new issues inserted `ready=0`, then `updateReadiness`).
  - `recordDeliveryClosure` :771, whose `labelProof` is at :845 and parses `readinessSchema` unconditionally.
  - `updateReadiness` :889, which parses `readinessSchema` and computes `satisfied` over `rule.conditions`.
- **Existing:** `src/core/delivery.ts` `authorize` :463, with the agent readiness guard at :534-571 (a local zod parse of the readiness JSON).
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `github.configure` command :1820-1828, project read `source.readiness: readinessSchema.nullable()` :2454. `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` project read `readiness` :4801.
- **Existing:** web — `web/src/settings-changes.ts` (`sourceRowsFrom` :150, which prefills `[{label ready}]`/`all` when `source.readiness` is null; `sourceChanges` :236; `sourceCommand` :390) and `web/src/source-config.tsx` (initial values :48-55; panel "2 · Readiness matching" :446-570, which shows "Saved readiness is unavailable…" when the value is null; `blocked` :71).
- **Existing:** `src/cli/source.ts` — `readinessText` :56, the `content-unavailable` gap :103, render row :153, `editSchema.readiness` :220, `sourceEditCommand` :275-430 (conflict :282, `edit.readiness ?? source.readiness` :355, diff and change lines :384-420). `src/standalone/operator.ts` — the GitHub source form (readiness textarea :323) and the `github.configure` POST builder (`JSON.parse(required("readiness"))` :580).
- **New:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `readinessRuleViewSchema`. `GitHubSourceStore.readinessRule(projectId)` (private). No new files; all tests extend existing files.
- **Follow:** `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts:26` (direct `reconcileSelection` snapshots on real SQLite); `test/sources/github-source-config.test.ts:33` (configure, restart and stale version) and :991 (migration); `test/delivery/pr-completion.test.ts:560-650` (own-closure flow); `test/delivery/delivery-store.test.ts:30` (delivery grants and `authorize`); `test/sources/github-service.test.ts:1242-1276` (a local dependency that blocks admission); `test/sources/operator-cli-source.test.ts:109` (prepare-source).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 → T2 → T3. All tasks run in order on one branch with one owner and one PR; none may run concurrently. T2 cannot be split further: the read-contract change is type-checked by `tsc` for `src/cli`, by `tsc -p web` for `web/src`, and by the root `tsc`, which compiles `web/src/settings-changes.ts` through test imports. A partial change leaves a red build. T2 therefore has sub-steps (a)–(d), each with its own focused check. T1 and T2 share `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts`/`domain.ts` neighbours with #1006, which is why the branch starts only after #1006 has merged.

#### 1. Optional readiness rule in core: storage, evaluation, guards

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** #1006 merged and the branch rebased on it. Read its merged default inserts and `updateReadiness` first.
**Files and symbols:**

- `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts`: `githubConfigurationSchema.readiness` → `readinessSchema.nullable()`.
- `src/core/domain.ts`:
  - Backfill (:648) and `project.create` (:1839) bind `JSON.stringify(null)` for `readiness`, with no other changes to those statements.
  - `githubConfiguration()` parses `readinessSchema.nullable()` and returns `Readiness | null`.
- `src/core/github-source.ts`:
  - Private `readinessRule(projectId)`.
  - `updateReadiness`: `filterSatisfied` with an explicit null branch.
  - `recordDeliveryClosure`: `labelProof` is true when the rule is null.
- `src/core/delivery.ts` `authorize`: parse the readiness JSON as nullable and skip both guards when null.
- Tests listed below, including `test/sources/operator-source-credential-browser.test.ts:118` (`readiness?.mode`).

**Test:**

- `test/sources/github-source-config.test.ts`:
  - New project: `githubConfiguration(id).readiness === null`, and the raw column text is `null`. This is the default-change test.
  - Extend the migration test (:991): delete the source row and `migrate()` again. The backfilled rule is `null`, version 1 and no active selection.

The exact keyed replay of the null configure returns the original receipt with no extra bump. After the configure, a previously activated selection is no longer active at the new version, and admission reports `source-unknown` until the next complete reconcile.
