content.title: Expose diagnostic capture control in the CLI and LaunchAgent configuration

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Expose diagnostic capture through reviewed CLI project changes and support LaunchAgent retention configuration.

**Current behavior and evidence:** At e6bf9d21, project.configure accepts diagnosticCapture, but the CLI has no diagnostic-capture option. The LaunchAgent renderer does not include the two diagnostic retention settings. Redundancy checks covered CLI parsing/preparation, domain configuration, diagnostic environment parsing, launchd rendering and operations guidance; the acceptance inventory still marks CLI capture configuration unproved.

**Desired behavior:** project prepare --diagnostic-capture enhanced|baseline creates a reviewable change document and applies only through the existing receipt path. Provide a supported way for LaunchAgent installations to receive ENSEMBLE_DIAGNOSTIC_RETENTION_DAYS and ENSEMBLE_DIAGNOSTIC_STORAGE_MIB, through rendering or documented configuration. Preserve current defaults and validation.

**Key interfaces:** Project prepare/change-document and receipt flow, project.configure.diagnosticCapture, diagnostic retention configuration and LaunchAgent installation.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Both capture modes produce the intended project configuration change in a reviewable document.
- [ ] Invalid values are rejected; omitting the option does not overwrite the existing setting.
- [ ] Apply retains existing authorization, revision, replay and receipt behavior.
- [ ] The supported LaunchAgent configuration route delivers both retention values; documentation explains configuration and reload/restart.
- [ ] Defaults and allowed ranges remain consistent with diagnostic configuration validation.
- [ ] Focused tests cover CLI prepare/apply and retention configuration; update the relevant CLI qualification inventory with actual evidence.

**Validation:** Current gaps were verified by source inspection. Implementation runs pinned npm ci and npm run check and bounded fixture validation of the supported LaunchAgent configuration route.

**Out of scope:** A React Settings control or new Pen frames, new retention policy, deleting durable safety history, production service changes and paid/live model execution.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/919
**Planned against:** `cb/issue-919-diagnostic-capture-cli` at `2603a60585eda286f08da7b320e9e57b28ed9769`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Authority: the issue and its [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/919#issuecomment-6130130182) (acceptance criteria and out-of-scope list). Baseline: CI run 38648160889 passed every job on this exact SHA (static checks, all test shards, `check`); no baseline check is rerun locally.

### Approach

1. Add `--diagnostic-capture enhanced|baseline` to `project prepare`. It adds `diagnosticCapture` to the one `project.configure` command that CLI3 already prepares, previews and applies; apply, authorization, revision, replay and receipt code are untouched.
2. Render `ENSEMBLE_DIAGNOSTIC_RETENTION_DAYS` and `ENSEMBLE_DIAGNOSTIC_STORAGE_MIB` into the LaunchAgent, only when set, and expose them as `--diagnostic-retention-days` and `--diagnostic-storage-mib` on `service install` and `service upgrade`. The values are stored in the install record so an upgrade keeps them. The hand-render route (`npm run operations -- render-launch-agent`) gets the same two optional trailing flags.
3. Share one range/default definition between the service's environment parser and the renderer, so the two cannot drift.
4. Document the route, flip the one unproved qualification row to `bounded` with the new test evidence, and remove the stale "needs a reviewed renderer change" text.

### Guardrails

- Out of scope: the React Settings control and any `design/design.pen` frame (issue item 3; it needs a design first and is not in the acceptance list), new retention policy, changes to retention defaults or ranges, deleting durable safety history, production service changes, paid or live model execution, and any change to `project.configure` domain behaviour, `diagnosticCaptureMode`, the operator API or the receipt `result` shape.
- Defaults unchanged: with no flag, `renderLaunchAgent` output is byte-identical to today's (the existing exact-field test in `test/operations/launchd.test.ts` must keep passing unmodified), and install records written without the new fields must still parse (`recordSchema` stays `.strict()`; the new fields are optional).
- Omitting `--diagnostic-capture` must not put `diagnosticCapture` in the command. A value equal to the current mode produces no change (existing "No change" error).
- Never install or load a real LaunchAgent, or touch `launchctl` or `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, in tests or validation; use the fake launchd host and temporary directories only.
- Plan-mismatch budget: a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example, `service upgrade` to the installed release dir does not work as the reload route, `project.configure` does not accept a capture-only change, or the read does not report `diagnosticCapture`) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; after that, stop and report for replanning. Ordinary implementation defects (integration, test, fixture, documentation, inventory-count and CI repairs, type errors, lint/format, test-shard timing weights) stay with the ticket owner, are repaired in place with the correction recorded in the delivery record, and do not consume that budget.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption.
- Stop for material design or contract changes (for example, a request to change retention ranges, add a purge, change receipt shape, or build the UI control) and for exhausted grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Render rather than document (item 2).** Evidence: `src/cli/service.ts` `Service.activate` rebuilds the whole `Configuration` and re-renders the plist on every `install` and `upgrade`, and `requireOwned` refuses to touch an activation whose SHA-256 differs from `record.plistSha256`. A hand-edited plist or a `launchctl setenv` therefore either blocks the next upgrade or is silently lost, so no documented alternative is durable. Rendering is small because `LaunchAgentConfiguration` is a flat typed object with exact-match tests, and the renderer already validates every field. The upgrade route also gives the "reload/restart" the brief asks to document: stop, snapshot, re-render, bootstrap.
- **Defaults stay implicit.** The renderer emits a variable only when a value is set, so the service's own defaults (30 days, 1024 MiB) remain the single default. A value of `default` on the CLI clears a previously stored override (the counterpart of setting one). `ServiceOptions.diagnostic` is `{ retentionDays?: number | null; storageMib?: number | null }`: absent keeps the recorded value (install: unset), `null` clears, a number sets.
- **Shared bounds without SQLite.** `src/standalone/execution-diagnostics.ts` imports `core/store` (SQLite) and the LaunchAgent renderer is loaded by the operator CLI's service commands; so the variable names, ranges, defaults and `integerFromEnv` move to a new dependency-free `src/standalone/diagnostic-retention.ts`, imported by both. `diagnosticLimitsFromEnv` keeps its name, signature and behaviour (guarded by `test/execution/execution-diagnostics-store.test.ts` "limits from the environment").
- **Validation at each boundary.** Flags are validated at parse time (usage error, exit 2, before any filesystem or launchd action); the renderer revalidates (an invalid configuration still surfaces as the fixed `The LaunchAgent configuration is invalid`); the service still fails startup on a bad value.
- **Capture change document.** `diagnosticCapture` is already in `projectConfigurationSchema` and `operatorCommandSchema`, and the read path is `GET /projects/:id/configuration` (`src/standalone/operator-api.ts` ~4758). The read field is optional ("older services still parse"); when it is absent the change is still prepared with `from: null` and coverage gap `content-unavailable`, as `name` already does. Capture is not a stale-making axis, so `readImpact` stays as is. Receipt `result` for `project.configure` does not carry the mode; tests read it back through `domain.diagnosticCaptureMode` and `project get`.
- **Same-version upgrade as the reload route (assumption, checked in T3).** `upgradeServiceLocked` does not refuse a target equal to the installed version; the snapshot name embeds `from`, `to` and a one-second timestamp. T3 proves this with the fake host before docs rely on it; a failure is a plan mismatch (see Guardrails).
- **Entry points.** Capture write: CLI `project prepare` only (the web API command route already works; the Settings control is out of scope and stays a documented gap). Retention: `service install`, `service upgrade`, and the checkout `render-launch-agent` operations command. Gap: a hand-edited or externally rendered plist is unsupported by design.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/cli/configure-project.ts` — `projectWriteCommands["project prepare"]` reads `readProject`, builds `command` and `changes`, and calls `writePrepared`; `flags` is the allow-list enforced by `rejectUnusedFlags` (`src/cli/write.ts`), so other commands reject the new flag automatically.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/main.ts` `parseArgs` options map (~line 165-215) and `src/cli/types.ts` `Values` (~line 50-100) list every flag; the new flag must be added to both.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/configure.ts` — `Change`, `exactCommand` (validates against `operatorCommandSchema`), `writePrepared`, `applyFile`; `CliError("invalid-input", …)` exits 2 (`src/cli/main.ts` exit table).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/launchd.ts` — `LaunchAgentConfiguration`, `validateConfiguration`, `renderLaunchAgent` (EnvironmentVariables dict: PATH, `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_AUTH_FILE`, `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_ORIGIN`), `writeLaunchAgent`; callers `src/cli/service.ts` (dynamic import) and `src/standalone/operations-cli.ts` (`render-launch-agent`, currently exactly 10 args).
- **Existing:** `src/cli/service.ts` — `configurationSchema` (strict) / `recordSchema`, `Service.activate(version, root, base)` (builds the `Configuration`), `installServiceLocked` (passes `{dataDirectory, authFile, origin, port}`), `upgradeServiceLocked` (passes `record.configuration`), `parseLifecycleArgs`, `lifecycleOptions`, `serviceCommand`, `SERVICE_USAGE`. `tsconfig` sets `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: build the `Configuration` with conditional spreads, never `key: undefined`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/execution-diagnostics.ts` — `integerFromEnv`, `diagnosticLimitsFromEnv` (used by `src/standalone/cli.ts` `productionService`, which is what the LaunchAgent runs via `operator`).
- **New:** `src/standalone/diagnostic-retention.ts` — the two variable names with `{min, max, fallback}` and `integerFromEnv`.
- **Follow:** `test/operator/operator-diagnostic-capture.test.ts` (`startCliService`, `harness`, `s.issue`, `s.bearer`) and `test/workspaces/operator-cli-change.test.ts` `setup` (ro/rw logins, `databaseDigest` unchanged on prepare, receipt/replay assertions) for the CLI tests; `test/operations/service-lifecycle.test.ts` `setup`/`installed`/`FakeLaunchd` and `programArguments` for lifecycle tests.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic: T1 and T2 are roots; T3 depends on T2; T4 depends on T1 and T3. T1 and T2 touch disjoint files and may run concurrently. T3 and T4 share no files with each other's inputs but T4 documents T3's flags, so it follows. Shared-file constraints: only T4 edits docs and the inventory; only T1 edits `src/cli/main.ts` and `src/cli/types.ts`; only T3 edits `src/cli/service.ts`. A single owner can run T1 then T2/T3 then T4 sequentially.

#### 1. `project prepare --diagnostic-capture`

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** `src/cli/configure-project.ts` (`project prepare` usage, `flags`, `run`), `src/cli/main.ts` (parseArgs options: add `"diagnostic-capture": { type: "string" }`), `src/cli/types.ts` (`Values`: add `"diagnostic-capture"?: string | undefined`), tests in `test/operator/operator-diagnostic-capture.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/operator/operator-diagnostic-capture.test.ts` add CLI tests using `startCliService`, `harness`, a `read` and a `read-write` login. Assertions: (a) `project prepare P --diagnostic-capture baseline --out F` on the read login exits 0, writes mode `0600`, leaves `databaseDigest` unchanged, the document has `kind: "project.configure"`, `command` keys exactly `diagnosticCapture, expectedVersion, projectId, type`, `preview.changes` deep-equals `[{field:"diagnosticCapture", from:"enhanced", to:"baseline"}]`; (b) `project apply --file F` on the read login exits 3 with the mode unchanged; on the read-write login exits 0, receipt keys `key, kind, recorded, result` as in the existing API test, `d.diagnosticCaptureMode(P) === "baseline"`, `project get` shows `Diagnostic capture:   baseline`; re-applying the same file returns the same receipt without another version bump; (c) after another actor renames the project, applying a document prepared earlier exits 4 and the mode is unchanged; (d) `project prepare P --name X` after (b) produces a command without `diagnosticCapture`, and applying it leaves the mode `baseline`; (e) `--diagnostic-capture enhanced` prepare/apply restores `enhanced`; (f) `--diagnostic-capture off` and an empty value exit 2 with no document written and no `/commands` request; the same flag on `project prepare-create` exits 2 (flag not an option); (g) `--diagnostic-capture baseline` when already baseline exits 2 with the "No change" message and writes nothing. Include one sensitivity check: temporarily dropping the `command.diagnosticCapture` assignment makes (a) fail.
**Implementation:** Add the flag to the usage string, `flags` and `run`. Parse with a local helper accepting only `enhanced`/`baseline` (else `CliError("invalid-input", "--diagnostic-capture must be enhanced or baseline.")`). content.title: Let the operator turn runtime providers on and off

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Let the operator enable or disable each execution runtime (Codex, Claude) for the installation, live, from Settings and the CLI. No runtime is required any more.

Decisions were settled in a triage grilling session and are recorded in ADR-1012, "Let the operator enable and disable each execution runtime" (`docs/adr/1012-operator-controlled-runtime-enablement.md`). ADR-1008's Selection section points to it. Glossary: **Execution runtime**, **Disabled runtime** (the operator's choice) as opposed to **not enabled** (the effective state, with several causes). Avoid "runtime provider".

**Current behavior:**
The service runs every harness in its fixed production list. It requires Codex: the harness list must include the default harness, and a Codex start failure stops the service. Claude is "not enabled for that run" only when `claude` is missing at startup. The operator cannot turn either runtime off. New profiles default to Codex.

**Desired behavior:**
- **Setting:** each runtime has an installation-wide enabled setting, persisted in the domain store alongside the existing installation settings (the same place as the Claude token reference). A missing setting means enabled, so upgrades are unchanged.
- **No required runtime:** any runtime can be disabled, including all of them. The service starts with none enabled. A runtime that is enabled but fails to start, Codex included, is reported unavailable and does not stop the service.
- **Live effect:**
  - Disabling stops new admissions for that runtime immediately. Running turns finish and are never cancelled. Work bound to it waits with the existing "not enabled" wait and never falls back to another runtime.
  - Enabling starts the runtime in the running service through the existing secondary-runtime start and stop paths.
- **Refusal:** enabling is refused while the runtime's binary does not resolve on the service `PATH`. The refusal names the missing binary, and the setting stays disabled. If the binary resolves but the runtime fails to start, the setting is saved as enabled and the runtime is reported unavailable with a readiness Fix.
- **Profile default:** new profiles default to the first enabled runtime in the order Codex, Claude, and to Codex when none is enabled.
- **Readiness and doctor:**
  - A new top check, "An execution runtime is enabled", fails with a Fix to Settings → Runtime when none is enabled.
  - Each runtime's own checks report Not configured, with the reason "Disabled in Settings" or "`<binary>` not found on PATH".
  - Fail appears only when a runtime is enabled and unavailable.
  - A disabled runtime raises no destructive alert.
- **Confirmation:** disabling a runtime that has bound or running work asks for confirmation and states the count, for example "N tasks use Claude. Running turns finish; their next turns wait until Claude is enabled again." The CLI requires `--yes` in this case. Without bound work there is no confirmation.
- **CLI:** a `runtime` area with `list`, `enable <codex|claude>` and `disable <codex|claude>`, using a typed `runtime.configure` operator command with a normal mutation receipt. Update `docs/design/operator-cli.md` in place: runtime enablement is a supported mutation, while runtime and model setting edits stay excluded.
- **Design:** Pen frames (through the Pen MCP only) for:
  - the Settings → Runtime row in four states: enabled and running; enabled and unavailable with Fix; disabled; refused because the binary is missing (inline reason, toggle stays off);
  - the disable confirmation;
  - readiness with no runtime enabled.

  Save with `scripts/pen-save-all.applescript` and refresh `design/DESIGN.md` through MCP. The composer and task waits reuse existing copy.

**Key interfaces:**
- The service's harness enablement (`harnessEnabled`, `runtimeNotEnabled`, `runtimeHarnesses`, and the "Runtime harnesses must include the default harness" check): enablement becomes the persisted setting combined with startup state. The required-default rule and the fatal Codex start are removed.
- Runtime status read: distinguish disabled from missing-binary from start failure.
- Operator contracts: the new `runtime.configure` command and its receipt; readiness check IDs.
- The profile creation default harness.
- Code that reaches the Codex runtime directly (for example `verifyCodexLogin()`) must keep degrading to `unavailable` when Codex is disabled.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Per-runtime enabled state persists across restarts and is shown in Settings → Runtime, readiness/`ensemble doctor` and `ensemble runtime list`.
- [ ] Both runtimes can be disabled. The service starts and serves the operator UI with none enabled, and readiness shows the no-runtime check failing with its Fix.
- [ ] An enabled Codex that fails to start no longer stops the service. It shows as unavailable with a Fix.
- [ ] Disabling a runtime with a running turn lets the turn finish. Its next turn waits as not enabled and does not run on the other runtime. Re-enabling admits it without a restart.
- [ ] Enabling with the binary missing is refused with a clear reason on the web and CLI, and the setting stays disabled.
- [ ] Disabling with bound work requires confirmation on the web and `--yes` on the CLI. Without bound work it does not.
- [ ] New profiles default to the first enabled runtime.
- [ ] Tests (real SQLite, fake host) cover toggling with and without bound or running work, the missing-binary refusal, start failure, none enabled, and persistence across restart.
- [ ] Pen frames and `design/DESIGN.md` are updated. SPEC's runtime paragraph and `docs/design/operator-cli.md` describe the new contract.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes, and bounded live validation toggles Claude on a real service, as `docs/acceptance.md` requires.

**Out of scope:**
- Per-profile enablement.
- Runtime or model setting edits beyond enablement.
- Migrating bound conversations between runtimes, or any fallback.
- A Claude token CLI command.
- Power holds (#984) and assignment waits (#987).

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/989
**Planned against:** `main` at `b31881848d126e9e9c1d1163dea7ab979cf4425f`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

The accepted contract is the triage **Agent Brief** comment on #989. Its decisions, desired behaviour, key interfaces, acceptance criteria and out-of-scope list are authoritative. This plan does not copy them.

### Approach

1. Persist one enabled flag per execution runtime in the domain store. Add a typed `runtime.configure` domain command next to `claude-token.configure`.
2. Make the service's runtime set live. Effective enablement is the persisted setting combined with whether the binary resolves and how start went. Enabling and disabling reuse the existing secondary-runtime create, attach, start-with-timeout and detached-stop paths, so no runtime is required.
3. Expose the state through `harnessStatuses()`, readiness and `ensemble doctor`, a new operator API mutation with refusal and confirmation errors, an `ensemble runtime` CLI area, and Settings → Runtime.
4. Design and docs follow the same contract.
5. One bounded live journey toggles Claude on a real service.

### Guardrails

- **Never fall back.** Work bound to a harness that is not enabled or unavailable waits through the existing `runtimeWaitReason` → `state.wait` path. It is never routed to another runtime.
- **Unchanged copy and behaviour:**
  - The wait strings and the `profile-runtime-not-configured` / "Not enabled" copy stay unchanged.
  - The shell's destructive alert stays only for `unavailable`. A disabled runtime never raises it.
- **Running work is never cancelled by a toggle.**
  - Disabling stops new admissions immediately.
  - A runtime that still owns `submitting`, `running` or `held` executions keeps running until none remain. Only then is it stopped.
  - Unresolved ownership holds and the documented recovery boundary are preserved. A held execution keeps its runtime alive rather than losing its inspector.
- **Codex callback semantics stay as they are.** Codex's mid-run failure and callback handling in `attachRuntime` and `untilFailure` is unchanged. Only the start-failure path stops being fatal.
- **Out of scope (from the brief):**
  - per-profile enablement;
  - runtime or model setting edits;
  - migrating bound conversations, or any fallback;
  - a Claude token CLI command;
  - power holds (#984) and assignment waits (#987).
- **Glossary.** Use "execution runtime", "disabled runtime" (the operator's choice) and "not enabled" (the effective state). Do not introduce "runtime provider" in code, UI or docs.
- **Pen.** Edit `design/design.pen` only through the Pen MCP server. Pen MCP edits stay in memory: the Pen app must save them, either with `osascript scripts/pen-save-all.applescript` (needs Accessibility permission) or by the user saving in Pen. The lead/user does that save before `design/DESIGN.md` is refreshed and committed.
- **Plan-assumption budget vs ordinary repairs.**
  - The budget applies only when an approved-plan seam or repository assumption proves factually wrong, for example `runtimeFactory` cannot build a runtime after start, or the waiting intent is not re-scanned on wake. Such a mismatch gets one diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. After that, stop and return a replan request.
  - Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.
- **Routine corrections.** Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record each correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- **Delivery record.** Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

**Rule for disabling a runtime with bound or running work: wait, never refuse.** This is the brief's decision, with refusal rejected in its ADR.

- **Counted work.** "Bound or running work" means the distinct tasks with an execution intent whose `task_execution_bindings.harness` is that harness and whose state is non-terminal (`ready`, `capacity-waiting`, `held`, `submitting`, `running`). This is the same set as `src/standalone/state.ts:406`.
- **Confirmation gate.** The server owns it. A disable whose count is above 0 and that lacks `confirmed: true` is refused with 409 `runtime-confirmation-required`, carrying the count. This closes the gap between the count read and the write.
  - The web UI shows the confirmation from a fresh count and then sends `confirmed: true`.
  - The CLI sends `confirmed: true` only with `--yes`. Without `--yes`, it prints the count and the brief's sentence and exits non-zero.
  - With a count of 0, the server accepts the disable without confirmation.
- **Drain, then stop.** A disabled runtime with no `submitting`, `running` or `held` execution for its harness is stopped at once through the detached-stop path. Otherwise it stays in `this.runtimes` and is stopped when its last such execution settles.
  - Re-enabling while it drains cancels the pending stop and keeps the same runtime, with no second start.
  - After a restart with the setting disabled, the runtime is never started. Held work stays held exactly as it does for a missing binary today.

**Turning a runtime on.**

- **Missing binary.** Enabling first resolves the runtime's binary (`codex` / `claude`) on the service `PATH` through `resolveOnPath`. The resolver is injectable through `StandaloneServiceOptions` for tests.
  - If the binary is missing, the request is refused with 409 `runtime-executable-missing`, naming the binary. Nothing is persisted, so the setting stays disabled.
  - At service start, an enabled runtime whose binary no longer resolves becomes not enabled with the reason `executable-missing`. Codex now behaves like Claude here, instead of failing to spawn.
- **Start failure.** If the binary resolves but start fails or exceeds `secondaryRuntimeStartTimeoutMs`, the setting is saved as enabled and the runtime becomes `unavailable`.
  - The command still returns its receipt.
  - The live-enable path applies that timeout to both harnesses. The service-start path keeps Codex's current untimed start but catches its failure.
- **Recovery for an unavailable runtime.** Enabling a runtime that is already enabled but `unavailable` re-runs the start path with a fresh `runtimeFactory` instance. The failed instance goes through the detached stop. Readiness Fix and Settings copy name this as an alternative to a restart.
- **Idempotent reconcile.** Each `runtime.configure` commits the setting through the domain receipt. It then calls `service.reconcileRuntime(harness)`, which brings the live runtime to the persisted setting. A replayed key re-runs the reconcile and returns the stored receipt, so lost responses converge.
- **Serialised toggles.** Toggles on one harness are serialised through a per-harness promise chain. A toggle while the service is not started, or not accepting work, is refused with 503 `unavailable`.

**Status shape.**

- `harnessStatusSchema` gains `enabled: boolean` (the persisted setting) on every variant.
- The `not-configured` variant gains `reason: "disabled" | "executable-missing"`.
- `runtimeSettingsSchema` (`GET /api/operator/runtime`) gains `runtimes: [{ harness, enabled, boundTasks }]` for the confirmation count and `runtime list`.
- The existing `runtime` (Codex) field in the workspace read keeps its shape.

**Readiness.**

- **New check.** A new first check, `runtime-enabled`, is labelled "An execution runtime is enabled". It fails with Fix "Enable a runtime in Settings → Runtime" when no setting is enabled, and passes otherwise. The number of checks becomes nine.
- **Disabled runtime.** `codex-executable`, `codex-login`, `claude-executable` and `claude-token` report `not-configured` with the reason "Disabled in Settings".
- **Enabled, binary missing.** They report `not-configured` with the reason "`<binary>` not found on PATH". This replaces #981's in-use `fail` for a missing `claude`, as the brief requires. The `runtime-harness` check still fails for an active profile whose runtime is not enabled.
- **Enabled and unavailable.** This is the only `fail`.

**Profile default.**

- **Domain.** `profile.create` without a `runtime` uses the first enabled harness in the order codex, claude, else codex. The domain owns this because the setting lives there.
- **Web.** The create form's initial runtime comes from `harnesses[].enabled` in the same order.

**Power supervision.** Supervision must not depend on which runtimes were enabled at start. The service sets up `ExecutionPower` when the existing predicate holds for any started runtime, or when `this.runtimeFactory === createRuntime` (production) and `options.power?.enabled !== false`. A service started with none enabled and then enabled live is supervised.

**Error codes.** `OperatorApiError` gains `runtime-executable-missing` and `runtime-confirmation-required` (both 409). Their client schemas in `src/operator/contracts.ts` carry `harness`, plus `boundTasks` for the confirmation error. Only fixed strings are rendered.

**CLI.**

- `runtime list` needs `cli.identity`, `workspace.read` and `capacity.read`.
- `runtime enable|disable <codex|claude> [--yes] [--request-id UUID]` needs `cli.identity`, `configuration.write` and `capacity.read`. It is a direct write that follows `task stop` in `src/cli/task-control.ts`, with no prepare/apply file. The brief names only these verbs.
- `runtime.configure` joins `operationTypeSchema`, so `operation show` can read its receipt back. The receipt is `{ commandType: "runtime.configure", resourceId: "system:runtime:<harness>", harness, enabled }`.

**ADR-1012.** ADR-1012, the CONTEXT.md glossary entries and the ADR-1008 Selection pointer are not in the baseline. Uncommitted drafts exist only in a separate triage worktree. T1 lands them in the repo from the brief's decisions.

### Implementation context

**Existing:**

- **`src/standalone/service.ts`**
  - The constructor (around line 560) enforces "Runtime harnesses must include the default harness".
  - The `start()` runtime loop (lines 983–1066) rethrows default-harness create and start failures and records `runtimeNotEnabled` for `RuntimeNotEnabledError`.
  - `startRuntime` / `attachRuntime` (lines 1238–1340) apply the secondary timeout and failure promise only to non-default runtimes.
  - `harnessEnabled` (line 1467) and `runtimeWaitReason` (line 1475) feed admission at line 4478.
  - `harnessStatuses` (line 1866) and `verifyCodexLogin` (line 1883) already degrade to `unavailable`.
  - Power setup is at line 1084.
  - The `stop()` runtime teardown and `detachedRuntimeStops` live in the same file.
- **`src/standalone/cli.ts`.** `productionRuntimeHarnesses` / `productionService` feed `runtimeHarnesses`.
- **`src/standalone/claude.ts:start`.** Throws `RuntimeNotEnabledError` (defined in `src/standalone/codex.ts:537`) when `claude` does not resolve.
- **`src/core/domain.ts`.**
  - Singleton installation tables are created at about line 495 and seeded at about line 620.
  - `claudeTokenReference()` is at line 789.
  - The `claude-token.configure` and `getting-started.configure` cases are at line 2401.
  - `profile.create` (line 1934) uses `defaultProfileRuntime` from `src/core/execution-runtime.ts:40`.
  - `src/core/command-results.ts` holds the per-command result schemas.
- **`src/operator/contracts.ts`.**
  - `harnessStatusSchema` (around line 127).
  - The domain command union (around lines 1755–1850).
  - Receipt variants (around line 2040).
  - `runtimeSettingsSchema` (line 2072).
  - `operationTypeSchema` (line 3015).
  - `cliCapabilities` (line 2946).
- **`src/standalone/operator-api.ts`.**
  - The command dispatch for `claude-token.configure` is at line 6030.
  - `readWorkspace` (line 1824) and the operations read-back scope mapping (line 4634) are in the same file.
  - `src/standalone/operator-receipts.ts:133` maps receipts.
- **Readiness.**
  - `src/operator/readiness.ts` holds the fixed `readinessCheckIds` order.
  - In `src/standalone/readiness.ts`, the `Readiness` checks `claudeExecutable` (line 285) and `runtimeHarness` (line 367) live, with `ReadinessDeps.harnessStatuses` and the `labels` and `fixes` tables.
  - `src/cli/doctor.ts` renders checks generically.
- **Web.**
  - `web/src/recovery.tsx:RuntimeSettings` contains the "Execution runtimes" panel (lines 151–186).
  - `web/src/execution-runtime.ts` holds `harnessStateLabel` and `unavailableAlert`.
  - `web/src/app.tsx:884` holds the shell alerts.

content.title: Show power-supervisor holds as a task wait reason

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Derive a `power-held` wait from the power supervisor's admission hold, so a held installation never predicts "Starts now." or leaves a task queued with no reason.

**Current behavior:**
When the power supervisor holds admission (persisted `PowerAdmissionState.held`, with a reason such as "Power-event history is incomplete or ambiguous"), no turn starts. However, the operator admission read and `deriveWaits()` never consult that state. The composer options read says "Starts now.", and the task stays `queued` with an empty wait list on task detail, the post-create line, Inbox and the CLI. The service already adds a `power-held` admission reason for native questions, but not for task waits. No operator surface (readiness, `ensemble doctor`, web) explains a power hold today. Evidence: `docs/evidence/first-run-journey.md`, attempt 1.

**Desired behavior:**
- A new wait code `power-held`, labelled "Held by power supervision", is derived whenever the persisted power admission state is held. It is installation-wide, so it applies to every open task and to the composer prediction for every project.
- Order: directly after the runtime waits (`runtime-unavailable`, `claude-token-unavailable`, `profile-runtime-not-configured`) and before `local-dependency`. The same order applies on the server task read, composer options, CLI and web, all through the shared `waitCodes` order.
- Like other holds it carries **no Fix**. Nothing else explains the hold, so the wait itself carries the supervisor's current hold reason text: add one bounded, optional detail field to `Wait`, shown under the label in the web UI and on the CLI's wait line. Do not invent a link target.
- When the hold releases, the wait disappears on the next read. Nothing is persisted for the wait.
- When power supervision is disabled or absent (`powerStatus()` is null), no `power-held` wait is derived.

**Key interfaces:**
- `waitCodes`, `waitLabels`, `waitSchema` / `Wait`: new code and an optional detail string (bounded like `label`).
- `WaitFacts` / `deriveWaits()`: a new input, for example `powerHold?: string | null`, the reason when held.
- The operator API's task wait and project/composer wait derivations: both read the power admission state through the existing service accessors (`powerStatus()` / the state's `powerAdmissionState()`).
- Web wait rendering and the CLI wait output: show the detail.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] With the power admission held, task detail, the post-create line, Inbox and the CLI show "Held by power supervision" with the hold reason and no Fix.
- [ ] With the power admission held, composer options for a healthy project do not say "Starts now." and list the power wait.
- [ ] After the hold releases, the same reads show no power wait and the composer predicts "Starts now." again.
- [ ] Unit tests for `deriveWaits` cover held, released and ordering against runtime and dependency waits.
- [ ] A service or operator API integration test covers held and released states using the real state store (fake host).
- [ ] `npm run check` passes. Update the wait-reason docs (the first-task user flow and the SPEC wait list) to include the new wait.

**Out of scope:**
- Any operator control to release or disable power supervision (this is a known recovery gap; raise a separate issue if needed).
- Adding power status to readiness or `ensemble doctor`.
- Assignment-level admission waits (#987, which follows this issue).
- Changing power supervisor behaviour or its hold reasons.

**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/984 **Planned against:** `origin/main` at `757e3314e21417fbf43445004b792fd7516ddd64` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null The accepted contract is the triage Agent Brief on this issue (https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/984#issuecomment-6171085343). Where the issue body asks for a link, the brief governs: no link target, a bounded detail string instead. ### Approach Add one wait code, `power-held` ("Held by power supervision"), and one optional `detail` string to `Wait`. `deriveWaits()` takes a new fact, `powerHold`. `OperatorApi` fills it from `service.powerStatus()` for the task read and for the composer's project waits. `orderWaits` and the existing renderers carry the wait unchanged to task detail, the post-create line, the composer prediction, Inbox and the CLI. Each renderer gains one place that prints `detail`. ### Guardrails - Keep the #950 rules: a read-side projection with no persistence and no Fix for holds. One `waitCodes` order applies everywhere. Admission, scheduler and power supervisor behaviour, and their hold reasons, stay unchanged. - `power-held` sits directly after `profile-runtime-not-configured` and before `local-dependency`. It is not a runtime wait: leave `runtimeWaitCodes` and the composer's `assigneeWaits` unchanged, so an explicit assignee never hides it. - `detail` is optional (omitted when absent, never `null`) and bounded like `label`. It is generic wait context, not power-specific. Existing waits stay byte-identical. - Out of scope: a release or disable control for power supervision, power status in readiness or `ensemble doctor`, assignment-level waits (#987), provider on/off (#989), Pen frames and `design/DESIGN.md`. The detail line uses the existing `metadata muted` text style and adds no frame. - **Plan-mismatch budget:** a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Examples: `powerStatus()` does not reflect the persisted hold, the fixture cannot enable power, or a contract bound sits elsewhere. When that budget runs out, stop and request a replan. - **Ordinary defects:** implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not use that budget. Record routine corrections, such as an equivalent path, fixture setup or test name, in the existing delivery record and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for a material design or contract change, or when a grant is exhausted. - Reuse the existing delivery record and any valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants. ### Planning decisions - **Source of the fact:** `this.service.powerStatus()` (`RuntimeOperatorApi` already declares it, and `OperatorApi` does not call it yet). It returns `{admissionHeld, admissionReason}` from the persisted `PowerAdmissionState`, or `null` when no supervisor runs. Following the brief, `null` produces no wait. Known residual: `StandaloneState.begin()` checks the persisted `wakeHeld` row even with supervision off. A data directory held earlier and reopened with `power: { enabled: false }` would still hold admission, and no wait would show. Only non-production options can disable supervision, because real harnesses are always supervised (`powerSupervisionEnabled`). A hold caused by an invalid cursor can have `reason: null`, and it must still produce the wait, with no `detail`. - **Bounds:** `contracts.ts` caps `waits` at `.max(13)`, which equals today's code count, in two places: composer options (around line 893) and the task read (around line 1258). content.title: Show assignment-level admission failures as task wait reasons

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Feed non-lead assignment admission failures into the derived waits, so a task held only by an inadmissible assignment shows why and how to fix it.

**Blocked by:** #984 (same wait-code list and derivation; land it first and rebase on its ordering).

**Current behavior:**
The scheduler refuses a queued or pending assignment when `DomainStore.assignmentAdmission()` returns reasons beyond task admission: `profile-revoked`, `assignment-profile-revision-stale`, `assignment-instructions-revision-stale`, `profile-not-permitted`, `assignment-held`. The operator task waits only receive task-level `admission()` reasons. The executing-profile facts only report runtime state. So a task with a healthy lead and one such assignment stays queued with no wait and no Fix on task detail, Inbox and the CLI. (Review: https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/pull/983#discussion_r4269971650)

**Desired behavior:**
- For each assignment that is next to run (the same candidates the executing-profile facts already consider: a queued current turn request, or pending with no request), collect its assignment-only admission reasons. These are the reasons in `assignmentAdmission()` that task admission did not already produce. Pass them into wait derivation.
- **Decision:** keep the projection approach. Pass the reasons into `deriveWaits` as facts; do not restructure waits to be computed by admission itself.
- New wait codes, one per cause, in this order, placed after `power-held` and before `local-dependency`:
  - Assignment profile revoked. Fix: `open-profile` for the assignment's profile.
  - Assignment profile changed (stale profile revision). Fix: `open-profile` for that profile.
  - Assignment instructions changed (stale instructions revision). No Fix.
  - Assignment profile not permitted by project routing. No Fix.
  - Assignment held. No Fix.

  Labels are plain operator wording and should name the assignment's profile where `waitLabels` style allows. Choose code strings consistent with the existing kebab-case codes.
- Any assignment reason not in the list above maps to the existing generic `admission-blocked`, never to nothing.
- The same order applies on server, CLI and web through the shared `waitCodes` order. With several inadmissible assignments, the first wait per code wins (existing `orderWaits` rule).

**Key interfaces:**
- `DomainStore.assignmentAdmission(assignmentId)`: read-only source of the reasons; do not change its semantics.
- `WaitFacts`: new input for the next-to-run assignment's admission reasons (plus its profile id for the Fix).
- `waitCodes` / `waitLabels` / `deriveWaits()`, and the CLI `cliFix()` (reuses `open-profile`).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A task whose non-lead pending assignment has a revoked profile shows the revoked-profile wait with an Open profile Fix on task detail, Inbox and the CLI.
- [ ] A task whose assignment has a stale profile revision shows the profile-changed wait with an Open profile Fix.
- [ ] A stale instructions revision, a profile not permitted and a held assignment each produce their wait without a Fix.
- [ ] A lead assignment's task-level reasons are not duplicated as assignment waits.
- [ ] Unit tests for `deriveWaits` cover each new code and ordering. Integration tests with the real SQLite store cover at least the revoked-profile and stale-revision cases end to end.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes. The wait list in the first-task user flow and SPEC is updated.

**Out of scope:**
- New operator commands for re-binding or refreshing an assignment's revisions.
- Power holds (#984).
- Changing scheduler admission behaviour.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/987
**Planned against:** `main` at `01bd875ebcb6f9872b64e445bc3d2c61ea3bea6c`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

The accepted contract is the triage Agent Brief (https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/987#issuecomment-6171086943). Its blocker #984 is delivered in the base (PR #991: `power-held` slot, `waits` capped at `max(waitCodes.length)`, optional `Wait.detail`).

### Approach

Keep waits a read-side projection (Brief decision). `OperatorApi` collects, for each next-to-run assignment, the reasons `DomainStore.assignmentAdmission(id)` returns beyond the task's own `DomainStore.admission(taskId)` reasons, and passes them with the assignment's profile id and disclosable profile name into `deriveWaits` as a new `WaitFacts` field. `deriveWaits` maps each to one of five new codes placed after `power-held` and before `local-dependency`, or to the existing `admission-blocked`. Server, CLI and web already render waits generically from `waitCodes`/`waitLabels`/`fix`/`detail`, so they pick up the codes in the same order.

### Guardrails

- Do not change `DomainStore.assignmentAdmission()`, `DomainStore.admission()`, scheduler admission, refusal or any persisted state. This is a projection only.
- Wait order stays defined once by `waitCodes`; no surface sorts or filters on its own. `orderWaits` keeps the first wait per code, so with several inadmissible assignments the first candidate's wait (and its profile) wins.
- Every assignment reason the scheduler can see for a candidate yields a wait: the five mapped codes, otherwise `admission-blocked`. Never drop a reason.
- A profile name is shown only through `this.safe(name, excluded)`; when it fails the exclusion check, omit `detail` (never `null`).
- Out of scope (Brief): new operator commands to re-bind or refresh assignment revisions (the existing `assignment.apply` stays unexposed here), power holds, scheduler behaviour, composer predictions (`projectWaits`, `assigneeWaits`), Board/task-list rows and legacy server-rendered pages, which show admission reasons rather than waits.
- **Repair budgets.** A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example: the candidate set does not match what the scheduler admits, `admission(taskId)` reasons are not a superset of the task-level part of `assignmentAdmission`, or a named test seam cannot express a case) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; then stop and return a replan report. Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Projection, not derive-from-admission.** The issue asked to consider computing waits directly from admission. Rejected, as the Brief decided, on this evidence: (1) `wait-reasons.ts` documents waits as "a read-side projection only: admission keeps its own reasons and order", and the flow order (runtime, power, dependencies, source, approval, capacity) differs from admission's push order; (2) about half the waits are not admission reasons at all (`runtime-*`, `claude-token-unavailable`, `power-held`, `approval`, `capacity` come from harness status, power status, coordination and capacity); (3) the scheduler's own check (`service.ts` `validateAssignment`) adds reasons that are not domain admission (`recovery-continuation-unresolved`, `repository-access-revoked`, expected-revision mismatches) and refuses rather than waits on revision mismatches (`immutableRevisionMismatches`), so "admission = waits" would still need a mapping layer. Drift is instead closed by the guaranteed `admission-blocked` fallback in `deriveWaits` for any unmapped assignment reason, the same rule task-level reasons already follow.
- **Assignment-only reasons = `assignmentAdmission(id).reasons` minus raw `domain.admission(taskId).reasons`.** `assignmentAdmission` starts from `admission(taskId, isLead)`; the lead flag (`deliveryContinuation`) only removes reasons (`task-unready`, closed `source-hold`, `source-withdrawn`), so the non-lead task reasons are a superset of its task part. Subtracting them satisfies "a lead assignment's task-level reasons are not duplicated" without re-deriving `isLead`. Use the raw domain reasons, not `OperatorApi.admission()`'s mapped ones (that maps `source-*` to `source-held`).
- **No `expected` argument.** Use the one-argument `assignmentAdmission(id)`, matching the assignment row's `waitReason` and `operator-runtime.ts` `statusForAssignment`. Expected-revision mismatches make the scheduler refuse the request (`state.begin` `refuse`), which takes it out of the queued candidate set, so they are not a standing wait.
- **Candidates are exactly `executingWaitFacts`'s:** each assignment whose current turn request (`service.currentTurnRequest(id, version)`) is `queued`, and each `pending` assignment with no request. Extract that selection into one private helper used by both, so the runtime facts and the admission facts cannot disagree on "next to run".
- **Codes, labels, Fix** (in `waitCodes` order after `power-held`):

  | Admission reason | Wait code | Label | Fix |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `profile-revoked` | `assignment-profile-revoked` | Assignment profile revoked | `open-profile` (assignment's profile) |
  | `assignment-profile-revision-stale` | `assignment-profile-stale` | Assignment profile changed | `open-profile` (assignment's profile) |
  | `assignment-instructions-revision-stale` | `assignment-instructions-stale` | Assignment instructions changed | none |
  | `profile-not-permitted` | `assignment-profile-not-permitted` | Assignment profile not permitted | none |
  | `assignment-held` | `assignment-held` | Assignment held | none |
  | any other | `admission-blocked` (existing) | Waiting to start | none |

  Codes avoid reusing the admission strings `assignment-profile-changed` / `assignment-instructions-changed`, which already mean expected-revision mismatches. The profile is named through #984's `detail` field (the disclosable profile name), because `waitLabels` is a static per-code record; CLI and web already render `detail`. The revoked profile's settings page can un-revoke it (`web/src/profile-config.tsx`), so `open-profile` is the recovery path.
- **Revocation also bumps the profile version** (`profile.configure` sets `version = version + 1`), so a revoked assignment normally also reports `assignment-profile-stale`. Keep both: the scheduler refuses on the stale revision independently (`immutableRevisionMismatches`), and `waitCodes` order makes revoked primary.
- **#989 interaction.** A provider turned off under #989 reaches waits through `profileWaitFacts` runtime facts (`profile-runtime-not-configured`), not `assignmentAdmission`. If #989 adds an admission reason instead, it lands on `admission-blocked` until it gets a code. No change here.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` — `waitCodes`, `waitLabels`, `WaitFacts`, `deriveWaits()`, `orderWaits()`, `cliFix()` (`open-profile` prints `Settings → Profiles → <id>`).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `taskWaits()` calls `deriveWaits` with `admissionReasons: admission.reasons` and `lead: this.executingWaitFacts(t, excluded)`; `executingWaitFacts()` selects candidates; `profileWaitFacts()` returns nothing for revoked profiles; `safe()` applies exclusions.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `assignmentAdmission()` (reasons listed in the table plus `assignment-completed`), `admission()`.
- **Existing renderers (no edit expected):** `src/cli/task-write.ts` (`Waiting:` lines, `detail`, `cliFix`), `web/src/wait-reasons.tsx` (Fix href `/app/profiles/<id>/settings`, `detail`), `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` `holdNotices()` (generic `Execution held (<lowercased label>)` branch). `src/operator/contracts.ts` caps waits at `waitCodes.length`, which grows automatically.
- **Follow:** #984's `power-held` change (commit `01bd875e`) for the shape of a new code across `wait-reasons.ts`, tests and docs; `test/operator-api.test.ts` "runtime waits come from the pending assignment's profile, not only the lead's" for the non-lead assignment seam; `test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` "Task detail lists waits in order…" for the Open profile href assertion.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 → T2`, acyclic. T2 needs T1's `WaitFacts` field and codes in `wait-reasons.ts`, so they run sequentially; no concurrent tasks.

#### 1. Assignment wait codes in the shared derivation

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` (`waitCodes`, `waitLabels`, `WaitFacts`, `deriveWaits`); `test/operator-wait-reasons.test.ts`; `docs/user-flows/first-task.md` (wait table); `docs/SPEC.md` (wait-reason paragraph).
**Test:** In `test/operator-wait-reasons.test.ts`, with `deriveWaits` pure inputs:
- Each mapped reason on one assignment `{ profileId: P, profileName: "Worker", reasons: [r] }` yields exactly its code, the table's Fix (`{ kind: "open-profile", profileId: P }` for revoked and stale; `null` otherwise), `links: []`, `detail: "Worker"`; with `profileName: null` the wait has no `detail` key.
- An unmapped reason (for example `assignment-completed`) yields `admission-blocked`.
- Ordering: facts with `project-paused`, a runtime wait, `powerHold`, `local-dependency` and all five assignment reasons produce `project-paused`, runtime, `power-held`, the five codes in table order, then `local-dependency`.
- Two assignments with the same reason and different profiles keep only the first (its Fix and detail).
- `waitCodes` slice between `power-held` and `local-dependency` equals the five codes in order; CLI `task-write` lines for one new code print `Waiting: Assignment profile revoked`, `  Worker`, `  Fix: Settings → Profiles → P`.
**Implementation:** Insert the five codes and labels per the table. Add `WaitFacts.assignments?: readonly { profileId: string; profileName: string | null; reasons: readonly string[] }[]` (documented as admission reasons of next-to-run assignments beyond task admission). In `deriveWaits`, for each assignment and reason push the mapped wait with `detail` when `profileName` is set, else `admission-blocked`. Add the five rows to the first-task table (after "Held by power supervision") and extend the SPEC paragraph: an assignment's revoked or changed profile opens the profile; changed instructions, a profile not permitted by routing and a held assignment have no Fix; each names the assignment's profile.
**Validate:** From the worktree root with Node from `.node-version`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-wait-reasons.test.js`; expect all tests pass, including the new cases, and `npm run typecheck` exits 0.
**Complete when:** the new codes derive with the table's Fix/detail and order, and docs list them.

#### 2. Feed next-to-run assignment admission into task waits

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the branch.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`executingWaitFacts`, new private candidate helper, new private `assignmentWaitFacts(t, excluded)`, `taskWaits`); `test/operator-api.test.ts`; `test/operator-cli-task.test.ts`; `test/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts`; `test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** Real SQLite store through `createOperatorFixture` + `seed` + `OperatorApi`, following the pending-assignment runtime test (healthy Codex lead, project paused by `seed`, non-lead profile in `routing.configure` candidates, `assignment.create` pending with no request):
- **Revoked:** `profile.configure` with `revoked: true` on the non-lead profile. `readTask(taskId).data.waits` codes start `project-paused`, then `assignment-profile-revoked` (Fix `open-profile` for that profile, `detail` the profile name), then `assignment-profile-stale`; `project-paused` appears once and there is no `admission-blocked`.
- **Stale profile revision:** `profile.configure` changing `instructions` (version bump, not revoked) yields `assignment-profile-stale` with `open-profile` and no revoked wait.
- **Stale instructions / not permitted / held:** bump project instructions (`project.configure` instructions change), remove the profile from `routing.configure` candidates, and for held use `f.seedPersistedState` to set the assignment `state='held'` and insert a `queued` `turn_requests` row for it (a held assignment is a candidate only through a queued request; follow "a running assignment with a queued turn reports its own runtime waits"); each yields its code with `fix: null`.
- **No duplication / healthy:** with a healthy permitted non-lead assignment, waits are unchanged from today (`project-paused` plus any runtime waits); the lead assignment's task-level reasons never reappear as assignment or `admission-blocked` waits.
- **Exclusion:** with the profile name in the exclusion list, the wait has no `detail`.
- **CLI:** in `test/operator-cli-task.test.ts`, `task get` for the revoked case prints `Waiting: Assignment profile revoked`, the name line and `  Fix: Settings → Profiles → <id>` in order, and `--json` waits equal `readTask` waits.
- **Inbox:** in `test/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts`, `holdNotices` for waits `[assignment-profile-revoked, assignment-held]` yields notices titled `Execution held (assignment profile revoked)` and `Execution held (assignment held)` in that order.
- **Task detail:** extend "Task detail lists waits in order…" with a task whose non-lead assignment profile is revoked: `Assignment profile revoked` is listed and `Fix: Open profile` links to `/app/profiles/<profileId>/settings`.
- Sensitivity: with `taskWaits` not passing `assignments`, the revoked and stale API cases fail.
**Implementation:** Extract the candidate selection from `executingWaitFacts` into a helper returning `{ assignment, request }[]`; `executingWaitFacts` keeps its current behaviour on top of it. `assignmentWaitFacts` computes `taskReasons = new Set(d.admission(taskId).reasons)` once, then for each candidate `reasons = d.assignmentAdmission(id).reasons.filter(r => !taskReasons.has(r))`, skipping candidates with none, with `profileName = this.safe(d.profile(profileId).name, excluded) ?? null`. Pass it as `assignments` in `taskWaits` only.
**Validate:** From the worktree root, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-task.test.js dist/test/operator-inbox-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator-wait-reasons.test.js` and `node --test --test-name-pattern="Task detail lists waits" dist/test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** revoked, stale-profile, stale-instructions, not-permitted and held non-lead assignments each surface their wait on the task read, CLI, Inbox and task detail, with no duplicated task-level waits.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Revoked non-lead pending assignment shows revoked wait with Open profile on task detail, Inbox, CLI | 2 | T2 Revoked API case, CLI, Inbox and Task detail cases |
| Stale profile revision shows profile-changed wait with Open profile | 1, 2 | T1 per-code case; T2 Stale profile revision case |
| Stale instructions, not permitted, held each wait without Fix | 1, 2 | T1 per-code cases; T2 third case |
| Lead's task-level reasons not duplicated | 2 | T2 Revoked (single `project-paused`, no `admission-blocked`) and No duplication cases |
| `deriveWaits` unit tests cover each new code and ordering; SQLite integration covers revoked and stale | 1, 2 | T1 tests; T2 Revoked and Stale profile revision cases |
| Same order on server, CLI, web | 1, 2 | T1 ordering case; T2 CLI `--json` equality and Task detail case |
| Unmapped assignment reason never dropped | 1 | T1 `admission-blocked` case |
| `npm run check` passes; first-task flow and SPEC updated | 1, final | T1 docs; Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the worktree root with Node from `.node-version` and npm from `package.json`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate; expect exit 0 (typecheck, lint, format, build, full tests). CI runs the same check on the PR head.
- Baseline: CI run 38589242671 on the base SHA passed the required `check` job (Node 24). The non-required `check-node-26` job failed in one unrelated browser test ("retained omission chronology phone head observations…"), as it also did on `24237649`; a recurrence there is not a regression from this ticket. Focused base runs of `operator-wait-reasons`, `operator-inbox-presentation`, the `operator-api` wait tests and the CLI wait test passed locally.

### Review focus

- The candidate helper must leave `executingWaitFacts`'s runtime-wait choice unchanged (first candidate with a runtime wait, else the first, else the lead).
- Each candidate costs one `assignmentAdmission` read on every task read; the set is bounded by the task's assignments, like the existing runtime facts.

content.title: Local review: finish unconfirmed-write handling and stabilise the setup browser test

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Keep a draft write that is still in flight when its page unmounts as an exact, checkable unconfirmed write, close the P3 review items from #965, and stabilise the setup browser test.

**Current behavior:**
- Local review draft writes (anchor stage, draft save, edit, discard) go through the shared review state's `write()`. When the page unmounts, its cleanup only marks an in-flight `review.send` as `unknown`. A draft write becomes unconfirmed only when its response eventually arrives after unmount (the `!alive` branch). If that response stalls, `state.pending` stays `true` and `state.unconfirmed` stays `null`. Reopening the task then disables every Local review write and offers no "Check whether it saved" action.
- A refused write that falls back to the panel can show the same refusal twice, in the composer and in the panel, once that composer is reopened.
- The composer's "Check whether it saved in Local review." pointer is plain text, and the panel warning does not take focus.
- No dedicated tests cover (a) a write answered after its page unmounted, or (b) a stage replay held because no draft is loaded.
- `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`, "Setup keeps every value on a checkout mismatch and rechecks on create", sometimes times out in a `page.waitForFunction` focus check (default 5 s) under load (CI run 38483463669, and locally during #949).

**Desired behavior:**
- When a page unmounts while a draft write is still awaiting its response, that exact request (command, including its request key, and its `DraftWrite` intent) is immediately kept as the shared state's unconfirmed write, and `pending` no longer blocks the next page on its own. Reopening the task shows the unconfirmed-write notice with its single "check" action, which replays the same request under the same key. A late response from the original request must not clear or duplicate that held check, and must never trigger a second write under a new key.
- A refusal appears in exactly one place: the composer when it is on screen, otherwise the panel.
- The composer pointer is a link to the Local review panel (`#local-review`). Following it, or falling back to the panel, moves focus to the panel warning.
- The setup test waits on the real readiness signal: the focused, invalid path field after the "fix fields" outcome renders. It must not rely on the default timeout race. It passes reliably under parallel load.

**Key interfaces:**
- The shared local-review state (`state.pending`, `state.unconfirmed`, `subscribe`/`notify`) and the page effect cleanup that currently handles only `state.send`.
- `holdUnconfirmed(command, intent, result?)`, `write(command, intent, refreshWhenRecorded)`, and the unconfirmed-write `check` action ("Replays the exact request of an unconfirmed draft write, never a new one").
- Optional: `review.changed` and `state.notify()` are two routes to the same re-render. Collapse them into a single subscriber slot only if it falls out naturally. Otherwise state in the PR why you left them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Browser regression test: start a draft write whose response is held, navigate away, reopen the task. The unconfirmed notice and its check action are present, other writes are disabled only by that unconfirmed write, and the check replays the identical request key. Releasing the original response afterwards does not create a second write or lose the check.
- [ ] Test for a write answered after its page unmounted.
- [ ] Test for a stage replay held because no draft is loaded.
- [ ] A refused write that falls back to the panel shows its refusal once after the composer is reopened (test).
- [ ] The composer pointer is a link to `#local-review`, and the panel warning receives focus (test asserts focus).
- [ ] The setup browser test's wait is bounded on the readiness signal. Run it repeatedly under load (for example several parallel runs) with no timeouts, and report the evidence in the PR.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes.

**Out of scope:**
- Surviving a full reload with an unconfirmed write (an accepted, documented limit: the server draft is authoritative).
- Changes to `review.send` handling beyond what the shared fix requires.
- Raising global test timeouts to mask the flake.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/974
**Planned against:** `origin/main` (detached) at `b67ebff04f1c2962b2a754a9b6d3c81e8bf6a70c`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Contract: the triage Agent Brief on #974 (accepted) plus the issue body. Acceptance bullets are cited below as AC1-AC7 in the brief's order: AC1 held-write regression test, AC2 write answered after unmount, AC3 stage replay held without a draft, AC4 refusal once, AC5 pointer link and focus, AC6 setup test stable under load, AC7 `npm run check`.

### Approach

One PR, four slices. T1 keeps a draft write that is still awaiting its answer when its page unmounts as the shared state's exact unconfirmed write (the P2 fix) and adds the AC1-AC3 tests. T2 and T3 close the P3 review items in the same files. T4 fixes the setup flake. Its cause is a product race in the shared `sendDraft` focus step, not a slow test (see Planning decisions), so the fix is a commit-aware focus step plus a deterministic regression test. T1 to T3 are sequential. T4 is independent.

### Guardrails

- `state.unconfirmed` stays plain data `{command, intent, outcome}`. Its check replays the same request under the same key, and a write is never repeated under a new key. A late answer from a page that is gone must not clear, duplicate or re-create the held check, and must not start a follow-up write.
- Out of scope, per the brief: surviving a full reload with an unconfirmed write (the server draft stays authoritative), `review.send` handling beyond what the shared cleanup requires, and raising any global or per-test timeout. No `design/` edits. The `design/` snapshot is untouched, and the pointer copy ("Check whether it saved in Local review.") does not change.
- Optional clarity item (`review.changed` vs `state.notify()`): declined. `changed` is the owning page's re-render handle and `notify()` fans out to every mounted page through it. Collapsing them replaces call sites without removing either route. State this in the PR.
- **Plan-mismatch budget** (one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles) applies only when an approved-plan seam or repository assumption proves wrong. Those are: (a) the page cleanup in `useLocalReviewController` is the one seam where an in-flight draft write can be captured, and holding it there leaves no state with `pending` true and `unconfirmed` null; (b) the setup flake is the `sendDraft` frame-callback race diagnosed below, and a commit-aware focus request in `useDraft` / `ConfigurationDraft` fixes it for every `sendDraft` caller; (c) the Files and Changes composers both render the shared `ReviewComposer`, with the check living only in the Local review panel. **Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.** That covers selector or wait fixes, formatting, lint, type errors, fixture setup, stale expectations in neighbouring tests and CI reruns. Routine corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority are recorded briefly in the existing delivery record, with affected evidence renewed. Stop for a material design or contract change or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **In-flight write held at unmount (T1).** Keep the in-flight request as a per-page `useRef` inside `useLocalReviewController`, not as new shared state. Only the page that started a write may hold it; another mounted page's cleanup must not. Cleanup calls the existing `holdUnconfirmed(command, intent)` with no result, which yields the synthetic `command-outcome-unknown` warning. `state.pending` is left `true`, so it never blocks the next page without an unconfirmed write to check, and it is cleared by the check that settles the write (`write()` already ends with `state.pending = state.unconfirmed !== null`). `pending` is not derived from `unconfirmed` because it must also cover the post-answer refresh and settle.
- **Late answers are ignored, not re-held.** After `await execute(command)`, `write()` returns at once unless `inFlight.current?.command === command`. Cleanup nulls that ref, so the old page's continuation touches nothing: no refresh, no settle, no new key, no re-write of `state.unconfirmed`. This replaces the `!alive.current` branch, which re-held on the late answer and could therefore re-create a check the next page had already consumed. It is also correct if `taskId` changes in place. `alive` stays for `send` and `reconcile`.
- **Refusal in one place (T2).** `refuse()` writes the composer error and, when the form is not on screen, the same object to `state.notice`. Hand-over is by identity. When the form comes on screen, `ReviewComposer` clears `state.notice` if it is the composer's own error object. When the form leaves while the composer still holds an error and the panel slot is empty, it gives the error back to the panel ("otherwise the panel").
- **Focus (T3).** "The panel warning" is the unconfirmed `ActionOutcome`; focus lands on its "Check whether it saved" action, the same target the shared `focus` prop already uses. Two entry points share it. (1) Following the composer pointer link focuses the already-mounted warning synchronously in the click handler. (2) "Falling back to the panel": a hold made by a live page while no composer form is on screen (`!state.composerShown`) mounts the warning with `focus`, because the control the operator used is gone, as in `task-workspace.tsx` (`focusUnconfirmed`) and `settings.tsx` (`DraftMessage`). A warning restored on a later visit, or made by a dead page, never takes focus. A hold with the composer on screen leaves focus alone because the pointer link is the route. Refusal notices in the panel do not take focus; the brief names only the warning.
- **Setup flake: diagnosis and evidence (T4).** `project-setup.tsx` disables every field while `locked(d)` (pending, unknown, recorded). `settings.tsx` `sendDraft` focuses the rejected field with a bare `requestAnimationFrame` right after `await d.submit()`. The re-render that re-enables the fields is a separate scheduler task. When the frame callback runs first, `focus()` hits a still-disabled input and is a no-op, and nothing retries. The existing wait (`document.activeElement` is the invalid path field with `~/src/relay`) is already the real readiness signal. In the failing order it never becomes true, so no longer timeout helps.
  - CI run 38483463669, attempt 1: the test failed after 6.16 s with `page.waitForFunction: Timeout 5000ms exceeded` at `dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js:152:16`. Passing runs take about 1.7 s.
  - Local probe on this base (a scratch script, not committed): `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` wrapped to log `disabled` and whether focus took. Under heavy load (40 parallel journeys plus 20 CPU burners) 1 of 40 logged `{label:"Local repository path", disabled:true, took:false}`. The 39 others logged `disabled:false, took:true`.
  - Deterministic reproduction on the same base: `window.requestAnimationFrame` replaced by `cb => queueMicrotask(() => cb(performance.now()))` just before clicking Create. Frame callbacks then always precede React's scheduled render. The wait for a focused invalid field failed 3 of 3.
  - Other tests wait on the same focus (`operator-settings-browser`, `operator-project-config-browser`, `operator-account-browser` and others), so the fix is shared.
  - Fix: focus follows the commit that shows the outcome. `ConfigurationDraft` counts announced changes (`revision`). `useDraft` reports the revision each commit has rendered. `afterRender(fn)` runs `fn` at once if the latest revision is committed, else on the commit that reaches it. `sendDraft` queues its focus there instead of using a frame callback. No timers or retries. The triage brief assumed a test-only fix; the diagnosis shows none can work, and the brief's outcome ("waits on the real readiness signal, passes reliably under load") is met by the product fix plus the deterministic test.
  - Bounded proof: T4's adversarial-ordering test must fail on the base and pass after the change. If it still fails with the commit-aware step, stop and replan; do not add retries or timeouts.
- **Docs.** `docs/SPEC.md` Local review (the "Preserve drafts through navigation and refresh" bullet, ~L1006) gets one sentence in place. A draft write that is lost, or still unanswered when the operator leaves the task page, stays checkable from the Local review panel on return. A browser reload discards that pending check, and the server draft stays authoritative (an anchor staged for a comment that was never saved is left unused). The reload limit is currently undocumented despite the brief calling it documented.
- **Baseline.** CI run 38519501587 on exactly `b67ebff0` ran `npm ci`, the Playwright install, `npm run test:fixture-preflight` and `npm run check` on Node 24 (`check`) and Node 26 (`check-node-26`); both succeeded, so the baseline is not re-run locally. Focused checks on this base, after `npm run build` with Node 24.21.0: the setup mismatch test and four local-review tests pass. `origin/main` has since advanced to `e8e6da69` (#976 and #975 merged). The delta touches `design/`, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/pen-save-all.applescript`, `web/src/setup.css` and one 10-line assertion in the setup phone test (~L1181). It does not intersect any planned file, symbol or insertion point, so it is compatible.
