- Entry-point coverage to report in the PR: the composer pointer and refusal handover apply to both the Files and Changes composers through the shared `ReviewComposer` (Files is exercised by tests; Changes is by construction); the Local review panel is the only check and focus target; no other screen, deep link or notification exposes draft writes; the `sendDraft` change reaches all `submitDraft` callers.
- Independent review of the integrated candidate with the usual verdict (`ship`, `fix-first` or `rethink`) before merge.

### Review focus

- T1: that no path leaves `pending` true with `unconfirmed` null; only the starting page holds a write; the identity guard also covers the nested stage -> save write.
- T4: that the shared `sendDraft` change leaves every other settings page's focus behaviour intact (watch the neighbouring suites), and that nothing in `settings-state.ts` imports DOM types.
- T3: that auto-focus happens only for live-page holds with no composer form on screen.

### Allowed deviations

- Test names, helper names, and which existing test is extended versus a sibling added, provided each assertion above is covered.
- File paths and `dist/test/…` paths when #973 has renamed the test files.

### Re-plan triggers

- The adversarial-ordering test still fails with the commit-aware focus step (do not add retries or timeouts).
- A held write cannot be captured at unmount without making `pending` or the check ownership depend on state outside the page's controller.

content.title: Action feedback: one plain outcome message for Settings saves

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/946
**Planned against:** `main` at `f2b9ffb231f5be89a2d3bec40206be7d4f8cc5d9`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Web-only change. Move every Settings save outcome into one shared component: a quiet success line, or one alert with a single action for rejected, changed-elsewhere and unknown outcomes. It sits beside a collapsed **Details** disclosure that can be copied. `ConfigurationDraft` carries plain copy and the receipt fields for Details. `DraftOutcome` renders the single message. Each surface then deletes its duplicate lines (`SavedNotice`, receipt text, routing Aside time, extra placement status, extra alerts) and moves its "Review latest …" conflict button into the alert. Credential-reference rows show the saved line after the form closes. One cross-surface browser test proves that each outcome shows exactly one message on desktop and phone. The contract is `docs/user-flows/feedback.md`, and the design is section 12 of `design/DESIGN.md` (frames 154–160 and components `ugjxZ`, `NaPr2`, `TsFAB`, `Q5Ff9`, `kUOab`).

### Guardrails

- The recovery semantics stay as they are. Rejected and conflicting saves keep their input. An unknown outcome still locks the other fields until it is checked. The unknown action ("Check whether it saved") still calls `ConfigurationDraft.reconcile`, which resends the exact frozen bytes. `CommandLifecycle`, `matchesConfigurationReceipt`, keys and versions are unchanged.
- Out of scope: task-side writes, the composer, replies, question answers, local review, sign-out, CLI credentials and read-only status copy (#947); project setup's ready check and inline lead profile (#949); readiness (#948); the checklist and Fix actions (#950); the CLI receipt output.
- Server, core and contract files are off limits: `src/**`, including `src/operator/contracts.ts`, `src/standalone/*` and `src/core/*`, which #886/PR #956, #877–#880 and #914 edit. `test/operator-configuration.test.ts`, `test/operator-api.test.ts`, `test/github-source-config.test.ts` and `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts` are also off limits, because PR #956 edits them. Do not edit `design/design.pen` unless T7's divergence branch applies.
- Message text never contains command names, IDs, versions, request keys, raw codes, or the words recorded, receipt, observation, admission, reconcile, submission or revision. Those values appear only in Details. Success lines carry no caveats. Every failure message ends with "Your changes are still here." Messages have at most two short sentences.
- Plan-mismatch budget: this applies only when an approved-plan seam or repository assumption below is factually wrong. Examples: `DraftOutcome` is not the shared owner of the save outcome, or a surface cannot show its saved line from `ConfigurationDrafts.saved()`. That case allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; stop and request a replan after that. Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, assertion-copy, documentation, lint/format and CI defects are not plan mismatches. The ticket owner repairs them in scope without using that budget, and records the correction in the delivery record.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Shared module for #947.** The outcome UI goes in a new `web/src/action-feedback.tsx`, not in `settings.tsx`. #947, #949 and #950 reuse the same success line, alert-with-one-action and Details components outside Settings drafts. `settings.tsx` keeps only the draft adapter (`DraftOutcome`).
- **The draft owns the copy; the component owns the presentation.** `settings-state.ts` already computes `notice`, and surfaces read `d.notice` directly (`discovery-credential.tsx:255`, `project-setup.tsx:514`, `source-config.tsx:610`). Keeping the copy there avoids a second source of text. `ConfigurationDraft` gains a `details` record (`command`, `resource`, `version`, `requestKey`, `code`; each optional) set in `send()` and `reject()`. It is captured before `CommandLifecycle.settle` resets the frozen command on rejected and conflict outcomes: the command type and key come from the command that `lifecycle.begin()` returns, resource and version from the receipt, and the code from `CommandState.code`. `purge()` and `adoptVersion()` clear it.
- **Copy.** Recorded: "Saved." (a surface may pass a one-sentence plain summary through a `success` prop, for example routing's "Saved. Routing now uses Ada and Eli."). Pre-send or schema reject: "Couldn't save: check the highlighted fields. Your changes are still here." Too large: "Couldn't save: the change is too large. Your changes are still here." Rejected: "Couldn't save. Your changes are still here.", where the GitHub credential-reason branch uses `sourceCredentialCopy(...)` + " Your changes are still here.". Conflict: "A newer version was saved elsewhere." with the single action **Review changes**. Unknown: "We couldn't confirm the save." with the single action **Check whether it saved**. Adopt: "Loaded the latest version. Your changes are still here." If Pen frames 154–160 can be read through MCP and give different wording within these rules, follow the frames.
- **Severity.** Rejected uses `Alert variant="destructive" role="alert"`. Changed elsewhere and unknown use a new `warning` variant with `role="alert"`. The success line is plain text with `role="status"` and no Alert. `web/src/ui/alert.tsx` has no warning variant today. Add `warning` using new `--nova-warning-fg` and `--nova-warning-bg` tokens in `web/src/tokens.css`, beside `--nova-destructive-*`. Take the values from the Pen variables if MCP is available. Otherwise use an amber pair with at least 4.5:1 text contrast on `--background`, and record the choice.
- **Conflict action.** `DraftOutcome` gains `review?: () => void`. On `conflict` it renders the one button inside the alert. Each surface deletes its separate "Review latest … revision" button. For sync preview, the button that appears after `recorded` is also deleted: a recorded preview shows only the success line.
- **Details.** Use a native `<details>`/`<summary>Details</summary>` (collapsed by default) holding a monospace `<dl>`, plus a **Copy** button that calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with `key: value` lines. It appears only when at least one field exists. Native disclosure needs no new dependency and is keyboard-accessible.
- **One saved time.** `savedLine` becomes `Saved HH:MM` when this session saved the loaded version, and returns `null` otherwise, because a version must not appear in visible text. The panel subtitle (`statusLine` in `project-config.tsx`) is the only saved-time line. The routing Aside heading "Saved · HH:MM / version N" becomes the static "Saved routing", and its candidates line stays. `SavedNotice`, `ReceiptText` and `.settings-saved` are deleted.
- **Silent credential rows.** `ReferenceRow` and `DiscoveryCredentialRow` call `settled()`, which runs `d.startOperation()` and wipes `notice`. `ConfigurationDrafts.saved(type)` survives that purge (`savedRecords`). When the form is closed, the row renders a success line from that record, such as "Saved HH:MM." Saves and clears both go through it. The row's destructive `d.notice` Alert is replaced by the shared outcome component.
- **Remove all repositories.** In `source-config.tsx:557`, delete the destructive Alert. The `removeAll` checkbox in the change list remains the single confirmation, and its consequence goes in a change-list line ("Removes every repository from <project>.").
- **Pen frames.** `design/DESIGN.md` at the base already lists frames 154–160 and refreshes section 12 (commit e21abd49, #951). That acceptance criterion is satisfied at the base unless the implementation diverges from the frames; see T7.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/settings.tsx` — `DraftOutcome` renders the button, `draft.notice` Alert and `draft.receipt` Alert (two messages). `ReceiptText` produces the "Recorded …" copy, and `SavedNotice` adds a third copy. `submitDraft` refreshes on recorded and focuses the first invalid field on rejected.
- **Existing:** `web/src/settings-state.ts` — `ConfigurationDraft.send/reject/submit/adoptVersion` write `notice`. `ConfigurationDrafts.get` records `savedRecords` through `onSaved`, and `placementReceipts()` feeds the extra placement status in `sync-placement.tsx`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/settings-view.ts` — `savedLine` and `clock`. `web/src/project-config.tsx` — `statusLine` (panel subtitle). Surfaces that use `DraftOutcome`: `routing-config.tsx:130`, `project-config.tsx:309`, `source-config.tsx:591`, `profile-config.tsx:215,429`, `recovery.tsx:140`, `sync-placement.tsx:89,244,311`, `discovery-credential.tsx:113,320`, `project-setup.tsx:425`. Surfaces that use `SavedNotice`: routing, project-config, source-config, profile-config, recovery.
- **Existing:** `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts` — `startSettings(journey, path, viewport)`, plus the `desktop` and `phone` (390×844) viewports. Tests cause an unknown outcome with `page.route("**/api/operator/commands", r => r.abort())` and a conflict by saving the same resource through `f.service` first (see `test/operator-project-config-browser.test.ts:136,195,346`).
- **New:** `web/src/action-feedback.tsx` — `ActionOutcome({ tone: "success"|"error"|"warning", message, action?, details? })`, which renders `data-slot="action-outcome"`, and `OutcomeDetails({ fields })`. `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts` gains `outcomeMessages(page)`, which returns `page.locator('[data-slot="action-outcome"]')`.
- **Follow:** `web/src/ui/alert.tsx` `cva` variants for `warning`, and `test/operator-project-config-browser.test.ts` for browser setup and assertions.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 → {T2, T3, T4, T5} → T6, with T7 independent and finishing before T6. T1 owns every shared file (`settings.tsx`, `settings-state.ts`, `settings-view.ts`, `settings.css`, `tokens.css`, `ui/alert.tsx`, `action-feedback.tsx`, test fixture). T1 also repairs every existing assertion broken by the shared copy change, in any test file, so the suite is green before surface work. T2–T5 edit disjoint `web/src` files and can be reviewed and tested independently. However, all of them may need assertion edits in the shared `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts`, so either run them sequentially under one owner on one branch, or serialize edits to that file. One PR for the whole ticket. Coordinate with other in-flight work: if #912 merges first, rebase `web/src/settings.css` (a comment-only edit). #947, #949 and #950 should start after this merges, since they consume `action-feedback.tsx`.

#### 1. Shared single-outcome component, plain draft copy and Details

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols (permitted paths):** `web/src/action-feedback.tsx` (new: `ActionOutcome`, `OutcomeDetails`); `web/src/settings.tsx` (`DraftOutcome` rewrite with `review?` and `success?` props, unknown button "Check whether it saved"; delete `ReceiptText` and `SavedNotice`); `web/src/settings-state.ts` (`ConfigurationDraft.notice` copy, new `details`); `web/src/settings-view.ts` (`savedLine` → `Saved HH:MM` or `null`); `web/src/ui/alert.tsx` (`warning` variant); `web/src/tokens.css` (`--nova-warning-fg/bg`); `web/src/settings.css` (outcome line and Details styles; delete `.settings-saved`); delete the `SavedNotice` import and JSX only in `web/src/routing-config.tsx`, `web/src/project-config.tsx`, `web/src/source-config.tsx`, `web/src/profile-config.tsx`, `web/src/recovery.tsx`; `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts` (`outcomeMessages`); `test/operator-settings-state.test.ts`; `test/operator-settings-presentation.test.ts`; assertion-only edits for old copy in `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-project-config-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-profile-config-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-source-credential-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-model.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/operator-settings-state.test.ts`, use a fake client that returns recorded, rejected (with `fieldPaths` and `code`), conflict and unknown results. For each, assert the `notice` copy from Planning decisions, that `notice` contains none of /recorded|receipt|observation|admission|reconcile|submission|revision|version/i, and that `details` holds the command type, request key, resource and version (recorded) or code (rejected/conflict). Assert that reconcile after unknown resends identical bytes (keep the existing assertion). In `test/operator-settings-presentation.test.ts`, assert that `savedLine` returns `Saved 10:52` for a matching version and `null` otherwise.
**Implementation:** As described in Planning decisions. `DraftOutcome` renders one `ActionOutcome` chosen by `draft.phase`: `pending` shows only the "Saving…" label, `recorded` shows the success line, `rejected` shows the error with no action, and `conflict` shows a warning with `review` when given (Planning decisions covers each surface's review button). `unknown` shows a warning with the Check button, `editing` with a notice (adopt) shows a success-tone line, and the Details come from `draft.details`. Remove the second `draft.receipt` Alert.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-settings-state.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator-project-config-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-browser.test.js`; expect all tests to pass.
**Complete when:** Every `DraftOutcome` shows at most one `[data-slot="action-outcome"]`, `SavedNotice` and `ReceiptText` no longer exist, and the listed tests pass.

#### 2. Project configuration tabs: General, Routing, GitHub source, Sync & placement

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the branch.
**Files and symbols (permitted paths):** `web/src/routing-config.tsx` (Aside heading; `review` prop; success summary naming candidates), `web/src/project-config.tsx` (`statusLine` uses the new `savedLine` and omits the saved part when it is `null`; `review` prop), `web/src/source-config.tsx` (delete the remove-all Alert, add the change-list line, `review` prop, adopt-drop notice in plain copy), `web/src/sync-placement.tsx` (preview `review`; delete the post-recorded preview button; replace the `placementReceipts` "Recorded placement outcome: task …; project …; version …" status with nothing, because the placement `DraftOutcome` already shows "Saved."; `UnsettledPlacement` uses the shared unknown outcome), `test/operator-project-config-browser.test.ts`, and assertion edits in `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts` and `test/operator-source-credential-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/operator-project-config-browser.test.ts`, the routing save test asserts `outcomeMessages(page)` has count 1 with the text "Saved." and that `.settings-status` contains exactly one `Saved \d\d:\d\d`. The remove-all test asserts that `page.getByRole("alert")` has count 0 before Save and that the checkbox is the only confirmation. The placement test asserts no text matching /Recorded placement|version/.
**Implementation:** As listed. `ConfigurationDrafts.placementReceipts` may be deleted if it has no remaining caller (it is in `settings-state.ts`, which T2 may edit only for that deletion).
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-project-config-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-source-credential-browser.test.js`; expect a pass.
**Complete when:** Routing shows 1 message instead of 5, and General, GitHub source and Sync each show one; the tests pass.

#### 3. Profiles (create and edit) and capacity

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1.
**Files and symbols (permitted paths):** `web/src/profile-config.tsx` (`review` prop replacing the "Review latest profile revision" button; create success "Saved." plus the existing "Create another profile" action unchanged), `web/src/recovery.tsx` (capacity `DraftOutcome`; no raw project IDs in text), `test/operator-profile-config-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.ts`, and assertion edits in `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** Profile create, profile edit and capacity save each assert `outcomeMessages(page)` count 1 and no text matching /Recorded|profile\.create|version 1|system:capacity/. The profile conflict test asserts that one warning alert contains the only **Review changes** button and that the typed input is kept.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-profile-config-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-browser.test.js`; expect a pass.
**Complete when:** Profile create and edit and capacity each show exactly one message; the tests pass.

#### 4. Discovery credential and Claude token rows confirm visibly

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1.
**Files and symbols (permitted paths):** `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx` (`ReferenceRow`, `DiscoveryCredentialRow`: closed-row success line from `p.drafts.saved(type)`; replace the `d.notice` Alert with `ActionOutcome`), `test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** For the discovery set, discovery clear, Claude token set and Claude token clear, the test asserts that after save the form is closed and the row shows exactly one `[data-slot="action-outcome"]` with the text /^Saved/. The unknown clear asserts one warning with "Check whether it saved" and that replay sends the same key (keep the existing exact-bytes assertion).
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.js`; expect a pass.
**Complete when:** Saves and clears are no longer silent; the tests pass.

#### 5. Project setup create

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1.
**Files and symbols (permitted paths):** `web/src/project-setup.tsx` (rejection shows one message: keep the field errors and the shared `DraftOutcome` alert, and delete the separate `setup-alert` "Project not created" Alert at about line 334. The recorded `setup-recorded` Alert becomes the single success outcome, with the plain heading "Created <name>. It's paused.", no "revision 1", and its existing actions kept. `ghDraft` notice uses `ActionOutcome`.) Also `web/src/setup.css` if the removed classes need it, and `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** Create asserts one outcome with no /Recorded|revision/. The checkout-mismatch rejection asserts that `page.getByRole("alert")` has count 1 and that the values are kept. The unknown-create replay keeps its exact-bytes assertion and shows a single "Check whether it saved".
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.js`; expect a pass.
**Complete when:** Setup create and rejection each show one message; the tests pass.

#### 6. Cross-surface one-message browser test on desktop and phone, and docs

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T2, T3, T4, T5, T7`
**Prerequisites:** T2–T5 complete; T7 result recorded.
**Files and symbols (permitted paths):** `test/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.ts` (new), `docs/user-flows/feedback.md` (Status line: Settings saves implemented; other surfaces still planned), and `README.md` only if it lists the feedback flow as planned.
**Test:** New file, using `startSettings` with each of `desktop` and `phone`. For General (`/app/projects/:atlas/settings`) and Routing (`?tab=routing`): (a) success: edit, Save, and assert that `outcomeMessages(page)` has count 1, its text matches /^Saved\./, and none of the forbidden words, IDs or `version` appear. (b) Rejected: submit an invalid value and assert count 1, `role=alert` and "Your changes are still here." (c) Changed elsewhere: change the resource through `f.service` first, Save, and assert count 1 with exactly one button, "Review changes". (d) Unknown: abort `**/api/operator/commands` and assert count 1, exactly one button "Check whether it saved", and disabled fields. Then expand Details, assert that the Command, Resource, Version, Request key and Code labels are present where applicable, click Copy, and assert the clipboard text (grant `clipboard-read`/`clipboard-write` permissions on Chromium). On desktop only, assert one success message each for the profile edit, capacity, sync preview, Claude token save and clear, and discovery save.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.js`; expect all cases to pass on both viewports.
**Complete when:** The new test passes and the docs state what is implemented.

#### 7. Design frames check (Pen; no edit expected)

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** The Pen app is running, so its MCP server is reachable. It was not reachable during planning.
**Files and symbols (permitted paths):** none by default. Only if the divergence branch applies: `design/design.pen`, edited through the Pen MCP server and saved through the native Pen UI, never parsed, plus `design/DESIGN.md` refreshed through MCP.
**Implementation:** Through the Pen MCP server, read frames 154 `JGenC`, 154b `TZhQ0`, 155 `hRBAj`, 156 `RsAq8`, 157 `sbOOH`, 158 `x4tTqV`, 159 `IS6X0`, 160 `HYN4M` and components `ugjxZ`, `NaPr2`, `TsFAB`, `Q5Ff9`, `kUOab`. Confirm they exist and match the implemented copy and structure, and record the `nova-warning-*` values for T1. If the implementation diverges materially (for example, the frames show a different single action), edit the frames and refresh `DESIGN.md` in Pen; that is a separate design change from the code tasks. If the Pen app is unavailable, the baseline `design/DESIGN.md` node table (lines 409–412) and section "Action feedback" (lines 551–574) are the acceptance evidence, and the copy follows `docs/user-flows/feedback.md`.
**Validate:** Run `rg -n 'JGenC|TZhQ0|hRBAj|RsAq8|sbOOH|x4tTqV|IS6X0|HYN4M' design/DESIGN.md` from the repository root; expect all eight node IDs. Also record the MCP read result, or the fact that Pen was unavailable.
**Complete when:** The frames are confirmed present, or edited if the implementation diverged. This is not a code task and does not block T1–T5.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Each save shows exactly one outcome message (success line; one alert with one action for rejected, changed-elsewhere and unknown); routing 5 → 1 | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 | `outcomeMessages` count assertions in T2–T5; T6 (a)–(d) |
| `SavedNotice`, the receipt alert and duplicate saved-time lines are removed; the panel keeps one "Saved HH:MM" | 1, 2 | T1 deletion plus typecheck; T2 `.settings-status` single `Saved HH:MM` assertion |
| Shared Details disclosure with the receipt fields and Copy | 1, 6 | T1 `details` state test; T6 Details/Copy assertion |
| No service vocabulary, IDs, versions or codes; no success caveats; failures say the input is kept | 1, 6 | T1 notice regex test; T6 forbidden-text and "Your changes are still here." assertions |
| Discovery credential and Claude token save and clear confirm visibly | 4, 6 | T4 row assertions; T6 desktop cases |
| Removing all repository access uses one confirmation (checkbox, no alert) | 2 | T2 remove-all test: alert count 0 |
| Pen frames 154–160 drawn; `DESIGN.md` refreshed | 7 | Satisfied at the base (e21abd49); T7 `rg` check plus MCP confirmation |
| Browser tests assert one message per outcome on desktop and phone | 6 | `test/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.ts` on both viewports |
| Unchanged: input kept, unknown blocks edits, retry never duplicates | 1, 4, 5, 6 | Existing exact-bytes replay assertions kept; T6 (d) disabled fields |

### Final validation

- From the repository root on the integrated delivery candidate, with the Node version from `.node-version` (24.21.0) and npm@12.2.0: run `npm ci`, then `npx playwright install chromium webkit` if the browsers are absent, then `npm run test:fixture-preflight && npm run check`. Expect typecheck, lint, format check, build and the full test suite (Chromium and WebKit journeys) to pass. CI (`.github/workflows`) runs the same steps on the PR. Base `f2b9ffb2` CI run 38358259313 passed.
- No live runtime or manual gate: this is operator-UI copy and structure, covered by the fixture browser tests. The only external dependency is the Pen app for T7, and the baseline `DESIGN.md` evidence covers its acceptance if Pen is unavailable.

### Review focus

- Check that the unknown outcome cannot be dismissed or replaced by a new operation before it is checked, and that moving the conflict button into the alert keeps `adoptLatest` semantics (`source-config` adopt with dropped rows).
- Check that the credential-row success line does not reveal the reference name or value.

content.title: Readiness checks: ensemble doctor, Settings panel and Add Claude

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/948
**Planned against:** `main` at `f2b9ffb231f5be89a2d3bec40206be7d4f8cc5d9`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

One service-side readiness module runs seven read-only checks and returns a closed, value-free result. Two GET reads expose it: `/api/operator/readiness` (all checks) and `/api/operator/readiness/claude-token` (the Claude token check alone, used by the Add Claude panel's live **Token readable** row). `ensemble doctor` and a Settings → Readiness panel both render the same `/api/operator/readiness` response, parsed with one shared schema. The Add Claude panel goes at the top of the runtime page's left column. It shows the runbook's token-file commands with Copy, reuses the existing `ClaudeTokenRow` for the `file:`/`env:` reference and Clear, and adds the live check. Contracts: `docs/user-flows/readiness-check.md` and `docs/user-flows/claude-runtime.md`. Design: `design/DESIGN.md` "Readiness and Add Claude (151, 152, 152b)".

### Guardrails

- Checks change nothing. They make no domain writes, no command receipts, no model turns, no `thread/start` or `turn/start`, no GitHub writes and no token reads beyond the existing value-free `readClaudeToken` and `gh auth status` detection. They do not mkdir, chmod or open the SQLite owner lock. Re-running is the only action, and there is no cache: each read runs fresh.
- Output never contains secret values or paths. That covers the token value, the token path, the env variable name, the data directory, the auth file path and gh tokens. Reasons and fix lines are fixed strings from a closed set. Thrown `Error.message` text and path values are never interpolated. Profile names may appear in the runtime harness reason.
- Status is exactly `pass`, `fail` or `not-configured`, with one fix line per non-pass result. A not-configured item is never reported as a failure.
- The Claude sandbox self-test stays per turn and reports on the waiting task, not here.
- Unchanged: the existing Settings-index `ClaudeTokenRow`, its Clear behaviour, the `claude-token.configure` command and its validation, discovery configuration, and Codex runtime start.
- Out of scope:
  - Getting-started checklist and Fix actions (#950), project setup (#949), action-feedback rewrites (#946/#947).
  - Profile-form and first-task entry points to Add Claude (#949/#950).
  - Codex executable placement outside the fixed launchd `PATH`.
  - A non-zero doctor exit for failing checks.
  - Any production or Haze installation change.
- Concurrency ownership:
  - **#886 / PR #956:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`, `operator-receipts.ts`, `src/core/domain.ts` and `src/core/command-results.ts` are off limits. `src/standalone/service.ts` gets only the one additive method in T2. Rebase on #956 if it merges first.
  - **#946:** this ticket must not edit `web/src/settings.tsx`, `settings-state.ts`, `settings-view.ts`, `settings.css`, `discovery-credential.tsx`, `ui/alert.tsx`, `tokens.css`, `action-feedback.tsx` or `test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.ts`. Import from them only.
  - **#880/#879/#878/#877/#914:** these touch service, API and core seams. Keep T2's wiring additive and rebase when they land.
- Plan-mismatch budget versus ordinary repairs:
  - **Plan mismatch:** a factual assumption of this plan turns out wrong, for example a named seam, symbol, route-wiring point, fixture or file ownership does not behave as described, or #946's merged API cannot be consumed without editing its files. That allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles inside the stated scope. Then stop and request a replan.
  - **Ordinary repairs:** implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, formatting and CI defects. Repair them in scope without consuming that budget. Record the correction briefly in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence.
  - Investigate unknown overlap with in-flight work before proceeding. Stop for material design or contract changes or an exhausted grant.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

**Codex login**
- The check re-runs the public `CodexRuntime.verifyLoginAndPolicy()` (`account/read {refreshToken:false}` then `config/read`) on the service's running App Server. That is the same authentication initialization the service performs at start, and it requests no model turn.
- This checks what the running service actually uses. It avoids spawning a second App Server with an unscrubbed environment. The service's spawn environment and runtimes map are private, so this needs one additive `StandaloneService` method (T2).
- A Codex harness that is unavailable, a missing method (as on fixture fakes) or a timeout reports `fail`.

**Codex executable and git**
- Both resolve by searching `process.env.PATH` directories for an executable regular file (`fs.access` `X_OK`), the same PATH `CodexRuntime` and `runGit` inherit.
- Nothing is spawned. Nothing like `which` exists today, so there is one small helper in the readiness module.

**GitHub discovery**
- The check reuses `OperatorApi.readDiscoveryStatus()` (public; it runs only `gh auth status` and resolves no token), passed in as a dependency.
- Not configured gives `not-configured`. Configured and `available` gives `pass`. Otherwise it is `fail`, with fix "Run `gh auth login`, or Settings → discovery credential".

**Claude token**
- No reference gives `not-configured`.
- A reference gives `pass` only when `service.claudeTokenStatus().state === "available"`.
- A `file:` failure reason is "Token file " + the fixed `readClaudeToken` problem string, for example "permits group or other access". It never includes the path.
- An `env:` reference reports "Token variable is unavailable". `restart-required` reports "Restart the service to use this variable".
- The fix line points to Add Claude.

**Runtime harness**
- The check considers each harness used by a non-revoked profile (`domain.profiles()` and `profileRuntime`).
- It passes when each used harness is `available` in `service.harnessStatuses()` and every Claude profile passes `unsupportedRuntimeField(runtime, harnessSettings("claude"))` (`src/core/execution-runtime.ts:69`). Codex profiles carry no model or effort.
- No non-revoked profile gives `not-configured`.
- Claude's supported list is read lazily before the first Claude turn (`src/standalone/claude.ts` `settingsStatus`). While it is `null`, Claude profiles are not counted as accepted. The check reports `fail` with the fixed reason "Claude's supported models are not known yet" and the fix "Run a Claude task; supported models are read before its first turn, then run the check again". `readiness-check.md` records this.
- The reason lists failing profile names and fields; the fix is the contract line.

**Data and auth paths**
- The data directory must pass `assertCanonicalDirectoryPath` and be a real directory owned by `process.getuid()` with `(mode & 0o077) === 0`.
- The auth file must be a regular non-symlink file owned by the service user with mode `0600`, under a canonical parent.
- Paths come from the existing `[dataDir, authFile]` pair at `src/standalone/cli.ts:155`. A failure gives a named rule, for example "Operator auth file must be owned by the service user with mode 600", never a path.

**Response shape and execution**
- New shared schema in a new `src/operator/readiness.ts`, not the 3,500-line `contracts.ts`: `readinessCheckSchema = { id, label, status, reason: string|null, fix: string|null }` (strict).
  - `id` is one of `codex-executable | codex-login | git | github-discovery | claude-token | runtime-harness | data-paths`, in that fixed order.
  - `readinessSchema = envelope({ checks: readinessCheckSchema[] })`.
  - `claudeTokenCheckSchema = envelope(readinessCheckSchema)`.
- Checks run concurrently, each bounded: Codex login 10 s; the existing 10 s gh limit is kept.

**`ensemble doctor`**
- New single-word CLI command, special-cased like `logs` in `src/cli/main.ts`.
- It reuses the existing `diagnostics.read` capability, so `cliCapabilities` and its inventory do not change.
- It exits 0 whenever the read succeeds, whatever the check results. Existing service/transport error exits are unchanged. The JSON `data` is the unmodified service `data`.

**Add Claude**

- It shows the runbook commands (`docs/operations/standalone-macos.md#claude-subscription-token`) with the suggested private path `$HOME/.ensemble/claude/claude-token`. The commands create that directory with `mkdir -m 700 -p`. #### 1. Readiness checks module and shared schema

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`

**Test:** `test/readiness.test.ts` builds `Readiness` with plain fake deps and a temp directory (`mkdtemp`, `chmod`). It asserts the following:
- **Codex executable / git:** an executable file in a temp PATH dir gives `pass`. Missing or non-executable gives `fail` with the contract fix line.
- **Codex login:** `verified` gives `pass`. `failed`, `unavailable`, and a promise that never settles (fake timers or a short injected timeout) each give `fail` with "Run `codex login` as the service user".
- **GitHub discovery:** unconfigured gives `not-configured`. gh signed-in and available gives `pass`. Configured but unavailable gives `fail`.
- **Claude token:** none gives `not-configured`. A 0600 file with a token gives `pass`. A 0644 file gives `fail` with reason "Token file permits group or other access". Symlink and missing cases are covered too. `env` missing and `restart-required` give their fixed reasons.
- **Runtime harness:**
  - No profiles gives `not-configured`.
  - A Codex profile with codex `available` gives `pass`.
  - Codex `unavailable` gives `fail` "Restart the service…".
  - A Claude profile with a model outside the `harnessSettings` list gives `fail`, with the profile name and `model` in the reason.
  - Claude settings `null` gives `fail` "Claude's supported models are not known yet".
  - A revoked Claude profile is ignored.
- **Data paths:** a private canonical dir plus a 0600 auth file gives `pass`. A 0755 data dir, a 0644 auth file and a symlinked dir component each give `fail` with a named rule.
- **Ordering and privacy:** `read()` returns all seven ids in fixed order and parses with `readinessSchema`. The serialized result contains none of the canary strings: token value, token path, env name, temp dir path, auth file path.
- **No-write sensitivity:** file mtimes and modes under the temp dirs are unchanged after `read()`.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Checks run with `Promise.all` and per-check bounds. Every reason and fix is a literal from the module. Never interpolate a caught error or a path.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/readiness.test.js`; expect all cases to pass.
**Complete when:** the module and schemas exist and the unit suite passes.

  - Then `launchctl bootout` the exact label and confirm it with `launchctl print`, which must fail (exit 113). Confirm the PID has exited and the port is closed, then delete the scratch root.
  - Unproved ownership, an unknown bootstrap outcome or an exhausted deadline: no bootout and no signals. Keep the scratch root and report a hold. Never kill by name.
  - A failed pass condition is recorded as a failure. It is repaired offline and needs separate authorization for another attempt.
- **Evidence:** record the candidate SHA, the steps, the results and the limits. It must state that this proves the candidate on a real launchd instance, not an existing production installation, and give the counts (0 turns, 0 GitHub writes).
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check`; expect exit 0 with zero failures on the candidate. Then run the live check once; expect every pass condition above and proved cleanup.
**Complete when:** docs are updated, the full check is green on the candidate SHA, and the evidence file records the passed live check.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Seven checks, each Pass/Fail/Not configured with one fix line; sandbox self-test stays per turn | 1, 2 | `test/readiness.test.ts`; `test/readiness-http.test.ts` |
| Codex login initializes App Server auth without a model turn | 1, 2, 6 | T2 recorded-methods test; T6 live (no executions) |
| `ensemble doctor` and Settings panel identical from the same read; no secrets or token path | 3, 4 | T3 parity and canary assertions; T4 API-equality and canary assertions |
| Add Claude: commands with Copy, saves `file:`/`env:`, live Token readable, Clear as today | 5 | `test/operator-add-claude-browser.test.ts`; unchanged `operator-claude-token-browser` |
| Pen frames 151–152b drawn; `design/DESIGN.md` refreshed | — | Already on main via #951 (`e21abd49`): `design/DESIGN.md` lines 408, 544–549; no edit |
| Service tests per check; CLI and browser tests over both surfaces | 1–5 | Suites named in T1–T5 |
| Bounded live check on launchd service recorded in `docs/evidence/` | 6 | Disposable LaunchAgent run and `docs/evidence/948-readiness-*.md` |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, on Node 24.21.0 and npm 12.2.0, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate; expect exit 0 (type checking, lint, format, build and all tests, zero failures). CI runs the same on the PR.
- After that passes, run the single bounded live check from T6 on that exact SHA. A code change after the live run requires a new full check, and the live result stays scoped to the qualified SHA unless separately re-authorized.

### Review focus

- No interpolated paths or error messages in reasons. Canary coverage across the API, CLI human/JSON output and both panels.
- `verifyCodexLogin()` must not disturb an in-flight turn or mark the runtime failed on a read error. The 10 s bound must hold.
- T2's additive edits rebase cleanly over #956 and the other in-flight seam work. No `operator-api.ts` edit.
- T5 consumes #946's merged components without editing #946-owned files.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- The running Codex runtime cannot be re-verified without restarting it or spawning an unscrubbed App Server.
- Claude supported-model acceptance needs a model-turn or task-workspace read to be correct.
- #946 lands with a different Settings or Claude row ownership model.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/947
**Planned against:** `main` at `54f87db355f9011292c8daddf14a40d241ba869f`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Apply the `docs/user-flows/feedback.md` contract to every task-side write named in #947 by reusing the shared `ActionOutcome` / `OutcomeDetails` component from #961 (`web/src/action-feedback.tsx`). Each write keeps its existing lifecycle (request key, frozen draft, unknown/conflict handling); only the message layer changes: one pending indicator (the button label), one outcome message in plain words, and receipt fields (command, resource, version, request key, kind, code) in Details. Read-only screens keep their data but move hashes, IDs, raw states and codes into Details or metadata and say what the state means. The server-rendered `/runtime` task page that Stop and Resume redirect to is checked against the same wording rules. Docs, Pen frames (136, 161–165 and the Part 2 sweep) and `design/DESIGN.md` are reconciled last against the shipped copy.

### Guardrails

- Unchanged: frozen drafts and blocked edits on unknown outcomes, exact-request reconciliation (no duplicate delivery), request keys and command payloads, Stop/Resume semantics and the retained `/runtime/control/stop` form post, CLI credential issuance semantics. No API, schema, service-domain or CLI receipt-output change. The operator CLI keeps its receipt output.
- "Check the list" for CLI credential create/rotate re-reads the credential list only; it never resubmits (create/rotate have no request key).
- Sign-out shows no receipt and no Details.
- Out of scope: approval writes, Settings saves (#946, done), project setup (#949), getting-started/Fix actions (#950), new endpoints, CSS redesign beyond what `action-feedback.css` already provides, and renaming `/runtime` form button labels ("Best-effort Stop", "Resume task") that live harnesses `test/s04d/live-operator.mjs` and `test/s05/live-journey-ui.mjs` select by name.
- Message text must pass the Settings wording rule already encoded in `test/operator-settings-state.test.ts` ("every outcome reads in plain words…"): no recorded, receipt, observation, admission, reconcile, submission, revision, digits/IDs, command names or codes; every failure says whether input is kept.
- Plan-mismatch vs ordinary defect: if an approved-plan seam or repository assumption here is factually wrong (for example a named symbol, file, test seam or state field does not exist or behaves differently from the Implementation context), that uses this plan's allowance of one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping for a replan. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Reuse, don't extend, the shared component.** `ActionOutcome` already provides success/error/warning tones, a single action, focus handoff and Details with Copy. Task-side surfaces render it directly; add a prop only if a surface proves it cannot be expressed (record why). Follow `web/src/settings.tsx:detailRows` for the Details field labels (Command, Resource, Version, Request key, Code; add Kind where a receipt carries one).
- **Receipt evidence stays reachable.** Replace "Receipt key <key> · <kind>" (`task-workspace.tsx` ~1784) with Details rows "Request key" and "Kind". `test/operator-search-browser.test.ts:612` currently finds `Receipt key ${originalKey}`; it must open Details and assert the Request key row value instead, preserving the acceptance evidence.
- **Sign-out.** `app.tsx:logout` already re-reads the session via `setBootstrap`. Change: an unconfirmed sign-out (non-401 `ClientError`) sets a pending-check flag instead of message text; when the re-read returns signed out, show nothing extra (success: the sign-in screen is the outcome); when it returns still authenticated, show one warning in the authenticated shell only ("We couldn't sign you out. You're still signed in." with no Details). Remove the duplicate render at `app.tsx:591` / `:823` so the message renders in exactly one place, and drop the "Current session requires sign-in." suffix.
- **CLI credentials.** `operator-credentials.tsx:act` keeps the automatic list re-read on every outcome. Success: Rotate shows one success line naming the credential and that the old one stays active until revoked (DESIGN.md rule); Revoke closes the dialog and shows one success line on the panel ("Revoked <name>."); Create's confirmation stays the one-time token dialog. Failure: an error alert names the cause from the client error and says the list was re-read; unknown create/rotate shows one warning with the single action **Check the list** that calls `list.refresh()` only; codes go to Details. Revoke failures stay inside the dialog.
- **Stop dialog.** `task-header.tsx` replaces the three-item `consequences` list and the extra metadata line with one or two sentences (e.g. "Stops new work on this task and asks running turns to end; some effects may still finish. Files, history and results are kept."). The affected-assignments line may remain as the description if the total stays at two sentences; otherwise fold it in.
- **`/runtime` Stop/Resume result.** Both handlers redirect to the runtime task page (`src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts`). Check and fix that page's Task controls paragraph (currently three-plus clauses with "observes", "admission") and the Stopping status line against the wording rules; keep button labels and the route error bodies in `src/standalone/operator.ts` (shared by every runtime POST) unchanged, and record the check result in the PR. Update `test/operator-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts:599` (`/^Stopping; effects may continue/`, which mirrors `web/src/task-overview.ts`) and any live-harness text matches only where wording changes.
- **"revision" → "version" in read-only copy** is deliberate (PR #951 note): change visible labels such as `inbox-detail.tsx` "Revision / revision N"; keep data fields and SPEC terminology unchanged.
- **Design files are not text-mergeable.** `design/design.pen` is encrypted and edited only through the Pen MCP (`mcp__pencil__*`); the MCP cannot save, so saving requires opening the file in the Pen app and saving with computer use. The Pen app was not reachable during planning (`get_app_state` failed), so frames 161–165 and the sweep were not read; PR #951 states section 12 (frames 154–167) and the 99-frame sweep were already drawn, so T9 verifies and reconciles rather than redraws, with frame 136 the one known required change.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/action-feedback.tsx` — `ActionOutcome`, `OutcomeDetails`, `OutcomeField` (from #961); styles in `action-feedback.css`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/composer-state.ts` — `ComposerState` submit path sets `notice` for pending ("Submitting the recorded creation request…"), recorded ("Task recorded as Ready. Creation does not establish execution."), unknown and rejected (`Submission rejected (<code>)`); `task-composer.tsx` renders the recorded phase in `<section aria-label="Creation receipt">` with "Execution observations" and "creation receipt" copy, plus admission copy at ~344 and ~452.
- **Existing:** `web/src/question-response.tsx` — submit handler sets `state.notice`/`state.failureCode`; `Reason: {state.failureCode}` at ~451; state in `question-response-state.ts`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` — reply/comment-review send at ~660–810 sets `state.notice` to `<state>: <code>. …` strings and `auxNotice` "Observation / review receipt recorded"; receipt line at ~1784; state in `task-workspace-state.ts`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/local-review.tsx` — five failure notices from ~296 onward carry raw codes; one `state.notice` alert at ~954.
- **Existing:** `web/src/app.tsx` — `logout()` (~705) and two `logoutNotice` renders (~591 sign-in branch, ~823 shell).
- **Existing:** `web/src/operator-credentials.tsx` — `act()` (~108) shared by create, rotate and revoke; `failure`/`revokeFailure` strings.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-header.tsx` — `consequences` array (~56) and `TaskHeaderActions` Stop dialog.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` — runtime task page HTML (~517 Task controls paragraph; ~481 "Stopping; effects may continue"); `/runtime/control/stop|resume` handlers (~784–797) redirect to it.
- **Existing (read-only copy):** `turn-identity.tsx:40–56`, `task-files.tsx:60–72` (inline SHA-256), `inspection-changes.tsx` (reason codes, comparison IDs), `retained-evidence.tsx:~263/~299`, `recovery.tsx:~64/~296/~331`, `inbox-detail.tsx:~113`, `tasks.ts:161/174` ("Admission held"), `search.tsx`.
- **Follow:** `web/src/settings.tsx:detailRows`/`DraftOutcome` for Details rows; `test/operator-action-feedback-browser.test.ts` for desktop+phone outcome journeys; `test/operator-settings-state.test.ts` "every outcome reads in plain words…" for the wording regex.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic. T1–T8 have `Depends on: none`; T9 depends on T1–T8. T1–T8 touch disjoint source files; shared test files (`operator-task-browser`, `operator-search-browser`) and `web/src/tasks.ts` (edited by T8, imported by T1's composer) mean concurrent owners must coordinate those files; a single owner may take them in any order. T9 must not run concurrently with #949's Pen/`DESIGN.md` edits (see Re-plan triggers).

Shared setup for every **Validate** below: from `/` of the implementation checkout with `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH` (Node 24 from `.node-version`), after `npm ci`, run `npm run build` first.

#### 1. Task composer: one pending indicator, one plain outcome

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/composer-state.ts` (`notice` strings, add receipt detail fields as state), `web/src/task-composer.tsx` (recorded/unknown/rejected render, section label, admission copy at ~344/~452); tests `test/operator-task-composer.test.ts`, `test/operator-task-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-composer-layout-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** State test: drive recorded-Ready, recorded-draft, unknown and rejected outcomes; assert each `notice` fails the plain-wording regex, rejected says input is kept, and detail fields contain the request key and code. Browser: pending shows only the button label (no status line); recorded shows one `[data-slot=action-outcome]`; rejected shows one alert with code only inside Details; unknown shows one warning with one action and the frozen draft; no visible "Creation receipt", "Submission", "admission", "observation".
**Implementation:** Remove the pending notice line (button label "Creating…"/"Saving…" only). Recorded: "Task created." / "Draft saved." via `ActionOutcome` success; keep the Open task link and the execution status block, relabelled in plain words. Rejected: "Couldn't create the task: <cause>. Your input is still here." Unknown: one warning, action re-sends the exact original request (existing lifecycle). Rename the section label away from "Creation receipt".
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/operator-task-composer.test.js dist/test/operator-task-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-composer-layout-browser.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** composer messages meet the contract and the three files pass.

#### 2. Question answers

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/question-response.tsx` (submit handler ~160–185, status block ~440–456), `web/src/question-response-state.ts`; tests `test/question-response-state.test.ts`, `test/operator-question-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-question-cards-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** For recorded, unknown, conflict and failed: one outcome message, plain wording, failure says selection kept; failed code appears only in Details (no `Reason:` line); unknown keeps the answer frozen with one action.
**Implementation:** Replace `notice` strings ("Answer sent." etc.; no "admission"), render through `ActionOutcome`, move `failureCode` into Details, keep `QuestionHolds` as separate read-only context.
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/question-response-state.test.js dist/test/operator-question-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-question-cards-browser.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** checks pass with no `Reason:` text on screen.

#### 3. Task workspace reply and comment review

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` (send/post handlers ~660–810, `auxNotice`, receipt line ~1784, trailing reconciliation paragraph), `web/src/task-workspace-state.ts` (`notice`, `receipt`); tests `test/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-comments-browser.test.ts` (lines ~250, ~330, ~439, ~463 assert old strings), `test/operator-search-browser.test.ts:612`.
**Test:** Reply and comment review each show one pending label and one outcome; rejected/uncertain say the draft is kept; no "Receipt key", `<state>: <code>`, "Observation / review receipt recorded"; Details holds Request key and Kind; the search test opens Details and finds the original request key.
**Implementation:** Collapse `auxNotice` + `state.notice` + receipt line into one `ActionOutcome`; the uncertain path keeps the single "check" action that reconciles with the original operation; drop the static "Failed or uncertain operations retain the draft…" paragraph (now carried by failure messages).
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-comments-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-search-browser.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** checks pass and the request key is reachable only via Details.

#### 4. Local review

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/local-review.tsx` (failure notices ~296–450, alert ~954, send status ~1014–1050); tests `test/operator-local-review-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-review-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** Each of the five failure paths shows one alert naming the cause, says the draft is kept, and shows its code only in Details; save/send success shows one line; the "one identical status line before sending" acceptance (docs/acceptance.md) still holds.
**Implementation:** Route the notices through `ActionOutcome` with codes in Details; keep send labels unchanged.
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/operator-local-review-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-review-browser.test.js`; expect all pass.

**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/operator-credentials.tsx` (`act`, `failure`, `revokeFailure`, rotate/revoke handlers); test `test/operator-cli-credentials-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** Rotate success shows one line naming the credential; revoke success closes the dialog and shows one line; a failed request shows the cause and that the list was re-read; an unknown create and an unknown rotate each show one warning with **Check the list**, and clicking it issues a GET of the credential list and no POST (assert via request log); revoke failure stays inside the dialog.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Use the `command-outcome-unknown` error message the client already raises to choose the unknown path.
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/operator-cli-credentials-browser.test.js`; expect all pass including the no-POST assertion.
**Complete when:** checks pass.

#### 6. Sign-out

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/app.tsx` (`logout`, `logoutNotice`, renders ~591 and ~823); test `test/operator-account-browser.test.ts` ("desktop account menu: pointer, keyboard, pending and unknown-outcome sign-out").
**Test:** Unknown sign-out where the re-read returns signed out: sign-in screen with no warning. Unknown sign-out where the re-read returns authenticated: exactly one warning in the shell, no Details. Pending shows "Signing out…" only.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions.
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/operator-account-browser.test.js`; expect all pass. Baseline note: this file's desktop sign-out test intermittently fails on base with `page.screenshot: Timeout 5000ms exceeded … waiting for fonts to load` (CI run 38420947522 on the base SHA; locally 1 of 3 full-file runs, 0 of 1 isolated). A screenshot font-wait timeout there is a known pre-existing flake, not this slice's regression; any other assertion failure is a defect.

#### 7. Stop dialog and `/runtime` Stop/Resume page

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/task-header.tsx` (`consequences`, `TaskHeaderActions`), `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` (runtime task page Task controls paragraph and Stopping status), `web/src/task-overview.ts` only if its mirrored Stopping label changes; tests `test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-runtime.test.ts`; live harness text matches in `test/s04d/live-operator.mjs` / `test/s05/live-journey-ui.mjs` only if matched wording changes.

#### 8. Read-only status copy

**Task ID:** `T8`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/turn-identity.tsx`, `task-files.tsx`, `inspection-changes.tsx`, `retained-evidence.tsx`, `recovery.tsx`, `inbox-detail.tsx`, `tasks.ts` (`reasonLabels`), `search.tsx`; tests `test/operator-files-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-retained-inspection-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-retained-evidence.test.ts`, `test/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-task-list.test.ts`, `test/operator-search-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.ts`.

#### 9. Contract docs, Pen frames and DESIGN.md

**Task ID:** `T9`
**Depends on:** `T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8`
**Prerequisites:** shipped copy from T1–T8; Pen app running and reachable by the Pen MCP.
**Files and symbols:** `docs/user-flows/feedback.md` (Status: move delivered surfaces to implemented; leave approvals and anything not delivered as planned), `design/design.pen` (frame 136 `LJKCn`; frames 161 `thtaf`, 162 `zxH2a`, 162b `Gi4zR`, 163 `o6kBCw`, 164 `h0FyJW`, 165 `TGj4A`; Part 2 sweep frames listed in review notes 167 `nrZYd`), `design/DESIGN.md` (CLI credentials notes ~482/~508, Action feedback section ~551).

Save by opening `design/design.pen` in the Pen app and saving with computer use (the MCP cannot save), then confirm the file changed in Git. Refresh `design/DESIGN.md` through the MCP (frame 136 row, the "Check the list below before retrying" note, any copy now shipped). If the Pen app or computer use is unavailable, stop this slice and report it as a blocker rather than editing `design.pen` any other way.
**Validate:** run `git diff --stat -- design/ docs/user-flows/feedback.md` (expect `design/design.pen` and `design/DESIGN.md` changed); `grep -n "Check the list" design/DESIGN.md` hits the CLI credentials notes (the source-credential "Check whether it saved" note at ~456 stays, since that save resends an exact request); re-read frame 136 via the MCP and expect **Check the list**; `npm run format:check` passes.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Each write: one pending indicator and one plain outcome; no Receipt key, `Reason: <code>`, `<state>: <code>`, "Creation receipt" | 1–7 | Each slice's browser/state check |

The PR's CI `check` and `check-node-26` jobs must pass on the head SHA.
