content.title: One-pass project setup: inline lead profile and ready check

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/949
**Planned against:** `main` at `54f87db355f9011292c8daddf14a40d241ba869f`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Change only the guided setup page (`web/src/project-setup.tsx`) and the helpers it reuses, as the `docs/user-flows/project-setup.md` contract describes. The service, the API and the command schemas stay as they are. Step 1 renders an inline profile form, reused from `ProfileCreate`, when no live profiles exist. It records through the existing `profile.create` command and selects the new profile in the setup draft. A `beforeunload` guard protects changed setup input. After `project.create` is recorded, a ready check replaces the current "Created … It's paused." block. The ready check:

- lists what was saved;
- derives wait items from the workspace read already loaded, the existing `GET /api/operator/readiness` (#948) and the project's existing composer-options read (capacity);
- offers **Resume and create first task**, which sends the existing `project.configure { paused: false }` command and opens `/app/tasks/new?project=<id>`;
- offers **Keep paused**, which links to `/app/projects/<id>/settings`.

The setup changes ship first. Pen frames 145–147 and `design/DESIGN.md` are reconciled after them, one design edit at a time with #947.

### Guardrails

- Unchanged: `project.create` still records a paused project and starts nothing. No API, contract-schema, domain or service change. Resume uses the existing `project.configure` command with `expectedVersion` and its key lifecycle, and nothing resumes without the operator's click. Repository access stays exactly the step 3 list. Discovery behaviour (117b alert, gh login offer, Retry) stays the same.
- A profile created inline is an ordinary profile. Setup never deletes or revokes it, even when setup is abandoned. Pause project in project configuration stays the way to reverse Resume.
- Outcome messages use the #946 `ActionOutcome`/`DraftMessage` model and must pass the plain-wording rule in `test/operator-settings-state.test.ts` (no IDs, versions, command names or codes in message text, and every failure says whether input is kept). Readiness reasons and fix lines are already fixed, privacy-safe strings (#948). Show them as the Readiness panel does, and never add profile names, paths or token values.
- Out of scope: the Getting started checklist and Fix actions on task waits (#950, blocked by this ticket); the profile-form Add Claude entry (`claude-runtime.md`, planned); in-app (SPA) navigation prompts, where the contract asks only for the browser's leave prompt; discarding the draft on in-app navigation; and new endpoints.
- A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption is different from an ordinary implementation defect. A wrong seam or assumption means a named file, symbol, endpoint, schema field, draft behaviour or test seam in Implementation context does not exist or behaves differently. It gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, then stops for a replan. Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not use that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Inline profile reuses ProfileCreate's pieces, not a second form implementation.** Export from `web/src/profile-config.tsx` `emptyProfile`, `RuntimeFields`, `claudeSettings` and a new `profileCreateCommand(values)`, which builds exactly the object `ProfileCreate` sends today. `ProfileCreate` then uses that function. The inline form has the contract's fields: name, summary, instructions and runtime, with Codex preselected through `runtimeValues({harness:"codex"})`. It sends `capabilities: ""`, which the `text` schema allows. It uses its own draft key `profile.create:setup`, so it never collides with the Settings page's `profile.create` draft.
- **No nested form.** Step 1 sits inside the setup `<form>`. The inline **Create profile** button is `type="button"`. It calls `inline.reject(runtimeErrors(...))` or `inline.submit(client, profileCreateCommand(values), csrf)` (the same sequence as `submitDraft`, minus the event), then `p.refresh()` when the profile is recorded. Enter in an inline field calls `preventDefault` and creates the profile, so it never implicitly submits `project.create`.
- **Selecting the new profile.** When the inline draft is recorded, call `d.set("leadProfileId", <profileId>)` on the setup draft and show the success line "Profile created. Other setup values kept." (`design/DESIGN.md` §145). The lead select reappears once the workspace re-read lists the profile. Until then the existing "Chosen lead (loading profiles)" option covers it. If profile creation fails, the inline input stays, its message shows, and setup values are unchanged. The inline form shows only while the workspace has loaded with zero non-revoked profiles. It replaces the `ActionLink` to `/app/settings/profiles/new` and the "No lead profiles yet" note. The "Unconfigured" lead option stays available in the select.
- **Leave prompt.** Register a `beforeunload` listener (`preventDefault()` plus `returnValue = ""`) while the setup draft or the inline profile draft is `dirty` and no `project.create` has been recorded. Remove it afterwards. `ConfigurationDraft.dirty` is set only by `set()`, never by `initialize()`, so an untouched page never prompts.
- **New visit after a recorded create.** The ready check replaces "Open project configuration" and "Create another project" (frames 146–147 show only Resume and Keep paused). On mount, setup calls `d.startOperation(blank())` when the `project.create` draft is `recorded`, and `d.initialize(blank())` otherwise. Without this, a return visit would reopen a stale ready check. Pending and unknown drafts are untouched, because `startOperation` already refuses them.
- **Wait items come from a pure function.** Add `readyCheckItems(input)` in `web/src/setup-model.ts`. The input is the recorded `leadProfileId`, the workspace (profiles with `runtime`, `runtime`, `harnesses`), the readiness read (loading, unavailable or checks) and capacity. It returns ordered wait items (`text`, optional readiness `fix` line, optional `link {label, href}`), a `blocked` flag, a `checking` flag and `capacityFull`. The items:
  - Lead unconfigured, missing or revoked: "No lead profile. Tasks wait for a lead before starting." This is admission reason `project-lead-unconfigured`/`-revoked`, and the current setup copy already says tasks wait for a lead.
  - `workspace.runtime` unavailable, or the lead harness status `unavailable`: the existing `unavailableAlert(status)` copy.
  - Lead harness status `not-configured`: "<Claude|Codex> runtime isn't enabled for this service." This is the contract's "profile runtime not configured".
  - Codex lead: the reason and fix of each non-pass `codex-executable` or `codex-login` check.
  - Claude lead: the reason and fix of a non-pass `claude-token` check, with link **Add Claude** → `/app/settings/runtime` (Add Claude lives on that page per #948).
  - Readiness read failed: "Readiness couldn't be checked." with a Retry button that re-reads. This blocks, so the check fails closed. While the readiness read loads, the primary is disabled with "Checking readiness…".

  The other readiness checks (git, GitHub discovery, data paths and the runtime-harness count) do not name this lead's state, so the ready check does not list them.
- **"Checkout unverified" cannot follow a recorded create.** The domain verifies every repository before recording it (`src/core/domain.ts` around 685/731, `verifyRepository`). The ready check therefore lists each recorded repository as verified access and adds no re-verification read.
- **Capacity never disables.** Read `/api/operator/projects/<id>/composer-options` (`composerOptionsSchema`) once. When `projectUsage >= projectLimit` or `globalUsage >= globalLimit`, add the non-blocking line "Capacity is full now, so the first task will wait for capacity." A failed capacity read adds nothing.
- **Resume.** Use draft key `project.resume:<projectId>`, separate from the `project.configure:<projectId>` key that the project configuration General tab loads into. The command is `{type:"project.configure", key, projectId, expectedVersion: <create receipt version, 1>, paused:false}`. `matchesConfigurationReceipt` then expects version 2.
  - Recorded: call `p.refresh()` and navigate to `/app/tasks/new?project=<id>`. `ProjectSetup` gains a `navigate: (href: string) => void` prop that `app.tsx` passes from its existing `navigate`.
  - Unknown: `DraftMessage` shows its single "check" action, `reconcile` resends the exact request with the same key, and the Resume button stays hidden or disabled while the draft is pending or unknown. That is the contract's "blocks a second Resume until re-read", matching other configuration saves.
  - Conflict: `review` reads `/api/operator/projects/<id>/configuration`. If the project is already unpaused it navigates as on success. Otherwise it calls `adoptVersion(version)` so Resume can be sent again.
  - Rejected: one alert, and Keep paused stays available.
- **Explainer copy.** "Resume is a separate decision in project configuration." becomes "Resume is a separate step after creation; nothing runs until you choose it." The explainer keeps five items, which an existing test asserts.
- **Design files cannot be merged as text, and Pen was unreachable while planning.** `design/design.pen` is encrypted and may be edited only through the Pen MCP. The MCP cannot save, so the file must be saved by opening it in the Pen app and using computer use. `mcp__pencil__get_app_state` failed while planning ("failed to connect to running Pencil app"), so frames were not read. `design/DESIGN.md:406` already lists frames 145 `HGgoK`, 145b `ju0c4`, 146 `UdnEc`, 146b `PFBIv` and 147 `akpq9` from PR #951, so T3 verifies and reconciles those frames rather than drawing new ones.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/project-setup.tsx` — `ProjectSetup(p: SettingsProps)` owns the `project.create` draft (`useDraft(p.drafts, "project.create")`, `blank()`), step 1 lead select (around 340–383, with the `ActionLink` to `/app/settings/profiles/new` when `profiles.length === 0`), the "What creation does" explainer (around 399–416) and the recorded block (`recorded?.type === "project.create"` → `DraftMessage success="Created … It's paused."` with "Open project configuration" and "Create another project", around 833–874).
- **Existing:** `web/src/profile-config.tsx` — `ProfileCreate` builds the `profile.create` command inline (around 175–192), using private `emptyProfile`, `RuntimeFields`, `claudeSettings` and `PolicyAside`. Runtime helpers live in `web/src/execution-runtime.ts` (`runtimeValues`, `runtimeCommand`, `runtimeErrors`, `unavailableAlert`).
- **Existing:** `web/src/settings-state.ts` — `ConfigurationDraft` (`dirty`, `phase`, `submit`, `reconcile`, `reject`, `startOperation`, `adoptVersion`, `details.version`), plus `matchesConfigurationReceipt`. `web/src/settings.tsx` holds `useDraft`, `DraftMessage` (`check`, `review`, `success`), `DraftOutcome`, `submitDraft` and `SettingsProps`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/readiness.tsx` / `src/operator/readiness.ts` — `readinessSchema` (seven ordered checks, `status` pass/fail/not-configured, `reason`, `fix`), read at `/api/operator/readiness`. `web/src/add-claude.tsx` `AddClaudePanel` is rendered on `/app/settings/runtime` (`web/src/recovery.tsx` around 70).
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `workspaceSchema` (`profiles[].runtime`, `runtime`, `harnesses[]`), `composerOptionsSchema.capacity`, `projectConfigurationSchema.project.{paused,version}`, `project.configure` (`expectedVersion`, `paused`) and `profile.create` (`capabilities: text`).
- **Existing:** `web/src/app.tsx` — the route renders `<ProjectSetup … />` at around 868. `navigate(next)` is at around 560, and the composer reads `?project=` (around 907–915).
- **Existing:** `web/src/setup-model.ts` (pure setup helpers) with `test/operator-setup-model.test.ts`. `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts` uses `setupJourney` (options `profiles`, `projects`, `discovery`, `engine`, `viewport`), `commandRequest`, `savedOutcome` and `outcomeMessages`.
- **New:** `profileCreateCommand` (profile-config.tsx), `readyCheckItems` (setup-model.ts), a `ReadyCheck` component (project-setup.tsx or a sibling `web/src/ready-check.tsx`), and the `navigate` prop on `ProjectSetup`.
- **Follow:** `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts` "Setup checks an unknown create outcome by replaying the exact request" (`page.route("**/api/operator/commands", r => r.abort())`) for unknown Resume. `web/src/readiness.tsx` for showing reasons and fix lines.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:**
- The graph is acyclic: T1 → T2 → T3.
- T1 and T2 share `web/src/project-setup.tsx` and `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`, so they run in order and cannot run at the same time.
- T3 edits `design/design.pen` and `design/DESIGN.md`. #947 T9 edits the same two files. T3 must start from whichever of #947 and #949 merges first, and must not run at the same time as #947's design edits (see Re-plan triggers).
- No task is safe to run concurrently with another.

Shared setup for every **Validate** below: from the implementation checkout root with `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH` (Node 24 per `.node-version`), after `npm ci`, run `npm run build` first.

#### 1. Inline lead profile and leave prompt

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/profile-config.tsx` (export `emptyProfile`, `RuntimeFields`, `claudeSettings`; new `profileCreateCommand`; `ProfileCreate` uses it); `web/src/project-setup.tsx` (step 1 inline form, `beforeunload` effect); `web/src/setup.css` only if layout needs it; tests `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-profile-config-browser.test.ts` (regression only).
**Test:** In `operator-setup-browser.test.ts`, use `setupJourney(journey, { profiles: false })`:
- Fill Project name, Instructions and a typed repository row first. Step 1 shows Profile name, Summary, Instructions and a runtime select whose value is `codex`, and no lead select.
- Press Enter in Profile name with the name empty. No `project.create` POST is sent, and the profile name field is marked invalid.
- Fill the name and click **Create profile**. Exactly one POST has `type: "profile.create"`, `runtime: {harness:"codex"}` and `capabilities: ""`.
- "Profile created. Other setup values kept." shows. The lead select's value equals the new `profileId`. Project name, Instructions and the repository row are unchanged.
- Create the project. The `project.create` body has `leadProfileId` equal to the new profile.
- Failure: fill a 513-character profile name and click Create profile. One error outcome shows "…Your changes are still here.", the inline name keeps its value, and the setup values are unchanged.
- Leave prompt: on a fresh page, `page.evaluate` dispatching `new Event("beforeunload", {cancelable:true})` returns `defaultPrevented === false`. After filling Project name it returns `true`. After a recorded create it returns `false`.
- Update the existing first-run test (line 254), which asserts the "Create a lead profile" link: it now asserts the inline form.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions (inline profile, no nested form, selecting the new profile, leave prompt).
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-profile-config-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-state.test.js`; expect every test to pass.
**Complete when:** the inline profile path and the leave prompt pass their browser checks, and ProfileCreate still passes its tests.

#### 2. Ready check with Resume and Keep paused

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the working branch (shared files).
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/setup-model.ts` (`readyCheckItems`); `web/src/project-setup.tsx` (ready check replaces the recorded block; recorded-draft reset on mount; explainer line; `navigate` prop); `web/src/app.tsx` (pass `navigate` to `ProjectSetup` only); `web/src/setup.css` if needed; `docs/user-flows/project-setup.md` (Status: implemented); `docs/acceptance.md` project-setup coverage line (add the ready-check journeys); tests `test/operator-setup-model.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- Unit tests for `readyCheckItems` in `operator-setup-model.test.ts`:
  - Codex lead with all checks passing and capacity free: no items, not blocked.
  - Lead null: one blocking lead item.
  - Codex lead with `codex-login` failing: a blocking item carrying that check's fix line.
  - Claude lead with `claude-token` not configured: a blocking item linking to `/app/settings/runtime`.
  - Lead harness `not-configured`: a blocking item.
  - `workspace.runtime` unavailable: a blocking item.
  - Readiness loading: `checking`, blocked.
  - Readiness unavailable: blocked.
  - Capacity full: `capacityFull`, not blocked.
  - No item text matches the plain-wording regex from `operator-settings-state.test.ts`, and none contains a profile name.
- Browser tests in `operator-setup-browser.test.ts`. Each ready-check test uses `page.route("**/api/operator/readiness", …)` to fulfil a `readinessSchema`-valid payload, so the result does not depend on the host's Codex.
  - (a) **Resume:** Codex lead, all checks pass. After create, the ready check lists instructions, repository access and the linked Project, and says Paused. "Resume and create first task" is enabled. Clicking it sends one POST `{type:"project.configure", paused:false, expectedVersion:1}`. The URL becomes `/app/tasks/new?project=<id>` and the composer's project select has that value. `domain.project(id).paused === 0` and `f.runtime.turns === 0`.
  - (b) **Blocked:** a Claude lead created through the fixture domain, with readiness `claude-token` not configured. The primary is disabled, the reason sits beneath it, and the **Add Claude** link has href `/app/settings/runtime`. No `project.configure` POST is sent.
  - (c) **Keep paused:** the href is `/app/projects/<id>/settings`. Clicking it shows project configuration with Paused. No command POST is sent and the project stays paused.
  - (d) **Capacity full:** wrap `**/composer-options` to return usage equal to the limit. The capacity line shows and the primary stays enabled.
  - (e) **Unknown Resume:** abort the first `project.configure` POST. One warning shows with its check action and no enabled Resume button. Unroute and click the check. The replayed POST has the same `key`, and the page navigates to the composer.
  - Update the first test (lines 145–180), which used "Open project configuration" and "Create another project". The second project is created by navigating to `/app/settings/projects/new`, which now starts a clean form.
  - Keep the WebKit and phone setup smokes passing with the ready check visible.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions (wait items, capacity, Resume, new visit, explainer). The ready check renders below the form where the recorded block is now, and moves focus to its heading or message the way `DraftMessage` does after a send.
**Validate:** run `node --test dist/test/operator-setup-model.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-state.test.js dist/test/operator-task-composer.test.js`; expect every test to pass.
**Complete when:** the four browser journeys (Resume, blocked, Keep paused, unknown) and the capacity journey pass, and the docs say the flow is implemented.

#### 3. Pen frames 145–147 and DESIGN.md

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:**
- T1 and T2 merged into the working branch.
- If #947 has merged, this branch has been updated to that `main` first.
- The Pen app is running and reachable by the Pen MCP (`mcp__pencil__get_app_state` succeeds), and computer use is available to save.
**Files and symbols:** `design/design.pen` (frames 145 `HGgoK`, 145b `ju0c4`, 146 `UdnEc`, 146b `PFBIv`, 147 `akpq9`), `design/DESIGN.md` (frame table row at around 406 and notes at around 532–539).
**Implementation:**
- Through the Pen MCP only, read the five frames and compare them with the shipped UI:
  - inline form fields and the "Profile created. Other setup values kept." line;
  - the ready-check saved list and Paused statement;
  - blocking items with the reason beneath the disabled primary, and **Add Claude** as the Claude token fix;
  - the non-blocking capacity line;
  - Keep paused as the only secondary action;
  - the lead-unconfigured item.
- Edit any drift through the MCP.
- Save by opening `design/design.pen` in the Pen app and saving with computer use (the MCP cannot save). Confirm `git status` shows the file changed, or record that no frame needed a change.
- Refresh the `design/DESIGN.md` notes through the MCP to match: capacity line, Add Claude fix and lead item.
- If the Pen app or computer use is unavailable, stop this slice and report it as a blocker. Never edit `design.pen` any other way. T1–T2 may still go to review with the design gap stated.
**Validate:**
- Re-read each frame through the MCP and expect it to match the shipped copy.
- Run `git diff --stat -- design/` and expect `design/DESIGN.md` to have changed (and `design/design.pen` when frames changed).
- Run `npm run format:check` and expect it to pass.
**Complete when:** the frames are verified or updated and saved, and DESIGN.md matches the shipped UI.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| With no profiles, inline profile form (Codex preselected); creating selects it and keeps every other setup value | 1 | T1 no-profile journey |
| Browser warns before leaving setup with changed fields | 1 | T1 beforeunload checks (fresh, dirty, recorded) |
| Ready check replaces the alert, lists what was saved and wait items (Claude token → Add Claude), Resume primary, Keep paused secondary; capacity never disables and says the task will wait | 2 | T2 unit tests; browser (a), (b), (c), (d) |
| Resume uses the existing project command; unknown outcome blocks a second Resume until re-read | 2 | T2 browser (a), (e) |
| Projects still start Paused; nothing runs until Resume | 1, 2 | T2 (a) and (c) paused before Resume, `turns === 0`; existing create tests |
| Pen frames 145–147 drawn; `design/DESIGN.md` refreshed | 3 | T3 MCP re-read and diff |
| Browser tests for the no-profile path, a blocked ready check, Resume and Keep paused | 1, 2 | T1 journey; T2 (a)–(c) |

### Final validation

content.title: Getting-started checklist and Fix actions on waits

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/950
**Planned against:** `origin/main` (detached) at `e8e6da699cd41ffc513d1e01f6eec38632ef1582`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Contract: the #950 acceptance criteria (cited AC1–AC9 in order) and the flows they name, `docs/user-flows/getting-started.md` and `docs/user-flows/first-task.md`, under epic #945's unchanged guarantees. Blockers #948 and #949 are closed and their outcomes are in the base (`src/standalone/readiness.ts`, `web/src/readiness.tsx`, `web/src/add-claude.tsx`, `web/src/ready-check.tsx`, `web/src/setup-model.ts` `readyCheckItems`).

### Approach

One PR, seven slices. The service derives one ordered list of wait reasons per task (T1) from current state, using a pure ordering module in `src/operator/` that the server, the web app and the CLI share. The task read and composer-options read carry that list. Task detail, the post-create composer, Inbox detail (T3) and the CLI (T2) render it, and the composer predicts start or wait before submission from the same module (T4). The Home checklist (T5) is a pure web model over reads that already exist, plus two installation facts on the workspace read: whether any task has started a turn, and whether getting started was dismissed. Dismissal is a new installation-scoped command, following `claude-token.configure`. T6 brings the Pen frames and docs in line with the build. T7 records the bounded live first-run journey.

### Guardrails

- Unchanged: admission, readiness, capacity and hold rules. Wait reasons are a read-side projection only, and `domain.admission()` keeps its reasons and order. Projects are still created paused, and Resume is explicit. Repository access is exactly what the operator adds.
- Fix actions (AC6) perform exactly the named action. Resume project sends one `project.configure {paused:false}` after a confirmation, and nothing else. Every other Fix is navigation (project configuration, Settings → Readiness, Settings → Add Claude, the profile). A Fix never clears a task, source, dependency, approval, Stop, writer or capacity hold, and never changes a lead, credential or repository.
- Out of scope: the paused X01–X08 work (#734), changes to `readyCheckItems` and the ready check (#949), task-list and board reason chips (`web/src/tasks.ts` `taskReasons`), new readiness checks, and any edit to `web/src/local-review.tsx`, `web/src/settings.tsx` or `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts` (owned by #974).
- **Plan-mismatch budget** (one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles) applies only when an approved-plan seam or repository assumption proves wrong. These are: (a) the operator API can derive the lead's runtime, Claude token and profile-runtime waits synchronously from `service.harnessStatuses()`, `service.claudeTokenStatus()`, `service.harnessSettings()` and `unsupportedRuntimeField`, without the async readiness probe; (b) "a task has started a turn" is exactly a task-bound `execution_intents` row with `turnId IS NOT NULL`, and intents are never deleted; (c) a singleton table plus a `getting-started.configure` command, following `claude-token.configure`, fits the domain command and receipt pipeline; (d) adding `waits` to `taskSchema` and `composerOptionsSchema` breaks no consumer beyond those this plan names. **Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget.** That covers selector or wait fixes, type and lint errors, formatting, fixture setup, stale expectations in neighbouring tests, mechanical test-path moves from #973, rebases over #974, and CI reruns. Routine corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority are recorded briefly in the existing delivery record, with affected evidence renewed. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for a material design or contract change or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Server-side ordered waits (AC3–AC5).** The CLI is a separate HTTP client, and Inbox detail and task detail both read `/api/operator/tasks/:id`. Putting the ordered list in that read is the only way all three show the same reasons in the same order without each re-deriving them. The new module `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` (pure, no DOM, no Node APIs) owns these:
  - `waitCodes`, in the fixed flow order: `project-paused`, `project-lead-unconfigured`, `project-lead-revoked`, `runtime-unavailable`, `claude-token-unavailable`, `profile-runtime-not-configured`, `local-dependency`, `imported-blockers-blocked`, `imported-blockers-unknown`, `source-held`, `approval`, `admission-blocked`, `capacity`. Dependency, approval and source holds keep one "hold" group in the flow's position; `admission-blocked` covers any other unmapped admission reason (for example `task-not-open`), so nothing is silently dropped.
  - `orderWaits(input)`: builds the list from admission reasons, the lead-runtime facts, open approval interaction ids, blocking local dependencies, open native blockers, the source URL and capacity usage. `task-unready` is a Draft, not a wait, so it is excluded, as `taskStatusLine` already does.
  - The `Wait` shape: `{ code, fix: {kind:"resume-project"|"choose-lead"|"readiness"|"add-claude"|"open-profile", projectId?|profileId?} | null, links: {kind:"task"|"request"|"source"|"tasks-running", id?|url?, label}[] }`. Labels are fixed strings. A link label may carry a task title or `owner/repo#n` passed through the existing `safe()` exclusion.
  - `waitLabels` and `cliFix(wait)`, which return the CLI command or Settings path: `ensemble project prepare <id> --out project.json --paused false` then `ensemble project apply --file project.json`; `ensemble project prepare <id> --out project.json --lead-profile <ID>` for lead waits; `ensemble doctor`; "Settings → Add Claude"; "Settings → Profiles → <profile>".

  The task read and composer-options read validate `waits` with a strict zod schema in `src/operator/contracts.ts`.
- **Lead-runtime waits mirror the ready check's rules (#949), server-side.** The lead is the bound lead profile if one exists, otherwise the project lead (as `taskLead` does). With the lead's harness `h`:
  - `runtime-unavailable` when `harnessStatuses()` shows `h` unavailable, or `h` is codex and `runtimeStatus()` is unavailable.
  - Otherwise `profile-runtime-not-configured` when `h` is not configured for the service, or `harnessSettings(h)` is known and `unsupportedRuntimeField(profile.runtime, settings)` is set. Its Fix is "open-profile".
  - Separately, `claude-token-unavailable` when `h` is claude and `claudeTokenStatus().state !== "available"`.

  The async Codex-login probe stays in readiness and the Home Runtime row. It is not evaluated on every task read.
- **Capacity (AC3).** Capacity is listed (`capacity`) when the task is otherwise eligible, open and ready, and project or global usage is at its limit, or the task's execution state is `waiting` because of capacity. It has no Fix. Its link opens `/app/tasks?state=Running`, labelled with usage (`2 of 2 project turns running`), which shows what is using capacity.
- **Composer prediction (AC2).** `composer-options` gains the project-level `waits` (paused, lead, runtime, token, profile, capacity). `TaskComposer` merges in `local-dependency` for selected dependencies that are not done, calling the same `orderWaits`. It states "Starts now." or "It will wait: <first reason label>." above Create and start, with the rest listed. Save draft is unaffected.
- **Checklist row states (AC1).** Rows are derived in a pure model, `web/src/getting-started-model.ts` `checklistRows`, from the readiness read, `/api/operator/discovery`, the workspace read and `workspace.gettingStarted`. No wizard progress is stored.
  - **Runtime:** Done when the `codex-executable` and `codex-login` checks pass.
  - **GitHub:** Done when the discovery credential is configured and available. Its action is **Use GitHub CLI login (@login)** when `gh` is signed in and nothing is configured (the same `discovery.configure {credentialRef:"gh:github.com"}` as `project-setup.tsx`), otherwise Set discovery credential. It reads "Optional for repository-free projects" and never blocks or takes the primary.
  - **Lead profile:** Done when any non-revoked profile exists.
  - **Project:** Done only when a project exists and is not paused. When only paused projects exist, the action is **Resume** for the first paused project, with confirmation, sending `project.configure {paused:false}`. This is the 143b correction from #945.
  - **First task:** Done when `gettingStarted.turnStarted`.
  - **Claude (optional):** Optional when not configured, Done when the `claude-token` check passes, otherwise Needs attention with Add Claude.
  - **Status rule:** an incomplete required row (Runtime, Lead profile, Project, First task) is Needs attention when a later required row is Done or a turn has started (a regression), otherwise Next for the first one and Not started for the rest. Only the first incomplete required row gets the primary button, matching the badges in DESIGN.md "Getting started".
- **Home and account-menu visibility (AC1).** Home (`/app`) shows the full checklist in place of the "Create a project in existing operator controls to begin." line while `!turnStarted`. After a turn has started, Home shows only rows in Needs attention, dismissed or not, because the flow says a regressed row returns "even after dismissal". The account menu shows **Getting started**, opening the new route `/app/getting-started` (the same checklist with a secondary Dismiss), until it is dismissed. After that it shows **Show getting started**, which undoes the dismissal. Both send `getting-started.configure {dismissed}`.
- **Dismissal is per installation.** It uses a domain singleton table `installation_getting_started (singleton, dismissed)` and the command `getting-started.configure`, with receipt scope `system:getting-started` and result `{commandType, resourceId:"system:getting-started", dismissed}`. This mirrors `claude-token.configure` (domain schema, `scopeOf`, `execute` case, table create plus seed row, contracts command and result schemas, operator-api branch, the `settings-state.ts` receipt matcher). It is operator-only (`this.operator(command)`). Browser storage was rejected because the flow says per installation.
- **turnStarted** comes from `StandaloneService` (or `ExecutionState`): `SELECT 1 FROM execution_intents i JOIN task_execution_bindings b ON b.workId = i.workId WHERE i.turnId IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1`. `turnId` is set only by the `submitting → running` transition (`state.ts` ~L4584), and no code deletes `execution_intents`.
- **Design.** Frames 143–150 exist (`design/DESIGN.md` L405–407; drawn in #951). AC7 is met by reconciling them with the build: correct 143b (a paused project shown as Done must show Resume), align 148–150 with the order and Fix labels above, add or annotate the account-menu Getting started, Dismiss and undo states, and fold the "Drawn ahead of the build" note (39, 161, 166c) into as-built. If an approved frame's visual choice conflicts with a decision here that the flow docs do not settle (for example the GitHub row's badge), the frame wins and the delivery record notes it. A conflict with the flow docs follows the flow docs, and the frame is corrected.
- **Baseline.** CI run 38529948245 on exactly `e8e6da69` passed `check` (Node 24) and `check-node-26`, so the full suite is not re-run locally. Focused seam checks on this base after `npm run build` with Node 24.21.0: `UI03 critical journeys … 1366` in `dist/test/operator-task-browser.test.js` (asserts the empty-Home copy this ticket replaces) passed, and `task create derives ids …` in `dist/test/operator-cli-task.test.js` passed. The Pen app was not running during planning, so frames were not opened. T6 reads them first.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` `admission()` (L1446) produces the admission reason codes. `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` `admission()` (L2077) maps them to `admissionSchema`. The task read (≈L2740–2830) builds `task`, `lead`, `assignments` (each with `waitReason`), `admission`, `execution`, `localDependencies` and `source`. `taskLead()` (L2093) resolves the bound or project lead. Composer options and capacity come from the helper ending ≈L2070. `readWorkspace()` (L1820) carries `projects`, `profiles` (with `runtime`), `runtime` and `harnesses`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` `claudeTokenStatus()` (L1817), `runtimeStatus()`, `harnessStatuses()` (L1847) and `harnessSettings()`. `src/core/execution-runtime.ts` `unsupportedRuntimeField`.
- **Existing (web):** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` "Pending requests and holds" section (≈L1230–1250) renders `reasonLabels[r]` per admission reason. `web/src/task-overview.ts` `taskStatusLine` (L84). `web/src/task-composer.tsx` loads composer options (L72) and shows post-create admission reasons (L211). `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` `holdNotices` and `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx` (L68, L101). `web/src/task-views.tsx` empty Home (L401–410). `web/src/account-menu.tsx` `link()` (L99). `web/src/app.tsx` route list (L304–312). `web/src/tasks.ts` `reasonLabels`.
- **Existing (CLI):** `src/cli/main.ts` `task get` (L398) human output; `src/cli/task-write.ts` `taskStatusLines` (L70), also used by `task-control.ts`.
- **New:** `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` (above). `web/src/wait-reasons.tsx` `WaitReasons({waits, client, session, drafts, onChanged})` renders the primary reason with its Fix and lists the rest, each with its own Fix or link. `ResumeProjectFix` holds the confirmation and one `project.configure` via `useDraft`/`DraftMessage`, reading the project version from `/api/operator/projects/:id/configuration` as `ready-check.tsx`'s `review` does. `web/src/getting-started-model.ts` `checklistRows`, `web/src/getting-started.tsx` `GettingStarted({mode:"home"|"page"})`.
- **Follow:** `web/src/ready-check.tsx` and `web/src/setup-model.ts` `readyCheckItems` for runtime and token wording and the Add Claude and Edit profile links. `web/src/project-setup.tsx` (≈L592–613) for Use GitHub CLI login. `claude-token.configure` across `src/core/domain.ts` (L297, L349, L2357, table L480/L603), `src/operator/contracts.ts` (L1827, L2017), `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (L5796) and `web/src/settings-state.ts` (L56) for the installation command. `web/src/action-feedback.tsx` for outcome copy (#947 rules: no command names or codes in messages).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** acyclic. T1 → {T2, T3}; T3 → T4; T1 → T5; {T3, T4, T5} → T6; {T2, T4, T5, T6} → T7. T2 touches only `src/cli/*` and its test, so it may run concurrently with T3 in a separate worktree. T3, T4 and T5 all edit `src/operator/contracts.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` or `web/src/task-composer.tsx`, so they run in sequence. Do not build concurrently in one checkout (shared `dist/`).

**#974 overlap:** #974 is in flight. It edits `web/src/settings.tsx` (`sendDraft` focus via a new `ConfigurationDraft.revision`/`afterRender`), `web/src/settings-state.ts` (`ConfigurationDraft`, ≈L79+), `web/src/local-review.tsx` and tests including `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts` and `test/operator-settings-state.test.ts`. This plan edits none of those except one receipt-matcher case in `settings-state.ts` (≈L51–60, a different region) in T5. It consumes `useDraft`, `DraftMessage` and `sendDraft` unchanged. **Recommended order:** land #974 first, then rebase #950. The Resume and Dismiss focus behaviour then inherits the commit-aware focus fix. The rebase is mechanical, and either order merges.

**#973 overlap:** open PR #973 moves test files into subdirectories (for example `test/operator-cli-task.test.ts` → `test/coordination/…`). Edit whichever path exists at your base and use the matching `dist/test/…` path in commands. That is a mechanical correction, not a replan.

Validation setup used below as **(S)**: from the checkout root, with `/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin` (Node 24.21.0) or the `.node-version` toolchain first on `PATH`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build`.

#### 1. Ordered wait reasons in the task and composer-options reads

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** new `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts`; `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`waitSchema`, `waits` on `taskSchema` data and `composerOptionsSchema` data); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (a private `waits(taskId)` and project-level `projectWaits(projectId)`, wired into the task read and composer options); new `test/operator-wait-reasons.test.ts`; `test/operator-api.test.ts`.
**Test:** `operator-wait-reasons.test.ts` (pure): for each code, one input producing exactly that wait with the expected `fix` kind or links. One input with every reason present returns them in `waitCodes` order. `task-unready` alone yields `[]`. An unknown admission reason yields `admission-blocked`. In `operator-api.test.ts` (real SQLite, fake host), task reads assert `waits` codes, in order, for: a paused project with no lead (`["project-paused","project-lead-unconfigured"]`), a revoked lead, a Claude lead with the Claude harness not configured (`profile-runtime-not-configured`, fix `open-profile` with the profile id) and with no token reference (`claude-token-unavailable`), an incomplete local dependency (link `task` with the blocker id), and capacity full (project limit 1 with one running reservation). A paused-project composer-options read returns `project-paused` first.
**Implementation:** Build `orderWaits` and the schema as decided above. In the operator API, gather the inputs (admission reasons, lead and harness facts, open approval interaction ids already read for the task, `localDependencies`, `source.nativeBlockers` and URL, capacity from the existing helper) and pass label text through `safe()`. Keep `admission` unchanged for existing consumers.
**Validate:** (S), then `node --test dist/test/operator-wait-reasons.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js`; expect all pass. `npm run typecheck` passes.
**Complete when:** both reads return validated, ordered `waits`, and the tests above pass.

#### 2. CLI task reads print the same waits with the command or Settings path

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1.
**Files and symbols:** `src/cli/main.ts` (`task get` human output); `src/cli/task-write.ts` `taskStatusLines`; `test/operator-cli-task.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `operator-cli-task.test.ts`, `task get` on a paused project with no lead and an incomplete dependency prints `Waiting:` lines in the order paused, no lead, dependency. The first line is followed by `Fix: ensemble project prepare <id> --out project.json --paused false` and the apply step, then the lead `Fix:` line, and the dependency line names the blocking task id with no `Fix:`. `--json` output contains the same `waits` array as the HTTP read. The existing `Admission` line in `taskStatusLines` is replaced by a `Waiting` entry that lists labels in order, or reads `none`; update its existing assertions.
**Implementation:** Render with `waitLabels` and `cliFix` from `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts`. No new command is added.
**Validate:** (S), then `node --test dist/test/operator-cli-task.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-task-control.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** CLI reads list the waits in order, with the command or Settings path for each Fix.

#### 3. Task detail, post-create composer and Inbox detail show waits with Fix actions

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1.
**Files and symbols:** new `web/src/wait-reasons.tsx` (`WaitReasons`, `ResumeProjectFix`); `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` (replace the admission-reason paragraphs in "Pending requests and holds"); `web/src/task-overview.ts` `taskStatusLine` (use `waits[0]` for the "Ready · …" reason); `web/src/task-composer.tsx` (post-create: "Task created. It will wait: <reason>." with the primary Fix beside it, per frames 39, 161 and 166c); `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` `holdNotices` (derive notices from `task.waits` in order and keep the "Approval/Answering does not clear it" details); `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx`; CSS in the existing stylesheet of each component; tests `test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts`, `test/operator-task-overview.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- Browser, task detail: a task in a paused project with no lead shows "Project paused" first with **Resume project**, and "Project has no lead" listed with "Choose a lead" linking `/app/projects/<id>/settings`. Click Resume project: a confirmation states the consequence, and Cancel sends nothing. Confirm, then intercept `**/api/operator/commands` and assert exactly one body, `{type:"project.configure", paused:false, expectedVersion}`. After the success line, "Project paused" is gone and the lead wait is now primary. A second task with an incomplete local dependency shows that wait with a link to `/app/tasks/<blocker>` and no Fix button. The dependency remains after Resume (AC6). A Claude-lead task with no token shows **Add Claude** linking `/app/settings/runtime`.
- Unit: `holdNotices` returns notices in `waits` order for a task with source hold, dependency and paused (paused first). `taskStatusLine` uses the first wait.
- Run the browser tests at 1366×900 and 390×844, as existing detail tests do.
**Implementation:** As decided. Readiness Fix links to `/app/settings` (the Readiness panel), Add Claude to `/app/settings/runtime`, open-profile to `/app/profiles/<id>/settings`, choose-lead to `/app/projects/<id>/settings`, an approval to `/app/tasks/<task>?request=<id>`, and source to the source URL. Messages follow #947 copy rules.
**Validate:** (S), then `node --test dist/test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-inbox-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator-inbox-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-task-overview.test.js`; expect all pass. Sensitivity: making `ResumeProjectFix` also send `task.resume` must fail the one-command assertion.
**Complete when:** task detail, the post-create line and Inbox detail render the server order with working Fix actions, and the tests pass.

#### 4. Composer predicts start or wait before submission

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 (shares `web/src/task-composer.tsx`).
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/task-composer.tsx`, `web/src/composer-state.ts` and/or `web/src/composer-summary.ts` (prediction line near Create and start); `test/operator-task-composer.test.ts` (or `test/operator-composer-layout-browser.test.ts` for the rendered check).
**Test:** Composer for an enabled project with a lead and spare capacity shows "Starts now." Pausing the project (fixture) and reloading shows "It will wait: Project paused." Selecting a not-done dependency on an enabled project shows "It will wait: Waiting on a task dependency." and removing it restores "Starts now." Save draft shows no prediction-driven change.
**Implementation:** `orderWaits` merges `composerOptions.waits` with the selected dependencies. The line uses the first label; the others are listed beneath. It replaces the generic "subject to project state…" sentence where the composer has the facts (`docs/SPEC.md` L518–520 already allows this).
**Validate:** (S), then `node --test dist/test/operator-task-composer.test.js dist/test/operator-composer-layout-browser.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** the composer states start or wait before submission, from the same order.

#### 5. Getting-started checklist on Home and in the account menu, with undoable dismissal

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 (shared contracts and operator-api files; T5 runs after T4 in the same branch).
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/domain.ts` (`getting-started.configure` command schema, `scopeOf`, `execute` case, `installation_getting_started` table and seed, a `gettingStartedDismissed()` read); `src/operator/contracts.ts` (command, result, and `workspaceSchema` `gettingStarted: {turnStarted, dismissed}`); `src/standalone/service.ts` or `state.ts` (`turnStarted()`); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`readWorkspace`, command branch); `web/src/settings-state.ts` (receipt matcher case); new `web/src/getting-started-model.ts` and `web/src/getting-started.tsx`; `web/src/task-views.tsx` (Home); `web/src/account-menu.tsx`; `web/src/app.tsx` (`/app/getting-started` route and title); tests: new `test/operator-getting-started-model.test.ts`, `test/domain.test.ts` (command), `test/operator-api.test.ts` (workspace facts), `test/operator-task-browser.test.ts` (replace the empty-Home assertion at ≈L1063), `test/operator-account-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- Model, one case per row and state: Runtime Done/Next/Needs attention (codex-login fail after Lead profile Done). GitHub Done; signed-in `gh` offers "Use GitHub CLI login (@fixture-user)"; GitHub is never primary. Lead profile Done/Next. Project with only a paused project is not Done, and its action is Resume (the 143b case). First task Done on `turnStarted`. Claude Optional/Done/Needs attention. Only one row is primary. After `turnStarted`, the Home-mode rows are only the Needs-attention ones.
- Domain: `getting-started.configure {dismissed:true}` then `{dismissed:false}` toggles the read. An exact replay returns the recorded receipt. An agent actor is refused.
- API: the workspace read has `turnStarted:false` on a fresh store and `true` after a fixture task-bound intent records a `turnId`.
- Browser: a fresh install's Home shows "Get Ensemble running" with Runtime Done (fake host) and Lead profile primary, and the old copy is gone. Account menu → Getting started opens `/app/getting-started`. Dismiss hides the menu entry and shows "Show getting started". Clicking that restores the entry. After a fixture turn starts, Home has no checklist. Removing the Claude token reference after configuring one makes Claude reappear on Home as Needs attention.
**Implementation:** As decided. Row actions link to the flows: Lead profile → `/app/settings/projects/new` (inline profile, #949), Project → setup or the Resume confirmation (reuse `ResumeProjectFix` from T3), First task → `/app/tasks/new?project=<first enabled>`, Runtime → `/app/settings` Readiness, Claude → `/app/settings/runtime`.
**Validate:** (S), then `node --test dist/test/operator-getting-started-model.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-task-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-account-browser.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Home and the account menu show the derived checklist, dismissal round-trips, and the tests pass.

#### 6. Pen frames and docs reflect the build

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T3`, `T4`, `T5`
**Prerequisites:** T3–T5 behaviour final.
**Files and symbols:** `design/design.pen`, through the Pen MCP only (`mcp__pencil__*`; the Pen app must be running): frames 143 `AnubR`, 143b `Ttbda`, 144 `stx1O`, 148 `q9Ogr`, 149 `Ky9f4`, 149b `CLbNV`, 149c `itg8q`, 150 `A0xMwZ`, and where needed 39 `Z6U3T4`, 161 `thtaf`, 166c `N7QIqz`. Also `design/DESIGN.md` ("First run and onboarding" L528–577 and "Drawn ahead of the build" L627–630), `docs/user-flows/getting-started.md` and `first-task.md` (Status lines → implemented, plus any as-built detail such as the `/app/getting-started` route and the Home-after-first-turn rule), `docs/SPEC.md` L518–530 (prediction and Fix wording in place).
**Implementation:** Open each frame with the MCP and compare it with the build (screenshots from the T3–T5 browser tests). Correct 143b's Project row (paused → Resume, not Done). Make the reason order and Fix labels in 148–150 match T1/T3. Add or annotate the account-menu Getting started, Dismiss and Show getting started states. Fold the drawn-ahead note into the as-built text. Then refresh `design/DESIGN.md` through the MCP. **Save:** the MCP cannot save. When MCP edits are done, ask Chris to save `design/design.pen` in the Pen app, then confirm the file changed on disk (`git status design/design.pen`) before committing. Never use computer use to save. If the Pen app is not running, ask Chris to open it, and continue other slices meanwhile.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, `git diff --stat design/ docs/` shows `design/design.pen` and `design/DESIGN.md` changed. An MCP re-read of 143b shows the Project row with Resume. `npm run format:check` passes.
**Complete when:** the frames and DESIGN.md match the build, the user has saved, and the flow docs describe the implemented state.

#### 7. Bounded live first-run journey evidence

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `T2`, `T4`, `T5`, `T6`
**Prerequisites:** the integrated candidate passes `npm run check` (Final validation).
**Files and symbols:** new `docs/evidence/first-run-journey.md` (dated record), following the evidence boundary style of `docs/evidence/ui07-integrated-operator.md` and `ui07-project-setup.md`.
**Implementation:** On a fresh temporary data directory with the real Codex App Server runtime and the production web bundle, the implementation agent runs one attempt:
1. Sign in.
2. Home checklist: record the row states.
3. Project setup, repository-free, with an inline lead profile.
4. Ready check → Resume and create first task.
5. The composer says "Starts now."
6. Create and start; the task reaches `running` (a turn id is recorded).
7. Home drops the checklist.

Bound it to one turn with a trivial outcome. Stop the task after the turn starts if it is still running, and remove the data directory. Record the commit, Node and npm versions, timings, row states and booleans only, with no prompts, tokens, paths or account identities. Note what it does not qualify (Claude, GitHub repositories, physical devices). On failure, record it and stop; do not retry beyond one more attempt after an ordinary fixable cause.
**Validate:** The record exists, names the exact commit, and shows each step passed. `npm run format:check` passes.
**Complete when:** the dated evidence is committed.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| AC1 Home checklist replaces the old line; rows derived each read; regress; leave Home after first turn; undoable dismissal | 5 | Model row tests; domain toggle; browser Home, account menu and regression journey |
| AC2 Composer states start or wait before submission | 4 | Composer prediction tests |
| AC3 Wait reasons with single-command Fix; holds link without Fix | 1, 3 | API wait tests; task-detail browser Fix, link and confirmation tests |
| AC4 Fixed order; first primary, rest listed | 1, 3 | Order unit test; browser primary-then-list assertion |
| AC5 Inbox and CLI show the same reasons and order; CLI prints command or path | 2, 3 | CLI `task get` test; `holdNotices` order test |
| AC6 Fix never clears holds or grants access | 3 | One-command intercept; dependency remains after Resume; sensitivity check |
| AC7 Frames 143–144, 148–150 drawn; DESIGN.md refreshed | 6 | MCP re-read; DESIGN.md diff; user save confirmed |
| AC8 Automated coverage for each row and wait reason | 1, 5 | `operator-wait-reasons` per-code cases; `operator-getting-started-model` per-row cases |
| AC9 Bounded live first-run journey recorded | 7 | `docs/evidence/first-run-journey.md` |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root, with the `.node-version` toolchain, run `npm ci && npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate before T7 and before requesting review; expect typecheck, lint, format, build and the full suite to pass with 0 failures. CI runs the same check (Node 24 and 26) on the PR head.

### Review focus

- That `waits` can never imply a Fix for a hold (approval, source, dependency, capacity, Stop or writer holds carry links only), and that label text passes the exclusion `safe()`.
- The `getting-started.configure` receipt scope and replay match the installation-command precedent. A dismissed installation still shows regressed rows on Home.

content.title: Move repository verification out of core behind the existing injection point

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Move host repository verification out of the domain core through its existing injected verifier.

**Current behavior and evidence:** Inspection at e6bf9d21 finds checkoutOrigin and verifiedRepository in the core importing child_process and filesystem APIs. DomainStore already accepts an injected verifyRepository; standalone setup and service code also consume verification. #884 is closed and the hardened Git environment is present, but the architectural move remains outstanding. Redundancy checks covered core Git verification, domain injection, standalone setup/service callers and shared Git execution.

**Desired behavior:** The standalone layer owns filesystem/Git verification and supplies it through the existing injection boundary. The core retains portable contracts and cannot launch a subprocess through a default verifier. Preserve verification results and error identity, including setup's operator field feedback.

**Key interfaces:** DomainStore's verifyRepository injection, checkoutOrigin, verifiedRepository, RepositoryVerificationError, linked repository validation, and the shared hardened Git runner.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Production core code does not spawn processes or depend on standalone implementation modules.
- [ ] Standalone construction injects the host verifier; setup and service verification reuse the host implementation.
- [ ] Origin provider/mismatch checks, canonical paths, Git common-directory identity and ref validation preserve existing semantics.
- [ ] Verification error identity and operator field feedback remain intact.
- [ ] Shared Git environment hardening and bounded execution are preserved.
- [ ] Focused fixtures cover valid repositories and existing failure cases; core journeys use injected verification.

**Validation:** Triage evidence is source inspection, not runtime reproduction. Implementation runs pinned npm ci and npm run check plus relevant repository/setup regressions.

**Out of scope:** New repository providers, changes to accepted origin/ref rules, remote workers, permission widening or unrelated Git refactoring.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/914
**Planned against:** `main` at `f2b9ffb231f5be89a2d3bec40206be7d4f8cc5d9`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Requirements: the [agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/914#issuecomment-6130129498) acceptance criteria (AC1–AC6 below, in brief order).

### Approach

Move `checkoutOrigin` and `verifiedRepository` verbatim in behaviour into a new standalone module that runs Git through the shared hardened runner `runGit` (`src/standalone/git-process.ts`) and owns `realpath`. Core keeps only portable contracts (`RepositoryVerificationError`, `RepositoryVerificationReason`, `parseGitHubOrigin`, `linkedRepositorySchema`/`LinkedRepository`) plus a new `RepositoryVerifier` function type. `DomainStore`'s existing third constructor parameter becomes `RepositoryVerifier` with a fail-closed default that never spawns; `StandaloneService` injects the standalone verifier and its own `provisionTask` and `operator-setup.ts` import the standalone implementation. Delivered as one PR in two slices: an additive, independently testable standalone module (T1) and the wiring/removal slice (T2).

### Guardrails

- Preserve exactly: reason codes and their order (path-invalid → not-checkout → origin-mismatch/origin-provider/origin-missing → ref-unavailable), the `actual` value on `origin-mismatch`, case-insensitive owner/name comparison, origin consulted only when `expectedOrigin` is given, the `^{commit}` peel only with `expectedOrigin`, the 40–64 hex ref check, `realpath` of path and of `--git-common-dir`, `checkoutOrigin`'s `timeout` argument (default 5000 ms; folder listing passes 2000 ms), and `DomainStore`'s field mapping (`repositories.N.ref` for `ref-unavailable`, else `repositories.N.path`; `repositories` for `github.configure`).
- Every verification Git call goes through `runGit` (hardened `gitEnvironment()`, bounded time and output). Any non-`ok` `runGit` result maps to the same reason the corresponding `execFile` rejection produced. No file under `src/core` imports `node:child_process` or `node:fs*`, or imports from `src/standalone`.
- Out of scope: new providers, changed origin/ref rules, remote workers, permission widening, unrelated Git refactoring (e.g. `currentBranch`, workspace Git), and documentation rewrites (`docs/SPEC.md` "Git subprocess rule" already describes repository verification as hardened and bounded).
- Plan-mismatch budget vs ordinary repairs: only a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example: `DomainStore` gains another production construction site needing injection, `runGit` cannot express the existing bounds, or a caller depends on core verification in a way this plan does not list) uses the one focused diagnosis plus at most two repair cycles; record it in the delivery record and stop for replanning if exhausted or if fixing it changes the architecture above. Ordinary implementation, integration, type, lint, formatting, test, fixture, documentation and CI defects — including adding the standalone verifier to a direct `DomainStore(db)` test construction whose journey needs real verification — are repaired by the ticket owner in scope and do not consume that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Fail-closed default instead of a required parameter.** `DomainStore(db, onChange?, verifyRepository?)` keeps its optional third parameter; the default rejects with a plain `Error("Repository verification is not configured")` and spawns nothing. Making it required would touch ~40 `new DomainStore(db)` sites (many in files PR #956 edits) for journeys that never verify. The only production construction site is `src/standalone/service.ts` (`new DomainStore(db, () => …)` in service start-up), and the guided-setup journeys in `test/project-setup.test.ts` go through `StandaloneService`, so a missing injection fails those tests.
- **New module, not `operator-setup.ts`.** `src/standalone/repository-verification.ts` is consumed by both `operator-setup.ts` and `service.ts`; keeping it separate lets T1 land and be tested without touching any shared file.
- **`runGit` bounds** mirror the existing setup probe (`currentBranch` in `operator-setup.ts`): `timeoutMs` = existing timeout (5000, or `checkoutOrigin`'s argument), `terminationGraceMs: 100`, `observationMs: 500`, `maxOutputBytes: 1024 * 1024` (equal to `execFile`'s default `maxBuffer`). Decode stdout as UTF-8 and `trim()` as today.
- **Concurrency.** PR #956 (#886) edits `src/core/domain.ts`, `src/standalone/service.ts`, `test/github-source-config.test.ts`, `test/domain.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts`; #880 will edit `src/standalone/service.ts` after #886; #878/#879/#877 touch service/API seams. This ticket's shared edits are deliberately tiny: in `domain.ts` only the import lines, the constructor parameter type/default and nothing in `configureGitHub`/`createProject` bodies; in `service.ts` only the import block, the `new DomainStore(...)` call and the `verifiedRepository` call in `provisionTask`. Rebase onto whichever lands first; resolve these hunks mechanically (ordinary integration repair).

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source.ts` — `checkoutOrigin(path, timeout = 5000)` and `verifiedRepository(input, expectedOrigin?)` (≈lines 81–227) use `execFile`/`promisify`/`realpath` and `gitEnvironment` from `./child-environment.js`; these are the only `node:child_process`/`node:fs` imports in `src/core`. `RepositoryVerificationError`, `parseGitHubOrigin`, `linkedRepositorySchema` live in the same file and stay.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStore` constructor `verifyRepository: typeof verifiedRepository = verifiedRepository`; used by `configureGitHub` (no expected origin) and `createProject` (expected origin, per-row field mapping via `RepositoryVerificationError.reason`).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — imports `verifiedRepository` from core; constructs `new DomainStore(db, onChange)` without a verifier; `provisionTask` re-verifies imported-task repositories with `verifiedRepository` (no expected origin).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts` — `listHomeFolders` calls `checkoutOrigin(dir, probeTimeout)`; `verifyCheckout` calls `verifiedRepository` and maps `RepositoryVerificationError` to `{state:"rejected", reason, origin: actual}`.
- **Existing:** `test/git-environment.test.ts` — "every production Git spawn uses the shared hardened environment" expects Git-spawning files `[src/core/github-source.ts, src/standalone/git-process.ts]` and lists runner-only callers; its `ponytail:` comment anticipates this ticket.
- **Existing:** `test/project-setup.test.ts` — "the verifier reports typed reasons…" and "repository verification ignores inherited GIT_* overrides" exercise the core functions directly; "unsafe refs…" casts a spy `as unknown as typeof verifiedRepository`; guided-create and "origin and ref checks report one field…" tests go through `StandaloneService`/`OperatorApi`.
- **Existing:** `test/s07a/live-delivery.mjs` — live script constructing `new DomainStore(db)` then `project.create`/`github.configure` from `dist/`, and hashing `src/core/github-source.ts` among evidence files.
- **New:** `src/standalone/repository-verification.ts` — `checkoutOrigin` and `verifiedRepository` with the current signatures and semantics, using `runGit` and `realpath`.
- **New:** `src/core/github-source.ts` — `export type RepositoryVerifier = (input: z.output<typeof repositoryLinkSchema>, expectedOrigin?: { owner: string; name: string }) => Promise<LinkedRepository>`.
- **New:** `test/repository-verification.test.ts` — verifier-semantics tests against the standalone module.
- **Follow:** `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts:currentBranch` for `runGit` usage; `test/fixtures/setup-home.ts` (`createSetupHome`, `git`) and `test/fixtures/git-environment.ts` (`gitEnvironmentProbe`, `withHostileGitEnvironment`, `hardenedGitEnvironment`) for fixtures.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 → T2`; acyclic. T1 touches no file named by PR #956, #880, #878, #879 or #877 and may be implemented and reviewed while those are in flight. T2 edits shared files (`src/core/domain.ts`, `src/standalone/service.ts`, possibly `test/github-source-config.test.ts`) and needs T1's module; it is not independent of #886/#880 and should be rebased onto current `main` immediately before its validation. No two tasks may run concurrently.

#### 1. Standalone repository verifier on the shared Git runner

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Permitted paths:** `src/standalone/repository-verification.ts` (new), `test/repository-verification.test.ts` (new).
**Files and symbols:** New `checkoutOrigin(path: string, timeout = 5000)` and `verifiedRepository(input, expectedOrigin?)` exported from `src/standalone/repository-verification.ts`, importing `RepositoryVerificationError`, `parseGitHubOrigin`, `LinkedRepository`, `repositoryLinkSchema` from `../core/github-source.js` and `runGit` from `./git-process.js`. Core is not edited in T1 (the core copy is removed in T2).
**Test:** In `test/repository-verification.test.ts`, port the two direct-verifier tests from `test/project-setup.test.ts` to import from the new module: (a) with `createSetupHome()` checkouts `atlas`/`relay`/`gitlab` under `src/` and expected `acme/atlas`: relay → `origin-mismatch:acme/relay`; atlas ref `nope` → `ref-unavailable`; relay+`nope` → `origin-mismatch:acme/relay` (mismatch first); gitlab → `origin-provider`; gitlab and atlas-with-origin-removed without expected origin → verified; (b) under `withHostileGitEnvironment` + `gitEnvironmentProbe().withPath`, verification with expected origin returns `gitCommonDirectory` equal to the realpath of `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, `checkoutOrigin` returns `{owner:"acme",name:"atlas"}`, ≥4 invocations are recorded and each sees exactly `hardenedGitEnvironment`. Add: a relative path → `path-invalid`; a non-existent absolute path → `path-invalid`; an existing non-checkout folder → `not-checkout`; a checkout with no origin and expected origin → `origin-missing`; a symlinked checkout path returns the canonical `realpath` as `path`.
**Implementation:** Copy the two functions' logic unchanged, replacing each `execFileAsync("git", args, {timeout, env})` with `runGit({ args, timeoutMs, terminationGraceMs: 100, observationMs: 500, maxOutputBytes: 1024 * 1024 })`; treat `status !== "ok"` exactly like the former rejection (same reason thrown) and read `stdout.toString("utf8").trim()` on success. Keep the inline comment about the setup `^{commit}` peel.
**Validate:** From the repository root with Node from `.node-version` after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/repository-verification.test.js`; expect all new tests to pass. Then `npm run typecheck && npm run lint`; expect no errors.
**Complete when:** The standalone verifier exists, its tests pass, and nothing else changed.

#### 2. Remove core verification and inject the standalone verifier

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 complete; branch rebased onto current `main` (absorb #886/#880 if merged).
**Permitted paths:** `src/core/github-source.ts`, `src/core/domain.ts`, `src/standalone/service.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts`, `test/project-setup.test.ts`, `test/git-environment.test.ts`, `test/s07a/live-delivery.mjs`, and — only to inject the standalone verifier or change a verifier type import — any other `test/**` file that constructs `DomainStore` directly and whose journey requires real repository verification (candidates: `test/github-source-config.test.ts`, `test/github-review-regressions.test.ts`, `test/operator-configuration.test.ts`, `test/operator-http.test.ts`, `test/operator.test.ts`, `test/recovery.test.ts`, `test/retained-evidence-store.test.ts`).
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/core/github-source.ts`: delete `checkoutOrigin`, `verifiedRepository`, `execFileAsync` and the `node:child_process`, `node:fs/promises`, `node:util` and `./child-environment.js` imports (keep `isAbsolute`); add `RepositoryVerifier` type.
- `src/core/domain.ts`: import `RepositoryVerificationError` and `type RepositoryVerifier` (drop `verifiedRepository`); constructor third parameter `private readonly verifyRepository: RepositoryVerifier = unconfiguredVerifier`, a module-level function that rejects with `Error("Repository verification is not configured")`. No change to `configureGitHub`/`createProject` bodies.
- `src/standalone/service.ts`: import `verifiedRepository` from `./repository-verification.js` instead of core; pass it as the third `DomainStore` argument (`new DomainStore(db, () => …, verifiedRepository)`); `provisionTask` keeps calling it.
- `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts`: import `checkoutOrigin`, `verifiedRepository` from `./repository-verification.js`; `RepositoryVerificationError` still from core.
- `test/project-setup.test.ts`: remove the two tests ported in T1; change the spy cast to `RepositoryVerifier`; add the fail-closed test below.
- `test/git-environment.test.ts`: expected Git-spawning files become `[src/standalone/git-process.ts]`; add `"repository-verification"` to the runner-only list; add an assertion that no `src/core/**` source matches `node:child_process`, `node:fs` or `/standalone/` imports; replace the `ponytail:` comment accordingly.
- `test/s07a/live-delivery.mjs`: inject `verifiedRepository` from `../../dist/src/standalone/repository-verification.js` into its `DomainStore`; add `src/standalone/repository-verification.ts` to the hashed evidence file list.
**Test:** (1) New in `test/project-setup.test.ts`: `new DomainCommands(new DomainStore(db))` (no verifier) executing a guided `project.create` with one repository at a real `atlas` checkout rejects with `DomainPolicyError` `invalid-input`, `fieldPaths` `["repositories.0.path"]`, and `counts()` is unchanged. (2) Existing service-backed tests in `test/project-setup.test.ts` ("guided create records … verified repositories …", "origin and ref checks report one field, keep nothing and never echo credentials") and `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts` checkout-verification cases pass unchanged — they prove service injection and operator field feedback. (3) `test/git-environment.test.ts` scan passes with the new expectations; sensitivity: temporarily re-adding `import { execFile } from "node:child_process"` to `src/core/github-source.ts` makes it fail (do not commit).
**Implementation:** Edit in the order above. Then run the full suite; for each failure caused by a direct `new DomainStore(db)` whose journey verifies a real checkout, inject the standalone `verifiedRepository` (ordinary fixture repair).
