content.title: Return typed command results instead of rebuilding receipts from untyped rows

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/886
**Planned against:** `main` at `e21abd499cf95f4c35a89942fc577eec19ac2786`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean (temporary planning scratch excluded by path)
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Introduce one concrete command-result module with runtime schemas and a result map keyed by domain command type. Carry validated results through fresh execution, asynchronous verification, durable replay and in-flight duplicate sharing. Keep concrete command calls returning their existing result value shapes; use a correlated discriminated command/result union at union dispatch seams. Build the existing operator receipts with direct typed field projections and retain final receipt-schema parsing.

### Guardrails

- Preserve all public receipt shapes, persisted result JSON shapes, command scopes, canonical payload hashes, key-conflict behavior, transaction boundaries and post-commit notification behavior. No database migration, new public envelope or command tag in persisted receipts.
- Preserve SQLite numeric flags as validated `0 | 1`; boolean receipt fields use explicit comparisons. Preserve nullability, numeric limits, original revision replay, and private-field exclusion. Invalid persisted/provider data must fail closed; assertions do not validate it.
- Configuration/credential clearing, dependency removal and existing replay/reconciliation paths remain available. No new action, UI design, paid/live runtime turn, deployment, cutover or paused X01–X08 work.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- The lead accepted a command-keyed result map with an internal correlated union, preserving concrete execute return values and durable JSON. A tagged public envelope would unnecessarily change existing callers. Generic signatures are acceptable only when their implementation proves correlation through validated exhaustive branches, rather than casting a union to a requested generic result.
- Result schemas validate complete command result shapes while preserving existing fields: project, profile, task, assignment, routing, delivery, GitHub configuration, GitHub activation, credential status and capacity. Shared shapes can serve several command keys. Do not hide required fields behind `Record<string, unknown>` in projections or add a generic registry/framework.
- `github.preview` is the operator alias of domain `github.activate`; the receipt uses the preview name while the validated activation result retains its existing fields. Operation lookup has only scope/type/key, so validate its stored result with the requested operation's explicit domain-type mapping. Preserve existing create-versus-configure version consistency checks and conflict response on mismatched stored shape.
- Fresh result validation belongs inside the command transaction before receipt insertion; malformed generated/stored fields therefore cannot commit a success receipt. Replay validation follows the existing payload-hash conflict check, without reapplying or reverifying a previously committed command. Async repository verification validates provider output before recording linked repositories, with existing verification refusal semantics.

### Implementation context

- `src/core/domain.ts`: `commandSchema`, `DomainCommand`, `ParsedCommand`, `parseCommand`, `scopeOf`, `commandHash`; `DomainStore.apply` returns row-shaped or configuration results; `executeParsed` atomically writes `command_receipts`; `replayed`/`recordedResult` parse stored JSON; `recordedCommand`, `execute`, `createProject`, `configureGitHub`; `DomainCommands.execute` shares promises by scope/key and compares hashes.
- `src/standalone/operator-receipts.ts`: `commandReceipt`, `ReceiptShapeError` own configuration/adoption receipt projection and final parsing. `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`: `executeDomain`, `execute`, `previewGitHubSelection`, `readOperation` also project task/placement/credential receipts and read recorded operations. Coordination/recovery/control receipt builders are separate contracts.
- `src/standalone/service.ts:configureCapacity` currently casts a domain return to `CapacityLimits`; remove this assertion once the result is typed. `src/standalone/operator.ts` and `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` also execute domain commands; keep their existing behavior and typecheck wiring.
- New `src/core/command-results.ts`: concrete `DomainCommandResultMap`, correlated `DomainCommandOutcome`, exhaustive command-type validation and named schemas/parsers. Type-only use of `DomainCommand` avoids a runtime dependency cycle; reuse supported GitHub/delivery/runtime schemas where appropriate.
- Existing precedents: `githubConfiguration` validates JSON collections with Zod; `DeliveryStore.configuration` validates persisted policy; domain tests use real SQLite; operator configuration/API/source tests use injected fixture runtime and readers.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 → T2 → T3`, acyclic. One delivery owner integrates shared files. T1 owns only new result module and new isolated tests, and may run beside #873 (typed errors), #881 (Stop state), #932 (recovery mapping) and #944 (source credentials) after confirming they do not claim those new paths. T2 is gated on integration/readback of all four older owners because they share `domain.ts`, `service.ts` or `operator-api.ts` contracts; refresh their committed changes and renew affected evidence before editing. T3 follows T2 and the same older integration gate. Existing shared test files must not be edited concurrently. Do not infer safe file ownership merely from the absence of native dependencies.

Shared setup: in the implementation checkout use `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH` for this run (Node `24.21.0`, npm `12.2.0`); later sessions obtain equivalent pinned tools. Run `npm ci`, then `npm run build` before compiled tests. Every validation command below runs from that checkout root.

#### 1. Define and test the validated command-result boundary

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Confirm new-file ownership is disjoint from older delivery owners.
**Files and symbols:** New `src/core/command-results.ts`, `test/command-results.test.ts`, and `test/command-results-types.ts` (compiled by the existing tsconfig). Type-only imports of existing domain command types; no edits to `domain.ts` yet.
**Test:** Runtime table fixtures cover every domain command key and required shape, retaining original row/configuration fields. Reject missing IDs/revisions, wrong UUID/state/nullability, invalid numeric flags (including 2 and strings), non-finite/fractional revisions, malformed GitHub collections, invalid capacity limits and malformed credential status. Demonstrate valid nullable/zero flags and original numeric/boolean distinctions. Compile-time fixtures prove concrete command keys select the correct result, reject mismatched result shapes with `@ts-expect-error`, and prove the key map covers exactly `DomainCommand['type']`; exhaustive discriminated switches must fail when a variant is omitted.
**Implementation:** Define per-shape runtime schemas and map every concrete command type explicitly. Provide runtime parsing from `unknown` to the typed correlated outcome through checked branches, preserving existing result values/fields. Use compile-time exhaustive coverage rather than `as Result<T>` or an asserted generic registry. Keep normalization/validation separate from receipt formatting; a parser may not silently coerce malformed values into valid receipts.
**Validate:** `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/command-results.test.js`; expect all runtime cases and compile-time fixtures to pass. `npm run typecheck` must pass including the negative fixtures.
**Complete when:** Every domain command result shape has runtime and compile-time coverage without assertion laundering; older owners can review the module independently.

#### 2. Type fresh, asynchronous, replay and in-flight execution

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 boundary evidence passed; older #873/#881/#932/#944 integration gate satisfied and affected base changes reconciled.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/domain.ts` methods listed above and `DomainCommands.inFlight/execute`; `src/standalone/service.ts:configureCapacity`; extend `test/domain.test.ts`, `test/github-source-config.test.ts` and `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts` only where boundary wiring needs fixtures. New module parser wiring from T1.
**Test:** Fresh synchronous task/configuration calls return their original fields; exact stale retries after later mutations/reopen return the original result and perform no second side effect; changed payload conflicts. Deferred async project/GitHub verification permits matching concurrent keys to share the original promise/result, rejects changed payload while pending, and cleans failed in-flight entries for retry. Reopen and replay bypass repository verification. Inject malformed repository verification output and malformed persisted result JSON/shape; assert no new success receipt/side effect, no replay reapply and preserved refusal/uncertainty semantics. Test malformed fresh result validation rolls back both mutation and receipt, and retain notification-failure reconciliation coverage. Compare persisted JSON shape and canonical command hash fixtures unchanged.
**Implementation:** Validate `apply` results inside `executeParsed` before insertion; preserve the untagged stored value. Add typed requested-command validation to `replayed` and `recordedCommand`; give `recordedResult` a typed lookup path without breaking existing two-argument consumers. Carry concrete type correlation through sync/async dispatch and in-flight promises using the validated discriminated outcome, unwrap existing concrete result values at public methods, and retain current hash/cleanup ordering. Validate repository results at async verification entry before use. Remove the capacity result cast; audit other domain-command callers for inference gaps without changing their behavior.
**Validate:** `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/command-results.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/github-source-config.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-api.test.js`; expect existing and added boundary tests to pass. `npm run typecheck` passes with concrete async and replay result inference.
**Complete when:** Every production execution/replay/in-flight path exposes validated, correlated results, original persisted payloads and duplicate/conflict/recovery semantics survive, and receipt formatting no longer needs to compensate for an unvalidated execution path.

#### 3. Project existing receipts exhaustively and prove entry-point parity

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 persistence/async/replay boundary tests passed.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-receipts.ts:commandReceipt`; `src/standalone/operator-api.ts:executeDomain/execute/readOperation/previewGitHubSelection`; extend `test/operator-configuration.test.ts` and `test/operator-api.test.ts`, plus compile-time fixtures in `test/command-results-types.ts`. `src/operator/contracts.ts` receipt schemas remain unchanged.
**Test:** Keep existing receipt assertions unchanged. Add a table spanning task mutations, placement, assignment adoption, project/profile/routing/GitHub/capacity and credential status receipts, with existing field names/kinds/nullability/flags. Compare fresh POST, matching concurrent key, stale retry and persisted operation lookup after reopen where that operation supports lookup. Preview uses activation validation but emits preview receipt and skips provider access on replay. Requested wrong operation type or corrupt stored fields returns the existing conflict result; unknown key stays not-recorded. Changed payload conflicts across fresh and pending paths. Preserve private instructions, credential reference/key/value and repository paths exclusion. Type fixtures prove exhaustive domain receipt variants and prevent mismatched command/result projection.
**Implementation:** Build receipts from typed results with exhaustive branch handling and final `commandReceiptSchema.parse/safeParse`. Remove `raw as Row`, credential shape assertions, and `String/Number/Boolean` calls in affected command receipt construction; use typed values, explicit integer-flag comparisons and null handling. Preserve create/configure consistency and `ReceiptShapeError` lookup mapping. Thread typed results through `executeDomain`, direct task/placement branches, capacity and preview, and typed operation lookup. Preserve separate coordination/recovery/control contracts and #873 error mapping. Document the internal result boundary in the existing `docs/design/s04a-command-boundary.md` if its current description changes; no public behavior claim changes.
**Validate:** `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-configuration.test.js dist/test/operator-contracts.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-api.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-source-activation.test.js dist/test/operator-command-lifecycle.test.js`; expect unchanged receipt assertions plus new replay/correlation cases to pass. Inspect `commandReceipt` and affected `execute` receipt branches with `rg -n 'as Row|String\(|Number\(|Boolean\(' src/standalone/operator-receipts.ts src/standalone/operator-api.ts`; distinguish unrelated read projections, which are out of scope, and confirm no matches remain in receipt construction. `npm run typecheck` passes.
**Complete when:** Web/API mutations, operation reconciliation and shared CLI/source entry points expose identical receipts from typed results; no affected receipt builder performs row casts or primitive coercion. No UI redesign or new control entry point is needed.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Receipt construction has no Row casts or primitive coercions | T3 | Focused source inspection and typecheck |
| Existing receipt response tests pass unchanged | T3 | Existing operator API/configuration/contracts suites |
| Validated command-keyed results across storage/provider/sync/async paths | T1, T2 | Runtime shape fixtures, malformed boundary rollback/replay tests, type fixtures |
| Fresh, persisted and concurrent same-key receipts match; changed payload conflicts | T2, T3 | Async duplicate/reopen tests and public receipt comparisons |
| Exhaustiveness catches missing variants without public/schema changes | T1, T3 | Exact-key coverage and negative compile-time fixtures; unchanged receipt/schema/hash assertions |
| Runtime receipt parsing, nullable/boolean/numeric conversion and recovery preserved | T2, T3 | Corruption/conflict/notification tests, explicit flag projection and final schema parsing |

### Final validation

- At the integrated delivery candidate, from the implementation checkout root after pinned `npm ci`, run `npm run check`; all typecheck, lint, formatting, build and tests must pass. Renew affected evidence after older-owner integration changes; CI runs the same check.
- Run no live model/runtime/provider probes. Local fixture server tests require permission to bind loopback; retry only a concretely blocked command with escalation if sandbox EPERM recurs.
- Independent integrated review checks malformed persisted/provider data cannot obtain an asserted type, in-flight result correlation cannot pair the wrong variant, original JSON/receipt privacy is preserved, and command errors remain consistent after older-owner changes.

content.title: Reuse prepared SQLite statements

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/880
**Planned against:** `main` at `e21abd499cf95f4c35a89942fc577eec19ac2786`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Unrelated changes present (`.scratch/886-*.log` excluded by path)
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add a bounded, per-service `Database` facade that caches parameterized prepared statements by their exact SQL string and delegates execution to the one SQLite connection. Wire one facade through production database consumers while retaining `StandaloneService.db` as the raw `DatabaseSync` lifecycle handle. Clear retained references on schema-changing operations, rollback, and shutdown; let the pinned Node runtime close the underlying connection. The cache stores statements only, never rows or results.

### Guardrails

- Preserve SQL parameter binding, transaction and migration behavior, SQLite persistence, existing narrow fake `Database` implementations, and stored data/schema. Do not add a schema migration or change persisted formats.
- Keep the cache owned by one service/database instance. Preserve the raw `DatabaseSync` field and lifecycle/readback behavior in `StandaloneService`.
- Do not introduce dynamic SQL template rewriting, change hundreds of call sites, claim latency improvements without measurement, or claim a bound on total native statement memory. Do not add a dependency or change the supported Node range.
- Keep external runtime/provider probes, deployment, cutover, and writes outside this issue.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.

### Planning decisions

- Keep `Database`'s required fake-facing contract unchanged (`exec` and parameterized `prepare` with `run/get/all`). The new facade implements that contract around a `Database` and forwards optional `isTransaction`; its prepared-statement wrappers delegate every bind value unchanged and reject calls after facade closure. A dedicated fake-backed counter can therefore verify reuse without requiring fake implementations to add methods.
- Use an LRU `Map<string, Statement>` with a default capacity of 512 entries, configurable smaller in tests. This is a finite bound sized to retain the roughly 470 static `prepare` call sites observed at the planned baseline (`state.ts` 279, `coordination.ts` 109, `domain.ts` 82), while still bounding dynamic query variants. Eviction removes the cache's strong reference; it does not promise immediate native finalization or a hard bound on native memory before garbage collection.
- Node v24.21.0 provides `DatabaseSync.createTagStore()` and `SQLTagStore.clear()`, but its tagged API binds values through template-literal holes and cannot transparently execute the existing SQL strings containing `?` placeholders. The pinned `StatementSync` prototype has no `close()` or `finalize()` method. Use ordinary cached `DatabaseSync.prepare(sql)` statements to preserve the existing binding contract. The official [Node.js v24.21.0 SQLite documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/sqlite.html) describes the pinned runtime API; a local probe on Node 24.21.0 confirmed that `DatabaseSync.close()` makes a previously prepared statement unusable with `ERR_INVALID_STATE`. The facade clears its references and marks itself closed on the first close attempt, even if the raw close throws, so retained wrappers cannot execute afterward. A later `close()` call must still invoke the raw-close callback again rather than short-circuiting because the facade is already logically closed. Do not claim explicit per-statement close on Node 24.21 or immediate finalization on LRU eviction.
- Invalidate cache entries on `ROLLBACK` and when `exec` or a cached prepared `run` executes schema-changing SQL (including `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `REINDEX`, `VACUUM`, and `PRAGMA` mutations). Preserve entries across ordinary `BEGIN` and `COMMIT`. This makes rollback/migration reuse observable and avoids relying on stale cache ownership after DDL; test through real SQLite and assert prepare counts and rows/schema, not elapsed time.
- Wire the facade once at `StandaloneService.start()` and pass it to the existing production consumers. The issue targets 470 inline prepares across the three hot modules at this baseline; those files already accept the `Database` contract and need no call-site rewrite. Keep standalone raw DB startup pragmas and lifecycle on `DatabaseSync`.
- Only `src/standalone/service.ts` is the shared implementation seam with current active plans: #873, #881, #886 and #944 include service edits. T1 below is disjoint and may proceed alongside them. T2 needs the root's exact service edit grant and a fresh compatible-base screen against whichever holders are then admitted; it does not wait on unadmitted plans. #932's actual files (`operator-api.ts`, recovery UI and their tests) are disjoint from this service-only wiring; do not gate on it. Do not edit `domain.ts`, `coordination.ts`, or `state.ts` for this plan.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/store.ts` — exports the narrow `Database` contract used by core stores, with `exec` and `prepare` returning the three parameterized operations.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts:StandaloneService.start` — opens one `DatabaseSync` at line 532 and passes it to `Store`, the core/state/coordination stores and other production SQLite consumers; `StandaloneService.stop` and failed-start cleanup close it near lines 1108 and 1501. Normal stop already retains the raw handle and owner after a thrown close so a later stop can retry; failed-start cleanup currently clears both unconditionally in `finally`, even if raw close failed. T2 adds only the bounded ownership repair needed for this cache lifecycle: retain the open raw handle/owner after failed-start close failure so an explicit later stop can retry. `StandaloneService.db` is also used for open-state checks and test readback.
- **New:** `src/core/database-cache.ts` — `CachedDatabase`, a bounded LRU facade implementing `Database`, plus a narrow cache-invalidation and close lifecycle. It owns statement wrappers and delegates SQL/binds to the underlying database.
- **Follow:** `test/store-bindings.test.ts` — real SQLite migration/rollback tests and fake-compatible narrow-interface precedent; `test/standalone.test.ts`'s “failed stop closes SQLite and allows restart on the same service object” verifies the service's existing close/restart path.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 → T2`, acyclic. T1 owns only the new facade module and a new dedicated unit-test file; it can run alongside other issue work. T2 owns `src/standalone/service.ts` and passes one facade to its existing production DB consumers. Before T2, screen the exact service delta against admitted #873/#881/#886/#944 work and obtain the root's scoped service-edit grant; integrate only verified compatible changes and renew affected checks. Do not wait for #932 or any unadmitted older plan. The owner keeps the two slices integrated because T2 depends on T1's constructor/close contract.

#### 1. Add bounded statement-cache facade

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** None. Work only in a compatible implementation checkout at the verified base; do not edit shared service code.
**Files and symbols:** New `src/core/database-cache.ts` (`CachedDatabase`, bounded LRU entry map, prepared-statement wrapper, schema/rollback invalidation); new `test/database-cache.test.ts`. Import the existing `Database` type from `src/core/store.ts`; do not change required members or existing fake implementations.
**Test:** Use a real `DatabaseSync` through a counting `Database` adapter. Prepare the same parameterized `SELECT` repeatedly with different values and assert one raw `prepare` call, distinct results, and that an intervening insert/update is visible (no result caching). Inside a transaction, update and read, roll back, then repeat the same query and assert the original committed value and a fresh prepare after rollback invalidation. Run a cached query, alter its table through `exec`, and assert the same SQL returns the new schema/column data after a new prepare. Exercise DDL via prepared `run` and assert invalidation. With capacity 2, access A/B/A/C/B and assert the bound never exceeds 2 and B recompiles after eviction. Give two facades separate real databases with identical SQL and assert each compiles independently and reads its own value. Inject a close callback around a real file-backed `DatabaseSync` that throws before raw close on its first invocation and closes normally on its second. Assert the first attempt clears cached references, marks the facade unusable, and causes both a retained wrapper and new `prepare` to reject; assert a second `facade.close()` invokes the callback again and closes the exact same raw handle. Reopen the file with a new facade and verify persisted committed data and integrity. Record the order as cache invalidation → raw close attempt 1 → cache invalidation → raw close attempt 2. Also pass an unchanged minimal fake `Database` through the facade and verify all three operations and binds work without requiring any new fake methods.
**Implementation:** Preserve the SQL string verbatim and delegate the existing `...parameters` unchanged. LRU-hit refreshes recency; miss prepares once and stores a wrapper; eviction drops only the oldest cache reference. The wrapper guards operations against use after close. Invalidate after schema-changing `exec`/prepared `run` and on rollback; ordinary transaction begin/commit keeps entries. A close callback lets production clear references before each raw-close attempt. The first attempt permanently closes the facade to queries and invalidates all wrappers, whether raw close succeeds or throws; repeated `close()` calls still invoke the callback so the owning service can retry closing a retained raw connection. The callback must not be made one-shot or skipped by facade idempotence. Do not call unavailable `StatementSync.close()`/`finalize()`.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after the shared `npm ci`, run `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run build:service && PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH node --test dist/test/database-cache.test.js`; expect service TypeScript compilation and all focused cache, binding, rollback, schema, bound, fake, close and reopen assertions to pass.
**Complete when:** The new facade reuses exact-SQL prepared statements within its finite per-instance LRU, preserves execution semantics, invalidates at specified boundaries, and the focused real-SQLite/fake tests pass.

#### 2. Wire one facade through the standalone service

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 passes. Before the shared service edit, the root supplies the scoped grant and confirms a fresh compatible base after screening only the admitted holders that touch `src/standalone/service.ts`; integrate their verified service changes first. Preserve any disjoint work and re-run the affected checks if the base moved.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `StandaloneService.start` at the `DatabaseSync` construction and production store wiring; failed-start cleanup near line 1108; `StandaloneService.stop` near line 1501. Update `test/standalone.test.ts` for both normal-stop retry/facade invalidation and failed-start close-fails-once ownership recovery; do not modify the overlapping database unit-test file from this task.
**Test:** Keep the existing “service shutdown retains an open database owner and can retry close” normal-stop regression and extend it to assert facade invalidation and that the subsequent stop retries the same raw connection before restart. Add a separate failed-start cleanup regression using a real local SQLite database and fake runtime: the runtime factory captures the service through the existing narrow private test-access cast, patches that instance’s raw `DatabaseSync.close` to throw once, then throws a startup marker error. Assert failed-start cleanup reports failure, leaves the raw connection open and the data-directory owner held, makes `service.start()` reject as incomplete and a retained facade wrapper reject, and allows a later explicit `service.stop()` to retry the same raw close and release ownership only after it succeeds. Restore the instance method and clean up in `finally`. Do not add a public database factory option or patch `DatabaseSync.prototype`. The focused facade test from T1 proves compile reuse, wrapper invalidation and repeat close callback ordering; these two service cases separately prove normal-stop retry and the bounded failed-start ownership repair.
**Implementation:** Keep `this.db` as the raw `DatabaseSync` used for open-state checks and close readback. Create one `CachedDatabase` after the existing startup pragmas, store it separately, and pass that same instance to `Store`, workspace comparisons, operator credentials, conversation history, diagnostics, `DomainStore`, GitHub sources, routing attempts, scheduler, workspace bindings, `ExecutionState`, `CoordinationStore`, inbox startup reconciliation and `DeliveryStore`. Route failed-start and normal-stop teardown through the facade's clear-then-raw-close lifecycle. Every close attempt clears/invalidate facade references before calling `rawDatabaseSync.close()`, and repeated stop attempts invoke the callback again even though the facade already rejects queries. Preserve normal-stop behavior: retain `this.db` and its owner while `this.db.isOpen` remains true after a thrown close, then allow a later stop to retry. Add the bounded failed-start repair: when cleanup's raw close throws and the connection remains open, retain that raw handle and owner rather than unconditionally dropping/releasing them in `finally`; make the partial startup non-running and permit a later explicit stop to retry closure. In both paths, do not release ownership or permit restart/database access until raw closure is confirmed; after failed-start cleanup retained the open handle, `start()` must continue rejecting as incomplete and an old wrapper must remain unusable. Once closed, clear the facade and raw handle, release ownership in the existing order, and construct a fresh facade for each service restart. Keep all other failed-start cleanup ordering and behavior unchanged.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after T1 and the authorized compatible service integration, run `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run build && PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH node --test dist/test/database-cache.test.js dist/test/standalone.test.js`; expect both builds and the selected tests to pass, including failed-stop close/restart, clean database close and integrity check.
**Complete when:** Every production consumer for this service generation shares one bounded cache; the public/raw service database lifecycle remains intact; stop, failed startup and same-object restart leave no callable cached wrapper and preserve database integrity.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Repeated identical SQL reuses compilation with different bound values and current persisted/transactional data; rows/results are never cached. | 1 | Counting real-SQLite assertions in `database-cache.test.ts`. |
| Rollback and schema changes invalidate cache entries and queries still read valid current schema/data. | 1 | Rollback, `exec` DDL and prepared DDL prepare-count/schema assertions in `database-cache.test.ts`. |
| Cache retention stays within the configured bound, and distinct database instances keep distinct caches. | 1 | Capacity-2 LRU and two-database assertions in `database-cache.test.ts`. |
| Existing minimal fake `Database` implementations remain compatible. | 1 | Fake-only test uses the existing interface without added fake methods. |
| A raw-close failure invalidates facade queries but retains the raw handle/owner; normal stop retries, and failed-start cleanup preserves ownership for a later explicit stop retry; only confirmed closure permits restart with a fresh cache. | 1, 2 | Fail-once facade callback test verifies invalidation/order; existing normal-stop lifecycle test verifies retry; new real-SQLite/fake-runtime failed-start test verifies retained handle/owner, blocked restart/query, later retry, reopen and integrity check. |
| All existing behavior and tests remain passing without persistence/schema changes. | 2 | Final `npm run check` on the integrated candidate. |

### Final validation

- From the implementation checkout root, after `npm ci` using `.node-version` and the pinned npm, run `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run check` on the final integrated candidate; expect typecheck, lint, formatting, both builds, and the full automated suite to pass. Record the exact Node/npm versions and result. No live model/provider/runtime probes are required for this database-only change.

### Review focus

- Confirm the LRU bound describes retained cache references only; do not imply immediate native finalization on eviction or an overall native-memory hard bound on Node 24.21. Confirm each close attempt clears the cache before raw close; wrappers stay invalid after a close failure, but a later facade/service close retries the callback against the retained raw handle. Distinguish the already-supported normal-stop retry from the new narrow failed-start repair; verify neither path drops ownership or permits restart before confirmed closure. Verify migrations/rollback do not reuse stale cache entries or change persisted data.

content.title: Stop spawning Git per task on polled read endpoints

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/878
**Planned against:** `main` at `e21abd499cf95f4c35a89942fc577eec19ac2786`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Unrelated changes present (.scratch/886-*.log excluded by path)
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Use a synchronous, bounded projection of the persisted task-workspace binding for path-only redaction. Route polled task-list, project and Inbox exclusions through that projection so each read uses last-known stored data and launches no per-task Git process. Keep identity and health validation at startup recovery, before execution and explicit workspace inspection.

### Guardrails

- Preserve repository/workspace paths in the exclusion set, credential and instruction redactions, fail-closed behavior when exclusion inputs are unavailable or exceed existing bounds, and the current workspace-visibility fences around list, project and Inbox reads.
- Preserve current response and schema fields. Passive reads do not refresh or mutate persisted workspace health; they return only fields and holds already exposed. Do not add a workspace-health field, UI action, endpoint or polling UI change.
- Missing/replaced workspace paths are held when startup recovery, execution admission or explicit workspace inspection performs its existing validation. Uncertain Git retains its conservative hold. Do not replace these checks with stored-identity reuse or allow a passive path projection to authorize execution.
- Preserve taskWorkspace, WorkspaceManager.get, forExecution, recover, and explicit inspection validation semantics. Do not add per-task Git polling, a cross-request health cache, or a new persisted format.
- Keep the scope to redaction path lookup and its health-check boundary. Do not include #877's broader request-local exclusion preparation/sanitizer caching or #875 SQL filtering.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- Add a narrow service method that reads workspaceBindings.get(taskId) and returns only the stored root and repository path strings needed by redaction. It must not check filesystem identity or Git and must include stored paths even when the binding is already held, matching current path-redaction behavior after taskWorkspace returns a held binding.
- Update the existing shared OperatorApi.exclusions path only. Task-list pages call taskSummaryRead; project summaries call per-task exclusions; Inbox calls taskSummaryRead per task. These are the three issue surfaces. Other taskWorkspace callers in inspection and artifact reads retain their current validation because their behavior needs a current binding.
- The current task-list/project/Inbox response schemas do not expose workspace health. Interpret “last-known workspace health” as preserving the existing persisted binding state without poll-time refresh or mutation; no new health response is part of this contract.
- #877 is currently Todo without an active implementation plan, and #875 is absent from the verified Project snapshot. Neither is an implementation dependency. #880 is Ready to implement and touches service.ts; #886, #932 and #944 are Ready to implement and touch operator-api.ts; #873 and #881 are In progress and include shared service/API work. The single implementation owner must screen the actual admitted changes to those two files against the supplied clean implementation checkout before editing, integrate only compatible admitted work, and renew focused checks if its base moved. No work is gated merely on unadmitted #877 or absent #875.
- Count controlled Git child starts in fixtures, not elapsed-time improvements. The API regression should use a repository-backed task and snapshot launch events after provisioning so setup Git is excluded.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** src/standalone/operator-api.ts:OperatorApi.exclusions gathers current path exclusions, but for a task calls service.taskWorkspace(taskId). This routes to validation on every read.
- **Existing:** src/standalone/operator-api.ts:readTaskListPageOnce, readProjectOnce and readInbox reach that lookup through per-task exclusions or taskSummaryRead. workspaceSnapshot and requireWorkspaceSnapshot fence persisted binding visibility around each response.
- **Existing:** src/standalone/service.ts:taskWorkspaceVisibility hashes stored workspace identity; taskWorkspace delegates to validated WorkspaceManager.get. conversationExclusionsForAssignment already reads workspaceBindings.get directly to include the workspace root, source paths, worktree paths and Git common dirs.
- **Existing:** src/standalone/workspaces.ts:WorkspaceManager.recover, get, forExecution and validateReady own startup, execution and explicit current-binding checks. test/workspaces.test.ts already proves missing workspaces become held, held state is not silently recreated, uncertain Git stays held, and execution reads rerun identity checks.
- **Follow:** test/operator-api.test.ts test “project task summaries share task workspace and repository exclusions” for unchanged path redaction; test/operator-inbox.test.ts test “Inbox revalidates earlier workspace and task binding after later row awaits” for retaining snapshot race rejection; test/fixtures/controlled-git.ts records exact child starts for launch-count assertions.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 → T2. T1 changes the service/API read seam and proves all three polled surfaces use stored path exclusions without launching Git. T2 verifies the defined validation checkpoints and documents the timing contract. The slices are sequential because T2's checkpoint assertions depend on the new passive-read path. No tasks may run concurrently. Keep one delivery owner for the integrated source and tests.

#### 1. Project stored workspace paths for polled redaction

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Start from the implementation checkout supplied by the root at its verified base. Before source edits, inspect changes in src/standalone/service.ts and src/standalone/operator-api.ts from the then-admitted holders named in Planning decisions; preserve unrelated work and resolve unknown overlap before editing.
**Files and symbols:** src/standalone/service.ts — add a narrow taskWorkspaceRedactionPaths(taskId) projection beside taskWorkspaceVisibility, backed by workspaceBindings.get; src/standalone/operator-api.ts — change only OperatorApi.exclusions to consume those paths; test/operator-api.test.ts, test/operator-task-list.test.ts, and test/operator-inbox.test.ts — controlled-Git and output regressions, including the Inbox read-race fixture.
**Test:** Use the existing operator fixture with WorkspaceManagerOptions.gitExecutable set to controlledGit().executable. Create a local Git repository, create a task, and call service.provisionTask(taskId, [{ repositoryId, path }]); put the resulting root/source/worktree/Git-common paths in a task title or other already-disclosed text. After provisioning, record the fixture's Git start count. Read the task-list page, its project, and Inbox (seed an open question so the Inbox projection includes the task). Assert none of the three reads increases Git starts, and assert each returned title or Inbox task title omits every configured path while ordinary safe text remains. Keep and adapt the Inbox race test so deleting an earlier stored binding during a later task's awaited read still rejects the stale response. Assert no path appears in serialized API results.
**Implementation:** Add a synchronous method that first validates the task through domain().task(taskId), then reads the persisted binding once and returns a deduplicated array containing binding.path plus each repository's sourcePath, workspacePath, and non-null gitCommonDir; return an empty array when there is no binding. Do not include a filesystem check, call to WorkspaceManager.get, state mutation or Git call. In exclusions, append those paths only for its task-specific case, preserving current bounds, credentials, instruction revisions and catch-to-unavailable behavior. Leave response construction, workspaceSnapshot/visibility checks, and every other taskWorkspace caller unchanged. Retarget the Inbox race barrier to the new path projection while preserving its existing mutation and stale-response assertions.
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, after the shared pinned install, run PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run build && PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH node --test dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-task-list.test.js dist/test/operator-inbox.test.js; expect service and web builds plus all focused tests to pass, including unchanged redaction, zero post-setup Git child starts and Inbox binding/task race rejection.
**Complete when:** All three polled API reads redact stored workspace paths without launching Git per task, and their current visibility/fail-closed behavior remains covered.

#### 2. Preserve health validation checkpoints and document passive reads

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's focused tests pass. Use the same integrated candidate; do not add a new response field or health action.
**Files and symbols:** test/workspaces.test.ts — stored projection versus full validation and execution identity checks; test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.ts — explicit inspection through OperatorApi.readWorkspaceDirectory; docs/acceptance.md — revise A17 in place to state that polling uses last-known stored binding data and that startup recovery, before execution and explicit workspace inspection remain validation points.
**Test:** With a real repository-backed fixture and controlled Git, remove or replace the worktree after a ready binding is stored. First read task-list/project/Inbox and assert there are no Git starts and the persisted binding remains at its last-known state. Then call explicit readWorkspaceDirectory for that task and assert the missing or replaced workspace is reported unavailable and its binding is held. Keep the existing execution assertion that forExecution performs a fresh identity read even after recent validation. Retain the existing uncertain-Git and restart/recovery tests, asserting a bounded uncertain identity failure leaves the binding conservatively held; do not convert uncertainty to ready from the passive read.
**Implementation:** Change no production health-check code. Revise A17's workspace clause to name startup recovery, execution and explicit inspection as health checks, and state that polled path-redaction reads use stored last-known binding data without refreshing it. Keep missing-workspace execution holds and recovery behavior intact.
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root after T1, run PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run build && PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH node --test dist/test/workspaces.test.js dist/test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.js dist/test/workspace-inspection.test.js; expect missing/replaced state to be detected at explicit checks, uncertain Git and startup recovery to retain holds, and execution to perform a fresh identity read.
**Complete when:** The three validation checkpoints and delayed passive detection are directly described and tested without changing schemas, held-state policy or execution authorization.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Task-list, project and Inbox polling launch no per-task Git subprocesses, including path exclusion work. | 1 | Controlled-Git post-provision launch-count regression for all three API surfaces. |
| Current workspace/source/worktree/Git-common paths remain redacted and ordinary safe response content remains available. | 1 | API output and serialized-response assertions in the existing and extended redaction tests. |
| Missing or replaced workspaces are detected and held at startup recovery, before execution and explicit workspace inspection; uncertain Git retains its conservative hold. | 2 | Existing recovery/execution/Git-uncertainty tests plus explicit directory-inspection regression. |
| Passive reads preserve last-known stored workspace health and current response schemas; they do not trigger detection. | 1, 2 | Stored-state and zero-launch assertions; schema checks through the existing endpoint tests. |

### Final validation

- From the integrated implementation worktree root, after PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm ci, run PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run check on the final candidate; expect typecheck, lint, format, service/web builds and the complete test suite to pass. Record pinned Node and npm versions and the final result.
- No live provider, runtime, deployment or cutover probe is required for this read-path change.

### Review focus

- Verify that no polled call path reaches WorkspaceManager.get through redaction directly or through a helper, and that task-specific paths are read from the same persisted binding source as current exclusions.
- Verify that stale path detection remains at the three defined checkpoints, execution always gets fresh identity validation, the Inbox and visibility fences still reject races, and the test's zero-process claim excludes setup launches using an explicit post-provision count baseline.

content.title: Use indexed checks in scheduler wake instead of reloading all turn requests

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/879
**Planned against:** `main` at `e21abd499cf95f4c35a89942fc577eec19ac2786`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Unrelated changes present
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Give scheduler wakes a narrow SQLite query facade: indexed existence/identity reads inside mutation loops and projections containing only pending completion, missing fallback events and non-stale uncommitted routing attempts. Integrate it without moving scheduling decisions or changing their order. Retain historical/operator APIs for their existing callers; #875 owns operator projections.

### Guardrails

- Preserve work and assignment identities, delivery binding/version checks, current task/admission/hold gates, historical-resolution exclusions, FIFO order, routing fallback payloads, stale routing detection and reporting repair identity. Every query in a mutation loop reads current database state after earlier iterations; no once-per-wake cache of requests, committed IDs or unresolved work.
- Keep delivery settlement/withdrawal before pending completion finalization, then successful-terminal disposition, fallback reconciliation, stale-routing reconciliation, initial routing, initial assignment creation, queued delivery creation, pending inbox creation, reporting repairs, startup capture and scheduler wake; retain the bounded refusal rebind pass and generation checks.
- No public schema, persisted representation, domain guarantee, runtime policy, paid inference, live provider probe, deployment/cutover or paused native work changes. New indexes are additive and idempotent; never drop or rewrite records. Operator UI/history entry points retain existing APIs.
- Continue routine implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record corrections and renew affected evidence. A wrong factual seam or repository assumption in this plan allows one focused diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary implementation defects do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- A new service-only `SchedulerWakeQueries` uses the existing `Database` interface. This settles cross-store reads without expanding core APIs: stores already share one database, and `StandaloneService.start` migrates domain, routing attempts, scheduler requests and coordination before waking. It returns only identities and needed status/ordering metadata; existing `domain.routingOperation(id)` and `routingAttempts.operation(projectId, taskId, taskVersion)` hydrate qualifying routing records.
- Pending means all currently actionable rows, not an arbitrary LIMIT that can miss work. Materialization scales with pending work, not unrelated completed history. Missing fallback selection excludes any existing event by exact routingOperationId, preserving the current unique event identity and retrying missing events until a lead exists. Newly committed fallback creation in the initial routing branch remains unchanged.
- Use case-sensitive `disposition GLOB 'lead-review:*'`, equivalent to current `startsWith("lead-review:")`. Use NOT EXISTS against `coordination_inbox_events.routingOperationId` for missing events and against `routing_operations.id` for uncommitted attempts. The attempt status predicate is exactly `status <> 'stale'`, preserving pending/routing/assigned/lead-review attempts awaiting stale reconciliation.
- Existing `turn_requests.workId` UNIQUE, `routing_operations.id` PRIMARY KEY and `coordination_one_routing_fallback` indexes cover identity/anti-join probes. Add query indexes through `SchedulerWakeQueries.ensureIndexes()` after all table migrations: assignmentId/state/sequence for unsettled request IDs; partial pending completion index on createdAt/requestId WHERE status='pending'; partial routing fallback index on id WHERE disposition GLOB 'lead-review:*'; partial routing-attempt index on createdAt/operationId WHERE status<>'stale'. Existing assignmentId/sequence index covers oldest-request selection. Domain rowid order remains fallback order; completion order remains createdAt/requestId; attempts retain createdAt/operationId. Verify actual SQLite plans rather than claiming wall-clock speedups.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts:wakeScheduler` contains five request-history reads: initial identity, initial-creation error's first assignment request, delivery identity snapshot, recipient unresolved queued/active/held requests, repair identity. The error path currently uses the oldest matching request (`ORDER BY sequence`), not newest or current-version work.
- **Existing:** completion loop calls `coordination.completionRequests()` and filters pending, checks completed intent and exact task/lead binding, then calls `finalizeDeliveryCompletion`. Domain routing history is loaded twice; `routingAttempts.operations()` also loads full history before stale/committed exclusion.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts:heldWorkIds`, `find`, `assignmentPage` show narrow SQL; `src/core/store.ts:Database` has exec/prepare/get/all and requires no native SQLite-only facade features. `coordination.isHistoricalWorkResolved` embodies refusal, valid recovery-continuation and supersession-chain exemptions; do not duplicate its logic in SQL.
- **New:** `src/standalone/scheduler-wake-queries.ts:SchedulerWakeQueries` owns read-only query methods; ensureIndexes performs only additive local index initialization. `hasWork(workId)` SELECT 1; `oldestAssignmentWorkId(assignmentId)` workId ORDER BY sequence LIMIT 1; `unsettledAssignmentWorkIds(assignmentId)` workId WHERE state IN ('queued','active','held') ORDER BY sequence; `pendingCompletionIdentities()` requestId/taskId/leadAssignmentId/leadWorkId in existing completion order; `missingRoutingFallbackOperationIds()` qualifying operation IDs in rowid order; `uncommittedRoutingAttemptIdentities()` operationId/projectId/taskId/taskVersion in existing attempt order. Runtime-validate projected persisted values with small schemas; do not load prompts, reviewedResultIds, judgment/snapshot/outcome JSON for excluded history.
- **Baseline:** pinned Node 24.21.0/npm 12.2.0 verified; npm ci and npm run build pass. The focused existing scheduler/drain/coordination/domain/routing command passed 89/89 after the same command was retried with host access for the sandbox-denied ps cleanup fixture. Logs: `/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/879-ci.log`, `879-build.log`, `879-focused.log`. Full npm run check is required at delivery, not claimed from planning. Existing `.scratch/886-{build,ci,focused}.log` are unrelated baseline artifacts excluded by path and preserved.
- **Tests:** real SQLite query coverage in new `test/scheduler-wake-queries.test.ts`; service regressions in new `test/scheduler-wake.test.ts`, following `test/scheduler.test.ts` gated fake runtime and `test/background-service.test.ts:serviceAccess` controlled private-wake access. Existing `test/fixtures/coordination.ts` covers historical identities and reopen; use its fixture where useful.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic `T1 -> T2`. T1 owns the new query module and its tests and can proceed independently of other tickets whose actually admitted mutable files are disjoint. T2 owns service integration and new wake regressions; gate it on T1 and the controller's current admitted `src/standalone/service.ts` writer, naming that dependency when present. Do not wait behind unadmitted plans. Preserve others' changes. One coherent PR; no planned edits to existing core/state/routing/history APIs or design files.

#### 1. Narrow current-state queries with persistence evidence

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Verified base, pinned toolchain, npm ci.
**Files and symbols:** New query module and `test/scheduler-wake-queries.test.ts`, as inventoried above.
**Implementation:** Implement exact predicates/projections and index initialization using the shared Database facade. Query methods have no memoized results. Preserve optional absence rather than throwing for identity existence checks. Cross-table queries execute only after owning schemas exist. Index initialization is repeatable on fresh and existing databases without changing schema versions or rows.
**Test:** Seed applicable tables in real SQLite with mixed queued/active/completed/held request history, pending/rejected/finalized completions, committed assigned/fallback operations, existing/missing fallback events, and stale/non-stale committed/uncommitted attempts. Assert exact qualifying identities and order. Insert/hold/resolve between successive reads to prove freshness; oldest assignment request selection includes historical completed work. Seed 10,000 unrelated historical rows including large prompts/JSON, assert returned/materialized projections remain identical and excluded payloads are never parsed. Reopen and rerun ensureIndexes, assert row contents/counts unchanged and SQLite query plans use identity/status indexes rather than full historical scans; use a recording Database wrapper conforming to the existing interface to check narrow selected columns and query row counts. Existing fallback/attempt records with malformed excluded JSON must not be parsed.
**Validate:** From ticket checkout with `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/scheduler-wake-queries.test.js`; expect all predicates, freshness, ordering, reopen and materialization checks green.
**Complete when:** Narrow queries and persistence/index evidence pass before service integration uses them.

#### 2. Scheduler integration preserving mutation ordering

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 evidence green; overlapping admitted service writer reconciled by lead.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/service.ts` imports/private query facade initialization/cleanup and `wakeScheduler`; new `test/scheduler-wake.test.ts`.
**Implementation:** Initialize the facade after coordination migrations; clear it with service generation stores on stop/failure and guard access in wake. Replace each inventory read in place. Use fresh hasWork checks in initial/delivery/repair iterations; on initial-creation error, select oldest work ID then hold it. For inbox blocking use scoped unsettled IDs and retain `.some(workId => !coordination.isHistoricalWorkResolved(workId))`. Hydrate only projected missing fallback operations and non-stale uncommitted attempts with existing targeted methods; handle optional attempt absence conservatively. Pending completions keep the exact completed intent/task/lead binding check and finalize one at a time, with existing failure behavior. Keep scheduler.queued/startup capture and public history readers unchanged.
**Test:** Instrument old full-history SchedulerStore.list, CoordinationStore.completionRequests, DomainStore.routingOperations and RoutingAttemptStore.operations to throw only during controlled wake. Exercise repeated wake and two separate assignments/deliveries/results within one wake; assert no duplicates or missed turn/event, and downstream reads observe rows created/held earlier in the wake. Cover the initial error/oldest-request hold branch, queued repair replay, unresolved held blocking plus refused/recovered/superseded historical-held exclusions, exact delivery identity/version mismatch refusal, pending completion awaiting the correct completed lead work, multiple pending completions preserving order, and routing fallback exactly once with missing lead/restart retry. Cover stale routing after task/profile/guidance/permission changes and committed/stale attempts excluded. Repeat with large unrelated historical data and assert unchanged bounded materialization and runtime turn counts; do not use elapsed-time thresholds. Where an awaited completion yields, mutate a later request/hold before resuming and confirm its later admission sees current state. A sensitivity check reintroducing a full history read or cached existence result must fail the corresponding instrumentation/freshness regression; discard the intentional fault.
**Validate:** From the same checkout/toolchain run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/scheduler-wake-queries.test.js dist/test/scheduler-wake.test.js dist/test/scheduler.test.js dist/test/scheduler-drain.test.js dist/test/coordination.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/routing.test.js`; expect all existing and new scenarios green. Process-cleanup fixtures require host ps access if sandbox denial recurs; retry only the concretely failed command through escalation.
**Complete when:** Controlled production wakes use no full historical APIs and preserve state, order, identity and fresh mutation visibility in every listed regression.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wake does not load all turn requests, completions or routing operations | T1, T2 | Projection/materialization and throwing-history instrumentation checks, including attempt history |
| Existing scheduler tests pass unchanged | T2 | Existing scheduler/drain tests in focused command; existing files need no edits |
| Each iteration observes earlier inserts/holds; no stale wake snapshot | T1, T2 | Inter-read mutations and multi-delivery/result/repair wake regressions |
| Historical resolution, delivery identity, fallback and completion order unchanged | T2 | Explicit held-history, exact-binding, fallback replay and completion sequencing tests |
| Large unrelated history does not increase wake materialization | T1, T2 | 10,000-row projection/recording-wrapper and production-wake assertions |

### Final validation

- From ticket checkout under pinned Node 24.21.0/npm 12.2.0, run `npm ci` then `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate, as required by AGENTS.md and issue #879. Existing full suite needs loopback/process host permissions; inspect inside sandbox and escalate the concretely failed command only. Focused planning evidence does not replace this required delivery check.
- Review frozen final diff for source acceptance and query semantics, including lifecycle/reopen, recovery exclusions and mutations during awaits. No paid/live runtime or provider qualification is required by this performance refactor.
- Confirm other entry points: shared service wake callers and startup/refusal rebind use the same queries; operator/history screens retain existing APIs. There is no new state-changing operator action and no archive/restore counterpart to implement. Query failure follows existing generation/background failure handling, with preserved records.

### Review focus

Verify the error path selects oldest work, pending predicates exclude only the same historical states, SQL prefix matching is case-sensitive, anti-joins use exact identities, schema initialization precedes queries, and awaited finalization cannot leave later mutation loops using stale data. Verify instrumentation catches indirect history reads as well as direct wake calls.
