<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/873
**Planned against:** `main` at `8a86bd6505967829aa9d8969252207b9c0a8c6bc`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Replace the operator API's message regexes, message sets and message-specific field-path branch with typed errors emitted at the source and one class-based adapter mapping. Before changing those sources, inventory every current source-to-response classification so the migration preserves intentional HTTP statuses and payloads. Consolidate #889 in the same change: core remains the sole authority for project matching and imported-task fields, and `task.configure` uses the shared domain adapter.

### Guardrails

- Preserve command and receipt schemas, error messages, and response payload shapes. Keep `fieldPaths` attached to the typed source error where the source knows them.
- Imported `title`, `outcome`, and `ready` edits return 403; the `ready` status change from 409 is deliberate. A project mismatch remains 403. Core enforces both rules once.
- Classify each old message match against its source semantics, including false matches such as `Operator delivery only permits issue.comment`; do not preserve an accidental 409 merely because a string happened to match.
- Keep the change bounded to the source-to-response paths currently classified by `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`. Do not mass-convert unrelated invariant or infrastructure errors in the listed modules.
- Routing stale semantics in #872 and targeted lookup adoption in #875 are outside this plan. Do not alter `DomainStaleDispositionError` behavior or lookup strategy.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- Use the existing `DomainConflictError`, `DomainPolicyError`, and `DomainNotFoundError` taxonomy in `src/core/domain.ts`, and add `DomainOperationError` only where a source knows that the effect may be uncertain. Map these categories to 409 `conflict`, policy 403 `forbidden` or 400 `invalid-input` (including source-provided field paths), 404 `not-found`, and 503 `command-outcome-unknown`, respectively. Existing narrow API errors keep their established codes. Unexpected failures retain the 503 unknown-outcome fallback. Treat `Operator delivery only permits issue.comment` as a typed forbidden policy failure, correcting its accidental regex-derived 409 to 403.
- The approved brief explicitly chooses 403 for all three imported provider fields and retains 403 for project mismatch, resolving #889 without reopening a product decision.
- Record the current classifier inputs, producing source/symbol, intended typed category and HTTP code/payload in an implementation checklist before replacing any classifier. Resolve the intended result from the originating operation and existing tests. Keep the example false-positive as a regression case. Only intended differences are permitted; add or retain a regression assertion for every changed status.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainConflictError`, `DomainNotFoundError`, `DomainPolicyError`, `DomainCommands.execute`, `projectMatch`, and imported-task command branches own domain errors, provider-field policy and cross-project enforcement.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `OperatorApi.executeDomain` maps configuration/domain failures; `OperatorApi.execute` handles task and coordination commands and currently contains message-based mappings plus duplicate task-update checks.
- **New:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainOperationError` identifies a source failure whose command outcome may be uncertain; `operator-api.ts` maps it to 503 `command-outcome-unknown` through the shared typed error adapter.
- **Existing:** `src/core/coordination.ts`, `local-review.ts`, `task-review.ts`, `delivery.ts`, and `retained-evidence.ts`; `src/standalone/service.ts`, `delivery.ts`, and `retained-evidence.ts` — sources for the bounded set of failures currently inspected by the API. Convert only those branches identified by the pre-change inventory.
- **Follow:** Existing specialized error classes such as `LocalReviewAnchorRequiredError`, `LocalReviewBatchTooLargeError`, `LocalReviewRecipientUnavailableError`, and `RecoveryRejectedError` for narrow behavior that already has typed API handling.
- **Tests:** `test/operator-api.test.ts`, `test/operator-configuration.test.ts`, `test/domain.test.ts`, `test/coordination.test.ts`, `test/task-comments.test.ts`, and `test/operator-cli-task.test.ts` cover API mapping, repository field paths, domain rules, coordination restrictions, key conflicts/unknown outcomes, and imported task writes.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** One cohesive task, acyclic. The typed taxonomy, originating error sites, API adapter and imported-task rule all converge on `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` and `src/core/domain.ts`; keep them with one owner and integrate together. No slices are safe to implement concurrently.

#### 1. Type source errors and centralize operator classification

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** None.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/domain.ts` (`DomainConflictError`, `DomainPolicyError`, `DomainNotFoundError`, `DomainCommands.execute`, `projectMatch`, imported task updates); the inventoried source branches in `src/core/coordination.ts`, `local-review.ts`, `task-review.ts`, `delivery.ts`, `retained-evidence.ts`, `src/standalone/service.ts`, `delivery.ts`, and `retained-evidence.ts`; `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`executeDomain`, `execute`); tests listed in Implementation context.
**Test:** Extend API-level tests to execute representative commands for each mapped category and assert status, `code`, original public message/payload, and `fieldPaths` where applicable. Use a repository configuration failure to check `repositories` field paths; a domain not-found command/read to check 404; a revision/key conflict and cross-task restriction to check 409; a policy denial to check 403; and an operation whose completion is uncertain to check 503 `command-outcome-unknown`. Exercise all former regex/set/special-case inventory rows, retaining an assertion for each intentional status and including the `Operator delivery only permits issue.comment` false-match. Seed an imported task and submit separate `title`, `outcome`, and `ready` updates plus a mismatched `projectId`; assert each returns 403 and changes no persisted task fields. Verify a local task update still succeeds.
**Implementation:** First record the source-to-response inventory for every branch selected by the current regexes, set membership checks, and repository-verification special case, with its source, current response, intended typed error/response, and covering test. Then emit the corresponding conflict, policy, not-found or operation error at each inventoried source while preserving its message and attaching field paths where known. Route adapter results solely through one error-class/category mapper; remove every `error.message` status decision, message set, regex and repository-verification message branch. In the same pass, make imported `title`/`outcome`/`ready` rejection a core `DomainPolicyError("forbidden", …)` and retain `projectMatch` as the only project check; remove the duplicate API pre-checks and send `task.configure` through `executeDomain`. Keep definite policy failures distinct from operation-uncertain errors so callback timing does not turn an established 400/403/404/409 into 503 or an uncertain result into a definite denial.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build` and `node --test dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-configuration.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/coordination.test.js dist/test/task-comments.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-task.test.js`; expect the build and all selected tests to pass, including the new source/status/payload and imported-task assertions.
**Complete when:** The operator API has no status classification based on `error.message`; inventory rows have typed sources and regression coverage; core alone enforces imported-field/project-match rules; all three imported fields and project mismatch return 403; focused validation passes.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| HTTP status decisions do not depend on `error.message`; source failures are typed and mapped centrally. | 1 | Inventory-backed API regressions and selected `operator-api`, `domain`, `coordination`, and `task-comments` tests. |
| Existing response behavior and payloads are preserved, with each intentional status difference identified and covered. | 1 | Inventory-backed status/code/message/field-path assertions; focused build and test command. |
| Core alone enforces imported provider fields and project match; imported `title`, `outcome`, `ready`, and cross-project updates each return 403. | 1 | Imported-task API regression assertions and `operator-cli-task` tests; unchanged task state after each rejection. |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` against the integrated delivery candidate; expect type checking, lint, format checking, build and the complete automated test suite to pass.

### Review focus

- Check that the source-to-response inventory includes every old classifier arm, including false-positive message matches and the repository field-path special case; verify operation uncertainty remains distinct from typed definite refusal.
- Check `task.configure` has one project/provider-policy enforcement path and the API preserves 403 for all required cases.

content.title: Compute and validate redaction exclusions once per request

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/877
**Planned against:** `main` at `e21abd499cf95f4c35a89942fc577eec19ac2786` (detached clean tracked planning checkout)
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Unrelated changes present
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Capture an immutable exclusion base synchronously before the first await in each operator read attempt. Derive task and dedicated-instruction disclosure variants from that base, sharing the same context through nested reads. Prepare exact-value validation and deduplication once for each resulting immutable list and reuse it across every text field. Keep live identity, workspace, policy and credential checks separate from this reusable work.

The authoritative contract is [#877](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/877), including its accepted Agent brief. Deliver one coherent candidate; the slices below are behavioral checkpoints, not separate PR requirements.

### Guardrails

- Preserve current redacted/null/omitted output, 16000-character operator limits, 64KiB text/value limits, 128-value and 256KiB exclusion-byte bounds, duplicate accounting, exact-value/pattern overlap behavior and dedicated instruction disclosure. Missing, malformed, oversized or uncovered inputs fail closed. Preserve the task-local retained-row, assignment and history-binding bounds.
- No mutable cross-request credential/policy cache. Contexts and their copied lists belong to one read attempt. A fenced instruction retry creates a fresh context; a second change retains the existing unavailable outcome. Necessary live credential/identity/policy reads are not part of the once-only base acquisition metric.
- Prepared-list memoization recognizes only copied, frozen arrays owned by the preparation factory. Arbitrary frozen arrays and legacy mutable arrays receive ordinary fresh validation; mutable array changes cannot reuse stale prepared values. No raw secret values in instrumentation, logs, receipts or evidence.
- Preserve asynchronous fences before disclosure and external effects, session-expiry checks, task/project/workspace identities, retained policy fingerprints, command replay and unknown-effect outcomes. A post-effect receipt uses a fresh disclosure epoch if configuration changed; failing disclosure never retries an external effect or undoes its persisted receipt. This optimization cannot release execution/Stop/recovery holds.
- SQL filtering is #875; workspace path projection is #878; source-gh support and lifetime resolved-token exclusions are #944. No new public schema, persistence migration, sandbox/privacy guarantee, design changes, deployment/cutover, provider writes, paid/model probes or paused native/ChatGPT work.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- Use an explicit request/attempt context, passed to internal helpers, rather than an OperatorApi instance field or async-global cache. Concurrent requests and concurrent task projections must not see each other's lists. Deduplicate task-variant work by the exact task/project, disclosure set and captured-history identity; different history/disclosure variants cannot share a coarser task-only key.
- Capture tagged profile/project instruction revisions once, with the covered revision keys and configuration/credential/path inputs. Dedicated disclosure variants omit only their selected tags from that captured snapshot, avoiding a second global revision traversal. Copy nested inputs rather than retaining mutable domain/configuration objects. Decide bounds before traversing counters, as today.
- Add a preparation factory in conversation-history.ts which owns a copied frozen exclusion array and prepared exact values. A narrow module-private WeakMap associates only those owned arrays with prepared data. Existing readonly-array consumers, retained fingerprints/path checks, boundDetail and isDisclosable keep their interfaces. The WeakMap contains immutable list preparation only; it never resolves credentials or stores request policy/context. Ordinary sanitizeConversationText callers remain compatible.
- Validate the raw supplied count, individual type/character/UTF-8 limits and aggregate bytes before deduplication. Existing OperatorApi exclusions already filters empties and deduplicates before sanitation; preserve that specific assembly behavior too. Current sanitizer sorts text-dependent match spans, not exclusion values. Keep original-text matching, pattern anchors and per-text span sorting/merging; no claim that a span sort can be reused across different text.
- Capture the initial live-fence inputs in the same synchronous section as the base, reusing captured values where feasible. Post-await visibilityToken/referenceFence and task/workspace/session checks remain live. They must fence arbitrary env reference names, Claude file value/problem changes, discovery resolved-gh values and token-set membership, and all relevant configuration revisions. A changed fence rejects stale disclosure rather than updating an old context in place. Existing readWithInstructionFence supplies only its bounded instruction retry.
- The older #944 plan explicitly owns github-source-credential.ts, source-only gh exclusions and removal of the eight-token eviction in gh-credential.ts. It requires lifetime exclusion values even after Clear. When that work is integrated, use its delivered exclusion helper for base and live reference fences, including the lifetime token-set digest when no source/discovery reference remains. Never restore env-suffix handling for a gh source or discard resolved values on Clear. Do not implement #944 here.
- When #878 is integrated, keep its synchronous taskWorkspaceRedactionPaths seam in task derivation, preserve workspace visibility checks, and retarget await barriers to an actual remaining asynchronous seam. Do not restore taskWorkspace/Git work for polling or add an artificial await merely to test this plan.
- Edit gates follow actual admitted file ownership, not every unadmitted plan: operator-api.ts overlaps #886 receipts, #932 recovery and #944 source handling; service/API integration can also overlap #873, #881 and #878. #880/#879 service work matters only if a delivered seam changes. The root confirms the exact admitted base/owner handoff before edits; independent planning remains concurrent.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** src/standalone/operator-api.ts — exclusions gathers all project/profile revisions, control paths, discovery/Claude credentials and each project's GitHub/routing/delivery credentials and repository paths; checks captured task revisions, then awaits taskWorkspace. safe/disclosable/exact repeat sanitizer preparation for each field. visibilityToken, referenceFence, instructionFence, readWithInstructionFence, workspaceSnapshot and requireWorkspaceSnapshot own current fences.
- **Existing:** readProjectOnce and readComposerOptionsOnce compute a general list and a list per task; readTaskListPageOnce and readInbox call taskSummaryRead per task. readTask reuses one array across many fields. readExecutionInputs obtains general and selected-instruction variants separately; readAssignmentHistory re-redacts each completed item.
- **Existing:** retainedEvidencePolicy is repeatedly called for initial and current policies by retained evidence/artifact/local-review paths. sameRetainedPolicy/currentReviewPolicy/assertReviewPolicy compare identities and fingerprints; current-policy checking must not be replaced with cached success.
- **Existing:** src/standalone/conversation-history.ts — sanitizeConversationText/isDisclosable share bounded original-text span redaction; ConversationHistoryStore.readAssignment currently sanitizes each completed row. src/standalone/execution-diagnostics.ts — boundDetail recursively calls the sanitizer for every string leaf. src/standalone/retained-evidence.ts consumes readonly arrays through isDisclosable; these array interfaces remain supported.
- **New:** conversation-history.ts — prepareConversationRedactor and its factory-owned immutable-list association; operator-api.ts — ExclusionReadContext/captureExclusionBase and task/disclosure derivation helpers. Names are planned additions, not existing symbols.
- **Follow:** test/operator-targeted-exclusions.test.ts for capped task-local lookup and unknown/captured identity guards; test/operator-inbox.test.ts for a deferred later-row read invalidating an earlier row; test/operator-retained-evidence.test.ts for post-await exclusion changes; test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts for overlap and capture/read privacy.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic `T1 → T2 → T3`. T1 establishes unchanged prepared redaction. T2 uses that contract to implement the request context and primary projections. T3 completes shared call sites and race/identity evidence. Keep these sequential because T2/T3 share operator-api.ts and T3 depends on T2's context. Use one implementation owner; no concurrent edits to these shared files.

**Shared validation setup:** From the root-supplied clean implementation checkout (`$IMPLEMENTATION_ROOT`), verify `node --version` is v24.21.0 and `npm --version` is 12.2.0, then `npm ci`. The run's temporary PATH is `/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH`; use the pinned equivalent if that run directory no longer exists. Build before direct compiled-test commands. Run existing test fixtures without paid/live provider or model access. If the sandbox concretely blocks fixture localhost/process access, retry only that failed command through approved host execution.

#### 1. Reusable immutable-list redaction with identical output

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Shared setup and admitted-file check.
**Files and symbols:** src/standalone/conversation-history.ts — preparation factory, sanitizer and isDisclosable; new test/conversation-redaction-preparation.test.ts; test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts — existing behavioral regression corpus. ConversationHistoryStore.readAssignment may prepare its supplied current list once per invocation; capture/persistence keeps fresh current exclusion acquisition and its original omission boundary.
**Implementation:** Split bounded list preparation from text matching. The factory returns its immutable owned list and redaction behavior; register only that owned array for the compatible sanitizer path. Invalid preparation remains unavailable. Legacy raw arrays validate anew. Prepare once outside the completed-row loop in readAssignment when relevant; do not compute exclusions for started/delta/omitted-only capture events.
**Test:** Assert exact expected strings for repeated, contained, partially overlapping, adjacent, Unicode, empty and duplicate exclusions plus authorization/Bearer/password/URL patterns. Cover 128/129 raw entries, raw duplicate aggregate bytes around 256KiB, each value's character/UTF-8 boundary, malformed values and 64KiB input text. Prove original input mutation after factory copying cannot change the prepared result, mutable legacy arrays reflect later changes, and arbitrary frozen arrays are not trusted as factory-owned. Use a bounded counting iterable/getter fixture to count actual raw input access during factory preparation; repeated sanitization/disclosability/recursive leaves must not reread or revalidate that list. Each new immutable list still prepares independently. Per-text matching/span ordering remains exercised with different texts, rather than testing a factory-call count alone.
**Validate:** In `$IMPLEMENTATION_ROOT`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/conversation-redaction-preparation.test.js dist/test/s05-conversation-history.test.js`; expect unchanged corpus output and bounds/ownership/preparation checks passing. Run `npm run typecheck` for the compatible exported seam.
**Complete when:** Owned immutable lists reuse preparation while every legacy/privacy boundary retains expected output.

#### 2. One synchronous base for list, project, Inbox and detail projections

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's boundary checks pass; integrate any admitted older operator-api exclusion changes first.
**Files and symbols:** src/standalone/operator-api.ts — exclusions decomposition, request context, safe/disclosable/exact, taskSummary/taskSummaryRead, readProject/readProjectOnce, readTaskListPage/readTaskListPageOnce, readComposerOptions/readComposerOptionsOnce, readInbox and readTask; new test/operator-exclusion-preparation.test.ts; existing test/operator-targeted-exclusions.test.ts, operator-api.test.ts, operator-task-list.test.ts and operator-inbox.test.ts.
**Implementation:** Create the context synchronously before each entry's first await, then pass it through nested projection helpers. Capture global tagged inputs/coverage and initial fence once; derive general and task variants with existing bounds and workspace path seam. Prepare resulting owned lists once and share them for all fields. Promise-sharing for concurrent derivation must be request-local and distinguish captured-history/disclosure variants. Failures do not publish partially prepared lists. Retain final workspace/task/credential fences; readWithInstructionFence allocates a fresh base for each retry and discards the failed attempt.
**Test:** Seed multiple projects/profiles with retained revisions, several tasks and several assignments/dependencies/results. Exercise project, list page, Inbox and detail on the real service/SQLite fixture. Count actual profileRevision/instructionRevision reads, base credential/config acquisition and immutable-list preparation independently from live fence reads. Assert one base traversal per unchanged attempt, one preparation per distinct list, task variants contain their own workspace paths, and field count/task count does not multiply global revision reads. Repeated and simultaneous requests use new identities and changed instructions/credentials are honored. Hold a later task await, change an earlier task/workspace or add an instruction revision, release it, and assert either the documented fresh retry or unavailable response with no stale canary. A second instruction change exhausts the existing retry; all attempts remain isolated. Repeated domain lookup metrics distinguish required live config/reference fences instead of falsely asserting all metadata reads disappear.
**Validate:** In `$IMPLEMENTATION_ROOT`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-exclusion-preparation.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-targeted-exclusions.test.js dist/test/operator-task-list.test.js dist/test/operator-inbox.test.js`; expect output/identity bounds and once-per-attempt metrics passing. Run `npm run typecheck`.
**Complete when:** The four primary response families share the immutable base and preserve stale-response rejection and bounded retry.

#### 3. Consistent context propagation and post-await credential/privacy evidence

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2's primary projection and fence evidence passes. Obtain the actual admitted integration handoff for #944/#878 or screen their absence without waiting for unadmitted plans.
**Files and symbols:** src/standalone/operator-api.ts — all remaining exclusions/sanitizer consumers in the entry-point audit below, instructionExclusions, retainedEvidencePolicy/currentReviewPolicy and command-side disclosure helpers; src/standalone/conversation-history.ts and execution-diagnostics.ts only for prepared-list wiring if needed; test/operator-exclusion-preparation.test.ts, operator-instructions.test.ts, operator-execution-diagnostics.test.ts, operator-retained-evidence.test.ts, operator-task-review.test.ts, operator-workspace-inspection.test.ts, operator-comparisons.test.ts and operator-command-lifecycle.test.ts. Revise docs/SPEC.md's existing read-fence paragraph in place to explain reuse and fresh bounded retry, without changing disclosure guarantees; no ADR is needed for this internal optimization.
**Implementation:** Audit every production call site using `rg -n 'exclusions\(|sanitizeConversationText\(|isDisclosable\(|boundDetail\(' src/standalone/operator-api.ts src/standalone/conversation-history.ts src/standalone/execution-diagnostics.ts`. Carry the same explicit context through each top-level read and nested read that contributes its response. Where retained policy checks currently reacquire inputs, compare the captured immutable base against live policy/identity metadata and task/workspace facts instead of rebuilding global instructions. Never replace a current-policy check with its initial policy object. Keep byte/policy array fingerprints and dedicated variants stable. Commands that can change configuration/effects establish a fresh post-effect receipt context when required; do not carry pre-effect credentials into receipt disclosure.
**Entry-point audit:** workspace/profile/project configuration; composer; task/record pages and question; assignment and dedicated instruction views; execution list/detail/inputs/events; assignment history; review/search/artifact; runtime settings/recovery/options/operation/source observation; retained result/item/anchor, local review draft/list/operation and staging/send/reconciliation; command comment/preview/review receipt disclosure. Workspace directory/preview/comparison callbacks that only validate identity keep their live semantics. Record which families acquire/derive lists and which use identity-only callbacks. Shared browser, advanced operator, CLI and direct API consumers inherit the service behavior; no UI controls change.
**Test:** Use existing deferred seams and fake-gh fixture only. Rotate a configured env value whose name avoids TOKEN/SECRET, change the reference itself, change GitHub/routing/delivery configuration, rotate a Claude file value and change it to unreadable, and add a newly resolved gh token while a response is held. Assert no old prepared context discloses the newly private canary; preserve existing unavailable/conflict/omission outcomes. After #944 integration, include source-only gh with discovery unset, more than eight resolved values, and Clear while held; the lifetime exclusion digest must still fence token-set changes and old values remain redacted. Retained item and local-review reads must reject stale task/project/workspace/session evidence; logout discards results and preserves existing draft/privacy behavior. Conversation and recursive diagnostic reads reuse preparation across fields but still re-redact current secrets. Exercise a successful keyed command followed by a disclosure conflict and replay: exactly one recorded effect/receipt, no resend or hold release. Test parallel requests and failed derivation recovery so a rejected promise/list cannot poison the next request.
**Validate:** In `$IMPLEMENTATION_ROOT`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-exclusion-preparation.test.js dist/test/operator-instructions.test.js dist/test/operator-execution-diagnostics.test.js dist/test/operator-retained-evidence.test.js dist/test/operator-task-review.test.js dist/test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.js dist/test/operator-comparisons.test.js dist/test/operator-command-lifecycle.test.js dist/test/s05-conversation-history.test.js`; expect all race, retained/session, receipt replay and unchanged redaction checks passing. Run `npm run typecheck` and `git diff --check`.
**Complete when:** Every relevant service entry point has documented context ownership and focused evidence, fresh credential/policy checks still fail closed, and the existing shared UI/API/CLI paths remain consistent.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exclusion base acquired once per request attempt, before awaits | T2, T3 | actual revision/input acquisition counters across primary and nested response families; fresh bounded retry identities |
| Validation/deduplication once per immutable list | T1, T2 | counted raw-list access, repeated sanitizer/disclosable/diagnostic use, per-list preparation identities |
| Redaction output and all existing tests unchanged | T1–T3 | expected-string corpus, numeric/malformed bounds and existing redaction suites |
| No policy/credential change during an await exposes text | T2, T3 | deferred env/reference/file/token-set/config/task/workspace/session races |
| Conversation, retained evidence and local review share safe behavior | T3 | completed-row/recursive-field reuse and retained/session/receipt recovery checks |
| No stale cross-request cache or missing task/disclosure coverage | T1–T3 | immutable ownership, mutable legacy revalidation, simultaneous requests, tagged disclosure variants and captured revision guards |

### Final validation

- At the integrated delivery candidate, from `$IMPLEMENTATION_ROOT`, run `npm run check`; expect pinned typecheck, lint, format check, service/web build and complete tests passing. CI uses the same check. Host execution is appropriate only for a concrete identical sandbox localhost/process restriction; retain its failed attempt and exact successful retry evidence.
- Run `git diff --check`, review the final call-site audit and sanitized acquisition/preparation/live-fence counts, and confirm tracked changes stay in the declared scope. No performance ratio, time/token savings or broad privacy qualification claim follows from these counters.
- Require independent integrated review covering request ownership, frozen-list provenance, disclosure variants, credential races and command/retained recovery. Reuse unaffected existing UI/runtime evidence; this internal refactor requires no paid/live-model or installed-service probe.

### Review focus

- Verify all base captures precede the first actual await, nested reads share the correct attempt, and no failed/retried context survives into another request.
- Check lifetime/source-only gh exclusions after #944 integration and path-only polling after #878 integration; preserve their delivered seams rather than reverting older work.
- Inspect how current-policy checks use live inputs after reads/effects, not just successful happy-path preparation counts.
