**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-operate-journey.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-packed.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-http.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-integrated-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-question-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-task-composer.test.js`; expect all pass (the browser suites prove the UI Stop, question and composer paths are unaffected).
**Complete when:** Every acceptance journey passes through the packaged CLI and the shared behaviour matches the UI entry points.

#### 8. Documentation, inventory and evidence record

**Task ID:** `T8`
**Depends on:** `T7`
**Prerequisites:** T7 results.
**Files and symbols:** `README.md` (Operator CLI bullet), `docs/development.md` (Operator CLI: the new commands, flags, effects, answers-file shape, retry and journal rule), `docs/SPEC.md` (Operator CLI section), `docs/design/operator-cli.md` (capability names, `task.stop`/`task.resume` contract and receipts, effect vocabulary, unresolved-only journal rule, inbox parameters, `add-dependency` spelling, that `operation get` does not cover these types), `docs/acceptance.md` (CLI04 slice-evidence pointer; scenarios stay **Unproved** until #901), new `docs/evidence/issue-898-cli5-<run date>.md`, `test/operator-cli-inventory.test.ts` documented list.
**Implementation:** State current behaviour in place with no dated sections, distinguishing implemented from planned (CLI4, CLI6, CLI7 and CLI8 stay planned). No ADR change: ADR-1010 already covers the operator CLI, and the new commands and the unresolved-key rule are recorded in the design document. The evidence record names the candidate SHA, environment (Node, npm, Playwright) and the covered operations with denial, revision and retry cases, and the entry-point table: tasks, dependencies, messages, questions, approvals (React composer, task workspace, inbox and the retained `/coordination` and `/runtime/control` pages use the same commands or hold logic); Stop and Resume (React Stop dialog and retained forms use the keyless methods; the CLI uses receipted commands; **gap:** the React UI has no Resume control and no UI uses the new commands); `inbox`, `question get`, `approval get` (CLI and API only; the web UI reads the same projections). Reverse paths and irreversible actions as in Planning decisions. Limits: no `operation get` for these types, no second machine or private transport, no live runtime, Stop is best-effort, the inbox is a full scan (#875), unresolved journal keys persist until retried.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Docs and evidence match behaviour, the entry-point table and gaps are recorded, and no scenario is marked passed.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Task creation, configuration and dependency changes keep imported-provider ownership, readiness and admission rules | 4 | T4 create, configure and dependency checks, including the imported-task refusals and admission-aware effect |
| Addressed messages and operator follow-ups with completed-lead rules; recipient and queue effect shown; no mention-based conversation or rerun | 4 | T4 message and follow-up checks |
| Attention inbox and every supported question form, answer validation and stale handling; explicit answers, never a recommendation | 3, 5 | T3 inbox filters; T5 inbox, question get and answer checks |
| Approve or deny only the exact action, target, revision and material; redaction and withholding preserved; no inferred approval | 5 | T5 approval checks |
| Stop and Resume as authenticated machine commands; Stop best-effort; Resume clears only operator Stop and keeps other holds | 1, 2, 6 | T2 receipt, hold and HTTP checks; T6 CLI checks |
| Stable receipts and expected revisions; saved, queued, cancellation-requested results and unknown outcomes reported accurately | 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 | T1 journal and matcher checks; T2 replay and atomicity; T4–T6 retry and effect checks |
| Journeys, structured forms, stale, held and done cases, read-only denial, replay and UI entry-point parity | 7 | T7 journeys, denial table, replay and parity checks plus the browser suites |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root on Node 24.21.0 (`~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH`, per `.node-version`), after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate; expect typecheck (including `web/`), lint, format, build and the full suite to pass, including the Chromium and WebKit suites. Playwright Chromium and WebKit are cached on this host; CI pins npm 12.2.0 and runs Node 26 (`check`, `check-node-26`), and local npm may differ (11.19.0 at planning time), so CI on the pull request is authoritative for the pinned toolchain.
- A timing test that fails alone under host load (one `codex-runtime.test.ts` case failed that way once during CLI1) is rerun once by file and recorded; do not edit it unless this change caused the failure.
- Baseline at the planned SHA (`main` at `f0a43304`, CI green on both Node jobs): `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run build:service` passed; 20/20 tests passed over `operator-cli`, `-write`, `-http`, `-inventory`, `-adopt` and `operator-operations`, and 102/102 over `operator-runtime`, `supervisor`, `operator-follow-up`, `operator-inbox`, `runtime-question-service`, `operator-api`, `domain`, `operator-contracts`, `operator-cli-write`, `operator-cli-adopt` and `operator-cli-config-journey`. The full check was not rerun at planning; the last recorded full result is in `docs/evidence/issue-896-cli3-2026-10-11.md`. Record any drift if `main` moves.
- No live Codex or Claude runtime, second machine, Keychain or new UI layout is needed: Stop observation uses the fixture runtime and every journey is deterministic. Missing live or private-remote evidence stays **Unproved** for #901.

### Review focus

- Stop and Resume: the receipt, hold change and replay are one transaction; Resume never clears a hold other than the operator Stop; a replayed Stop is never reported as in effect when it is not; the unresolved-only journal rule is applied to every CLI5 write.
- Approvals send only what the service disclosed and the caller's revision and hash bound; withheld material is never approvable; no answer or decision is inferred or defaulted.
- Server authority: every pre-read gate is also enforced by the service and tested over direct HTTP; read-only denial leaves no state change.
- Each state-changing control has its counterpart, and the irreversible ones (create, message, follow-up, answer, decision) are flagged in help and docs.

### Allowed deviations

- Verb and flag spellings beyond the fixed shapes (`task create|configure|message|follow-up|stop|resume`, `inbox list`, `question get|answer`, `approval get|decide`), the `add-dependency` and `remove-dependency` spellings, receipt field names of the two task-control kinds, internal module names, human wording and help text may differ when docs, help and tests agree.

### Re-plan triggers

- Stop or Resume cannot be recorded atomically with the hold change in `ExecutionState`, or recording a receipt requires altering the hold, supervisor or scheduler contract.
- An existing command (`task.create`, `task.configure`, `dependency.*`, `message`, `question.*`, `approval.decide`) cannot be driven from the CLI without changing its schema, hash or receipt.
- A new route, coverage gap code, exit code or web layout is needed, or exact approval material cannot be sent without relaxing redaction or withholding.

content.title: CLI7: Capture and inspect bounded execution diagnostics

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/900
**Planned against:** `main` at `eb03ca244167d2caeacffafff7adb44fc4a3143d`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Deliver CLI7 on the CLI1/CLI2 seams (`src/cli/*`, bearer auth, the fail-closed `operatorRouteAuthority` table, capability negotiation, the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope, exit codes and opaque cursors). Implementation branch: `cb/900-execution-diagnostics`, from `main` at or after the planned SHA. One PR, nine observable slices.

1. **Store (T1).** New `src/standalone/execution-diagnostics.ts`: additive SQLite tables for execution capture identity, bounded sanitised payload items, coalesced gap rows and a usage counter; fixed 64 KiB item and 16 MiB execution bounds, configurable age (30 days) and installation cap (1 GiB), age-then-oldest eviction, keyset reads by a stable sequence. Writes are best-effort and never throw into execution. Retention lands with the store, before any capture exists (T4), so no payload is ever stored unbounded.
2. **Control (T2).** Optional `diagnosticCapture: "enhanced" | "baseline"` on the existing `project.configure` command; default enhanced.
3. **Adapter (T3).** Optional `Runtime.onDiagnosticEvent` and `Runtime.observedSettings`, implemented by `CodexRuntime` for tool-like items, turn status and thread settings. No message text, deltas or reasoning content.
4. **Service capture (T4).** Supplied-input segments recorded before `startTurn`, observed settings, runtime events, coordination tool calls and service events, bound by the existing work, task, assignment, thread and turn identities; retention timer; env-configured limits.
5. **Reads (T5).** Four read-authority routes and capabilities `execution.read` and `diagnostics.read`.
6. **CLI (T6, T7).** `execution list|get|inputs [--compare-current]` and `logs` with filters, resumable cursors, `--follow` and `--output jsonl`.
7. **Bounded live evidence (T8)** and **docs, inventory and evidence record (T9).**

Capture never gates execution: no await is added to admission, no safety table is read for decisions or written, and a capture, storage or pruning failure becomes an explicit gap.

### Guardrails

- **Unchanged contracts:** conversation history capture, store and reads (`conversation-history.ts` is imported only for `sanitizeConversationText`; #874 owns its batching); the three instruction views and their provenance literal `{source:"retained-revision-records", reconstructed:true, submittedPrompt:"not-captured"}` (they describe a reconstruction, so it stays true); `execution_*` and `runtime_terminal_evidence` tables, recovery receipts, retained result and review evidence, command receipts and instruction revisions (T1 proves with a digest of every non-diagnostic table that store writes and prunes never change them; T4 compares execution outcomes with a control run); admission, holds, supervisor and recovery, #789 background-failure reporting and #790 runtime-retention guarantees; every existing command schema and persisted request hash (T2 golden); browser Origin/CSRF and cookie sessions; the `operatorRouteAuthority` fail-closed table; envelope and exit-code meanings (extended, not changed); all CLI1 and CLI2 commands and output; `src/cli` imports no SQLite and no `src/standalone` module except `operator-hidden-password.js` (existing test).
- **Diagnostic invariants:** best-effort. A diagnostic write, prune, read or cursor failure never throws into a runtime listener, the scheduler, `executeAdmitted` or the supervisor, never holds, retries, completes or releases anything, and is never evidence of success. No per-token, delta or output-stream records. Reasoning and echoed user-message content are never collected, and absent tool events are never evidence that no tool ran. Supplied inputs are never described as the runtime's effective prompt.
- **Privacy:** sanitise string leaves with the existing exclusions and patterns before persistence (never the serialised JSON, whose escaping defeats exact-value matching), re-sanitise with current exclusions on every read, and fail closed to `omitted/redaction-unavailable` when exclusions are unavailable. Only `execution inputs` leaves the bound profile and project instruction text unredacted; `logs`, `execution list|get` and every runtime, tool and service payload redact all instruction text. No unredacted switch, export or credential-file output.
- **Out of scope:** CLI writes, request journal and `operation` (#896–#899), qualification (#901); Claude events and settings (#825/#826; `ClaudeRuntime` may later implement the two optional members); any web UI (`design/design.pen` has no frame for diagnostics or a capture control; if a task appears to need a layout, report a blocker instead of inventing one); process stderr and background-failure capture (#789); ChatGPT and native Codex (#726/#734 paused); remote workers (#778).
- **(a) Plan-seam mismatch: one diagnosis plus two repair cycles in total**, only when a factual assumption in this plan about the repository or an approved seam is wrong. Examples: `item/*` notifications cannot be projected from `CodexRuntime` without changing its terminal or safety handling; `executionPrompt` cannot be split into parts without changing the submitted bytes; a `project.configure` field cannot be added without changing existing hashes or receipts; a named route, symbol or call flow behaves differently. After the diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, stop and report for a replan.
- **(b) Ordinary in-scope repairs: owner repairs, no allowance, they do not consume (a):** implementation bugs, type, lint and format errors, fixture and test setup, equivalent paths or names, documentation and evidence text, rebase conflicts with #825, #826 or #896, and CI or flaky-test retries (including Node 26 and npm 12.2.0 lockfile or runner fixes). Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes, or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews; no integration amendment is needed unless a published integration decision changes.

### Planning decisions

- **Execution identity.** The existing `workId` (`turn_requests.workId`, with `requestSequence`) names an execution; no second run id. Capture covers task-bound assignment executions; direct `run` executions keep baseline behaviour. Rows bind taskId, projectId, assignmentId, assignmentVersion, instructionsRevision, profileRevision, conversationRevision, harness, and threadId/turnId once bound. Listing pages `turn_requests` by task, assignment or project (keyset on `sequence`) with per-row primary-key lookups (`ExecutionState.byWorkId`, `taskBinding`, `recoveryIdentity`), so it never scans history (#875 stays separate). An execution with no capture row reads `not-captured`.
- **Store shape.** `diagnostic_executions` (PK `workId`; identity; `mode`; `eventSource` supported|unsupported; `finishedAt`; `payloadBytes`), `diagnostic_items` (`sequence` AUTOINCREMENT is the cursor; `workId`, `kind` input|setting|runtime|tool|service, `name`, `severity`, `itemId`, `state` available|omitted, `reason`, `payload`, `payloadBytes`, `originalBytes`, `createdAt`; indexes on `(workId, sequence)` and `createdAt`), `diagnostic_gaps` (PK `(workId, code)`: `count`, `bytes`, `firstAt`, `lastAt`, `maxPrunedSequence`), singleton `diagnostic_usage(totalBytes)`. Counters change in the same transaction as the insert or delete. Pruning deletes only `diagnostic_items` rows and upserts a coalesced `expired` or `evicted` gap, so execution and gap metadata persist. Capture gap codes: `capture-baseline`, `capture-failed`, `capture-interrupted`, `input-failed`, `size-limit`, `redaction-unavailable`, `execution-limit`, `item-limit`, `expired`, `evicted`, `late-event`, `early-buffer-limit`, `unsupported-event`.
- **Bounds.** 64 KiB is the UTF-8 size of the serialised sanitised payload. A field over its cap (command 4 KiB, any other string leaf 48 KiB, input segment 64 KiB raw) is replaced whole by `{omitted:"size-limit",bytes:N}` and never cut, because a cut can leave part of a redacted value; an item still over 64 KiB becomes `state: omitted/size-limit`. Per execution: 16 MiB and 8192 rows, beyond which only a coalesced `execution-limit` or `item-limit` gap row is written. The installation cap evicts the lowest sequences in 256-row batches after an insert crosses it and at each prune; age expiry deletes rows with `createdAt` strictly older than the window; batches yield to the event loop. Defaults are constants; age and cap come from `ENSEMBLE_DIAGNOSTIC_RETENTION_DAYS` (1–365) and `ENSEMBLE_DIAGNOSTIC_STORAGE_MIB` (16–1048576), parsed in `src/standalone/cli.ts`; invalid values fail startup. The quota bounds payload text only, not the database, WAL or backups.
- **Supplied inputs.** `executionPrompt` becomes `executionPromptParts(request)`, the same text split into `request`, `role`, `review-references`, `project-instructions` and `profile-instructions` (with revision numbers), and `executionPrompt` joins them with the unchanged separator, so captured segments and submitted bytes cannot drift. Before `startTurn` the service records each segment plus `submitted: {bytes, sha256}` of the exact string. Write-time exclusions follow `ConversationHistoryCapture`: the capture-start list plus the current list. Instruction segments use those lists with the bound and current instruction texts of the execution's own profile and project removed, so only those texts stay readable while credentials, patterns, control and workspace paths stay redacted; every other segment and payload keeps the full lists. A failure is an `input-failed` gap and the turn proceeds. The view labels itself a captured submission of Ensemble-supplied inputs; a labelled `reconstructed` block appears only when no captured instruction segment exists. `assignment instructions` is unchanged and points to `execution inputs` through the `workId` it already returns.
- **Settings.** One `setting` item of named entries with a source: `service-admitted` (harness, sandbox, approval and account type from the intent, and the profile's configured runtime from `domain.profileRuntime`), `runtime-reported` (`model`, `modelProvider`, `reasoningEffort`, `serviceTier` from the `thread/start` response) or `unknown`. `CodexRuntime` keeps its own bounded map (128 threads) because `threadSnapshots.settings` is retained only when `nativeExecutable` is set, which requires the qualified `codex-cli 0.159.0` build, and this host runs `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- **Runtime events.** `CodexRuntime.projectDiagnosticEvent` (beside `projectConversationEvent`, inside try/catch) emits normalised events: `commandExecution` started/completed (command, cwd, status, exitCode, aggregatedOutput), other tool-like types (`fileChange`, `mcpToolCall`, `dynamicToolCall`, `webSearch`) and every other type including `reasoning` as type, id and status only, and `turn/completed` status. `agentMessage` (conversation history) and `userMessage` are not emitted. Only `commandExecution` fields are evidenced (S01 traces); unknown shapes degrade to type-only and T8 records what a live turn shows. Coordination tool calls are captured in the service by wrapping the `onToolCall` listener (name, bounded arguments, success, bounded result text); the response is returned unchanged.
- **Service events.** A closed set: `input-captured`, `thread-bound`, `turn-bound`, `terminal-observed`, `execution-settled` (final intent state and sanitised reason), `unexpected-request` and `terminal-anomaly` (method or reason, for matched active work). "Filtered service diagnostics" means these execution-bound records.
- **Binding and buffering.** A per-thread `ExecutionDiagnosticsCapture` (keyed by `runtimeKey(harness, threadId)` like conversation captures) buffers events (at most 256 items and 1 MiB) until `startTurn` returns and the turn binds, then persists only the exact turn in one transaction. Wrong-turn events are dropped, overflow adds `early-buffer-limit`, and a finished capture stays registered (closed, at most 128 per service, oldest dropped) so events after `finish` add a coalesced `late-event` gap. Baseline-mode projects write the execution row and a `capture-baseline` gap and subscribe to nothing; a runtime without `onDiagnosticEvent` records `eventSource: unsupported`. At start, `closeOpen()` marks rows lacking `finishedAt` interrupted (`capture-interrupted`).
- **Control.** `diagnosticCapture` is an optional member of the operator and domain `project.configure` variants (absent = unchanged) stored in new table `project_diagnostic_capture(projectId, mode)`; no row means `enhanced`. It uses the existing `expectedVersion` check and receipt (receipt unchanged), is read through `GET /projects/:id/configuration` and `project get`, applies to executions admitted afterwards and erases nothing, and both values are settable, so it is reversible. It is not a new command, so #896's receipt and golden-hash work is untouched. The CLI write path belongs to #896's `project prepare` (see Overlap).
- **Reads and gaps.** Four GET routes, all `read`. Capture vocabulary maps onto the closed CLI coverage set without new codes: omitted or size-limited items → `item-omitted`; sanitised text → `content-redacted`; failed redaction → `redaction-unavailable`; expired, evicted, failed, interrupted, late and limit gaps → `evidence-gap`; baseline or not-captured → `evidence-unavailable`; paging → `more-pages` and `limit-capped`. Event pages stop at 200 items or 1 MiB of payload (at least one item). Cursors are the global sequence: `after` above the sequence high-water mark is a 409 (`cursor-stale`); `after` below a pruned sequence yields an explicit `expired` or `evicted` gap with counts.
- **Following.** The CLI polls the events route every `--interval` (1–30 s, default 2) with one page buffered, up to `--max-duration` (default 900 s, maximum 86400). Each poll is a fresh bearer request, so expiry or revocation ends the follow with exit 3. It ends when the execution is finished and drained, at the duration bound, or on SIGINT, and prints the resume cursor. `--output jsonl` (logs only) writes one `ensemble.cli/v1` record per line: `item`, `gap`, `end` or `error`. `logs --cursor` realises the design's representative `--after CURSOR`, because `--after` and `--before` already filter by time in CLI2.
- **Live evidence.** AC7 requires bounded real-runtime evidence; T8 runs one actual Codex journey (one task, one turn start) through the real service and the packaged CLI and records which surfaces appeared and which did not. A surface the run cannot show stays Unproved. Existing S01 traces show only `commandExecution`, `reasoning`, `userMessage` and `agentMessage` items.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `start()` builds `ConversationHistoryStore` (L439), timers (L801) and tear-down (L821, L864, L1200, L1277); `attachRuntime` (L904) wires runtime listeners and `handleToolCall` (L2710); `executeAdmitted` (L3952) binds the thread, creates the conversation capture (L4051), calls `runtime.startTurn(threadId, workspace, this.executionPrompt(request))` (L4060), binds the turn, waits, finishes the capture and settles; `executionPrompt` (L3570) joins `request.prompt`, role, review references and the bound project and profile instruction text; `conversationExclusions` (L4445) and `conversationExclusionsForAssignment` (L4482).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/codex.ts` — `Runtime` (L482), `RuntimeToolCall` (L215), `RuntimeConversationEvent` (L228), `startThread` (L1576), `startTurn` (L1667), `projectConversationEvent` (L2017). `src/standalone/conversation-history.ts` — `sanitizeConversationText`, `ConversationHistoryCapture` (bind, buffer, discard) and the "additive diagnostic storage" store. `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` `SchedulerStore` (`turn_requests`) and `src/standalone/state.ts` `ExecutionState`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `exclusions` (L427), `safe`, `instructionExclusions`, `readWithInstructionFence`, `readAssignmentInstructions`, `readProjectConfiguration` (L3647); `operator-web.ts` `read` and `knownApi`; `operator-credentials.ts` `operatorRouteAuthority`; `src/operator/contracts.ts` `cliCapabilities` (L2724), `projectConfigurationSchema` (L2231), operator `project.configure` variant (L1846); `src/core/domain.ts` `project.configure` (schema L75, apply L1530), `migrate`, `commandHash`.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/main.ts` (`run`, `EXIT`, `USAGE`, `parseArgs`), `src/cli/browse.ts` (`browseOutput`, `pageLimit`, `cursorQuery`, `decodeCursor`, `readWithCursor`, `COVERAGE_GAPS`), `src/cli/browse-assignment.ts` (command exemplars), `src/cli/commands.ts`, `src/cli/types.ts` (`Values`, `CliDeps`).
- **Tests and fixtures:** `test/fixtures/operator-cli.ts` `startCliService` (real service, bearer, session; `s.f.service`, `s.f.seedPersistedState`), `test/fixtures/cli-harness.ts` (`harness`, `fakeServer`), `test/fixtures/instruction-history.ts` `seedInstructionHistory`, `test/fixtures/database-digest.ts`, `test/fixtures/retained-evidence.ts` `captureNativeResult`, the `HistoryRuntime` fake in `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts`, the scripted app-server child in `test/codex-runtime.test.ts`, `test/operator-cli.test.ts` (back-dated `operatorCredentials().issue` for expiry, `revoke`).
- **New:** `src/standalone/execution-diagnostics.ts` (`ExecutionDiagnosticsStore`, `ExecutionDiagnosticsCapture`, `diagnosticLimitsFromEnv`, `DiagnosticCursorError`); `RuntimeDiagnosticEvent` and `RuntimeObservedSettings` in `codex.ts`; `DomainStore.diagnosticCaptureMode`; `StandaloneService.executionDiagnostics()`; `OperatorApi.readExecutionList|readExecution|readExecutionInputs|readExecutionEvents`; `src/cli/browse-execution.ts`, `src/cli/logs-follow.ts`; `test/cli7/live-diagnostics.mjs`.
- **Follow:** `ConversationHistoryCapture` for bind and buffer semantics; `readAssignmentInstructions` for the disclosing projection and fence; `browse-assignment.ts` `assignmentHistory` for cursors and `browseOutput`; `test/wi03/live-turn-capture.mjs` and `test/s04d/live-operator.mjs` for guarded live harnesses.
- **Overlap (record in the delivery record, rebase mechanically; no task here waits on another issue):**
  - **#825** (implementing): `codex.ts` `Runtime` (adds optional `startTurn` settings argument; ours adds two optional members beside it); `service.ts` `executeAdmitted`'s `startTurn` call (it adds the settings argument; ours hoists the prompt to a local and keeps `threadId, workspace, prompt` first), `attachRuntime` (ours adds one listener and wraps `onToolCall`), `start()` (it edits spawn environment near L640–680; ours adds the store beside L439), `conversationExclusionsForAssignment` (it adds the resolved token; ours calls it unmodified and filters the execution's own instruction texts afterwards, so the token is excluded from diagnostics automatically); `domain.ts` (`claude_runtime_credentials` and `claude-token.configure` beside our `project_diagnostic_capture` and `project.configure` field). Ours never touches `recordTurnProcess`, `RuntimeSafetyPort`, `execution_recovery_identities` or `claude.ts`. `ClaudeRuntime` lacks the two members, so its reads show `runtimeEvents: unsupported` and service-admitted settings only.
  - **#826** (Ready, plan https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/826#issuecomment-6112128888): `contracts.ts` (`workspaceSchema.harnesses`, `generation.failure`, `claude-token.configure`; ours new execution schemas, capability names, the `project.configure` and `projectConfigurationSchema` field), `operator-api.ts` (`readWorkspace`, the `readTask` mapping of `executionGeneration`, `exclusions()` gaining the Claude reference and value, which our reads inherit; ours new read methods and `readProjectConfiguration`), `operator-web.ts` and `operator-credentials.ts` route lists, `test/operator-cli-http.test.ts` and `test/operator-cli-inventory.test.ts` pinned lists. Ours never reads or writes `executionGeneration.failure`. No web file is touched.
  - **#896** (Ready, plan https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/896#issuecomment-6112394721): `contracts.ts`, `operator-api.ts` (it extracts receipt building from `execute` into `operator-receipts.ts`; ours does not edit `execute`), `operator-web.ts`, `operator-credentials.ts`, `domain.ts` (`capacity.configure` guard and `recordedResult`; ours the `project.configure` field and table), `cliCapabilities` (it appends `configuration.write`, `operation.read`, `capacity.read`, `configuration.impact`; ours appends `execution.read`, `diagnostics.read`; the pinned list needs a mechanical merge in either order), `src/cli/main.ts` (`parseArgs`, `USAGE`, dispatch), `src/cli/types.ts` `Values`, `src/cli/commands.ts`, `src/cli/browse-workspace.ts` (its `capacity get`; ours one `project get` line), docs. Its T1 golden hashes include `project.configure` (`5f3ea446…`); ours must leave it unchanged. We never touch `ServiceClient` writes, `requests.jsonl` or `operation get`. `diagnosticCapture` is not in its `project prepare` flags; adding `--diagnostic-capture` there is one optional pass-through, recommended to its owner or CLI8, not done here.
  - **#874, #875, #877:** reuse, do not absorb. We import only `sanitizeConversationText`, use primary-key reads and call the existing exclusions helpers; adopt #877's prepared redactor if it has merged. Open PRs #845 and #909 touch CI and macOS scripts only.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1, T2 and T3 are roots; T4 depends on T1, T2, T3; T5 on T2, T4; T6 on T5; T7 on T6; T8 on T7; T9 on T8. The graph is acyclic and every dependency names a declared task. T1 (new module), T2 (`domain.ts`, `contracts.ts`, `operator-api.ts`, CLI `project get`) and T3 (`codex.ts`) share no files and may run concurrently. T4 edits `service.ts` and needs the T1 store, T2 mode read and T3 members. T2, T5 and T6 share `contracts.ts`, `operator-api.ts` and the inventory and HTTP tests, so they run in order; T4–T9 are otherwise sequential.

#### 1. Diagnostic store, bounds, redaction and retention

**Task ID:** `T1`

| Compact and coalesced gaps and all safety records preserved; capture, storage or pruning failure never establishes success or changes admission, holds or recovery; quota scope and backup limits explained | 1, 4, 9 | T1 and T4 digests and failure isolation; T9 documentation |
| Oversized, absent, late events, redaction, storage failure, quota, restart, cursor gaps, bounded buffering and revocation tested; bounded real-runtime evidence with unsupported observations stated | 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 | Named checks in each slice; T8 live record |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root on Node 24.21.0 (`~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH`, per `.node-version`), after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate; expect typecheck, lint, format, build and the full suite to pass, including the Chromium and WebKit suites. Playwright browsers are cached; CI pins npm 12.2.0 and runs Node 26, and local npm may differ (11.19.0 at planning time), so CI on the pull request is authoritative for the pinned toolchain.
- A browser-diagnostics test was observed flaky on Node 26. If it alone fails in an unrelated way, rerun its file once and record the run; do not edit it unless this change caused the failure.
- Baseline at the planned SHA: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build:service` passed, and 41/41 tests passed across the CLI, credential, instruction, conversation-history and capture-observer suites. Record any drift if `main` moves.
- T8 is the only task that needs a live runtime (run once, after `npm run build`, before the final check); no Claude runtime, second machine, Keychain or new UI layout is needed.

### Review focus

- A diagnostic write, prune or read can never throw into execution control, add an await to admission, or touch a safety table; failure paths are tested against a control run.
- Redaction is applied to string leaves, before persistence and at every read; instruction text is unredacted only in `execution inputs`; oversize is omission, never a cut.
- Captured segments equal the submitted bytes by construction, and no label calls them the effective prompt.
- Cursor and prune semantics never imply completeness; every gap maps to the closed coverage set.
- Each state-changing control has its counterpart (baseline and enhanced) and the irreversible expiry is documented.

### Allowed deviations

- Flag spellings beyond the fixed shapes (`execution list|get|inputs`, `logs --execution`), internal module and file names, payload field names inside `detail`, event `name` strings and exact gap wording may differ when help text, docs and tests agree.

### Re-plan triggers

- Projecting `item/*` events or splitting the prompt requires changing terminal, safety, admission or the submitted bytes.
- The capture control cannot be a `project.configure` field without changing existing hashes or receipts, or needs an `ALTER` of an existing table.
- A new CLI coverage gap code, exit code or web layout is needed, or the live run shows that the inputs cannot be captured before `startTurn`.

content.title: CLI8: Qualify the external-agent operator journey

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/901
**Planned against:** `main` at `a873153d48d957b4956589d659e0702230300cb4`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

CLI8 is a qualification slice, not a feature slice. Build one attributable inventory that covers every operation in the ten-area command inventory and CLI01–CLI06. Renew still-valid CLI1–CLI7 slice evidence by rerunning each slice's focused suites at the CLI8 candidate. Add one assembled journey harness, `test/cli8/live-journey.mjs`. Its deterministic fixture mode runs in CI. Its explicit `--live` mode runs a bounded Codex journey through the packed `ensemble` executable, installed outside the checkout on the host. A separate phase repeats the investigation from a second trusted machine over private HTTPS when Chris grants that access. Then record dispositions honestly (Passed, Bounded or Unproved), update the operator guidance and leave every missing obligation Unproved.

### Guardrails

- No production deployment or cutover, paid resource, public endpoint, Tailscale Funnel, ChatGPT connection, remote-worker setup or Claude run. The live journey uses only the existing ChatGPT.app Codex launcher login, as CLI7 did. Do not read `~/.env` or any operator credential.
- Do not add CLI commands, flags, routes or receipts to pass this ticket. When the inventory finds a missing operation, record it as Unproved with its concrete gap. Repairs are limited to defects in existing promised behaviour that the qualification exposes. Each such repair needs a focused regression test. A repair that would change the accepted contract stops for review.
- Preserve action policy, execution holds, the documented recovery boundary and the deferred-integration boundary (ADR-1006). Diagnostics must never release a hold or establish success. Remote clients get no service administration.
- **Live-turn budget:** each host run allows at most 2 model turns: the failing turn and the post-correction turn. A start-turn guard rejects any other `startTurn` before it reaches Codex. The ticket allows at most 2 host runs (4 model turns): the first run plus one rerun after a repair. The remote phase allows 0 model turns. Any further live run needs a new grant.
- **Second machine and private HTTPS:** do not configure Tailscale Serve, connect to, copy to or execute on another machine without Chris's explicit grant. The grant must name the peer, the execution channel and the temporary Serve route. Follow the precedent in `docs/evidence/s04d-operator-2026-09-30.md`. Read back and remove every Serve route, and confirm no Serve config remains. Never relabel a same-host, TLS-proxy or loopback run as second-machine evidence.
- **Cleanup:** use unique `cli8-<uuid>` connection names, a temporary `ENSEMBLE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` and owner-only temporary roots. Revoke every issued credential, remove the Keychain items and verify their absence, stop the service and verify App Server exit by process identity, and remove the fixtures. Provider-side Codex thread records may remain and are recorded as a limit.
- **Repair classes:**
  - (a) An approved-plan seam or repository assumption turns out to be wrong. Examples: the H1 continuation behaviour, a harness seam that does not exist, or the packed install not working outside the checkout. This allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Then stop with the evidence.
  - (b) Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the owner. They do not use that allowance. Record each one briefly in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence.
  - Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for a material contract or design change, or when a grant or budget is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Second machine availability (read-only preflight, 2026-10-12):**
  - Tailscale is installed and running. The tailnet has a cert domain and MagicDNS.
  - Two macOS peers are online: `hermes` and "Chris's MacBook Air". Linux service nodes are also online.
  - `~/.ssh/config` has no alias for either Mac.
  - Remote execution access, Node ≥ 24 on a peer and a Serve grant are not evidenced.
  - In 2026-09, automatic review rejected exposing a fixture to the tailnet with Serve until Chris explicitly authorised it (s04d record).
  - So T4 is isolated behind an explicit grant. It runs a macOS peer with `--token-file`, because the Keychain is unreliable over a non-GUI session and the CLI has no plaintext fallback. If T4 cannot run, the remote and private-HTTPS obligations stay Unproved and are not weakened.
- **The failed task is a result-level failure caused by a deliberate instruction defect**, not a runtime fault:
  - Profile v1 omits the `CLI8_REQUIRED_PHRASE: <word>` line.
  - The task outcome tells the lead to run one shell command, `printenv ENSEMBLE_MANAGED_ASSIGNMENT || echo unset`. The lead then reports `FAIL missing-required-phrase` through `ensemble_report_result` when the phrase is absent, or `PASS <word>` when it is present.
  - This yields live tool activity (CLI7 observed none live) and a correction that is visibly attributable.
  - It also settles the CLI1/CLI2 limit "propagation of `ENSEMBLE_MANAGED_ASSIGNMENT` into Codex tool shells" from the captured command output.
- **The external agent is a scripted client** driving the installed binary. The record labels it a scripted external client, not autonomous model-driven diagnosis.
- **Credential sources:** the harness issues credentials through the session-only credential endpoints the Settings UI uses, with cookie and CSRF. UI-rendered provisioning (create, one-time reveal, list, rotate before revoke, revoke with readback) is qualified by renewing CLI1's Chromium suite `test/operator-cli-credentials-browser.test.ts` at the candidate. Pre-seeded `operatorCredentials().issue()` tokens are not used in the journey.
- **Evidence reuse rule:** slice evidence is still valid only when its focused suites pass at the CLI8 candidate. These suites were run as the planning baseline at `a873153d`: 45 files, 180/180 passed (list in T1). Later merges touched the relevant surfaces: #925 targeted reads, #928 harness config/route authority, #930 runtime naming, #920 git environment and #929 recovery. The CLI7 live record (`06c12130`) predates #928/#930, so CLI8's live run supersedes it as live evidence. The CLI7 record is kept as history.
- **Known gaps settled as Unproved, not implemented:**
  - The `project prepare` CLI write for `diagnosticCapture` is listed in the CLI7 record as a "#896 follow-up or CLI8". The issue forbids new commands, so it is recorded as missing project-configuration coverage.
  - The design excludes these from the CLI. They are recorded as out of scope, not missing: installation-wide source refresh, `source.review`, handback settlement, the keyless bound-turn recovery, React adoption, Resume and recovery controls, and `operation get` for task, attention, delivery and placement receipts.
- **H1 (bounded proof in T2):** after a lead turn ends having reported a result, no further turn is admitted until the operator acts. Then `assignment apply-current` followed by `task follow-up`, or `task message` if the lead is not `completed`, admits exactly one turn bound to the adopted revisions.
  - CLI7's live run saw an unrequested second admission after a turn that reported no result, so this must hold before any live turn.
  - T2's fixture mode decides which command is used. If neither keeps the turn count at 2, that is a class (a) mismatch and T3 does not start.
- **Inventory guard:** a machine-readable inventory plus a guard test is the mechanism that stops a representative journey from qualifying omitted commands. The guard test checks it against the CLI's live command registry.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:**
  - `src/cli/commands.ts`: `browseCommands` and `writeCommands` are the CLI command registry. `auth login|status|logout` and `connection list|use|remove` live in `src/cli/main.ts`.
  - `src/cli/main.ts` login: Keychain storage needs a TTY on stdin and stderr. Otherwise `--token-file`. Non-darwin without a token file gives `credential-store-unavailable`.
  - `src/cli/connections.ts`: config directory `ENSEMBLE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR`. Keychain service `ensemble-cli`, account is the connection name.
- **Existing (tests and harnesses):**
  - `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts` `installPacked`: `npm pack`, then offline `npm ci` from a derived lockfile, then the installed binary. It also covers TLS-proxy HTTPS and redirect rejection.
  - `test/cli7/live-diagnostics.mjs`: live harness pattern covering the Codex launcher check, the start-turn guard, the real service plus `LocalOperatorHttp`, token-file login, a sentinel, the sanitised JSON output and verified cleanup.
  - `test/fixtures/operator-cli.ts` `startCliService(..., { runtimeFactory })`: real service with a bearer path, a session and an injectable runtime.
  - `test/operator-cli-inventory.test.ts`: documented command lists.
  - `docs/evidence/release-candidate-inventory.json`: precedent for an attributable inventory.
- **New:**
  - `docs/evidence/issue-901-cli8-inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.json`: one row per command or operation, with area, scenarios, evidence (test files, harness step, slice record), observed effect, denial, revision and retry cases, `real|synthetic`, and state `passed|bounded|unproved` with the gap.
  - `test/operator-cli-qualification-inventory.test.ts` guards that inventory.
  - `test/cli8/live-journey.mjs` (modes `--fixture`, `--live --max-turns 2`, `--phase remote`).
  - `test/cli8-journey-harness.test.ts` runs fixture mode in CI.
  - `package.json` script `cli8:live`.
  - `docs/evidence/issue-901-cli8-YYYY-MM-DD.md` and the sanitised `issue-901-cli8-live-YYYY-MM-DD.json`.
- **Follow:**
  - `test/cli7/live-diagnostics.mjs` for live safety, the guard and cleanup.
  - The CLI1–CLI7 records for record structure: candidate, covered operations, entry points, results, limits.
  - The s04d record for the Serve grant, readback and removal.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 has no dependencies. T2 has no dependencies. T3 depends on T2. T4 depends on T3. T5 depends on T1, T3 and T4. The graph is acyclic. T1 and T2 are ready together and safe to run concurrently: T1 owns `docs/evidence/*inventory*` and the inventory test, and T2 owns `test/cli8/**`, the harness test and `package.json`. T3 and T4 are live and sequential, and share the retained disposable data directory. T5 alone edits `docs/acceptance.md`, `docs/development.md`, `README.md` and the dated record. **Live:** T3 (Codex, ≤2 turns per run). **Second machine:** T4.

#### 1. Renewed slice evidence and the command inventory

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- New `docs/evidence/issue-901-cli8-inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.json`.
- New `test/operator-cli-qualification-inventory.test.ts`, which imports `browseCommands` and `writeCommands`.
- Read only: the CLI1–CLI7 records, `docs/design/operator-cli.md#command-surface` and `docs/acceptance.md#operator-cli-acceptance`.

**Test:** `operator-cli-qualification-inventory.test.ts` loads the inventory JSON and asserts:
- (1) The set of command rows equals `browseCommands ∪ writeCommands ∪ {auth login, auth status, auth logout, connection list, connection use, connection remove, task get}`.
- (2) Every design-table operation without a command (for example the `diagnosticCapture` prepare) has an explicit `unproved` row with a gap.
- (3) Every row names at least one scenario CLI01–CLI06, an existing evidence path or `harness:<step>`, and a state from the closed set.
- (4) Each of CLI01–CLI06 has a scenario disposition.

Sensitivity: delete one row locally and the test fails naming that command.

**Implementation:**
- Rerun the T1 suite list at the candidate and record the pass counts per slice.
- Build the inventory from the slice records' covered-operation tables, adding the T3 and T4 harness steps as placeholders that T5 finalises.
- Mark rows backed only by synthetic fixtures `bounded` and rows with no evidence `unproved`.

**Validate:**
- From the worktree, after `npm ci && npm run build`, run `node --test $(for f in operator-credentials operator-cli-http managed-assignment-environment operator-cli-credentials-browser operator-cli operator-cli-packed operator-cli-browse operator-browse-pages operator-cli-evidence operator-cli-assignment operator-instructions operator-artifact-source operator-cli-inventory operator-cli-change operator-cli-config-journey operator-cli-routing-capacity operator-cli-adopt operator-cli-write operator-operations operator-config-impact operator-cli-source operator-cli-source-activation operator-cli-delivery operator-cli-comments operator-cli-source-delivery-journey task-comments operator-cli-task operator-cli-operate-journey operator-cli-attention operator-inbox operator-cli-task-control operator-task-control recovery-rejections operator-recovery-options operator-recovery-commands operator-recovery-operations operator-cli-recovery operator-cli-recovery-write operator-cli-recovery-journey execution-diagnostics-store operator-diagnostic-capture execution-diagnostics-service operator-execution-diagnostics operator-cli-execution operator-cli-follow operator-cli-qualification-inventory; do printf 'dist/test/%s.test.js ' $f; done)`. Expect 0 failures.
- Also run `ENSEMBLE_KEYCHAIN_LIVE=1 node --test dist/test/operator-cli-keychain.test.js`, which uses a throwaway item. Expect a pass and the item absent afterwards.

**Complete when:** the inventory covers the full registry plus every design-table operation, the guard test passes, and the renewed per-slice results are recorded.

#### 2. Assembled journey harness with fixture mode and the H1 proof

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- New `test/cli8/live-journey.mjs`.
- New `test/cli8-journey-harness.test.ts`.
- `package.json` script `"cli8:live": "node test/cli8/live-journey.mjs --live --max-turns 2"`.
- Reuses `installPacked` logic (extract it into a shared fixture only if needed), the session credential endpoints and `startCliService`-style wiring.

**Test:** `cli8-journey-harness.test.ts` runs `node test/cli8/live-journey.mjs --fixture` with a scripted runtime. Turn 1 runs the `printenv` command item and reports `FAIL missing-required-phrase`. Turn 2 reports `PASS <word>`. It asserts the following.
- **H1:** exactly 2 `startTurn` calls, the second only after adoption and follow-up (or message). A third attempt is rejected before the runtime.
- **Install:** the packed binary is installed outside the checkout, in a temporary prefix.
- **Read-only investigation:**
  - `task list` and `task search FAIL --type result` find the task.
  - `result get` shows FAIL.
  - `execution list` and `execution inputs --compare-current` show the captured profile v1 segment and the submitted SHA-256.
  - `logs` shows `commandExecution` and the `ensemble_report_result` tool item.
  - `assignment instructions` and `profile revisions` are read.
- **Read-only write denial:** `profile apply` exits 3, and a direct `POST /api/operator/commands` with the read-only bearer gets 403 `insufficient-scope`. The database digest is unchanged.
- **Correction:** `profile prepare --instructions-file` writes a `0600` document whose diff adds exactly the phrase line. `profile apply --file` creates revision 2. An identical rerun replays the receipt.
- **Concurrent edit conflict:** a session edit between prepare and apply makes apply exit 4.
- **Lost response:** a separate no-dispatch `project prepare`/`apply` (rename) through a response-dropping proxy exits 6. Then `operation get` reads `recorded`, and the rerun replays with one version bump.
- **Adoption:** `assignment apply-current` gives `boundIsCurrent`.
- **Follow-up:** turn 2's execution inputs show profile revision 2 with the phrase. `result get` shows PASS.
- **Revocation during follow:** `logs --follow` with the read-only credential exits 3 after a session revoke.
- **Local logout:** `auth logout` leaves the server credential active (`GET /api/operator/cli` still 200), until it is revoked.
- **Remote authority:** bearer posts to `/runtime/control/*` and session-only routes get 403.
- **Cleanup:** credentials revoked and fixtures removed.
- **Output:** sanitised evidence JSON with every CLI invocation's command, exit code, `real|synthetic` and sentinel absence.

**Implementation:**
- Modes:
  - `--fixture`: scripted runtime, loopback, token-file.
  - `--live --max-turns 2`: the Codex launcher at `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex`, refused if absent. Keychain login through a pseudo-terminal (`/usr/bin/script -q /dev/null`) for the read/write connection, and a token file for the read-only connection.
  - `--retain DIR`: keep the owner-only data directory for T4.
  - `--phase remote --data DIR --origin HTTPS_ORIGIN`: max turns 0. Issue fresh credentials, write remote token files, and print the remote command list and expected results.
- Use phase-gated start-turn admission: turn 2 is admitted only after the harness sets the post-adoption flag.
- On any assertion failure, still run cleanup and exit nonzero with a sanitised failure.

**Validate:** from the worktree, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/cli8-journey-harness.test.js`. Expect a pass, with exactly 2 start-turn calls recorded and cleanup booleans true. Then run `node test/cli8/live-journey.mjs` with no flags and expect exit 2 refusing live execution.

**Complete when:** fixture mode passes in the test runner, H1 holds (otherwise apply class (a) and stop), and live and remote modes are gated by explicit flags.

#### 3. Host live journey with the packaged CLI outside the checkout (LIVE)

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:**
- T2 fixture mode passes, including the H1 proof.
- The Codex launcher exists, and `codex --version` and the launcher SHA-256 are recorded.
- No Claude grant is needed.

**Files and symbols:** the new `docs/evidence/issue-901-cli8-live-YYYY-MM-DD.json` (sanitised harness output). Harness repairs go in T2's files.

**Implementation:**
- Run `npm run cli8:live -- --retain <owner-only dir>` once. Optionally rerun once after a repair, within the 4-turn ticket budget.
- The service listens on loopback HTTP (the supported host transport).
- The binary is installed from `npm pack` into a temporary prefix outside the checkout. The record shows its absolute path and that it is not under the checkout.
- Record: candidate SHA, Node, npm, Codex version and SHA, installation identity, credential ids (not tokens), each CLI step's exit and effect, and the live observations:
  - captured segments
  - the submitted digest match
  - settings sources
  - the `commandExecution` output, which settles the `ENSEMBLE_MANAGED_ASSIGNMENT` propagation (Passed if `1`, otherwise a recorded failure against the CLI1 limit)
  - the `ensemble_report_result` tool item
  - service events
  - the gaps
- Also record sentinel absence from outputs, database and WAL bytes, and the cleanup results.
- If the model does not follow the FAIL/PASS script, record the observed result. A rerun is allowed only within the budget. Never fabricate the failure.

**Validate:** from the worktree, after `npm run build`, run `npm run cli8:live -- --retain "$DIR"`. Expect exit 0, `startTurnCalls` ≤ 2, the investigation, correction, adoption and follow-up steps all present, the sentinel `absent`, every credential revoked, the Keychain item absent, and the App Server exit `verified`.

**Complete when:** the live JSON is committed and the retained data directory is either handed to T4 or removed.

#### 4. Second-machine private-HTTPS journey (SECOND MACHINE)

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites and resume condition:** an explicit grant from Chris that names:
- (1) the trusted macOS peer (`hermes` or "Chris's MacBook Air" are online candidates)
- (2) the execution channel (for example Tailscale SSH or an SSH host alias he provides)
- (3) a temporary `tailscale serve --bg --https=<port> http://127.0.0.1:<port>` route for the disposable service
- (4) permission to copy the packed tarball and lockfile to the peer and install it there, which needs Node ≥ 24 on the peer

Until all four exist, T4 does nothing. If they are not available by the time T1–T3 are complete, T4 completes as **Unproved: prerequisite unavailable**. It removes the retained data directory, and T5 records the resume condition.

Resuming after delivery is a new run under a new grant. It may use one fresh host run of 2 model turns, plus this phase, and adds a new dated record.

**Files and symbols:** none beyond the T2 harness. The output goes into the T3 live JSON or a `-remote` sibling.

**Implementation:**
- Read Serve and Funnel status, then enable the granted route and read it back.
- Restart the service on the retained data directory with `--phase remote` and the canonical `https://<peer-visible host>.ts.net` origin. The start-turn guard rejects every turn.
- On the peer, install the packed binary outside any checkout, under a temporary prefix. Log in with `--token-file` (mode `0600`) for the read-only and read/write connections.
- Confirm `service-identity` matches the host installation id.
- Run the read-only investigation (find the failed task, inputs, compare, logs) and the read-only write denial.
- Run one no-dispatch read/write action: project rename prepare/apply plus `operation get`.
- Check that an `http://` non-loopback URL is refused, and redirect rejection if feasible.
- On both machines: revoke the credentials, remove the token files, the prefix and the config directory, disable the Serve route and read back no Serve config.

**Validate:** the harness's remote checklist reports every step with its exit code and expected result. `tailscale serve status --json` shows no remaining Serve config afterwards, and `tailscale funnel status --json` shows no Funnel. If T4 is not run, Validate is the recorded Unproved disposition plus the cleanup of the retained directory.

**Complete when:** the remote journey has been recorded as Passed or Bounded with its peer identity (hostname and OS only), or recorded as Unproved with the exact missing prerequisite. In either case cleanup is verified.

#### 5. Qualification record, dispositions and operator guidance

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T1, T3, T4`
**Prerequisites:** the T1 inventory, the T3 live JSON and the T4 outcome.
**Files and symbols:**
- New `docs/evidence/issue-901-cli8-YYYY-MM-DD.md`.
- Finalise the T1 inventory JSON.
- `docs/acceptance.md` (the CLI01–CLI06 evidence-state table and the command-inventory paragraph under `#operator-cli-acceptance`).
- `docs/development.md` `## Operator CLI`.
- `README.md` "Where it stands" operator CLI bullet.

**Implementation:**
- The record follows the slice-record structure: candidate and environment (versions, client and service identity, host and peer), the scenario dispositions, the renewed slice evidence table, the live and remote observations labelled real or synthetic, entry points, finite pass/fail/unproved outcomes, cleanup and limits.
- Set each CLI0x state from the evidence only. CLI01 and CLI06 cannot be Passed without T4.
- Development guidance:
  - installing from `npm pack` outside the checkout
  - credential creation and rotation in Settings
  - Keychain versus `--token-file`
  - the remote HTTPS requirement over a private Tailscale route, with system trust or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for private CAs
  - troubleshooting by exit code: 2 invalid input, 3 authentication or scope, 4 conflict or `cursor-stale`, 5 unavailable, TLS or redirect, 6 uncertain (with the `operation get` or same-key retry procedure), 7 unsupported service
  - `service-identity-changed`, `credential-store-unavailable` and `managed-assignment`
  - supported limitations
- Keep #933's README, acceptance, development and `package.json` hunks untouched, and rebase over it if it merges first.

**Validate:** from the worktree, run `npm run build && npm run format:check && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-qualification-inventory.test.js`. Expect formatting clean and the guard passing with the final states. Manual check: every inventory row with state `passed` cites real evidence, and no row is upgraded without a citation.

**Complete when:** the record, inventory and docs agree, and every missing obligation is Unproved with a concrete gap.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Inventory maps the evidence to CLI01–CLI06 and every promised operation, including denial, revision and retry cases, with missing obligations Unproved | 1, 5 | Inventory guard test, renewed suite results |
| Packaged executable outside the checkout on both client locations, with private HTTPS, secure credential storage, read-only and read/write | 2, 3, 4 | Harness install-prefix check; T3 Keychain and token-file; T4 remote checklist, or Unproved |
| Bounded real-runtime failure, investigation, diff, exact apply, adoption and subsequent execution | 2, 3 | T2 fixture test; T3 live JSON |
| Attention, source/delivery and recovery qualified by reusing valid slice evidence; fixtures not presented as real effects | 1, 5 | T1 renewed CLI4/CLI5/CLI6 suites; labels in the record |
| Browser/service credential lifecycle reusing CLI1 | 1, 2 | `operator-cli-credentials-browser` rerun; harness session issuance and revocation |
| Direct-API read-only denial, expiry and revocation during follow, browser protections, concurrent conflict, lost-response reconciliation on the assembled service | 1, 2, 3 | T2/T3 harness steps; `operator-cli-http` and `operator-cli-follow` reruns |
| Honest labels for old, expired, redacted, unsupported and oversized evidence; diagnostics hold no release authority; administration outside remote authority | 1, 2 | `execution-diagnostics-*` reruns; harness `/runtime/control` and session-only 403 |
| Versions, identities, real versus synthetic, finite outcomes, cleanup; missing checks Unproved | 3, 4, 5 | Live JSON and record |
| Pinned validation and packed-client checks; operator guidance and limitations | 1, 5 | Final validation; `operator-cli-packed`; development docs |

### Final validation

- From the worktree with Node 24.21.0 first on `PATH`, run `npm ci && npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate. Expect typecheck, lint, format and build to pass, and all tests to pass except the opt-in Keychain skip.
