content.title: Result lookup collides across replacement conversations with the same work revision

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/903
**Planned against:** `main` at `f0a43304342796c5085d555903cd472498ebbd4d`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Treat `workId` as the exact work identity for results, which every other result reader already does. In `CoordinationStore.recordResult`, look up the prior result by the bound `workId` instead of `(assignmentId, workRevision)`. Remove the table constraint `UNIQUE(assignmentId, workRevision)` from `coordination_results` and keep the existing `workId UNIQUE`. Existing databases get a forward-only rebuild of `coordination_results` that drops only that constraint and copies every row unchanged, with its `rowid`. Leave work-revision allocation in `ExecutionState` (per assignment and conversation revision, as `docs/SPEC.md` "Newest is judged within the lead's current conversation" requires) unchanged.

### Guardrails

- The exact callback-key path stays first and unchanged. The `coordination_receipts` lookup by `(threadId, turnId, callId)` returns the stored response and `resultByWork(receipt.workId)` before any binding check. Changed content for an existing key still throws `Coordination callback identity reused with different content`.
- Existing rows are never rewritten or re-attributed. This includes a legacy receipt that the collision already attributed to an older work. Replay of that key returns the result it recorded. There is no backfill, deletion, automatic recovery or hold release.
- Same-work retries keep their current behavior. A new callId with identical content for the same `workId` reuses that work's result. Different content conflicts with `Result already recorded with different content`.
- `recordResult` remains one transaction. Result, inbox or unresolved-destination, assignment completion, reporting-repair, review index, retained evidence, pending-effect settlement and receipt writes commit or roll back together. Do not change the retained-evidence savepoint behavior.
- Out of scope: the receipt-writer extraction and `insertToolReceipt` sharing (#888); `src/standalone/state.ts` work-revision allocation and `replaceConversation`; recovery or ownership holds; completion and result-delivery rules; persisted-column renames (#881/#887); and any service, runtime or UI change.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record each correction and renew the affected evidence. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the owner and do not use the plan-mismatch allowance. A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Examples: a caller that depends on the `(assignmentId, workRevision)` constraint, a migration that cannot run outside the `migrate()` transaction, or SQLite rename behavior that breaks child foreign keys. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks or reviews. Use an integration amendment only when a published integration decision changes and needs durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Exact identity is `workId`.** `execution_intents.workId` is globally unique. `task_work_revisions` maps each `workId` to exactly one `(assignmentId, conversationRevision, workRevision)`. `coordination_results.workId` is already `UNIQUE`. `resumableResult`, completion gates (`coordination.ts` ~L4305, ~L4344), `recordSuccessfulTerminal` (~L2531) and `hasResultForWork` already select results by `workId` joined to `task_work_revisions`. The only readers that use `(assignmentId, workRevision)` are the `priorResult` query (~L972) and the table constraint. Do not add a `conversationRevision` column or backfill; `workId UNIQUE` is the compatible uniqueness contract.
- **Migration and read strategy (decided, not human-required).** Old receipts and results stay readable as stored, because both lookups key on columns that already exist (`workId`, receipt key). The only schema change relaxes one constraint by rebuilding the table. All rows, values and `rowid`s are preserved. `rowid` must be preserved because `task-review.ts` orders and pages by it. The rebuild follows the repository precedents `ExecutionState.migratePreTurnReceipts` (`src/standalone/state.ts` ~L2046) and `Store.migrateExecutionStateToV6` (`src/core/store.ts` ~L180), and ADR-1003 (Ensemble owns its schema and migrations). Data is not rewritten. Older binaries can still open the migrated database because their `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op. This adds no downgrade commitment beyond the current one.
- **Migration mechanics.** Add a private `migrateResultWorkIdentity()` and call it first in `CoordinationStore.migrate()`, before the `transaction(...)` block, because `PRAGMA foreign_keys` cannot change inside a transaction. On a fresh database the table does not exist yet, so skip. When the stored table SQL has no `UNIQUE(assignmentId, workRevision)` constraint (whitespace-insensitive match), skip. Before rebuilding, refuse with `Unrecognized coordination result schema; migration refused` and change nothing in two cases. The first case is a column list that is not exactly the 11 known columns. The second is a trigger, or any non-auto index other than `coordination_results_task_created`, on the table. Otherwise, follow the `migratePreTurnReceipts` sequence. Save the current `foreign_keys` value, set it `OFF`, then in one immediate transaction run `CREATE TABLE coordination_results_v2` with the new DDL, then `INSERT ... (rowid, <11 columns>) SELECT rowid, <11 columns>`, then `DROP`, `ALTER ... RENAME TO coordination_results` and recreate `coordination_results_task_created`. Fail and roll back if the row count changes or `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` returns rows. Restore the `foreign_keys` value in `finally`. Use one DDL constant for both the fresh `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and the rebuild, so the two cannot drift.
- **Proof already done (no proof task).** A scratch probe on a temporary SQLite database used the production fixture from `test/coordination.test.ts`, Node 24.21.0 and the baseline above. At baseline, identical content returned `work-lead-old` with `replayed: false` and one result, and differing content threw `Result already recorded with different content`. With the `workId` lookup plus the rebuild applied to a scratch copy, both cases returned `work-lead-new`, `replayed: false` and two results. A legacy-constraint database reopened, dropped the constraint, kept `PRAGMA foreign_keys = 1` and the child foreign keys to `coordination_results`, replayed the old callback key exactly, and stayed stable across repeated reopens.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/coordination.ts`. `CoordinationStore.migrate` (~L480) creates `coordination_results` (~L494–508, with `UNIQUE(assignmentId, workRevision)`) and `coordination_results_task_created` inside `transaction(...)`. `recordResult` (~L898) does the following in order: exact receipt replay (~L913–935), `currentBinding`, the child and inbox gates, `priorResult` by `assignmentId`/`workRevision` (~L971–977), result/inbox/unresolved insert, completion, review index, evidence savepoint, `execution_pending_effects` settlement by `binding.workId`, and the receipt insert from `result.*` (~L1132). `resultByWork` is at ~L4491. Production callers reach it through `src/standalone/service.ts`, and their signatures do not change.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts`. `ExecutionState` allocates `task_work_revisions.workRevision` as `MAX+1` per `(assignmentId, conversationRevision)` (~L3946). `replaceConversation` (~L2712) increments `assignment_conversations.revision`. Read only; neither changes.
- **Existing:** `test/coordination.test.ts`. `fixture()` uses real file SQLite with `reopen()` and `addWork()`, which always inserts work revision 1. `report()` is the callback helper. `replaceLeadConversation` (~L1669) forces old work revision 5 and avoids the collision, so leave that helper and its two tests unchanged. `"exact receipts replay after completion before live binding checks"` and `"result and inbox or unresolved hold commit atomically"` are the patterns for the new tests.
- **Existing:** `test/retained-evidence-store.test.ts`. `"a receipt commit failure rolls back the result and complete retained evidence"` and `"a callback with a stale thread or turn remains rejected before retaining evidence"` already cover evidence atomicity and stale rejection on the unchanged evidence path.
- **New:** `CoordinationStore.migrateResultWorkIdentity` (private) and a module constant holding the `coordination_results` DDL without the legacy constraint.
- **Follow:** `src/standalone/state.ts:ExecutionState.migratePreTurnReceipts` for the guarded rebuild: schema recognition, `foreign_keys` save and restore, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `foreign_key_check`, and rollback.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2. Both are in `src/core/coordination.ts` and `test/coordination.test.ts`, so run them sequentially in one branch and PR (`cb/903-result-work-identity`). The graph is acyclic. Only T2 is behavior-visible. T1 establishes the persistence boundary that T2 depends on, because without T1 the second result insert fails on the legacy constraint.

#### 1. Relax result uniqueness with a guarded, row-preserving migration

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/coordination.ts` (DDL constant; `CoordinationStore.migrate`; new private `migrateResultWorkIdentity`); `test/coordination.test.ts` (new legacy-schema helper and tests).
**Test:** Add tests in `test/coordination.test.ts` that use `fixture()`. Add a helper that rebuilds `coordination_results` with the exact baseline DDL (copied verbatim from `f0a43304` `coordination.ts` L494–508, including `UNIQUE(assignmentId, workRevision)`) while foreign keys are off. The helper copies rows with their `rowid` and recreates `coordination_results_task_created`.
(a) `"legacy result uniqueness migrates on reopen preserving rows and replay"`: record a result for `work-child-a` (`call-legacy`), apply the helper, assert the stored SQL contains the legacy constraint, then call `f.reopen()`. Assert that the stored SQL no longer contains `UNIQUE(assignmentId`. Assert that the rows (including `rowid` and all 11 columns) equal the pre-migration snapshot. Assert that `PRAGMA foreign_keys` is 1, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` is empty and `coordination_results_task_created` exists. Assert that `recordResult(call-legacy)` returns `replayed: true` with the same `resultId` and response, and that a second `f.reopen()` is a no-op with the same rows.
(b) `"unrecognized legacy result schema refuses migration unchanged"`: apply the helper, add a trigger on `coordination_results`, then `f.reopen()`. Assert that it throws `/Unrecognized coordination result schema/`, and that the stored SQL and rows are unchanged (read the file with a fresh `DatabaseSync`).
(c) A fresh `fixture()` has no legacy constraint and no `_v2` table remains.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions, migration mechanics. Do not change the `priorResult` lookup in this slice.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test --test-name-pattern="legacy result|unrecognized legacy result" dist/test/coordination.test.js`. Expect all matched tests to pass. Then run `node --test dist/test/coordination.test.js dist/test/retained-evidence-store.test.js dist/test/operations-final-candidate.test.js` and expect 0 failures.
**Complete when:** Legacy databases migrate exactly once, preserving rows and `rowid`. Unknown shapes are refused unchanged. Fresh databases use the new DDL. Existing coordination, retained-evidence and backup/restore tests pass.

#### 2. Select prior results by exact work and cover replacement conversations at work revision 1

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 complete with its focused check passing.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/coordination.ts` (`recordResult` `priorResult` query: `FROM coordination_results WHERE workId = ?` bound to `String(binding.workId)`); `test/coordination.test.ts` (new helper `replaceLeadAtRevisionOne(f)` and tests).
**Test:** Add a helper next to `replaceLeadConversation`. It adds `work-lead-old` at revision 1, records `call-lead-old` and keeps the result `old`, marks the intent `completed`, and calls `f.state.replaceConversation(lead)`. It then adds `work-lead-new` (revision 1 in conversation 2) and delivers the old self-addressed event with `bindDeliveryBatch` and `completeDeliveryBatch`. Assert that both `task_work_revisions` rows have `workRevision = 1`. Tests:
(a) For summaries `["Completed work", "Different work"]`, `recordResult(report("thread-lead-new","turn-lead-new","call-lead-new", summary))` returns `result.workId === "work-lead-new"`, `replayed: false`, and a `resultId` that differs from `old`. Assert exactly two results. The stored receipt for `call-lead-new` has `workId "work-lead-new"` and `workRevision 1`. The `assignment-result` pending effect for `work-lead-new` is `settled`. The lead inbox gains no extra event beyond what the recipient rules produce, so compare the count before and after against a single result insert. Then `f.reopen()`. `recordResult(call-lead-old)` and `recordResult(call-lead-new)` each return `replayed: true` with their own `resultId` and the original response. A changed summary under `call-lead-new` throws `/different content/`. Row counts for results, inbox events and receipts do not change.
(b) A same-work retry still reuses its result: a new callId on `thread-lead-new`/`turn-lead-new` with identical content returns the same `resultId`, with no new result or inbox row. Differing content throws `/Result already recorded with different content/`.
(c) Stale callbacks stay rejected: a new callId on `thread-lead-old`/`turn-lead-old` after replacement throws `/not bound/`, and results, inbox events, receipts and `retained_result_evidence` counts are unchanged.
(d) Rollback: in the replacement state, add `CREATE TRIGGER ... BEFORE INSERT ON coordination_receipts ... RAISE(ABORT,'injected receipt failure')`. `recordResult(call-lead-new)` throws. No result for `work-lead-new`, no new inbox, unresolved-destination or receipt row exists, the pending effect stays `pending`, and the assignment state is unchanged. After dropping the trigger, the same call succeeds once.
(e) Legacy footprint read strategy: in a T1 legacy database in the replacement state, insert a receipt row for `call-collided` on `thread-lead-new`/`turn-lead-new` attributed to `work-lead-old`, with content matching the report hash. This simulates a pre-fix collision. After `f.reopen()`, `recordResult` of that exact call returns `replayed: true` and the old `resultId`. No rows are rewritten or added.
Sensitivity: with the `priorResult` change reverted, (a) must fail. It returns `work-lead-old` for identical content and conflicts for differing content.
**Implementation:** Change only the `priorResult` query and its parameters. Leave every other step of `recordResult`, including the receipt insert from `result.*`, as is (#888 owns that writer). Callers do not change.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout root, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/coordination.test.js dist/test/retained-evidence-store.test.js dist/test/recovery-continuation.test.js dist/test/no-turn-recovery.test.js`. Expect 0 failures, including the new tests.
**Complete when:** Replacement-conversation callbacks at revision 1 record the new work's result under both content variants. Exact-key replays return their own recorded results across reopen. Stale and rollback cases leave no effects. Recovery suites pass.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Real SQLite tests cover old and replacement conversations both at work revision 1, identical and differing content | 2 | T2 test (a), with the revision-1 assertion in the helper |
| New callbacks produce the new work's result identity; old callback-key replay returns only its recorded result | 2 | T2 tests (a) and (e) |
| Stale callbacks rejected without duplicate inbox/result/evidence effects | 2 | T2 test (c); existing `retained-evidence-store` stale test |
| Lookup and uniqueness use compatible exact work identities, with an explicit migration/read strategy | 1, 2 | T1 tests (a) to (c); T2 query; Planning decisions, migration and read strategy |
| Fixtures reopen an existing database and verify retained receipts/results and callback replay | 1, 2 | T1 test (a); T2 tests (a) and (e) after `f.reopen()` |
| Receipt/result/inbox/evidence writes atomic; failure rolls back | 2 | T2 test (d); existing `"result and inbox or unresolved hold commit atomically"` and `"a receipt commit failure rolls back the result and complete retained evidence"` |
| Preserve unresolved recovery/ownership holds and normal completion/result delivery | 2 | T2 Validate (recovery-continuation, no-turn-recovery, coordination suites); final `npm run check` |

### Final validation

- From the implementation checkout root, with Node 24.21.0 (`.node-version`) first on `PATH` and npm 12.2.0 (`packageManager`; use `npx -y npm@12.2.0` if the local npm differs), run `npm ci && npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate. Expect typecheck, lint, format, build and all tests to pass. CI runs the same check on Node 26.
- No live runtime or UI evidence is required. The change is confined to the SQLite store and its migration, and no runtime, service or UI contract changes. No documentation change is required: `docs/SPEC.md` already states that work revisions restart per conversation and that earlier-conversation results are never resumed. Record that in the PR.

### Review focus

- The migration runs outside the `migrate()` transaction with foreign keys temporarily off. Confirm that `foreign_keys` is restored on every path, including the refusal path and a failure mid-rebuild, and that child tables (`coordination_inbox_events`, `coordination_follow_ups`, `coordination_unresolved_result_destinations`, retained evidence, task review) still reference `coordination_results` after the rename.
- After this change `result.workId === binding.workId` on the prior-result path. #888's "differing result/binding identity" fixture is then no longer reachable through `recordResult`, so #888 should rebase on this change.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- Any production code turns out to rely on `UNIQUE(assignmentId, workRevision)`, for example `ON CONFLICT` targets or error-message mapping.
- A real legacy database shape is found that the guarded rebuild refuses. Handling it would require a broader or lossy migration, which goes back for a human decision.

content.title: Run every Git invocation with one hardened environment

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/884
**Planned against:** `main` at `f0a43304342796c5085d555903cd472498ebbd4d`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Run every Git subprocess Ensemble starts with one hardened environment and, in `src/standalone`, one bounded runner. Implementation branch: `cb/884-hardened-git-environment`, from `main` at or after the planned SHA. One PR, five observable slices.

1. **Shared environment and core (T1).** `gitEnvironment()` moves into `src/core/child-environment.ts` beside `childProcessEnvironment`; `src/standalone/git-process.ts` re-exports it. The three `execFile("git")` calls in `src/core/github-source.ts` use it, so repository verification is hardened without moving it (#914 owns the move).
2. **Runner (T2).** `git-process.ts` gains `runGit`, the lifecycle now private to `WorkspaceManager` (timeout, abort signal, SIGTERM then SIGKILL, bounded exit observation, combined output cap, pipe detach), generalised only by an optional stdin and a structured result. `WorkspaceManager.git` becomes a thin adapter.
3. **Inspection and comparison (T3).** `checkGitIgnore` and `readGit` call the runner and keep their own result types; `stopOwnedChild` and `waitForExit` are deleted.
4. **Setup (T4).** `operator-setup.ts` runs its branch probe through the runner and drops `probeEnv` and the `env` argument of `checkoutOrigin`.
5. **Guard and docs (T5).** A source scan fails a future raw Git spawn that skips the shared environment; `docs/SPEC.md` states the contract.

### Guardrails

- **Unchanged contracts:** every Git command line and argument (no `-c` flag is added or removed for any caller); each caller's timeout, termination grace and observation window, and output cap (workspaces: per-operation deadlines, 2 s/2 s, 1 MiB; comparison: 1.5 s per child within a 5 s total, 50 ms/250 ms, 2 MiB; ignore check: 2 s, 100 ms/500 ms, 1 MiB, 2 MiB input; setup probes: 2 s, 1 MiB; core verification: 5 s `execFile`); `WorkspaceManager`'s public surface (`gitExecutable` must be absolute, `gitTimeoutMs`, `gitTerminationGraceMs`, `gitTerminationObservationMs`, `gitFailureObserver`, sticky `cancelGitWork`) and the `WorkspaceGitError.uncertain` rule (`kind !== "failed" || (started && !exitObserved)`); comparison's `GitRead` reasons and `gitFailureReason` mapping; inspection's `IgnoreResult`; `RepositoryVerificationError` reasons and `actual`; `DomainStore`'s `verifyRepository` injection; operator field paths and feedback; credential-free children (`childProcessEnvironment` still removes the Claude and delivery tokens).
- **Exact-child termination only:** the runner signals the `ChildProcess` it spawned and nothing else. No kill by command, name or process group. A child whose exit is not observed is never reported as settled: workspaces mark it uncertain, comparison reports `time-limit`, inspection reports `incomplete`.
- **Out of scope:** moving verification out of core (#914); repository-config hardening such as `core.fsmonitor`, hooks or filters for workspaces and verification; a `git worktree prune` caller (none exists today); `execFile` bounds in core; the Codex and Claude runtime spawn environments (agent processes run their own Git and keep their environment); any web file (no UI change, no design frame needed).
- **(a) Plan-seam mismatch: one diagnosis plus two repair cycles in total**, only when a factual assumption in this plan about the repository or an approved seam is wrong. Examples: the `WorkspaceManager` lifecycle cannot be generalised into `runGit` without changing its observable results (uncertainty, observer calls, abort behaviour); inspection's stdin and exit-code-1 handling or comparison's `unsettled` result cannot be expressed through the runner's result union; a production Git caller outside the inventory below that needs an inherited `GIT_*` variable or a transport protocol to work in a supported setup. After the diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, stop and report for a replan.
- **(b) Ordinary in-scope repairs: owner repairs, no allowance, they do not consume (a):** implementation bugs; type, lint and format errors; fixture and test setup (including the PATH shim and hostile-environment helpers); equivalent paths or names; documentation text; rebase conflicts; and CI or flaky-test retries (including Node 26 and npm 12.2.0 lockfile or runner fixes). Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes, or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews; no integration amendment is needed unless a published integration decision changes.

### Planning decisions

- **The environment builder lives in core.** `src/core/github-source.ts` cannot import `src/standalone`, `child-environment.ts` already is the core-owned builder for helper children, and building an environment spawns nothing, so ADR-1003 and #914's end state (`src/core` does not spawn) hold. Injection alone is not enough: `service.ts` (`provisionTask`) and `operator-setup.ts` (`verifyCheckout`) call `verifiedRepository` directly and tests call it with no injection, so the default must be hardened. `checkoutOrigin(path, env?, timeout)` loses `env` (its only caller was setup's `probeEnv`) and becomes `checkoutOrigin(path, timeout = 5000)`.
- **The runner is the `WorkspaceManager` lifecycle, moved not rewritten.** It is the superset (abort signal, grace and observation timers, detach and `unref` when pipes stay open); comparison and inspection are strict subsets of it. Result union (never rejects): `{status:"ok", stdout}`; `{status:"exit", exitCode, signal, stdout}` for a child that ran to completion and exited non-zero or by signal; `{status:"interrupted", kind: "failed"|"timed-out"|"cancelled"|"output-limit", spawned, childExitObserved, childExitSignal}` for spawn failure, timeout, abort, output cap or a post-spawn error. The environment is always `gitEnvironment()`; there is no `env` option, so a caller cannot opt out. Options: `executable` (default `"git"`, test-only override), `args`, `cwd?`, `input?` (written then closed; otherwise stdin is ignored), `timeoutMs`, `terminationGraceMs`, `observationMs`, `maxOutputBytes` (stdout plus stderr), `signal?`. #914 reuses it for `rev-parse` and `remote get-url`.
- **Adapters keep each caller's classification.** Workspaces: `ok` returns `stdout.toString("utf8").trim()`; `exit` and `interrupted` become `WorkspaceGitError` through the existing `reportGitFailure` (observer called once per failure, `exit` maps to kind `failed` with the child's signal); an already-aborted signal still rejects `cancelled` without spawning and without an observer call. Comparison: `ok` and `exit` map as today (`exit` keeps `exitCode` and `output`, including the empty-output exit 1 of `config --get-regexp`); `interrupted` maps to its kind when the child exit was observed and to `unsettled` when not. Inspection: `ok`, or `exit` with code 1, parse stdout; anything else is `{complete:false}`.
- **Accepted classification tidy.** A spawn that never starts (missing executable) was reported by comparison as `unsettled` (`time-limit`) after the 300 ms stop windows; through the runner it is `failed` (`git-failed`) at once. No test covers it; it is the only comparison result that changes.
- **Behaviour changes accepted by the issue, not open decisions.** The issue states that the environment changes for workspaces and repository verification and requires no prompts, lazy fetches or protocol widening. (1) Those paths stop seeing inherited `GIT_*` (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_ASKPASS`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, …). Audit: no production code reads or sets `GIT_*` for them; the generated LaunchAgent passes only `PATH` and `ENSEMBLE_*`; tests set `GIT_*` only in the comparison suite, which already runs hardened. (2) A repository that needs the network to supply objects (a partial clone with absent blobs or commits) now fails closed: `worktree add` fails (the binding stays `provisioning` with a creation-incomplete reason) and verification reports `ref-unavailable`, where Git used to fetch. `docs/SPEC.md` records it (T5). `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` only stops opportunistic index refresh during `status`.
- **Evidence gathered at planning (Apple Git 2.54.0).** On the planning checkout `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run build:service` pass, 66 tests in `workspaces`, `workspace-inspection`, `workspace-comparison`, `project-setup`, `operator-setup-api` and `operator-setup-model` pass, and 34 in `claude-runtime-service`, `operator-workspace-inspection`, `operator-comparisons` and `turn-capture-service` pass (Node 24.21.0, npm 11.19.0 locally); CI on `main` at the planned SHA is green. With `GIT_DIR` pointing at a decoy repository and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0` overriding `remote.origin.url`, today's `verifiedRepository(link, {acme, real})` fails with `origin-missing`: the core path is observably affected by inherited `GIT_*`, so the T1 test fails before the change. Under `gitEnvironment()` the commands every caller runs (`rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `remote get-url origin`, `symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD`, `status --porcelain=v1`, `worktree add` and `worktree remove`) succeed on a local repository, so `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=""` does not break local provisioning. Report the real order in which new tests were seen to fail before the change.
- **Verification technique.** A test-only `git` shim (`test/fixtures/git-environment.ts`) appends its `GIT_*` environment to a log and `exec`s the real Git. Callers with a `gitExecutable` option receive it directly; `execFile("git")` callers (core, setup) find it first on `PATH`. A hostile helper sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:ssh:https`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=0` and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1` in `process.env` only around the call under test (fixture setup keeps using plain Git) and restores them in `finally`. Every recorded invocation must show exactly `{GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL:"", GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH:"1", GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS:"0", GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT:"0"}`. The existing promisor-helper test in `test/workspace-comparison.test.ts` already proves these values stop a lazy fetch; do not duplicate it.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/git-process.ts` — `gitEnvironment()` (strips every `GIT_*`, sets the four hardened variables on top of `childProcessEnvironment()`), `waitForExit` and `stopOwnedChild`; used only by `workspace-inspection.ts`, `workspace-comparison.ts` and `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` (asserts the Git environment carries no Claude token; keep its import working).
- **Existing:** `src/core/child-environment.ts` — `childProcessEnvironment`, `credentialFreeEnvironment`, `setChildCredentialExclusions`. `src/core/github-source.ts` — `checkoutOrigin` (L145) and `verifiedRepository` (L171) run three `execFileAsync("git", …)` calls with `childProcessEnvironment()`; called by `DomainStore.verifyRepository` (default parameter, `domain.ts`), `StandaloneService.provisionTask` (`service.ts`, direct) and `operator-setup.ts` `verifyCheckout` (direct).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/workspaces.ts` — `WorkspaceManager.git` (L768) wraps private `runGit` (L981) with `spawn(..., env: childProcessEnvironment())`, the only Git runner without the hardened environment; `WorkspaceGitError` (L162), `reportGitFailure` (L1171), `isUncertainGitError`. Operations: `rev-parse`, `status`, `worktree add --detach`, `worktree remove`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/workspace-inspection.ts` `checkGitIgnore` (L660; `check-ignore -z --stdin`, stdin piped, hardened env) called from `ignoredPaths` and the directory listing. `src/standalone/workspace-comparison.ts` `readGit` (L288; `GitRead`, `gitFailureReason`) called by the `run` closure in `compareRepository`. `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts` — `probeEnv`, `currentBranch` (`execFile`, sets two variables, no `GIT_*` stripping), `listHomeFolders`, `verifyCheckout`.
- **Existing tests:** `test/workspaces.test.ts` (controlled Git fixture `test/fixtures/controlled-git.ts`: stall, overflow, descendant holding the pipe, sticky cancellation, observer readback), `test/workspace-inspection.test.ts` (failing and stalled `gitExecutable`), `test/workspace-comparison.test.ts` (time-limit, output-limit, inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, promisor helper), `test/project-setup.test.ts` (`verifiedRepository` reasons; `createSetupHome`, `checkout` from `test/fixtures/setup-home.ts`), `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts` and `test/operator-setup-model.test.ts` (folder listing and checkout probes). `scripts/run-tests.mjs` runs `dist/test/*.test.js`, so new test files need no registration.
- **New:** `test/fixtures/git-environment.ts` (`gitEnvironmentProbe()` → `{executable, binDirectory, invocations(), clear(), close()}`; `withHostileGitEnvironment(fn)`); `test/git-process.test.ts` (runner contract); `test/git-environment.test.ts` (source guard).
- **Follow:** `test/fixtures/controlled-git.ts` for writing a shim script with literal absolute paths; `test/workspace-comparison.test.ts` "comparison ignores an inherited alternate index" for the set-and-restore pattern.
- **Overlap (record in the delivery record, rebase mechanically):** no source file is shared with #900, #903, #898, #826, #875, #874, #872, #897 or #887. Shared documentation only: `docs/SPEC.md` (the Operator CLI section in #900 and #898 and the profile and runtime paragraphs in #826 and #887 are different hunks from the Workspaces and Comparisons paragraphs edited here). #914 depends on the `runGit` and `gitEnvironment` surface fixed here.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 is the root; T2 depends on T1; T3 depends on T2; T4 depends on T1 and T2; T5 depends on T3 and T4. The graph is acyclic and every dependency names a declared task. T3 and T4 touch disjoint source files (`workspace-inspection.ts` and `workspace-comparison.ts` against `operator-setup.ts`) and may run concurrently after T2 if split; `git-process.ts` and `test/fixtures/git-environment.ts` are shared and read-only for them except that T3 deletes `stopOwnedChild` and `waitForExit`. T1, T2 and T5 share `git-process.ts` or the fixture and run in order. One owner is expected; the whole issue fits one PR.

#### 1. Shared environment and hardened core verification

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** None.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/child-environment.ts` (new `gitEnvironment(base = process.env)`: `childProcessEnvironment(base)`, delete every `GIT_*`, set the four variables); `src/standalone/git-process.ts` (replace the local definition with `export { gitEnvironment } from "../core/child-environment.js"`, drop the now-unused import); `src/core/github-source.ts` (`checkoutOrigin(path, timeout = 5000)`; the three `execFileAsync` calls pass `env: gitEnvironment()`; remove the unused `childProcessEnvironment` import); `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts` (call site only: `checkoutOrigin(dir, probeTimeout)`); new `test/fixtures/git-environment.ts`; `test/project-setup.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/project-setup.test.ts`, new test "repository verification ignores inherited GIT_* overrides", using `createSetupHome` and `checkout` from `test/fixtures/setup-home.ts` to make `~/src/atlas` with origin `git@github.com:acme/atlas.git`. Inside `withHostileGitEnvironment` with the probe's `binDirectory` first on `PATH`: `verifiedRepository({repositoryId:"R", path, ref:"main"}, {owner:"acme", name:"atlas"})` resolves with `gitCommonDirectory` equal to the real common directory (it fails with `origin-missing` before the change); `checkoutOrigin(path)` returns `{owner:"acme", name:"atlas"}`; `probe.invocations()` holds at least the three verification invocations and each equals the hardened set exactly. After the helper restores the environment, assert `process.env.GIT_DIR` is unset again. Existing `verifiedRepository` reason assertions run unchanged.
**Implementation:** Move, do not copy, the function body. Keep `waitForExit` and `stopOwnedChild` in `git-process.ts` for now. The fixture shim is a `#!/bin/sh` script with literal absolute paths: append `env | grep '^GIT_' | sort` between invocation markers to a log file, then `exec` the real Git found by `which git` at creation; `invocations()` parses the log into one `Record<string,string>` per call (split at the first `=`).
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/project-setup.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime-service.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-api.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-model.test.js`; expect all tests to pass.
**Complete when:** The core verification calls run with the shared environment, proved against hostile `GIT_*` values and by recorded invocation, and existing verification behaviour is unchanged.

#### 2. Bounded runner and the workspace adapter

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's fixture and `gitEnvironment` location.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/git-process.ts` (new `runGit`, `GitRunOptions`, `GitRunResult`, `GitRunFailure`); `src/standalone/workspaces.ts` (delete private `runGit` and `GitRunOptions`; `WorkspaceManager.git` and `reportGitFailure` adapt the runner result; `childProcessEnvironment` import removed); new `test/git-process.test.ts`; `test/workspaces.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/git-process.test.ts` with `/bin/sh` scripts as `executable` and tiny grace and observation windows: stdout is returned and the environment is the hardened set under `withHostileGitEnvironment`; `input` reaches stdin (`cat` echoes it); `printf partial; exit 3` gives `exit` with code 3 and stdout `partial`; a stalled child with `timeoutMs: 20` gives `interrupted/timed-out` with `childExitObserved: true`; output above `maxOutputBytes` gives `interrupted/output-limit`; an abort after spawn gives `interrupted/cancelled`, and an already-aborted signal gives `cancelled` with `spawned: false` and no marker file written by the script; a missing executable resolves `interrupted/failed` with `spawned: false`. `test/workspaces.test.ts`, new test "workspace Git runs with the hardened environment": under `withHostileGitEnvironment` with the probe as `gitExecutable`, provision a two-repository task, reopen and re-validate, then archive-and-clean it; the binding states and results match the unhardened flows, and every recorded invocation (`rev-parse`, `status`, `worktree add`, `worktree remove`) equals the hardened set. Every existing test in the file passes unchanged.
**Implementation:** Move the body of `runGit` into `git-process.ts` and generalise only what the decision above lists. Keep the timer, `onExit`/`onClose`, `beginFailure`/`finishFailure`, detach-and-`unref` and the sticky-abort semantics line for line; replace the final `resolve`/`reject` with the three result variants; add `stdio: input === undefined ? ["ignore","pipe","pipe"] : ["pipe","pipe","pipe"]` with a `stdin` error listener that begins a `failed` interruption and `stdin.end(input)`. Pass `env: gitEnvironment()` unconditionally. In `WorkspaceManager.git`, keep `assertNotCancelled()`, the per-operation deadline lookup, and the argument list `["-C", cwd, ...args]`; map the result as the Planning decisions state.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/git-process.test.js dist/test/workspaces.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime-service.test.js`; expect all tests to pass, including the controlled-Git stall, overflow, descendant and sticky-cancellation tests unchanged.
**Complete when:** Workspace Git uses the shared runner and environment with identical uncertainty, observer and cancellation results, and the runner contract is proved directly.

#### 3. Inspection and comparison use the runner

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2's `runGit`.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/workspace-inspection.ts` (`checkGitIgnore` keeps its signature and `IgnoreResult`; remove the `spawn`/`ChildProcess` imports and `gitEnvironment`/`stopOwnedChild` imports if unused); `src/standalone/workspace-comparison.ts` (`readGit` keeps its signature and `GitRead`; same import cleanup); `src/standalone/git-process.ts` (delete `waitForExit` and `stopOwnedChild`); `test/workspace-inspection.test.ts`; `test/workspace-comparison.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/workspace-inspection.test.ts`, new test: under `withHostileGitEnvironment` with the probe as `gitExecutable`, list a repository-scoped directory containing an ignored file; the ignored entry is still hidden and reported, and every recorded invocation equals the hardened set. `test/workspace-comparison.test.ts`, new test with the same pattern for a branch and an uncommitted comparison: results equal a comparison run without hostile values, and every recorded invocation equals the hardened set. Existing failing, stalled, time-limit, output-limit, candidate-limit, delayed, inherited-`GIT_INDEX_FILE` and promisor tests pass unchanged (they are the regression for the `exit`/`interrupted` mappings and the `unsettled` rule).
**Implementation:** `checkGitIgnore` passes `input` (the NUL-joined paths, still refusing inputs over 2 MiB first), `maxOutputBytes: 1 MiB`, `timeoutMs`, and the existing 100 ms/500 ms windows; parse stdout for `ok` or `exit` with code 1, return `{complete:false}` otherwise, keeping the allowed-path and trailing-NUL validation. `readGit` keeps its deadline arithmetic and `-C root --no-replace-objects -c core.fsmonitor=false` prefix, passes `maxOutputBytes: workspaceComparisonLimits.maxGitOutputBytes` and the 50 ms/250 ms windows, and maps results as the Planning decisions state.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/workspace-inspection.test.js dist/test/workspace-comparison.test.js dist/test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.js dist/test/operator-comparisons.test.js dist/test/turn-capture-service.test.js`; expect all tests to pass and no unused import to remain.
**Complete when:** Neither module spawns a process or builds its own child lifecycle, and their results and failure classes are unchanged.

#### 4. Setup probes use the runner

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T1`, `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T1's `checkoutOrigin` signature and T2's `runGit`.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts` (`currentBranch` calls `runGit({args:["-C", dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "-q", "HEAD"], timeoutMs: probeTimeout, terminationGraceMs: 100, observationMs: 500, maxOutputBytes: 1 MiB})` and keeps the 255-character and empty-output rules; delete `probeEnv`, `execFileAsync` and the `node:child_process`, `node:util` and `childProcessEnvironment` imports if unused); `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts` or `test/operator-setup-model.test.ts` (whichever owns the folder-listing and checkout-probe tests).
**Test:** New test: under `withHostileGitEnvironment` with the probe first on `PATH`, `listHomeFolders` for a home folder holding a checkout returns the same entry (`kind: "git"`, `origin: "acme/atlas"`, `branch: "main"`) as without hostile values, `verifyCheckout` returns `state: "verified"` with the same origin and branch, and every recorded invocation (`remote get-url`, `symbolic-ref`, `rev-parse`) equals the hardened set. A checkout on a detached `HEAD` still reports `branch: null`. Existing setup tests pass unchanged.
**Implementation:** Replace the `execFile` branch probe with the runner and keep its `catch`-to-`null` behaviour (`interrupted`, `exit` and thrown errors all return `null`).
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-setup-api.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-model.test.js dist/test/project-setup.test.js`; expect all tests to pass.
**Complete when:** Setup probes and verification share the hardened environment and keep their verification-error identity and field feedback.

#### 5. Inventory guard, documentation and integrated check

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T3`, `T4`
**Prerequisites:** T3 and T4 merged on the branch.
**Files and symbols:** new `test/git-environment.test.ts`; `docs/SPEC.md` ("Workspaces and execution access" and the "Comparisons and turn capture" sentence about `GIT_*`).
**Test:** `test/git-environment.test.ts` scans `src/**/*.ts` (located from `import.meta.url`, two levels above `dist/test`). Every file that imports `node:child_process` and contains a `"git"` string literal must also call `gitEnvironment(`; the expected matches are exactly `src/standalone/git-process.ts` and `src/core/github-source.ts`; `workspaces.ts`, `workspace-inspection.ts`, `workspace-comparison.ts` and `operator-setup.ts` must no longer import `node:child_process` at all (type-only imports included). At the planned SHA the scan flags `github-source.ts`, `workspaces.ts` and `operator-setup.ts`, so it fails before the change. A self-check feeds the scanner a synthetic source with `spawn("git", …)` and no `gitEnvironment(` and expects it to be flagged. Mark the scan with a `ponytail:` comment: it reads text, cannot see a dynamically built command, and becomes "`src/core` does not import `node:child_process`" when #914 lands.
**Implementation:** In `docs/SPEC.md`, add to "Workspaces and execution access" one revised-in-place statement: every Git subprocess the service starts (workspace provisioning, cleanup and identity checks, file and comparison reads, setup probes and repository verification) clears inherited `GIT_*` variables, never prompts, lazily fetches objects or allows transport protocols, and uses bounded time and output, so a repository that needs the network to supply objects fails closed; and trim the comparison sentence to reference it while keeping its fsmonitor, replacement-ref and filter text. No dated or amendment wording.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/git-environment.test.js`; expect all tests to pass. Then `npm run lint && npm run format:check`; expect no findings.
**Complete when:** A new unhardened Git spawn in `src` fails the suite, and the contract is documented.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Every Git invocation, including the remaining core repository-verification calls, uses the same hardened environment (issue acceptance) | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | Per-caller recorded-invocation tests in T1–T4 and the source guard in T5 |
| Inventory production Git callers; all use the shared hardened environment | 5 | `test/git-environment.test.ts` scan expects exactly the runner and core verification files |
| Hostile `GIT_*` values do not reach or change any caller | 1, 2, 3, 4 | `withHostileGitEnvironment` tests in `project-setup`, `workspaces`, `workspace-inspection`, `workspace-comparison` and setup suites |
| No interactive prompt, lazy network fetch or protocol widening | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Exact hardened set asserted at the child; existing promisor-helper test shows the set blocks a fetch |
| Timeouts, output caps, cancellation and uncertain child exit keep their bounds and are never reported as settled | 2, 3 | `test/git-process.test.ts`; unchanged controlled-Git, time-limit, output-limit and stalled-executable tests |
| Workspace add, remove, archive status and recovery re-validation still work | 2 | Hardened workspace test plus the unchanged `workspaces` suite (no `worktree prune` caller exists) |
| Repository origin and ref checks, and setup's verification-error identity and field feedback, are unchanged | 1, 4 | Unchanged `project-setup` reason assertions; setup probe test |
| Cancellation and uncertainty are exact-child only, never by name or command | 2 | Runner kills only the spawned `ChildProcess`; `git-process.test.ts` abort and timeout cases |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root with Node 24.21.0 first on `PATH` (the version in `.node-version`; CI runs Node 24 and Node 26 with npm 12.2.0, and the Node 26 job is checked on the PR), run `npm ci` then `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate before the PR is marked ready; expect typecheck, lint, format check, build and the full suite to pass. Playwright is cached; the browser suites in the full check need no extra setup.
- No bounded live runtime probe is required: the change adds no Codex, Claude, GitHub or UI behaviour. The service-level suites in T3 already exercise inspection, comparison and capture through the real service and SQLite. Do not spend paid or live runtime calls for this issue.

### Review focus

- Fidelity of the runner against the original `WorkspaceManager.runGit` (timers, detach, sticky abort, observer once per failure) and the three adapters' mappings, above all comparison's `unsettled` and the workspace `uncertain` flag.
- That the core environment function adds no `src/standalone` import to `src/core` and no process spawn.
- That the SPEC statement matches the environment actually applied.
- Entry points to report: workspace provisioning and cleanup (task and archive flows), Files and Changes reads, turn capture, project setup (folder picker, checkout verification), project create and configure, and imported-task repository re-verification. All consume these modules unchanged; no screen, context menu, extension, deep link or notification needs editing. The change adds no state-changing action and no irreversible operation, so no counterpart is needed.

### Re-plan triggers (task-specific)

- A supported setup that needs an inherited `GIT_*` variable, a credential helper prompt, git-lfs smudge or a transport protocol for workspace provisioning or verification. Return it as a product decision rather than weakening the environment.
- A production Git caller in `src` that the inventory missed and that cannot use the runner or `gitEnvironment()` without changing its observable result.

content.title: Use targeted task, assignment and recovery reads in the operator API

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/875
**Planned against:** `main` at `f0a43304342796c5085d555903cd472498ebbd4d`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Replace the history-wide rebuilds on the operator read paths with SQL-filtered reads, and turn `requireTask` and the assignment lookup into primary-key reads, without changing any response, status, ordering or disclosure bound. Implementation branch: `cb/875-targeted-operator-reads`, from `main` at or after the planned SHA (main has since advanced to `a1a1f53c`, #915; its delta is `src/core/coordination.ts` and `test/coordination.test.ts` only, disjoint from this plan). One PR, five observable slices.

1. **Lookups (T1).** `DomainStore.required()` throws a typed `DomainNotFoundError` (same message). `requireTask` becomes `domain.task(id)` plus an equivalent primary-key project-visibility check; `requireAssignment` serves `readAssignmentRecovery`; the three duplicated 10,000-identity guards become one helper.
2. **Store reads (T2).** Additive, parity-tested reads: recovery records by assignment/version/work or by task, one current turn request per assignment, turn requests by task, a task's executions, queued deliveries by task, capped row counts, plus the indexes that make them index searches.
3. **Exclusions (T3).** `exclusions()` evaluates its global 128-row bounds with capped counts before it builds any row, then reads only the task's own rows. This is the privacy boundary; T4 and T5 wait for its evidence.
4. **Adoption (T4).** `selectAssignmentExecution` (operator API and the retained `/runtime` pages), `readRuntimeSettings`, `readAssignmentRecovery` and `CoordinationView.readTask` use the targeted reads.
5. **Proof (T5).** One integrated test shows that unrelated history changes neither the output nor the number of history rows read by task list, task detail, project, Inbox, runtime settings, assignment recovery and the retained pages.

### Guardrails

- **Unchanged contracts:** every operator read response (fields, order, `observedAt` semantics); statuses and codes (`404 not-found` for an unknown or invisible task or assignment, `400 invalid-input` for a malformed ID, `503 unavailable` above 10,000 catalogue identities for the task list, composer options and the Inbox); `DomainStore.taskCatalog()` keeps its `LIMIT 10001` sentinel (`test/operator-task-list.test.ts` asserts length 10001 directly); the Inbox item assembly, sort, fingerprint, cursor format and 100-row pages (#898 adds filters on top); `catalogFingerprint`; the `projects()` instruction-revision join; the retained full-history methods `ExecutionState.recoveryView/list`, `SchedulerStore.list`, `CoordinationStore.queuedDeliveries` and the `StandaloneService.recoveryView/turnRequests/list` wrappers (scheduler, supervisor and tests use them; they become the parity oracles); persisted row content (this plan adds indexes only).
- **Visibility rule:** a task is readable only if its `domain_tasks`/`tasks` row exists and its project is listed by `projects()` (the project's current instruction revision row exists). The replacement must give the identical answer, including when that revision row or the `tasks` base row is missing.
- **Disclosure bounds stay global and fail closed:** `exclusions(projectId, taskId)` still returns `undefined` when the installation holds more than 128 turn requests or more than 128 recovery identities, the task has more than 128 assignments, more than 400 history bindings are supplied, a retained row names no known assignment, or a captured profile or project revision is not covered. Do not scope the 128-row bound to the task; any change to it or to visibility needs a separate explicit decision. No code deletes `turn_requests` or recovery identities, so once an installation has recorded more than 128 of either every task-scoped read withholds prose today; this plan preserves that and only removes the cost of discovering it.
- **Existing tests unchanged:** no existing test file is edited. New tests go in new files (this also avoids conflicts with in-flight PRs that append to `test/domain.test.ts` and `test/coordination.test.ts`).
- **Out of scope:** #877 (request-local exclusion base and prepared redactor), #878 (per-task Git on polled reads), #879 (scheduler wake queries), #873 (message-to-status mapping, `executeDomain`, `conflicts`), the optional typed catalogue overflow error, `DomainStore.leadBindings()` and `assignments(taskId)` scans (not history), paging inside `CoordinationView.readTask`, `requireProject`, web and CLI code, docs, and any layout (no UI change; if a task appears to need one, report a blocker).
- **(a) Plan-seam mismatch: one diagnosis plus two repair cycles in total**, only when a factual assumption in this plan about the repository or an approved seam is wrong. Examples: a targeted read cannot reproduce its retained full-history oracle on a real fixture without changing observable output or order; `ExecutionState.recoveryRecord` cannot be extracted without changing `recoveryView()`; `task(id)` plus `projectListed` cannot reproduce the retired scan on a fixture; the capped counts cannot express the existing global bound; a stakeholder-visible visibility or disclosure change turns out to be unavoidable. After the diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, stop and report for a replan.
- **(b) Ordinary in-scope repairs: owner repairs, no allowance, they do not consume (a):** implementation bugs; type, lint and format errors; fixture and test setup (including the forbidden-method sets in the guards); equivalent paths, names or line numbers; documentation text; rebase conflicts with #900, #898, #826, #877, #878, #873, #872, #879 or #887; and CI or flaky-test retries (including Node 26 and npm 12.2.0 lockfile or runner fixes). Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes, or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews; no integration amendment is needed unless a published integration decision changes.

### Planning decisions

- **What "does not scale with total historical work" means.** Rows read from history tables (`turn_requests`, `execution_intents`, `execution_recovery_identities`, `task_execution_bindings`, `coordination_delivery_batches`) by one read depend only on the rows of the tasks and assignments that read covers plus the two capped counts, never on other tasks' or unbound history. The task list, project and Inbox still enumerate the bounded catalogue (at most 10,000 identities): the Inbox must inspect every task, and that is not history. T5 measures exactly this.
- **`requireTask` = `task(id)` + `projectListed`.** The retired loop returned a task iff `d.tasks(p.id)` (join `domain_tasks`/`tasks` on `t.projectId`) listed it for a project in `projects()`. `DomainStore.task` runs the same join by primary key and `projectListed(projectId)` runs the `projects()` join for one project by primary key, so the two are equivalent by construction; T1 proves it on the failure fixtures. `requireProject` is unchanged.
- **Typed not-found is mapped by the API, once.** `OperatorApi.existing(read)` converts only `DomainNotFoundError` into `OperatorApiError(404, "not-found")` and is used by `requireTask` and `requireAssignment` (which today swallows every error into 404). Mapping in `apiFailure` (operator.ts) was rejected: it would change statuses of every other read and of POST commands (which report an unclassified failure as `command-outcome-unknown`), and #873 owns the generalised mapping. A non-missing failure now propagates (503 on reads) instead of being reported as 404.
- **`readAssignmentRecovery` finds its task by primary key** (`requireAssignment`), not by scanning `taskCatalog()` x `assignments()`. It never had the 10,000 guard and now has no catalogue dependency, so it is unaffected by overflow. Side effect, aligned with `readTask`, whose lookup was never limited by the catalogue cap: an assignment on a task sorted beyond the first 10,001 catalogue ids was a 404 by truncation and is now readable. This is not a visibility-policy change; T1 pins it.
- **One catalogue guard, `taskCatalog()` untouched.** `OperatorApi.catalog()` calls `taskCatalog()` and throws `OperatorApiError(503, "unavailable")` above 10,000; `readTaskListPageOnce`, `readComposerOptionsOnce` and `readInbox` use it. The optional typed overflow error would force `taskCatalog()` to throw and break the existing test that asserts the sentinel, so it is skipped.
- **Recovery records.** The per-work body of `ExecutionState.recoveryView()` moves verbatim into `private recoveryRecord(workId)`; `recoveryView()` and the new reads only differ in which `workId`s they pass, always ordered by `execution_recovery_identities.rowid` as today. `recoveryFor(assignmentId, version, workId?)` joins `task_execution_bindings` on `(assignmentId, assignmentVersion)`; `recoveryForTask(taskId, alsoWorkId?)` selects `workId IN (bindings of the task UNION the optional work)` so `readAssignmentRecovery` can still include the unbound record of its selected request without changing record order. A non-integer version returns no records, as the in-memory filter did. Witness and disposition lookups stay inside `recoveryRecord`.
- **Selection.** `selectAssignmentExecution` chose the newest `active` request, else the newest request of the assignment's version, by `sequence`. `SchedulerStore.current(assignmentId, version)` runs those two `ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 1` queries (no prompts for other requests), `executionForWork` replaces `list().find(workId)`, and with a request the record is `recoveryFor(id, requestVersion, request.workId)[0]`; without one it is the newest by `generation.requestSequence` of `recoveryFor(id, requestVersion)`.
- **Task executions and deliveries.** `CoordinationView.readTask` built `history` from every intent plus a binding lookup and filtered every queued delivery. `ExecutionState.taskExecutions(taskId)` returns the `{intent, binding}` pairs of one task (the existing JS sort by `workId` and the `recoveryDispositionForWork` lookup stay) and `CoordinationStore.queuedDeliveriesForTask(taskId)` is `queuedDeliveries()` with `AND taskId = ?`, same `ORDER BY createdAt, batchId`.
- **Counts before rows.** `SchedulerStore.countUpTo(limit)` and `ExecutionState.recoveryCountUpTo(limit)` run `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM <table> LIMIT ?)`, so the check costs at most `limit` rows. `StandaloneService.retainedRowsExceed(limit)` is true when either count exceeds `limit`. A malformed unrelated recovery row no longer poisons every task's exclusions (it was parsed only because the full view was built); the task's own rows are still parsed and any failure still returns `undefined`.
- **Indexes (additive, `IF NOT EXISTS`, no data change).** `turn_requests_taskId_sequence` and `turn_requests_assignmentId_sequence` on `(column, sequence)` (the same names #900 uses for the same purpose; if #900 has merged, reuse its loop), and `task_execution_bindings_task(taskId)` and `task_execution_bindings_assignment(assignmentId, assignmentVersion)`. Verified plan-time with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on a scratch SQLite 3.53.4 (Node 24.21.0): the five statements for recovery by assignment, recovery by task, turn requests by assignment, turn requests by task and a task's executions are index `SEARCH`es; the queued-delivery statement scans only the partial index `coordination_one_queued_delivery` (queued rows only). No other index is added (`domain_assignments(taskId)` is outside this issue).
- **Test strategy.** The retained full-history methods are the oracles, so parity needs no recorded goldens. Two guards give non-scaling evidence: a `forbid` Proxy that throws on named full-history methods (deterministic, immune to background service work) and a `node:sqlite` `StatementSync.prototype.all/get` spy keyed by `sourceSQL` that counts rows returned from history tables (verified on Node 24.21.0; `sourceSQL` is typed in `@types/node` 26.6.5). The row-count comparison allows a small fixed slack for idle background statements.
- **Docs.** No user-visible behaviour or contract changes (`docs/SPEC.md` and `docs/design/ui03-tasks.md` already state the 10,000 catalogue and 128-revision budgets this plan preserves), so no document is edited. The CLI2/CLI3 evidence records list #875 as a limit; evidence records are dated history and stay unedited.
