**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/targeted-read-stores.test.js dist/test/coordination.test.js dist/test/coordination-view.test.js dist/test/recovery.test.js dist/test/recovery-continuation.test.js dist/test/no-turn-recovery.test.js dist/test/standalone.test.js`; expect exit 0 and no failures.
**Complete when:** Every new read matches its full-history oracle in rows and order on the mixed fixture, the indexes exist on new and reopened databases, and the existing store and recovery suites pass unchanged.

#### 3. Exclusions: capped counts before rows (privacy boundary)

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1, T2`
**Prerequisites:** T1 (`forbid`), T2 (`retainedRowsExceed`, `turnRequestsForTask`, `recoveryForTask`, `seedOrphanHistory`).
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`exclusions`, the `if (taskId)` block at L497); `test/fixtures/read-guards.ts` (add `historyRowCounter()`: spies `StatementSync.prototype.all` and `get` via `t.mock.method`, counts rows returned by statements whose `sourceSQL` names `turn_requests`, `execution_intents`, `execution_recovery_identities`, `task_execution_bindings` or `coordination_delivery_batches`, and returns a reader); new `test/operator-targeted-exclusions.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/operator-targeted-exclusions.test.ts`: a one-task world written locally like `seed(f, true)` in `test/operator-api.test.ts` (profile, project, ready task, one admitted turn) whose task title is a known string; `readTask(taskId).data.task.title` is the string when exclusions are available and `null` (with `contentUnavailable` true) when withheld.
- *Request bound:* with orphan `turn_requests` rows added until `f.service.turnRequests().length === 128` the title is present; one more row (129) withholds it. Same for recovery identities (orphan intent plus identity, no requests) at 128 and 129.
- *Counts before rows:* at 129 of either kind, a service wrapped by `forbid(f.service, ["recoveryView", "turnRequests", "list", "recoveryForTask", "turnRequestsForTask"])` still resolves `readTask` with a withheld title (no row read); at 128 only `recoveryView`, `turnRequests` and `list` are forbidden and the title is present. `historyRowCounter` (spy on `StatementSync.prototype.all/get` keyed by `sourceSQL`) shows at most two history-table rows returned by `api["exclusions"](projectId, taskId)` at 129 (slack 4 for idle background statements).
- *Fail-closed regressions (these pass on the unmodified baseline too):* withheld title when the task's assignment captured an uncovered revision (`UPDATE domain_assignments SET instructionsRevision = 99`); when a `turn_requests` row of the task names an unknown assignment; when a recovery binding of the task names an assignment not in the task; when 401 history bindings are passed (`api["exclusions"](projectId, taskId, bindings)` is `undefined`, 400 is defined); when the task has 129 assignment rows (copies of its assignment row with new IDs; 128 is defined).
**Implementation:** In the `if (taskId)` block: first `if (this.service.retainedRowsExceed(128)) return undefined;`, then `assignments = d.assignments(taskId)` and the existing `assignments.length > 128 || historyBindings.length > 400` check, then `requests = this.service.turnRequestsForTask(taskId)` and `recovery = this.service.recoveryForTask(taskId)`; `retained = [...requests, ...recovery.flatMap(r => r.binding ? [r.binding] : []), ...historyBindings]` and the rest (known-assignment test, per-assignment revision coverage, workspace values) is unchanged. All of it stays inside the existing `try`, so any failure still returns `undefined`.
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-targeted-exclusions.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-task-list.test.js dist/test/operator-instructions.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-assignment.test.js dist/test/operator-inbox.test.js`; expect exit 0 and no failures.
**Complete when:** The global 128-row and 400-binding bounds, the assignment bound and revision-coverage failures behave exactly as before, the bound is decided from capped counts without building any history row, and the privacy suites pass unchanged. T4 and T5 require this evidence.

#### 4. Adopt the targeted reads in selection, runtime settings, assignment recovery and the task view

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T1, T2, T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 passed (boundary gate); T1 for the `readAssignmentRecoveryOnce` head.
**Files and symbols:** `test/fixtures/read-guards.ts` (add `guardedCoordinationView(f)`: a `CoordinationView` over a second connection whose `ExecutionState` forbids `list` and `recoveryView` and whose `CoordinationStore` forbids `queuedDeliveries`); `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` (`RuntimeOperatorApi`: drop `list`, `recoveryView`, `turnRequests`; add `currentTurnRequest`, `executionForWork`, `recoveryFor`, `recoveryForTask`; `selectAssignmentExecution`; `executionHoldSection`; `taskPage`'s two `recoveryView()` calls become `recoveryForTask(taskId)`); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`readRuntimeSettingsOnce`, the `recoveryView()` filter of `readAssignmentRecoveryOnce`); `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts` (`readTask` `history` and `queued`); new `test/operator-targeted-selection.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/operator-targeted-selection.test.ts` over `seedCatalog(f)` plus `seedOperatorRecovery` and an assignment whose only request is `held` with a recovery identity that has no binding (insert by SQL). Oracles are the retired bodies reproduced in the test:
- `legacySelect(assignment, service)` (verbatim copy of the old `selectAssignmentExecution` body over `service.turnRequests()`, `recoveryView()`, `list()`) deep-equals `selectAssignmentExecution(assignment, service)` for every assignment of every task, including the unbound and the multi-version cases.
- Swap-in oracles through `t.mock.method`: replace `service.recoveryForTask` with `(t, w) => service.recoveryView().filter(r => r.binding?.taskId === t || r.workId === w)` and compare `readRuntimeSettings()` and `readAssignmentRecovery(a.id)` (all assignments, including the unbound-selected one) with `observedAt` removed; replace `state.taskExecutions` and `coordination.queuedDeliveriesForTask` with the legacy `list()`/`taskBinding`/`queuedDeliveries().filter` forms and compare `CoordinationView.readTask(taskId)` for every task (built over a second connection as `test/operator-api.test.ts` L530 does); compare the bodies of `/runtime/task/:id` and `/runtime/assignment/:id` from `runtimeOperatorRoutes(service)` with and without the swap, normalising generated `name="key" value="<uuid>"` fields.
- *Reads are scoped:* with `f.service` wrapped by `forbid(..., ["recoveryView", "turnRequests", "list"])` and `guardedCoordinationView(f)` passed as the third `OperatorApi` argument, `readTask`, `readAssignment`, `readRuntimeSettings` and `readAssignmentRecovery` resolve for every task and assignment.
**Implementation:** `selectAssignmentExecution(assignment, api: Pick<RuntimeOperatorApi, "currentTurnRequest" | "recoveryFor" | "executionForWork">)`: `request = api.currentTurnRequest(id, Number(assignment.version))`; `requestVersion = request?.assignmentVersion ?? Number(assignment.version)`; `record = request ? api.recoveryFor(id, requestVersion, request.workId)[0] : newest by generation.requestSequence of api.recoveryFor(id, requestVersion)`; `intent = request ? api.executionForWork(request.workId) : undefined`; same return shape. `readRuntimeSettingsOnce`: `this.service.recoveryForTask(taskId).filter(r => r.binding && known.has(r.binding.assignmentId))`. `readAssignmentRecoveryOnce`: `selected = this.selection(a).request` and `this.service.recoveryForTask(taskId, selected?.workId).filter(<unchanged predicate>)`. `CoordinationView.readTask`: `history` from `this.state.taskExecutions(id).map(({intent, binding}) => ({...same fields, recoveryDisposition lookup unchanged})).sort(workId)`, `queued` from `this.coordination.queuedDeliveriesForTask(id)`. Remove nothing else.
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-targeted-selection.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-configuration.test.js dist/test/operator-coordination.test.js dist/test/coordination-view.test.js dist/test/no-turn-recovery.test.js dist/test/operator-task-review.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-browse.test.js`; expect exit 0 and no failures.
**Complete when:** Selection, runtime settings, assignment recovery, the task view and the retained runtime pages return output identical to the retired implementations on the mixed fixture without calling any full-history read, and the existing suites pass unchanged.

#### 5. Integrated non-scaling proof

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T1, T3, T4`
**Prerequisites:** T3 and T4 passed. The test and its helpers name only retained methods, so they compile against unmodified production code: as a bounded sensitivity check, run the built test once with `src/` temporarily restored to the planned SHA (helpers kept) to confirm it fails there (forbidden methods are called; rows grow with the orphan count), restore, and record the result in the PR. It is not a gate.
**Files and symbols:** new `test/operator-targeted-reads.test.ts`; reuses `test/fixtures/read-guards.ts` (`forbid`, `historyRowCounter`, `guardedCoordinationView`) and `test/fixtures/operator-history.ts` (`seedOrphanHistory`).
**Test:** `test/operator-targeted-reads.test.ts`: world = `seedCatalog(f)` plus `seedOperatorRecovery(f, uncertainTaskIds, 5)`. `OperatorApi` over `forbid(f.service, ["recoveryView", "turnRequests", "list"])` with `guardedCoordinationView(f)`. Reads: `readTaskListPage()`, `readTask` (every task), `readProject(projectId)`, `readInbox()`, `readRuntimeSettings()`, `readAssignment` and `readAssignmentRecovery` (every assignment), and `/runtime/task/:id` and `/runtime/assignment/:id`.
- *Regime A (bound not reached):* let `room = 120 - max(turnRequests().length, recoveryView().length)`; record the normalised outputs and `historyRowCounter` totals per read at K = 0, then `seedOrphanHistory(f, room)` and repeat. Outputs deep-equal the K = 0 outputs (`observedAt` and generated keys removed) and each read's history-row total is at most the K = 0 total plus 8.
- *Regime B (bound exceeded):* add 300 more orphan generations: every read still resolves without a forbidden call, the per-read history-row total is at most the regime A total, and per task `id`, `state`, `version`, `ready`, `execution`, `admission` and `attention` equal regime A's while `title` is `null`; the retained runtime pages (which render no redacted prose) are equal to regime A.
- *Contract spot checks:* a completed task keeps its `completed` execution state and attention codes; an `uncertain` task keeps `execution.holds` and its single `execution-uncertain` attention code; the Inbox still lists its intervention item.
**Implementation:** Test code and the fixture helpers only; fix any production gap the test exposes in the owning slice (an ordinary repair).
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-targeted-reads.test.js dist/test/operator-inbox.test.js dist/test/operator-task-list.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-http.test.js`; expect exit 0 and no failures.
**Complete when:** Output and history-row cost of every listed read are independent of unrelated history in both regimes.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Task list, task detail, project and Inbox reads no longer scale with total historical work (issue AC1; fixtures with large unrelated history do not materialize it) | 3, 4, 5 | T5 regimes A and B (guarded service and view, row counters, output equality); T3 "counts before rows" |
| Existing operator API and recovery tests pass unchanged (AC2) | 1–5 | Each slice's Validate list runs the existing suites; no existing test file is edited; Final validation runs all |
| Task and assignment lookups are primary-key reads (AC3) | 1 | T1 "No scans" (`projects`, `tasks`, `taskCatalog` forbidden), `requireTask` parity |
| 404 behaviour for unknown task and assignment IDs is unchanged and tested (AC4) | 1 | T1 "404s over the API and HTTP", unlisted-project and malformed-ID cases |
| Filtered recovery, intent, request, binding and queued-delivery reads return the same rows in the same order, keep tie-breaks and the disposition lookup (brief) | 2, 4 | T2 oracle parity (including unbound record and rowid order); T4 swap-in oracles for `readTask`, runtime settings, assignment recovery and the retained pages |
| Typed not-found reads with an explicit equivalent project-visibility check (brief) | 1 | T1 `legacyRequireTask` matrix incl. missing revision row and missing base row |
| Catalogue overflow enforced consistently before projection; 503 retained; 10,000 and 10,001 boundary tested (brief) | 1 | T1 "Catalogue guard" (10,000 passes, 10,001 is `unavailable` for list, composer, Inbox; recovery by key unaffected) |
| Fail-closed exclusions, historical revision coverage and the global 128-row disclosure bound preserved; disclosure bounds tested (brief) | 3 | T3 request and identity 128/129, assignment and binding bounds, uncovered revision, unknown-assignment rows |
| Missing or inconsistent project revisions and recovery holds compare equal to existing views (brief) | 1, 2, 3 | T1 deleted-revision fixtures; T2 holds in `seedCatalog` and `seedOperatorRecovery`; T3 uncovered-revision regression |

### Final validation

- From the implementation worktree root, after `npm ci` (Node 24.21.0 from `.node-version` first on `PATH`; CI pins npm 12.2.0 and runs Node 26; Playwright is cached), run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate and again after any repair that touches production code; expect typecheck, lint, format check, build and the full test suite to pass, including the Chromium and WebKit suites and every new file.
- The new tests rely on `StatementSync#sourceSQL` and `mock.method` on the `node:sqlite` prototype, verified on Node 24.21.0 and typed in `@types/node` 26.6.5; CI on Node 26 confirms. No live runtime, paid call, deployment or cutover is part of this issue.
- Baseline at planning time (`f0a43304`, Node 24.21.0): `npm run build:service` exited 0 and 79 tests in `operator-api`, `operator-inbox`, `operator-task-list`, `operator-runtime`, `domain`, `coordination-view`, `recovery` and `operator-instructions` passed.

### Review focus

- Parity of each targeted read with its full-history oracle, above all record order (`execution_recovery_identities.rowid`), the unbound selected record in `readAssignmentRecovery`, and the `request ? find(workId) : newest by requestSequence` branch of selection.
- That no bound was scoped or loosened: the two global counts, the 128-assignment and 400-binding limits and revision coverage all remain, and the counts run before any row is built.
- That `requireTask` visibility matches the retired scan on every fixture, and that no 404-to-503 or 503-to-404 change leaked to other reads (only `requireTask` and `requireAssignment` map `DomainNotFoundError`).
- That the additive indexes use the names agreed with #900 and exist on both new and reopened databases.
- Entry points checked: web task list, project, task detail, Inbox, Settings runtime and assignment recovery, CLI `task list|get`, assignment reads and `capacity get`, and the retained `/runtime` and `/coordination` pages all read through the same unchanged API or view; none needs an edit and none gains an action.

### Re-plan triggers (task-specific)

- A parity oracle cannot be matched without changing observable output, order, a status code or a disclosure bound, or a decision is needed to scope or raise the global 128-row bound, change visibility, or keep an unrelated malformed row failing every task's exclusions: return it as a product decision instead of choosing.
- A conflicting `DomainNotFoundError` (different name, base class or message) lands from #873 before this branch merges.
- An existing test cannot pass unchanged: that is a contract change, not an ordinary repair.

content.title: Batch conversation delta writes instead of one fsynced commit per token

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/874
**Planned against:** `main` at `5ef46a8e9c3ea6debf0eadcc7bc47fe1deb822b0`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Batch the diagnostic delta byte counts inside `ConversationHistoryCapture`, the per-turn object that already owns bind, finish and discard. Pending counts per item stay in memory and are written in one SQLite transaction when an item completes or is omitted, when the turn finishes, when the capture is discarded (which includes service shutdown), when 64 distinct items are pending, or one second after the first unwritten delta. `started`, `completed` and `omitted` rows stay immediate. `ConversationHistoryStore` gains one batched write method. `service.ts`, `codex.ts` and the schema do not change.

### Guardrails

- Unchanged: the table schema, `ConversationHistoryStore.record` (including its per-call delta path and 64 KiB per-delta validity), `readAssignment`, redaction (`sanitizeConversationText`, `isDisclosable`; both are imported by `execution-diagnostics.ts` and `retained-evidence.ts`), exact thread/turn binding, early-buffer caps, and exclusions evaluated only for completed items. Completed text, omissions and `started` rows are written when they occur, as today.
- Out of scope: `PRAGMA journal_mode/synchronous` and every execution, recovery and coordination write (no global durability reduction); prepared-statement reuse (#880); exclusion sharing and redaction ordering (#877, #918); service component fields (#885); `codex.ts`, `claude.ts`, `service.ts`, operator contracts and UI; `docs/evidence/` records.
- Accepted limit, recorded in the issue: a crash may lose about one second of unwritten diagnostic delta byte counts. Do not claim more durability than that, and do not add a configuration option for the interval.
- A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example: the flush cannot live in the capture, `service.ts` turns out to need a change, or the capture lifecycle cannot flush on discard) allows one diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs are owner repairs with no allowance and do not consume that budget. They include rewriting an assertion this contract change obsoletes, type, lint and format fixes, timing or fake-timer fixes in the new tests, and mechanical rebases. Record each correction in the existing delivery record and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. An integration amendment is only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Placement.** The capture owns the lifecycle needed for a timer (`bind`, `finish`, `discard`; the service already calls `discard()` from `clearConversationCaptures()` in `stop()` before runtimes stop and the database closes). A timer in the store would have no owner (many tests construct stores on throwaway databases). A service-side batcher would touch `service.ts`, which other open work edits.
- **Flush rules.** The first unwritten delta arms a one-shot 1000 ms `setTimeout(...).unref()`. It is not reset by later deltas, so an unwritten count is at most about one second old. `flush()` always clears the timer and writes all pending items in one `transaction()` (`src/core/store.ts`). It also runs before any non-`started` event is persisted, so a `completed` or `omitted` row never precedes its item's count. It runs in `finish()` before `omitIncomplete`: otherwise the UPDATE marks the row `omitted` and the lifecycle-guarded UPSERT would drop the count. It runs in `discard()`, so graceful shutdown and failed turns lose nothing; an unbound capture has no pending counts and writes nothing. It runs when a 65th distinct item would be added; 64 matches `maxPendingConversationItems` in `codex.ts`, which bounds memory to 64 map entries.
- **Late deltas.** The UPSERT keeps `WHERE lifecycle IN ('started','streaming')`, so a delta for a settled item cannot reopen it; at worst it costs one no-op write. `CodexRuntime` stops projecting deltas for an item once it completes, and `ClaudeRuntime` emits no deltas.
- **Storage failure.** `flush()` never throws, because the timer callback would otherwise be an uncaught exception. A failed batch is dropped, which keeps memory bounded, and the transaction rolls back. Later deltas persist normally, as in the old per-delta behaviour.
- **Write budget.** Per item: one `started` write, one completion or omission write, and at most one more write when the count was pending at that point; plus one write per second of continuous streaming. Hundreds of deltas no longer add hundreds of fsynced commits.
- **Contract change.** An in-flight row is `started` with `deltaBytes` 0 until the first flush. Only one existing assertion depends on the old timing (see T1). The readers (`readAssignment` through the coordination view, operator API, `assignment history` CLI, task workspace and the coordination HTML "Partial assistant item; N streamed bytes" line) keep their shapes and now show a count that lags by up to about a second. No other entry point writes deltas; there is no user-initiated state change and no new irreversible operation, schema change or migration, so no counterpart is needed. Rollback is reverting the commit.
- **Baseline.** #900 (PR #916) merged to `main` while this plan was being prepared (`a1a1f53c` to `5ef46a8e`). That delta changes none of this plan's files (`conversation-history.ts`, `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts`), and `service.ts` gains only adjacent diagnostics lines. CI `check` and `check-node-26` both passed on `main` at `5ef46a8e`. On a clean `git archive` of `5ef46a8e`, `tsc` was clean and `s05-conversation-history` plus `s05-conversation-ui` passed 11/11 with Node 24.21.0. A throwaway prototype of this design in that export passed the 8 new tests in T1 (5 runs) and the T1 and T2 service tests (3 runs, 20/20 across the three files), and failed only the one assertion T1 rewrites. The prototype is not part of the plan; implement from the slices below.
- **Known unrelated CI flake.** On `main` at `a1a1f53c`, CI `check` on Node 24 failed once in `test/browser-diagnostics.test.ts` ("timed-out execution preserves a live client...", assertion `elapsedMs >= 80`) while `check-node-26` passed on the same SHA. It touches no code here. If it recurs on this PR, rerun once and report it; do not edit that test under this issue.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/codex.ts` — `CodexRuntime.projectConversationEvent` handles `item/agentMessage/delta` (L2195) and emits one `delta` event per notification (`bytes` is the UTF-8 length) while the item is `capturing`. Per-item limits are 64 KiB and 4096 fragments; per-turn limits are 64 pending and 256 total items. `src/standalone/claude.ts` emits only `started` and `completed`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `runtime.onConversationEvent` (L1208) calls `receiveConversationEvent` (L4952), which routes to the capture keyed `runtimeKey(harness, threadId)`. `beginConversationCapture` (L4658) builds the capture after the thread binds. The turn run binds it with `bind(exactBinding)` or calls `discard()`, calls `finish()` after `waitForTurn` (L4453), and calls `discard()` in `finally`. `stop()` runs "conversation-capture cleanup" (L1388), which calls `clearConversationCaptures()` (L4969) and so `discard()` on each capture. The database uses `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; synchronous = FULL` (L508), so every unbatched write is one fsynced commit. All required lifecycle hooks exist; `service.ts` is not edited.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/conversation-history.ts` — `ConversationHistoryStore.record` (L168) issues the delta UPSERT per call. `ConversationHistoryCapture` (L389): `receive` (L398) buffers until `bind` (L421) replays; `finish` (L447) runs `omitIncomplete`; `discard` (L458); `persist` (L463) makes one `store.record` call per event.
- **Existing:** `src/core/store.ts` — `transaction(db, fn)` is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, then `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`, and is already used by `src/standalone/execution-diagnostics.ts`. The service uses one synchronous connection, and `flush()` is only called from event, timer or async-continuation turns, never inside another transaction.
- **New:** `src/standalone/conversation-history.ts` — module function `validDeltaBytes(bytes)` (safe integer, > 0, <= `maxHistoryTextBytes`); constants `deltaFlushMs = 1000` and `maxPendingDeltaItems = 64`; `ConversationHistoryStore.recordDeltaBytes(binding, deltas)` and private `addDeltaBytes`; capture fields `pendingDeltas` and `flushTimer`; private `addDelta` and `flush`.
- **New:** `test/conversation-history-batching.test.ts` — capture-level tests over an in-memory `DatabaseSync` with fake timers.
- **Follow:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` (`this.timer.unref()`, L355) for timer hygiene; `test/browser-diagnostics.test.ts` (L375, `t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout"] })` with `t.mock.timers.tick`) for fake timers; `HistoryRuntime`, `fixture`, `createTaskAssignment`, `query`, `waitUntil` and `waitForExecutionState` in `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts` for service-level tests.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic: T1 is the root; T2 depends on T1. Run them sequentially with one owner: T2 adds a test to `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts`, which T1 also edits, and its assertions need T1's behaviour. No ready tasks may run concurrently. Shared files with other work, as of `main` `5ef46a8e`, open PRs (#920 for #884, draft, head `6f38e7b2`), branch `cb/898-operate-tasks-attention` (`5ef46a8e`, no commits yet) and the published plans:
- **#900 (PR #916):** merged and in this baseline. It imports `sanitizeConversationText`, which stays unchanged, and adds `execution-diagnostics.ts`. No file overlap. Independent.
- **#884 (draft PR #920):** `git-process`, `workspaces`, `workspace-*`, `github-source`, `child-environment`, `operator-setup` and their tests, plus `docs/SPEC.md` at the Git subprocess paragraph (about L394) and the comparison paragraph (about L789). We edit `docs/SPEC.md` only at the assistant history paragraph (L1068). Different hunks, so a textual merge is safe. Independent in either order.
- **#875 (plan 6114106348):** `operator-api.ts`, `domain.ts`, `state.ts`/`scheduler.ts`/`coordination.ts` reads, `operator-runtime.ts` and `coordination-view`. Its plan records no overlap with #874, and none of those files is edited here. Independent.
- **#898 (plan 6113716740) and #826 (plan 6112128888):** per their plans: `contracts.ts`, `operator-api.ts`, `operator-runtime.ts`, `state.ts`, CLI files, and in `service.ts` only the Stop/Resume (`afterStop`) and harness-status regions. No overlap. Independent.
- **#872** (`domain.ts` and the `service.ts` routing loop), **#897** (CLI source and delivery commands) and **#887** (`state.ts` stop-interrupt text, `operator-runtime.ts`, `service.ts`/`supervisor.ts` messages): no shared file or symbol. Independent.
- **Same-file risks outside that set**, all in other regions or mechanical: #877 (`sanitizeConversationText` and the completed branch of `persist`), #918 (`sanitizeConversationText`, not ready), #880 (statement caching behind `Database`; the new tests count `exec`/`run`, not `prepare`, so they stay valid), and #885 (`service.ts` fields; this plan does not edit `service.ts`). A concurrent run needs at most a mechanical rebase of `conversation-history.ts`.
- **Verdict:** #874 may run concurrently with #884, #875, #898, #826, #872, #897 and #887, and with the open #845.

#### 1. Batch delta byte counts in the capture

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none` (reserved root marker; not a task ID)
**Prerequisites:** none. No separate proof task: the design was checked against the current code (see Planning decisions, Baseline).
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/conversation-history.ts` (`ConversationHistoryStore`, `ConversationHistoryCapture`, new `validDeltaBytes`, `recordDeltaBytes`, `addDeltaBytes`, `addDelta`, `flush`); `test/conversation-history-batching.test.ts` (new); `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts` (only the test "keeps incomplete delta bytes out of SQLite and redacts both turn-start and current values").
**Test:** In `test/conversation-history-batching.test.ts`, use an in-memory `DatabaseSync`, wrapped as the narrow `Database` from `src/core/store.ts` so `commits` counts durable commits. `exec` of `BEGIN*` marks a transaction open, `COMMIT` closes it and adds 1, and `ROLLBACK` closes it. A `prepare(sql).run` outside a transaction whose SQL starts with `INSERT` or `UPDATE` adds 1. Reset `commits` to 0 after constructing `ConversationHistoryStore`. Build a `ConversationHistoryCapture` with `captureStartExclusions: []` and `currentExclusions: () => []`, and bind it to work-1, task-1, assignment-1, thread-1, turn-1 with every revision 1. A `row(itemId)` helper returns `{ ...row }`, because `node:sqlite` rows have a null prototype and `deepEqual` needs plain objects. Every test calls `t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout"] })` and closes the database in `finally`. The 8 tests:
1. "deltas cost one commit per item event or flush interval, never one per delta": bind, `started(a)` gives commits 1. 500 × `delta(a, 3)` leaves commits 1, with row a `started` and `deltaBytes` 0. `tick(999)` leaves 1. `tick(1)` gives 2 with row a `streaming` and `deltaBytes` 1500. 300 more deltas then `tick(1000)` gives 3 and `deltaBytes` 2400. `tick(10000)` leaves 3 (an idle capture arms no timer). `completed(a, "done")` gives 4 with row a `completed`, text "done" and `deltaBytes` 2400.
2. "pending counts are written before completion, omission and turn end": items `done`, `dropped` and `open` are each `started` then `delta(4)`. `completed(done)` makes both `done` and `dropped` show `deltaBytes` 4 (one flush covers all items). `delta(dropped, 1)` then `omitted(dropped, "size-limit")` gives row `omitted` with `deltaBytes` 5. `delta(open, 2)` then `finish()` gives row `omitted` with reason `turn-ended` and `deltaBytes` 6 (flush precedes `omitIncomplete`). Then `runAll()`, `tick(5000)` and one more `delta(open, 9)` leave commits and `deltaBytes` unchanged.
3. "late, foreign and post-completion deltas never reopen or move a settled item": after `completed(a, "done")`, receive `delta(a, 7)` on the same turn, one with `turnId: "other"` and one with `threadId: "other"`. `tick(1000)` adds exactly one commit (the same-turn delta's guarded no-op UPSERT). Row a is still `completed` with text "done" and `deltaBytes` 0, and only one row exists.
4. "deltas buffered before the turn binds are written as one aggregate": an unbound capture receives `started(a)`, 100 × `delta(a, 2)` and a delta for `turnId: "other"`; no rows exist. After `bind` commits is 1, and after `tick(1000)` it is 2 with rows `[a, streaming, 200]` only.
5. "discard writes bound counts once and an unbound discard writes nothing": unbound `delta` then `discard()` and `runAll()` leave 0 rows. For a bound capture, `delta(a, 2)` then `discard()` gives commits 1 and `deltaBytes` 2. After `runAll()`, a further delta is ignored and commits stays 1.
6. "pending items are bounded by flushing before the cap is exceeded": 64 distinct items with `delta(1)` leave commits 0. A 65th distinct item gives commits 1 and 64 rows. `tick(1000)` gives 65 rows and commits 2.
7. "invalid delta sizes are ignored and counts saturate at the safe-integer bound": deltas of 0, -1, 1.5, NaN and 65537 leave 0 rows after `runAll()`. `store.recordDeltaBytes(binding, new Map([["a", Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER]]))` then `new Map([["a", 5]])` leaves `deltaBytes` at `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.
8. "a failing flush never throws, leaves no open transaction and loses only that batch": create a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger that raises `ABORT`. Two items get deltas and `tick(1000)` does not throw, `db.isTransaction` is false and there are 0 rows. Drop the trigger, then `delta(a, 2)` and `tick(1000)` gives rows `[[a, 2]]`. Recreate the trigger, then `delta(c, 1)`; `finish()` and `discard()` do not throw.
In `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts`, change the first half of "keeps incomplete delta bytes out of SQLite...": replace the immediate `countRows(...) === 1` and `lifecycle === "streaming"` assertions with `await waitUntil(() => countRows(f.root, workId) === 1)`. Then emit `{ threadId, turnId, itemId: "flush-trigger", kind: "omitted", reason: "size-limit" }` for the bound turn (the omission is a deterministic flush trigger, so the test needs no real timer) and assert `rotating-item` is `streaming` with `deltaBytes` 12 and `text` null. Do not assert the unflushed state in service-level tests: a real one-second timer could fire on a stalled CI worker, and T1 test 1 owns that proof with fake timers. The later completed-text SELECT must add `AND itemId = 'rotating-item'` because the omitted item adds a second row. Everything else in that test is unchanged.
**Implementation:** (1) In `conversation-history.ts`, import `{ type Database, transaction }` from `../core/store.js`, add `deltaFlushMs = 1000`, `maxPendingDeltaItems = 64` and `validDeltaBytes`. (2) Store: move the delta UPSERT out of `record` into private `addDeltaBytes(binding, itemId, bytes, now)` with the SQL unchanged. The `record` delta branch becomes `if (validDeltaBytes(event.bytes)) this.addDeltaBytes(...)`. Add public `recordDeltaBytes(binding, deltas: ReadonlyMap<string, number>)`, which takes `checkedNow()` once and calls `addDeltaBytes` for every entry with a safe-integer value > 0 inside `transaction(this.db, ...)`. (3) Capture: add `pendingDeltas = new Map<string, number>()` and `flushTimer`. In `persist`, a `delta` event calls `addDelta(event.itemId, event.bytes)` and returns. Any event other than `started` calls `flush()` before the existing handling. `finish()` calls `flush()` before `omitIncomplete` (inside the existing `binding && !closed` guard). `discard()` calls `flush()` before setting `closed`. `addDelta` ignores invalid sizes, calls `flush()` first when the item is new and `pendingDeltas.size >= maxPendingDeltaItems`, stores the clamped sum (`Math.min(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, ...)`), and sets `this.flushTimer ??= setTimeout(() => this.flush(), deltaFlushMs).unref()`. `flush()` always runs `clearTimeout` and resets `flushTimer`, then returns if there is no binding or nothing pending. Otherwise it snapshots and clears `pendingDeltas`, calls `store.recordDeltaBytes(binding, snapshot)` in a `try`, and ignores any error with the existing "diagnostic storage failure" comment style. It must never throw. Do not add an option, do not edit `service.ts` or `codex.ts`, and do not touch `sanitizeConversationText`.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci` with Node 24.21.0 first on `PATH`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/conversation-history-batching.test.js dist/test/s05-conversation-history.test.js dist/test/s05-conversation-ui.test.js`; expect `ℹ tests 19`, `ℹ pass 19`, `ℹ fail 0`. Then run `npx biome lint --error-on-warnings src/standalone/conversation-history.ts test/conversation-history-batching.test.ts test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts && npx biome format src/standalone/conversation-history.ts test/conversation-history-batching.test.ts test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts`; expect no findings. Sensitivity check: temporarily make `addDelta` call `store.recordDeltaBytes(binding, new Map([[itemId, bytes]]))` directly; test 1 must fail with commits 501 instead of 1; then revert it.
**Complete when:** the 8 new tests and the rewritten service test pass, the full `s05-conversation-history` and `s05-conversation-ui` files pass, the sensitivity check is recorded, and lint and format are clean.

#### 2. Prove turn end and shutdown through the service, and document the limit

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 complete with its Validate command passing (this is the boundary evidence for the timer and flush, which this slice exercises through production wiring).
**Files and symbols:** `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts` (new test using `HistoryRuntime`, `fixture`, `createTaskAssignment`, `query`, `waitUntil`, `waitForExecutionState`); `docs/SPEC.md` (the paragraph beginning "The assignment view retains sanitized completed assistant text"; the sentence "Partial text is not persisted." is at L1068).
**Test:** Add "turn end and service shutdown write pending delta byte counts" directly after the T1-edited test. Use `new HistoryRuntime()` and `fixture(runtime)`, then `const second = await createTaskAssignment(f.service, f.projectId, f.profileId)`, then `runtime.plan({ id: "ending-turn" }, { id: "shutdown-turn" })`. Run `f.activate()`, `waitForTurnStart(initialStarts)`, `second.activate()` and `waitForTurnStart(startsBeforeSecond)`. On each bound turn emit `started` and then `delta`, with `bytes` 7 for item `ending-item` and 5 for `staying-item`. Call `runtime.complete(endingTurn.turnId)` and `waitForExecutionState(f.service, f.workId, "completed")`. Then assert (reading rows with `query(...)` by `workId`, spread into plain objects) that the first work's row is `{ lifecycle: "omitted", omissionReason: "turn-ended", deltaBytes: 7 }`. Then `await f.service.stop()` and assert the second row is `{ lifecycle: "streaming", omissionReason: null, deltaBytes: 5 }`. The shutdown flush happens in `clearConversationCaptures()` via `discard()`, before runtimes stop and the database closes. Keep the file's usual `finally` with `service.stop().catch(...)` and `rmSync`.
**Implementation:** Add the test. In `docs/SPEC.md`, after the sentence "Partial text is not persisted.", add: "Streamed byte counts for an unfinished item are batched and written when the item completes or is omitted, at turn end or shutdown, or about one second after the first unwritten delta, so a crash can lose about one second of those counts; completed text is unaffected." Revise in place; add no dated section or log, and do not edit `docs/evidence/`.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/s05-conversation-history.test.js`; expect `ℹ tests 11`, `ℹ pass 11`, `ℹ fail 0`; repeat it 3 times to show the test is stable. Run `rg -n "about one second after the first unwritten delta" docs/SPEC.md`; expect exactly one match. Run `git diff --stat origin/main -- src/standalone/service.ts src/standalone/codex.ts src/standalone/claude.ts`; expect empty output.
**Complete when:** the service-level test passes repeatedly with the shipped `StandaloneService` wiring and the SPEC states the batching and its loss bound.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Streaming persistence scales with items plus bounded timer flush intervals, not individual deltas | 1 | T1 test 1 (500 deltas give one `started` commit, then one commit per interval, then one at completion) and test 6 (cap bounds pending items) |
| Conversation history tests still pass | 1, 2 | `s05-conversation-history` and `s05-conversation-ui` in the T1 and T2 Validate commands; full `npm run check` in Final validation |
| A test covers flush on completion | 1 | T1 test 2 (`completed`) and the rewritten service test in T1 |
| A test covers flush on turn end | 1, 2 | T1 test 2 (`finish()` before `omitIncomplete`) and the T2 service test |
| Omission flushes pending counts | 1 | T1 test 2 (`omitted`) and the rewritten service test, which uses an omission as the flush trigger |
| Early buffering, late and wrong-turn events | 1 | T1 tests 4 and 3 |
| Discard and shutdown flush once, and no timer survives disposal | 1, 2 | T1 tests 2 and 5 (`runAll()` after disposal writes nothing) and the T2 shutdown assertion |
| Storage failures stay diagnostic and bounded | 1 | T1 test 8; existing "history write failures cannot hold or fail the exact bound execution" |
| No completed item returns to streaming; counts saturate; invalid sizes ignored | 1 | T1 tests 3 and 7 |
| Exact binding, redaction and completed text persistence unchanged | 1 | Existing `s05-conversation-history` suite (canary redaction, wrong thread and turn, reopen) passes unmodified apart from the one rewritten assertion |
| No global SQLite durability reduction and no scope creep | 2 | T2 `git diff --stat` check on `service.ts`, `codex.ts`, `claude.ts`; no `PRAGMA` or schema line changes in review |
| The accepted one-second loss is stated in the operating contract | 2 | T2 `rg` check for the new `docs/SPEC.md` sentence |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, after `npm ci` with Node 24.21.0 (`.node-version`) first on `PATH` and npm 12.2.0 (the `packageManager` pin, which CI installs globally), run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate (after T2); expect exit 0 (type check, `biome lint --error-on-warnings`, `biome format`, build and the complete test suite, including the Playwright browser tests with the cached browsers). CI `check` (Node 24) and `check-node-26` must both pass on the PR. The new tests use fake timers and `db.isTransaction`; CI's Node 26 run is the evidence for that runtime.
- No live runtime probe is required: the change does not touch `codex.ts` or `claude.ts`, and the recorded live scripts (`test/s05/live-*.mjs`) only hash `conversation-history.ts` as evidence; no test pins the hash. See the CI flake in Planning decisions.

### Review focus

- In `finish()`, `flush()` must run before `omitIncomplete`; reversing them silently drops the counts of unfinished items.
- The timer callback and `flush()` must never throw, because an escaped exception would take down the coordinating process.
- `discard()` must write nothing for an unbound capture (the `!turnBound` and missing-binding paths).
- Check that no code path calls `flush()` inside an open transaction, and that no `docs/evidence/` file changed.

### Re-plan triggers

- The flush cannot be implemented inside the capture, or requires editing `service.ts`, `codex.ts`, the table schema or SQLite `PRAGMA`s.
- A consumer or test needs per-delta immediate visibility, beyond the single obsolete assertion rewritten in T1.

content.title: CLI6: Prepare and submit evidence-bearing recovery

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/899
**Planned against:** `main` at `aa1671ae9f7a8c8f311527319096475825a7bf1f`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Deliver CLI6 on the CLI1–CLI5 seams (`src/cli/*`, bearer auth, the fail-closed `operatorRouteAuthority` table, capability negotiation, the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope and exit codes, `sendCommand` with its per-command `match`, the append-only `requests.jsonl` journal, digest-bound owner-only documents, `operation get`, the effect vocabulary). Implementation branch `cb/899-evidence-bearing-recovery` from `main` at or after the planned SHA; one PR, seven observable slices.

1. **Shared contracts, typed rejections, held-generation fixture (T1).** The strict command shapes of the five existing recovery operations move to `src/core` (so `src/operator/contracts.ts` can import them); definite recovery rejections become one typed error; a shared fixture builds real held generations.
2. **Read (T2).** `GET /api/operator/assignments/ID/recovery-options`: current assignment/work/conversation identity, holds, the exact generation material each path binds, per-path eligibility and blockers.
3. **Write (T3, T4).** Five receipted commands on the existing `POST /api/operator/commands` route that call the existing service methods unchanged, three receipt kinds, and `operation get` readback.
4. **CLI (T5, T6).** `recovery get`; `recovery prepare PATH` (owner-only `ensemble.cli.recovery/v1` document from observed identity plus an explicit operator evidence file); `recovery submit --file`.
5. **Journeys, entry-point parity, packed binary, docs, evidence (T7).**

The five operations are exactly the advanced authenticated routes in `docs/design/ui02-foundation.md`: historical pre-turn adoption, pre-turn recovery, historical no-turn adoption, no-turn recovery and conversation replacement. They are session-only today; this slice gives bearer read/write credentials the same service methods, nothing more.

### Guardrails

- **Unchanged contracts:** behaviour, persisted rows and replay material of `adoptHistoricalPreTurnRejection`, `recoverPreTurnExecution`, `adoptHistoricalNoTurnSubmission`, `recoverNoTurnExecution`, `replaceConversationCommand` (`execution_pre_turn_commands` keys, witnesses, receipts, continuation audits); the stored command material is the inner command exactly as the retained routes pass it, so a command recorded through either entry point replays through the other; the existing exception messages; the retained `/runtime/control/*` handlers and signatures, `RuntimeOperatorApi`, `operator-runtime.ts`; `assignmentRecoverySchema` and `GET .../recovery` output and the React recovery page; every existing `operatorCommandSchema` variant and persisted hash; browser Origin/CSRF; the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope, exit codes (no new code) and coverage gap set (no new gap); CLI1–CLI5 and CLI7 commands and output, except one added line in `assignment get`.
- **Append-only:** `operatorCommandSchema`, `commandReceiptSchema`, `cliCapabilities` and `operationTypeSchema` gain entries at the end; nothing is reordered (`web/src/composer-state.ts` reads `operatorCommandSchema.options[0]`).
- **No new authority:** no force unlock, no release by time, acknowledgement, Resume or elapsed observation; no exposure of the keyless bound-turn `resolveHeldExecution` (it has no operator route today); no signal, kill or termination by the CLI or service beyond the existing `TerminationVerifier`; no dispatch (a recovery receipt leaves the old request held; continuation still needs replacement plus a NEW `task message`); no change to operator Stop/Resume; no model-tool surface. The CLI never defaults, infers or derives independent review, termination, settled-effects or workspace evidence, and has no `--yes`, `--confirm`, `--force` or attestation flag. No `web/` file: `design/design.pen` has no CLI frame; if a task appears to need a layout, report a blocker.
- **Neutral layer:** new files under `src/core`, `src/operator`, `src/cli` and `operator-recovery.ts` carry no Codex-naming literal (#887's planned guard). The archived-resume message and its refine stay in `src/standalone/pre-turn-recovery.ts`.
- **Out of scope:** CLI4 (#897), CLI8 (#901), runtime and model settings (#826), diagnostics (#900, merged), the bound-turn receipt, a React submission control, service administration, ChatGPT and native Codex (#726/#734 paused).
- **(a) Plan-seam mismatch: one diagnosis plus two repair cycles in total**, only when a factual assumption about the repository or an approved seam is wrong. Examples: the material exposed by `recoveryMaterial` cannot rebuild a command that the unchanged service method accepts for a real held generation; `readAssignmentRecoveryOnce` records cannot be keyed one-to-one by `workId`; the typed error cannot cover a rejection without changing a persisted message; a retained route stores different inner material than the bearer path passes; the held-generation fixture cannot run under `startCliService`. After the diagnosis and two repair cycles, stop and report for a replan.
- **(b) Ordinary in-scope repairs: owner repairs, no allowance, they do not consume (a):** implementation bugs; type, lint and format errors; fixture and test setup (including lifting fixture code and `startCliService` options); equivalent paths, names, flag and verb spellings; documentation and evidence text; mechanical rebase conflicts with #897, #887, #826, #881, #873 or #886; CI and flaky-test retries (Node 26, npm 12.2.0 lockfile or runner fixes, #921 and the browser-timing class). Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes, or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews; no integration amendment is needed unless a published integration decision changes.

### Planning decisions

- **Scope is the five existing operations.** `rg` finds no operator route for the keyless bound-turn `resolveHeldExecution`; the issue names "adoption/recovery/conversation-replacement", matching the five advanced routes. Bound-turn recovery stays an entry-point gap for the evidence record.
- **Transport is receipted commands, not new POST routes.** Precedent: #898's `task.stop`/`task.resume`. The route is already `write`-classified, bounded to 64 KiB, bearer and session capable. New types (appended): `recovery.pre-turn.adopt`, `recovery.pre-turn.recover`, `recovery.no-turn.adopt`, `recovery.no-turn.recover`, `recovery.conversation.replace`. Each carries `assignmentId` (receipt scope `assignment:ID`) plus the existing inner fields flattened (recoveries keep their nested `receipt`); the API verifies the work is bound to that assignment, then calls the service method with the inner command only (`key` plus fields, no `type`, no `assignmentId`). Replay and conflicts are the service's own: `execution_pre_turn_commands.commandKey` is global, so reuse of a key for other material or another recovery type conflicts (409) rather than selecting another scope's receipt.
- **Shared strict shapes live in `src/core/recovery-contracts.ts`, the Codex refine stays.** `src/operator/contracts.ts` imports only `src/core`. T1 moves the structural, key-less bodies (`processIdentitySchema`, generation, evidence, attestations, `rpcError`, receipts, replacement) to core; `pre-turn-recovery.ts` rebuilds the current exported schemas as `body.extend({key}).strict()` and keeps `archivedResumeMessage` and its refine, and re-exports the same names so no importer changes. zod 4.6.5: `.extend` on a strict object stays strict and `.shape` survives `.refine` (probed). A parity test pins that both accept and reject the same inputs apart from the standalone-only refine.
- **Identity comes from the service, evidence from the operator.** `preTurnContext`/`noTurnContext` (state.ts) already select every identity field a command binds (`workRevision`, `requestSequence`, process identity, `writerSequence`, `conversationRevision`, `predecessorWorkId`, `predecessorThreadId`) with the same joins the service re-checks, and the intent reason is the `retainedReason` the adoption compares. A new targeted `ExecutionState.recoveryMaterial(workId)` exposes those plus the intent and request reasons and the binding, so `recovery-options` never re-implements eligibility SQL and needs no full-history read. The CLI fills those fields from the read, and takes everything independent from an explicit `--evidence-file`: reviewed source/harness/evidence/decision hashes, review and approval URLs, the persisted `rpcError` (pre-turn adoption), `invocationLedgerSha256` (no-turn adoption), every attestation as `true`, and for recoveries `termination`, `effects` and `workspace`. Missing, `false`, extra or malformed items exit 2 before any document or request. The attestations remain operator assertions that the service cannot verify; the CLI cannot make them true and records that limit.
- **`recovery-options` composes `readAssignmentRecoveryOnce`.** Its filtered, redacted records (newest 20, `omittedCount`) are the base; since #875 (#925) merged they come from the targeted `recoveryForTask(taskId, selected?.workId)`, and this slice adds no `recoveryView()` caller. Each visible record is enriched by `workId` through `recoveryMaterial`. Strings that must match exactly (`retainedReason`, process identity, `predecessor`) go through `OperatorApi.exact(...)`: a value changed by redaction or an unavailable exclusion reads `null` with gap `content-redacted` or `redaction-unavailable`, and the adoption or recovery path is blocked `reason-withheld`/`identity-withheld` (fail closed; probe showed a one-letter instruction text mangles a wait reason).
- **Disclosure decision (recorded, not a stakeholder question).** The read discloses the held generation's process identity (`processId`, `processStartedAt`, `bootId`) to both credential scopes. Evidence: AC1 requires work identity and "their required inputs"; the retained Runtime page already shows it to the signed-in session (`recoveryRecordEvidence`); thread/turn identifiers and the redacted hold reason are already readable by read-only credentials in the CLI7 execution summaries (`executionSummarySchema`); design: both scopes cover "permitted diagnostic content". It carries no credential, path or instruction text. Review focus names it.
- **Eligibility is advisory and uses a closed vocabulary.** `blockedBy` is a subset of `not-held`, `ownership-released`, `context-unavailable`, `witness-missing`, `witness-present`, `other-witness`, `already-reconciled`, `reason-withheld`, `identity-withheld`, `task-held` and `unresolved-execution`. Replacement is blocked by `task-held` (`service.taskHold(taskId)`, the three tables `replaceConversationCommand` checks, so an operator Stop blocks it until Resume) and by `unresolved-execution` (probed: while the generation is still held, replacement fails "Assignment has unresolved execution" and `taskHold` is `undefined`); T1 extracts that SQL from `replaceConversation` into `assignmentHasUnresolvedExecution` so the read and the command share one source. The service stays authoritative. A definite refusal is a 409 and the CLI prints a post-read of blockers and the latest recovery observation (`termination-unknown` and `termination-conflict` are recorded by the supervisor), so a missing, expired or stale proof is an actionable failure and never reads as a Resume.
- **Typed rejections.** Probed at `f8530539` and again at `aa1671ae`: a duplicate adoption with a fresh key surfaces `UNIQUE constraint failed: execution_no_turn_submissions.workId` (it would map to 503 `command-outcome-unknown`, exit 6, although nothing applied); stale replacement, replacement while the assignment has unresolved execution, key reuse, wrong reason, wrong generation and recovery of a reconciled generation are plain `Error`s with fixed messages. T1 adds `RecoveryRejectedError` (recovery-types.ts), throws it at the recovery sites in `state.ts` and `supervisor.ts` with messages unchanged, and adds explicit already-recorded checks to the two adoption methods. `executeRecovery` maps it to 409 inside its own branch, not through the shared `conflicts` message set that #873 is retiring. Infrastructure failures stay untyped and uncertain; a `ZodError` stays 400.
- **Key rule: the CLI3 default, not #898's unresolved-only rule.** These are irreversible one-shot operations: an identical document resubmitted replays the recorded receipt by `journal.find(service, digest)`; a definitely rejected key is not reused; `--request-id` is used as given. Identity: scope `assignment:ID`, type the command type, key a UUID persisted before sending. The service treats a stale or replayed duplicate with a new key as a definite conflict.
- **Effects.** `Effect` gains `completed` (design: reserved for synchronous operations; #897 adds the same literal, a one-line mechanical merge). Adoption `saved` (witness persisted, holds unchanged), recovery `completed` (verified termination, ownership reconciled; the request stays held and nothing is dispatched), replacement `saved`. Output states "not resumed, nothing dispatched".
- **`operation get` for the five types.** Scope `assignment:ID` is appended to `operationScopeSchema`; `readOperation` delegates recovery types to `readRecoveryOperation`, which reads the row by key (`preTurnCommandRecord`), requires the row's scope to be the type's, checks the assignment through the stored work binding (replacement through its stored command), rebuilds the receipt with the same builder as the POST, and reads another shape as 409. Another type's key reads `not-recorded`. CLI reconciliation = this read-only check, else exact same-key retry.
- **Reverse operations.** Intentionally irreversible and flagged in help, output, docs and evidence: adoption (immutable witness), recovery (immutable receipt, capacity released), conversation replacement (revision increment). `prepare` has no server state. No counterpart exists or is invented.
- **Fixture approach (probed).** A held no-turn generation was built inside `startCliService` by passing a runtime factory to `createOperatorFixture` and `terminationVerifier` through `service`; the bearer recovery read then returned the record with writer, capacity and uncertainty holds. T1 copies, without editing, `fixture()` from `no-turn-recovery.test.ts` and `heldFixture()` from `recovery-continuation.test.ts` into `test/fixtures/recovery-generations.ts`, parameterised by service and runtime, with a switchable verifier. No live runtime; no real termination.
- **Baseline at planning time** (`main` at `aa1671ae`, which is `f8530539` plus #875/#925 only; Node 24.21.0; exact `git archive` exports of both SHAs built outside the shared planning checkout, which stays detached and clean at `f8530539`): `tsc` clean; `node --test` on `no-turn-recovery`, `recovery-continuation`, `recovery`, `operator-cli-inventory`, `-http`, `-write`, `-adopt`, `-operate-journey`, `-task-control`, `operator-api`, `operator-runtime`, `operator-operations`, `operator-targeted-reads` and (after `npm run build:web`) `operator-runtime-recovery-browser`: 170 pass at `aa1671ae` (165 without the two new suites at `f8530539`). | Expose assignment/work/conversation identity, eligibility, holds, supported paths and required inputs | 2, 5 | T2 `operator-recovery-options` cases; T5 `recovery get` output, JSON and coverage |
| Prepare an inspectable, exact, version-bound request; submit the existing adoption/recovery/replacement operations only when service requirements hold | 3, 6 | T3 positive and exact-rejection cases; T6 prepare document and submit cases |
| Require explicit evidence references/hashes and every attestation; no synthesized evidence; flags cannot replace assertions | 3, 6 | T3 400 table; T6 evidence matrix and rejected flags |
| Preserve ownership/capacity/survivor holds, stale identity checks and preserved/reconciled workspace; no force unlock or release by time | 1, 3, 7 | T1 typed rejections; T3 identity, termination and hold cases; T7 journeys (holds intact, no dispatch, Resume unchanged) |
| Receipt reconciliation for uncertain outcomes; missing, expired or stale evidence is actionable failure, not Resume | 4, 6, 7 | T4 readback; T6 lost-reply and 409 cases; T7 replay, restart and verifier-off journey |
| Complete positive and negative paths, deterministic fixtures, rejected read-only writes, stale revisions, restart/replay, unchanged UI | 1, 3, 6, 7 | T1 fixture; T3 and T6 negative tables; T7 journeys, read-only table, UI parity and browser suites |

### Final validation

CI on the pull request runs the pinned npm 12.2.0 and Node 26; the browser-timing class (#921) is retried as an ordinary repair and not reported as a failure of this slice.

- Disclosure of process identity on `recovery-options` to both credential scopes, and fail-closed handling when redaction changes an exact string.
- That `blockedBy` is advisory and the CLI never sends a request the service would not independently check; that no omitted or `false` assertion can reach the service.
- Typed rejection coverage (no definite refusal reported as uncertain, no infrastructure failure reported as definite) and cross-entry replay of the same stored command.

content.title: Routing stale classification matches error text and misreads 'not a candidate'

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/872
**Planned against:** `main` at `5ef46a8e9c3ea6debf0eadcc7bc47fe1deb822b0`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add one typed `DomainStaleDispositionError` in `src/core/domain.ts`, throw it from the five `DomainStore.recordRouting` branches that really mean "this disposition is stale", and replace the message regex in the `StandaloneService` routing loop catch with an `instanceof` test. Keep the explicit `routingStaleReason` snapshot recheck first. `"Selected profile is not a candidate"` stays a plain `Error`, so it is no longer stale: it propagates out of the scheduler pass into the existing background-failure route. One PR, two tasks (core error plus domain tests; service classification plus service tests and one design-doc sentence).

### Guardrails

- Classification must not read `error.message`. Keep every existing `recordRouting` message byte-identical (existing tests in `test/domain.test.ts` match `/held/`, `/external admission/i`, `/stale|changed|revision/`, `/conflict/`).
- Keep `RoutingStaleReason` values and the persisted `staleReason` mapping unchanged: external-admission rejection still stores `task-held`, every other typed stale stores `domain-disposition-rejected`. No schema, migration, operator-view or contract change.
- Out of scope: the HTTP/operator-API error conversion, `DomainNotFoundError`, and any other `throw new Error(...)` conversion (#873); targeted-read changes (#875); changing `routingStaleReason` or the pre-record snapshot recheck.
- Leave other unmatched `recordRouting` and `assignment.create` failures behaving as today (they propagate, not stale): `Routing credentials unavailable`, `Assigned routing requires an assignment`, `Non-assigned routing cannot create an assignment`, `Routing fallback requires a configured task lead`, `DomainConflictError("Routing operation conflict")`, `DomainConflictError("Assignment identity already exists")`, and `DomainPolicyError` (`Task belongs to another project`, `Profile revoked`, `Profile is not permitted for this project`).
- Accepted consequence (from the issue's Agent brief): a selected non-candidate against an unchanged candidate set is an invalid disposition and ends the service through the background-failure route (`handleBackgroundFailure` sets the generation fatal and writes the bounded `unexpected-background-failure` diagnostic). It must not mark the attempt stale or retry.
- Plan-mismatch allowance (a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption, for example a different throw site or catch location than recorded here): one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; then stop and return for replanning.
- Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs (including test-helper tweaks and formatting) are owned by the implementer and consume no allowance. Record them briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence. Stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants; investigate unknown overlap.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews; use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision.

### Planning decisions

- **Typed error placement and shape.** It lives in `src/core/domain.ts` beside `DomainConflictError` (L314) and `DomainPolicyError` (L321) because `src/core` cannot import `src/standalone` (where `RoutingStaleReason` lives). It extends `Error` directly, not `DomainConflictError`, so it cannot be caught by any future conflict mapping (#873 maps `DomainConflictError` to 409; `recordRouting` is reached only from `service.ts`). Constructor `(message: string, readonly reason: "external-admission" | "stale")`, `name = "DomainStaleDispositionError"`. The service maps `reason` to the unchanged stored values.
- **Which branches are stale** (all inside `recordRouting`, `src/core/domain.ts` L1411-1500): `External admission rejected routing disposition` (reason `external-admission`); `Routing decision is stale or task is held` (task version, guidance revision, routing disabled or admission ineligible); `Routing candidate set changed`; `Candidate profile revision changed`; `Routing decision became stale: task already assigned`. These cover the issue's revision, admission/hold, candidate-set/revision, already-assigned and external-admission classes.
- **"Not a candidate" is a hard failure.** The candidate-set equality check precedes the selected-profile check, so reaching `Selected profile is not a candidate` means the candidate set is unchanged and the selection is invalid. The routing client already rejects unlisted choices (`src/standalone/routing.ts` L707), so this is reachable only by corrupt state or a bug; failing loud is correct and a stale retry would loop. This is settled by the issue's Agent brief, not a new product decision.
- **Credential-unavailable stays a hard failure** because today's regex does not match it and the issue does not list it.
- **Assumption check (verified at planning time):** `StandaloneService.domain()` returns the same `DomainStore` instance (`domainState`, L1866) that the routing loop uses (L3243), so a test can wrap `recordRouting` on that instance; any error thrown out of the loop reaches `observeBackgroundFailure` via `wakeScheduler` (L3235) and sets `backgroundFailureObserved()`. No separate proof task is needed.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStore.recordRouting` (L1411) throws plain `Error` for all stale and non-stale branches; its only production caller is `src/standalone/service.ts` (routing loop, `recordRouting` call about L3445). The catch at about L3477-3490 calls `this.routingStaleReason(domain, state, snapshot)` first (snapshot recheck, L3196), then `message === "External admission rejected routing disposition"` (stale `task-held`), then `/stale|held|candidate|revision|already assigned/i` (stale `domain-disposition-rejected`); otherwise it rethrows. `routingAttempts.markStale(operationId, reason)` persists the reason.
- **Existing tests:** `test/domain.test.ts` — held-task case (about L484, `/held/`), external-admission case (about L574), change loop (about L596-745, `/stale|changed|revision/`), routing commit test (about L760); fixture helpers `fixture()`, `run()`, `key()`. `test/s04b-integration.test.ts` — `routedFixture` (L203), `FakeRoutingClient` (L162), `routeResponse` (L184), `command`, `row`, `waitUntil`, and the in-flight stale test (about L892) that pins the explicit-recheck outcomes. `test/background-service.test.ts` — `backgroundDiagnosticSink` precedent.
- **New:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStaleDispositionError`.
- **Follow:** `DomainPolicyError` (readonly constructor field plus `name`) for the class shape; `test/s04b-integration.test.ts` "revision, routing, candidate and hold changes stale an in-flight recommendation" for the deferred-response technique.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic: T1 is the root (`Depends on: none`); T2 depends on T1. Sequential on one branch and one owner. No other planned task can run concurrently on these files. Shared mutable files: `src/core/domain.ts` and `test/domain.test.ts` (T1 only); `src/standalone/service.ts` and `test/s04b-integration.test.ts` (T2 only). Cross-issue verdict: **safe to run concurrently with #898, #884 (PR #920), #875, #874, #826, #897 and #887**, in separate worktrees; the only textual contact is the `domain.ts` error-class block (see Review focus).

#### 1. Typed stale-disposition error from `recordRouting`

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/domain.ts` (`DomainStaleDispositionError` beside `DomainPolicyError`; `DomainStore.recordRouting`); `test/domain.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/domain.test.ts`, using the existing `fixture()`/`run()` helpers: (1) in the existing change loop (`task`, `opt-out`, `pause`, `guidance`, `candidates`, `blocker`, `profile`), keep the message regex and also assert the thrown error is `instanceof DomainStaleDispositionError` with `reason === "stale"`; (2) the held-task case and the `externallyAdmitted` returning false case assert `instanceof DomainStaleDispositionError`, with `reason === "external-admission"` for the latter; (3) add one test where an explicit `assignment.create` for the task exists first, then `recordRouting` throws `DomainStaleDispositionError` (`task already assigned`) and `routingOperations(a)` is empty; (4) add one test with a second, non-candidate profile (create `profile.create` for a second profile that is not in `candidateProfileIds`), `recordRouting` with `disposition: "assigned"`, `assignment.profileId` = that profile and `candidateRevisions` matching the unchanged candidate set: assert it throws an error whose message matches `/not a candidate/`, is NOT `instanceof DomainStaleDispositionError`, and leaves no assignment or routing operation; (5) assert a wording-independence guard: `Routing credentials unavailable` (assigned input with `credentialRef: null`) and `Routing operation conflict` (same id, different payload) are also not `DomainStaleDispositionError`. Sensitivity check: with the throw sites reverted to plain `Error`, (1)-(3) must fail.
**Implementation:** Add the class (`reason: "external-admission" | "stale"`). In `recordRouting`, throw it for exactly the five branches listed in Planning decisions, with unchanged messages (`external-admission` for the first, `stale` for the rest). Leave every other throw in the function and in `apply("assignment.create")` unchanged.
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, with `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/domain.test.js`; expect exit 0, zero failures.
**Complete when:** the five branches throw the typed error, the other branches do not, and the domain tests above pass.

#### 2. Service classifies by type; regex removed

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the delivery branch (needs `DomainStaleDispositionError`).
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/service.ts` (routing-loop catch around `domain.recordRouting`, about L3477-3490; import `DomainStaleDispositionError` from `../core/domain.js`); `test/s04b-integration.test.ts` (`routedFixture` gains an optional `backgroundDiagnosticSink`, passed to the `StandaloneService` options, so the fatal path does not write to stderr; new tests); `docs/design/assignment-routing.md` (one sentence).
**Test:** In `test/s04b-integration.test.ts`, using `routedFixture` with a `FakeRoutingClient` whose first response is a deferred promise: wait for `client.requests.length === 1`, wrap `f.service.domain().recordRouting` on the instance, then resolve the response with the worker. Cases: (a) wrapper throws `new DomainStaleDispositionError("reworded: nothing special", "stale")` (wording free of the old keywords): the `routing_attempt_operations` row becomes `status = 'stale'`, `staleReason = 'domain-disposition-rejected'`, `domain.assignments(taskId)` empty, `backgroundFailureObserved()` false; (b) wrapper throws `new DomainStaleDispositionError("reworded", "external-admission")`: stale with `staleReason = 'task-held'`; (c) wrapper throws a plain `new Error("stale held candidate revision already assigned")`: the attempt is NOT stale, `backgroundFailureObserved()` becomes true, and the sink receives one diagnostic with `errorCode: "unexpected-background-failure"` (this is the message-independence proof); (d) real invalid selection: wrapper calls the real `recordRouting` with `assignment.profileId` replaced by the lead profile id (an existing profile not in `candidateProfileIds`) against the unchanged candidate set: the real `Selected profile is not a candidate` error propagates, the attempt is not stale, `backgroundFailureObserved()` is true, no assignment or routing operation is recorded, and `client.requests.length` stays 1 (no retry); (e) real stale race through the typed path: wrapper first applies a real `task.configure` change via `command(...)` and then calls the real `recordRouting`, which throws the real typed error; assert stale (the explicit recheck may supply the reason, `task-revision-changed`; assert only `status = 'stale'` and the absence of a background failure). Keep the existing in-flight stale test unchanged as the recheck-preservation evidence. Sensitivity check: with the regex restored, (c) and (d) fail.
**Implementation:** In the catch, compute `staleReason = this.routingStaleReason(domain, state, snapshot) ?? (error instanceof DomainStaleDispositionError ? (error.reason === "external-admission" ? "task-held" : "domain-disposition-rejected") : undefined)`; keep `if (!staleReason) throw error;` then `markStale` and `continue`. Delete the `message` variable, the string comparison and the regex. Add one sentence to the freshness paragraph of `docs/design/assignment-routing.md` (the "Bind each routing decision ..." paragraph): stale classification at record time uses a typed domain error; a selected profile outside an unchanged candidate set is an invalid disposition that fails loudly instead of retrying.
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, with Node 24.21.0 first on `PATH`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/s04b-integration.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/routing.test.js dist/test/background-service.test.js`; expect exit 0, zero failures.
**Complete when:** no regex or message comparison remains in the routing catch (the catch contains no `.test(message)` call or message comparison), and tests (a)-(e) pass.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Routing stale classification does not depend on error message text | 1, 2 | T2 test (c) (misleading plain-Error message is not stale) and (a)/(b) (reworded typed errors are stale); T1 sensitivity check |
| "Selected profile is not a candidate" path is covered with the intended outcome (hard failure, not stale, no retry) | 1, 2 | T1 test (4); T2 test (d) |
| Real stale races (revision, hold/admission, candidate set/revision, already assigned, external admission) classify as stale | 1, 2 | T1 tests (1)-(3); T2 tests (a), (b), (e) and the unchanged in-flight stale test |
| Explicit snapshot recheck preserved | 2 | Existing "revision, routing, candidate and hold changes stale an in-flight recommendation" test unchanged and passing |
| Error wording change does not change classification; wider HTTP error conversion (#873) not folded in | 1, 2 | T2 (a) and (c); diff touches no `operator-api.ts` |

### Final validation

- From the implementation worktree root, with Node 24.21.0 first on `PATH` (CI pins npm 12.2.0 and runs Node 26), after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate before review hand-off and again if review repairs change code; expect exit 0. A flaky test tracked in #921 may fail on CI Node 26; a failure in a file this change does not touch and that is listed in #921 is not a regression (re-run once and cite #921).
- No live or paid runtime probe is required or authorized.

### Review focus

- That no other `recordRouting` throw changed behavior: only the five listed branches become typed; `Routing credentials unavailable` and `DomainPolicyError`/`DomainConflictError` paths still propagate exactly as before.
- Textual contact with in-flight work is limited to the `domain.ts` error-class block (#875 adds `DomainNotFoundError` near L312, #873 adds typed errors there) and appended tests in `test/domain.test.ts`; resolve any rebase conflict mechanically by keeping both additions.
