content.title: CLI4: Manage GitHub sources and delivery through the CLI

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/897
**Planned against:** `main` at `5ef46a8e9c3ea6debf0eadcc7bc47fe1deb822b0`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Deliver CLI4 on the CLI1–CLI3 seams (`src/cli/*`, bearer auth, the fail-closed `operatorRouteAuthority` table, capability negotiation, the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope and exit codes, the CLI3 write transport `sendCommand`, the append-only `requests.jsonl` journal, digest-bound change documents and `operation get`). Implementation branch `cb/897-cli-github-sources-delivery` from `main` at or after the planned SHA; one PR, eight observable slices.

1. **Server contract (T1, T2).** Two capabilities (`source.write`, `delivery.write`); `operation get` readback for `github.configure` and `github.preview`; the closed set of definite comment-path rejections stops surfacing as `command-outcome-unknown` (503). No command, receipt or route is added: every operation here already exists as an `operatorCommandSchema` variant that the React UI and retained pages use, so the CLI is their second client.
2. **Request seam (T3).** Receipt matching for the delivery, comment and refresh receipts.
3. **Sources (T4, T5).** `project sources` (read), `project prepare-source` plus the existing `project apply` (new change-document kind `github.configure`), `project preview-source` (preview and activation) and `project place-task` (placement).
4. **Delivery (T6, T7).** `delivery get`, `delivery refresh`, and the staged `delivery review-comment`, `confirm-comment`, `send-comment`.
5. **Journeys, UI parity, packed binary, docs and evidence (T8).**

### Guardrails

- **Unchanged contracts:** every existing `operatorCommandSchema` variant, its persisted request hash and its receipt (`github.configure|preview|place`, `delivery.refresh`, `comment.review|confirm|send` are driven as they are); `commandReceiptSchema`; `operatorRouteAuthority` (no route is added; bearer requests still never reach cookie, legacy HTML or slot routes; `POST /api/operator/source-refresh` stays write-only and unexposed); domain GitHub source behaviour (configure replaces the whole configuration, new selections are inactive, any configure invalidates activation and observations, activation needs a complete provider read, placement rules), the delivery store and coordinator (`reconcile`, authority and approval binding, provider effects only through the existing coordinator), browser Origin/CSRF and cookie sessions; the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope, exit codes and coverage gap set (no new code); all CLI1–CLI3 and CLI7 commands and output including `RequestJournal.find` default reuse; `project apply` for the six existing change kinds; `operation get` for the seven existing types; `src/cli` imports no SQLite and no `src/standalone` module except `operator-hidden-password.js` (existing test; `src/core/*` contracts are allowed).
- **Append-only:** `cliCapabilities` and `operationTypeSchema` gain entries at the end; no union is reordered (`web/src/composer-state.ts` reads `operatorCommandSchema.options[0]`).
- **No new authority.** The only GitHub write reachable is the existing operator `issue.comment`; no merge, close, label, edit or PR action, no `source.review`, no handback settlement, no installation-wide source refresh, no discovery or repository setup, no provider credential value is read, printed or stored (a reference name `env:NAME` is set or cleared exactly as the UI does), no `web/` file (`design/design.pen` has no CLI frame; if a task appears to need a layout, report a blocker). A read, preview, review or replay never sends, approves or activates.
- **Out of scope:** CLI5 (#898), CLI6 (#899), CLI8 (#901), runtime and model settings (#826), execution diagnostics (#900, merged), ChatGPT and native Codex (#726/#734 paused), production cutover.
- **(a) Plan-seam mismatch: one diagnosis plus two repair cycles in total**, only when a factual assumption in this plan about the repository or an approved seam is wrong. Examples: the comment-path rejection messages cannot be mapped without changing the delivery store, coordinator or a receipt shape; `github.configure` cannot be rebuilt from the project configuration read with kept-by-id selections and links (private definitions would have to be sent again); `operationId` equal to `reviewId` is rejected on some service path, or an exact `comment.review` replay does not return the review's current decision; `operation get` cannot project `github.configure|preview` from the stored domain result without changing that result; the scripted delivery provider cannot produce a lost-reply, uncertain or read-failure sequence without changing production provider code. After the diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, stop and report for a replan.
- **(b) Ordinary in-scope repairs: owner repairs, no allowance, they do not consume (a):** implementation bugs; type, lint and format errors; fixture and test setup (refactoring `startCliService`, lifting `seedPlacement`, adding scripted-provider levers); equivalent paths, names, flag and verb spellings; documentation and evidence text; mechanical rebase conflicts with #898, #873, #886, #877, #826 or #875; and CI or flaky-test retries (Node 26, npm 12.2.0 lockfile or runner fixes, #921 and the browser-timing class). Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes, or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews; no integration amendment is needed unless a published integration decision changes.

### Planning decisions

- **Base drift.** `origin/main` advanced to `0cb1dd74` (#920, hardened Git environment: `src/core/child-environment.ts` `gitEnvironment`, `src/core/github-source.ts` `verifiedRepository`/`checkoutOrigin` now call it, plus standalone Git callers and tests) during planning. The delta changes only the environment of repository-link verification, which `github.configure` uses, and no code symbol this plan edits (`docs/SPEC.md` changed in the workspace section, not the Operator CLI section). The focused baseline and the probes below were re-run in an isolated export of `0cb1dd74` with identical results; `main` CI at `0cb1dd74` is green on `check-node-26` and failed on `check` (Node 24) in Chromium timing suites (`sign-in layout … phone`, `production Changes …`), the browser-timing class that #921 tracks, none of it in anything this plan touches. Implementation branches from current `main`.
- **Source configuration is a change document, not a new write path.** `project prepare-source` writes an `ensemble.cli.change/v1` document of new kind `github.configure` (exact `github.configure` command, `source.version` as the expected revision, a redacted preview, digest); `project apply --file` sends it. `AREA`, `targetOf` (`project:ID`), `expectedOf`, the `configuration` receipt match (`commandType`, `resourceId`) and the journal already fit it, so reviewed-material, revision and retry behaviour are the CLI3 ones. Edits come from one strict `--edit-file` (private query, filter and path text stays out of argv and out of every preview line): `addSelections`, `removeSelections`, `readiness` (replaces), `linkRepositories`, `unlinkRepositories`, `setRefs`, `credentialRef` (`env:NAME` or null) and `confirmUnlinkAll`. Kept selections go as `{id, keep: true}` and kept links as `{repositoryId, ref}` so no private definition or path is re-sent; new ids are the next free `S-n` above every saved and edited id (as `nextSelectionId` in `web/src/settings-changes.ts`); duplicate ids or links, unknown removals and a removal of every link without `confirmUnlinkAll` exit 2 before a document exists; a saved selection id, link or readiness that this read cannot name (`null`, redacted) exits 4 `conflict`, as the UI's "advanced editor" block does. The command must equal the one `sourceCommand` builds for the same edit (tested against `web/src/settings-changes.ts`).
- **Domain facts the CLI states, verified by probe at both SHAs.** A new selection is inactive. Any `github.configure` bumps `source.version`, so every selection (including ones kept) reads `active: false` until previewed again at the new version; saving also marks the project's observations incomplete until the next refresh (automatic, 5 minutes by default) and invalidates imported blockers. Removing a selection discards its private definition (not restorable from the CLI; re-adding needs the original text). `github.preview` activates only after a complete provider read, binds to the configuration version, and a replay of an old receipt returns the original `active: true` without provider access, so `preview-source` reports the live post-read state next to the receipt. Activation does not import tasks or prove a sync.
- **Reads need no new route.** `project sources` composes `GET /projects/:id/configuration` (source version, selections with `active`, readiness, links, placements) and `GET /source-observations` (state `complete|partial|never|unavailable`, attempt times) for the project; `delivery get` reads `GET /tasks/:id` (`delivery`, `source`, `commentPolicy`). Capabilities are the existing `workspace.read` and `task.read`. Coverage: unreadable names `content-unavailable`, `partial` observations `evidence-gap`, `unavailable` observations `redaction-unavailable`, omitted blockers, actions, checks or feedback `item-omitted`, a binding `readError` `evidence-gap`.
- **Two new capabilities.** `source.write` (apply of a source document, `preview-source`, `place-task`, and `operation get` for the two new types) and `delivery.write` (`refresh`, `review-comment`, `confirm-comment`, `send-comment`). The commands exist on current services, but a CLI that sends them to a service that lacks the matching readback and classification must fail `unsupported-service` before any read.
- **`operation get` covers `github.configure` and `github.preview` only.** Both are domain receipts with a unique stored shape (`recordedResult(projectId, key)`), and `preview` is disclosure-gated like `previewGitHubSelection` (an excluded `selectionId` reads `503 unavailable`). `github.place` stores a task row indistinguishable from other task commands (CLI5 records the same limit), and the delivery commands live in the delivery store keyed by review id, confirm key and operation id, so their reconcile path is exact same-key retry (the service replays the stored receipt), `delivery get` (an action's `operationId` is the `send-comment` request key) and `delivery refresh`. The unknown-outcome text names `operation get` only for listed types.
- **Delivery request identities.** Scope `task:TASK_ID`, type the command type, key a UUID persisted in `requests.jsonl` before sending. `review-comment` sets `operationId` equal to its own key (`reviewId`); `send-comment --review-id R` therefore sends with key `R`, which is the delivery operation id that the approval binds (probe: review, confirm, send, one provider effect). Without a review the send key is `--request-id` or a generated UUID, and that UUID is the operation id. These commands use the CLI3 default `journal.find(service, digest)` reuse and not #898's `chooseKey` or unresolved-only rule, which would repost an identical comment after success; so an identical rerun replays the recorded receipt instead of posting twice, and a deliberate repeat needs a new `--request-id`. A `denied` or `confirmed-failure` receipt is also replayed under the same key, and the error text says to rerun with a new `--request-id` after fixing the cause.
- **Pre-send checks are advisory; the service is authoritative.** `send-comment --review-id R` first replays the exact `comment.review` (same key, `operationId`, body and task version), which returns the review's current decision (probe: `approved`, revision 2); the CLI refuses with exit 4 unless it is `approved`, without sending, so an early send cannot burn the operation id (a send before approval records `denied` for that id permanently). Other gates (`commentPolicy.available`, approval mode requires a review, `--expected-task-version` equals the task version) give precise exit 4 before any request. Direct HTTP always reaches the same server checks, tested.
- **Comment outcomes.** `confirmed-success` exits 0 (`effect: completed`). `denied` exits 4 `policy-denied` and `confirmed-failure` exits 4 `conflict`, both "nothing was posted" with the reason. `uncertain`, `attempting` or `prepared` exit 6 with the full identity and: do not resend with a new key; run `delivery refresh`, then `delivery get`. The posted text carries a hidden `<!-- ensemble-operation:ID -->` marker that the provider read-back uses; docs say so.
- **Definite rejections on the comment path are 503 today.** Probe at both SHAs through `OperatorApi.execute`: confirm with a wrong hash or revision, a second confirm, a review or send with a stale task version, a reused key with other material and a review of a local task all return `503 command-outcome-unknown`, because those errors are plain `Error`s that miss the `conflicts` set. The CLI and the UI would treat them as uncertain. T2 adds the closed message set to the existing `conflicts` set (409) and "External action denied by project policy" to the 403 list; messages outside it stay 503. #873 will replace message matching with typed errors; if it has merged, T2 reduces to the tests.
- **`delivery refresh` is installation-wide and write-classified.** `delivery.refresh` calls `DeliveryCoordinator.refresh()`: `reconcile()` (which can re-attempt `prepared` or retryable-failed actions and read back `uncertain` ones) and an inspection of every registered PR; the task id only selects a task to validate. The receipt records the request, not the result, and a provider read failure is swallowed (`binding.readError` becomes `provider-read-unavailable`), so the command post-reads: output `effect: completed`, `data.outcome: complete|partial` with the binding's `observedAt` before and after, `readError` and every action whose state changed or stayed unreconciled. Partial exits 0 with gap `evidence-gap` and says so; it is never reported as refreshed. The command is `POST /api/operator/commands`, which route authority already classifies `write`; a read-only credential gets `insufficient-scope` and no provider call (tested).
- **Installation-wide source refresh is not exposed** (`POST /api/operator/source-refresh`; React Sync tab and task workspace). It is not in the acceptance criteria, has no receipt, and sync runs every 5 minutes; `project sources` shows the observations. Recorded as an entry-point gap for CLI8.
- **Deterministic fixtures only.** `startCliService` gains `previewReader` and (with #898) `service`, which carries `github.readerFactory` and `delivery`; delivery journeys serve the existing `createReleaseDeliveryFixture` (scripted GitHub dispatcher that asserts the `api.github.com` origin and only scripted routes, real `GitHubHttpDeliveryProvider`, `commentWrites`, `requests`) through a new `serveCli`. No live GitHub, real credential or `~/.env` access, and no production write.
- **Reverse operations and irreversible actions** (flag in help, docs and the evidence record). Selections add and remove (removal discards the saved definition); links link and unlink; credential reference set and clear; all guarded by revision. `preview-source` has no deactivate counterpart: saving any configuration deactivates every selection, and removing the selection does too. `place-task` is repeatable until the task has an assignment, then final. `refresh` is repeatable and needs no counterpart. A pending comment review cannot be withdrawn: `confirm-comment --decision denied` is the durable counterpart, and an approved or denied decision is final (a changed request is a new review). `send-comment` posts a public GitHub comment that Ensemble cannot edit or retract. The CLI keeps no optimistic state to roll back.

**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-source-activation.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-source.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js dist/test/github-source-config.test.js dist/test/github-reconciliation.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Activation and placement run through the packaged entry with the domain's prerequisites, accurate live-state reporting and retry safety.

#### 6. CLI delivery: inspect and refresh

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T1, T3`
**Prerequisites:** T1 capabilities, T3 `match`.
**Files and symbols:** new `src/cli/delivery.ts` (`delivery get TASK_ID` with `cli.identity`, `task.read`; `delivery refresh TASK_ID [--request-id UUID]` with `cli.identity`, `task.read`, `delivery.write`); `src/cli/commands.ts`; `test/fixtures/operator-cli.ts` (`serveCli(t, f, options)` extracted from `startCliService`; `startCliService` calls it); `test/fixtures/s07b-delivery.ts` (`scriptedDeliveryProvider` levers as needed, for example a comment write whose read-back fails once); new `test/operator-cli-delivery.test.ts`; `test/operator-cli-inventory.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/operator-cli-delivery.test.ts` serving `createReleaseDeliveryFixture` through `serveCli`, with `delivery.configure` grants for `issue.comment` and a registered PR (`register()`), read-only and read/write connections.
- `delivery get`: human and JSON show the completion mode, policy version, blockers, the PR (repository, number, head, state, observation time, checks, feedback count), the actions with `operationId`, kind, state and reason, the comment policy and the bound issue; JSON equals the relevant slice of the bearer task read; omitted counts give `item-omitted`, a `readError` gives `evidence-gap`; a local task shows no source and comments unavailable; read-only digest unchanged and zero provider requests.
- `delivery refresh`: the receipt is the `review`/`delivery.refresh` receipt, `data.outcome` is `complete` and the PR's observation time advances; with the scripted provider's read failure the command exits 0 with `outcome: partial`, `readError: provider-read-unavailable`, the previous observation retained and gap `evidence-gap`; an `uncertain` action is read back to `confirmed-success` with the provider's comment count unchanged; an action still unreconciled is listed; the output states that the refresh is installation-wide and may re-attempt prepared or retryable actions; a lost reply exits 6 and an identical rerun succeeds; a read-only credential exits 3 with the digest unchanged and zero provider requests; the same command by session `POST` gives the same receipt.
**Implementation:** `refresh` takes a best-effort pre-read (never blocks the command), sends with `match` for `kind: "review"`, `operation: "delivery.refresh"`, the task and the key, post-reads, and reports the diff. Default journal reuse applies (the service does not dedupe refresh, so a rerun refreshes again).
**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-delivery.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js dist/test/delivery-service.test.js dist/test/task-comments.test.js dist/test/operator-cli.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Delivery and linked PR state are inspectable, and refresh is a write-authority command that reports partial outcomes instead of success.

#### 7. CLI delivery: staged external comments

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `T2, T3, T6`
**Prerequisites:** T2 classification, T3 matching, T6 fixtures and `delivery.ts`.
**Files and symbols:** `src/cli/delivery.ts` (`delivery review-comment TASK_ID --body-file FILE --expected-task-version N [--request-id UUID]`; `delivery confirm-comment TASK_ID --review-id UUID --expected-revision N --material-hash HASH --decision approved|denied [--request-id UUID]`; `delivery send-comment TASK_ID --body-file FILE --expected-task-version N [--review-id UUID] [--request-id UUID]`; all with `cli.identity`, `task.read`, `delivery.write`); `src/cli/main.ts` (options `body-file`, `expected-task-version`, `review-id`; `expected-revision`, `material-hash`, `decision` are shared with #898); `src/cli/types.ts`; new `test/operator-cli-comments.test.ts`; `test/operator-cli-inventory.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/operator-cli-comments.test.ts` on the T6 fixture, in `approval` and `allow` grant modes, read-only and read/write connections, and the scripted provider counting `commentWrites` and `requests`.
- Approval flow: `review-comment` prints the review id, revision 1, decision `pending`, material hash, target issue, body, task, source and policy versions and the confirm command, posts nothing (`commentWrites` 0) and `delivery get` is unchanged; `confirm-comment` with the printed revision and hash approves (revision 2); `send-comment --review-id` posts once (`commentWrites` 1, body carries the operation marker, the action `operationId` equals the review id) and `delivery get` shows `confirmed-success`; output states the comment is public and cannot be retracted.
- Material and revision binding: a changed body at send time exits 4 before any request (the replay conflicts) and nothing is posted; direct HTTP with the changed body and the review id returns a `denied` receipt, so the server does not rely on the CLI check; a wrong hash, a wrong revision and a second confirm exit 4 (409) and leave the decision unchanged; a policy or source change after approval makes the send `denied` (exit 4, nothing posted) and a task-version change is a 409 (exit 4); `--decision denied` is durable and a later send exits 4 without a request; a send before approval exits 4 by the replay check, and a direct early send records `denied` for that operation id only; a stale `--expected-task-version` exits 4.
- Policy: no grant or an unbound task exits 4 before any request; in `approval` mode `send-comment` without `--review-id` exits 4 without a request, while direct HTTP gets a `denied` receipt; in `allow` mode a direct send posts once.
- Duplicate, restart and unknown: a lost reply on the send exits 6 with the identity, then the lead turn is settled (`f.terminal()`, because `reopen()` refuses while work runs) and `s.restart()`, and an identical rerun reuses the key and returns the recorded receipt with `commentWrites` still 1; an identical rerun after success posts nothing more and says it replayed; a new `--request-id` posts a second comment; a provider outcome left `uncertain` exits 6 with the do-not-resend guidance, `delivery refresh` reconciles it to `confirmed-success` and `commentWrites` is 1; the same UUID as `--request-id` for a review and a send are two identities and never select each other's receipt.
- Read-only: all three commands exit 3 with the digest unchanged and zero provider requests; a flag from another command exits 2.
- Parity: the same stale, mismatched, denied and held cases through the CLI and through session `POST /commands` give the same status class and leave the same state.
**Implementation:** Build commands with `operationId` equal to the review key; validate with `exactCommand`; digest from service, type, task, expected version, body hash and review id; take the key from `--request-id`, else `journal.find`, else a random UUID (for `send-comment --review-id` the key is the review id); call `sendCommand` with a `match`; map the delivery state as in Planning decisions; keep the body out of the journal.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-comments.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-delivery.test.js dist/test/task-comments.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-write.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Review, confirm and send run through the packaged entry with exact material and revision binding, accurate non-success reporting and no duplicate provider effect.

#### 8. Journeys, UI parity, packed binary, documentation and evidence

**Task ID:** `T8`
**Depends on:** `T5, T7`
**Prerequisites:** T5 and T7.
**Files and symbols:** new `test/operator-cli-source-delivery-journey.test.ts`; `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts` (one packed-binary invocation per new area: `project sources`, `delivery get`); `test/operator-cli-inventory.test.ts` (final inventory: 2 browse and 8 write commands added, exact capabilities); `README.md` (Operator CLI bullet), `docs/development.md` (Operator CLI: commands, edit-file shape, effects, retry and reuse rule, exit codes for comment outcomes), `docs/SPEC.md` (Operator CLI section), `docs/design/operator-cli.md` (capability names, command table, `operation` types, comment-outcome mapping, inactive-on-create and deactivation facts), `docs/acceptance.md` (CLI04 slice-evidence pointer; scenarios stay **Unproved** until #901), new `docs/evidence/issue-897-cli4-<run date>.md`.
**Test:** `test/operator-cli-source-delivery-journey.test.ts` over the T4–T7 fixtures.
- Journey per acceptance criterion: configure sources, review the diff, apply, preview-activate, read observations and placements, place a conflicting task, inspect delivery, refresh, review, confirm and send a comment, each read back through the session projections the React UI renders (`GET /projects/:id/configuration`, `/source-observations`, `/tasks/:id`).
- Denial table: every new write command with the read-only credential exits 3, and the same command types by direct `POST /commands` are 403 `insufficient-scope`; digest of all persisted tables (credential last-use aside) identical and the provider fixture saw no request.
- Replay and uncertainty: for apply, preview, place, refresh and send, a lost reply exits 6, a service restart on the same database and port keeps the receipt, and the rerun records one effect and at most one provider comment; the same key with different content exits 4; one UUID used for a project, a task and a review never selects another's receipt.
- Parity: stale, held, denied and mismatched cases through the CLI and through session `POST` agree; the source edit equals the UI command.
**Implementation:** Tests and documents only; fix any parity gap in the owning slice. Docs state current behaviour in place with no dated sections, distinguishing implemented from planned (CLI5, CLI6 and CLI8 stay planned). The evidence record names the candidate SHA, environment (Node, npm, Playwright), covered operations with denial, revision and retry cases, the entry-point table and the limits. Entry points: sources (React Source and Sync tabs and the retained project page use the same commands), activation and placement (Sync tab), delivery refresh (React workspace and the retained `/coordination/control/delivery/refresh` form call the same service method; the CLI uses the receipted command), comments (React workspace uses the same commands); gaps: no CLI for installation-wide source refresh, `source.review`, handback settlement or local line-comment review, no list of pending reviews, no deactivate counterpart, the React UI has no change documents or receipt readback.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-source-delivery-journey.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-packed.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-http.test.js dist/test/operator-project-config-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-comments-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-delivery-integration-browser.test.js && npm run lint && npm run format:check`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Every acceptance journey passes through the packaged CLI, shared behaviour matches the UI entry points, and docs and evidence match behaviour with no scenario marked passed.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Source configuration and supported add/remove operations with exact change previews, revision checks and inactive-on-create | 4 | T4 prepare/apply tests, UI command parity |
| Preview/activation prerequisites and placement rules; incomplete reads, conflicts, failures and partial outcomes exposed, activation never marked successful from a replay | 4, 5 | T5 activation and placement tests; T4 observation coverage |
| Delivery and linked PR inspection; refresh through the same policy checks as write authority | 1, 6 | T1 read-only denial table; T6 `delivery get` and `refresh` tests |
| Comment review, confirm and send with exact material and revision binding; a read or preview never sends or approves | 2, 3, 7 | T2 status table; T7 approval, binding and policy tests |
| CLI3 request identities and receipts for uncertain source and delivery commands, no blind repeat or re-key | 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 | T1 readback; T3 matching; per-slice lost-reply, restart and replay checks |
| Read-only denial, stale previews, placement conflict, changed comment material, duplicate, restart and unknown outcomes, UI/CLI policy parity | 8 | T8 journey, denial table, replay and parity tests |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root on Node 24.21.0 (`~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH`, per `.node-version`), after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate; expect typecheck (including `web/`), lint, format, build and the full suite to pass, including the Chromium and WebKit suites. Playwright Chromium and WebKit are cached on this host. CI pins npm 12.2.0 and runs Node 24 and Node 26 (`check`, `check-node-26`); local npm may differ (11.19.0 at planning), so CI on the pull request is authoritative for the pinned toolchain.
- A browser or timing test that fails under host load or on CI in a surface this change does not touch (#921, the `sign-in layout … phone` class seen on `main`) is rerun once by file and recorded; do not edit it unless this change caused the failure.
- Baseline at the planned SHA (`main` at `5ef46a8e`, CI green on both jobs): in an isolated export `tsc --noEmit` for the repository and `web/`, `biome lint --error-on-warnings` and `biome format` over `src test web scripts` passed; 84/84 tests passed over `operator-cli`, `-write`, `-http`, `-inventory`, `-adopt`, `-change`, `-config-journey`, `operator-operations`, `task-comments`, `github-source-config`, `operator-configuration`, `operator-contracts` and `operator-api`; at `0cb1dd74` the same set plus `git-environment` and `project-setup` passed 93/93. `npm ci` and the full check were not rerun at planning; the last recorded full result is `docs/evidence/issue-896-cli3-2026-10-11.md`. Record any drift if `main` moves.
- No live GitHub, live Codex or Claude runtime, real credential, `~/.env`, second machine, Keychain or new UI layout is needed: source reads use injected readers, delivery uses the scripted provider that is closed to external hosts, and every journey is deterministic. No production GitHub write is performed or authorized. Missing live or private-remote evidence stays **Unproved** for #901.

### Review focus

- `send-comment`: the approval binding (review id equals operation id, exact replay before sending), that `denied`, `confirmed-failure` and `uncertain` are never reported as posted, that an identical rerun replays rather than posts, and that read-only credentials cause no provider request.
- Source edits: no private query, filter, path or reference name in any output or preview line; kept rows never re-send private text; deactivation, observation invalidation and removal irreversibility are stated; the edit equals the UI's command.
- Server classification: the T2 set is closed and never reclassifies a genuine unknown; `operation get` for `github.preview` never discloses an excluded `selectionId`.
- Each state-changing control has its counterpart or an explicit irreversible flag in help and docs; `refresh` partial outcomes are surfaced.

### Allowed deviations

- Verb, flag and edit-file field spellings beyond the fixed command shapes (`project sources|prepare-source|preview-source|place-task`, `delivery get|refresh|review-comment|confirm-comment|send-comment`), internal module names, human wording and help text may differ when docs, help and tests agree. The capability names `source.write` and `delivery.write` and the key conventions in Planning decisions are fixed.

### Re-plan triggers

- The comment-path rejections cannot be classified without altering delivery store, coordinator or receipt contracts, or a source command cannot be driven without re-sending private definitions or relaxing redaction or withholding.
- A new route, command or receipt variant, coverage gap code, exit code or web layout is needed.

content.title: CLI3: Review and apply profile/project configuration changes

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/896
**Planned against:** `main` at `eb03ca244167d2caeacffafff7adb44fc4a3143d`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Deliver CLI3 on the CLI1/CLI2 seams (`src/cli/*`, bearer auth, the fail-closed route-authority table, capability negotiation, the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope and exit codes). Implementation branch: `cb/896-cli-configuration-changes`, from `main` at or after the planned SHA.

1. **Service seams (T1, T2).** Receipt readback by `(scope, type, key)` over the existing `command_receipts` store; an optional compare-and-swap guard on `capacity.configure` (the only supported configuration write with no revision); and a targeted, bounded read of the assignments a profile or project change affects.
2. **CLI write foundation (T3).** A write transport that classifies definite versus unknown outcomes, an append-only local request journal that records the full service/scope/type/key identity before anything is sent, per-command flag allowlists, and `operation get`.
3. **Change documents (T4, T5).** `prepare` reads current state with read-only calls and writes an owner-only, digest-bound JSON change document holding exactly one typed command; `apply --file` revalidates the document and sends only that command through the existing `POST /api/operator/commands`. Covers profile and project create/configure/restore/revoke (T4), then project routing and installation capacity (T5).
4. **Adoption (T6).** `assignment apply-current` sends the existing version-checked `assignment.apply` command.
5. **Journey, shared-UI compatibility, docs and evidence (T7).**

No prepare, diff or read dispatches work. The service stays the only policy, revision and receipt authority; the CLI offers typed operations only.

### Guardrails

- **Unchanged contracts:** every existing operator command schema and its persisted request hash (proved by golden hashes in T1); browser-session Origin/CSRF protection and cookie sessions; the fail-closed `operatorRouteAuthority` table; the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope and exit-code meanings (extended, not changed); all CLI1/CLI2 commands and their output; `src/cli` imports no SQLite and no `src/standalone` module except `operator-hidden-password.js` (the existing "imports no service state" test) and uses the shared `src/operator/contracts.js` schemas.
- **Out of scope:**
  - Harness, runtime, model or effort settings. #824 is merged and #826 owns their configuration. The CLI never sends a profile `runtime`; the domain keeps the stored value when it is omitted, and `profile get` already shows it read-only. CLI-created profiles take the service default runtime.
  - GitHub source and delivery adapters, repository links and the GitHub Project link (`github.*`, `delivery.configure`, `project.create` `repositories`/`githubProject`): #897. `discovery.configure` is setup discovery, also out.
  - Tasks, dependencies, messages, questions, approvals, Stop/Resume and recovery (#898, #899), diagnostics (#900), and assembled qualification (#901).
  - Any web UI change. No new React layout is planned and `design/design.pen` has no frame for one; if a task appears to need one, report a blocker instead of inventing it. #726/#734 stay paused.
- **No confirmation or force flag.** Apply never prompts, rebases, merges or overwrites; a stale revision, changed material, wrong service or tampered document stops it. No generic command bypasses the typed operations.
- **Privacy:** change documents hold private instruction text and are owner-only (`0600`, created only as a new file). The request journal, stderr, error envelopes and any retry hint carry identities and digests, never instruction, guidance, capability or token material.
- **Plan-seam mismatch (one diagnosis plus two repair cycles in total).** Applies only when a factual assumption in this plan about the repository or an approved seam is wrong, for example: stored `command_receipts.result` cannot rebuild a receipt for one of the seven types without #886's typed results; the 64 KiB command-body limit or the strict `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` build blocks a described shape; or a named route, symbol or call flow behaves differently from this plan. After one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, stop and report for a replan.
- **Ordinary in-scope repairs (owner repairs, no allowance, do not consume the budget above):** implementation bugs, type/lint/format errors, fixture and test setup, equivalent paths or names, documentation and evidence text, and CI or flaky-test retries. Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes, or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews; no integration amendment is needed unless a published integration decision changes.

### Planning decisions

- **One document, one command, one receipt.** Project creation, project configuration, routing, profile creation, profile configuration and capacity each get their own document kind (`project.create`, `project.configure`, `routing.configure`, `profile.create`, `profile.configure`, `capacity.configure`). The receipt scope is the command's domain scope: the project ID, `profile:<id>`, or `system:capacity`. CLI scope strings are `project:<id>`, `profile:<id>` and `system:capacity`; the readback route maps `project:<id>` to the stored bare project ID.
- **The key is not in the document.** The document is the reviewed material (the digest covers every field except `digest`). The request key is an execution identity held in the journal, so one document cannot silently acquire a second identity. `apply` uses `--request-id` if given, else the journal key already recorded for the same service and document digest, else a new UUID persisted before sending. Every CLI3 command is revision- or value-checked, so even a deliberately new key cannot duplicate an effect.
- **Digest limits.** The digest detects modification or substitution of the file by accident or in transit. It is not a MAC and does not defend against a same-user writer who recomputes it; the server's revision checks and the service-identity check still apply.
- **Capacity guard.** `capacity.configure` has no version, and the React page states it has no compare-and-swap guarantee. The acceptance requires concurrent-edit detection for every supported configuration write, so add an optional `expectedCurrent` (`globalLimit`, and a per-project override map where `null` means none) to the operator and domain command schemas. It is compared inside the command transaction before any update and raises `DomainConflictError` (409 `conflict`). Commands without it parse, hash and behave exactly as before; replay returns the recorded result before the guard runs. The React page keeps its existing last-writer-wins behavior and wording.
- **Readback.** `GET /api/operator/operations?scope=&type=&key=` returns `state: "recorded"` with the same receipt `POST` returned, or `state: "not-recorded"`. Receipts are rebuilt from the stored result by a function extracted from `OperatorApi.execute` into `src/standalone/operator-receipts.ts`, so the POST and the readback cannot drift and private row text (instructions, guidance) is never projected. A stored result whose shape does not match the requested `type` is a 409 `conflict`. This does not absorb #886's typed-result refactor or #873's error classification.
- **Impact read.** The only existing per-assignment revision facts are inside `readTask`, which would need one heavy read per task. T2 adds `GET /api/operator/projects|profiles/:id/impact` returning bounded assignment rows (ID, task, project, profile, state, lead flag, bound and current revisions, derived stale flags; default and maximum 200, `total`, `truncated`). Lead bindings whose assignment row has not been created yet are not listed; the document says so. The list is informational with its observation time and is never an apply-time fence.
- **Restore is instruction content only.** `--restore-revision N` takes the text of retained revision N from the dedicated instructions view and proposes it as a new revision. It fails closed with `invalid-input` and no document when that text is `redacted` or `omitted`, because proposing sanitized text would silently change the instructions. Name, summary, capabilities and `revoked` are set by their own flags. Identical-to-current content is rejected as "no change" so no empty revision is created.
- **Diff against redacted or withheld values.** Current text comes from the disclosed instruction views and configuration reads. When it is `redacted`, `omitted` or `null`, the diff says so (`content-redacted`, `redaction-unavailable`, or "(unavailable)") and apply still relies on the revision check. Routing guidance is replace-only and never read, matching the React page; the diff shows the proposed text and "current not readable".
- **Write outcome classification.** Definite not-applied: connection refused or DNS failure, TLS verification failure, a 3xx, and any 4xx. Unknown (`command-outcome-unknown`, exit 6, retryable): any other transport failure or timeout after the request may have been sent, a 2xx whose body is not the expected receipt, a receipt that does not match the request, and any 5xx. A 403 `forbidden` on `POST /api/operator/commands` is a domain policy denial and is reported as `policy-denied` (exit 4); `insufficient-scope` and `credential-invalid` stay authentication (exit 3).
- **Creation pre-check.** A duplicate profile or project ID with a fresh key surfaces from the service as an unclassified 503 (#873 owns typed classification). For creation documents, when the journal holds no earlier attempt for the key, `apply` first reads the target's configuration and reports `conflict` if it already exists.
- **Command size.** The service rejects non-question command bodies above 64 KiB (`MAX_FORM_BYTES`). `prepare` and `apply` check the exact serialized body and fail with `invalid-input` instead of sending.
- **Strict flags.** Write commands reject any flag outside their allowlist with exit 2 before any request. CLI2's "ignore unused flags" behavior is unchanged for browse commands.
- **Reverse operations.** Instruction restore, profile revoke/unrevoke (`--revoked`), project pause/unpause, routing enable/disable and candidate changes, and capacity override set/clear are all reachable through `prepare`. Intentionally irreversible, and stated in help and docs: project and profile creation (there is no delete; revoke or pause instead) and adoption (the bound revision only moves forward; to return to older text, restore it as a new revision and adopt again).
- **Entry points for shared behavior.** Profile, project, routing and capacity writes use the same commands as the React Settings pages. `assignment.apply` is exposed by the retained `/runtime/control/instruction-apply` page; the React UI has no adoption control and none is added (no design frame). Restore, change documents and operation readback are CLI/API-only. T7 records this table and the gaps.
- **Assumption evidence.** Stored results are the same rows `execute` projects (`DomainStore.executeParsed` stores `JSON.stringify(result)`); T1's first check proves POST/readback equality for all seven types, and a failure triggers the plan-seam budget. Exact restore text relies on `instructionBody` setting `redacted: text !== raw`.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/cli/main.ts` — `main` parses argv with strict `parseArgs`, dispatches `auth`/`connection`/`task get` itself and everything else through `browseCommands` (`src/cli/commands.ts`); `connect` negotiates capabilities through `ServiceClient.identity` and compares `installationId`; `EXIT` maps error codes to exit codes; the JSON error envelope writes `outcome: "unknown"` only for `command-outcome-unknown`.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/transport.ts` — `ServiceClient` is GET-only (`request`, `get`, `getBytes`, `identity`), never follows redirects, and maps 5xx to `unavailable`. `src/cli/connections.ts` — `CliError(code, message, extra)`, `ConnectionConfig.write` (temp file, `0600`, rename) and `readTokenFile` (O_NOFOLLOW, regular file, owner, no group/other bits) are the patterns for the journal and document I/O. `src/cli/browse.ts` — `uuidArg`, `enumArg`, `coverage`, `browseOutput`, the closed `COVERAGE_GAPS`. `src/cli/render.ts` — `table`, `keyValues`, `isoTime`, `oneLine`, `unavailable`.

**Implementation:** Routing: read `/projects/:id/configuration`; defaults are the current `enabled` and the current non-revoked candidates (the React page's behavior), and the command always carries `enabled` and `candidateProfileIds`; send `guidance`/`credentialRef` only when requested. Capacity: build `projectOverrides` only for listed projects (`default` becomes `null`) and `expectedCurrent` from the same read; the effect note says the scheduler is woken after the commit and may admit waiting work.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-routing-capacity.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-change.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Routing and capacity change only through reviewed documents with server-enforced concurrent-edit detection and accurate effect reporting.

#### 6. Explicit current-instruction adoption

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 (transport, journal, registry; transitively T1's `configuration.write`).
**Files and symbols:** new `src/cli/adopt.ts`; `src/cli/commands.ts`, `src/cli/main.ts` `USAGE`.
Command: `assignment apply-current ASSIGNMENT_ID --expected-version N [--request-id UUID]` (`--expected-version` required).
**Test:** New `test/operator-cli-adopt.test.ts`.
- Stale lead A adopts: exit 0, assignment version +1, receipt revisions equal the current profile and project revisions, `assignment instructions` then reports `boundIsCurrent: true`; with a recorded execution request (use `captureNativeResult`) its revisions are unchanged and `matchesBound` is false, and the output says the next turn uses the current revisions and an active turn is not rewritten.
- A stale `--expected-version`, whether supplied up front or made stale by a competing adoption between the CLI's assignment read and its send (a fetch hook), gives exit 4 `conflict` and leaves the binding unchanged; a revoked profile gives `policy-denied` (exit 4); an unknown assignment exits 2; a missing `--expected-version` exits 2 before any request; a read-only credential exits 3 with no change.
- Same `--request-id` replays the recorded receipt and bumps the version once; a lost reply (the stub forwards the request, then throws) gives exit 6 with the full identity, and `operation get --scope project:<projectId> --type assignment.apply` reads the receipt; re-running without `--request-id` reuses the journal key and returns the same receipt.
**Implementation:** Read `GET /assignments/:id` for `projectId` and `version` (capabilities `assignment.read`, `configuration.write`), build `assignment.apply` with `expectedVersion` from the flag, journal, send. The journal material digest is the hash of installation, assignment and expected version. State in help that adoption is one-way and affects only the next turn.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-adopt.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-write.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-assignment.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Adoption is explicit, version-checked, receipted, idempotent and never rewrites an active turn.

#### 7. Journey, shared-UI compatibility, docs and evidence

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `T4, T5, T6`
**Prerequisites:** T4, T5 and T6 merged on the branch; a full `npm run build` for the packed test.
**Files and symbols:** new `test/operator-cli-config-journey.test.ts`; `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts` (one write command through the installed binary); `test/operator-cli-inventory.test.ts` (final command and capability lists); docs `README.md` (Operator CLI bullet), `docs/development.md` (Operator CLI section: commands, documents, journal, effects, exit codes), `docs/SPEC.md` (Operator CLI section), `docs/design/operator-cli.md` (capability names, the three new route shapes, document and journal behavior, the capacity guard, `policy-denied`/`wrong-service`/`change-document-invalid`/`journal-unavailable`, that restore is instruction-only, and that the design's `create` verbs are `prepare-create` followed by `apply`), `docs/acceptance.md` (CLI3 slice-evidence pointer; scenarios stay **Unproved** until #901) and new `docs/evidence/issue-896-cli3-YYYY-MM-DD.md` (the run date).
**Test:** `test/operator-cli-config-journey.test.ts` runs one real-SQLite service journey through the in-process `harness` (`main`):
- prepare with a read-only credential, review the diff and impact, apply with a read-write credential, read back the receipt with `operation get`, and confirm the same profile and project values through the bearer and the session-cookie configuration reads;
- create profile and project, revoke and unrevoke, restore old content as a new revision, then adopt it on a stale assignment;
- race a session edit and a task creation with an initial assignment against prepared documents;
- tamper, wrong service, stale adoption, a read-only denial, and an unreadable journal;
- reply loss: the stub forwards the request then throws, `apply` exits 6, a separate CLI invocation (new process state) runs `operation get` and sees the receipt, a service restart on the same database and port (add a `restart()` helper to `startCliService` that stops the HTTP listener, calls `f.reopen()` and restarts on the same port with fresh credential and auth wiring) still replays, and re-running `apply` returns the identical receipt with the project, profile or capacity changed exactly once;
- identical UUIDs in distinct scopes: one key used for a project, a profile and a capacity document each applies and reads back only its own receipt, and reusing it under the wrong scope or type cannot select another receipt; the same key with different material in the same scope exits 4;
- shared UI: after a CLI edit, a session-origin `profile.configure` or `project.configure` with the pre-edit `expectedVersion` returns the existing 409 conflict, session and bearer configuration reads agree, and the capacity command without a guard still applies.
- Help output lists no `--runtime`, `--model` or `github` option; the existing Chromium and WebKit settings and setup suites run unchanged.
**Implementation:** Write the journey and docs; verify docs state current behavior in place (no dated sections), distinguish implemented from planned (CLI4+ commands stay planned), and list the CLI3 limits: no runtime/model fields, no repository or GitHub linking, bound leads without an assignment row are not in the affected list, `capacity get` reuses the heavier runtime read pending #875, creation is not reversible, adoption is one-way, no real second machine or Keychain run. The evidence record names the candidate SHA, environment (Node, npm, Playwright), covered operations (profile, project, routing, capacity prepare/apply, restore, revoke, adoption, `operation get`, `capacity get`) with their denial, revision and retry cases, the entry-point table (React Settings for profile/project/routing/capacity; retained `/runtime/control/instruction-apply` for adoption; none for restore, documents, readback) and the remaining gaps.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/operator-cli-config-journey.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-packed.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-inventory.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-http.test.js dist/test/operator-web-integration.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** The journey, packed binary, inventory and unchanged UI suites pass, docs and the evidence record match the behavior, and the entry-point table and gaps are recorded.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Profile and project creation, supported configuration, project instructions, routing and capacity; no GitHub adapters or runtime/model controls | 4, 5 | T4 checks 1, 2, 5 and the no-`runtime` assertions; T5 routing and capacity checks; help lists no `github.*`, `runtime` or `model` option |
| Owner-only change document with service identity, targets, expected revisions, exact fields and digest; readable diff; preparation-time affected list that is not an apply fence; no dispatch | 2, 4, 5 | T2 impact checks; T4 checks 1 and 7; T4 database-digest assertion |
| Exact reviewed material applied; substitution, wrong service and concurrent edits detected; no prompt, silent rebase or overwrite | 1, 4, 5 | T4 checks 6, 8, 9; T5 routing/capacity concurrency; T1 capacity guard |
| Immutable revisions, revoke and restore, old content restored as a new revision, version-checked adoption for the next turn only | 4, 6 | T4 checks 2, 3, 4; T6 adoption checks |
| Request key and receipt path with readback; identity bound to service, scope/type and UUID; persisted before send; caller keys; reconciliation; identical replay; changed material conflicts; another scope cannot select the receipt | 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 | T1 operations and goldens; T3 journal and transport; T4 check 5; T6 replay; T7 journey (reply loss, restart, identical UUIDs in distinct scopes) |
| Committed versus queued reported accurately; auth, policy, conflict, unavailability and unknown errors exposed; no secrets in retry logs | 3, 4, 5, 6 | T3 transport table; T4 checks 2 and 11; T5 effect notes |
| Complete journey, create/revoke/restore, concurrency, assignment creation between prepare and apply, tampering, stale adoption, reply loss/restart/replay, identical UUIDs, read-only denial, shared UI and hashes | 1, 7 | T7 journey and unchanged UI suites; T1 goldens |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root on Node 24.21.0 (`~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH`, per `.node-version`), after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate; expect typecheck, lint, format, build and the full suite to pass, including the Chromium and WebKit suites. Playwright browsers are cached; CI pins npm 12.2.0 and runs Node 26. Local npm may differ (11.19.0 at planning time); CI on the pull request is authoritative for the pinned toolchain.
- A browser-diagnostics test was observed flaky on Node 26. If it alone fails in an unrelated way, rerun its file once and record the run; do not edit it unless this change caused the failure.
- Baseline at the planned SHA: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build:service`, and the CLI, credential, instruction, domain, settings-browser, packed, API and HTTP suites passed (43 and 49 tests in the two focused groups). Record any baseline drift if `main` moves.

### Review focus

- Unknown-outcome handling is fail-closed everywhere a request can leave the machine, and the journal line precedes the request.
- Restore and diff never propose sanitized text as if exact; redaction states are visible.
- The capacity guard sits inside the command transaction and replay still returns the recorded result.
- No private text reaches the journal, stderr, error envelopes or retry hints.
- Each state-changing command has its documented counterpart or is flagged irreversible (creation, adoption); the entry-point table is complete.

### Allowed deviations

- Flag spellings, internal module boundaries and file names under `src/cli` may differ from this plan when help text, docs and tests agree. The command shapes the design fixes stay: `profile prepare`, `profile apply --file`, `assignment apply-current --expected-version`, and `operation get --scope`.

### Re-plan triggers

- A CLI3 receipt cannot be rebuilt from stored results without #886's typed results or a persisted schema change.
- The capacity guard needs a persisted version column or migration.
- Any scope change that sends `runtime`/model fields or `github.*` commands from CLI3, or a needed React layout with no design frame.

content.title: CLI2: Browse work, instructions, history and retained evidence

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/895
**Planned against:** `main` at `4e2a119fe84fff32440934550bd4ad215b3e7f80`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add a read-only browse surface to the packaged CLI on the CLI1 seams: the bearer path and fail-closed `operatorRouteAuthority` table in `LocalOperatorHttp`, `GET /api/operator/cli` capability negotiation, the `ensemble.cli/v1` envelope and the exit-code map. Reuse existing service reads wherever they already carry the right projection. Add only additive GET routes, all class `read`, where the issue needs something that does not exist: assignment detail, dedicated instruction reads with bound-versus-current comparison, and paged result and message lists. Extend three existing reads without changing their defaults: task list filters, an assignment-history page size, and explicit stale-cursor errors. Add evidence-source and digest headers to artifact bytes. The CLI gains 18 commands in three area modules over shared plumbing (opaque cursor tokens, `pagination` and `coverage` envelope fields, byte download, capability gating). Implement on `cb/895-cli-browse-work-evidence` from `main` at the planned SHA as one pull request; commits and the PR carry no AI attribution (AGENTS.md).

Authority: the issue's acceptance criteria, the [operator CLI design](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/4e2a119fe84fff32440934550bd4ad215b3e7f80/docs/design/operator-cli.md), [ADR-1010](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/4e2a119fe84fff32440934550bd4ad215b3e7f80/docs/adr/1010-operator-cli.md), the parent contract in [#893](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/893), and CLI01/CLI02/CLI05 in [acceptance](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/4e2a119fe84fff32440934550bd4ad215b3e7f80/docs/acceptance.md#operator-cli-acceptance). Delivered CLI1 behaviour is in [the CLI1 plan](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/894#issuecomment-6110914685) and `docs/evidence/issue-894-cli1-2026-10-11.md`.

### Guardrails

- CLI2 scope only: read-only browsing of projects, profiles, tasks, assignments, instructions, conversation history, results and artifacts. Not in scope: create/prepare/apply/adopt (CLI3 #896), GitHub source and delivery inspection or operations (CLI4 #897), `inbox`/`question`/`approval`, task controls and sending messages (CLI5 #898), `recovery` (CLI6 #899), `execution`/`logs`/captured inputs/diagnostic capture/follow (CLI7 #900), assembled qualification (CLI8 #901), receipts and `operation`, and the paused #726/#734/X01–X08 work. Add none of those command areas.
- Every route used by a CLI2 command is class `read` for both credential scopes and persists nothing (bearer credential last-use metadata excepted). A read-only credential must complete every CLI2 command. Do not reclassify a needed GET as `write`.
- Existing UI projections and contracts are unchanged for valid requests: defaults and caps (task list 100/100, search 50, history 200, evidence manifest unpaged), response shapes and status codes. Only additive routes/params, plus two edge changes: an unknown but well-formed task-list or search cursor becomes `409 conflict` (was `400` and a silent empty page respectively). The web client sends neither.
- General reads keep full instruction redaction. The disclosure variant of `OperatorApi.exclusions` is used only by the three new instruction methods. Dedicated views still redact credential values and references, control/workspace/repository paths and credential patterns, and omit text with an explicit reason when exclusions cannot be computed. Never add an unredacted switch or credential-file export.
- Label reconstruction honestly: revision text is "reconstructed from retained revision records", never the submitted prompt, the runtime's effective prompt or a transcript. Conversation history is bounded, sanitized assistant text. Absence of tool or event data is not evidence that none occurred.
- Never replace unavailable historical evidence with current workspace contents. Keep `readArtifact`'s existing behaviour: a result with a retained manifest is served only from retained bytes. The CLI writes only the `--out` file it creates exclusively with mode `0600`.
- Preserve CLI1: auth/connection/`task get` behaviour (output prefix lines, exit-code map additions only), redirect rejection, token handling, managed-assignment refusal for every new command, and the rule that `src/cli/**` imports no `node:sqlite` or service module except `operator-hidden-password.js`. The packaged executable and host-local `npm run service|operations|operator-auth` stay compatible.
- No `design/design.pen` or web UI change. If implementation shows a UI layout is needed, stop and report a blocker; do not invent a frame.
- Do not refactor shared reads owned by #873/#875/#877/#883/#886. Before T1 and T2, run `git log -5 --oneline origin/main -- src/standalone/operator-api.ts` and `gh issue view 875`/`877`. If one landed, adopt its seam (especially a once-per-request exclusion set from #877) instead of duplicating it.
- **Plan-mismatch budget (a):** if an approved seam or repository fact in this plan is wrong, record one focused diagnosis and use at most two repair cycles. Approved assumptions: the disclosure variant is obtainable by omitting only instruction-revision texts from `exclusions()` while keeping its coverage validation; every reused GET persists nothing (offline probe at planning time: workspace, task list, search, task, review, history, both configurations and evidence reads left a whole-database digest unchanged); `readTask` can be sliced for paged results/messages with identical projections; `CoordinationView.readAssignmentHistory` can carry a limit. If the cycles are exhausted, or the fix would change the accepted contract (for example a needed read must persist), stop and replan.
- **Ordinary repairs (b):** in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, formatting/lint and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume budget (a). This includes updating existing assertions on the capability list, path or symbol corrections, fixture setup, flaky waits, npm 11/12 differences and renewed evidence. Record a correction briefly in the delivery record when requirements, coverage, architecture and authority are unchanged.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision needing durable consumption. Stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Command inventory** (all read-only, human and `--output json`; every command also refuses inside a managed assignment). Existing `task get` stays.

  | Command | Reads (all `GET /api/operator/…`) | JSON `data` |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `project list`, `profile list` | `workspace` | `{projects, runtime}` or `{profiles, runtime}` (the served `data` subset) |
  | `project get ID`, `profile get ID` | `projects/ID/configuration`, `profiles/ID/configuration` | as served (includes routing, source selections, profile `runtime` harness/model) |
  | `project instructions ID [--revision N]`, `profile instructions ID [--revision N]` | `…/instructions[?revision=N]` (new) | as served |
  | `project revisions ID`, `profile revisions ID` | same read | `{currentRevision, revisions}` |
  | `task list [--project ID] [--state S] [--limit N] [--cursor T]` | `task-list` (extended) | `{tasks}` page as served |
  | `task search QUERY [--project ID] [--type task\|decision\|result] [--after T] [--before T] [--historical] [--limit N] [--cursor T]` | `search` | `{matches}` |
  | `task messages ID [--limit N] [--cursor T]` | `tasks/ID/messages` (new) | page as served (`messages`, `total`) |
  | `assignment get ID` | `assignments/ID` (new) | as served |
  | `assignment history ID [--limit N] [--cursor T]` | `assignments/ID/history?limit` | `{items, turnOmissions, omittedItemCount, omittedTurnCount}` |
  | `assignment instructions ID` | `assignments/ID/instructions` (new) | as served |
  | `result list ID [--limit N] [--cursor T]` | `tasks/ID/results` (new) | page as served (`results`, `total`) |
  | `result get TASK RESULT` | `tasks/TASK/results?resultId=`, `tasks/TASK/review?resultId=`, `tasks/TASK/results/RESULT/evidence` | `{result, review, evidence}` |
  | `result evidence TASK RESULT ITEM [--out PATH]` | `…/evidence/ITEM` | item as served (`--out` writes verified bytes) |
  | `artifact get TASK ARTIFACT --out PATH` | `tasks/TASK/artifacts/ARTIFACT` | `{artifactId, path, size, sha256, mime, source}` |

  Result and artifact discovery is `result get`, which lists recorded artifacts and retained evidence items with `artifactId`/`itemId`. There is no separate `artifact list`. Delivery state stays in `task get` and is CLI4's to extend. JSON `data` equals the API's `data` (the named subset for project and profile lists), minus pagination internals (`nextCursor`, `catalogFingerprint`) that move into `pagination`/`coverage`.
- **Limits.** New routes (`results`, `messages`) default to 50 and cap at 200. Existing routes keep their lower caps and defaults: task list 100, search 50, history 200 (new optional `limit` 1–200, absent means 200). The CLI always sends an explicit `limit` (default 50, accepts 1–200) and clamps to the route cap, reporting `pagination.maxLimit` and gap `limit-capped`. Project, profile, revision, evidence-manifest (≤320 items), review (≤128 results) and instruction reads are single bounded reads; they report `complete` and counts and have no cursor. Projects plus profiles stay small in practice because `exclusions()` fails closed beyond 128 combined (names then read as `null`, which the CLI reports as gap `content-unavailable`). The CLI never fetches a following page unless asked.
- **Cursors.** The server cursor stays a keyset id (task id, search record id, result id, message event id, history `beforeSequence`/`beforeOmissionSequence`). The CLI returns it as an opaque token `base64url({v:1,k:kind,q:canonicalQuery,c:serverCursor,f:fingerprint?})` and rejects (exit 2 `invalid-input`) a malformed token, a token of another command, or one used with different filters. An unknown well-formed cursor is `409 conflict` on task list, search, results and messages; with `--cursor` set the CLI reports it as `cursor-stale` (exit 4, not retryable, message says to restart without `--cursor`). Task-list continuity: the token carries `catalogFingerprint`; a differing fingerprint on the next page adds gap `catalog-changed` and `coverage.continuity:"changed"` (entries may repeat or be missed; restart for a consistent listing). History keysets cannot go stale; pruning shows as fewer items plus the omitted counts.
- **Envelope additions** (additive; schema stays `ensemble.cli/v1`; top-level `observedAt` stays the client time). List reads add `pagination:{limit,maxLimit,returned,nextCursor|null}`. Every CLI2 read adds `coverage:{observedAt,complete,gaps:[…],notes:[…],continuity?}` where `observedAt` is the service read time (the oldest of several reads). `gaps` is a closed set: `more-pages`, `limit-capped`, `catalog-changed`, `older-history-omitted`, `item-omitted`, `content-redacted`, `content-unavailable`, `redaction-unavailable`, `evidence-gap`, `evidence-unavailable`, `review-unavailable`. `complete` is true only when no gap is present. `task get` also gains `coverage` (`content-unavailable` when `contentUnavailable`). Human output prints a `Gap:` line per gap and a `More:` line with the exact next command.
- **Filters** are server-side: task list `projectId` (unknown project is 404) and `state` (open/done/cancelled) on the catalog, search's existing filters (`--after`/`--before` take ISO-8601 or epoch milliseconds and map to the existing millisecond filters). Filtering by execution state or attention is not offered: it needs per-task computation owned by #875, so a client-side filter would be silently incomplete. `task list` summaries already carry execution state, holds and attention codes for scanning.
- **Instruction reads** (new routes, `read` authority, session and bearer alike; the browser UI does not use them):
  - `exclusions(projectId?, taskId?, historyBindings?, options?)` gains `options.instructions: "exclude" | "disclose"` (default `exclude`). `disclose` skips only the push of instruction-revision texts into `values`; coverage validation, credential refs and values, control paths, repository and workspace paths and the 128-revision budget are unchanged. The new methods take `visibilityToken()` before and after the await and throw `503 unavailable` on change, like `readAssignmentHistory`.
  - Text goes through `sanitizeConversationText` with the disclose exclusions, so credential patterns (`token=…`, bearer, URL credentials) are redacted too. Each body is `{revision, state:"available"|"omitted", reason:"redaction-unavailable"|null, text|null, redacted}`; `redacted` is true when sanitization changed the stored text; `omitted` when exclusions are unavailable, the sanitizer rejects the text, or the result exceeds 16000 characters.
  - Profile views add `name`, `capabilities`, `revoked` and `runtime` (from `profileRuntime(profileId, revision)`) for that revision. `GET profiles|projects/ID/instructions[?revision=N]` returns `{summary, currentRevision, revisions:[{revision,current,instructionChars,…}], selected, provenance}`; no `revision` selects the current one; unknown or out-of-range revision is 404; non-integer is 400.
  - `GET assignments/ID/instructions` returns `bound` (the assignment's persisted `profileRevision`/`instructionsRevision`), `current`, `comparison:{profile:{sameRevision,sameContent},project:{…},boundIsCurrent}` (`sameContent` compares raw stored text on the server and is `null` if either side is omitted) and `execution` (`null`, or the latest turn request's `workId`, `requestSequence`, revisions and `matchesBound`, from `selection(a).request`). Older revisions are read with `--revision`; history items already carry their own revision numbers. `provenance` is the constant `{source:"retained-revision-records", reconstructed:true, submittedPrompt:"not-captured"}`; the view excludes the assignment brief and supplied messages (available from `assignment get`).
  - The CLI prints no computed diff; both sides are shown. CLI3 owns diff rendering.
- **Assignment detail** `GET assignments/ID` resolves the task with `domain().assignment(id).taskId` (O(1); unknown is 404) and returns the matching `assignmentSchema` entry from `readTask(taskId)` plus `{taskId, projectId, taskVersion, lead, execution}`. Adopt a targeted read inside it if #875 has landed.
- **Paged results and messages** call `readTask(taskId)` and slice `data.results`/`data.messages` in their existing order, so projections and redaction are identical to `task get` by construction; `total` and `nextCursor` come from the slice. `results` also accepts `resultId` (single item, 404 if absent; incompatible with `cursor`). `409` for a cursor not in the list.
- **Artifact bytes** keep `readArtifact`'s selection logic. It returns `source:"retained"` (manifest-backed) or `"recorded-workspace"` (pre-retention result whose workspace file still matches the recorded sha256; a changed file is the existing `409`). Both response sites in `operator.ts` add `x-ensemble-evidence-source` and `x-ensemble-sha256` (digest of the verified body). The CLI recomputes the digest; mismatch is `integrity-mismatch` (exit 5, retryable) and no file is kept. `result evidence … --out` checks `item.sha256`/`size` the same way.
- **Capabilities.** `cliCapabilities` becomes an exported const in `contracts.ts` used by `handleBearer` and the CLI. Order: `cli.identity`, `task.read` (unchanged first), then `workspace.read`, `task.list`, `task.search`, `task.records` (T1), `assignment.read`, `instructions.read` (T2), `result.read`, `artifact.read` (T3). Each slice appends only the families it completes. `apiVersion` stays 1. Each command declares the capabilities it needs; a missing one is `unsupported-service` (exit 7) before any read.
- **Error additions.** `cursor-stale` → exit 4 (`conflict`); `integrity-mismatch` → exit 5 (`unavailable`, retryable); `output-exists`/`output-failed` → exit 2 (`usage`). Server 404 stays exit 2 `not-found`, 409 stays exit 4, 503 stays exit 5.
- **Entry points and gaps** (reported in the evidence record): task list/search/detail/history/results/evidence/artifact reads also exist in the web UI and share the same server projections. Instruction bodies, revision lists and bound-versus-current comparison are CLI/API-only: the web shows `instructionPresent` only, by design ADR-1010 and no design frame. - The disclose variant of `exclusions()` is reachable only from the three instruction methods; no other caller changes behaviour, and general-read redaction tests still pass.
- Cursor honesty: no path returns an empty complete-looking page for an unresolvable cursor; `complete` is never true while a gap exists.
- Artifact and evidence retrieval never serves workspace bytes for a result that has a retained manifest, and the CLI never leaves a partial or unverified `--out` file.
- Every new route is `read`, absent from session-only, and persists nothing (digest checks).

### Allowed deviations (task-specific)

- Flag spelling, human table layout and help text may change if the command inventory, JSON `data` shapes, gap codes and exit codes in this plan are kept and the docs, help and inventory test agree.
- Internal helper placement (for example `readTaskRecordPage` as one method or two) may change within the files named.

### Re-plan triggers (task-specific)

- A reused GET persists state, or a needed read cannot be served to a read-only credential.
- The disclosure variant cannot be produced without changing general-read exclusions, or #877/#875 lands an incompatible seam that cannot be adopted within the two repair cycles.
- A UI layout or `design/design.pen` change turns out to be required.

### Readiness prerequisites (unattended execution)

- **Node/npm:** Node 24.21.0 at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` must be first on `PATH` (default `node` is 26.9.0). CI pins npm 12.2.0 (`packageManager`); the local npm is 11.19.0 and `npm pack --json` prints an array there but an object keyed by package name in 12.x, which `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts` already accepts, so run locally with 11.19.0 and rely on CI for the pinned npm unless `npm install -g npm@12.2.0` is possible.
- **Browser:** Playwright 1.64.0 with Chromium and WebKit builds are in `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` (verified offline); needed only by the regression browser suites and the full check. CI installs them with `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit`.
- **Keychain:** not needed for CLI2. The CLI1 Keychain live test is not part of this slice. Tests use the in-memory credential store and token files.
- **OpenSSL/network:** `openssl` (4.0.3 locally) only for the existing packed HTTPS case; network only for a cold `npm ci` or installing npm 12.2.0. No live Codex runtime, remote machine or GitHub write is required.

Baseline evidence at `4e2a119f` with Node 24.21.0 and npm 11.19.0, after the existing install: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run build:service` clean; `node --test` on `operator-cli`, `operator-cli-http`, `operator-credentials`, `operator-task-list`, `operator-search`, `operator-api` and `operator-web-http` passed 69/69; `operator-cli-packed`, `operator-retained-evidence`, `operator-task-review`, `coordination-view`, `operator-search-browser` and `operator-task-browser` passed 45/45. A read-only probe showed the existing workspace, task-list, search, task, review, history, both configuration and retained-evidence reads leave a whole-database digest unchanged.

content.title: Claude harness C0: Probe the Claude Agent SDK surfaces

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/822
**Planned against:** `main` at `111f46d744db3d8f15b562a5014ae12945d2c4c2`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Run the issue's eight probes against the Claude Agent SDK in one disposable root outside the repository and
record the outcome of each in `docs/evidence/`. Commit the probe scripts under `test/claude-c0/` (a harness, a
driver and one module per probe group) so the recorded commands are reproducible. Install the SDK only inside the
disposable root; the repository gains no dependency. Every probe is split into named facets, and each facet ends
`passed`, `failed` or `untested` with a reason. T2 is the bounded proof that the SDK launches, its subprocess
identity is capturable and a token-only turn authenticates under an isolated configuration; probes that need a
model turn depend on it. T8 assembles the evidence record and cleans up. Deliver as one PR from
`cb/822-claude-sdk-probes`.

### Guardrails

- **Scope.** The deliverables are `test/claude-c0/**`, `test/claude-c0-harness.test.ts` and
  `docs/evidence/issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-*`. Do not touch `src/**`, `web/**`, `package.json`,
  `package-lock.json`, ADR-1008, SPEC, README, acceptance or CONTEXT. `ClaudeRuntime` and the SDK dependency belong
  to C3 #825. README, SPEC and acceptance text about Claude belongs to C5 #827. Add no probe beyond the issue's
  eight; the facets below are their sub-observations.
- **Disposable boundary.** The SDK install, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, decoy `HOME`, workspace, outside-write targets
