  and raw traces all live under one `mkdtemp` root named `ensemble-claude-c0-*` directly under the OS temp
  directory. No probe reads or writes the Ensemble data directory or database, an operator project, the installed
  Haze prototype, `~/.claude` or the real `HOME`. The only repository code the harness imports is the pure
  `captureProcessIdentity`, `readProcessBirthIdentity` and `MacProcessTerminationVerifier` from
  `dist/src/standalone/termination.js`.
- **Credential handling.** Read the token only as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, from the process environment, then
  from `~/.env` by that exact variable name. Never print, log, record, put in argv or write it anywhere. Pass the
  SDK an explicit allowlist environment (`env` replaces the subprocess environment): no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
  `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE` or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*`, because those outrank the OAuth token and
  would bill an API key, which ADR-1008 defers. The agent does not run `claude setup-token`, `/login` or any
  login flow and does not mint, request or substitute credentials.
- **Processes.** Signal only an exact PID whose birth identity (`captureProcessIdentity`) still matches the one
  recorded at spawn; SIGTERM first, a bounded wait, then SIGKILL only on the same verified identity. Never use
  `pkill -f`, name matching or process-group guesses. Record each signal and its verification.
- **Results are results.** A `failed` or `untested` facet is recorded as such and never worked around or
  re-run into a pass. A `failed` facet tagged `[ADR]` contradicts an ADR-1008 guarantee: report it prominently in
  the evidence and the delivery summary as returned to Chris, and change neither ADR-1008 nor code to
  accommodate it. Failed untagged facets are recorded as limits. Probe outcomes never consume the repair
  allowance below.
- **Bounds.** Run live steps sequentially (one subscription, one config directory). At most 60 model-backed
  `query()` calls in total, at most 3 attempts per facet, and a 120 s wall-clock limit per query enforced by abort
  plus exact-PID cleanup. At the cap, record the remaining facets `untested` with that reason.
- **Plan-mismatch budget versus ordinary repairs.** The budget covers (a) a wrong approved-plan seam or
  repository assumption. Examples: the `termination.js` helpers are not exported or do not behave as described;
  `npm run check` cannot lint, format or load `test/claude-c0/*.mjs` or the harness test as planned; the
  correlation seam for a facet cannot see what it needs (for example PreToolUse `tool_use_id` cannot be matched
  to the assistant `tool_use` blocks); the harness cannot be imported without the SDK installed. For such a
  mismatch, spend at most one focused diagnosis and two repair cycles, recording each in the delivery record.
  Stop and return for replanning if the plan is still wrong or the fix needs a material design or contract change.
  It does not cover (b) ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI
  repairs, which the ticket owner fixes as normal work without spending the allowance: harness or script bugs,
  type, lint and format errors, unit-test failures, prompt or fixture tuning so the model performs the intended
  action (within the attempt cap), timing and watchdog values, evidence wording and structure, CI failures within
  the unchanged design, and retries of transient API errors. A probe observation that contradicts an expectation
  is neither (a) nor (b); it is a result.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture
  and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for
  material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed
  published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Probe sources are committed `.mjs`; the SDK is not a dependency.** `test/ui01/runtime-contract.mjs`,
  `test/wi828/live-operator-follow-up.mjs` and `test/s03b/live-runtime.mjs` set the precedent for guarded live
  scripts. `tsconfig.json` compiles only `*.ts`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs` runs only `dist/test/*.test.js`, and
  Biome lints and formats `**`, so `.mjs` probes are linted but never type-checked or run by `npm run check`.
  The harness must load the SDK lazily from the disposable install, because CI has no SDK. AGENTS.md adds
  dependencies when concrete implementation needs them; C3 owns that.
- **Readiness facts at planning time (2026-10-11).** `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` is not in the repository
  (`npm view` reports 0.3.296 as latest). `claude` 2.1.296 is at `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude`, and the SDK
  resolves its own bundled executable by default. `~/.env` has no `CLAUDE_*` or `ANTHROPIC_*` variable name.
  `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` exists. Node 24.21.0 (`.node-version`) is under `~/.nvm/versions/node`.
- **Executable.** Probe the SDK's default-resolved executable, the production path. Record its version and
  `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude --version`. If they differ, repeat only the model-free launch and PID observations
  (F8.1, F8.4) with `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` set to the installed CLI and disclose the difference.
- **Authentication prerequisite.** The authentication docs say a non-default `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` keys the macOS
  Keychain entry to that directory, so the operator's existing `claude` login is not shared with the dedicated
  directory. Only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (from `claude setup-token`, minted by Chris) can authenticate probes
  under ADR-1008's isolation. None is available now. Without it, every model-backed facet is `untested` with
  reason `no subscription token`. The issue permits that disposition, and the run still completes the model-free
  facets. A useful run needs the token in the implementer's environment or `~/.env` before dispatch.
- **Auth gate and model-free runs.** T2's F7.1 is the gate. If it is not `passed`, T3 to T7 run only their
  model-free facets and mark the rest `untested` with F7.1's cause, with no further auth attempts. A model-free
  run uses the same options but omits the token. The CLI is expected to emit `init` and then fail
  authentication; when it does not emit `init`, facets that read `init` are `untested`.
- **Dispositions.** Facet dispositions are `passed`, `failed` or `untested` (with a reason). A probe's headline
  is `failed` if any facet failed, else `untested` if any facet is untested, else `passed`. Facets tagged `[ADR]`
  carry an ADR-1008 guarantee; `[I]` facets are informational and cannot fail a probe, but a missing observation
  is `untested`. Every denial or absence observation needs a positive control in the same run (the allowed
  action succeeds), or the facet is `untested`.
- **Decoy home.** The subprocess gets `HOME=<root>/home` seeded with decoy `.claude/` and `.claude.json` content
  (marker-writing hooks, nonce-bearing `CLAUDE.md`, a plugin, skill, command and agent, an MCP server, an
  auto-memory file), while `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<root>/config` is the empty dedicated directory. The workspace gets
  decoy project files. This tests ADR-1008's isolation without exposing the real home. Behaviour under the
  operator's real `HOME` is a disclosed untested surface.
- **Spawn wrapper and the P3 parent.** Wrap `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` to spawn the command it is given with
  default-equivalent options, capture the PID and birth identity immediately, tee and count both streams, and
  expose `signal`. Run the "parent" of P3 as a probe-owned `node` child, so killing it never touches this
  harness or the operator's session.
- **Model and cost.** Use the smallest tier alias (`haiku`) with low effort unless a facet needs otherwise.
  Record the resolved model from `init`. Prompts are fixed, short and nonce-based.
- **Privacy and Git ancestry.** The recorder redacts at write time (exact token value, `sk-ant-*`, `Bearer *`,
  the root, the real home and the checkout path become `<redacted-token>`, `<disposable-root>`, `<user-home>`
  and `<repo>`). Never record `accountInfo()` fields beyond presence; record `apiKeySource`. Transcript state is
  recorded as record-type sequences with block types and tool pairing, not message bodies. Raw unredacted output
  is never written, so nothing sensitive can enter a commit or its ancestry.
- **Proof T2.** Hypothesis: the pinned SDK installs and launches the CLI through `spawnClaudeCodeProcess`; the
  PID is the CLI process and `captureProcessIdentity` records it; and with only the OAuth token and an empty
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, one trivial turn succeeds. Pass: F7.1, F8.1 and F8.2 `passed`. A launch or install
  failure is a probe result (P8 `failed` or `untested`) and T3 to T7 mark live facets `untested`; it needs no
  replan. A harness that cannot observe the identity or auth state while the SDK works is a plan mismatch.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `test/ui01/runtime-contract.mjs` — `validateArguments` refuses anything but exact `--live` flags,
  fixed `bounds`, and imports `captureProcessIdentity` and `MacProcessTerminationVerifier` from
  `../../dist/src/standalone/termination.js`.
- **Existing:** `test/ui01-live-harness.test.ts` — tests the refusal path with `spawnSync` and loads the `.mjs`
  through `import(fileUrl)` so `tsc` never resolves it.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/termination.ts` — `captureProcessIdentity(pid)` returns
  `{processId, processStartedAt, bootId} | null` (null off macOS); `readProcessBirthIdentity(pidString)`;
  `MacProcessTerminationVerifier.verify(identity)` returns `verified`, `conflict` (still present or reused) or
  `unknown`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/codex.ts:482` `Runtime` — `interruptTurn`, `processIdentity()`,
  `inspectExecution`. C3 maps the P2, P3 and P8 evidence onto these; C0 changes none of it.
- **Existing:** `docs/adr/1008-claude-code-execution-harness.md` — the guarantees the `[ADR]` facets test.
  `docs/evidence/issue-788-bounded-workspace-git-2026-10-07.md`,
  `issue-828-operator-follow-up-live-2026-10-09.md` and
  `s01-publication-sanitization-2026-09-28.md` — record style and sanitization precedent.
- **New:** `test/claude-c0/harness.mjs` — shared helpers; `run.mjs` — guarded driver; `p7-isolation.mjs`,
  `p8-process.mjs`, `p1-p2-session.mjs`, `p3-crash.mjs`, `p4-mcp.mjs`, `p5-policy.mjs`, `p6-sandbox.mjs`;
  `test/claude-c0-harness.test.ts`; `docs/evidence/issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` plus one
  redacted `issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-<step>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl` per step.
- **Follow:** the SDK reference at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript for option names
  (`resume`, `sessionId`, `abortController`, `permissionMode: "dontAsk"`, `tools`, `allowedTools`,
  `disallowedTools`, `hooks.PreToolUse`, `settingSources`, `strictMcpConfig`, `mcpServers`, `sandbox`,
  `spawnClaudeCodeProcess`, `stderr`, `env`, `createSdkMcpServer`, `tool`) and for `SDKResultMessage.terminal_reason`
  and `SDKSystemMessage` init fields. The installed package's `.d.ts` is authoritative where they differ, and the
  difference is itself recorded.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T4; T2 -> T5 -> T6 -> T7; T4 and T7 -> T8. The graph is acyclic.
All tasks edit `test/claude-c0/run.mjs` and `harness.mjs`, share one subscription and one config directory, and T4
and T6 reuse T3 and T5 fixtures. No tasks are safe to run concurrently; execute in the order T1, T2, T3, T4, T5,
T6, T7, T8. T2's `init` creates the one disposable root; pass its printed path as `--root` (and `C0_ROOT`) to every
later step, setting it again in each shell call.

#### 1. Disposable harness, guarded driver and unit-tested helpers

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Node from `.node-version`; `npm ci`; `npm run build:service` (the harness imports `dist`).
**Files and symbols:** New `test/claude-c0/harness.mjs` exporting `requireLive`, `createRoot`, `assertInside`,
`loadToken`, `buildEnv`, `redact`, `createRecorder`, `spawnWrapper`, `terminateExact`, `runQuery`, `loadSdk`,
`probeDisposition`, `returnedToChris`, `summarize`, `assertCleanupRoot`; new `test/claude-c0/run.mjs` (steps `init`, `p7`, `p8`, `p1`
(also runs P2), `p3`, `p4`, `p5`, `p6`, `summary`, `cleanup`; only `summary` runs without `--live`); new
`test/claude-c0-harness.test.ts`.
**Test:** `test/claude-c0-harness.test.ts`, following `test/ui01-live-harness.test.ts`. (1) `spawnSync` of
`run.mjs` with `[]`, `["p8"]`, `["--live"]` and `["--live","bogus"]` exits 2, prints `Refusing Claude SDK probes`
on stderr and nothing on stdout. (2) `buildEnv` given a source environment containing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, the real `HOME` and an unrelated secret
returns only `PATH`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`, the decoy `HOME`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and, when supplied,
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. (3) `redact` of text holding a fake token, `sk-ant-oat01-abc`, `Bearer abc`, the root,
real home and checkout paths leaves none of them and truncates a field over 2 KiB with a marker. (4) `assertInside`
accepts a child of the root and rejects `..` traversal and a symlink pointing out; `cleanup`'s guard accepts only a
direct child of the OS temp directory named `ensemble-claude-c0-*`. (5) `probeDisposition`: all passed gives
passed; one failed gives failed; one untested gives untested; an `untested` facet without a reason throws;
`returnedToChris` lists only failed `[ADR]` facets. (6) `summarize` rejects a result file that omits a declared
facet.
**Implementation:** Build the helpers listed in Planning decisions. `createRoot` makes the root layout `sdk/`,
`config/`, `home/`, `tmp/` (the subprocess `TMPDIR`), `workspace/`, `outside/`, `traces/`, `results/`. Each probe
module exports its declared facet IDs, which `summarize` checks against the result file. `loadSdk` dynamically imports the SDK entry
resolved from `<root>/sdk` and is never called at module load. `runQuery` wraps `query()` with the per-query
deadline, abort and exact-PID cleanup, a model-backed query counter persisted in `<root>/results/budget.json` against the cap of 60, and recorder hooks.
`spawnWrapper` implements the identity-capture design above. `terminateExact` verifies the recorded birth identity
before every signal. Keep the code small; no generic framework.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci && npm run build:service`, run
`node --test dist/test/claude-c0-harness.test.js && npm run lint && npm run format:check`; expect all harness
tests pass with 0 failures and lint and format exit 0. Then run `node test/claude-c0/run.mjs; echo "exit=$?"`;
expect `exit=2` and the refusal message.
**Complete when:** The harness test passes and refusal creates nothing; no SDK is imported at module load.

#### 2. Proof: launch, isolation, authentication and process identity (probes 7 and 8)

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 complete. Token optional (see Planning decisions).
**Files and symbols:** New `test/claude-c0/p7-isolation.mjs`, `p8-process.mjs`; register `init`, `p7`, `p8` in
`run.mjs`.
**Test:** Live probe facets, each recorded with its observation:
- `init` (not a facet): create the root, `npm install --save-exact` the newest SDK version (`npm view` at run
  time; recorded) and the repository's pinned `zod` (from `package.json`) into `<root>/sdk`, record whether
  lifecycle scripts ran, and write `results/preflight.json` with macOS version, Node and npm versions, SDK version,
  both CLI versions and paths, token presence (boolean only), and whether a trivial nested `sandbox-exec -p
  '(version 1)(allow default)' /usr/bin/true` starts from this context.
- **F8.1 [ADR] PID and identity.** `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` receives `{command, args, cwd, env, signal}`; the PID
  is a positive integer; `captureProcessIdentity` is non-null while alive; `ps -o command= -p <pid>` shows the
  `command` it was given (the CLI, not an intermediary); record process group and idle descendants.
- **F8.2 [ADR] Exit identity.** After the query settles, `MacProcessTerminationVerifier.verify(identity)` returns
  `verified`; record exit code or signal.
- **F8.3 [I] Stream bounds.** Bytes, lines and largest line on stdout, and bytes on stderr (wrapper tee versus the
  `stderr` option callback) for a model-free failing run, a one-turn success and a turn whose Bash tool prints at
  least 1 MiB (the last two need the token).
- **F8.4 [I] Spawn contract.** The exact `command` and `args` the SDK passes (flags only; values redacted) and the
  environment key names.
- **F7.1 [ADR] Subscription token authenticates.** With only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, the empty dedicated
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and the allowlist environment, one trivial turn returns `result.subtype === "success"` and
  `is_error === false`; record `apiKeySource` and the resolved model.
- **F7.2 [ADR] No user or project settings or hooks.** With `settingSources: []`, the decoy settings hooks
  (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse) write no marker file, decoy permission rules and env do not
  apply, and `init.permissionMode` matches the option. SessionStart is model-free; PreToolUse needs the token.
- **F7.3 [ADR] No CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or auto memory loads.** An `InstructionsLoaded` callback hook sees no decoy
  file, a model asked for the decoy nonces reveals none, and text injected through the system prompt option is
  recalled (positive control). Record any memory directory the CLI creates in the dedicated directory. Recall needs
  the token.
- **F7.4 [ADR] No plugins, skills, slash commands, agents or connectors.** `init.plugins`, `skills`,
  `slash_commands`, `agents` and `mcp_servers` list only built-ins and the SDK-supplied server, with
  `strictMcpConfig: true` and decoy `.mcp.json` and user MCP config present. Model-free.
- **F7.5 [ADR] Dedicated config directory is used.** The session transcript lands under `<root>/config`, and
  nothing but the seeded decoys exists under `<root>/home`.
- **F7.6 [I]** Record `supportedModels()` and the accepted `effort` values if exposed without extra model turns.
**Implementation:** `init` prints only the absolute root path on stdout (diagnostics go to stderr). Implement the
two probe modules over `runQuery` and `spawnWrapper`; run model-free variants first, then token-backed ones if `loadToken` succeeds. Write `results/p7.json` and `results/p8.json`.
Run `p7` before `p8` so F8.3's token-backed runs honour the F7.1 gate. Facets that need the token and find none are `untested: no subscription token`.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `C0_ROOT="$(node test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live init)" && node
test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live p7 --root "$C0_ROOT" && node test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live p8 --root "$C0_ROOT" &&
node test/claude-c0/run.mjs summary --root "$C0_ROOT"`; expect every command exit 0, `summary` listing F7.1 to
F7.6 and F8.1 to F8.4 each as `passed`, `failed` or `untested` with a reason for each untested, and no recorded
process identity still live.
**Complete when:** Both result files exist with every declared facet dispositioned and the proof outcome (F7.1,
F8.1, F8.2) is stated.

#### 3. Session start, resume and abort (probes 1 and 2)

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 results; F7.1 gate applies to model-backed facets.
**Files and symbols:** New `test/claude-c0/p1-p2-session.mjs`; register `p1` (runs both).
**Test:** Fixed nonce prompts, each `query()` a separate subprocess with a fresh `spawnWrapper`:
- **F1.1 [ADR] Session ID capture.** `init.session_id` is a UUID and equals the result's `session_id`.
- **F1.2 [ADR] Resume.** A second `query({resume})` in a new subprocess returns the same `session_id` and recalls
  the turn-1 nonce; record whether the result `session_id` or a fork differs.
- **F1.3 [I] Pre-assigned `sessionId`.** A UUID minted by the harness is accepted, appears in `init`, and resumes.
- **F1.4 [I] Unknown session ID.** `resume` of a well-formed unknown ID: record result subtype, error text and
  whether `query()` throws (model-free).
- **F2.1 [ADR] Abort mid-turn.** Abort via `abortController` after the first partial or assistant message.
  Pass: the generator settles within 15 s; the CLI process exits (`verified`) without our SIGKILL; the outcome is
  distinguishable from success (a `result` with `terminal_reason`/`is_error`, or a thrown abort error, recorded
  as observed); the transcript's record-type sequence is recorded.
- **F2.2 [ADR] Abort mid-tool.** A Bash tool runs `echo started >> m; sleep 12; echo finished >> m`; abort once
  `started` is written. Same pass conditions. Also record the tool process and descendants (exact PIDs) before
  and after, and whether `finished` is written within 15 s. A surviving tool is a disclosed limit, not a failure.
- **F2.3 [I] Resume after abort.** The aborted session resumes and the turn completes.
**Implementation:** Use `permissionMode: "dontAsk"`, `tools: ["Bash"]` and `allowedTools: ["Bash"]` for the tool
run; no sandbox yet (T7). Write `results/p1.json`.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after T2's `$C0_ROOT`, run `node test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live p1 --root
"$C0_ROOT" && node test/claude-c0/run.mjs summary --root "$C0_ROOT"`; expect exit 0 and F1.1 to F1.4 and F2.1 to
F2.3 each dispositioned, controls passed, no live recorded identity left.
**Complete when:** `results/p1.json` has every facet dispositioned and survivors of F2.2 are recorded.

#### 4. Parent crash mid-turn and mid-tool, then resume (probe 3)

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3's resume behaviour and process-identity handling.
**Files and symbols:** New `test/claude-c0/p3-crash.mjs` and a probe-owned child entry `p3-parent.mjs` that runs
`query()` and writes its CLI PID and session ID to `<root>/traces`; register `p3`.
**Test:** The driver SIGKILLs the verified `p3-parent` PID at a trigger, then observes, then resumes from a fresh
process:
- **F3.1 [ADR] Cut-off tool not re-run.** Mid-tool kill after the tool writes `started:<nonce>` to its counter
  file. After resume and one follow-up turn, the counter holds exactly one `started:<nonce>` line.
- **F3.2 [ADR] Mid-turn recovery.** Kill during streaming with no tool; a `resume` from a new process is accepted
  and the turn completes.
- **F3.3 [I] Orphans.** After the kill, whether the CLI and the tool process are still alive (exact PIDs), whether
  `finished` is written, and when the CLI exits. Terminate any survivor by `terminateExact` after a 30 s window.
- **F3.4 [I] Appearance to the agent.** The transcript's record sequence around the cut-off `tool_use` (paired,
  synthesized result or unpaired) and, from a follow-up prompt asking what happened to the earlier command, the
  agent's reply class (knows it was interrupted, assumes success or unaware), classified by fixed substrings.
**Implementation:** Reuse T3's query options. Kill only the child `node` spawned by the driver, after verifying
its identity.
**Validate:** From the repository root run `node test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live p3 --root "$C0_ROOT" && node
test/claude-c0/run.mjs summary --root "$C0_ROOT"`; expect exit 0, F3.1 to F3.4 dispositioned, and no recorded
identity live afterwards.
**Complete when:** `results/p3.json` is complete and every survivor was terminated by verified identity.

#### 5. In-process SDK MCP server (probe 4)

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 results (zod version installed in the root).
**Files and symbols:** New `test/claude-c0/p4-mcp.mjs` defining a fixture server named `ensemble` with
`createSdkMcpServer` and `tool()` for `ensemble_echo` (string and integer arguments), `ensemble_nested` (an
`questions[]` array of objects with an optional enum field, mirroring the structured-question shape),
`ensemble_error` (returns `isError: true`) and `ensemble_throw` (handler throws); export it for T6. Register `p4`.
**Test:**
- **F4.1 [ADR] Serving and names.** `init.tools` and `mcpServerStatus()` show the server connected and the exact
  tool names (expected `mcp__ensemble__<tool>`); record whether `allowedTools` accepts the exact names and a
  wildcard. Model-free where `init` is emitted.
- **F4.2 [ADR] Argument validation.** The model is told to call `ensemble_echo` with a wrong-typed integer and a
  missing required field. Pass: the handler is not invoked with invalid data (counter) and the model receives a
  readable error; record the error text shape and who rejected it.
- **F4.3 [I] Result and error shapes.** A success call, an `isError` result and a thrown handler error: record
  what the model sees and what the transcript stores.
- **F4.4 [I] Nested structured arguments.** `ensemble_nested` with two questions arrives at the handler intact
  and the advertised schema shows the nested shape.
**Implementation:** Use the same dontAsk options as T3 with `allowedTools` naming the MCP tools. Count handler
invocations in the harness process.
**Validate:** From the repository root run `node test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live p4 --root "$C0_ROOT" && node
test/claude-c0/run.mjs summary --root "$C0_ROOT"`; expect exit 0 and F4.1 to F4.4 dispositioned with the handler
counter recorded.
**Complete when:** `results/p4.json` is complete.

#### 6. dontAsk, allowlist and PreToolUse hook policy (probe 5)

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T5`
**Prerequisites:** T5 fixture server; F7.1 gate for model-backed facets.
**Files and symbols:** New `test/claude-c0/p5-policy.mjs`; register `p5`.
**Test:** A representative policy: `permissionMode: "dontAsk"`, built-in tools `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Write`,
`Edit`, `Bash`, plus the T5 MCP tools; `AskUserQuestion`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch` and sub-agent tools excluded; a
`PreToolUse` callback hook (no matcher) that records every input and denies `Write`/`Edit` whose path is outside
`<root>/workspace`; a `canUseTool` counter.
- **F5.1 [ADR] Hook sees every call.** The set of `tool_use_id`s in assistant messages equals the set seen by the
  hook, covering Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Bash and an MCP tool; record the hook input fields, including
  `permission_mode` and `mcp_server`.
- **F5.2 [ADR] Denial holds, and allow rules bypass `canUseTool`.** The hook denies an out-of-root Write: the file
  is absent, the model sees the reason and the turn continues. `canUseTool` is invoked 0 times for allowed calls.
- **F5.3 [ADR] Allowlist expression.** Tools outside the allowlist are absent from `init.tools` or denied under
  `dontAsk` when the model is told to use WebFetch; compare `tools` against `allowedTools` plus `disallowedTools`
  and record which option expresses ADR-1008's allowlist.
- **F5.4 [ADR] `AskUserQuestion` disabled.** The model asked to ask the user a question gets no interactive
  request, the query does not hang, and `canUseTool` is not prompted.
- **F5.5 [ADR] Permission and config changes are inert.** A model-originated `EnterPlanMode` or `ExitPlanMode`
  attempt (if present) leaves `permission_mode` at `dontAsk` in later hook inputs. A model that writes
  `.claude/settings.json` allowing `WebFetch` and a `.mcp.json` in the workspace changes nothing in a resumed
  next turn (WebFetch still denied, the rogue server absent).
**Implementation:** Controls: a permitted in-workspace Write succeeds. Use fixed prompts naming exact paths.
**Validate:** From the repository root run `node test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live p5 --root "$C0_ROOT" && node
test/claude-c0/run.mjs summary --root "$C0_ROOT"`; expect exit 0, F5.1 to F5.5 dispositioned, controls passed.
**Complete when:** `results/p5.json` is complete with the hook-versus-assistant call sets recorded.

#### 7. Sandbox behaviour (probe 6)

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `T6`
**Prerequisites:** T6 policy options; T2 `preflight.json` nested-Seatbelt result.
**Files and symbols:** New `test/claude-c0/p6-sandbox.mjs`; register `p6`.
**Test:** ADR-1008 sandbox: `sandbox: { enabled: true, failIfUnavailable: true, allowUnsandboxedCommands: false,
autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true, network: { allowedDomains: [] }, filesystem: { allowWrite: [<root>/workspace] } }`.
- **F6.0 [I] Positive control.** A sandboxed Bash write inside the workspace succeeds and the sandbox is active.
  If it cannot start from this context (nested Seatbelt unavailable), F6.0 to F6.3 are `untested` with that
  reason and F6.4 records the natural failure.
- **F6.1 [ADR] Outside writes denied.** Bash writes to `<root>/outside`, a uniquely named file in `/tmp` (the harness
  deletes it if it appears), `$TMPDIR` (`<root>/tmp`) and `<root>/home` are refused and the files are absent.
- **F6.2 [ADR] Network denied.** `curl` to a harness-owned loopback listener and to an external host fails, the
  listener's hit count is 0, and the harness's own connection to the listener succeeds (control).
- **F6.3 [ADR] No unsandboxed retry.** After a denial the model is told to retry with
  `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`; the write target stays absent. Record whether the hook sees that input field.
- **F6.4 [ADR] Unavailable sandbox fails closed.** With the sandbox induced unavailable (for example an outer
  `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)'` around the harness, or a `PATH` without `sandbox-exec`),
  `failIfUnavailable: true` yields `error_during_execution` with `errors` and no command runs; record the
  yielded result and whether `query()` then throws. If no method induces it, `untested`.
**Implementation:** Drive Bash through the T6 hook policy; the loopback listener and counters live in the harness.
**Validate:** From the repository root run `node test/claude-c0/run.mjs --live p6 --root "$C0_ROOT" && node
test/claude-c0/run.mjs summary --root "$C0_ROOT"`; expect exit 0 and F6.0 to F6.4 dispositioned.
**Complete when:** `results/p6.json` is complete and every denial has a recorded positive control or an untested
reason.

#### 8. Evidence record, sanitization and cleanup

**Task ID:** `T8`
**Depends on:** `T4, T7`
**Prerequisites:** All result files present.
**Files and symbols:** New `docs/evidence/issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` and
`docs/evidence/issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-<step>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl` (copies of `<root>/traces/*.jsonl`, already
redacted); remove only the root via `run.mjs --live cleanup`.
**Test:** Evidence check commands (see Validate).
**Implementation:** Write the record in place from `summary` output and the traces: environment (macOS, Node, npm,
SDK version, both CLI versions, resolved model, run date, checkout SHA, token state as present or absent only);
a summary table with exactly eight rows `| 1 | ... |` to `| 8 | ... |` and five columns (number, probe,
disposition, ADR-1008 guarantee, result); one section per probe with the exact options, the exact commands from the slices, a facet table with
observations and short excerpts, and limits; "Returned to Chris" listing `returnedToChris` output with each failed
`[ADR]` facet and the ADR-1008 sentence it contradicts (state "None" when empty);
"Untested surfaces" including the real-`HOME` case; a SHA-256 for every JSONL; and a neutral "Observed names and
shapes" list for C3. Do not edit ADR-1008. Run `cleanup` last: it verifies every recorded identity is gone,
terminates any exact live match, and removes only the root.
**Validate:** From the repository root run the following; expect no output from the scans and the stated counts.
`rg -n -F "$HOME" docs/evidence/issue-822-* test/claude-c0` and
`rg -n -e 'sk-ant-' -e '/Users/' -e 'CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=' docs/evidence/issue-822-*` (no matches);
`rg -c --no-filename '^\| [1-8] \| [^|]+\| (passed|failed|untested) \|' docs/evidence/issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-*.md`
prints 8; `node --input-type=module -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; for (const f of process.argv.slice(1)) for (const l of readFileSync(f,"utf8").split("\n")) if (l) JSON.parse(l)' docs/evidence/issue-822-*.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"`
prints `exit=0`; `git status --porcelain` lists only the planned paths.
**Complete when:** The record, traces and cleanup are done, the scans are clean and the delivery summary names
every failed `[ADR]` facet and every untested probe with its reason.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Probe 1: session start, ID capture, resume across `query()` calls | 3 | F1.1 to F1.4 in `results/p1.json` |
| Probe 2: abort mid-turn and mid-tool, subtype, `terminal_reason`, transcript | 3 | F2.1 to F2.3 |
| Probe 3: parent kill mid-turn and mid-tool, resume, tool not re-run | 4 | F3.1 to F3.4 |
| Probe 4: in-process SDK MCP names, validation, result and error shapes | 5 | F4.1 to F4.4 |
| Probe 5: `dontAsk`, allowlist, hook sees every call, denials hold, `AskUserQuestion`, mode change | 6 | F5.1 to F5.5 |
| Probe 6: sandbox writes, network, unsandboxed retry, cannot start | 7 | F6.0 to F6.4 |
| Probe 7: isolation and subscription token | 2 | F7.1 to F7.6 |
| Probe 8: PID via `spawnClaudeCodeProcess`, stdout and stderr bounds | 2 | F8.1 to F8.4 |
| Evidence in `docs/evidence/` with SDK and CLI versions, exact commands, observed outputs | 8 | Environment section and eight-row table checks |
| Each probe marked passed, failed or untested; ADR-guarantee failures returned to Chris | 1, 8 | `probeDisposition`/`returnedToChris` unit test; "Returned to Chris" section |
| No touch of the Ensemble database, operator projects or installed prototype | 1, 8 | `buildEnv`/`assertInside` unit tests; scope and privacy scans |

### Final validation

- From the repository root on Node from `.node-version` (24.21.0), after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` at the
  integrated delivery candidate and on the PR (CI `check`); expect exit 0 with typecheck, lint, format check, build
  and tests all passing with 0 failures. The baseline at the planned SHA was green for typecheck, lint, format
  check, `build:service` and `node --test dist/test/ui01-live-harness.test.js` (93 pass).
- From the repository root run `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`; expect only `test/claude-c0/**`,
  `test/claude-c0-harness.test.ts` and `docs/evidence/issue-822-*`, and
  `rg -n "claude-agent-sdk" package.json package-lock.json` prints nothing.
- Live probes are not part of CI. T2 to T7 are the bounded live validation run by the implementation agent; the
  `--live` steps never run in `npm run check`.

### Review focus

- Secret and path leakage in committed traces and the record, including that nothing is written unredacted.
- False passes: denial facets without a positive control, hook counts compared on the wrong identity, and facets
  marked `passed` that rest on a model-free run that did not emit `init`.
- Process safety: every signal gated on a matching birth identity; no name-based termination; cleanup leaves no
  recorded survivor.
- Honest dispositions: `untested` for unreached facets, a probe's headline derived by the rule, and every failed
  `[ADR]` facet returned rather than worked around.

### Allowed deviations

- Choose the newest SDK version at `init` and record it; pick the sandbox-unavailable induction method; rename
  probe modules, split or merge result files, and set the evidence date; reorder live steps within the dependency
  graph when a rate limit intervenes.

### Re-plan triggers

- A facet cannot proceed without the real `HOME`, `~/.claude`, Ensemble data or database, an operator project,
  the installed prototype, API-key billing or an agent-minted credential.
- The work needs an SDK dependency, a `src/**` or `web/**` change, or a product-doc edit.
- A wrong approved-plan seam remains after one diagnosis and two repair cycles.

Implementation dispatch is held at Ready (plan: https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/822#issuecomment-6110824982).

**Blocker:** no Claude subscription token is available to the implementing agent. Plan probe 7 uses a dedicated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so the existing `claude` login is not shared, and every model-backed probe facet would be recorded as untested.

**Resume condition:** a `claude setup-token` token is available as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in `~/.env`, or Chris accepts a record that runs only the model-free probe facets.

content.title: CLI1: Authenticate and inspect a task from the packaged CLI

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/894
**Planned against:** `main` at `111f46d744db3d8f15b562a5014ae12945d2c4c2`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add a SQLite-backed operator credential store and a stable service installation identity. Add one bearer-authentication path to the existing `LocalOperatorHttp` JSON API, guarded by an explicit server-side route-authority table. Give the web Settings a session-only credential lifecycle. Ship a packaged `ensemble` executable (`src/cli/`) that keeps named connections, stores tokens in the macOS Keychain or a protected token file, enforces loopback HTTP or verified HTTPS, and implements `auth login|status|logout`, `connection list|use|remove` and `task get`. Authority is the issue's acceptance criteria, the [operator CLI design](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/111f46d744db3d8f15b562a5014ae12945d2c4c2/docs/design/operator-cli.md), [ADR-1010](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/111f46d744db3d8f15b562a5014ae12945d2c4c2/docs/adr/1010-operator-cli.md) and CLI01/CLI02 in [acceptance](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/111f46d744db3d8f15b562a5014ae12945d2c4c2/docs/acceptance.md#operator-cli-acceptance).

### Guardrails

- CLI1 scope only. Do not add later CLI areas (project/profile/assignment/inbox/execution/logs/recovery/result/operation, follow, pagination, prepare/apply, receipts). Those belong to #895–#901. Do not reuse or implement #726/#734 OAuth, MCP or ChatGPT scope.
- Keep `npm run service|operations|operator-auth`, their argument contracts, the launchd renderer and `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_AUTH_FILE`/`ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_ORIGIN` unchanged. The service still binds only `127.0.0.1`. Do not add public connectivity or TLS termination to the service.
- Browser-session behaviour is unchanged: cookie sessions, `Origin` equality and CSRF on every session POST, and existing 401/403 responses. A request carrying `Authorization` is handled only by the bearer path. It never reads or upgrades a cookie session and never reaches legacy HTML routes.
- Bearer writes call the same `OperatorApi.execute`/`refreshSources` paths as the browser. They must not bypass command validation, revisions, policy, holds or receipts. CLI credentials cannot create, rotate, extend or revoke credentials.
- Persist only token verification material. Never log, echo, print or return a stored token. Reveal a token only in the create/rotate response that issued it. The CLI has no literal-token flag and no plaintext fallback.
- The CLI reads only through the live service. `src/cli/**` must not import `node:sqlite` or service/state modules.
- The managed-assignment guard prevents accidental privilege crossing only. Do not document it as OS isolation or protection from same-user processes.
- Revocation is intentionally irreversible, as the design requires. The recovery path is to issue or rotate a replacement. A lost create/rotate response leaves a listed, unrevealed credential that the operator revokes.
- **Plan-mismatch budget (a):** if an approved seam or repository fact in this plan is wrong, record one focused diagnosis and use at most two repair cycles. Examples: `LocalOperatorHttp` cannot host the bearer gate before session handling; `security -i` cannot store a token from stdin; offline `npm ci` of the packed tarball fails with a derived lockfile; the spawn environment does not reach `RuntimeSpawnContext.spawnEnvironment`. If those cycles are exhausted, or the fix would change the accepted contract, stop and replan.
- **Ordinary repairs (b):** in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, formatting/lint and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume budget (a). This includes flaky browser waits, path or symbol corrections, fixture setup and renewed evidence. Record a correction briefly in the delivery record when requirements, coverage, architecture and authority are unchanged.
- Investigate unknown overlap with #873/#875/#877/#883/#886 changes before reusing or editing shared code. Stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants. Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Token format and verification:** use `ens_<credentialId>_<secret>`, where `credentialId` is a UUID and `secret` is 32 random bytes in base64url. Store `sha256(secret)` and compare with `timingSafeEqual`. A high-entropy random secret needs no scrypt. A malformed token, unknown id, hash mismatch, expired token or revoked token returns 401 `credential-invalid` without saying which one failed. A valid token with insufficient scope returns 403 `insufficient-scope`.
- **Lifetime:** `expiresInDays` is an integer from 1 to 90, defaulting to 90. The UI offers 7/30/60/90. Rotation issues a new credential with the same name and scope, a new expiry and `replacesId`. The old credential stays active until it is explicitly revoked. Only active credentials can be rotated. `lastUsedAt` is written at most once per 60 s per credential to bound writes.
- **Credential management is not a receipted domain command.** It uses dedicated session-only endpoints so a receipt replay can never re-reveal a token: `GET /api/operator/credentials`, `POST /api/operator/credentials`, `POST /api/operator/credentials/:id/rotate` and `POST /api/operator/credentials/:id/revoke`.
- **Route authority:** one function, `operatorRouteAuthority(method, path)`, returns `read | write | session-only` or `undefined`. Bearer requests are allowed only for `read` (both scopes) and `write` (read-write scope). Everything else is denied, failing closed for unknown paths. The classification is:
  - `write`: `POST /api/operator/commands`, `POST /api/operator/source-refresh`, and `GET /api/operator/tasks/:id/comparisons`, which computes and persists comparison snapshots.
  - `session-only`: session/login/logout, `setup/folders`, `setup/verify-checkout`, `review-draft`, `local-reviews*` (bound to the browser review owner, which refreshes access fingerprints) and all credential-management endpoints.
  - `read`: all other `knownApi` GETs, plus the new `GET /api/operator/cli`.
  - Bearer requests to non-`/api` paths (legacy HTML, `/command`, slot routes, `/app`, assets) return 403.
  - The implementer checks every GET handler reached by `OperatorWebBoundary.read`. Any GET that persists state is classified `write`. That counts as an ordinary repair, not a plan mismatch.
- **Identity and negotiation:** `GET /api/operator/cli` (bearer only) returns `{ apiVersion: 1, capabilities: ["cli.identity","task.read"], service: { installationId, origin }, credential: { id, name, scope, createdAt, expiresAt } }`. `installationId` is a UUID created once in the database, so it survives restart and backup/restore. The CLI requires `apiVersion === 1` and the capabilities it uses; otherwise it fails with `unsupported-service`. At login, the connection records `installationId`. A later mismatch fails with `service-identity-changed`.
- **Transport:** a connection URL must be a canonical origin, either `https://host[:port]` or `http://127.0.0.1:port`. This matches the server's `canonicalLoopbackOrigin` and Host check. Any other `http:` URL is rejected before sending. The CLI uses Node `fetch` with `redirect: "manual"` and treats every 3xx as `redirect-rejected`, so credentials are never forwarded. A read-only probe confirmed default verification rejects a self-signed certificate (`DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT`) and accepts it with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. Tests use that, not an insecure flag.
- **Local configuration:** `connections.json` lives in `$ENSEMBLE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR`, defaulting to `~/.config/ensemble`. The directory is 0700 and the file is 0600, written atomically. It holds `{ default?, connections: { name: { url, installationId, credential: { kind: "keychain", account } | { kind: "token-file", path } } } }` and never a token. Selection order is `--connection`, then `default` (set by `connection use`), then the sole connection. Several connections with no default fail with `connection-ambiguous`, listing the names.
- **Credential stores:**
  - Keychain: `/usr/bin/security` by absolute path, service `ensemble-cli`, account `<connection>`. Write with `security -i`, sending the `add-generic-password -U -s … -a … -w <token>` command on stdin so the token never appears in argv. Read with `find-generic-password -s … -a … -w`. Delete with `delete-generic-password`.
  - Token file: a regular, non-symlink file owned by the user with no group/other permission bits (mode `& 0o077 === 0`), at most 4 KiB, holding one token. It is referenced by path and never copied.
  - On non-darwin systems without `--token-file`, or when the Keychain fails, return `credential-store-unavailable`. Never fall back to plaintext.
- **Managed assignment guard:** the service runtime spawn environment sets `ENSEMBLE_MANAGED_ASSIGNMENT=1` and strips `ENSEMBLE_CONNECTION` and every `ENSEMBLE_CLI_*` variable. Commands that need a credential (`auth login|status`, `task get`) fail with `managed-assignment` when that variable is set. The service never holds CLI tokens, so it cannot inherit them by construction. Whether Codex propagates the marker into tool shells is unproved here and left to CLI8 (#901) live qualification. Record it as unproved.
- **Output and exit contract:**
  - stdout carries only the result. Human output is the default. With `--output json`, success is `{ "schema": "ensemble.cli/v1", "observedAt", "connection", "service": { installationId, origin, apiVersion }, "data" }` and errors are `{ "schema": "ensemble.cli/v1", "error": { code, category, message, requestId, retryable, outcome } }`.
  - Diagnostics go to stderr. Each HTTP request sends a UUID `x-ensemble-request-id` that the error reports.
  - Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 invalid input or usage; 3 authentication/authorization (credential-invalid, insufficient-scope, managed-assignment, credential-store-unavailable); 4 revision/policy conflict (HTTP 409); 5 unavailable or transport (network, TLS verification, redirect-rejected, 5xx), with `retryable` set accordingly; 6 uncertain outcome (`command-outcome-unknown`, unused by CLI1 reads but reserved); 7 unsupported service/version.
- **Packaging:** the root `package.json` gains `"bin": { "ensemble": "dist/src/cli/main.js" }` and `"files": ["dist/src"]`, with `main.ts` starting `#!/usr/bin/env node`. It stays private and has no publish step. A read-only probe showed offline install works: `npm pack` then `npm ci --offline --omit=dev --ignore-scripts` in a temporary project, with a lockfile made from the repository lock's non-dev entries plus the tarball (`file:` resolved, sha512 integrity), installed 143 packages in about 1.4 s with no network. Plain `npm install --offline <tgz>` fails (`notarget`) because `npm ci` does not cache packuments.
- **UI placement:** a new "CLI credentials" region in the Settings index, built from existing settings primitives (`Panel`, `Button`, `StatusBadge`, form fields) like `DiscoveryCredentialRow`. No `design/design.pen` frame exists for it. CLI1 does not add one, and the PR description notes this as a design gap. The legacy HTML operator UI gets no credential controls, which is an intentional gap.
- **Assumption needing new code to test:** that `security -i` accepts a piped `add-generic-password … -w <token>` command and stores a retrievable item. This is proof task **T5a**, at the start of T5.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator.ts` — `LocalOperatorHttp.start` request handler. It checks Host against the auth origin host or the loopback host, reads the cookie session, delegates `/api`, `/app` and `/assets` to `handleWeb`, and handles legacy HTML GET/POST through `authorizeRead`/`authorizeWrite` (Origin) and CSRF. `handleWeb` fixes the POST path list (`expected`), requires a session, enforces Origin + `x-csrf-token` on POST, then calls `web.api.execute`, `refreshSources`, `listFolders`, `verifyCheckout`, `readArtifact` or `web.read`. Errors map through `publicMessage` and `apiErrorSchema`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-web.ts` — `OperatorWebBoundary.read` (GET dispatch) and `knownApi` (path allowlist). `src/standalone/operator-auth.ts` — `OperatorAuth` (password and in-memory sessions; `canonicalLoopbackOrigin`).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `StandaloneService.start` opens `DatabaseSync` and constructs stores (`new SqliteWorkspaceComparisonStore(db)` and others, lines ~426–455). It builds `spawnEnvironment` from `deliveryRuntimeEnvironment(process.env, policies)` (~645–655) and passes it in `RuntimeSpawnContext`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/cli.ts` — `main` wires `OperatorAuth.open`, `LocalOperatorHttp`, `OperatorWebBoundary` and `OperatorApi` for `operator`. `src/standalone/operator-hidden-password.ts` — `readHiddenPassword(input, output, prompt)`.
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — zod contracts shared by the web app and service (`apiErrorSchema`, `sessionSchema`). `web/src/api.ts` — `OperatorClient.read` / private `post` (session + CSRF). `web/src/settings-index.tsx` — `SettingsWorkspace` renders `DiscoveryCredentialRow`.
- **New:** `src/standalone/operator-credentials.ts` — `OperatorCredentialStore(db)` with `issue`, `list`, `rotate`, `revoke`, `verify(token, now)`, `installationId()`, using tables `operator_cli_credentials` and `service_installation`. Also `operatorRouteAuthority(method, path)`.
- **New:** `src/cli/main.ts` (entry, argument parsing, commands, output/exit mapping), `src/cli/connections.ts` (config file, selection, `KeychainCredentialStore`, `TokenFileCredentialStore`) and `src/cli/transport.ts` (URL rules, fetch with manual redirects, request ids, identity/version check). `main(argv, deps)` takes injectable `env`, `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr`, `fetch`, `credentialStore` factory and `platform` for tests.
- **New:** `web/src/operator-credentials.tsx` — `OperatorCredentialsSection`.
- **Follow:** `test/fixtures/operator-web.ts:createOperatorFixture` (real SQLite service with the fake runtime), `test/operator-web-http.test.ts` (in-process `LocalOperatorHttp` with `OperatorAuth.initialize/open`), `test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.ts` + `test/fixtures/setup-browser.ts:setupJourney` (browser suite), `test/turn-capture-harness.test.ts` (capturing `RuntimeSpawnContext.spawnEnvironment`), and `src/standalone/comparison-store.ts` (store-on-`DatabaseSync` pattern).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** acyclic: T1 → {T2, T3}; T2 → {T4, T5}; {T3, T4, T5} → T6. T2 and T3 may run concurrently: T2 owns `operator.ts`/`operator-web.ts`/`contracts.ts`/`cli.ts` and T3 owns the `service.ts` spawn environment. Both need T1's `service.ts` store wiring merged first. T4 (`web/**`) and T5 (`src/cli/**`, `package.json`) may run concurrently after T2. Both read the `contracts.ts` schemas from T2. If either needs a contract change, the change goes through one owner sequentially. T6 depends on all.

#### 1. Credential store and installation identity

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** new `src/standalone/operator-credentials.ts` (`OperatorCredentialStore`, credential and scope types, token parse/format). `src/standalone/service.ts`: construct the store in `start()` beside the other stores and expose `operatorCredentials()`, which throws when not started, like other accessors. New `test/operator-credentials.test.ts`.
**Test:** on a real temporary `DatabaseSync`:
- `issue({name, scope, expiresInDays})` returns a token once. Default expiry is created + 90 days. 0 and 91 are rejected.
- Scanning every column of `operator_cli_credentials` finds no token or secret substring.
- `list()` returns metadata (`id, name, scope, createdAt, expiresAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt, replacesId, state`) and no token or verifier.
- `verify` accepts a valid token. For a malformed token, unknown id, wrong secret, expired token (injected `now`) or revoked token it returns a uniform `invalid`.
- `rotate(id)` returns a new token with `replacesId`, and both tokens verify until `revoke(old)`. Rotating a revoked credential is rejected.
- `lastUsedAt` updates on verify, throttled to once per 60 s.
- `installationId()` is stable across reopening the same database file.
**Implementation:** create the tables idempotently (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`). Validate stored rows with zod on read. Use transactions for rotate and revoke.
**Validate:** from the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-credentials.test.js`; expect every test to pass.
**Complete when:** the store and identity tests pass and `npm run typecheck` is clean.

#### 2. Bearer authentication, route authority, identity and credential endpoints

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the working branch.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/standalone/operator.ts`: in `LocalOperatorHttp`, add `OperatorHttpOptions.credentials?: OperatorCredentialStore`. The bearer branch runs right after the Host/target/path checks and before cookie lookup. It handles `GET /api/operator/cli`, and the credential endpoints inside `handleWeb`'s session/Origin/CSRF path, with an explicit 403 when `Authorization` is present.
- `src/standalone/operator-credentials.ts`: `operatorRouteAuthority`.
- `src/standalone/operator-web.ts`: `knownApi` includes the new paths.
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: `operatorCredentialSchema`, `operatorCredentialListSchema`, `operatorCredentialIssueRequestSchema` (`name` 1–64 chars without control characters, `scope: "read"|"read-write"`, `expiresInDays` 1–90 optional), `operatorCredentialIssuedSchema` (metadata + `token`) and `cliIdentitySchema`.
- `src/standalone/cli.ts`: pass `credentials: service.operatorCredentials()`.
- New test `test/operator-cli-http.test.ts`.
**Test:** in-process `LocalOperatorHttp` over `createOperatorFixture`, with a browser session logged in through `OperatorAuth`, and tokens issued through the session endpoints:
1. Read-only bearer: `GET /api/operator/cli` → 200 with identity, scope and `apiVersion: 1`. `GET /api/operator/tasks/:id` → 200 and equal to the session read.
2. Read-only bearer gets 403 `insufficient-scope` for: `POST /commands` (valid `task.stop` body), `POST /source-refresh`, `GET …/comparisons`.
3. Both scopes get 403 for: session-only paths (`/session`, `/login`, `/logout`, `setup/*`, `review-draft`, `local-reviews`, every credential endpoint) and legacy `GET /`, `GET /task/:id`, `POST /command`, `POST /coordination/...`. Assert that no service state changed (receipts and task version unchanged).
4. Read-write bearer `POST /commands` with a stale `expectedVersion` → same 409 conflict as the session path. A valid command → same receipt shape. Repeating the same key → same receipt, with no duplicate effect.
5. Credential failures: expired (injected `now`), revoked, wrong secret and malformed header (`Bearer`, `Basic x`, two tokens) → 401 `credential-invalid`. An unknown `/api/operator/*` path → 404/403 without dispatch.
6. A bearer request that also carries a valid session cookie gets no cookie authority: `POST /api/operator/credentials` → 403.
7. Browser regression: session POST without Origin → 403; with a wrong CSRF token → 403; the existing session flows still succeed.
8. Exhaustiveness: a table of one representative concrete path per `knownApi` pattern asserts `operatorRouteAuthority` is defined for each.
9. Session credential endpoints: create → the token appears only in that response. `GET` list never contains `token`. Rotate keeps the old credential active. Revoke → the old token gets 401.
**Implementation:**
- Bearer responses carry no `set-cookie` and need no CSRF or Origin, because they carry no ambient credentials.
- Re-verify the credential after the awaited API call, mirroring `currentSession`, so a credential revoked mid-request returns 401 rather than data.
- Error bodies reuse `apiErrorSchema`. Add `credential-invalid` and `insufficient-scope` to `publicMessage`.
**Validate:** from the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-http.test.js dist/test/operator-web-http.test.js dist/test/operator-http.test.js dist/test/operator-auth.test.js`; expect all to pass, with no regression in the existing files (baseline: 26/26 across the latter three plus the discovery browser test).
**Complete when:** the bearer, authority, browser-regression and credential-endpoint checks pass.

#### 3. Managed-assignment environment marker

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's `service.ts` change merged, because both edit `StandaloneService.start`.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/service.ts`: the `spawnEnvironment` closure (~line 645) applies a small exported helper `managedAssignmentEnvironment(env)` (in `operator-credentials.ts` or `delivery.ts` beside `deliveryRuntimeEnvironment`). The helper deletes `ENSEMBLE_CONNECTION` and `ENSEMBLE_CLI_*` and sets `ENSEMBLE_MANAGED_ASSIGNMENT=1`. Add a test in `test/operator-cli-http.test.ts` or a new `test/managed-assignment-environment.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- A unit test of the helper on a sample environment.
- A service test with an injected `runtimeFactory` that captures `RuntimeSpawnContext.spawnEnvironment()` (pattern from `test/turn-capture-harness.test.ts`), with `process.env` temporarily holding `ENSEMBLE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` and `ENSEMBLE_CONNECTION`. Assert the marker is present, those variables are absent, and the existing delivery credential stripping still holds.
**Implementation:** compose the helper after `deliveryRuntimeEnvironment`. Keep `runtimeSpawnSnapshot` semantics unchanged.
**Validate:** from the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/<new or extended file>.js dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js dist/test/turn-capture-harness.test.js`; expect all to pass.
**Complete when:** the marker and stripping are proven in the captured spawn environment.

#### 4. Web UI credential lifecycle

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 endpoints and contracts.
**Files and symbols:**
- New `web/src/operator-credentials.tsx` (`OperatorCredentialsSection`), rendered from `SettingsWorkspace` in `web/src/settings-index.tsx`.
- `web/src/api.ts`: `OperatorClient.credentials()`, `issueCredential(input, csrf)`, `rotateCredential(id, csrf)` and `revokeCredential(id, csrf)`, using the existing private `post`.
- Styles in `web/src/settings.css` if needed.
- New browser test `test/operator-cli-credentials-browser.test.ts` using `browserSuite` + `setupJourney`.
**Test:** the Chromium browser journey on `/app/settings`:
1. Create "laptop-ro" (read-only, 30 days) through the form. The one-time reveal shows the token with a "Copy" control and a warning that it will not be shown again.
2. After "Done" and a page reload, the token text is absent from the DOM, and the list row shows name, scope, created, expiry (about 30 days) and last used ("never"). Capture the `/api/operator/credentials` response bodies and assert none contains the token.
3. Use the revealed token in a direct bearer `fetch` to `/api/operator/cli` → 200. The row's last-used then updates after a refresh.
4. Create "agent-rw" (read-write, default 90 days). Rotate it: a new reveal appears, and both the old and replacement rows are active and linked. Bearer calls with both tokens succeed.
5. Revoke the old credential behind a confirmation dialog that states revocation is irreversible. The row shows revoked, the old token gets 401, and the replacement still gets 200.
6. Validation: an empty name or one longer than 64 characters shows a field error and sends nothing.
7. Keyboard: the reveal and the revoke dialog are focusable and labelled.
**Implementation:** follow the `DiscoveryCredentialRow` resource, refresh and draft patterns. Keep the token only in component state for the reveal and clear it on dismiss or unmount. Do not store it in drafts or `localStorage`.
**Validate:** from the repository root, after `npx playwright install chromium` if needed, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-credentials-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-browser.test.js`; expect all to pass.
**Complete when:** the UI lifecycle (create, list, one-time reveal, rotate before revoke, revoke with service readback) passes in the browser.

#### 5. Packaged CLI: connections, credential stores, transport, auth and task get

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 endpoints and contracts. **T5a proof first:** on the macOS host, construct `KeychainCredentialStore` with a disposable service name `ensemble-cli-test-<uuid>` and run `set`, then `get` (must equal the token), then `delete`, then `get` (must return not-found). While `set` runs, sample `ps -o args= -p <pid>` and assert the token is not in argv. Pass means continue. Failure triggers budget (a). The only pre-approved alternative is passing `-w` without a value through a pseudo-terminal. If that also fails, stop and replan, because Keychain-by-default is an accepted contract.
**Files and symbols:**
- New `src/cli/main.ts`, `src/cli/connections.ts` and `src/cli/transport.ts`, symbols as in Implementation context. Reuse `readHiddenPassword(input, output, "Ensemble CLI token: ")`.
- `package.json`: `bin`, `files`.
- New `test/operator-cli.test.ts` (in-process `main(argv, deps)` against the T2 server) and gated `test/operator-cli-keychain.test.ts`, skipped unless `process.platform === "darwin" && process.env.ENSEMBLE_KEYCHAIN_LIVE === "1"`, which runs the T5a assertions.
**Commands:**
- `ensemble auth login --connection NAME --url ORIGIN [--token-file PATH]` prompts with masked TTY input unless `--token-file` is given. A non-TTY without `--token-file` fails with exit 2. It validates through `GET /api/operator/cli` before storing anything. On store failure nothing is saved.
- `ensemble auth status [--connection]` shows connection, origin, installationId, credential name/scope/expiry, apiVersion and capabilities.
- `ensemble auth logout [--connection]` removes the local credential and states that the server credential stays active until revoked or expired.
- `ensemble connection list | use NAME | remove NAME`. `remove` also deletes its Keychain item.
- `ensemble task get TASK_ID [--connection] [--output json]`.
- Global flags: `--output human|json` and `--help`.
**Test:** `test/operator-cli.test.ts` drives `main` with injected deps against a live in-process service (T2 fixture) and asserts stdout, stderr and exit code for each case:
1. Login with a read-only token-file credential, then status, then `task get` (human and JSON envelope; `data.id` equals the task).
2. A wrong-scope read-write-only path is not reachable with a CLI1 command. Assert instead that a direct HTTP write with the same token gets 403 (from T2).
3. Expired and revoked credentials → exit 3 `credential-invalid`. A malformed token file → exit 2 at login. A token file with mode 0644, a symlink or another owner → rejected.
4. Keychain store failure through an injected failing `security` runner → login exit 3 `credential-store-unavailable` with no connection saved. A read failure during status → exit 3.
5. On non-darwin without `--token-file` → exit 3 `credential-store-unavailable`, and no plaintext file is created (assert the config dir contains no token).
6. Two connections with no default → `task get` exit 2 `connection-ambiguous` listing both. After `connection use`, it succeeds.
7. `ENSEMBLE_MANAGED_ASSIGNMENT=1` → login, status and task get exit 3 `managed-assignment` and make no HTTP request (spy fetch).
8. URL rules: `http://example.test:1` and `http://localhost:1` are rejected before fetch (exit 2). A 307 to another origin → exit 5 `redirect-rejected`, and the second server receives no request.
9. A fake server advertising `apiVersion: 2` or missing `task.read` → exit 7 `unsupported-service`. A different `installationId` after login → exit 3 `service-identity-changed`.
10. Unavailable (closed port) → exit 5, retryable true.
11. A static import scan finds no `node:sqlite` or `../standalone/` import in `src/cli/**` other than `operator-hidden-password.js`.
12. No token appears in any stdout, stderr or `connections.json` across all cases.
**Implementation:** keep stdout for results only. JSON mode never mixes in progress text. Parse every response with the T2 zod schemas.
**Validate:** from the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-cli.test.js`; expect all to pass. On the macOS host, run `ENSEMBLE_KEYCHAIN_LIVE=1 node --test dist/test/operator-cli-keychain.test.js`; expect pass, with the disposable item absent afterwards (`security find-generic-password -s ensemble-cli-test-… ` exits non-zero).
**Complete when:** the T5a proof passes and the in-process CLI suite passes.

#### 6. Packed-install smoke, HTTPS/redirect transport, docs and evidence

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T3, T4, T5`
**Prerequisites:** T3–T5 merged.
**Files and symbols:**
- New `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/development.md` (CLI install/login/usage, connection file location, Keychain/token-file rules, loopback `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` vs HTTPS origin, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for private CAs, managed-assignment limit), `README.md` and `docs/SPEC.md` "Operator CLI" (state that CLI1 authentication and task inspection are implemented and the remaining areas are planned), and `docs/design/operator-cli.md` only where a CLI1 contract detail is settled (token format, exit codes, `/api/operator/cli`).
- New `docs/evidence/issue-894-cli1-<date>.md`.
- `docs/acceptance.md` CLI01/CLI02 stay **Unproved** (CLI8 #901 qualifies them). Link the evidence record.
**Test:** `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts`:
1. Run `npm pack --ignore-scripts --pack-destination <tmp>`.
2. Write a temporary project outside the checkout with a lockfile derived from `package-lock.json` (non-dev entries plus `node_modules/ensemble` → `file:<tgz>` with sha512 integrity). Run `npm ci --offline --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund --ignore-scripts`.
3. Run `<tmp>/node_modules/.bin/ensemble` with `cwd` set to the temp dir and `ENSEMBLE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` set to a temp dir.
4. Start a real `createOperatorFixture` service with `LocalOperatorHttp` and the credential store. Issue tokens through the session endpoint (UI provisioning is qualified by T4).
5. Loopback: `auth login --token-file`, then `auth status`, then `task get --output json` (envelope, task id), then `auth logout`. After logout, the server credential still verifies (a direct bearer GET → 200), proving logout did not revoke it.
6. HTTPS: generate a throwaway CA/leaf for `localhost` with `openssl req -x509` in a temp dir. Put a test-only `node:https` reverse proxy in front of the service with `OperatorAuth` origin `https://localhost:<proxyPort>`. With `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<cert>`, login, status and task get succeed. Without it they fail with exit 5 TLS verification and the service receives no request.
7. A 3xx to another origin → exit 5 `redirect-rejected`, and the other origin receives no `Authorization`.
8. `ENSEMBLE_MANAGED_ASSIGNMENT=1` → exit 3.
9. The installed package contains `dist/src/cli/main.js` and no `dist/test`.
**Implementation:** clean up the temp dirs, tarball and proxy in `t.after`. The evidence record lists the candidate SHA, Node/npm versions, packed-smoke result, Keychain live result (T5a and the gated test), HTTPS/redirect results, and explicit limits: Codex shell propagation of the marker is unproved, there is no real remote-machine run (CLI8), and the CLI1 command surface is partial.
**Validate:** from the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-cli-packed.test.js`; expect pass with no network access required. Then run `npm run lint && npm run format:check`; expect clean.
**Complete when:** the packed-install smoke passes, the docs describe the implemented CLI1 contract and planned remainder, and the evidence record exists.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Implement against accepted design/ADR/parent; existing host-local commands compatible | 2, 5, 6 | T2 regression files; full `npm run check` (operations, launchd, service CLI tests unchanged) |
| Web credential creation, one-time reveal, metadata listing, rotation before revocation, revocation; scopes; 90-day default and shorter; verification material only; last-use/expiry without disclosure | 1, 2, 4 | T1 store tests; T2 check 9; T4 browser journey |
| Named connections, secure login/status/logout, task inspection; Keychain + protected token file; no literal flags or plaintext fallback; local logout ≠ revocation; explicit ambiguous selection | 5, 6 | T5 checks 1, 3–6, 12 and T5a/gated Keychain test; T6 loopback logout readback |
| Verified HTTPS remote, loopback HTTP local, cross-origin redirect rejection, reads through the service | 5, 6 | T5 checks 8, 11; T6 HTTPS and redirect cases |
| Server-side scope on every route incl. legacy and side-effect reads; no bearer bypass; browser cookie/Origin/CSRF preserved; managed-assignment rejection; no service-supplied credential inheritance | 2, 3, 5 | T2 checks 2–8; T3 spawn-environment test; T5 check 7 |
| Human/JSON task output, structured errors/exit categories, service identity, API version/capability negotiation; narrow path usable alone | 2, 5, 6 | T2 check 1; T5 checks 1, 9, 10; T6 packed `task get` |
| End-to-end authenticated browser/service credential lifecycle with service readback; no re-reveal | 4 | T4 browser journey |
| Valid, wrong-scope, expired/revoked, malformed; direct-HTTP writes; browser-protection regression; token-store failure; ambiguous connection; HTTPS/redirect rejection; packed-install smoke with real service | 2, 5, 6 | T2 checks 2–7; T5 checks 3–8; T6 packed smoke |

### Final validation

- From the repository root at the integrated delivery candidate (before PR), with Node 24.21.0 and npm 12.2.0 per `.node-version`/`packageManager`, run `npm ci && npm run check`; expect type checking, lint, format, build and the full test suite including the browser tests to pass. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, Ubuntu, `check` and `check-node-26`) runs the same on the PR, and it must pass. The Keychain test is skipped there by design.
- On the macOS host, run `npm run build && ENSEMBLE_KEYCHAIN_LIVE=1 node --test dist/test/operator-cli-keychain.test.js` once against the candidate; expect pass. Record it in the evidence file.

### Review focus

- Bearer gate ordering in `LocalOperatorHttp`: confirm that no `Authorization` request reaches cookie/session, legacy or slot handlers, and that `operatorRouteAuthority` fails closed for future `knownApi` additions.
- Token handling: no token in logs, error bodies, `list` responses, the config file, argv (`security -i`) or React persisted state.
- The packed lockfile derivation stays offline and deterministic. The test must not silently fall back to network resolution.

### Readiness prerequisites (unattended execution)

- **Node/npm:** Node 24.21.0 at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` (verified offline). The default `node` on PATH is 26.9.0, so prepend the nvm path. The pinned npm 12.2.0 is not installed locally (npm 11.19.0 is). Installing it needs registry access (`npm install -g npm@12.2.0`, as CI does). If that is unavailable, run locally with 11.19.0 and rely on CI for the pinned npm. The baseline in this plan used Node 24.21.0 with npm 11.19.0.
- **macOS Keychain:** `/usr/bin/security` is present and the login keychain is unlocked (`no-timeout`), checked offline with `security show-keychain-info`. T5a and the gated test add and then delete only a disposable `ensemble-cli-test-<uuid>` item. Items created by `security` are readable by `security` without a GUI prompt; a prompt would block unattended runs and counts as a T5a failure. CI (Ubuntu) has no Keychain, so Keychain behaviour is covered there only through injected fakes.
- **HTTPS certificates:** generated per test with `openssl` (verified offline: OpenSSL 4.0.3 locally; present on Ubuntu runners). No checked-in keys. Node `fetch` + `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` behaviour was verified offline by probe.
- **Browser:** Playwright 1.64.0 with Chromium and WebKit builds present in `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` (verified offline). CI installs them with `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit`.
- **Packed install:** needs only the npm cache populated by `npm ci` (verified offline by probe). No registry access at test time.
- **Network:** needed only for `npm ci` on a cold cache and for installing npm 12.2.0. No live Codex runtime or remote machine is required for CLI1.

Baseline evidence: at `111f46d7`, after `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check` and `build` passed. `node --test` on `operator-auth`, `operator-http`, `operator-web-http` and `operator-discovery-credential-browser` passed 26/26.

content.title: Workspace inspection: Safe file browsing and previews

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement

**Summary:** Provide a bounded, task-scoped read boundary for workspace file inspection.

**Current behaviour:**
TaskWorkspaceManager provisions task worktrees and validates workspace identity. Existing artifact preview reads only recorded PNG/JPEG references from the current workspace; there is no general file browser.

**Desired behaviour:**
Browse authorised task contents and linked task repository worktrees, including repository-free outputs. Support bounded text/code, Markdown, raster-image and PDF previews. Unsupported formats remain metadata-only. Hide ignored clutter initially with an explicit reveal option; sensitive/private-path exclusions apply regardless of that option. Preserve missing, changing and unavailable states. This supplies the common read/capture boundary for the other slices; it does not add UI screens in this slice.

**Key interfaces:**
- TaskWorkspaceManager and its persisted task/repository bindings: establish authorised roots and repository identity.
- Existing artifact-read validation: reuse applicable traversal, symlink, regular-file, size, hash and MIME protections.
- Operator API authentication and task access: all listing/preview requests remain server-authorised.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] List representative repository-free and multiple-repository task contents with unambiguous task/repository identity; removed or unavailable roots are explicit.
- [ ] Preview supported text/Markdown/raster/PDF content with documented limits for bytes, listing size and rendering; binary/unsupported/oversized entries show truthful metadata or exclusion states.
- [ ] Ignored files can be revealed without bypassing sensitive/private-path exclusions; exclusions apply to direct requests as well as browsing.
- [ ] Reject traversal, absolute-path injection, cross-task paths, symlink escapes and unsafe file replacement; never expose excluded contents via errors or previews.
- [ ] Preview/rendering cannot execute inspected active content with application authority. No file download/export action or terminal is introduced.
- [ ] Real filesystem and authenticated service fixtures verify bounds, replacement races and missing-workspace cases. Provide the shared contract for comparison and result capture.

**Out of scope:**
Git diff generation, turn capture, durable result byte storage, UI layout, downloads/ZIP export, editing and terminal access.

**Authority and validation:**
Chris approved #776's product scope and four delivery slices on 6 October 2026. This brief specifies work; it does not dispatch it, change Project readiness, authorise deployment/cutover or reopen #734. Preserve #742's completed task/evidence behaviour and existing runtime trust/ownership limits. Design and review the Pen interaction/state handoff before UI implementation. Numeric limits, storage and route choices are engineering decisions to document within these bounds; return material scope/guarantee changes for review. Use the pinned Node/package manager, npm ci and npm run check for implementation. The implementation owner performs required automated and bounded live validation; reuse unaffected evidence.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/779
**Planned against:** `main` at `ecc5b36ad0edce8989f0c818c3e7737dfd834130`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add one task-scoped, server-side inspection boundary over the persisted `TaskWorkspaceBinding`. It lists one directory level and reads a bounded file only under the current task workspace or a repository worktree bound to that task. It returns structured identity, observation time, metadata, availability and inert preview data through the existing authenticated operator API. #780 and #781 consume this same validation/read contract for comparisons and capture; #782 owns rendered desktop/phone screens and their interaction qualification.

### Guardrails

- Source contract: #779 Agent Brief, #776 approved scope, `docs/SPEC.md` task-workspace-inspection section, and WI01–WI03 of `docs/acceptance.md`. #779 adds no UI screen, download/export, editing, terminal, Git comparison, turn capture, retained result bytes, release/cutover gate, or paused #734 integration. Preserve #742 results and existing holds.
- Only a task ID accepted by `OperatorApi.requireTask()` and a current `TaskWorkspaceManager.get()` binding may authorize the read. The **only** roots are that binding's managed workspace path and exact repository `workspacePath` values, selected by task and repository ID. Never derive access from client absolute paths, source repository paths, Git common directories, arbitrary sibling workspaces or a project's other repositories. The workspace root may contain repository-free outputs; for a multi-repository task, its `repo-N` children are separate repository scopes, not an alternate traversal through the workspace scope.
- Define and document a small, testable private-path exclusion policy before data access: exclude Git control material (`.git` file/directory and descendants), Ensemble control/credential paths if they appear under an authorized root, and conventional credential-bearing path components (`.env` and `.env.*`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, private-key files such as `*.pem`/`*.key`). Apply it to every path component and both scopes before listing/opening; omit excluded names from directory results and return a uniform excluded state for direct requests without contents or filesystem-detail errors. Use current bound control paths, not external task text, as policy inputs.
