The service data directory is an ancestor of managed workspaces, so that ancestor is not itself a denied child. `showIgnored` changes only Git-ignored clutter visibility; it cannot override private exclusions. Document the precise policy and its limit: this is path exclusion, not semantic secret scanning or host-wide read isolation.
- Treat symlinks, nonregular preview targets, files with multiple hard links (`nlink > 1`), root replacement, mismatched device/inode/size/mtime, changed task/repository binding, missing roots, and read errors as unavailable/conflict states without returning bytes. The link-count rule conservatively refuses file aliases; it does not claim to identify their other paths. Never include host absolute paths or excluded names/content in responses or errors. A read during active writing is an observation, not a settled result; never retry by silently returning later bytes.
- Bound path depth/length, directory entries scanned/returned, Git ignore check time/output, file bytes, image dimensions, and PDF rendering handoff. Reject active HTML/SVG/PDF execution in the application origin: text/Markdown are inert UTF-8 data, raster/PDF are typed base64 data inside JSON, never raw navigable content or server-rendered markup. #782 must use a sandboxed or isolated renderer for PDF and enforce the supplied page/display limit before it may claim a visual PDF preview. Unsupported/binary/oversized entries remain metadata-only with explicit reason. No new access grant follows from a browser route.
- Continue routine implementation/fixture corrections under unchanged scope and record affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch permits one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that allowance. Investigate unknown overlap and stop for material contract, permission or privacy changes.
- #790 is being implemented from an earlier base and changes `service.ts`, `state.ts`, `codex.ts` and `coordination.ts`. Do not edit any shared mutable file or integrate this plan until #790's final reviewed head is merged, screened and its required evidence retained. The new inspection module and fixture design are separable, but this plan does not authorize concurrent implementation. #793/PR #801's approved design handoff is now merged at `70ee69d5078f15da4508d30e902c072a6d7020be`; the delta from this fixed plan baseline changes only `design/DESIGN.md` and `design/design.pen`, so it is compatible with #779's server boundary and gates #782 UI work, not #779.

### Planning decisions

- Use a structured scope (`workspace` or `repository` plus exact repository ID), relative path segments, and a current binding identity (`taskId`, `workspaceId`, repository ID when present). This gives repository-free and multi-repository reads distinct identities without persisting browser authority or leaking host paths. The existing manager allocates `repo-1`, `repo-2`, etc. and validates the managed root and worktree identities; its `get()` also reports held/archived or missing state.
- Fixed initial resource limits are engineering values: at most 32 path segments/2,048 UTF-8 path bytes; one directory level, 4,096 entries scanned and 256 returned, with explicit truncation; 1 MiB text/code/Markdown, 8 MiB PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP or PDF input, 16 megapixels for raster dimensions, and a maximum 10 displayed PDF pages in #782. These values belong in one exported limit object and `docs/SPEC.md`, so #780/#781 can use the same exclusion/read caps and #782 can enforce the rendering handoff. Changes within the accepted bounded-preview outcome are ordinary engineering; larger guarantees or extra formats require review.
- Repository ignore status comes from the selected bound worktree's Git ignore rules using a bounded, argument-safe `git check-ignore --stdin -z` call over the listed candidates. Cap stdout/stderr and deadline; on timeout cancel and observe the exact owned child using the existing workspace Git lifecycle pattern, never a process-name kill. A failure or timeout must not silently reveal ignored entries; return an explicit incomplete listing/ignore-status gap. Repository-free roots have no Git ignore identity; only the documented conventional clutter names may be hidden there, with the same explicit reveal option. Exclusions are evaluated first in both cases.
- Reuse the safety *pattern* in `previewRecordedArtifact()` (`task-review.ts`): canonical containment, no-follow open, regular-file and size check, before/after fd and pathname identity, bounded read, content hash and current-binding revalidation. That reader is for recorded PNG/JPEG references and does not provide a general privacy classifier or current-file read. Keep its recorded-artifact contract intact; factor a common helper only if tests prove no regression. Compute SHA-256 for successful current previews so consumers can identify the observed bytes; a hash alone is not a retained snapshot or a Git comparison.
- No separate feasibility proof is needed: existing real-SQLite workspace, artifact race, and authenticated HTTP fixtures exercise the target seam. T1 and T2 establish and test each safety boundary before T3 exposes it over HTTP. Failure of any identity, exclusion, race or size test holds dependent API work; repair the same owner slice before proceeding.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/workspaces.ts` — `TaskWorkspaceBinding`, `WorkspaceManager.get()`, `assertManagedRoot()` and `assertRepositoryPaths()` own persisted task/repository identity and availability. `src/standalone/service.ts:taskWorkspace()` delegates to the manager; `taskWorkspaceVisibility()` supplies a binding-change token. No new root grant or service mutation is expected.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/task-review.ts:previewRecordedArtifact()` reads only recorded PNG/JPEG references and checks symlink, size, hash, file replacement and changed bindings. `test/task-review-service.test.ts` has controlled replacement tests; preserve them.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts:requireTask()`, `exclusions()` and `readArtifact()` own task checks and safe operator projections. `src/standalone/operator-web.ts:OperatorWebBoundary.read()/knownApi()` maps typed GETs; `src/standalone/operator.ts:LocalOperatorHttp.handleWeb()` enforces session before and after awaited GETs; `src/operator/contracts.ts` validates response shapes. `test/operator-task-review.test.ts` proves actual HTTP logout/expiry rejection before artifact bytes are sent.
- **New:** `src/standalone/workspace-inspection.ts` — pure path/scope/exclusion classifier plus bounded listing and preview functions accepting a callback to fetch the current task binding/visibility; return typed states and no raw host paths. `test/workspace-inspection.test.ts` owns real filesystem/Git/SQLite boundary fixtures.
- **New:** `test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.ts` — actual authenticated HTTP read, task/repository access and response safety fixtures using `test/fixtures/operator-web.ts`. `docs/SPEC.md` records limits, exclusions and #779 implementation boundary only after tests pass.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 -> T2 -> T3` is acyclic. T1/T2 share the new module and its tests; T3 consumes them and edits operator routing/contracts. No concurrent edits within #779. The entire #779 implementation remains gated on screening #790's merged head before shared-file edits. Independent review follows the integrated T3 candidate; focused repairs return to its owner.

#### 1. Task-root identity, exclusion and bounded listing

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Confirm #790 integration head and `git status --short` are clean; compare its delta against `workspaces.ts`, `service.ts`, operator files and task-review seams before any shared-file edit. Use Node 24.21.0/npm 12.2.0 and run `npm ci` once in this checkout.
**Files and symbols:** New `src/standalone/workspace-inspection.ts` (`inspectionLimits`, scope/path validator, `listWorkspaceDirectory()`), new `test/workspace-inspection.test.ts`; read-only calls to `TaskWorkspaceBinding` and `service.taskWorkspace()` shape. No `WorkspaceManager` storage change expected.
**Test:** With real SQLite `WorkspaceManager` and disposable Git worktrees following `test/workspaces.test.ts`, provision one repository-free task and one task with two repos. Add ordinary outputs, ignored `.log` and `node_modules`, `.env`, Git control paths, nested directories, symlink to a sibling task/control file, removed repo root and >256 entries. Assert each listing carries exact task/workspace/repository identity, relative names, observed time, per-entry type/size or status, bounded count/truncation, and explicit missing/held/archived root state. Default hides ignored clutter; reveal shows it but never `.env`/`.git`/control contents. Reject absolute, `..`, encoded separator/control, duplicate/ambiguous scope and `repo-N` access through workspace scope. Check bounded Git ignore failure/timeout returns an incomplete gap rather than exposing uncertain ignored names. Recheck root/binding after asynchronous enumeration; injection of root replacement discards the listing.
**Implementation:** Validate structured scope and path components before filesystem access. Resolve only from the freshly loaded task binding; verify exact repository ID and manager state. Walk directory components without following symlinks; exclude private path components before `lstat`, limit iteration with `opendir`, classify file/directory/symlink/unsupported without descending, run bounded Git ignore classification only for the selected worktree, then verify root/binding and return a stable one-request observation. The workspace-root response exposes synthetic repository identities, never a second path to their contents.
**Validate:** From repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/workspace-inspection.test.js`; expect all T1 root, repository, ignore, private-path, limit and replacement assertions to pass.
**Complete when:** The service module can list only current, named task scopes and its real filesystem tests prove the private/excluded and missing-root outcomes before previews or HTTP exposure.

#### 2. Bounded inert file previews

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 identity/exclusion/race test passes; use the same scope and private policy, including for direct preview requests.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/workspace-inspection.ts` (`previewWorkspaceFile()` and shared bounded read helper); `test/workspace-inspection.test.ts`; touch `src/standalone/task-review.ts` and `test/task-review-service.test.ts` only if a proven common helper can preserve existing recorded-artifact behavior.
**Test:** In the same disposable roots, read UTF-8 code, Markdown and HTML source containing script text, PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP magic and dimensions, a small PDF, binary/NUL content, unsupported SVG, oversized files, a multiple-hard-link file and a large-dimension compressed image. Assert byte limit, MIME/magic consistency, UTF-8 validation, SHA-256/size/observation time on successful reads, JSON data only, and explicit metadata-only reasons otherwise. Direct requests to ignored files require reveal; direct `.env`, `.git`, nested private components, sibling task, source repository and symlink escapes never return bytes. Use an `afterOpen` barrier to replace the file, parent directory, root or current binding and to grow/truncate during read; assert conflict/unavailable with zero bytes and no secret text in errors. Retain the existing artifact race tests.
**Implementation:** Reuse T1's scope/path/exclusion check. `lstat` each component and canonical root, open final regular file `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW`, compare pathname/fd/root identity before reading, read at most cap+1 bytes, then recheck fd/name/root/current binding and hash the exact result. Reject changed or nonregular targets before publishing data. Detect supported types from bounded signatures plus strict UTF-8; return Markdown as source text, images/PDF as base64 data with MIME and explicit renderer budget, never executable HTML or a direct file URL. The PDF payload is a bounded read contract; #782 must enforce page/display limits and isolated rendering to claim a visual journey. Document exclusions and unsupported content honestly.
**Validate:** From repository root, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/workspace-inspection.test.js dist/test/task-review-service.test.js`; expect new preview/race assertions and unchanged recorded-artifact checks to pass.
**Complete when:** Every supported type has bounded, inert bytes and every excluded, unsafe, changing or unsupported direct read has an explicit no-bytes outcome.

#### 3. Authenticated operator contract and integration evidence

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 boundary tests pass. Recheck #790's merged delta before touching any operator/service file; preserve its startup, cancellation, fatal admission and background-settlement behavior.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`readWorkspaceDirectory()`, `readWorkspacePreview()` calling `requireTask`, `taskWorkspace`, visibility/current exclusions), `src/standalone/operator-web.ts` (two GET mappings and `knownApi`), `src/operator/contracts.ts` (strict response schemas), `src/standalone/operator.ts` only for necessary route/header handling; new `test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.ts`; `docs/SPEC.md` and `README.md` implemented-status wording as applicable.
**Test:** Through actual `LocalOperatorHttp` and authenticated session fixture, call listing and preview for repo-free/multi-repo tasks and an unrelated task ID; assert 401 for anonymous/expired/logout, 404 or safe excluded state for foreign/invalid scopes, no absolute paths/secret bytes in JSON/errors, strict unknown/duplicate query rejection, private path denial with `showIgnored=true`, and no session-expired payload after an awaited read. Observe the file-read boundary with an injection barrier, change binding or remove workspace midrequest, and assert 409/explicit unavailable with no data. Verify `Content-Type: application/json`, `nosniff`, `no-store`, no raw file response, no download/terminal/command route, and consistent task/repository/observed/hash metadata. Existing task/result/artifact reads still pass.
**Implementation:** Route only named GETs under `/api/operator/tasks/:taskId/files` and `/preview`, with typed query parsing and explicit `scope`, `repositoryId`, relative `path`, `showIgnored` (list and direct preview). Keep authentication in `LocalOperatorHttp`, and revalidate the live session after each awaited read before JSON headers. Keep all filesystem checks server-side; the browser supplies identifiers, never authority. Return strict typed availability states and limits for #780/#781/#782. Update docs with exact numeric caps, exclusion set, supported MIME, no-download and PDF renderer handoff, while clearly separating implemented service from later UI/comparison/capture work.
**Validate:** From repository root, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.js dist/test/workspace-inspection.test.js dist/test/operator-task-review.test.js`; expect authenticated service, private path, race and existing artifact tests to pass.
**Complete when:** The production service exposes only the bounded, authenticated read API; real SQLite/filesystem/HTTP fixtures pass and the shared #780/#781 capture contract is documented without claiming those dependants are implemented.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| #779 AC1 / WI01: repository-free and multi-repository listing, exact identity, removed/unavailable roots | T1, T3 | T1 real SQLite/Git listing fixture; T3 authenticated HTTP identity and missing-root fixture |
| #779 AC2 / WI02: bounded text/Markdown/raster/PDF, metadata-only binary/unsupported/oversized, documented byte/list/render limits | T1–T3 | T1 list cap; T2 format/signature/byte/dimension tests; T3 strict response and docs assertion/review |
| #779 AC3: reveal ignored files without revealing private paths | T1–T3 | T1 Git ignored/reveal/private matrix; T2 direct preview matrix; T3 HTTP `showIgnored=true` denial |
| #779 AC4 / WI03: traversal, absolute/cross-task, symlink and unsafe replacement rejection with no excluded content | T1–T3 | T1 scope/root and enumeration race; T2 file/parent/root/binding replacement barriers; T3 foreign task and midrequest HTTP tests |
| #779 AC5: inert previews and no download/export/terminal | T2, T3 | T2 text/Markdown/PDF payload type tests; T3 JSON/security headers and route inventory; #782 later qualifies actual visual PDF renderer |
| #779 AC6: real filesystem and authenticated service fixtures and common read/capture boundary | T1–T3 | T1/T2 real worktree/SQLite fixtures, T3 authenticated HTTP fixture, API contract and final check |

### Final validation

- From repository root with Node 24.21.0/npm 12.2.0, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check`; expect typecheck, lint, format check, build and complete test suite to pass. Reuse valid unchanged #742/#788/#789/#790 evidence, but rerun checks affected by post-#790 integration. Run the independent integrated candidate review, repair findings with the same owner, and rerun affected checks on the final head.
- Planning checkout has no `node_modules`, so no new local baseline test ran here. Parent-provided recent trusted CI 37685645050 covered the merged #789 candidate at `2a526c54`; it does **not** verify this exact `ecc5b36a` Playwright-only head or #779. The implementation owner must perform `npm ci` and the focused/full checks above before claiming qualification. No paid/live Codex, deployment, Haze or native-X testing is part of #779.

### Review focus

- Verify one root selector cannot traverse into another repository scope or task, including through symlink/rename races; ignored reveal does not alter the private-path result.
- Confirm PDF/Markdown/image payloads remain inert at this service boundary and the #782 renderer handoff makes no premature visual-safety claim.
- Check every availability/error response and `showIgnored` failure for accidental path/secret disclosure, and ensure no existing recorded-artifact or runtime ownership behavior regresses.

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement

**Summary:** Generate bounded repository comparisons and capture changes around actual task agent turns.

**Current behaviour:**
Results can contain supplied file names, commit SHAs and literal diff text. The service binds admitted work to exact runtime thread/turn identities and serialises workspace writers, but does not capture before/after file changes. Repository bindings retain a requested ref and starting commit, which need not identify a base branch.

**Desired behaviour:**
Provide Branch, Last turn and Uncommitted comparisons. Branch uses the merge base with the task's base branch against current contents, naming the base branch and exact baseline commit. Unknown base requires explicit selection of a locally available branch; no guess, fetch or checkout. Uncommitted supports staged/unstaged filters. Last turn is an actual workspace-capable agent turn, including repository-free workspaces, with bounded before/after observations, agent/turn identity and timestamps. Retain only the latest finished turn capture as turn history. Never label a previously finished turn as the currently running turn; expose absent and unsettled capture honestly.

Provide exact review anchors for either diff side, including deleted lines and ranges: task/repository, path, immutable content identity, side/range and comparison/result/turn context. Expose changes or unknown comparison without silently retargeting old anchors; #781 retains bounded context and #782 owns drafting/submission.

**Key interfaces:**
- TaskWorkspaceManager bindings and the safe inspection boundary: identify each repository and its authorised files.
- Execution intents, work/revision identity and runtime threadId/turnId binding: bind captures to the actual admitted turn.
- Normal-success handoff and held execution paths: integrate capture without weakening admission, ownership or recovery.
- Recorded result changes: preserve supplied claims separately from generated observed diffs.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Branch and Uncommitted produce readable bounded text diffs across committed/staged/unstaged/untracked/deleted/renamed fixtures; binary and unsupported entries remain visible.
- [ ] Each repository comparison names its own baseline and observation time; unknown base supports local selection. Missing refs/merge base stay unavailable without remote or working-tree mutation.
- [ ] Repository-free tasks support turn capture and show Git targets as unavailable.
- [ ] Successive turn fixtures verify before/after changes, exact task/work/agent/turn identity, latest-capture replacement and restart persistence. Do not infer Last turn from latest result.
- [ ] Failed/interrupted/uncertain execution exposes any partial observation with recorded outcome/time and explicit uncertainty; missing capture stays unavailable. No inspection or capture clears existing holds or claims execution has ended.
- [ ] Enforce documented file/byte/time limits and sensitive-path exclusions; changing/oversized/failed capture produces a gap rather than an unbounded wait or false exactness.
- [ ] Retained result evidence can preserve a referenced diff independently of latest-turn replacement; provide this handoff to the result-retention slice.
- [ ] Use real Git/filesystem and deterministic runtime fixtures. Qualify the changed capture hook with one bounded real-runtime journey during integrated qualification, reusing unchanged runtime evidence.

- [ ] Generated diffs expose exact content/side/range anchors for single-line and range comments, including deleted and renamed entries; path/line number alone is not treated as immutable identity.
- [ ] Fixtures cover stale/changed/missing comparisons and invalid ranges. Review anchors remain attached to original content and hand off bounded context to #781 without changing workspace files or ownership.

**Out of scope:**
Arbitrary revision picker, older-turn history browser, whole-workspace historical snapshots, Git fetch/checkout, stronger writer containment and runtime recovery redesign.

**Authority and validation:**
Chris approved #776's product scope and four delivery slices on 6 October 2026. This brief specifies work; it does not dispatch it, change Project readiness, authorise deployment/cutover or reopen #734. Preserve #742's completed task/evidence behaviour and existing runtime trust/ownership limits. Design and review the Pen interaction/state handoff before UI implementation. Numeric limits, storage and route choices are engineering decisions to document within these bounds; return material scope/guarantee changes for review. Use the pinned Node/package manager, npm ci and npm run check for implementation. The implementation owner performs required automated and bounded live validation; reuse unaffected evidence.


**Approved local code review amendment — 6 October 2026:** Chris authorised the added line-feedback and batched local-review scope. This updates the brief, not dispatch authority. Existing native dependencies and design-review gates remain unchanged.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/780
**Planned against:** `main` at `60da4d05552713d65f999918f7a6b61719bb81b5`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add a read-only, bounded comparison service and a durable capture slot around each admitted task agent turn. Build text diffs from exact, permitted byte observations, with Git supplying local baseline/index object identities and change metadata. Expose Branch, Uncommitted and Last turn through authenticated task-scoped API reads; leave rendering and review submission to #782. A latest finished capture and an independently visible pending/uncertain attempt preserve the distinction between a past finished turn and a current or held one. The generated comparison model carries immutable side/range anchors that #781 can retain with result evidence and #782 can use for draft feedback.

### Guardrails

- Source: #780 Agent Brief and its approved local code review amendment; `docs/SPEC.md` task workspace inspection, `docs/acceptance.md` WI03–WI06 and the anchor portion of WI10–WI11. #779 at this baseline already supplies managed binding, exclusion, no-follow read, race and preview-byte controls. Reuse or extract those controls for capture and comparison; never construct a second weaker root/path gate.
- A workspace binding's requested `ref` and starting `commit` are **not** a base branch. Do not infer one from `HEAD`, remote configuration, GitHub, or branch names. An unknown base is unavailable until an operator selects a locally present branch for that read. Do not persist selection as task policy, fetch, checkout or mutate working trees/indexes. Keep each repository's baseline and observation time distinct.
- Capture only task-bound, workspace-capable admitted turns. Preserve exact task, assignment/profile, work revision/request sequence, thread and turn identities; do not derive Last turn from a result. Capture failures never cause a successful runtime terminal to be classified as failed, and a visible diff never proves that a held execution ended. Keep existing writer, Stop, capacity, recovery and normal-success rules intact.
- Compare and serve only authorized task content. Exclude #779 private/control paths, ignored content unless explicitly requested where applicable, symlinks, hard links, escapes and changing files. Never execute inspected content, Git hooks, external diff/textconv, filters or remote operations. Bound path count, bytes, subprocess output/time and total capture time. Report a specific gap on exclusion, binary/unsupported content, overflow, timeout or inconsistent observation; never silently substitute later bytes.
- Generated observations are distinct from agent-supplied `reviewMetadata.changes` claims and from #781's durable result-linked copies. Only the latest finished turn is retained as turn history. The pending/held attempt may remain visible as unsettled until a later admitted turn replaces it; no older-turn browser or whole-workspace snapshots.
- No #734 X01–X08 work, #800 Pen/UI work, deployment/cutover, Haze changes, stronger execution containment, runtime recovery redesign, or GitHub external action is in this slice. #782 owns comparison UI and draft/send flows; #781 owns result-linked retention and bounded review context. Preserve #742 task/evidence behavior and the accepted S01 runtime trust and hold limits.
- Continue ordinary implementation, fixture, documentation, CI and integration repairs with the same owner under the existing progress gate; record and renew affected evidence. Those repairs do not consume plan-mismatch budget. A **factual mismatch in an approved plan seam** permits one focused diagnosis and at most two edit/validation cycles, then return the exact mismatch to the controller. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for changed requirements, architecture, privacy/authority, qualification allowance or an exhausted grant. No per-stage human approval for unchanged scope.

### Planning decisions

- **Repository comparison:** build per-repository observations from local Git trees/index plus safely read working files. Branch uses `merge-base <selected-local-base> HEAD`, then compares that tree to current contents (including staged, unstaged and untracked). Uncommitted staged compares `HEAD` to index; unstaged compares index to working contents and includes untracked files. Read object bytes by verified OID (`cat-file`) and working bytes through #779's stable, no-follow reader. Collect status/name/rename metadata with NUL-delimited, bounded local Git output, then accept both rename paths through the same exclusion gate before reading either side. Disable optional Git index writes, external diff/textconv and configured filesystem monitors for these reads; invoke argument arrays without a shell. Missing ref, merge base, object or stable index/worktree yields unavailable/gap. Never use a Git diff renderer that can expose excluded contents before filtering. This realizes WI04–WI05 without treating a starting commit as a branch.
- **Finite budgets:** shared production limits in a documented `comparisonLimits`: at most 4,096 candidate entries scanned, 256 returned files, 1 MiB per text side, 16 MiB aggregate captured source bytes per observation, 2 MiB rendered diff, 2 seconds per local Git child and 10 seconds per comparison/capture observation. A bounded process cleanup and final exit observation are required; if a child remains uncertain, return a gap and retain diagnostic state without launching replacement work against the same resource. These are engineering limits, not new product guarantees. Keep #779's tighter path/preview limits. Use test-only reduced deadlines for deterministic timeout fixtures.
- **Capture identity/lifecycle:** after the durable `state.begin` admission and before `runtime.startTurn`, save a pending capture header and bounded before observation for the exact task/work attempt; this cannot authorize a turn. Only after `state.bindTurn` (including the accepted exact prebinding reconciliation) attach `threadId/turnId`. Following terminal observation, take bounded after observation before publishing a finished capture. If terminal/binding/after observation is uncertain, preserve the known before/partial after, timestamps, explicit outcome/gap and unsettled status. On process restart, pending stays unsettled and existing holds remain; no auto-finish or recapture from later bytes. A later admitted turn with resolved ownership can replace the stale pending slot. On a settled terminal, atomically replace the task's finished slot and clear its matching pending slot. A running turn never relabels a previous finished capture as current.
- **Storage/anchors:** use a dedicated SQLite-backed comparison store initialized after host binding, with task/work/turn foreign identity checks, separate `latest_finished` and `pending` turn slots, one bounded current-comparison slot per task/target/repository, bounded per-side content/metadata, and transactional replacement. A comparison ID is immutable and unique to one observation; each text side has SHA-256 of exact bytes and a stored bounded line table. An anchor is `{taskId, repositoryId|null, path, comparisonId, context: branch|uncommitted|turn|result, resultId?/workId?/threadId?/turnId?, side: left|right, startLine, endLine, contentSha256}`. Deleted lines anchor the left side; a rename records old/new paths and anchors each side to its own path and hash. Validate contiguous one-based ranges against the stored side, including newline boundaries. No anchor is retargeted after refresh; a replaced/stale/missing comparison or changed content is explicit. #781 receives an exact bounded export/copy seam for comparison ID, side bytes, hashes, gaps and anchors before latest-slot replacement; its separate result lifetime is not implemented here.
- **Operator surface:** add authenticated, read-only `GET /api/operator/tasks/:id/comparisons` with a discriminated `target=branch|uncommitted|last-turn`, repository ID and local base/staged/unstaged selection as appropriate; add an exact `comparisonId` read for stable explicit refresh and anchor validation. Return explicit `available|unavailable|unsettled|gap`, observed time, baseline, entry metadata and bounded text/hunks/anchors, with no host paths. Validate query and response with Zod and recheck task/session, workspace binding and visibility across awaited reads as #779 does. These routes give #782 a stable server contract; do not add UI now.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/workspaces.ts` — `WorkspaceManager`, `SqliteWorkspaceBindingStore`, `TaskWorkspaceBinding` own stable task root and repository IDs, requested ref and starting commit; `forExecution` validates a ready binding.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/workspace-inspection.ts` — `listWorkspaceDirectory`, `previewWorkspaceFile`, path/private/control exclusions, binding snapshots and no-follow stable reads own the #779 boundary. Share the core safe traversal/byte reader with comparisons; preserve existing preview behavior.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `ExecutionState.begin`, `bindThread`, `bindTurn`, `taskBinding`, `recoveryIdentity`, terminal/hold and `holdUnfinishedOnOpen` own admitted identity and recovery. `src/standalone/service.ts` — `attemptRequest` resolves task workspace and admission; `executeAdmitted` starts/binds/waits for the runtime turn, handles callbacks, terminal success and holds. Hook capture there without moving the admission or completion decisions.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — assignment records supply the exact `profileId`/profile revision for agent attribution. `src/core/task-review.ts` — `reviewMetadata.changes` holds supplied files/commits/literal diff; `TaskReviewStore` preserves its source/result identities. `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-web.ts`, `src/operator/contracts.ts` expose authenticated task reads; `src/standalone/operator.ts` enforces session handling.
- **New:** `src/standalone/workspace-comparison.ts` — bounded local Git and safe byte observations, diff/hunk/anchor construction. `src/standalone/comparison-store.ts` — SQLite capture slots, exact ID reads, restart-safe transitions and export seam. `test/workspace-comparison.test.ts`, `test/turn-capture-service.test.ts`, `test/operator-comparisons.test.ts` cover the production seams; `test/fixtures/turn-capture-harness.ts` and root-level `test/turn-capture-harness.test.ts` exercise the same production-service/SQLite lifecycle offline before `test/wi03/live-turn-capture.mjs` permits one actual-runtime journey.
- **Follow:** `test/workspace-inspection.test.ts`, `test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.ts`, `test/workspaces.test.ts`, `test/task-review-service.test.ts`, `test/fixtures/operator-web.ts` for real filesystem/Git, SQLite restart, fake-runtime and authenticated HTTP patterns. `test/s05/live-journey.mjs` and `docs/acceptance.md` define prior bounded native evidence and the new journey requirement.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T4 -> T5` is acyclic. The safe-reader extraction, store schema, service hook and API share interfaces and must integrate sequentially in one owner checkout. Documentation belongs to the slice that establishes the behavior. An independent final review covers their combined final diff; no separate PR is required by this graph.

#### 1. Safe bounded repository comparisons and anchors

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** #779 delivered at baseline; no live runtime.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/workspace-inspection.ts` shared safe root/path/byte primitives; new `src/standalone/workspace-comparison.ts` comparison types, limits and `compareRepository`; `test/workspace-comparison.test.ts` and affected #779 inspection tests.
**Test:** Real temporary Git repositories with committed, staged, unstaged, untracked, deleted, renamed, binary, unsupported, ignored and sensitive paths. Assert per-repository merge-base SHA/branch/time; staged/unstaged filters; missing local ref/no merge base; no fetch/checkout/index mutation; exact left/right single/range anchors (including deleted/renamed), invalid ranges; no excluded content in served data or diagnostics and no excluded-path content read. Inject file/root replacement, oversized files, changing index, output overflow, child timeout and scan/time caps; expect explicit gaps and no false exactness. Include repository-free Git-unavailable response.
**Implementation:** Extract only the existing #779 validation needed to read exact allowed bytes. Inventory candidates within count/output deadlines, filter paths before object/working-byte retrieval, verify repository/workspace binding before and after awaits, read Git objects by OID and working files by no-follow descriptor, then form bounded text hunks and immutable side hashes/ranges. Binary/unsupported entries keep metadata without text anchors. Missing baseline returns unavailable. Document limits and local-base semantics in `docs/SPEC.md` or a linked design note.
**Validate:** From repository root after `npm ci` with Node `24.21.0`/npm `12.2.0`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/workspace-comparison.test.js dist/test/workspace-inspection.test.js`; expect all real Git/filesystem and unchanged #779 tests to pass.

#### 2. Durable turn capture and restart/hold semantics

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 safe byte and anchor tests pass.
**Files and symbols:** new `src/standalone/comparison-store.ts` store/slot/export API; `src/standalone/service.ts` `executeAdmitted` and startup wiring; `src/standalone/state.ts` exact work identity query as needed; `test/turn-capture-service.test.ts`, affected `test/task-review-service.test.ts`.
**Test:** Production service with real SQLite/temp workspaces and controllable fake runtime. Run two successive task-bound turns that write distinct files; assert exact task/work revision/request sequence, profile/assignment, thread/turn IDs, before/after hashes/times, latest finished replacement and reopen. During turn two, read prior finished plus current pending without mislabeling. Exercise repository-free workspace. For failed terminal, interrupted wait, callback hold, lost turn binding, service restart with pending observation, deleted/changing/oversized file and capture timeout, assert known partial bytes/gap/outcome and unchanged hold/writer/capacity state. Assert result-supplied `changes.diff` stays separate. Copy/export a finished comparison before replacement and verify copied bytes remain identical afterward.
**Implementation:** Initialize capture storage after `Store.ensureHost`; persist the pending header/before observation after admitted work and before `startTurn`. Bind the exact returned turn only after `state.bindTurn` succeeds. Observe after at terminal or catch/finally where safe; commit latest-finished replacement only with exact identity and observed terminal, otherwise retain unsettled pending evidence. Capture errors become gaps and never drive `state.complete`, `state.hold`, recovery or successor admission. Enforce bounded SQLite payloads and transactional replacement; expose immutable export for #781.
**Validate:** From repository root after T1 setup, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/turn-capture-service.test.js dist/test/task-review-service.test.js`; expect successive/restart/failure identity tests to pass with no weakened existing result behavior.
**Complete when:** Capture has exact runtime identity, durable latest/pending semantics and independent result export across restart and replacement.

#### 3. Authenticated comparison reads and exact context handoff

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 storage/hold tests pass.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` task read methods; `src/standalone/operator-web.ts` GET routing/known API; `src/operator/contracts.ts` Zod request/response and anchor schemas; `test/operator-comparisons.test.ts`, affected `test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.ts`.
**Test:** Authenticated HTTP requests for each target, filter/base selection and exact comparison ID against multi-repository and repository-free tasks. Assert per-repository baseline/time, no guessed base, stable old ID until explicit refresh, stale/changed/missing comparison state and invalid/out-of-task ranges. Assert session logout/expiry, task access, workspace binding/exclusion change during awaited Git/file read reject bytes, no leaked absolute paths or excluded content, and no work/hold/recovery state mutation.
**Implementation:** Parse only allowed query shapes; call T1/T2 through task-scoped reads and return discriminated availability/gap metadata plus bounded hunks and anchor tokens. Revalidate task/session/binding/visibility after awaits; exact ID retrieval must never retarget to current files. Keep routes read-only and separate from result `changes` projection. Record response contract and #781/#782 handoff in `docs/SPEC.md` or a focused design note.
**Validate:** From repository root after T1 setup, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-comparisons.test.js dist/test/operator-workspace-inspection.test.js`; expect authenticated service/API cases to pass.
**Complete when:** The server returns stable, exact comparison contexts and honest stale/unavailable states for UI/result consumers.

#### 4. Integrated deterministic qualification

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T1–T3 focused tests pass; no live attempt yet.
**Files and symbols:** affected real Git/SQLite/service tests; `test/fixtures/turn-capture-harness.ts` shared isolated production-service/SQLite setup, finite attempt/checkpoint and cleanup logic; `test/turn-capture-harness.test.ts` root-level offline tests included by `npm run check`; `test/wi03/live-turn-capture.mjs` live entry built but not executed; `docs/acceptance.md` WI03–WI06 and WI10–WI11 evidence mapping and comparison limit/route documentation; no UI files.
**Test:** One integrated fake-runtime journey through production admission, before capture, exact turn binding, file mutation, terminal and authenticated comparison read, then restart and retained ID read. Repeat deterministic failure fixtures for missing/held binding and assert no newer bytes fill an older gap. Compare current result metadata with generated observation and exercise immutable export before replacement. Against the **same production SQLite and service lifecycle** the actual live entry will use, inject delayed thread/turn start response and delayed terminal, assertion failure while execution is still active, supported bounded Stop/cancel and its uncertain outcome, and shutdown/reopen after a settled terminal. Assert the harness uses its recorded deadline/read count, checkpoints exact available work/thread/turn/process IDs and persistence, never duplicates dispatch, never silently removes an unresolved fixture or releases its holds, and never resets the one-attempt counter on reopen or repair. Do not fabricate a provider execution handle, archive state or conversation lifecycle absent from this operation. The fake runtime proves harness failure/recovery control only, not native behavior.
**Implementation:** Build the shared harness and guarded `--live --one-attempt` entry before any real invocation. Use existing `test/s05/live-journey.mjs` bounded source and fixture-lifecycle patterns; keep the actual runtime identity/observation mechanism only when supplied. Implement finite reconciliation and supported Stop/cancel handling so a failed assertion cannot trigger unconditional cleanup or a second turn. Resolve integration defects under the same owner. Map each source criterion to a named assertion and document accepted limits. Reuse unchanged S01/#742/#779/#790 evidence by scope; do not rerun general runtime feasibility probes. Self-review the integrated candidate and obtain one independent read-only full-diff review against #780 and repository standards **before** live dispatch; repair findings and renew affected checks/review under the existing gate.
**Validate:** From repository root after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/turn-capture-harness.test.js`, then `npm run check` and `git diff --check`; expect all offline harness failure/recovery cases, strict typecheck, lint, format, build and full tests passing under pinned Node/npm. Record full output, SHA, counts, no skipped relevant cases and independent full-diff review verdict.
**Complete when:** The integrated deterministic boundary, offline harness failure/recovery gate, required repository check and one independent full-candidate review pass before the sole live attempt.

#### 5. One bounded actual-runtime capture journey and final affected review

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T4`
**Prerequisites:** T4's offline harness failure/recovery tests, integrated checks and independent full-candidate review pass; approved existing-login Codex App Server/runtime profile is available; disposable isolated data/workspace roots and provider access are verified read-only; and the one-attempt allowance from this issue is unspent. No live dispatch to discover access. If any prerequisite is absent, preserve runnable offline candidate and report the exact missing operation/resume condition to the controller.
**Files and symbols:** T4's already-built `test/wi03/live-turn-capture.mjs` entry and `test/fixtures/turn-capture-harness.ts` using `StandaloneService` and real `CodexRuntime`, one task-bound repository-free turn, production SQLite/GET reads; evidence in `docs/evidence/wi03-turn-capture.md` (exact name may follow repository convention). `test/s05/live-journey.mjs` is a bounded source pattern, not a second required run.
**Test:** In a unique 0700 temporary data root, create one local project/task/profile and one managed repository-free task workspace; record source HEAD, Node/npm/Codex versions and runtime process identity. Through normal service admission and reporting obligations run **one** agent turn instructed to write a small fixed marker file under its assigned workspace, with `workspaceWrite`/`never`, only the local marker-write and required Ensemble reporting tools, no agent network or external-action tool requests, the existing authenticated Codex provider transport needed for the model turn, and no other task data. Before dispatch record a finite 30-second startup, 240-second total turn/reconciliation deadline (including at most 10 status reads at 5-second cadence after an uncertain return), and 10-second verified shutdown budget; do not restart the bound or issue a second turn. Pass only if exact task/work/agent/thread/turn IDs, real successful runtime terminal, before absence and after exact marker hash/time are durable; authenticated Last turn read returns that same capture; reopen of the SQLite store returns the same ID/bytes; no hold is falsely cleared; managed file/data/process cleanup is verified after settled completion. Record one-attempt consumption and any accepted runtime limitation. The marker file proves the hook observed an actual model-driven workspace write, not a manually mocked runtime result or replayed result.
**Implementation:** Invoke the already-qualified harness. Its durable checkpoint contains attempt ID, task/work/thread/turn and process identity when supplied, terminal/SQLite/capture observations, read count/deadline, cleanup and remaining allowance. If assertion fails or wait is uncertain, stop dependent dispatch, reconcile only within the recorded finite bound, use only supported bounded Stop/cancel, and retain runtime/fixture/holds when execution or effects remain uncertain. Do not force-terminate or delete evidence. A repair does not replenish the spent live attempt; a second attempt needs a new explicit allowance through the controller. After evidence capture, review only affected harness/evidence changes and any repaired code plus their interactions, preserving T4's full-diff coverage on unchanged ranges. If a repair changes the capture hook and invalidates live evidence after the allowance was spent, preserve the paused candidate and return the exact needed allowance to the controller; do not retry automatically.
**Validate:** From repository root after T4 and preflight, run `node test/wi03/live-turn-capture.mjs --live --one-attempt`; expect one actual Codex turn and every finite condition above with source/attempt/cleanup evidence. Then `git diff --check` and the final applicable `npm run check` on the clean candidate head; expect no errors and focused final review of affected changes. If local native runtime access is unavailable, do not substitute fake evidence or claim T5 complete.
**Complete when:** One bounded actual-runtime journey has attributable passing capture/reopen/cleanup evidence, T4's independent full-candidate review remains applicable, and the final affected review and clean-head checks pass.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Branch/Uncommitted readable bounded committed, staged, unstaged, untracked, deleted, renamed, binary/unsupported diffs | T1, T3 | Real Git fixture matrix and authenticated target/filter reads |
| Per-repository branch/merge-base SHA/time; unknown local selection; missing refs/base unavailable without mutation | T1, T3 | Multi-repository, unknown-base and Git immutability fixtures |
| Repository-free turn capture; Git targets unavailable | T1, T2, T3 | Repository-free service/HTTP fixture |
| Successive actual work/agent/turn before/after, latest replacement, restart; no result inference | T2, T4 | Two-turn production-service/SQLite and integrated read fixtures |
| Failed/interrupted/uncertain partial observation and missing-capture honesty without hold release | T2, T3, T4 | Terminal/exception/restart/held-work fixtures and state assertions |
| File/byte/time/exclusion/race gaps | T1, T2, T3 | Overflow, exclusion, replacement, timeout and awaited-read fixtures |
| Result-linked diff can outlive latest-turn replacement via #781 handoff | T2, T4 | Exact export/copy before replacement; supplied-claim separation fixture |
| Real Git/filesystem/deterministic runtime, offline failure/recovery harness and one actual-runtime hook qualification | T1–T5 | Focused suites, T4 harness cases and full review, `npm run check`, one recorded native marker-write journey |
| Immutable both-side single/range anchors, deleted/renamed lines | T1, T3 | Side hash/range/rename fixtures and schema validation |
| Stale/changed/missing comparison and invalid ranges, original context for #781 | T1, T2, T3 | Exact-ID refresh, invalid range, replacement/restart fixtures |

### Final validation

- From repository root with Node `24.21.0` and npm `12.2.0`, run `npm ci` once in the implementation checkout, focused commands per slice, then `npm run check` and `git diff --check` on the final candidate. The baseline #779 merge was reported green (1045/1045 and required CI), but this planner ran no tests and does not assert that evidence covers #780.
- Run T5's **one** actual-runtime attempt only after T4's offline harness failure/recovery cases, integrated checks, independent full-diff review and explicit live preflight pass. Save source/runtime identities, bounded observations, gaps/limitations, terminal/restart/cleanup evidence and exact attempt count. Reuse unchanged runtime protocol and #742 evidence; deterministic fake-runtime tests do not replace this changed-hook proof.
- Preserve T4's independent full-diff review through final integration; review T5 evidence/harness changes and repaired interactions only where affected. UI routes, menus, deep links and phone behavior remain #782; #780 adds server APIs only. #781 owns retained result/context lifetime. ### Review focus
