content.title: S03b: Schedule and supervise durable turns with capacity and recovery

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Schedule and supervise durable task turns with bounded capacity, conservative recovery, and automatic eligible-work resumption.

**Current behavior:**
The standalone service can persist execution intent and runtime bindings, provision task workspaces, revalidate assignment eligibility around explicit submission, serialize task writers, and retain Stop or uncertainty holds across restart. The domain command surface records projects, tasks, assignments, dependencies, permissions, revisions, and pause state. However, eligible turns still require explicit submission: no durable scheduler owns queued first turns, follow-ups, delegation admission, capacity accounting, bounded retries, sleep prevention, or complete supervisor recovery.

**Desired behavior:**
Ensemble should durably discover and admit eligible first turns, follow-ups, task-scoped lead turns, and delegated assignments. Effective admission must atomically revalidate readiness, pause/Stop, dependencies, permissions, revisions, writer ownership, recovery holds, and capacity. Admission defaults to four active turns globally and two per project; waiting requesters yield slots, capacity-one delegation cannot deadlock, and lowering limits holds new admissions without terminating active work.

The supervisor should integrate the qualified Codex runtime and task-workspace contracts. Stop durably prevents new task work, requests best-effort cancellation for every active task execution, and observes for a bounded interval without treating acknowledgement or elapsed time as release evidence. Crash, Stop, ambiguous submission, failure, missing/conflicting runtime identity, and known unfinished execution retain writer and capacity holds. A bound successful terminal result may use the approved cooperative handoff rule only after Ensemble-owned callbacks end and no other hold or known survivor remains.

Startup should restore and reconcile all holds before dispatch, reconcile a lost response only with the uniquely identified original execution, and automatically resume eligible work after reconciliation and all current controls permit it. Confirmed transient execution failures may retry at most twice using persisted accounting shared with Codex retry behavior; permanent failures and unknown effects must not retry automatically. Active execution should acquire a macOS sleep assertion; idle or ended supervision should release it, and forced sleep/wake must reconcile before further dispatch.

Operator recovery state and receipts must expose the affected assignment/generation, runtime identities, observations, pending effects, uncertainty reason, and release evidence. Ownership and capacity release must be atomic and must reject premature release. Unresolved holds remain visible and durable without a timer, acknowledgement, or force-unlock path.

**Key interfaces:**
- Scheduler/admission service: durable eligible-turn discovery, deterministic wakeups, current-control revalidation, and capacity acquisition/release.
- Execution supervisor and Codex runtime binding: durable execution identity, submission reconciliation, bounded cancellation observation, terminal classification, and cooperative handoff.
- Capacity configuration and accounting: editable global/per-project limits, waiting-turn yielding, and deadlock-free requester/assignee progression.
- Durable execution/recovery records: Stop, writer, capacity, uncertainty, retry, sleep/wake, and reconciliation evidence with atomic release receipts.
- Task-domain and workspace admission seams: consume current assignment/project revisions and workspace writer ownership without moving policy into the runtime.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Real SQLite and deterministic runtime fixtures cover first-turn, follow-up, lead-turn, and delegation admission; pause/Stop, dependency, permission, revision, initialization/storage, ambiguous submission/binding, stale/late result, crash, and restart races preserve every applicable independent hold.
- [ ] Global and per-project caps default to four and two, concurrent admission respects both, waiting requesters yield slots, capacity-one delegation progresses without deadlock, and lowering a cap blocks only new admissions until usage fits.
- [ ] Stop requests best-effort cancellation for all active task execution, observes for a bounded interval, and retains Stop/writer/capacity holds across restart whenever termination or effects remain uncertain; Resume clears only the operator Stop.
- [ ] Bound successful runtime completion permits exactly one successor only under the approved cooperative handoff predicate; crash, Stop, failure, ambiguity, stale identity, unfinished callbacks, and known survivors cannot release ownership.
- [ ] Startup reconciles durable execution and capacity state before dispatch, does not blindly replay lost or ambiguous submissions, and automatically resumes only work that is eligible after reconciliation.
- [ ] Confirmed transient failures retry no more than twice across restart with accounting shared with Codex retries; permanent failures and unknown effects do not auto-retry.
- [ ] Recovery views and receipts contain the evidence required to reconcile and atomically release holds, and premature release is rejected.
- [ ] A bounded real-runtime check covers dispatch, cancellation request, and normal handoff using the qualified runtime contract.
- [ ] The macOS sleep assertion exists only while execution is active, releases when idle or supervision ends, and deterministic sleep/wake fixtures reconcile before more dispatch.
- [ ] The pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check` pass, and evidence records source/runtime identity, observed results, and accepted limitations.

**Out of scope:**
- Actual coordination-tool delegation/result integration, assignment-routing integration, and the authenticated operator UI/session foundation owned by later slices.
- The assembled end-to-end local journey and live sleep/wake qualification owned by S05.
- Exercising or authorizing the operational host-restart fallback, which remains an S08 concern.
- Strict outside-read denial, complete descendant containment, universal live reattachment, exhaustive runtime tool observation, or a general model-tool allowlist.
- Rebooting the host, force-unlocking uncertain work, deploying/cutting over the service, altering shared Codex login/configuration, or changing the installed Haze prototype.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

**Superseded by:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/691#issuecomment-5894393070

<details>
<summary>Superseded implementation plan (revision 1)</summary>

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/691
**Planned against:** `main` at `95878b7ce7cc04e7a203133a4752c0292dcb9c3f`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean

### Approach

Add a durable scheduler around the S04a domain admission and S03a workspace/writer state. Queue each turn with stable identity; one SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transition rechecks current controls and acquires writer and capacity before any Codex call. A supervisor owns runtime identity, cancellation, conservative reconciliation, retry accounting and release. Start dispatch only after startup recovery. Expose capacity and recovery as service commands/read views; #703 owns their authenticated UI, and #693 supplies actual coordination events/results.

### Guardrails

- Preserve separate project/task/assignment identities, scoped permissions, captured instruction/profile revisions, and operator-owned dependency edges. Do not add a configurable task-owner role or infer execution authority from routing output.
- Preserve S03a workspaces/results. Crash, Stop, failed/ambiguous execution, stale identity, unfinished callback and known survivor retain writer/capacity holds. A bound successful terminal report with ended Ensemble callbacks and no other hold or known unfinished execution permits one cooperative successor; missing diagnostic tool items alone do not veto it. Do not claim physical exclusion of detached children.
- Admitted work may survive service/App Server death or Stop. No queued turn runs while Ensemble is unavailable. Never infer non-acceptance from zero search matches, historical resume, interrupt acknowledgement, empty terminal list or elapsed time. No force unlock, reboot, prototype database import, paid TypeSafe call, shared Codex configuration change, deployment or Haze cutover belongs here.
- Use deterministic assignment/result inputs for delegation and routing. #693 owns live coordination tools, result/inbox acknowledgement, and TypeSafe/result integration; #703 owns authenticated UI; S05 owns the assembled journey and live sleep/wake qualification; S08 owns operational host-restart qualification.
- For mechanical mismatches within this contract allow one focused diagnosis and at most two repair edit-and-validation cycles; normal test-first cycles do not count. Stop for a design/contract change, overlapping baseline change or exhausted budget, reporting evidence and the upstream decision needed.

### Planning decisions

- `DomainStore.admission`/`assignmentAdmission` are policy read seams; `ExecutionState.begin` is the writer transaction. Recheck their current predicates and versions inside the extended transaction, then reserve capacity. Preflight alone is insufficient because `WorkspaceManager.forExecution` awaits filesystem work. The existing single-service directory owner and SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` serialize local mutation.
- Represent each task-scoped lead conversation by one server-created task-keyed lead binding backed by the existing assignment/execution machinery, with the configured lead profile. It is not an operator-configured task-owner role. When routing is enabled, wait for #693's deterministic pending assignment rather than running a preliminary lead turn; disabled/unavailable routing queues the lead.
- A waiting requester yields only after qualified successful terminal status and a durable waiting reason. Do not release an active parent or unfinished callback to break a capacity-one deadlock. #693 delivers a child result as a later continuation.
- Attach capacity reservation to each admitted generation, including held/uncertain ones. Count reservations, not promises. Lowering 4-global/2-project limits affects new admission only. Add operator-only idempotent limit commands; #703 renders them later.
- Generic Codex `failed` or a transport timeout is not proof of a transient failure. Only a classified, bound, known-effect-safe transient may consume a durable shared retry budget; absent Codex retry telemetry/classification holds for attention instead of multiplying retries.
- Use `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i` for active macOS execution. An injectable power-event source reports sleep/wake; the production source polls `/usr/bin/pmset -g log`, persists the last timestamp plus full transition-line digest as its cursor, and holds admission if history is unavailable, truncated past the cursor or ambiguous. Parse only sleep/wake transition lines, not assertion chatter. Deterministic events prove reconciliation here; S05 qualifies physical sleep/wake.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStore.migrate`, `execute`, `admission`, `assignmentAdmission`, `assignment` own project/task/profile/assignment controls and versions; `DomainCommands` supplies idempotent async commands. `docs/design/s04a-command-boundary.md` defines the #691 read seam.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `ExecutionState.create`, `bindTask`, `begin`, `bindThread`, `bindTurn`, `complete`, `stopTask`, `resumeTask`, `holdUnfinishedOnOpen` and result checks own durable execution/writer identity. `begin` currently serializes workspace writers only; `complete` does not account for capacity.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `StandaloneService.start`, `dispatchTask`, `dispatch`, `stopTask`, `stop` own startup order, workspace validation, runtime launch and callbacks. `start` migrates S04a, recovers S03a workspaces, and holds unfinished execution before starting Codex. Dispatch is explicit today.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/workspaces.ts` — `WorkspaceManager.forExecution` validates a task binding and can await filesystem work. `src/standalone/codex.ts` — `Runtime`/`CodexRuntime` own thread/turn start/resume, bound terminal observation and unexpected-request holds; cancellation/reconciliation calls are absent.
- **New:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` — `TurnScheduler`/`SchedulerStore` own queued requests, wake/drain, lead binding, limits/reservations and retry allowances in the same SQLite DB. `src/standalone/supervisor.ts` — `ExecutionSupervisor` owns active identity, Stop observation, recovery views/receipts and restart reconciliation. `src/standalone/power.ts` — `ExecutionPower` owns the assertion and power-event hold.
- **Follow:** `test/task-writer.test.ts:fixture` and `test/standalone.test.ts:FakeRuntime` for real marked SQLite, delayed runtime events and restart; `test/domain.test.ts` for receipts; `test/codex-runtime.test.ts` for stdio RPC; `docs/evidence/s03a-workspace-writer-2026-09-29.md` for accepted writer limits.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T4 -> T5`; `T6` depends on `T3`; `T7` depends on `T5,T6`. Acyclic. T5 and T6 can run concurrently after T4 only in separate retry/power modules/tests; their shared `service.ts`/supervisor integration belongs to T7. T1–T4 are sequential because they edit `state.ts`, `service.ts` and shared admission/recovery tables.

#### 1. Durable requests and atomic effective admission

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** None.
**Files and symbols:** Add `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` (`TurnScheduler`, `SchedulerStore`, `TurnRequest`, lead binding); edit `src/core/domain.ts` (`DomainStore.assignmentAdmission`, migration/read), `src/standalone/state.ts` (`TaskExecutionBinding`, `ExecutionState.begin`), `src/standalone/service.ts` (`start`, `dispatchTask`, wake hooks), `src/standalone/index.ts` exports; add `test/scheduler.test.ts`.
**Test:** With real SQLite/marked directory and a gated `Runtime`, create two projects, ready tasks, repository-free S03a workspaces, an explicit pending assignment, follow-up, nested assignment, and a routing-disabled task with no assignment. Assert durable first/follow-up/delegation requests and distinct task-scoped lead bindings, stable work IDs after reopen, and no second `startTurn` on duplicate wake. Do not claim physical exclusion of detached children.

Never infer non-acceptance from zero search matches, historical resume, interrupt acknowledgement, empty terminal list or elapsed time. Stop for a design/contract change, overlapping baseline change or exhausted budget, reporting evidence and the upstream decision needed.

### Planning decisions

- `DomainStore.admission`/`assignmentAdmission` are policy read seams; `ExecutionState.begin` is the writer transaction. Recheck their current predicates and versions inside the extended transaction, then reserve capacity. Preflight alone is insufficient because `WorkspaceManager.forExecution` awaits filesystem work. The existing single-service directory owner and SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` serialize local mutation.
- Represent each task-scoped lead conversation by one server-created task-keyed lead binding backed by the existing assignment/execution machinery, with the configured lead profile. It is not an operator-configured task-owner role. When routing is enabled, wait for #693's deterministic pending assignment rather than running a preliminary lead turn; disabled/unavailable routing queues the lead.
- A waiting requester yields only after qualified successful terminal status and a durable waiting reason. Do not release an active parent or unfinished callback to break a capacity-one deadlock. #693 delivers a child result as a later continuation.
- Attach a shared capacity reservation to every admitted generation, including held/uncertain ones. Both managed `submitTask` and S02 diagnostic `submit` (the `src/standalone/cli.ts` `run` path) pass through `ExecutionState.begin`: all count against the four-turn global cap, and task-bound turns also count against their two-turn project cap. Direct unbound work has no project identity, cannot target the managed task-workspace root, and cannot bypass the global cap. Count reservations, not promises. Lowering limits affects new admission only. Add operator-only idempotent limit commands; #703 supplies configuration UI and #694 presents live capacity state.
- Generic Codex `failed` or a transport timeout is not proof of a transient failure. Only a classified, bound, known-effect-safe transient may consume a durable shared retry budget; absent Codex retry telemetry/classification holds for attention instead of multiplying retries.
- Use `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i` for active macOS execution. An injectable power-event source reports sleep/wake; the production source polls `/usr/bin/pmset -g log`, persists the last timestamp plus full transition-line digest as its cursor, and holds admission if history is unavailable, truncated past the cursor or ambiguous. Parse only sleep/wake transition lines, not assertion chatter. Deterministic events prove reconciliation here; S05 qualifies physical sleep/wake.

### Approach

Add a durable scheduler around the S04a domain admission and S03a workspace/writer state. Queue each turn with stable identity; one SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transition rechecks current controls and acquires writer and capacity before any Codex call. A supervisor owns runtime identity, cancellation, conservative reconciliation, retry accounting and release. Start dispatch only after startup recovery. Expose capacity and recovery as service commands/read views. #694 owns their scheduler history/control/recovery presentation in #703's authenticated shell and configuration foundation; #693 supplies actual coordination events/results.

### Guardrails

- Preserve separate project/task/assignment identities, scoped permissions, captured instruction/profile revisions, and operator-owned dependency edges. Do not add a configurable task-owner role or infer execution authority from routing output.
- Preserve S03a workspaces/results. Crash, Stop, failed/ambiguous execution, stale identity, unfinished callback and known survivor retain writer/capacity holds unless a narrowly classified failed generation obtains the T5 terminal-failure release proof and atomic transition; classification or a transient label alone never releases ownership. A bound successful terminal report with ended Ensemble callbacks and no other hold or known unfinished execution permits one cooperative successor; missing diagnostic tool items alone do not veto it. Do not claim physical exclusion of detached children.
- Admitted work may survive service/App Server death or Stop. No queued turn runs while Ensemble is unavailable. Never infer non-acceptance from zero search matches, historical resume, interrupt acknowledgement, empty terminal list or elapsed time. No force unlock, reboot, prototype database import, paid TypeSafe call, shared Codex configuration change, deployment or Haze cutover belongs here.
- Use deterministic assignment/result inputs for delegation and routing. #693 owns live coordination tools, result/inbox acknowledgement, and TypeSafe/result integration; #703 owns the authenticated shell and configuration foundation; #694 owns scheduler histories, controls and recovery presentation; S05 owns the assembled journey and live sleep/wake qualification; S08 owns operational host-restart qualification.
- For mechanical mismatches within this contract allow one focused diagnosis and at most two repair edit-and-validation cycles; normal test-first cycles do not count. Stop for a design/contract change, overlapping baseline change or exhausted budget, reporting evidence and the upstream decision needed.

### Planning decisions

- `DomainStore.admission`/`assignmentAdmission` are policy read seams; `ExecutionState.begin` is the writer transaction. Recheck their current predicates and versions inside the extended transaction, then reserve capacity. Preflight alone is insufficient because `WorkspaceManager.forExecution` awaits filesystem work. The existing single-service directory owner and SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` serialize local mutation.
- Represent each task-scoped lead conversation by one server-created task-keyed lead binding backed by the existing assignment/execution machinery, with the configured lead profile. It is not an operator-configured task-owner role. When routing is enabled, wait for #693's deterministic pending assignment rather than running a preliminary lead turn; disabled/unavailable routing queues the lead.
- A waiting requester yields only after qualified successful terminal status and a durable waiting reason. Do not release an active parent or unfinished callback to break a capacity-one deadlock. #693 delivers a child result as a later continuation.
- Attach a shared capacity reservation to every admitted generation, including held/uncertain ones. Both managed `submitTask` and S02 diagnostic `submit` (the `src/standalone/cli.ts` `run` path) pass through `ExecutionState.begin`: all count against the four-turn global cap, and task-bound turns also count against their two-turn project cap. Direct unbound work has no project identity, cannot target the managed task-workspace root, and cannot bypass the global cap. Count reservations, not promises. Lowering limits affects new admission only. Add operator-only idempotent limit commands/read models in #691; #694 owns live scheduler/capacity controls and recovery presentation, using #703's authenticated shell/configuration foundation and #692's existing configuration views.
- Generic Codex `failed` or a transport timeout is not proof of a transient failure. Only a classified, bound, known-effect-safe transient with positive proof that its original execution stopped may consume a durable shared retry budget; absent terminal/termination proof, ended callbacks, no-survivor evidence, settled effects, or Codex retry telemetry/classification holds for attention instead of multiplying retries.
- Use `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i` for active macOS execution. An injectable power-event source reports sleep/wake; the production source polls `/usr/bin/pmset -g log`, persists the last timestamp plus full transition-line digest as its cursor, and holds admission if history is unavailable, truncated past the cursor or ambiguous. Parse only sleep/wake transition lines, not assertion chatter. Deterministic events prove reconciliation here; S05 qualifies physical sleep/wake.

**Test:** Deterministic adapter returns an exact bound `turn/completed` failed terminal for the original thread/turn/generation, ended Ensemble callbacks, no known survivor or independent hold, settled effect-safety evidence, explicit transient classification and attempt count; assert one atomic old-writer/reservation release plus new queued retry generation, then full admission with no overlapping writer and at most two later turns after the first. A transient report with an unfinished callback, uncertain execution/survivor, missing bound terminal or unsettled effect must retain writer/reservation and create no retry; a T4 validated recovery receipt may instead prove termination and effect/workspace settlement before the same transition. Assert persisted count/backoff after reopen and one shared budget when Codex retry usage is reported. Permanent failure, generic `failed`, timeout/lost response, stale generation and Stop never auto-retry. Crash between recording eligibility and wake makes exactly one next request. Red baseline lacks retry state/classification.
**Implementation:** Persist attempt identity, reported Codex retries, next eligible time, classification and a generation-bound terminal-failure release proof before any new work ID. Proof requires the exact bound failed `turn/completed` terminal for the original thread/turn/generation, ended Ensemble callbacks, no known survivor/other hold and settled effects; after crash or ambiguous execution use only a validated T4 recovery receipt with independent termination plus effect/workspace settlement. A classified transient or safe effect alone is insufficient. In one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, recheck proof, generation, holds and shared retry allowance; record a distinct durable `resolved-failed` terminal state (not successful `completed` and not writer-owning `held`), release the failed generation's writer/reservation and create exactly one queued retry request/new generation atomically. Do not reserve for the retry in that transition: the scheduler later re-enters full current-control/capacity admission, so it cannot overlap the old writer, refresh a stale brief or consume a third allowance. Missing proof/telemetry remains held for attention. Use injected clock and bounded backoff; exhaustion raises attention without silence-based restart.
**Validate:** From repository root after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/retry.test.js dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js dist/test/task-writer.test.js`; expect ceiling/restart/no-retry and writer-release matrix green.
**Complete when:** Only positively terminated, effect-safe classified transients create a retry after atomic release of the failed generation, with one durable allowance across Ensemble/Codex accounting and no overlap.

#### 6. Active-only macOS assertion and wake gate

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T4`
**Prerequisites:** T4 provides durable active/held identities and the startup reconciliation gate used after wake.
**Files and symbols:** Add `src/standalone/power.ts` (`ExecutionPower`, `PowerEventSource`, `CaffeinateAssertion`); add `test/power.test.ts`; reserve shared `service.ts` wiring for T7.
**Test:** Inject fake assertion child/events. Exactly one `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i` process exists while one or more turns actively execute, releases when last active turn ends or supervision stops, and failed assertion is visible. Force sleep/wake between request selection and admission and after turn start; durable global wake hold blocks new runtime starts until admitted generations are reconciled. Duplicate wake/restart cannot duplicate dispatch. Missing/ambiguous production event cursor holds dispatch. Red baseline lacks assertion/wake gate.
**Implementation:** Own assertion child lifecycle with bounded shutdown and exit monitoring off the event loop. Persist processed macOS power-event cursor and wake hold before resuming drain. Parse power transitions and treat unreadable/ambiguous history conservatively; tests inject exact events. On wake, check every admitted generation through T4 reconciliation before clearing gate. Assertion bookkeeping never releases writer/capacity.
**Validate:** From repository root after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/power.test.js dist/test/recovery.test.js`; expect active-only assertion/wake gate green.
**Complete when:** Active execution owns the assertion and wake uncertainty blocks admission until reconciliation.

#### 7. Integrate and qualify S03b boundaries

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `T5`, `T6`
**Prerequisites:** T5/T6 focused checks pass and shared lifecycle wiring is reconciled.
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/service.ts` (`start`, `stop`, scheduler/supervisor/power lifecycle), `src/standalone/cli.ts` service exposure if needed, `src/standalone/index.ts` exports, `README.md`, `docs/design/standalone.md`; add `docs/evidence/s03b-scheduler-supervisor-2026-09-29.md`, `test/s03b/live-runtime.mjs`, `test/s03b-integration.test.ts`.
**Test:** In one real marked SQLite fixture, queue two projects, lead/worker/follow-up and synthetic child; combine cap-one yield, pause, Stop, crash/reopen, stale result and recovery receipt. Assert one request/one successor, retained holds, automatic eligible resumption and independent-project progress. Bounded live script uses existing authenticated Codex App Server and disposable task workspace for one dispatch, one cancellation request and one normal handoff; records source SHA, Node/npm/Codex identities, thread/turn IDs, observed states and limits, then cleans only its fixture. No physical sleep/wake or reboot. Red baseline lacks integrated drain/interrupt/power lifecycle.
**Implementation:** Start scheduler only after migration, workspace/execution recovery, runtime login and power reconciliation; on failure queued work stays durable/inert. Wire domain command wakes and terminal/hold changes into one drain; serialize shutdown with callbacks. Expose service-level capacity/recovery commands/read views for #694 integration into #703's authenticated shell; do not build scheduler histories, controls or recovery presentation here. Update docs to distinguish implemented S03b from #693/S05/S08 and write evidence pass/fail/unproved matrix.
**Validate:** From repository root with Node `24.21.0`/npm `12.1.0`, run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, `npm run check`, then `node test/s03b/live-runtime.mjs --live` with existing login; expect full check green and bounded dispatch/cancellation/handoff observations in evidence. If live runtime unavailable, retain check unproved and keep gate open.
**Complete when:** Every finite #691 row below passes, the bounded real-runtime boundary passes and docs name later-slice limits.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| A07 and A09 execution-send portions: durable identity and first/follow-up/lead/delegation admission; current control/revision/startup/storage races. #693 owns result/inbox acknowledgement. | 1, 4, 7 | `scheduler.test.ts` race matrix; `recovery.test.ts` reopen; `s03b-integration.test.ts` |
| A14 pause holds queued/new work while B proceeds; eligible work resumes after reconciliation | 1, 4, 7 | scheduler pause, recovery restart and integrated two-project case |
| R02/A27 4/2 defaults across direct and managed submissions, project caps for task-bound work, lowering, capacity-waiting without writer/reservation, later same-workspace admission, waiting yield and capacity-one progression | 1, 2, 7 | shared `ExecutionState.begin` ledger; scheduler/standalone mixed and five-direct cap/wake/reopen cases; same-workspace non-blocking case; parent–child–parent sequence |
| A15 Stop cancels all active task turns, observes boundedly, preserves independent holds; Resume clears only Stop | 3, 4, 7 | supervisor Stop matrix; recovery reopen; live cancellation |
| A16 bound success permits one handoff; crash/failure/ambiguity/stale identity/callback/survivor retain ownership | 3, 4, 7 | supervisor positive/negative; S03a regressions; live handoff |
| A08/A18 lost response/crash/original-execution reconciliation without historical-resume inference or blind replay | 4 | recovery identity/generation matrix |
| A17 workspace/files retained and premature recovery release refused | 4, 7 | recovery receipt/partial effects; S03a workspace regression |
| A27 persisted/shared two-retry ceiling; terminal-failure or T4 receipt proof before atomic old-generation release/new retry; no retry for unfinished, uncertain or permanent effects | 4, 5 | retry budget/reopen; negative unfinished/uncertain transient; positive qualified terminal-failure release/full readmission with no overlap |
| R03 active-only assertion and sleep/wake reconciliation | 6, 7 | power assertion/wake gate; integrated lifecycle |
| Pinned check and source/runtime/evidence record | 7 | `npm ci`, `npm run check`, bounded live script and evidence matrix |

### Final validation

- From repository root on `.node-version` Node `24.21.0` and `packageManager` npm `12.1.0`, run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run check`; expect typecheck, lint, format, build and all real-SQLite/fake-runtime tests green. Run `git diff --check` and inspect changed scope.
- Run `node test/s03b/live-runtime.mjs --live` against a disposable workspace with existing operator login; record exact source/runtime identity, observed dispatch, cancellation request, normal handoff and limits. S05 keeps assembled UI/delegation and physical sleep/wake; S08 keeps host-restart qualification. A failed required S03b check remains a blocker.

### Review focus

- Verify the exact `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` boundary shared by `submit`, CLI `run` and `submitTask`: every applicable control/capacity predicate is current in the same transition that acquires writer; no await between check and submitting state.
- Check completed, held and `capacity-waiting` generation semantics: a waiting request owns no writer/reservation; neither a late result nor a receipt for an older generation can free a newer writer/reservation. Verify transient classification cannot release a failed generation without exact terminal/ended-callback/no-survivor/effect proof or a validated T4 receipt, and retry creation is atomic with old-generation release before full re-admission.
- Check event-loop liveness during assertion monitoring, Stop observation and startup reconciliation, and sanitize recovery views/evidence.

content.title: S04c: Build authenticated operator UI foundation and configuration views

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Build the independently authenticated operator web foundation and connect its configuration and local-task views to the existing durable domain commands.

**Current behavior:**
The standalone service exposes a minimal loopback-only operator interface. It renders project, profile, routing, task, assignment and dependency records and submits versioned commands with stable retry keys. Existing tests cover durable configuration, paused/unready defaults, command replay, secret-safe credential status, loopback host checks and exact-origin POST rejection. The interface has no independent Ensemble login, authenticated session boundary, browser CSRF mechanism or approved private Tailscale access. Runtime and coordination integration is not implemented.

**Desired behavior:**
Provide the shared operator application shell, navigation and authenticated request boundary. Every private read and write must require a valid Ensemble session even when the service is reached over the private tailnet. Browser writes must additionally pass the selected origin and CSRF protections without weakening the existing host boundary. Authentication failures must reveal no private project, task, profile, routing or credential data.

Use the real durable project, profile, routing and local-task commands and read views. Preserve project-paused and task-unready defaults, validation and optimistic-version behavior, stable form retry identities, instruction/profile revisions and secret-safe credential rendering. Local-task creation must support an explicit create-and-start choice that marks the task Ready without bypassing a paused project.

Own the shared HTTP/session middleware, application layout, navigation and configuration/local-task routes. Expose a small authenticated route/view extension boundary through which #694 can replace deterministic runtime and coordination placeholders without rebuilding authentication, session handling, navigation or the command layer. Until then, runtime/coordination views must clearly report that those capabilities are unavailable and must not imply that an assignment record is admitted, running or successfully integrated.

Demonstrate bounded private reachability with an approved disposable Tailscale configuration while retaining the independent Ensemble login. A missing access prerequisite should be recorded once while independent implementation and automated verification continue.

**Key interfaces:**
- `StandaloneService.domain()` and `DomainCommands.execute()`: remain the sole read/mutation boundary for configuration and local tasks; do not add a second command or persistence layer.
- `LocalOperatorUi`: existing configuration, task and secret-safe view behavior to preserve or evolve behind the authenticated shell.
- `LocalOperatorHttp`: current loopback-only adapter whose host/origin protections must remain represented in the finished authenticated HTTP boundary.
- Shared authenticated route/view extension boundary: #703 owns middleware, layout, navigation and configuration/local-task routes; #694 owns real runtime histories, controls, coordination journeys and their data adapters.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Automated browser/service tests cover successful and rejected login, authenticated session use and invalidation, denied unauthenticated private reads and writes, and no private-data disclosure on authentication failure.
- [ ] Automated tests prove that missing or invalid CSRF/origin evidence and cross-origin writes are rejected without mutation, while valid authenticated same-origin writes succeed.
- [ ] Through the authenticated application, two projects can share a profile while retaining distinct project instructions; configuration validates and survives SQLite close/reopen; new projects remain paused.
- [ ] Local tasks can be created, read and edited through the authenticated application; identity/content survive reopen; ordinary creation is unready; create-and-start marks Ready without bypassing project pause and creates no external issue.
- [ ] Rejected form input and stale/changed command retries are surfaced safely; matching retries reuse the existing command receipt; routing credentials or credential references never appear in rendered output, responses, logs or model-facing content.
- [ ] Shared navigation and deterministic unavailable runtime/coordination views do not claim execution or end-to-end integration, and #694 can supply those routes without replacing the authentication/session foundation or duplicating commands.
- [ ] An approved disposable private-access setup demonstrates tailnet reachability plus independent Ensemble authentication; record the configuration, result and any bounded prerequisite or limitation without changing shared login/configuration.
- [ ] Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`; record the automated and bounded-live evidence and clean up disposable access configuration.

**Out of scope:**
- Scheduler implementation, assignment admission or execution supervision owned by #691.
- Coordination tools, routing decisions/result delivery and durable operator messages owned by #693.
- Real runtime histories, controls, questions/approvals and assembled operator journeys owned by #694; complete local end-to-end qualification remains #695.
- A second command layer or scheduler, live Haze access, shared Codex login/configuration changes, paid routing, deployment, cutover, optional visual polish or exhaustive browser/fault combinations.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/703
**Planned against:** `main` at `95878b7ce7cc04e7a203133a4752c0292dcb9c3f`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean

### Approach

Evolve the existing S04a loopback `LocalOperatorUi`/`LocalOperatorHttp` into one authenticated, session-guarded operator application. Keep `DomainCommands.execute` and `DomainStore` as the only configuration/local-task mutation and read boundary. Add a shared shell and guarded route registry for #694 to supply real runtime/coordination views later; until then, those sections say unavailable. Prove the HTTP/browser boundary with real SQLite and deterministic runtime responses, then exercise a separately approved disposable Tailscale HTTPS route without touching the current Tailscale or Codex installation.

### Guardrails

- Every private read, form, command and extension route is behind the same Ensemble login; the tailnet is transport, not authentication. State-changing requests also require an authenticated session, exact configured origin and session-bound CSRF token. Preserve the existing loopback bind and host refusal. Never trust arbitrary forwarded headers or enable credentialed CORS. Follow the [OWASP session](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html) and [CSRF](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) guidance for this boundary.
- Preserve S04a paused-project/unready-task defaults, optimistic versions, command receipts, stable rendered-form retry keys/create IDs, project-specific instructions, shared profile identities, revision snapshots and secret-safe routing read views. Create-and-start means Ready, not admission or project unpause. No web request calls `DomainStore.execute` directly or invents another command/persistence layer.
- #703 owns authentication, sessions, shell/navigation, project/profile/routing configuration and local-task create/read/edit forms, reusable views and bounded private-access evidence. #692 already supplies domain commands/views. #694 owns real scheduler/coordination histories, controls, questions/approvals, dependency/assignment edits, recovery presentation and next-turn messaging; #691 owns scheduler/capacity/recovery service commands, #693 owns coordination/routing results, and #695 owns the assembled local journey. Existing #692 assignment/dependency form helpers remain internal but are not exposed as #703 web controls. Do not imply that a domain assignment or deterministic placeholder is admitted/running.
- No live Haze access, paid TypeSafe call, shared Codex login/configuration change, deployment, production Tailscale change, prototype import or cutover. Use only an approved disposable tailnet node/socket for the live private-access proof; if the prerequisite is missing, record it once as unproved while completing independent tests. No credentials, credential references, session tokens or CSRF tokens in logs, error bodies, URLs, model-facing content or committed evidence.
- For mechanical mismatches within this contract allow one focused diagnosis and at most two repair edit-and-validation cycles; normal test-first cycles do not count. Stop for a design/contract change, overlapping baseline change or exhausted budget, reporting evidence and the upstream decision needed.

### Planning decisions

- Retain Node's existing `http` server and form POST boundary instead of adding a second web command stack. A new `OperatorAuth` loads one separately provisioned, absolute, owner-readable password-hash file (regular file, no symlink, mode `0600`); an interactive `operator-auth init` CLI reads the password without argv/echo and stores a salted asynchronous `scrypt` hash atomically. Missing/invalid auth configuration fails closed before the HTTP listener starts. `operator` mode reads `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_AUTH_FILE` (absolute path) and `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_ORIGIN` (canonical URL); neither setting is a secret. Provision with `npm run operator-auth -- init ABSOLUTE_AUTH_FILE` using a hidden TTY prompt. The password is never an argv/env value. This is independent of Codex login and `standalone.sqlite`.
- Keep only opaque, high-entropy session IDs in host-only `HttpOnly`/`SameSite=Strict` cookies; set `Secure` for configured HTTPS tailnet origin. Store token hashes, per-session CSRF secrets and bounded idle/absolute expiry in process memory; rotate on login, delete on logout/expiry, and invalidate all sessions on service restart. The loopback-only HTTP test configuration may omit `Secure` but cannot be exposed remotely. Use generic authentication errors, a bounded failed-login throttle and no account/secret echo. Test with an injected clock and deterministic random source.
- Configure one canonical browser origin explicitly: loopback HTTP for local tests, HTTPS tailnet FQDN for private access. The server continues binding `127.0.0.1`; accept only its own loopback Host or the configured external Host, and compare browser `Origin` to the exact canonical origin for every POST, including login/logout. Ignore `X-Forwarded-*` for authority. Use a synchronizer token in HTML form fields tied to the pre-login/login session and reject absent/mismatched tokens before any command. An HTTPS origin with non-loopback serving must present `Secure` cookies; missing HTTPS/private proxy configuration is a refusal, not a fallback to open HTTP.
- Export a narrow `OperatorRoute`/`OperatorRouteRegistry` contract: a method plus anchored path template (`:id` is validated), an authenticated handler receiving parsed params/form fields rather than raw request/response, and a typed `{kind:"html", body}` or `{kind:"redirect", location}` result; register before start. `LocalOperatorHttp` applies host, session, origin, CSRF, no-store and output headers before invoking any registered handler; plugins receive no raw `ServerResponse` or bypass switch. Reserve login/logout and existing configuration paths, reject duplicate registrations, and let #694 replace explicitly named unavailable slots with service-backed routes without editing session middleware or `DomainCommands`. The #703 `/command` HTTP allowlist contains only `project.create/configure`, `profile.create/configure`, `routing.configure` and `task.create/configure`; internal #692 assignment/dependency commands are not web-exposed until #694 installs guarded routes. Keep command keys and error results consistent; existing form retries replay receipts, changed payloads/version conflicts fail safely.
- Add one pinned Playwright Chromium dev dependency for actual browser tests and its install step to CI; the existing `node:test` runner still owns service/SQLite fault tests. `npm run check` includes browser tests after the browser binary is installed. This new test dependency is test-only, not the production UI stack.
- A live access fixture uses a separately approved ephemeral Tailscale node/socket and `tailscale serve` HTTPS to the loopback listener, with exact configured external origin. Tailscale documents [ephemeral state](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/ephemeral-nodes) and [Serve enable/disable](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/tailscale-cli/serve). Read back that disposable node's Serve status before and after, test from a second approved tailnet peer, then disable only that Serve mapping and log out/stop only that node. Never reset the user's existing Serve configuration.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator.ts` — `LocalOperatorUi.home`, `project`, `task`, `profile`, `assignment` render S04a forms/read views; `submit` maps form fields to `DomainCommands.execute`. `form` already fixes one key and create ID per rendered form. `LocalOperatorHttp.start` binds `127.0.0.1` and checks Host/POST Origin but currently serves unauthenticated private GET/POST.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStore.projects`/`project`/`profiles`/`profile`/`tasks`/`task`/`routing`/`admission` and `DomainCommands.execute` own durable versioned configuration/task state and receipts. `src/standalone/service.ts:StandaloneService.domain` exposes that store only after startup/migration. `src/standalone/cli.ts` `operator` constructs the local HTTP adapter after `service.start`.
- **Existing:** `test/operator.test.ts` uses real SQLite, fake runtime, loopback fetch and reopen; `test/domain.test.ts` proves command receipts/revisions. `docs/design/s04a-command-boundary.md` records the downstream view/command handoff; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.
- **New:** `src/standalone/operator-auth.ts` — `OperatorAuth`, `OperatorSession` and hash-file parser/session/CSRF lifecycle. `src/standalone/operator-auth-cli.ts` — interactive hash provisioning. `src/standalone/operator-routes.ts` — guarded `OperatorRoute`/`OperatorRouteRegistry` and typed handler result for #694. `test/operator-auth.test.ts`, `test/operator-http.test.ts` and `test/operator-browser.test.ts` isolate auth, HTTP and real-browser boundaries.
- **Follow:** `test/operator.test.ts:renderedForm` and `test/operator.test.ts:formValue` for stable retry fixtures; `docs/evidence/s04a-domain-2026-09-28.md` for the existing S04a limits and source identity. No scheduler, runtime history or coordination source exists at this base.
- **Baseline validation:** At the planned SHA, an isolated `git archive` extraction with Node `24.19.0` (pinned `24.21.0` unavailable locally) and pinned npm `12.1.0` passed offline `npm ci`, build and 30 focused domain/operator/standalone tests. The sandbox denied loopback bind on the first run; the same tests passed when only that test command was rerun with loopback permission. Implementation must use pinned Node `24.21.0` for final `npm run check`.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T4` is acyclic. T1 provides auth/session semantics to T2; T2 guards all routes before T3 presents real forms; T4 proves the completed surface privately. These slices share `operator.ts`/HTTP wiring and cannot be implemented as independent unmerged edits. #691/#693 work remains independent; #694 consumes the T2 route contract after #703 delivery.

#### 1. Provision independent login and session state

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** None.
**Files and symbols:** Add `src/standalone/operator-auth.ts` (`OperatorAuth`, `OperatorSession`, hash-file validation, login/logout/session/CSRF methods), `src/standalone/operator-auth-cli.ts` (interactive `init`); edit `package.json` for `operator-auth` script and `src/standalone/cli.ts` `operator` configuration/startup gate; add `test/operator-auth.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/operator-auth.test.ts` use a private temporary hash file and injected clock/random source: init writes mode `0600` without plaintext; wrong password yields no session and repeated failures throttle without exposing credential validity; correct password yields fresh opaque token and CSRF secret; fixation token is replaced; matching session validates, logout/idle/absolute expiry/restart invalidates; symlink, group-readable, malformed or missing file refuses listener configuration. Assert no password/hash/token/credential reference in public errors or captured logging. Red baseline has no independent auth or sessions.
**Implementation:** Define and validate the file format/version, absolute path, ownership/mode and one salted `scrypt` verifier; perform expensive hash work asynchronously. Provision through an interactive CLI that refuses overwrite and never accepts password argv. Generate/store only token hashes in memory with bounded expiry, failed-login throttling and constant-time comparisons; expose login, session lookup, CSRF validation and logout operations. `operator` reads the exact `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_AUTH_FILE` and `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_ORIGIN` settings and requires a valid file/origin before constructing HTTP, while `serve`/`run` remain unchanged. No standalone DB migration or Codex login touch.
**Validate:** From repository root after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-auth.test.js dist/test/standalone.test.js`; expect auth/refusal/lifecycle cases and existing startup tests green.
**Complete when:** The operator HTTP listener cannot start without independent credential configuration and verified session primitives exist.

#### 2. Guard every route and establish the shared shell contract

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 hash/session API and startup refusal.
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/operator.ts` (`LocalOperatorHttp.start`, `LocalOperatorUi` shell wrapping and unavailable sections), `src/standalone/cli.ts` `operator` origin/bind parameters; add `src/standalone/operator-routes.ts` (`OperatorRoute`, `OperatorRouteRegistry`, `OperatorHttpOptions`, typed authenticated handler/result); add `test/operator-http.test.ts` and `test/operator-browser.test.ts`, update existing `test/operator.test.ts` HTTP fixtures for required auth options; edit `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and add `docs/design/s04c-operator-ui.md` for the session/origin/route contract and pinned Playwright Chromium install/test.
**Test:** Real SQLite and fake runtime: unauthenticated GET `/`, `/project/:id`, `/task/:id`, `/profile/:id`, `/assignment/:id` and an extension GET reveal no private names/content; unauthenticated `/command` or extension POST makes no mutation. Browser Chromium: successful/failed login, host-only cookie and rotation, same-origin authenticated navigation, logout/expiry/restart rejection; POST with missing/wrong pre-login or session CSRF, missing/foreign Origin, forged Host or `X-Forwarded-Host` returns 403 without mutation; valid same-origin form POST succeeds. Inject an extension GET/POST, assert both inherit middleware; duplicate/reserved paths fail registration. Authenticated POST of #692 `assignment.create`, `assignment.apply`, `dependency.add/remove` and `imported-blockers.set` through `/command` is refused without mutation; `/assignment/:id` and runtime/coordination sections say unavailable, never “running.” Red baseline exposes project names without login and has no session/CSRF or extension gate.
**Implementation:** Parse the configured origin once; keep listener loopback-only and validate Host without trusting forwarded headers. Centralize request size, method/path, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` content-type, auth, origin and CSRF checks before calling `LocalOperatorUi.submit` or route handlers; reject malformed encodings and alternate content types without mutation. Render login and common page shell/navigation with no private content until authenticated; issue session cookie with remote `Secure`/`HttpOnly`/`SameSite=Strict`, no-store/nosniff/referrer/CSP headers, and safe generic errors. Route registry hands only authenticated context and typed responses to #694; unavailable slots are static, escaped views with no runtime status inference. Hide #692 assignment/dependency edit forms from authenticated pages and enforce the configuration/local-task-only `/command` allowlist server-side; #694 later owns those web controls through guarded extension routes. Keep existing form keys/IDs untouched, migrate `test/operator.test.ts` loopback fixtures to explicit test credentials/origin (never an unauthenticated constructor default), document the HTTP contract in `docs/design/s04c-operator-ui.md`, and place `npm exec -- playwright install --with-deps chromium` before `npm run check` in CI.
**Validate:** From repository root after `npm ci` and `npm exec -- playwright install chromium`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-auth.test.js dist/test/operator-http.test.js dist/test/operator-browser.test.js dist/test/operator.test.js`; expect auth/CSRF, browser navigation and extension-boundary cases green.
**Complete when:** Every built-in and registered private route uses one guarded session/origin/CSRF boundary, and #694 can replace unavailable sections without changing that boundary.

#### 3. Complete real S04a configuration and local-task workflows

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 authenticated route/shell and browser fixture.
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/operator.ts` (`LocalOperatorUi.home`/`project`/`profile`/`task`/`submit` and form result handling), `src/standalone/operator-routes.ts` configuration-route registration if needed; extend `test/operator.test.ts` and `test/operator-browser.test.ts`; update `docs/design/s04a-command-boundary.md` and `README.md` for authenticated behavior.
**Test:** Through authenticated Chromium forms and a real marked SQLite `StandaloneService` with fake runtime, create one shared profile and two projects with distinct instructions; assert both initially paused, same profile ID, independent instructions/revisions and readback after service close/reopen/login again. Configure routing opt-in, guidance, candidates and `env:TYPESAFE_KEY` reference; assert only “configured/unavailable” appears across HTML, responses and captured logs, never the reference/value. Create/read/edit local task: ordinary creation unready; explicit create-and-start sets Ready while paused project remains paused and `DomainStore.admission` still refuses; ID/title/outcome survive reopen and no external issue is created. Task detail labels `admission` as domain eligibility only, with scheduler/runtime unavailable. Repost exact rendered form body and assert one receipt/record; changed body with same key and stale version show sanitized conflict/retry guidance with no second mutation. Reject blank/invalid fields and HTML/script input without unsafe rendering. Domain assignment records, if shown, are labelled records rather than running turns. Red baseline lacks authenticated workflow and explicit create-and-start wording.
**Implementation:** Reuse `LocalOperatorUi.submit -> DomainCommands.execute` and the existing form UUID keys/create IDs; do not call `DomainStore.execute` from HTTP. Make create-and-start an explicit choice mapping only to `task.create.ready=true` and retain project pause; preserve optimistic expected versions for edits and current routing/profile revision displays. Render a safe, reusable project/profile/task layout with escaped values, selected form state and sanitized 400/409 errors; never reflect `credentialRef`, raw exception text or token in error pages. Show project/profile/routing/task facts and read-only dependency summary only; do not render the existing assignment/dependency edit forms as active #703 controls. Distinguish domain eligibility from actual admission/running execution. Keep #694 control/history/message routes as placeholders.
**Validate:** From repository root after `npm ci` and `npm exec -- playwright install chromium`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator.test.js dist/test/operator-browser.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js`; expect two-project, create/edit/retry/reopen/redaction and S04a regression cases green.
**Complete when:** Authenticated configuration and local-task forms use only real #692 commands, preserve defaults/receipts/revisions and survive restart without exposing secrets or claiming execution.

#### 4. Bounded private-access proof and handoff evidence

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 authenticated UI; separately approved disposable Tailscale node/socket and second approved peer for the live proof. If missing, report this one prerequisite and keep the live row unproved without changing shared configuration or delaying independent T1–T3 checks.
**Files and symbols:** Add `test/s04c/private-access.mjs` (bounded HTTP assertions against supplied HTTPS origin), `docs/evidence/s04c-operator-ui-2026-09-29.md` (source/Node/npm/browser/Tailscale identities, pass/fail/unproved matrix and cleanup); update `README.md` with disposable Serve and auth limits; no scheduler/coordination source edits.
**Test:** Start a fresh marked service fixture, dedicated auth hash and loopback operator listener configured for the approved HTTPS FQDN. On the disposable socket only, enable `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:<fixture-port>` and read back `tailscale serve status --json`. From a second approved tailnet peer, GET private paths without a cookie and POST a control without session/CSRF: no private bytes and no DB change; log in with fixture credential over HTTPS, verify a `Secure` cookie and authenticated project read, then reject foreign-Origin/missing-CSRF write and accept one same-origin form write. Read back that the disposable node uses Serve, not Funnel, and that Ensemble still listens on loopback; do not change a shared/public endpoint. Disable only that mapping with matching `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 off` flags, log out/stop only the disposable node, remove fixture files and verify Serve status is empty for that node. Red baseline has no authenticated HTTPS access or private-access record.
**Implementation:** Keep the live fixture finite and idempotent; do not create a tailnet node or alter Serve until disposable access is specifically available/approved. `private-access.mjs` accepts an explicit HTTPS origin and fixture credentials via hidden prompt or private file, makes read/write assertions and records no secret material. Capture exact source/runtime/browser/Tailscale versions, origin/bind policy, observed outcomes and limits; record any missing prerequisite once as unproved, not a pass. Document that #694 supplies real histories/controls and #695 the complete local journey. Cleanup targets only the test node/socket and fixture.
**Validate:** From repository root on the approved second peer (with this checkout), with explicit `ENSEMBLE_TEST_HTTPS_ORIGIN`, run `node test/s04c/private-access.mjs --live`; expect private unauthenticated denial, independent login, CSRF/origin refusal, one real #692 write and disposable Serve cleanup. Then with pinned Node `24.21.0`/npm `12.1.0` and Chromium installed, run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm exec -- playwright install chromium && npm run check`; expect typecheck, lint, format, build, all SQLite/service/browser tests green. If access is unavailable, retain this check as unproved and do not claim #703 complete.
**Complete when:** Automated checks pass, a bounded approved tailnet/independent-login proof passes with cleanup, and evidence clearly distinguishes #703 foundation from later runtime/UI integration.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Independent login, session lifecycle/invalidation; unauthenticated private reads/writes denied without disclosure (R04/A25) | 1, 2 | `operator-auth.test.ts` session matrix; `operator-http.test.ts` private-route denial; `operator-browser.test.ts` login/logout/restart |
| Exact origin and session-bound CSRF on built-in and extension writes | 2 | `operator-http.test.ts` forged/missing evidence; Chromium valid/invalid POST |
| Two projects share profile but keep instructions/revisions, routing settings secret-safe; paused default and durable reopen (A02/A11) | 3 | `operator-browser.test.ts` two-project/reopen/redaction; `domain.test.ts` receipts |
| Local task create/read/edit/reopen, unready default and Ready create-and-start without unpause or external issue (A03) | 3 | `operator-browser.test.ts` task forms and `DomainStore.admission` assertion |
| Rejected input, changed/stale retry and matching receipt replay; no credential data in UI/error/log/model output | 2, 3 | `operator.test.ts` retry; browser invalid/stale/redaction cases |
| Shared navigation and guarded replacement boundary; placeholders cannot claim runtime execution | 2, 3 | `operator-http.test.ts` extension auth/CSRF/collision; browser unavailable labels |
| Approved disposable private HTTPS tailnet access plus separate login, bounded cleanup and exact evidence | 4 | `private-access.mjs --live` from second peer; Serve readback/evidence |
| Pinned dependency install, full check and bounded-live record | 4 | `npm ci`, Playwright Chromium install, `npm run check` and evidence matrix |

### Final validation

- From repository root on pinned Node `24.21.0`/npm `12.1.0`, run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm exec -- playwright install chromium && npm run check`, then `git diff --check`; expect all type, lint, format, build, real-SQLite, HTTP and browser checks green. CI installs the same pinned Chromium before its `npm run check`.
- Run the T4 bounded private-access proof only with the approved disposable socket/node/peer; report exact versions, pass/fail/unproved outcomes and fixture cleanup. Missing required private-access evidence is not a pass; #694/#695 later exercise actual runtime controls and the assembled journey.

### Review focus

- Inspect all built-in and extension routes for an auth/CSRF bypass, cookie/proxy-origin confusion, session fixation or unsafe credential/error rendering. Confirm the HTTP adapter alone establishes operator identity; in-process `LocalOperatorUi` calls are trusted service code, not a remote authorization mechanism.
- Confirm #694 can register real routes without editing session middleware or duplicating `DomainCommands`, and deterministic placeholders cannot be confused with admitted/running execution.

## Implementation checkpoint — code ready, live private-access gate blocked

The authenticated operator UI implementation is complete locally on current `main@8fdf0d80798419248995ac182336fbc08f92d642`.

- Validated implementation commit: `d9ca92f2a8369ad6a279818885c702af1099850f`
- Evidence-only head: `56f7b374259aa35ed92c4e16313578917b5991f4`
- Exact runtime: Node 24.21.0 / npm 12.1.0
- `npm run check`: 141/141 tests passed, including Chromium/service coverage
- Focused malformed-form HTTP suite: 3/3 passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed
- Final independent audit: `ship` for code readiness

The required bounded private-access proof remains **UNPROVED**, so #703 is not complete and no PR has been opened. No Tailscale mutation was attempted. The current workstation is not an approved disposable node, no specifically approved second peer was designated, and the final read-only Serve/Funnel query could not reach the daemon socket.

The bounded procedure and cleanup contract are recorded in `docs/evidence/s04c-operator-ui-2026-09-29.md`. Completion requires one specifically approved disposable node/socket with empty Serve/Funnel state and one specifically approved second tailnet peer, followed by observed same-origin HTTPS access, independent Ensemble login/CSRF/private-data checks, and exact Serve cleanup.

## Completion boundary update — live Tailscale proof deferred

Chris explicitly directed on 30 September 2026: “Let’s skip 703’s Tailscale live validation for now.”

For this delivery, the bounded private-access row remains **UNPROVED** and is not relabelled as passing. It is explicitly deferred and no Tailscale mutation will be attempted. The recorded procedure and cleanup contract remain available for later qualification.
