content.title: S04d: Integrate runtime controls and qualify the operator web UI

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Integrate the S04b coordination/runtime capabilities with the S04c authenticated operator UI, and qualify the resulting S04d histories and controls.

**Current behavior:** The repository has a loopback-only S04a form/read surface for domain commands. The authenticated UI foundation belongs to #703; scheduler/coordination, result delivery and durable operator messages belong to #693. This ticket is their final UI integration slice, not a new foundation or the assembled S05 gate.

**Desired behavior:** Within the #703 application and its independent Ensemble login, an operator can inspect truthful task, assignment, routing, lead/assignee conversation and result histories, then use the completed service commands to manage local work. Views distinguish selected or queued assignees from admitted or running turns; initial results return to the task-scoped lead and nested results to their requester. Questions, answers, approvals, pause/Resume/best-effort Stop, instruction apply, dependency edits and durable next-turn messages retain their scope and state across restart. The UI must expose stopping, uncertainty, retained workspace/capacity holds and recovery evidence without implying that an acknowledgement, timer or force unlock resolved ownership. Display effective Ensemble policy and the actual runtime read/write/network/ambient-access limits; routing configuration and status must not reveal credentials or confer execution authority.

**Key interfaces:**
- Reuse #703's authentication, sessions, CSRF/origin boundary, shared navigation and project/profile/task forms. Add history and control routes behind that same boundary.
- Use S04a domain commands/read views and #693 scheduler, routing, coordination, result and message contracts. Keep logical command/message keys stable across retries so duplicate submissions do not duplicate effects or delivery.
- Render the runtime's bound turn status and service-owned holds as distinct facts. Normal handoff follows the approved #702 trust boundary; crash, Stop, failure and uncertainty holds remain conservative.
- Keep the project lead accountable with separate task-scoped lead histories; do not add a task-owner role.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Automated browser/service coverage exercises the existing setup and task views plus lead/assignee histories, routing settings/status, questions/approvals, controls, instruction/dependency edits, result destinations and durable messages. Include duplicate submission and restart.
- [ ] All newly integrated private read and control routes deny unauthenticated access and retain #703 session and origin/CSRF protections; bounded private access is demonstrated with the approved disposable Tailscale setup.
- [ ] Real-runtime history/control evidence confirms truthful running, stopping, uncertain and held presentations with recovery guidance. Record runtime/source identity, observed results and accepted limits.
- [ ] The UI distinguishes current policy from optional stronger isolation, shows default workspace writes with broad host-permitted reads, and does not claim exhaustive tool auditing or universal containment.
- [ ] Run the pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`; retain passing slice evidence and rerun affected evidence when a change or demonstrated failure invalidates it.

**Out of scope:** Rebuilding #703's UI/authentication foundation or #693's command/scheduler fault matrix; live steering; an independently configurable task-owner role; TypeSafe paid calls or credentials without separate enablement; deployment/cutover; exhaustive per-tool audit, strict outside-read denial, universal live reattachment or complete descendant containment. #695 owns the assembled end-to-end local qualification.

**Delivery boundary:** Native blockers #693 and #703 must pass before dispatch. Keep this issue in Backlog until then. The outcome and finite acceptance boundary in #694 and the live delivery authority in #649 remain controlling; this brief adds no new product gate.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/694
**Planned against:** `main` at `831439ce2bbc6f2485d206914d66cdab29f29b0a`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean

### Approach

Mount the completed scheduler/supervisor and coordination contracts into #703's authenticated server through its reserved `runtime` and `coordination` route slots. Keep HTML and form parsing in operator adapters, keep all state changes in existing service/domain/coordination APIs, and assemble those adapters in the production `operator` command. Add task/assignment links from the existing configuration pages, then qualify the private routes with real SQLite, browser restart coverage, a bounded real-runtime operator journey, and the existing disposable private-access harness.

### Guardrails

- Reuse `LocalOperatorHttp`, `OperatorAuth`, the shared shell, and `OperatorRouteRegistry`; every new read and write must inherit the existing login, exact-Origin, CSRF, body-bound, generic-error, and no-store boundary.
- Do not add another command store or scheduler. Where an existing domain or coordination command accepts a key, preserve it so exact retries replay the durable command/effect instead of duplicating work or delivery. Stop/Resume use their existing conservative state transitions rather than claiming a receipt contract they do not expose.
- Present service-owned facts separately: selected/queued assignment, admitted/running execution, runtime terminal state, Stop, writer/capacity/recovery holds, and retained evidence. Never imply that elapsed time, acknowledgement, Resume, or a rendered button released ownership.
- Keep the project lead accountable through its task-scoped assignment/history. Preserve initial-result-to-lead and nested-result-to-requester destinations; do not introduce a task-owner role.
- Render only the curated DTOs and bounded policy text. Do not expose runtime prompts/tool payloads, credential references, session material, or raw errors. State that the default is workspace writes with broad host-permitted reads, command network disabled, approval policy never, and that stricter isolation or exhaustive ambient/tool containment is not proved.
- Do not perform paid TypeSafe calls, deploy/cut over, replace persistent Tailscale configuration, reboot the host, or rebuild #693's fault matrix. #695 owns the assembled local journey.
- Keep #704 independent: it owns backup/restore tooling and operations. Avoid edits to its planned backup modules; if both tickets need `cli.ts` or service startup wiring, #694 limits its edit to route assembly and integrates current `main` before delivery.
- For mechanical mismatches within this fixed contract, allow one focused diagnosis and at most two repair edit-and-validation cycles; normal test-first cycles do not count. Stop for a design or contract change, overlapping baseline change, or exhausted repair budget, and report the evidence and remaining decision.

### Planning decisions

- Use two narrow operator adapters rather than widen `/command`: `RuntimeOperatorRoutes` owns service/supervisor reads and controls; `CoordinationOperatorRoutes` owns `CoordinationView` reads and commands. This follows the named pre-start slots already reserved and security-tested in `OperatorRouteRegistry`.
- Keep `/task/:id` and `/assignment/:id` as configuration summaries, adding links and truthful high-level operational summaries; detailed histories and controls live under `/runtime/...` and `/coordination/...`. This preserves #703's route ownership while making the real state reachable from task detail without route replacement.
- Use ordinary native forms. Keyed domain/coordination mutations carry one generated durable key unchanged on retry and are tested for receipt replay; Stop/Resume forms exercise the existing conservative state transition without claiming keyed replay. Do not add client-side JavaScript or live steering.
- Treat the existing S04c private-access result as foundation evidence, not evidence for new routes. Extend the opt-in disposable proof to visit a new private read and reject a new private write. An unavailable fixture leaves #694 incomplete; no completion waiver is implied by this plan.
- Persist the exact bounded approval material alongside its existing digest so the authenticated operator can inspect what is being approved and the service can still reject changed material. Render the canonical JSON escaped and task-scoped; never infer approval from a hash alone.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator.ts` — `LocalOperatorUi` renders configuration pages and `LocalOperatorHttp` supplies authentication, Origin/CSRF enforcement, bounded form parsing, the shared shell, and slot dispatch.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-routes.ts` — `OperatorRouteRegistry.registerSlot` reserves typed `runtime` and `coordination` route families and rejects overlap or post-start registration.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `StandaloneService` exposes execution intents, turn requests, recovery records, capacity, Stop/Resume, task holds, assignment revision apply through the domain, and `coordinationView()`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts` — `CoordinationView` returns task-scoped assignments, work history, results/destinations, messages, interactions, routing provenance and attention, and validates operator message/result/question/approval commands. It currently exposes approval hashes but not the exact material required by `decideApproval`, so T2 extends the persisted/view contract first.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/cli.ts` — the production `operator` command starts the service, authentication, `LocalOperatorUi`, and `LocalOperatorHttp`; it is the assembly point for both route slots.
- **Follow:** `test/operator-http.test.ts` for inherited security checks, `test/operator-browser.test.ts` for restart/browser form coverage, `test/coordination-view.test.ts` for scoped durable coordination fixtures, and `test/recovery.test.ts`/`test/supervisor.test.ts` for truthful recovery and Stop states.
- **New:** `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` — typed runtime read model, renderer, and route factory over a narrow `StandaloneService` interface.
- **New:** `src/standalone/operator-coordination.ts` — coordination renderer and route factory over `CoordinationView` plus the domain metadata needed for labels/links.
- **New:** `test/operator-runtime.test.ts`, `test/operator-coordination.test.ts`, and `test/s04d/live-operator.mjs` — focused adapter, restart/security, and bounded real-runtime evidence seams.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic. `T1` and `T2` may be implemented concurrently because they own separate new adapters/tests and consume existing APIs. `T3` depends on both and owns shared `operator.ts`, `cli.ts`, and browser/HTTP integration. `T4` depends on `T3` and owns live/private evidence and documentation. #704 may proceed in a separate worktree; coordinate only its possible `cli.ts` integration and merge current `main` before delivery.

#### 1. Expose truthful runtime history, policy, and controls

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Current S03b service APIs and #703 route slot at the planned baseline.
**Files and symbols:** Create `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` with `RuntimeOperatorApi`, runtime/task/assignment view DTOs, `RuntimeOperatorRoutes`, and `runtimeOperatorRoutes(api)`; create `test/operator-runtime.test.ts`.
**Test:** With a real disposable `StandaloneService`, real SQLite, and a controllable fake runtime, create two projects, a task-scoped lead and worker, queued/running/held work, Stop/recovery records, capacity settings, instruction/profile revisions, and local dependencies. Assert runtime, task, and assignment pages distinguish queued from running, show lead identity/history, hold/recovery evidence, dependency state, effective policy/access limits, and never render prompts, credential sentinels, or a force-unlock claim. POST the same stable key twice for capacity, dependency add/remove, and assignment instruction apply; assert one durable receipt/effect across restart. Exercise repeated Stop and Resume through their existing service API and assert conservative idempotent state behavior without claiming a command receipt; Resume clears only the operator Stop and never clears writer/recovery holds.
**Implementation:** Define narrow read/control methods backed by `list`, `turnRequests`, `recoveryView`, `powerStatus`, `capacityLimits`, `configureCapacity`, `stopTask`, `resumeTask`, `taskHold`, and versioned domain commands. Register GET routes for `/runtime`, `/runtime/task/:taskId`, and `/runtime/assignment/:assignmentId`; register explicit POST control routes beneath `/runtime/control/...`. Parse UUIDs, versions, limits, decisions, and command keys before calling the service. Render separate state/hold/evidence sections, task-scoped lead and assignee links, dependency/instruction controls, and static effective-policy/runtime-limit copy. Return safe local redirects after successful writes and bounded conflict/rejection pages through the shared HTTP adapter.
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-runtime.test.js`; expect all runtime adapter tests to pass with no leaked sentinel and exact retry/restart assertions green.
**Complete when:** The runtime slot exposes truthful durable histories and the listed controls entirely through existing service/domain ownership, including conservative Stop/recovery presentation.

#### 2. Expose task-scoped coordination, routing, results, and durable messages

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** `CoordinationView` and S04b persistence at the planned baseline.
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/core/coordination.ts` (`coordination_interactions` current-schema definition, stored approval material, interaction mapping) and `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts` (`CoordinationInteractionAttention`/task view safe material field); extend `test/coordination.test.ts` and `test/coordination-view.test.ts`. Create `src/standalone/operator-coordination.ts` with `CoordinationOperatorApi`, `CoordinationOperatorRoutes`, render helpers, and `coordinationOperatorRoutes(view, domain)`; create `test/operator-coordination.test.ts`.
**Test:** First add core/view tests that request approval for a concrete nested JSON value, restart, and assert the exact canonical material is retained, its digest still matches, an exact decision succeeds, changed material fails, and cross-task reads cannot expose it. Open a database created by the pre-T2 schema, run migration, and assert new approvals persist material while a pre-existing open approval with only a hash is visibly legacy/unapprovable but can be safely denied to resolve attention. Then reuse a real SQLite/fake-runtime fixture based on `test/coordination-view.test.ts` to create two tasks sharing a lead profile, nested work, initial and nested results, routing selection/fallback, a question, an approval, an unresolved result destination, and pending/delivered inbox events. Assert `/coordination/task/:taskId` and assignment views stay task-scoped, show separate lead histories, a link to the requesting assignment/conversation, exact result destinations, and escaped exact approval material, distinguish routing selection from execution admission, and omit raw prompts/tool payloads/credential sentinels. Submit message, answer, approval/denial, and result-recipient forms twice with the same key across restart; assert one command receipt/event/delivery and that paused/stopped recipients are not steered or woken early.
**Implementation:** Reuse the existing stable-key `canonical()` representation in `src/core/coordination.ts`, require its UTF-8 encoding to fit the HTTP form value boundary (8 KiB), and store that canonical JSON with the interaction while retaining `materialHash` as the comparison/authorization value; expose it only through the authenticated task-scoped `CoordinationView`. In `CoordinationStore.migrate`, inspect `PRAGMA table_info(coordination_interactions)` inside the existing transaction and add nullable `materialJson` when absent before preparing statements. Existing approval rows remain `NULL`: the view labels them as pre-material records and disables approval. Extend the decision schema/store only for this legacy case so an explicit denial may omit material, copies the stored hash into the denial event/receipt, and can never produce an approved disposition; this resolves attention without reconstructing or trusting unknown material. New approval requests require stored canonical material, and both decisions for them retain exact material/digest matching. Preserve replay and current-generation validation, and reject unsupported, oversized, stale, or changed material. Register GET routes for `/coordination`, `/coordination/task/:taskId`, and `/coordination/assignment/:assignmentId`, plus explicit POST routes for operator messages, question answers, approval decisions, and unresolved result reconciliation. Map only `CoordinationTaskView` and safe domain labels into escaped HTML. Link each question/approval to the requesting assignment's `/runtime/assignment/:assignmentId` history. Generate keyed forms with current interaction/revision/action/target/material fields, call the existing `CoordinationView` methods, and redirect to the scoped page. Explain fallback/disposition, selected/queued versus admitted/running, pending delivery, stale/denied approval, and completion status without inventing authority or live steering.
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-coordination.test.js`; expect all scoped read, secret-exclusion, duplicate/restart, and held-recipient assertions to pass.
**Complete when:** The coordination slot presents and mutates the existing task-scoped coordination contract without a second store or duplicate delivery path.

#### 3. Assemble the production UI and cover every new route through the shared security boundary

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1`, `T2`
**Prerequisites:** Passing adapter tests from T1 and T2.
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/operator.ts` (`LocalOperatorUi` task/project/assignment navigation and shared safe form helpers only), `src/standalone/cli.ts` (operator route assembly), and `src/standalone/index.ts` if public exports are required; extend `test/operator-http.test.ts`, `test/operator-view.test.ts`, and `test/operator-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:** Start the real service and authenticated loopback server with both slots registered. At the HTTP seam, enumerate every new GET/POST route and assert unauthenticated reads disclose no private marker, unauthenticated writes return 401, wrong/missing Origin or CSRF returns 403, duplicate/malformed fields are rejected, and authenticated valid requests preserve shared headers and safe redirects. In Chromium, navigate from project/task/assignment pages through lead/assignee histories, routing status, results, questions/approvals, Stop/Resume, instruction/dependency edits, and next-turn messages; restart service/auth, sign in again, and assert durable state/history plus invalidated old session. Include two projects/tasks to prove scoping and no secret rendering.
**Implementation:** Instantiate one `OperatorRouteRegistry` in the `operator` command, register both named slots before `LocalOperatorHttp.start`, and pass the same started service to the route adapters. Replace `Unavailable` navigation with links/summaries backed by the new adapters while preserving the existing configuration forms and `/command` allowlist. Reuse the shared escaping/form helpers or move only those helpers to a small internal module if both adapters need them; do not fork the auth/session shell. Add browser-visible status wording for empty/loading-not-applicable, paused, waiting, running, stopping, uncertain, held, failed, and completed states supported by the service DTOs.
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-http.test.js dist/test/operator-view.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime.test.js dist/test/operator-coordination.test.js dist/test/operator-browser.test.js`; expect all HTTP, browser, restart, security, state-wording, and duplicate-delivery checks to pass, including pinned Chromium.
**Complete when:** The production `operator` command serves the integrated runtime and coordination journey behind the unchanged independent login/security boundary.

#### 4. Qualify the bounded real-runtime and private-access operator evidence

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** Integrated operator checks pass and an approved disposable HTTPS/Tailscale fixture is available for the required private-access sub-check. Without it, keep #694 open and report the exact missing prerequisite while continuing independent work.
**Files and symbols:** Create `test/s04d/live-operator.mjs` and add `s04d:live` in `package.json`; extend `test/s04c/private-access.mjs` only to cover the newly mounted private read/write routes without weakening its foundation checks; create `docs/design/s04d-operator-integration.md` and `docs/evidence/s04d-operator-2026-09-30.md`; update `README.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/design/standalone.md`, and `docs/acceptance.md` only for the implemented boundary and recorded evidence.
**Test:** The opt-in live harness starts a disposable database/workspace with the real Codex App Server and authenticated operator surface, records source/runtime identities, observes a bound running turn in the UI, issues a best-effort Stop through the guarded route, observes stopping/held evidence without claiming release, restarts service/App Server, and verifies the retained history/control state and cleanup. The private-access harness uses an approved disposable HTTPS fixture to prove one new private runtime/coordination read is hidden before login and one new control POST rejects absent/wrong session, Origin, or CSRF while a same-origin guarded action succeeds without duplicate effect. Suppress prompt, tool, credential, session, and password contents.
**Implementation:** Make the live harness refuse execution without `--live`, use disposable identities/paths, bound every wait, record pass/fail/unproved fields and cleanup/process-exit evidence, and leave conservative holds visible on ambiguous outcomes. Update documentation to distinguish automated browser proof, the bounded real-runtime result, and private-access pass/fail/unproved status; retain accepted limits for broad reads, ambient access, unobserved descendants, and non-universal reattachment. Do not rerun unaffected S04b fault matrices or claim S05 completion.

content.title: S04b: Deliver coordination tools, results and durable operator messages

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Deliver the standalone service's scoped coordination, assignment routing, result/inbox and durable message contracts on top of #691.

**Current behavior:** S04a has durable domain commands and routing-operation records, but the current standalone service does not yet schedule coordinated lead/assignee turns or deliver their results and messages. #691 owns the scheduler; #703 owns the authenticated UI; #694 owns their final UI integration.

**Desired behavior:** Trusted task-scoped leads and assignees can delegate, report results, ask questions, receive answers and approvals, send durable next-turn messages, and request follow-up or completion under service-enforced authority. Optional project-enabled TypeSafe routing selects an eligible initial assignee without a preliminary lead turn; explicit permitted assignees bypass inference, and uncertainty returns to the lead. Results reach their recorded recipient exactly once logically: initial work to that task's lead, nested work to its requester. Paused, stopped, stale and uncertain work retains the relevant holds.

**Key interfaces:** S04a's versioned domain commands and routing records; #691's admission, capacity, turn and recovery controls; Codex's trusted execution binding; transactional result/inbox receipts. Define the small UI-facing read/command seam for #694 without rebuilding #703's shell.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Automated tests cover caller/generation authority, stale and denied actions, revision-bound follow-up/completion, scoped questions/approvals/messages and next-eligible-turn delivery.
- [ ] Deterministic TypeSafe responses cover explicit bypass, eligibility, busy-profile queueing, repair retention, fallback, stale response, revocation, opt-out, duplicate and restart behavior. No paid inference is required in this slice.
- [ ] Real SQLite and injected send/result/ack faults prove atomic result-plus-inbox recording, duplicate/reordered report handling, active-recipient wakeups and capacity-one delegation without bypassing holds.
- [ ] A bounded actual-Codex flow demonstrates task-scoped lead, delegation, result and follow-up; record runtime identity and limitations. Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** #703 authentication/shared UI; #694 final browser/runtime integration; #695 assembled local qualification or paid routing validation; a separate task-owner role, live steering, new access authority or stronger physical containment guarantees.

**Delivery boundary:** #691 is the native blocker. Keep this ticket in Backlog until it passes; `ready-for-agent` records specification readiness, not dispatch. Follow #693's finite completion checks and #649's live delivery authority without adding new gates.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1  
**Supersedes:** none  
**Replan report:** none

**Superseded by:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/693#issuecomment-5900357230

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/693  
**Planned against:** `origin/main` at `8fdf0d80798419248995ac182336fbc08f92d642`  
**Publication mode:** Reviewed  
**Local state:** Clean

### Approach

Build S04b in three foundations before integration: qualify Codex App Server dynamic-tool callbacks in the runtime adapter, add a SQLite-backed coordination model for trusted commands/results/inboxes/interactions, and implement deterministic direct TypeSafe routing behind an injected client. Then wire those foundations through the merged S03 scheduler so delegation, result return, continuation batching, reporting repair, routing fallback, and lead completion obey current admission, revision, capacity, Stop, pause, and writer rules. Expose only a typed UI-facing coordination facade; #703 retains ownership of authentication and shared UI, and #694 retains final runtime/UI assembly.

### Guardrails

- Preserve S01’s approved cooperative runtime boundary: bound successful terminal status, ended Ensemble callbacks, and no other hold or known unfinished execution permit handoff. App Server item history remains diagnostic, not an authoritative effect ledger.
- Derive agent authority only from Ensemble’s current bound thread, turn, assignment, and work revision. Assignment IDs, requester IDs, result destinations, and authority claims in tool arguments are untrusted data.
- Preserve the merged scheduler’s admission, revision, capacity, retry, Stop, pause, recovery, and workspace-writer behavior. Inference retries are separate from execution retries.
- Do not edit `src/standalone/operator.ts`, add HTTP routes, authentication, sessions, CSRF handling, shared HTML/navigation, Tailscale behavior, deployment, cutover, shared Codex configuration, or the installed Haze prototype. #703 owns authentication/shared UI; #694 owns final UI/runtime integration.
- Add the TypeSafe SDK and deterministic fake coverage, but do not read or create credentials and do not make a paid TypeSafe request. Representative paid routing validation remains S05/#695 work requiring separate authorization.
- Dynamic tools expose only the S04b coordination commands registered by Ensemble. Existing approval rejection and the selected `workspaceWrite`/`never` execution policy remain unchanged.
- For mechanical mismatches within this fixed contract, allow one focused diagnosis and at most two repair edit-and-validation cycles; normal test-first cycles do not count. Stop for a design or contract change, overlapping baseline change, or exhausted repair budget, and report the evidence and remaining decision.

### Planning decisions

- Model all coordination effects as idempotent SQLite commands. A provider callback receipt is keyed by trusted `threadId`, `turnId`, and `callId`, and stores the tool name, canonical payload hash, caller work revision, and result. An exact lost-response retry replays its stored result even after the turn ends; a reused identity with changed content conflicts; an unseen stale or unbound call is denied.
- Persist each result and its exact recipient inbox event in one transaction. Initial assignment results target the task-scoped lead assignment; nested results target the trusted requester assignment. New service-created assignments persist the concrete recipient assignment ID rather than a label inferred later.
- Use durable high-water delivery batches. One recipient conversation has at most one queued continuation batch; each included event records its delivery work ID individually. Events committed beyond the batch’s high-water mark remain pending and cause one later continuation, preventing lost wakeups without live steering.
- Treat completion as a two-phase lead action. The lead tool records a revision-bound completion request and reviewed result IDs; successful completion of that bound lead turn triggers a transactional recheck before the task becomes done. Worker success, prose, or process exit cannot complete the task.
- Use `@typesafe-ai/sdk` `0.6.0`, whose published package exposes `TypeSafeClient`, `choice`, and `systemOne`, behind a narrow injected client interface. Pin model `jev-1.13.0`, configure SDK retries to zero, and let Ensemble persist at most two inference attempts—one initial attempt and one bounded retry—independently of Codex execution retries. [Published SDK package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/%40typesafe-ai/sdk)
- Ask one Choice question whose choices are the captured eligible profile IDs plus `lead_review`. `lead_review`, malformed answers, absent context, no candidates, exhausted API attempts, or stale responses produce a single durable lead fallback. Persist returned confidence, probabilities, model, and usage only as provenance; do not invent a numerical confidence threshold.
- A routing recommendation does not reserve capacity or authorize execution. The final commit rechecks the task, routing configuration, candidate set, candidate revisions, permission, Stop/pause/dependency state, and writer ownership. A busy selected assignee remains selected and queues under existing admission controls.
- The current merged source is ready: final PR-head CI run `36637271962`, job `109640874045`, passed `check` with 127/127 tests; the clean planning checkout is the resulting squash merge.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/codex.ts` — `Runtime` and `CodexRuntime` own App Server initialization, thread/turn lifecycle, JSON-RPC server-request handling, approval denial, and terminal observation. All server requests currently enter the unexpected-request path.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `DomainStore` owns S04a projects, tasks, profiles, assignments, lead bindings, routing configuration, idempotent commands, admission checks, and the atomic `recordRouting` operation.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `ExecutionState` owns task/work/assignment/conversation bindings, admitted work revisions, result freshness, holds, recovery, and serialized writer release.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` — `SchedulerStore` and `TurnScheduler` own durable turn requests, FIFO admission attempts, and retry eligibility.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `StandaloneService.wakeScheduler`, `attemptRequest`, and `executeAdmitted` connect domain assignments to workspaces, execution state, scheduler requests, App Server threads, callbacks, and terminal handling.
- **New:** `src/core/coordination.ts` — `CoordinationStore` will own cross-domain SQLite transactions for trusted tool receipts, results, inboxes, delivery batches, delegation, durable interactions, follow-ups, and completion requests.
- **New:** `src/standalone/routing.ts` — `RoutingCoordinator`, `RoutingAttemptStore`, and `RoutingChoiceClient` will own bounded direct TypeSafe inference and its persisted attempt/provenance lifecycle.
- **New:** `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts` — `CoordinationView` will expose task-scoped read DTOs and validated operator commands without HTTP or authentication concerns.
- **Follow:** `test/s01/revision4_identity_probe.py` and `docs/evidence/s01-r4-identity-trace-2026-09-28.jsonl` for the installed `dynamicTools` / `item/tool/call` protocol: trusted `threadId`, `turnId`, `callId`, tool name and arguments, plus `{contentItems, success}` response.
- **Follow:** `src/core/domain.ts:DomainStore.recordRouting` for atomic revision checks and assignment creation, `src/core/domain.ts:DomainCommands` for in-flight sharing plus durable replay, and `src/standalone/service.ts:registerExecutionCallback` for preventing terminal handoff while an Ensemble callback remains active.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic. T1, T2, and T4 are independently ready and may run concurrently: they own `codex.ts`, coordination/domain persistence, and routing/package files respectively. T3 follows T2 because it extends the same coordination schema. T5 joins T1–T3 and owns the first `service.ts`/`state.ts`/`scheduler.ts` integration. T6 follows T4 and T5 and owns the second, routing-specific `service.ts` integration, avoiding concurrent edits to that shared file. T7 follows T6 for the final service accessor but does not touch `operator.ts`. T8 follows all implementation slices.

#### 1. Accept only registered, identity-bearing App Server dynamic-tool callbacks

**Task ID:** `T1`  
**Depends on:** `none`  
**Prerequisites:** Existing S01 revision-4 trace establishes the installed callback field and response shapes; no new protocol proof is required before coding.  
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/codex.ts` at `Runtime`, `CodexRuntime.start`, `CodexRuntime.startThread`, and `CodexRuntime.receive`; add `RuntimeToolDefinition`, `RuntimeToolCall`, `RuntimeToolResult`, `parseRuntimeToolCall`, and `Runtime.onToolCall`. Edit `test/codex-runtime.test.ts` fixtures and assertions.  
**Test:** First add fixture cases that initialize with experimental API capability, pass one function definition at `thread/start.dynamicTools`, and inject `item/tool/call` containing trusted thread/turn/call IDs. The red assertions require the registered handler to receive those outer IDs and parsed arguments and require exactly one success response. Add negative cases for unknown tool, malformed arguments, handler rejection, response-pipe failure, and ordinary approval callbacks; assert no handler invocation, a negative tool response or existing approval denial as appropriate, and preservation of the unexpected-request hold/anomaly behavior.  
**Implementation:** Send `capabilities.experimentalApi: true` during initialize. Allow `startThread(workspace, tools)` to register an immutable list of Ensemble function definitions. Parse only `item/tool/call` server requests with non-empty `threadId`, `turnId`, `callId`, registered `tool`, and object `arguments`; dispatch the promise-returning listener and serialize one `{contentItems:[{type:"inputText",text}],success}` response. Keep approval requests on `deniedServerRequest`; send unknown/malformed dynamic calls through the failure/hold path. Ensure a callback reply failure still fails the child and leaves execution ownership conservative.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js`; expect all adapter lifecycle, approval-denial, terminal, and new dynamic-tool cases to pass.  
**Complete when:** The fake App Server proves one successful registered callback with trusted outer identity, fail-closed malformed/unknown callbacks, unchanged approval denial, and exactly one attempted response per request.

#### 2. Commit current results and recipient inbox events atomically

**Task ID:** `T2`  
**Depends on:** `none`  
**Prerequisites:** none.  
**Files and symbols:** Create `src/core/coordination.ts` with `TrustedCoordinationCaller`, `CoordinationReceipt`, `AssignmentResult`, `InboxEvent`, `InboxDelivery`, and `CoordinationStore.recordResult`, receipt replay, pending-event, and delivery-batch methods. Create `test/coordination.test.ts`. Edit `src/core/domain.ts` assignment/result-destination validation and lead/routing assignment construction so new assignments retain concrete recipient assignment IDs. Update affected `test/domain.test.ts` fixtures.  
**Test:** Build a real SQLite fixture with two task-scoped lead assignments and nested worker assignments, plus current and stale work revisions. Start with tests that fail because no coordination tables or atomic result path exist. Assert: an initial result and its own task lead’s event commit together; a nested result targets only its requester; two tasks sharing one lead profile remain isolated; a stale work revision, wrong task/requester, unbound destination, or worker result after a newer revision creates neither result nor event; exact duplicate callback identity replays one stored result; changed payload conflicts; a simulated exception between result/event statements rolls back both. For batching, insert several events, bind one high-water batch and its stable delivery work ID, insert another event during processing, reopen SQLite, and assert the first events retain individual delivery bindings while the late event remains pending for exactly one later batch.  
**Implementation:** Create coordination receipt, assignment result, inbox event, and delivery-batch tables with foreign keys and uniqueness constraints. For a new command, validate the trusted caller’s current task/assignment/work revision inside the same immediate transaction; for an existing receipt, compare canonical payload and trusted binding before replay. `recordResult` writes the result, moves that assignment to completed, and inserts the exact recipient event before committing. Delivery binding records each included event and a captured high-water sequence; it never marks later events delivered and never derives recipients from transcript text. Update service-created assignment destinations to the task lead binding for initial work and trusted requester assignment for nested work.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/coordination.test.js`; expect all existing S04a command cases plus atomic result, isolation, replay, rollback, restart, and high-water batching cases to pass.  
**Complete when:** Every current result has one durable exact recipient, one atomic inbox event, safe duplicate replay, stale-result rejection, and restart-safe individual delivery accounting.

#### 3. Add scoped delegation, interactions, follow-up, and lead completion commands

**Task ID:** `T3`  
**Depends on:** `T2`  
**Prerequisites:** T2’s trusted caller and receipt/result/inbox schema.  
**Files and symbols:** Extend `src/core/coordination.ts` with `CoordinationStore.delegate`, `requestQuestion`, `requestApproval`, `answerQuestion`, `decideApproval`, `postOperatorMessage`, `requestFollowUp`, `requestTaskCompletion`, and `finalizeTaskCompletion`; add `CoordinationInteraction`, `ApprovalMaterial`, and completion-request DTOs. Extend `test/coordination.test.ts`; update exact assignment-state expectations in `test/domain.test.ts`.  
**Test:** Add red tests using current lead and worker callers. Assert that either may delegate only inside its task to an active project-permitted profile; nested destination/requester come from the caller rather than arguments. Verify questions, answers, operator messages, approval requests, and decisions survive reopen and create exactly one recipient event. Reusing an interaction command key with changed content conflicts. Approval decisions match the exact interaction revision plus canonical action/material hash; denial, stale approval, changed material, or permission revocation never satisfies `authorizationFor`. Verify follow-up is allowed only by the recorded requester or task lead, names the exact current result revision, advances the existing assignment to a new pending version while retaining its profile, and rejects stale or cross-task results. Verify only the task lead can request completion, and finalization rejects unreviewed current results, active/queued/held children, open interactions, pending events, Stop/writer/ambiguity holds, and stale task/lead work revisions.  
**Implementation:** Store interactions and completion requests as revisioned state machines with idempotent receipts. `delegate` validates the trusted caller and inserts one nested pending assignment with a generated durable ID and caller-owned result destination. `requestFollowUp` reopens the same assignment, increments its assignment version, preserves the profile and captured instruction/profile revisions, and records the exact predecessor result/work identity; reassignment is not implicit. Answers, decisions, and operator messages create recipient inbox events transactionally. Approval readback is a narrow exact-match query, not a bearer grant. Completion requests capture reviewed result IDs and the lead work revision; `finalizeTaskCompletion` accepts only a successfully completed matching lead generation after rechecking every completion gate.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/coordination.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js`; expect all authority, persistence, approval binding, retained-assignee follow-up, and completion-gate cases to pass.  
**Complete when:** Trusted assignees can delegate and wait, operators can durably answer/message/decide, follow-up reuses the assignment safely, and only a current task lead request can pass the full completion predicate.

#### 4. Make direct TypeSafe routing deterministic, bounded, and inspectable

**Task ID:** `T4`  
**Depends on:** `none`  
**Prerequisites:** No credential or live call. Use the current published SDK contract only through an injected narrow interface.  
**Files and symbols:** Create `src/standalone/routing.ts` with `RoutingChoiceClient`, `RoutingCoordinator`, `RoutingAttemptStore`, `RoutingSnapshot`, and `RoutingOutcome`; create `test/routing.test.ts`. Edit `package.json` and `package-lock.json` to add exact dependency `@typesafe-ai/sdk@0.6.0`.  
**Test:** Begin with fake-client tests that fail before the coordinator exists. Supply a brief, relevant findings, routing guidance, and captured candidate IDs/names/capabilities/revisions; assert the generated state contains only those fields and the choices contain the candidates plus `lead_review`, never credential references, environment values, full transcripts, workspaces, or unrelated history. Return each candidate, `lead_review`, malformed/unknown choices, thrown errors, timeout, and delayed responses. Assert strict candidate validation, pinned requested/returned model recording, confidence/probability/usage provenance, SDK retry disabled, two persisted Ensemble attempts at most, deterministic backoff, restart continuation within the remaining budget, and no interaction with the execution retry counter.  
**Implementation:** Wrap `TypeSafeClient.systemOne` and `choice` in the production adapter, inject the adapter and clock/backoff in tests, pin `jev-1.13.0`, and configure client retries to zero. Persist logical operation identity and every attempt before calling the client; mark success/failure/timeout afterward. Permit one retry only for the explicit transient classification within the persisted two-attempt budget. Convert `lead_review`, missing context/candidates, malformed response, stale returned candidate, non-retryable failure, or exhausted attempts to a structured fallback outcome. Treat late responses as stale unless their attempt is still the current unfinished attempt.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm ci` and `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/routing.test.js`; expect deterministic payload, response validation, retry-budget, restart, stale-response, and secret-exclusion cases to pass without network access.  
**Complete when:** Routing produces either one validated captured profile decision or one structured lead fallback, with a complete persisted attempt/provenance record and no paid request.

#### 5. Wire coordination tools and inbox continuations through the scheduler

**Task ID:** `T5`  
**Depends on:** `T1`, `T2`, `T3`  
**Prerequisites:** T1’s callback interface and T2/T3’s durable command contracts.  
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/state.ts` to add exact callback-to-current-work lookup and coordination-generation checks. Edit `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` so assignment turns have generation-specific request keys/work IDs and explicit predecessor work IDs. Edit `src/standalone/service.ts` startup, `wakeScheduler`, `attemptRequest`, `executeAdmitted`, and callback registration. Add tool definitions/dispatch in a new `src/standalone/coordination-tools.ts`. Create `test/s04b-integration.test.ts`; update `test/scheduler.test.ts`, `test/service.test.ts`, and relevant `test/s03b-integration.test.ts` expectations.  
**Test:** Start with a fake runtime exposing dynamic callbacks and real SQLite. Assert that threads receive only the scoped coordination definitions; a callback resolves authority from exact bound thread/turn/current work revision and registers its promise before durable work begins. Test spoofed assignment/requester IDs, stale/reordered calls, duplicate/lost responses, post-terminal unseen calls, malformed calls, callback failure, restart, and Stop races. Exercise lead delegation, nested delegation, result return, and two task-scoped histories using one lead profile. With capacity one, assert the delegator yields, the child runs, and one result continuation resumes the delegator without deadlock. While a recipient is active, commit multiple events plus one during batch processing; assert no live steering, one queued batch, individual delivery bindings, and one later batch for the late event. Pause/Stop must retain inboxes without dispatch. A successful turn with neither result nor durable waiting action gets one persisted reporting-repair continuation; a second miss holds attention.  
**Implementation:** Construct `CoordinationStore` during service startup. Register `ensemble_delegate`, `ensemble_report_result`, `ensemble_ask_question`, `ensemble_request_approval`, `ensemble_request_follow_up`, and `ensemble_request_completion` only on managed task threads. On a callback, synchronously locate the exact current execution binding, create/register the command promise via `registerExecutionCallback`, dispatch it, wake the scheduler after commit, and return only a bounded success/failure summary. Extend assignment request identity beyond `:initial`, using assignment version plus stable event/delivery identity and the latest completed same-conversation work as predecessor. `wakeScheduler` binds pending event batches into either an assignment’s initial prompt or one follow-up prompt; events committed after the captured high-water mark remain pending. On qualified terminal completion, persist ordinary execution completion, consume any matching completion request through T3’s finalizer, or enqueue the one allowed reporting repair. Reopen/recovery scans receipts, pending batches, repair state, and completion requests idempotently.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js dist/test/scheduler.test.js dist/test/service.test.js dist/test/s04b-integration.test.js`; expect trusted dispatch, callback-held terminal handling, continuation batching, capacity-one return, pause/Stop persistence, restart, reporting repair, and completion finalization cases to pass.  
**Complete when:** Actual service control flow can accept trusted coordination callbacks, persist their effects once, return results to the correct conversation through ordinary admission, and finish only through a qualified lead completion request.

#### 6. Integrate enabled routing, explicit bypass, disabled allocation, and fallback

**Task ID:** `T6`  
**Depends on:** `T4`, `T5`  
**Prerequisites:** T4’s deterministic routing outcome and T5’s scheduler/inbox integration.  
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/service.ts` options/startup/`wakeScheduler` to construct and invoke `RoutingCoordinator`; minimally extend `src/core/domain.ts:recordRouting`, lead binding/assignment helpers, and internal credential-reference access for atomic final dispositions and exact destinations. Extend `src/core/coordination.ts` with routing-fallback inbox reconciliation. Extend `test/routing.test.ts`, `test/domain.test.ts`, and `test/s04b-integration.test.ts`.  
**Test:** Add red service tests for: routing-enabled eligible task with no assignment calls the fake client without a lead turn and creates one assignment; an existing explicit permitted assignment makes zero calls; disabled routing creates the lead assignment and makes zero calls; missing credential, no candidates/context, explicit `lead_review`, API exhaustion, and malformed response create one lead binding plus one durable fallback event containing the brief and bounded evidence. Verify duplicate wakes/restart/delayed responses create neither competing assignments nor duplicate lead wakeups. Race the response against task/brief revision, project opt-out/pause, Stop, candidate removal/revocation, and dependency/hold changes; assert stale disposition and no dispatch. Fill capacity before a valid choice and assert the selected profile remains on the queued assignment rather than being substituted. Reopen a completed result and request repair; assert routing is not called and the original profile remains.  
**Implementation:** For tasks with no assignment, branch in this order: preserve an existing explicit assignment; if routing is disabled, ensure the task lead assignment; if enabled but unavailable or incomplete, commit the single fallback; otherwise claim/resume the persisted logical routing operation and call T4. Resolve the configured `env:NAME` reference only inside the production routing adapter and never expose its name/value through public DTOs or prompts. On a valid response, call the existing atomic routing transaction with captured task/routing/candidate revisions and an exact lead assignment destination. On fallback, persist the routing disposition and deterministic fallback event; startup reconciliation ensures a disposition committed before an event cannot lose the wakeup. Every assignment still enters the normal scheduler and current admission checks.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/routing.test.js dist/test/s04b-integration.test.js`; expect all enabled/disabled/bypass/fallback, stale-race, restart, no-duplicate, queued-selected-profile, and retained-repair cases to pass with the fake client’s network-call count matching expectations.  
**Complete when:** Each eligible unassigned task takes exactly one of explicit bypass, disabled lead allocation, validated direct routing, or single lead fallback, and only current permitted assignments reach scheduler admission.

#### 7. Expose the minimal UI-facing coordination seam without owning UI or auth

**Task ID:** `T7`  
**Depends on:** `T6`  
**Prerequisites:** Final S04b persistence and routing dispositions from T2–T6.  
**Files and symbols:** Create `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts` with `CoordinationView`, task history/result/message/attention/routing DTOs, and validated operator command methods. Create `test/coordination-view.test.ts`. Add a narrow `StandaloneService.coordinationView()` accessor in `src/standalone/service.ts`. Do not edit `src/standalone/operator.ts`.  
**Test:** Add red tests that create two projects/tasks and assert every read and command is scoped to the requested task. Reopen SQLite and verify conversation/work history, results, pending/delivered messages, questions, approvals, completion/fallback attention, and routing provenance survive. Execute operator-message, question-answer, and approval-decision commands with command keys and expected revisions; assert exact replay, changed-payload conflict, stale-version rejection, one recipient event, and no direct turn steering. Serialize every DTO and assert it contains no credential reference/value, App Server raw payload, unrestricted transcript, or other project’s records.  
**Implementation:** Build read DTOs from `DomainStore`, `CoordinationStore`, `ExecutionState`, and routing provenance rather than exposing table rows. Delegate mutations to T3’s validated commands with actor `operator`; do not duplicate business rules. Return confirmed command disposition and resulting revision/event identity. ### Approach

Build S04b in three foundations before integration: qualify Codex App Server dynamic-tool callbacks in the runtime adapter, add a SQLite-backed coordination model for trusted commands/results/inboxes/interactions, and implement deterministic direct TypeSafe routing behind an injected client. Then wire those foundations through the merged S03 scheduler so delegation, result return, unresolved-recipient reconciliation, continuation batching, reporting repair, routing fallback, and lead completion obey current admission, revision, capacity, Stop, pause, and writer rules. Expose a typed UI-facing coordination facade plus an explicitly test-only loopback view; #703 retains ownership of authentication and shared UI, and #694 retains final runtime/UI assembly.

### Guardrails

- Preserve S01’s approved cooperative runtime boundary: bound successful terminal status, ended Ensemble callbacks, and no other hold or known unfinished execution permit handoff. App Server item history remains diagnostic, not an authoritative effect ledger.
- Derive agent authority only from Ensemble’s current bound thread, turn, assignment, and work revision. Assignment IDs, requester IDs, result destinations, and authority claims in tool arguments are untrusted data.
- Preserve the merged scheduler’s admission, revision, capacity, retry, Stop, pause, recovery, and workspace-writer behavior. Inference retries are separate from execution retries.
- Do not edit `src/standalone/operator.ts`, add HTTP routes, authentication, sessions, CSRF handling, shared HTML/navigation, Tailscale behavior, deployment, cutover, shared Codex configuration, or the installed Haze prototype. #703 owns authentication/shared UI; #694 owns final UI/runtime integration.
- Add the TypeSafe SDK and deterministic fake coverage, but do not read or create credentials and do not make a paid TypeSafe request. Representative paid routing validation remains S05/#695 work requiring separate authorization.
- Dynamic tools expose only the S04b coordination commands registered by Ensemble. Existing approval rejection and the selected `workspaceWrite`/`never` execution policy remain unchanged.
- Implementation owns all in-scope test-first work, diagnosis, repair, and validation needed to satisfy these checks; do not stop because of an arbitrary repair-count cap. Escalate only a material product-contract, authority/security-boundary, issue-ownership, or overlapping-baseline change, with the evidence and remaining decision.

### Planning decisions

- Model all coordination effects as idempotent SQLite commands. A provider callback receipt is keyed by trusted `threadId`, `turnId`, and `callId`, and stores the tool name, canonical payload hash, caller work revision, and result. The service checks that durable receipt before current-generation attribution or `registerExecutionCallback`: an exact lost-response retry replays its stored result even after the turn ends without creating a late-callback hold, a reused identity with changed content conflicts, and only an unseen call proceeds to current-binding validation and callback registration. An unseen stale or unbound call is denied, preserving the existing conservative late-callback behavior.
- Persist each current result even when its recipient is missing or uncertain. When the exact recipient is known, commit the result and inbox event in one transaction: initial assignment results target the task-scoped lead assignment and nested results target the trusted requester assignment. When it is not known, commit the result plus a durable unresolved-recipient reconciliation hold and no guessed inbox event; an exact later reconciliation emits one event and clears the hold transactionally. New service-created assignments persist concrete recipient assignment IDs, while migration handles legacy textual destinations conservatively.
- S01 proves dynamic-tool callbacks on a newly started thread, but does not prove that registered tools remain available after App Server/service restart and `thread/resume`. The bounded live journey in T8 must prove a resumed turn can call the registered coordination tools with trusted identity; failure is a re-plan trigger, not something to infer from stored history.
- Use durable high-water delivery batches. One recipient conversation has at most one queued continuation batch; each included event records its delivery work ID individually. Events committed beyond the batch’s high-water mark remain pending and cause one later continuation, preventing lost wakeups without live steering.
- Treat completion as a two-phase lead action. The lead tool records a revision-bound completion request and reviewed result IDs; successful completion of that bound lead turn triggers a transactional recheck before the task becomes done. Worker success, prose, or process exit cannot complete the task.
- Use `@typesafe-ai/sdk` `0.6.0`, whose published package exposes `TypeSafeClient`, `choice`, and `systemOne`, behind a narrow injected client interface. Pin model `jev-1.13.0`, configure SDK retries to zero, and let Ensemble persist at most two inference attempts—one initial attempt and one bounded retry—independently of Codex execution retries. [Published SDK package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/%40typesafe-ai/sdk)
- Ask one Choice question whose choices are the captured eligible profile IDs plus `lead_review`. `lead_review`, malformed answers, absent context, no candidates, exhausted API attempts, or stale responses produce a single durable lead fallback. Persist returned confidence, probabilities, model, and usage only as provenance; do not invent a numerical confidence threshold.
- A routing recommendation does not reserve capacity or authorize execution. The final commit rechecks the task, routing configuration, candidate set, candidate revisions, permission, Stop/pause/dependency state, and writer ownership. A busy selected assignee remains selected and queues under existing admission controls.
- The current merged source is ready: final PR-head CI run `36637271962`, job `109640874045`, passed `check` with 127/127 tests; the clean planning checkout is the resulting squash merge.

Reopen/recovery scans receipts, pending batches, repair state, and completion requests idempotently.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js dist/test/scheduler.test.js dist/test/service.test.js dist/test/s04b-integration.test.js`; expect trusted dispatch, callback-held terminal handling, continuation batching, capacity-one return, pause/Stop persistence, restart, reporting repair, and completion finalization cases to pass.  
**Complete when:** Actual service control flow can accept trusted coordination callbacks, replay a post-terminal duplicate before liveness checks without retracting completed work, persist new effects once, return or visibly hold results for the correct conversation through ordinary admission, and finish only through a qualified lead completion request.

#### 6. Integrate enabled routing, explicit bypass, disabled allocation, and fallback

**Task ID:** `T6`  
**Depends on:** `T4`, `T5`  
**Prerequisites:** T4’s deterministic routing outcome and T5’s scheduler/inbox integration.  
**Files and symbols:** Edit `src/standalone/service.ts` options/startup/`wakeScheduler` to construct and invoke `RoutingCoordinator`; minimally extend `src/core/domain.ts:recordRouting`, lead binding/assignment helpers, and internal credential-reference access for atomic final dispositions and exact destinations. Extend `src/core/coordination.ts` with routing-fallback inbox reconciliation. Extend `test/routing.test.ts`, `test/domain.test.ts`, and `test/s04b-integration.test.ts`.  
**Test:** Add red service tests for: routing-enabled eligible task with no assignment calls the fake client without a lead turn and creates one assignment; an existing explicit permitted assignment makes zero calls; disabled routing creates the lead assignment and makes zero calls; missing credential, no candidates/context, explicit `lead_review`, API exhaustion, and malformed response create one lead binding plus one durable fallback event containing the brief and bounded evidence. Verify duplicate wakes/restart/delayed responses create neither competing assignments nor duplicate lead wakeups. Race the response against task/brief revision, project opt-out/pause, Stop, candidate removal/revocation, and dependency/hold changes; assert stale disposition and no dispatch. Fill capacity before a valid choice and assert the selected profile remains on the queued assignment rather than being substituted. Reopen a completed result and request repair; assert routing is not called and the original profile remains.  
**Implementation:** For tasks with no assignment, branch in this order: preserve an existing explicit assignment; if routing is disabled, ensure the task lead assignment; if enabled but unavailable or incomplete, commit the single fallback; otherwise claim/resume the persisted logical routing operation and call T4. Resolve the configured `env:NAME` reference only inside the production routing adapter and never expose its name/value through public DTOs or prompts. On a valid response, call the existing atomic routing transaction with captured task/routing/candidate revisions and an exact lead assignment destination. On fallback, persist the routing disposition and deterministic fallback event; startup reconciliation ensures a disposition committed before an event cannot lose the wakeup. Every assignment still enters the normal scheduler and current admission checks.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/routing.test.js dist/test/s04b-integration.test.js`; expect all enabled/disabled/bypass/fallback, stale-race, restart, no-duplicate, queued-selected-profile, and retained-repair cases to pass with the fake client’s network-call count matching expectations.  
**Complete when:** Each eligible unassigned task takes exactly one of explicit bypass, disabled lead allocation, validated direct routing, or single lead fallback, and only current permitted assignments reach scheduler admission.

#### 7. Expose the UI-neutral seam and an isolated integrated local test view

**Task ID:** `T7`  
**Depends on:** `T6`  
**Prerequisites:** Final S04b persistence and routing dispositions from T2–T6.  
**Files and symbols:** Create `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts` with `CoordinationView`, task history/result/unresolved-recipient/message/attention/routing DTOs, and validated operator command methods. Create `test/coordination-view.test.ts` and `test/s04b/local-view.mjs`; add package script `s04b:view`. Add a narrow `StandaloneService.coordinationView()` accessor in `src/standalone/service.ts`. Do not edit `src/standalone/operator.ts`.  
**Test:** Add red tests that create two projects/tasks and assert every read and command is scoped to the requested task. Reopen SQLite and verify conversation/work history, retained and unresolved-recipient results, pending/delivered messages, questions, approvals, completion/fallback attention, and routing provenance survive. Execute operator-message, result-recipient reconciliation, question-answer, and approval-decision commands with command keys and expected revisions; assert exact replay, changed-payload conflict, stale-version rejection, one recipient event, and no direct turn steering. Serialize every DTO and assert it contains no credential reference/value, App Server raw payload, unrestricted transcript, or other project’s records. Run the test-only loopback view in smoke mode against a disposable integrated service/database and fetch it from its ephemeral `127.0.0.1` URL; assert rendered sections for task identity, histories, results/unresolved holds, messages, questions/approvals, routing disposition, and attention, with no mutation route or non-loopback listener.  
**Implementation:** Build read DTOs from `DomainStore`, `CoordinationStore`, `ExecutionState`, and routing provenance rather than exposing table rows. Delegate mutations to T2/T3’s validated commands with actor `operator`; do not duplicate business rules. Return confirmed command disposition and resulting revision/event identity. Keep the production facade free of request/session/origin logic. Implement `test/s04b/local-view.mjs` as an explicitly non-production, read-only harness that creates a disposable service/database, binds Node’s HTTP server only to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port, renders the integrated facade, supports `--smoke`, and tears down all local state. It must not be imported by production code or add a route/shared asset to `operator.ts`, leaving #703 and #694 free to mount the seam.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/coordination-view.test.js`, then `npm run s04b:view -- --smoke`; expect scoped durable reads, idempotent/stale-safe commands, secret exclusion, no-live-steering assertions, loopback-only binding, all required local test-view sections, and clean disposable-state teardown.  
**Complete when:** S04b has a typed secret-safe coordination boundary and a working isolated integrated local test view, while the production shared operator/auth surface remains unmodified.

#### 8. Qualify one bounded real Codex coordination journey and document limits

**Task ID:** `T8`  
**Depends on:** `T1`, `T2`, `T3`, `T4`, `T5`, `T6`, `T7`  
**Prerequisites:** All deterministic suites and the local test-view smoke pass; existing operator Codex login is available. TypeSafe remains fake/disabled. Resumed-conversation dynamic-tool availability remains unproved until this slice observes it.  
**Files and symbols:** Create `test/s04b/live-runtime.mjs` and package script `s04b:live`. Create `docs/evidence/s04b-live-runtime-2026-09-29.md` and `docs/design/s04b-coordination-boundary.md`. Update implemented-versus-planned status in `README.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, and `docs/design/standalone.md` without changing accepted contracts.  
**Test:** The live harness creates a fresh temporary standalone data directory and disposable task workspace, configures explicit lead/worker profiles so routing bypasses TypeSafe, and sets capacity one. A real task-scoped Codex lead calls `ensemble_delegate`; the worker calls `ensemble_report_result`; then restart the service/App Server before delivery. Resume the same lead conversation for the durable result continuation and require that resumed turn to call `ensemble_request_follow_up`; assert the callback arrives with the original thread ID, a new bound turn ID, a call ID, and the registered tool name. The same worker reports the revision and the resumed lead requests completion. This explicitly proves—or fails to prove—dynamic-tool availability after `thread/resume`; a mere successful resume or stored history is insufficient. Record sanitized thread/turn/call/work/result/event IDs, revisions, terminal states, callback counts, scheduler transitions, final task state, Node/npm/Codex identities, and explicit pass/fail/unproved rows.  
**Implementation:** Make the harness bounded, fail-fast, and self-cleaning: stop the service/App Server, close SQLite, remove disposable data/workspaces, and leave no background process. Do not inspect/change shared login/configuration and do not call TypeSafe. If stored Codex threads have no supported deletion API, retain only those provider records and disclose that cleanup limit. Document the initial-thread and resumed-thread dynamic-tool observations separately, including a failed/unproved resumed result if the callback is not observed. Also document that TypeSafe live quality/cost remains unproved until S05 authorization, the integrated loopback view is test-only, operator authentication/shared UI remain #703, final UI/runtime assembly remains #694, and cooperative handoff retains its accepted incomplete-observation/detached-writer limits.  
**Validate:** From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check`, then `npm run s04b:view -- --smoke`, `npm run s04b:live`, and `git diff --check`; expect the deterministic suite and isolated local view to pass, the bounded real journey to observe a registered coordination callback on a resumed conversation and end with one completed task and no duplicate tool/result/event/turn identities, cleanup checks to find no surviving local process or disposable workspace, and the diff whitespace check to be clean.  
**Complete when:** Deterministic coverage and the isolated local test view are green, one actual Codex delegation/result/follow-up/completion flow proves dynamic tools on the resumed task conversation, no paid inference occurred, and the repository truthfully distinguishes implemented S04b behavior from #694/#695/#703 work.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Registered App Server coordination callbacks carry trusted outer identity, reply once, replay exact post-terminal receipts before liveness checks, and do not weaken approval denial | 1, 5, 8 | `codex-runtime.test`, service-level post-terminal duplicate fixture, bounded live trace |
| Registered coordination tools remain callable after real service/App Server restart and `thread/resume` | 8 | Bounded live resumed-conversation callback assertion |
| Current results are retained, deduplicated, atomically paired with exact recipient events or durably held for recipient reconciliation, and isolated across task-scoped lead histories | 2, 5, 7 | `coordination.test`, `s04b-integration.test`, local view unresolved-result section |
| Multiple results coalesce without live steering or lost wakeups, including restart and capacity one | 2, 5 | High-water/reopen fixture and capacity-one integration journey |
| Scoped assignees can delegate; initial results return to lead and nested results to requester | 3, 5, 8 | Coordination authority tests, integrated and live nested flow |
| Repairs retain assignee; stale follow-ups/results fail; reassignment is not implicit | 3, 6, 8 | Follow-up revision tests and routing-call-count assertion |
| Questions, answers, approvals, and operator messages are durable, exact-revision-bound, idempotent, and admission-safe | 3, 5, 7 | Interaction tests, service restart tests, coordination facade tests |
| Worker success cannot complete a task; a current lead request passes only after all completion gates | 3, 5, 8 | Completion negative matrix and live finalization |
| Enabled routing uses bounded brief/findings/capabilities/guidance; explicit assignment bypasses it; disabled routing uses lead | 4, 6 | Fake-client payload and service branch tests |
| Missing/no-fit/uncertain/API-failure routing wakes the lead once; stale responses never dispatch | 4, 6 | Retry/restart/race/fallback integration matrix |
| Busy selected work queues without substitution, and inference retries never consume/reset execution retries | 4, 6 | Persisted attempt-budget and capacity-held assignment tests |
| S04b provides a task-scoped, secret-safe facade and an integrated loopback-only local test view without changing #703’s auth/shared UI files | 7 | `coordination-view.test`, `s04b:view -- --smoke`, plus unchanged `operator.ts` review |
| One actual Codex coordination flow is demonstrated without TypeSafe spend, deployment, or cutover | 8 | `npm run s04b:live` evidence report and cleanup assertions |

### Final validation

- From `/Users/chris/dev/ensemble`, using Node from `.node-version` and npm pinned by `package.json`, run `npm ci`; expect an exact lockfile install including `@typesafe-ai/sdk@0.6.0`.
- Run `npm run check`; expect type checking, lint, formatting check, build, and every deterministic SQLite/fake-runtime/fake-routing test to pass.
- Run `npm run s04b:view -- --smoke`; expect the integrated read-only test view to bind only an ephemeral loopback port, render all S04b sections from a disposable service/database, and clean up.
- Run `npm run s04b:live`; expect one bounded real Codex lead/worker journey, an observed coordination-tool callback after restart and `thread/resume`, no TypeSafe request, one final completed task, and successful disposable-process/workspace cleanup.
- Run `git diff --check`; expect no whitespace errors.
- Compare final behavior with issue #693, R05 and R07–R10, and the A06/A09/A14–A18/A25/A26/A27 boundary rows; record every live row as passed, failed, or unproved rather than inferring a pass from terminal prose.

### Review focus

- Check that exact callback receipt lookup/replay happens before current-generation rejection and before `registerExecutionCallback`, so a post-terminal duplicate cannot create a late-callback hold; every unseen callback must still prove a current exact binding and genuinely new late callbacks retain the conservative hold.
- Check that missing, legacy, cross-task, or ambiguous result destinations retain the current result under one visible reconciliation hold and cannot guess-deliver, disappear, or permit task completion.
- Check every result, fallback, interaction response, and operator message transaction for “effect committed but wakeup lost” and “duplicate wakeup creates duplicate turn” crash points.
- Check completion finalization and follow-up scheduling against Stop, pause, newer revisions, unfinished callbacks, writer holds, and task-scoped lead identity.
- Check TypeSafe state and all view DTOs for credential, transcript, cross-project, or ambient runtime leakage.
- Confirm the implementation leaves `src/standalone/operator.ts` and #703’s shared auth/UI surface untouched.

### Re-plan triggers

- Stop if the installed App Server no longer supports `thread/start.dynamicTools` plus identity-bearing `item/tool/call` with the qualified response shape, or if the bounded live journey cannot make a registered coordination tool available on the resumed task conversation and no supported re-registration mechanism preserves that conversation; do not replace either proof with transcript inference or an untrusted payload identity.
- Stop if satisfying #693 requires modifying #703’s authentication/shared UI contract, enabling paid TypeSafe access, changing deployment/cutover/shared Codex configuration, or weakening the current admission/runtime trust contracts.

Semantic digest:

- **Baseline:** clean `origin/main@8fdf0d8`; final merged CI passed 127/127.
- **Parallel roots:** T1 runtime callbacks, T2 durable results/inboxes, and T4 deterministic routing.
- **Authority:** only current bound thread/turn/assignment/work revision; payload IDs never confer permission.
- **Durability:** every current result is retained as atomic result+event or a durable unresolved-recipient hold; exact receipts replay before liveness/callback registration; high-water continuation batching and revision-bound interactions/completion survive restart.
- **Routing:** direct TypeSafe Choice over eligible profile IDs plus `lead_review`; two persisted Ensemble attempts; no threshold and no paid validation.
- **Integration:** T5 owns coordination/scheduler wiring; T6 serially adds routing to `StandaloneService`.
- **UI boundary:** T7 adds a typed facade plus an isolated read-only loopback test view; `operator.ts`, auth, shared HTML/routes, deployment, and cutover stay untouched.
- **Evidence:** T8 runs one disposable real Codex delegation/result/follow-up/completion journey with fake/disabled TypeSafe and must observe a registered coordination callback after real restart and `thread/resume`; this resumed-tool surface is currently unproved.

## Independent plan audit

**Verdict:** `ship`

Reviewed revision 2 at https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/693#issuecomment-5900357230 against the issue, repository contracts, current code, and S01 callback evidence on `origin/main@8fdf0d80798419248995ac182336fbc08f92d642`.

The four revision-1 findings are resolved: unresolved recipients retain results for reconciliation; exact stored callback receipts replay before current-generation rejection; the minimal integrated test view is isolated from #703’s shared operator/auth surface; and the unsupported repair-cycle cap is removed.

Implementation must preserve stored-identity validation during receipt replay. The bounded live gate must observe dynamic-tool availability after restart and `thread/resume`; failure there triggers re-planning rather than an inferred pass.
