content.title: Report unexpected background service failures with redacted context

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Report unexpected service background failures and stop unsafe admission.

**Current behavior and verification:**
A real production service with SQLite and a fake runtime was started. The registered GitHub interval callback was invoked with refreshGitHub replaced by a rejecting seam: one injected failure produced no console.error/warn diagnostics; SQLite remained open and the scheduler kept running. Static inspection shows the same discarded-rejection pattern at power polling and domain wake callbacks. Only the GitHub timer was dynamically exercised. Cleanup-only catches and already-recorded expected failures are distinct and must not be indiscriminately rewritten.

**Desired behavior:**
Use a small common policy at existing background entry points. Expected provider failures already represented by durable holds retain that behavior without duplicate reporting. Unexpected failures receive a bounded diagnostic with an allowlisted operation identity and safe correlation IDs. For unknown integrity/storage/programming failures, stop new admission and initiate observable safe shutdown; retain all unresolved execution/effect holds. Reporter failure must not create an unhandled rejection or prevent admission from stopping.

**Key interfaces:**
- StandaloneService background GitHub/power polling and domain/post-turn wake callbacks.
- TurnScheduler timer/drain error ownership, coordinated with #785 without duplicating ownership.
- Existing service diagnostics and stop lifecycle; preserve sensitive runtime stderr draining.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Inject failures at GitHub polling, power polling and domain wake; verify diagnostics and the selected recoverable/fatal lifecycle outcome.
- [ ] Known expected failures keep their recorded hold behavior without redundant reports.
- [ ] Unknown integrity failures prevent new admission and invoke safe shutdown; unresolved execution remains held, including if shutdown itself fails.
- [ ] Use operation/error codes and allowlisted IDs; test synthetic credentials, private instructions and control paths to prove raw error payloads are not leaked.
- [ ] Reporter failures are handled with a bounded safe fallback and no unhandled rejection, recursive reporting or lost shutdown action.
- [ ] Retain diagnostic-free cleanup catches only where another explicit owner already accounts for the failure.

**Out of scope:**
- New external telemetry infrastructure, wholesale logging changes or logging raw runtime stderr. Do not silently turn storage/programming failures into normal retries.

**Validation and boundaries:**
Recheck current main before implementing. Add deterministic regression coverage using production classes, then run `npm ci` and `npm run check` on the pinned Node/npm versions. Triage used Node 24.21.0, npm 12.2.0, installed dependencies and compiled service code at `68275037979982c92d726983a4f48ce71482384e` on 6 October 2026. Temporary probes called production classes through controlled internal seams; the full suite, HTTP integration and live Codex were not run. This brief specifies the fix, not completed implementation.

Preserve durable ownership, uncertainty, cancellation and recovery contracts. No automatic release of holds, production deployment, installed Haze prototype changes, paid/model calls or reopening deferred X01–X05. Priority order in #784 does not create blocking dependencies or dispatch authority.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/789
**Planned against:** `main` at `24168ed399514b538bebc1e9b3471f09d1abac62`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Give the existing unattended service entry points one small, safe failure policy. Expected provider failures continue through their existing durable source/power holds. An exception escaping a background GitHub or power poll, domain wake, post-turn wake, or the scheduler's internally owned drain observer is an unexpected service failure: emit a redacted, correlated diagnostic once for that service generation, synchronously close new admission, then start the existing failure-preserving `stop()` sequence without awaiting it from the failing callback. Surface the fatal signal to the CLI so `serve` and `operator` finish their wait, close the operator listener, and exit unsuccessfully. Keep unresolved execution/effect holds and make diagnostic or shutdown failure observable without raw error payloads.

### Guardrails

- Preserve the GitHub source/dependency unknown-state holds, power-event reconciliation gate, scheduler request identity, runtime Stop/writer/capacity holds, and #788's workspace uncertainty/archival holds. A fatal diagnostic or shutdown is not a recovery receipt and never clears them. No automatic retry of an unknown storage/programming failure.
- Keep raw exceptions, causes, stacks, provider responses, credentials, private instructions, prompts, control paths and arbitrary IDs out of service diagnostics. Continue `CodexRuntime`'s sensitive stderr drain in `src/standalone/codex.ts`; do not log or retain that stream.
- Keep scope to service diagnostics and CLI teardown. No external telemetry, broad logging rewrite, live Codex/model calls, deployment, installed Haze changes, or deferred X01–X05. Leave cleanup-only catches and failures already durably represented by a hold with their current owners unless a focused test proves an unowned exception.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- Define fixed operation codes (`github-poll`, `power-poll`, `domain-wake`, `post-turn-wake`, `scheduler-drain`, `safe-shutdown`) and fixed error codes (`unexpected-background-failure`, `shutdown-failed`, `diagnostic-writer-failed`). Correlate with a service-generated UUID and bounded integer incident sequence; generate/capture the identity per successful start attempt, rather than accepting external IDs or printing `String(error)`. The first unexpected failure latches that generation and stops admission; further callbacks in that generation cannot start another shutdown or flood duplicate reports. An explicit direct `refreshGitHub()`/`wakeScheduler()` caller still receives its own rejection; this policy owns only unattended invocations.
- Treat an error as expected only when its existing subsystem converted it to a durable/visible state: `GitHubSynchronizer.perform()` records incomplete reader/blocker/status observations; `ExecutionPower.pollUnlocked()` holds admission for unavailable/incomplete power history and `reconcileSafely()` retains the hold on reconciliation failure. Do not match arbitrary exception messages or turn every rejected reader into a fatal error. A thrown storage/programming error that escapes these boundaries is fatal. Preserve #785's `TurnScheduler` observer and supply the service handler at construction; do not add a second catch to scheduler internals or duplicate direct-caller reports.
- Set a generation-scoped fatal admission latch before any diagnostic or asynchronous cleanup. Stop the scheduler and clear both poll timers synchronously, and test the latch after `attemptRequest()`'s asynchronous workspace/process-identity steps immediately before `ExecutionState.begin()`; `wakeScheduler()` and the direct dispatch path must also honor it. The last check and synchronous `begin()` have no interleaving point. Initiate `stop()` from a detached, immediately observed task outside the rejected callback/drain's await chain; coalesce a concurrent CLI/user stop with that in-flight stop so it cannot run cleanup twice. Do not await a drain from inside its own failure observer.
- Make the diagnostic sink bounded and non-authoritative. Production writes only the fixed allowlisted event to service stderr. A narrow test-only sink may throw, reject, or never settle: attach rejection handling immediately and use one short finite deadline, then attempt a static, direct stderr fallback once. Neither sink failure nor fallback failure recurses, rejects an unattended promise, or delays the fatal admission latch and shutdown. A failed `stop()` gets one separate `safe-shutdown` diagnostic and remains an unsuccessful fatal outcome; keep the already closed admission gate even when a shutdown stage fails.
- Expose a one-shot fatal notification from `StandaloneService` that is visible even if it fired before the CLI begins waiting. Capture the generation in registered timers, domain notification and post-turn continuations so a late result from an old service generation cannot shut down or wake a restarted instance. In `cli.ts`, race the signal waits in both `serve` and `operator` against this notification, await the coalesced shutdown, close the operator HTTP listener, and set a nonzero exit status. Preserve normal signal-driven shutdown and bounded `run`/`list` behavior. The CLI must not stay alive with an open operator listener after service teardown.
- #788 owns `service.ts`, `workspaces.ts`, `state.ts` and changes cancellation-before-settlement, held workspace state, and typed expected Git failures. Do not implement #789 in a shared checkout until #788 merges. On the merged head, screen its service stop/start/attempt paths and incorporate its sticky manager cancellation and settlement before DB close. #787's merged auth change (`588af417af49b445799643f13b17dee2997d09b0`) has no production overlap with these paths; rerun affected integration checks after incorporating it.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `StandaloneService.start()` installs the domain notification, power and GitHub intervals, and `TurnScheduler`; the first four callbacks currently discard rejected promises. `registerExecutionCallback()`'s `.finally()` wake also discards rejection. `attemptRequest()` awaits workspace validation and runtime process identity before the synchronous `ExecutionState.begin()` admission. `stop()` already stops the scheduler and timers first, then attempts independent cleanup and preserves errors; #788 will add workspace cancellation/settlement.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` — #785 already owns replacement/timer drain rejections through the optional `onBackgroundFailure` constructor observer. The service currently uses its fixed stderr default, without service lifecycle action. No scheduler source edit is planned.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/github-sync.ts` — expected reader failures become incomplete source/blocker/status observations; reconciliation/storage errors can escape `refresh()`. `src/standalone/power.ts` — expected history failures hold power admission, while state/poll errors can escape `poll()`; `ExecutionPower.stop()` waits for polling. `src/standalone/codex.ts` — the runtime resumes stderr without logging it.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/cli.ts` — `serve` and `operator` wait only for SIGINT/SIGTERM; the operator listener is closed in the latter branch's `finally`, and the outer `finally` stops the service. A service-only stop otherwise leaves the CLI/listener alive.
- **Existing:** `test/github-service.test.ts`, `test/power-service.test.ts`, `test/scheduler-drain.test.ts`, `test/standalone.test.ts`, and `test/codex-runtime.test.ts` provide production-class real SQLite/fake runtime, source/power hold, strict scheduler rejection, shutdown and sensitive-stderr fixtures. Keep the new end-to-end failure matrix in `test/background-service.test.ts` (or an equivalent single focused file) using controlled instances and short, bounded waits.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 → T2 → T3` is acyclic. T1 and T2 both change `service.ts`; T2 consumes T1's fatal signal, and T3 verifies their integrated CLI behavior. Keep them serial in one implementation owner. The whole chain waits for #788 to merge because `service.ts` and stop/settlement ordering overlap; independent read-only plan/review work may proceed now. No concurrent source writers.

#### 1. Own unexpected service background failures and stop admission

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Before editing, integrate/screen merged #788 against this fixed-base plan; verify the service stops workspace Git before awaiting scheduler settlement and retains unknown Git holds. Confirm #785 observer remains present and #787 auth delta is compatible. Use pinned Node 24.21.0/npm 12.2.0 and run `npm ci` in the implementation checkout.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `StandaloneService.start`, `stop`, `wakeScheduler`, `attemptRequest`, `registerExecutionCallback`, the GitHub/power interval callbacks, and a private generation-scoped background-failure handler/diagnostic writer; `test/background-service.test.ts` — production-service real-SQLite/fake-runtime injections. No `scheduler.ts`, `state.ts`, `power.ts`, `github-sync.ts`, or `codex.ts` change unless a verified merged-contract defect requires it.
**Test:** On a started production service with real temporary SQLite and a fake runtime, invoke each registered GitHub/power timer deterministically and trigger a domain change notification plus post-turn wake. For each, inject one storage/programming rejection at the appropriate production instance seam after setup. Assert exactly one allowlisted operation/error diagnostic with generated generation/incident IDs, immediate refusal of a queued or direct new turn before `state.begin`, a single initiated `stop()`, and no unhandled rejection under strict Node mode. Gate `runtime.processIdentity()` while the fatal callback fires, then release it and assert zero new turn starts. Repeat with the `TurnScheduler` internally owned failure observer after a replacement/timer drain failure: one service fatal report, no competing scheduler report, and direct `wake()` callers still own their rejection. In separate expected-failure cases, make the GitHub reader reject and the power history reader reject; inspect durable incomplete-source/power-hold state and assert no fatal diagnostic/stop or duplicate report. Inject a held execution and a shutdown-stage failure; verify stop still attempts subsequent safe stages, no new admission, and the hold remains after reopen. Give the diagnostic sink an error/rejected promise/never-settling promise carrying synthetic credential, private instruction and control path strings; assert a bounded fixed fallback, no raw substring in stderr or captured events, no recursion/unhandled rejection, and no lost stop. Retain `test/codex-runtime.test.ts`'s large-stderr drain regression.
**Implementation:** Add the fixed-code diagnostic shape and finite sink fallback locally to service diagnostics. Install one handler for unattended GitHub/power/domain/post-turn callbacks and pass it as #785's scheduler observer. Check generation and fatal latch before reporting; latch and synchronously block admission first, then start one observed, coalesced stop outside the failing callback's await chain. Prevent a late callback from a prior start from affecting the next start. Keep original errors internal to the failure boundary and preserve downstream expected-hold behavior.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --unhandled-rejections=strict --test dist/test/background-service.test.js dist/test/scheduler-drain.test.js dist/test/github-service.test.js dist/test/power-service.test.js`; expect the fatal/expected matrix, no unhandled rejection, and existing hold behavior to pass. Run the existing stderr-drain case in the final full check.
**Complete when:** All existing unattended service entry points have one guarded policy owner, unexpected failure stops new admission even when reporting/stop fails, and known held provider failures retain their prior owner.

#### 2. Close the CLI on a fatal service signal

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's strict-mode failure matrix passes; use the exact one-shot generation signal and coalesced stop promise established there.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — read-only fatal signal/stop outcome accessor if not finished in T1; `src/standalone/cli.ts` — `serve` and `operator` wait/teardown branches; `test/background-service.test.ts` — lifecycle integration fixture.
**Test:** Drive the service's fatal signal after each CLI wait is installed and also before it begins waiting; verify both observations complete. Use the same narrow signal-wait code in both CLI branches and exercise it with a production service and operator HTTP fixture: trigger the injected fatal GitHub timer, then assert the listener closes, the service database/owner settles (or the exact failed stop stage remains observable), exit status is nonzero, and the old service admits no new turn. Reopen with a fresh service to inspect retained holds; do not infer that a former generation's process-local latch quarantines a new process. Race SIGTERM with fatal notification and assert one coalesced service shutdown and one listener close. Preserve ordinary SIGTERM exit success and no premature teardown while the service is healthy. Test `run`/`list` remain bounded under their existing `finally` path; no new polling loop is introduced.
**Implementation:** Race the existing signal wait against the one-shot service fatal notification in both long-lived CLI modes. Use the existing `finally` cleanup, joining rather than duplicating the fatal stop. Preserve static failure diagnostics and set `process.exitCode` for the fatal path; do not log exception objects or untrusted data. Keep listener stop and auth close attempted even if service stop reports failure.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout after T1, run `npm run build:service && node --unhandled-rejections=strict --test dist/test/background-service.test.js dist/test/standalone.test.js dist/test/operator-http.test.js`; expect normal/fatal CLI lifecycle and existing service/operator shutdown cases to pass.
**Complete when:** A fatal background failure ends `serve` and `operator` unattended waits, closes the operator listener and exits unsuccessfully without a second stop race.

#### 3. Reconcile integration and run complete validation

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T1/T2 focused checks pass on the head containing #788 and #787.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/service.ts`, `src/standalone/cli.ts`, `test/background-service.test.ts`; update `docs/SPEC.md` or `README.md` only if the final implementation creates a user-visible lifecycle contract absent from the issue, and keep implemented-versus-planned wording accurate.
**Test:** Reopen the real SQLite fixture after a fatal failure and confirm unresolved execution/workspace holds survive; inspect the stopped generation, CLI failure result, and a clean normal signal path. Verify an old interval/domain/post-turn continuation cannot affect a restarted generation. Audit emitted stderr and captured diagnostic events against the synthetic secret/path cases and check the existing `CodexRuntime` stderr-drain test.
**Implementation:** Review the merged #788 stop sequencing, #785 observer, #787 auth/CLI delta and the final diff for silent catches, duplicate diagnostics, report recursion, admission races, false hold release, accidental raw error serialization, and listener/resource leaks. Make only compatible fixture or integration repairs under the stated budget.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout, with pinned Node 24.21.0/npm 12.2.0, run `npm ci` then `npm run check`; expect typecheck, lint, formatting, build and full tests to pass. Check `git diff --check` and `git status --short` for intended files only. Independently review the integrated candidate before handback.
**Complete when:** Full check passes on the integrated head and failure/hold/CLI readback supports every acceptance row without a raw-payload leak or an unresolved shutdown owner.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Shared policy reports unexpected GitHub/power/domain/post-turn and internally owned scheduler failures with safe operation/correlation IDs | 1 | Production-service callback matrix and #785 observer injection under strict rejection mode |
| Known provider failures keep their recorded holds without a second fatal report | 1 | GitHub incomplete-source and power-history hold/readback cases |
| Unknown integrity failures stop new admission and start safe shutdown, even across in-flight admission or shutdown failure | 1–3 | Gated process-identity race, failed-stop/reopen hold inspection, CLI fatal completion |
| Reporter throw/rejection/hang has a bounded redacted fallback, no recursion or unhandled rejection, and cannot suppress stop | 1 | Synthetic sensitive payload and sink-failure matrix plus strict-mode test |
| Sensitive runtime stderr continues to drain without logging raw content | 1, 3 | Existing `codex-runtime.test.ts` large-stderr regression and final diff audit |
| `serve` and `operator` close on fatal service failure; normal signal shutdown remains sound | 2–3 | Fatal-before/after-wait, operator-listener close and SIGTERM race tests |

### Final validation

- From the implementation checkout on the integrated head, use `.node-version` Node 24.21.0 and `packageManager` npm 12.2.0; run `npm ci` then `npm run check`. Record final SHA, focused strict-mode command/results, and real SQLite hold and CLI teardown readback. No live Codex or external telemetry is needed for this bounded issue.
- Planning baseline is clean fixed `main` at `24168ed399514b538bebc1e9b3471f09d1abac62`; its dependencies were absent in the read-only planning checkout, so no local focused tests were run here. Existing #785/#786 plans record a prior green CI run on earlier `5e98b7690d63b5c1076e926e13cf37ff7e82079b`; the implementation must establish green results on its actual integrated head.

### Review focus

- Ensure the fatal gate is in force before diagnostics or any await and is rechecked immediately before `ExecutionState.begin()`; an old generation cannot stop a new instance. Verify the background handler cannot await its own drain/poll callback, `stop()` is coalesced, and a failed stop never silently restores admission.
- Check diagnostic values are only fixed codes and service-generated correlation IDs; promises from the sink and shutdown are immediately observed. Verify #788's workspace cancellation/hold behavior remains intact and CLI operator listener teardown occurs for fatal failures as well as signals.

### Re-plan triggers

- Merged #788 changes the stop/settlement boundary so a background fatal cannot safely join it; a required guarantee needs a new durable global quarantine or public recovery authority; or implementing CLI fatal teardown requires a new process supervision/deployment policy. Return the concrete evidence and proposed contract change before expanding scope.

content.title: Bound runtime history retention while preserving late-conflict detection

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Triage Notes and retention proposal

**Category:** bug
**State:** needs-triage — implementation waits for the retention direction below.

### Established evidence

At current main `68275037979982c92d726983a4f48ce71482384e`, the production CodexRuntime parser and waitForTurn were exercised on Node 24.21.0 with 10,000 synthetic completed turns, consuming each terminal. terminalHistory retained all 10,000 entries; injecting a failed report for turn-0 then produced one terminal anomaly. This confirms both accumulation and the safety role of retained history.

The single run took approximately 34 ms and reported a 4,112,856-byte heap increase with uncontrolled GC. These are workload observations, not a steady-state leak estimate or production latency benchmark. The longevity probe did not create native questions, start a real App Server, or exercise restart.

Static inspection also found nativeEndpoints retained until runtime start, full-history scans in cancelNativeTurn and native replay lookup, and terminalHistory without a matching retirement/clear path. Native readbacks/settings, invalid-turn identities, failure evidence and thread tools need explicit lifecycle classification. Existing bounded conversation capture is a separate concern and should not be replaced.

Redundancy checks covered terminal receipt/consumption, runtime start/stop, native request/reply/cancel paths, service terminal-anomaly handling and durable execution state. No complete retirement mechanism was found. There is no .out-of-scope rejection registry.

### Recommended design, pending decision

Use **durable compact safety records plus bounded in-memory caches and active indexes**. Preserve the existing late-conflict/replay contract rather than introduce an age cutoff.

1. **Separate active work from historical evidence.** Keep callable endpoints and pending RPC/turn/callback state only while they are operationally needed. Index live native endpoints by exact turn and typed request identity so cancellation and replay matching do not scan settled history. Unresolved execution/effect authority remains durable and protected; retiring a payload does not resolve it.
2. **Reuse durable facts before adding storage.** Inventory ExecutionState and native reply/interaction records against each runtime decision. Add only the missing exact-identity/status/digest evidence and indexed lookup necessary to reproduce the current decisions after a cache miss. A terminal lookup must remain attributable to its execution binding and detect conflicts across relevant runtime restarts; adding a generation key must not accidentally hide a conflict for the same bound turn.
3. **Persist before retirement or dependent authority.** Preserve observed terminal status/conflict evidence before retiring it or permitting a decision that depends on it. Keep native reply intent, request identity (including typed RPC ID and runtime generation), input digest and final/uncertain disposition durably attributable. Reuse the existing before-write intent boundary; do not create a parallel reply authority.
4. **Bound caches by count/bytes, never by safety lifetime.** Retire settled payloads after dependent callbacks/reply processing end and required evidence is durable. Cache misses use indexed authoritative lookup without loading all history at startup. Thread configuration/tool snapshots remain reproducible for any binding that can resume. Numeric cache budgets are measured implementation choices within this invariant.
5. **Fail conservatively.** A missing/corrupt/unreadable authoritative record is not evidence of a fresh request, successful completion or permission to reply again. Preserve uncertainty and stop the affected decision. On a late conflicting terminal, invoke existing anomaly/retraction handling even after cache eviction. Old-child filtering and exact generation checks still apply.
6. **No disk pruning in this slice.** Existing durable history may continue growing; this issue bounds in-memory settled history and avoids repeated full-history scans. Any future durable deletion policy is a separate decision because it can change the evidence available for late conflict/replay handling.

A pure age-based eviction or bounded in-memory tombstone set is insufficient: once the last identity/status evidence disappears, the demonstrated turn-0 conflict can no longer be distinguished. A compact but unbounded map reduces payload cost without satisfying bounded settled memory.

### Acceptance for the proposed direction

- Settle substantially more turns and native questions than the configured cache budgets; report each retained collection, bytes where measurable, and lookup/cancellation timings under a stated workload.
- Evict a settled turn, then deliver an identical and conflicting terminal: preserve the normal duplicate semantics and late-conflict hold/retraction behavior.
- Replay a retired native request unchanged, with changed input, with a reused typed ID and with an old runtime generation; never expose a duplicate answer opportunity or write a duplicate reply.
- Verify active callbacks, writing/sent-unconfirmed replies and uncertain execution across eviction, stop, start and restart.
- Inject persistence/lookup failure and prove retirement cannot erase required authority or release holds.
- Preserve current native protocol qualification and conversation-capture behavior. Use deterministic fixtures; no paid/model calls are required for retention coverage.
- Record the accepted invariant in the domain/design documentation before implementation, then run pinned npm ci and npm run check for the implementation.

### Decision requested from @chrisbanes

Accept the durable compact-record / bounded-cache direction, with no time-based weakening of late-conflict or replay detection and no new disk-pruning policy? If accepted, finish the exact durable-field/interface inventory and convert this to an agent brief. This comment is a proposal, not an accepted ADR, implementation dispatch or new release gate.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief — approved retention direction

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Bound settled runtime history in memory while preserving durable late-conflict and replay evidence.

**Decision:** Chris approved keeping compact safety history on disk, using bounded memory caches and active indexes, preserving unresolved holds, and excluding disk-history deletion. This accepts the direction in the [retention proposal](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/790#issuecomment-6017106739). Numeric limits and storage details are implementation choices. This is triage readiness, not implementation dispatch.

**Current behavior and evidence:** The earlier production-parser probe on Node 24.21.0 at revision 68275037979982c92d726983a4f48ce71482384e retained 10,000 terminalHistory entries after consuming 10,000 synthetic terminals; a conflicting report for the first turn still raised an anomaly. Native endpoints also retain payloads, with cancellation and replay paths scanning accumulated entries. That probe did not qualify native-question longevity, restart, live Codex or the full suite. Recheck current main.

**Desired behavior:** Durable exact-identity evidence remains authoritative after cache eviction. Keep operationally needed active state in memory, retire settled payloads only after required persistence and callback/reply completion, and use indexed lookups on cache misses. Storage failures or missing expected evidence retain uncertainty. A cache miss must never itself authorize a new request, duplicate reply or ownership release.

**Key interfaces and evidence inventory:**
- CodexRuntime terminal receipt/waitForTurn/onTerminalAnomaly: preserve bound thread/turn identity, observed terminal status and conflicting-status evidence. Runtime generation checks must reject old-child events without hiding a conflict for the same bound execution across applicable restarts.
- ExecutionState and the service anomaly/retraction path: reuse durable execution bindings and outcomes; add only missing evidence/indexes. A retired turn must still identify affected work and successors.
- NativeEndpoint, native readbacks, replyUserInput and CoordinationStore native reply intent/outcome records: preserve runtime generation, thread/turn/item identity, typed RPC request ID, input digest, replay state, reply intent and confirmed/unavailable/uncertain disposition. Reuse the existing persisted before-write boundary.
- Active native request indexes: direct exact-turn/request lookups replace scans of all settled endpoints.
- Thread tools/settings and failure evidence: classify operational lifetime and preserve/reconstruct exact facts needed by resumable bindings; do not silently substitute changed current configuration.
- Runtime start/stop: load only needed records and bounded caches, preserve durable safety history, and retain existing recovery and old-child filtering.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Persist required safety evidence before retiring its only in-memory copy or exposing authority that depends on it; no new parallel source of reply authority.
- [ ] Settled history is bounded by documented count/byte budgets and avoids full-history scans/startup loads. Numeric budgets have workload evidence.
- [ ] After eviction, identical terminals retain duplicate semantics and conflicting terminals invoke existing hold/retraction handling.
- [ ] Retired native requests replayed unchanged, changed, with reused typed IDs or old generations cannot create duplicate answer opportunities or replies.
- [ ] Active callbacks, pending/writing/sent-unconfirmed replies and uncertain execution remain protected across eviction, stop, start and restart.
- [ ] Persistence/read failures and missing expected records cannot release holds or treat retired execution as new; legacy data without sufficient evidence remains explicitly uncertain.
- [ ] Synthetic longevity tests exceed cache budgets with both settled turns and native questions. Report retained collection sizes and controlled memory/lookup/cancellation measurements.
- [ ] Preserve bounded conversation capture and native protocol qualification. Record the accepted invariant and lifecycle triggers in domain/design docs before implementation.
- [ ] Run pinned npm ci and npm run check, with real SQLite and deterministic runtime fixtures.

**Out of scope:** Disk pruning, age-only forgetting of safety evidence, weaker late-conflict/replay guarantees, automatic hold release, harness replacement, production cutover and deferred X01–X05. No paid/live model calls are needed for deterministic retention testing.

**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Make compact SQLite evidence authoritative for exact terminal identity and native request/reply history. Retain only operationally live runtime objects and small byte/count-limited caches. Wire synchronous indexed evidence reads and writes into `CodexRuntime` before terminal completion or native request exposure, using the existing `ExecutionState` execution binding and `CoordinationStore` reply-intent transaction. A cache miss consults durable evidence; unreadable, corrupt, incomplete or legacy-unknown evidence blocks the affected action and preserves its hold. Document the invariant first, then implement and exercise real-SQLite deterministic runtime fixtures with many more settled turns and questions than the cache budgets.

### Guardrails

- Preserve the approved runtime trust/recovery contract, bound thread/turn attribution, old-child filtering, one reply authority, callback/Stop/uncertainty holds, existing late terminal anomaly/retraction path, native protocol qualification and bounded conversation capture. Cache eviction or restart never releases ownership or makes a request fresh. No disk-history deletion, age cutoff or automatic hold release.
- A production `CodexRuntime` must have its durable safety interface bound before `start()` or any test-only injected receive path can grant terminal/reply authority. Convert direct adapter tests to real temporary SQLite-backed setup; do not introduce an optional in-memory-only production fallback. Fake `Runtime` test doubles need no database implementation.
- Scope is runtime retention, indexed safety lookup and its service wiring. No paid/live Codex calls, harness replacement, deployment, cutover, installed Haze changes or paused X01–X05 work. Keep legacy data and its uncertainty visible; do not infer absent records mean no earlier event.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one focused diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary fixture/implementation repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants. Reuse the delivery record and adequate checks/reviews; an integration amendment is only for a changed published integration decision.
- #788 changes `service.ts`/`state.ts` stop and held-workspace paths; #789 follows #788 and changes `service.ts` fatal/CLI paths. Do not write shared production files concurrently with either. Implement #790 after their merged heads, screen the exact deltas, and retain their cancellation-before-settlement and fatal-admission behavior. Read-only planning on this fixed head does not claim those integrations passed.

### Planning decisions

- **Terminal authority and key.** Add a compact `runtime_terminal_evidence` record owned by `ExecutionState`, keyed by `(threadId,turnId)` across runtime generations, with nullable `firstStatus` (`completed`/`failed`, null only for legacy-unknown), sticky `conflicted`, optional exact `workId`, first/last runtime generation and integer first/last observation time. The generation is diagnostic and old-child filtering remains at the adapter; it must not partition conflicts for the same bound turn. Register/associate the exact execution binding when available and index `execution_intents(threadId,turnId)` to find all affected work/successors, including a completed predecessor. A duplicate same-status terminal preserves the first observation; an opposite status atomically marks conflict and invokes existing anomaly/retraction. Neither duplicate may overwrite a conflict with success. `waitForTurn()` consumes the persisted decision, not raw event status; a persist/read error fails the runtime path before completion/admission authority.
- **Legacy and first observation.** A one-time, transactional migration creates legacy-unknown evidence for preexisting bound turns lacking observed terminal status; it never fabricates completion from an intent state. An unknown legacy row, a bound old turn with missing evidence, duplicate bound identities, or a corrupt/unreadable row means hold/retraction or startup refusal as appropriate, not a new first observation. New process-generation turns may create first observed rows, including a terminal that arrives before the `turn/start` response, but only under the current child and the service's exact binding/prebinding checks before work completion. Keep unbound valid terminal identities as evidence with no work-completion authority; if later bound, reconcile the exact identity rather than losing the earlier report. The migration is one-time disk work, not a startup history load.
- **Native identity and sole reply authority.** Extend the existing `coordination_runtime_questions` record, not a second native reply ledger: backfill/index `runtimeGeneration`, `threadId`, `turnId`, `itemId`, `rpcIdKind` (`number`/`string`) and `rpcIdValue` from validated `identityJson`. Keep `endpointKey` unique and `requestDigest` as the canonical validated input digest; retain `qualificationJson`, answer/digest, `replyIntentId`, delivery/request states and ordered `outcomeJson`. Use a nonunique composite index on `(runtimeGeneration,threadId,rpcIdKind,rpcIdValue)` so a reused typed ID across turn/item is discoverable, and the existing exact endpoint key for equality; two matches are ambiguity, not permission. Add a partial pending-answer index on `(requestState,deliveryState,interactionId)` where `answerDigest IS NOT NULL AND replyIntentId IS NULL`, and an index on `coordination_interactions(requestingWorkId,interactionId)` for per-work cancellation. Keep `CoordinationStore.beginRuntimeReply()` as the only before-stdin-write transaction and `recordRuntimeReplyOutcome()` as the outcome owner. Replace global `runtimeQuestions().find()` and dispatch scans with exact interaction/endpoint and pending-answer/active-work SQL queries that fetch and validate only matching rows. A missing expected record or index/backfill disagreement yields uncertainty and no reply.
- **Native lifecycle.** Keep raw readback and callable endpoint only for the active current-generation turn; keep pending, writing and sent-unconfirmed endpoints until matching resolution/turn end or a conservative unavailable/uncertain outcome is durably recorded. End registered callback/reply processing before retiring their only in-memory payload. Use direct maps by exact endpoint, `(generation,thread,typed RPC ID)` and `(thread,turn)` to cancel/resolve/replay without scanning settled endpoints. The one accepted same-child, same-turn, identical retransmission remains limited to its existing single replay while the active readback exists. After retirement, a repeated identity is checked against the durable request digest/status and is stale/conflicting; it never becomes a fresh question. Old-generation messages from a replaced child remain rejected before lookup. Resolution with only thread and typed RPC ID uses the active index; lack of an exact active match is an anomaly, never a historical reactivation.
- **Other map lifetimes and exact settings.** `terminals` holds only started turns awaiting consumption and uses durable lookup for an early terminal; `failures` survives through the bound turn's failure/retry classification and is then retired, with needed classification outcome already in durable recovery/attempt evidence. `invalidNativeTurns`, `nativeReadbacks`, `nativeQualifications` and `nativeTurns` live through active turn/qualification and clear at terminal, replacement, stop or failure. `threadTools` and `nativeThreadSettings` become bounded caches over one compact `runtime_thread_qualification` row per thread in `ExecutionState`: exact `threadId`, registered tool-definition digest from `thread/start`, and, after first successful qualification, Codex version/hash plus model/provider/effort/tier/developer-instruction digest from the verified readback. A new qualification may fill an unset baseline once, never overwrite a prior one. Service-supplied tool definitions on resume must match the stored digest, and `thread/resume` readback must match stored settings before native qualification. If an older or changed binding lacks these exact facts, refuse native qualification and retain the question/hold; never substitute today's settings as if historical. Keep active snapshot entries pinned only while callbacks/turns depend on them. Do not change the selected Codex policy or extend native protocol coverage.
- **Initial budgets and measurement.** Start with a terminal-status cache of at most 256 entries and 64 KiB of counted UTF-8 key/value bytes; a retired native-request cache, if useful, at most 16 entries and 512 KiB including payload bytes; a per-thread qualification/tool cache at most 128 entries and 256 KiB. Zero settled native payload cache is acceptable if direct indexed reads meet measured lookup bounds. Count/byte limits apply jointly, evicting only settled entries; active protected entries are separately enumerated and tied to actual active/held work, not silently forced under a settled cache ceiling. These conservative initial values keep a maximal 256 KiB native request from escaping a byte cap; record the observed active and settled bytes separately. Numeric budgets are implementation choices, adjustable from measured deterministic evidence without changing the invariant.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/codex.ts` — `CodexRuntime.receive()` stores every terminal in `terminalHistory` and a consumable `terminals` map; `waitForTurn()` can resolve from the raw notification. `receiveNativeRequest()`, `receiveNativeNotification()` and `cancelNativeTurn()` scan historical `nativeEndpoints`; `start()` clears most native maps but not terminal history/endpoints on `stop()`. `failureEvidence()`, `threadTools`, `nativeThreadSettings`, `invalidNativeTurns`, `nativeReadbacks` and conversation capture need the lifetimes above.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `ExecutionState` owns `execution_intents`, exact task bindings, recovery identities, terminal observations, successor retraction and holds. The current exact binding query has revision gates, so historical terminal attribution should use a dedicated exact identity query rather than an admission-only binding predicate.
- **Existing:** `src/core/coordination.ts` — `coordination_runtime_questions` already holds exact `endpointKey`, JSON identity/request/qualification, canonical `requestDigest`, answer, unique `replyIntentId` and final/uncertain outcome. `recordRuntimeQuestion()` writes before operator exposure; `beginRuntimeReply()` writes intent before stdin, and `recordRuntimeReplyOutcome()` records resolution. Several of these methods plus `flushRuntimeAnswers()` scan and parse all historical questions.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — runtime listeners bind native requests, callbacks and terminal anomalies; `retractWriterAndSuccessors()` applies existing conflict holds. `executeAdmitted()` calls `waitForTurn()` then supervisor/completion, and `flushRuntimeAnswers()` supplies the persisted before-write callback. `start()` constructs state/coordination before runtime start; bind the safety interface there and preserve #788/#789 startup/stop gates. `src/core/structured-questions.ts` defines the typed RPC ID and exact endpoint key.
- **Follow:** `test/codex-runtime.test.ts` has direct parser/native fixture coverage; `test/structured-question-service.test.ts`, `test/native-input.test.ts`, `test/recovery.test.ts` and `test/standalone.test.ts` cover real SQLite question/recovery/service paths. `docs/design/standalone.md` states terminal trust and conservative recovery; `docs/evidence/ui01-runtime-input.md` records bounded native protocol qualification.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** `T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 → T5` is acyclic. T1 documents the invariant before code. T2 establishes terminal durability; T3 reuses the bound SQLite safety interface for native lookup; T4 retires payloads and exact settings while preserving T2/T3 evidence; T5 measures and integrates. These touch `codex.ts`, `state.ts`, `coordination.ts` and `service.ts` with shared interfaces, so one implementation owner works serially after #788/#789 merge. Independent final review follows the integrated candidate.

#### 1. Record the approved invariant and exact migration contract

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** Recheck merged main, issue #790 active brief/proposal and clean/compatible implementation checkout; screen #788/#789 merged deltas before source edits. Use pinned `.node-version` Node 24.21.0 and package-manager npm 12.2.0; run `npm ci` before code validation.
**Files and symbols:** `docs/design/standalone.md` runtime trust/recovery section; `CONTEXT.md` only if a new domain term is needed; `docs/evidence/` retention fixture record created during T5, not as a speculative design file.
**Implementation:** Document terminal/native exact identity, SQLite-before-authority order, cache-miss/legacy/corruption failure rule, active/pending/sent-unconfirmed retirement triggers, thread-setting proof and no disk-pruning rule. Make clear that bounded memory is independent of durable safety lifetime and that an unresolved hold is not resolved by retirement.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout, run `git diff --check`; expect the invariant to precede code changes and agree with #790/ADR-1004/SPEC rather than claim stronger runtime containment.
**Complete when:** A fresh implementer can identify the authoritative record and retirement trigger for each safety-bearing collection before editing runtime behavior.

#### 2. Make terminal status durable before completion authority

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's invariant is recorded; integration screen of #788/#789 shows compatible state/service startup and stop paths.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/state.ts` terminal evidence schema/migration and exact indexed lookup; `src/standalone/codex.ts` mandatory safety binding, `receive()`, `waitForTurn()` and terminal cache; `src/standalone/service.ts` binding/wiring and existing `onTerminalAnomaly`; `test/codex-runtime.test.ts`, `test/recovery.test.ts` or a focused `test/runtime-retention.test.ts` real-SQLite fixture.
**Test:** With a real SQLite file, record a bound completed terminal, consume/evict it, inject the same status and then failed status for turn 0 while many later turns exist; assert no second completion, one conflict anomaly, sticky persisted conflict, writer/successor hold/retraction and no successful `waitForTurn()` result. Close/reopen runtime/state and repeat; an old child's late event is ignored but the current child reporting the same bound identity still conflicts. Inject a SQLite write failure before first receipt and a read failure after eviction: assert no completed execution, no handoff, observable hold/failure. Create a legacy database with completed/held exact turns but no receipt; migration marks them unknown, and later terminal cannot silently complete or release them. Test early terminal before `turn/start` response against exact prebinding and ambiguity/missing identity.
**Implementation:** Add the compact table and one-time conservative migration; bind a synchronous safety port during service setup and require it in production `CodexRuntime`. Persist/compare terminal within the receive path before updating consumable state or emitting `turn/completed`; on conflict use current anomaly handling and sticky failed decision. Ensure `waitForTurn()` reads the authoritative decision rather than deriving it from the raw event. Retire a consumed settled status from memory under the budget; keep unconsumed active early-terminal state resolvable via indexed SQLite. Do not turn storage failures into a synthetic success/failure terminal.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --unhandled-rejections=strict --test dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js dist/test/recovery.test.js dist/test/runtime-retention.test.js`; expect exact duplicate/conflict, restart, migration and injected-failure cases to pass with real SQLite.
**Complete when:** A terminal can change execution authority only after durable exact evidence, and a settled evicted or restarted turn still identifies conflicts and affected work.

#### 3. Index the existing native reply record and close full-history lookups

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2's before-authority and failure checks pass; keep `CoordinationStore` as sole native intent/outcome owner.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/coordination.ts` migration, exact-key/typed-ID/interaction/pending-answer/active-work queries and `recordRuntimeQuestion`, `beginRuntimeReply`, `recordRuntimeReplyOutcome`; `src/core/structured-questions.ts` only if a shared typed-ID encoder is required; `src/standalone/service.ts` `handleUserInputOutcome`, `flushRuntimeAnswers` and per-work cancellation callers; `test/structured-question-service.test.ts`, `test/native-input.test.ts` and `test/runtime-retention.test.ts`.
**Test:** Backfill an old real SQLite native row (number RPC ID), then query `1` and `"1"` separately; assert exactly one typed match and no duplicate interaction. Exercise an unchanged exact-key replay, changed input under the same key, same typed ID with different turn/item, and two ambiguous historical matches. Assert each retains one operator question and at most one reply intent; conflict or missing/corrupt expected data yields held/unavailable or uncertain state. Inject failure in `beginRuntimeReply()` before stdin and `recordRuntimeReplyOutcome()` after stdin; assert zero writes in the first case, one uncertain intent in the second, and no retry on restart. Compare indexed `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` output to the declared indexes and verify the production answer flush/exact outcome paths do not call global `runtimeQuestions()`.
**Implementation:** Add and transactionally backfill validated identity columns and indexes on the existing question table; retain existing payloads and states. Replace global `.find()` scans in exact reply/request/outcome methods with one-row validated reads, and add indexed pending-answer/per-work queries for service dispatch/stop. Preserve the existing atomic `replyIntentId` before-write transition and non-upgradable uncertain/unavailable outcome. A legacy row whose identity, digest or index columns cannot be reconciled blocks affected native activity; do not invent an absent-row fresh verdict. Existing operator task-scoped history views may remain paginated separately; avoid repeated full-table parsing in background dispatch.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout, run `npm run build:service && node --unhandled-rejections=strict --test dist/test/structured-question-service.test.js dist/test/native-input.test.js dist/test/runtime-retention.test.js`; expect typed-ID, migration, authority and write-failure assertions to pass.
**Complete when:** Exact native replay/reply/outcome decisions use indexed durable records without scanning all settled questions or introducing another reply intent.

#### 4. Retire settled runtime payloads while preserving active callbacks and qualification

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T2/T3 persistence, typed lookup and failure tests pass; no callback or sent-unconfirmed reply may be dropped before its durable disposition.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/codex.ts` `nativeEndpoints`, `nativeReadbacks`, `nativeTurns`, `invalidNativeTurns`, `failures`, `threadTools`, `nativeThreadSettings`, native request/replay/resolve/cancel and start/stop/fail paths; `src/standalone/state.ts` compact thread snapshot if placed with execution bindings; `src/standalone/service.ts` callback-end and resume wiring; `test/codex-runtime.test.ts`, `test/structured-question-service.test.ts`, `test/runtime-retention.test.ts`.
**Test:** After eviction, replay a settled native request unchanged, changed, with typed-ID reuse, and from an old generation; assert no second request exposure or reply write. While active, test the existing one exact same-child retransmission and its single-replay bound. Hold a callback, a pending endpoint, a writing endpoint, a sent-unconfirmed reply, and an uncertain execution through cache churn; verify each remains protected, then settle/end it and inspect retirement plus durable disposition. Repeat stop/start and service restart with real SQLite; no answered request reopens. Resume with unchanged and deliberately changed model/tool/settings snapshots; only exact compatible facts qualify native input, with changed or missing legacy facts held/unqualified. Inject a read failure on a retired native lookup and confirm no new endpoint or reply. Verify direct turn cancellation and resolution inspect only active indexed entries.
**Implementation:** Replace historical endpoint scans with active exact-request/turn indexes. Retire callable payloads and raw readbacks at the lifecycle boundary described above; cache only settled evidence behind strict count/byte budgets. Persist compact exact thread qualification/tool facts and compare on resume; keep active pins until callbacks and writes end. Clear invalid-turn and failure maps only after their last decision, not at an arbitrary age. Keep conversation capture's own limits and old-child check unchanged.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout, run `npm run build:service && node --unhandled-rejections=strict --test dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js dist/test/structured-question-service.test.js dist/test/runtime-retention.test.js`; expect all active/settled/restart/replay/qualification cases to pass without duplicate reply authority.
**Complete when:** Settled endpoint payloads and thread snapshots obey budgets, active/uncertain states remain protected, and cancellation/replay/resolve no longer scan historical endpoints.

#### 5. Measure synthetic longevity, integrate and review

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T4`
**Prerequisites:** T2–T4 focused checks pass on the post-#788/#789 integrated head; no paid/live runtime grant is implied.
**Files and symbols:** `test/runtime-retention.test.ts` and deterministic stdio fixture under `test/ui01/` or existing native fixture, `docs/evidence/` measured retention report; integration repairs only in the files owned above.
**Test:** Drive at least 10,000 settled terminal turns and 2,000 settled native questions through production adapter/service paths with real SQLite, plus explicit evicted turn-0 conflict and old-question replay at the end. Enumerate every retained collection (`terminals`, terminal cache, native endpoint/readback/turn/invalid/failure maps, active indexes, thread settings/tools cache and service waiters/callbacks), distinguish active pins from settled cache, and assert each settled count/byte budget after each cohort. Under pinned Node with `--expose-gc`, sample heap after an explicit GC before and after equal-size settled cohorts, reporting raw heap values and delta without claiming a universal leak bound. Time indexed cold terminal/native lookup and direct cancellation over a fixed number of iterations with `process.hrtime.bigint()`, reporting median/p95/max and SQLite row counts with setup/hardware/runtime identity. Use hard pass assertions on correctness, budget caps and bounded test completion; treat latency/heap as workload evidence, not a universal production SLA. Verify index plans and no startup all-history materialization.
**Implementation:** Record the exact fixture size, payload shape, cache settings, active pins, measured counts/bytes, controlled heap/lookup/cancel data, and limits in `docs/evidence/`. Review the final integrated diff against #788/#789 service/state changes and the authorized #790 invariant. Fix only compatible defects, then obtain an independent read-only review of the integrated candidate.
**Validate:** From the implementation checkout with pinned Node/npm after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --expose-gc --unhandled-rejections=strict --test dist/test/runtime-retention.test.js`, then `npm run check` and `git diff --check`; expect the deterministic longevity assertions, full type/lint/format/build/tests and intended-file diff to pass. Preserve the measured report even if heap values vary.
**Complete when:** Both populations materially exceed configured cache budgets, all relevant collections and timing methods are reported, full checks pass and the independent review's actionable findings are resolved on the final head.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Durable terminal status/conflict and native identity/intent/outcome precede retirement or dependent authority | 2–3 | SQLite write-failure, before-write and exact-record tests |
| Bounded settled memory and indexed history access, without full-history cancellation/reply scans or startup load | 3–5 | Query-plan checks, collection byte/count assertions and cold lookup/cancel timings |
| Evicted identical terminal remains duplicate; conflicting terminal retracts the exact writer/successors across applicable restarts | 2, 5 | Turn-0 duplicate/conflict and restart fixture |
| Retired unchanged/changed/reused typed-ID/old-generation native requests cannot expose a new answer or duplicate reply | 3–5 | Native replay matrix and one-intent/readback assertions |
| Pending callbacks and pending/writing/sent-unconfirmed/uncertain replies and execution survive eviction, stop/start and restart conservatively | 3–4 | Delayed callback/write/resolution and reopen fixture |
| Persistence/read errors, corrupt/missing expected records and legacy incomplete evidence retain uncertainty | 2–4 | Injected SQLite failures, migration and missing-row cases |
| Native protocol qualification and bounded conversation capture remain intact; exact resumable settings are preserved or native input withheld | 4–5 | Existing UI01 native fixtures, changed-settings/legacy case and full check |
| Accepted invariant documented before code and synthetic longevity reports both turns and questions with controlled resource evidence | 1, 5 | Documentation diff order and evidence report with workload/method/results |

### Final validation

- In the implementation checkout on the merged integration head, use `.node-version` Node 24.21.0 and npm 12.2.0. Run `npm ci`, focused strict-mode SQLite/runtime tests, `npm run check`, `git diff --check`, and inspect final status. Record SHA, exact commands, test results, measured fixture/runtime identity and limitations. No live Codex/model calls are required for #790.
- This read-only planning checkout was clean at fixed `588af417af49b445799643f13b17dee2997d09b0`, with no `node_modules`; no baseline build/test was run here. The implementation owner must establish baseline and final checks on the actual merged head. The source packet includes the unminimized [retention proposal](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/790#issuecomment-6017106739) and [approved brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/790#issuecomment-6033309805); its planning-time readback had no active plan marker or linked implementation PR. Recheck those live facts before publication or execution.

### Review focus

- Ensure no path interprets an evicted cache miss or malformed legacy row as fresh native input, successful completion, or permission to issue a second reply; inspect `waitForTurn()` raw-event behavior specifically.
- Verify a terminal lookup key spans relevant generations while old-child messages remain filtered, the existing writer/successor retraction receives the exact bound identity, and reply intent is still committed only through `CoordinationStore` before stdin.
- Confirm active/sent-unconfirmed/uncertain payload retirement waits for callbacks and durable outcomes; budget accounting includes UTF-8 payload bytes, and no background native dispatch loads all historical questions.

### Re-plan triggers

- The merged #788/#789 head changes terminal or native reply authority such that these existing stores cannot own the proposed records; a completed legacy generation must be treated as a new observation to satisfy a required behavior; or exact native continuation requires replacing current qualified protocol/settings rather than withholding unproved input. Return concrete evidence and a proposed contract change before expanding scope.
