<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/838
**Planned against:** `main` at `116f12e039482f24aa8be16454254452a964c7e3`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Six sequential slices on one branch (`cb/issue-838-inbox-structured-questions`), then one PR, with no server, contract or API change. T1 adds the pure presentation helpers and the question-state fields everything else reads. T2 rebuilds the Inbox queue (compact filters, request cards with kind, action and relative age, designed empty states). T3 adds desktop auto-selection, the sticky-header/sticky-footer detail pane, and the phone detail header through one narrow seam in `app.tsx`. T4 gives approvals and interventions the designed detail pane with the independent hold beside the approval. T5 restyles the shared `QuestionResponse` (choice cards, two columns, progress, "Recommended by", failed, stale, recorded and unknown states). T6 records docs and the frame comparison and runs the full check. Existing selectors that change are updated in the slice that changes them, not deleted.

Source contract (retrievable): the issue's Scope and Acceptance; epic #834; `design/DESIGN.md` ("Layout and responsive composition", "Interaction guidance", "Screen reference map"); `docs/SPEC.md` "Human requests and execution controls" and "Everyday navigation and attention"; `docs/acceptance.md` UX02, UI01; PR #851's Inbox decisions. This plan restates none of them; a conflict between this plan and those sources is a re-plan trigger.

### Guardrails

- Behaviour, contracts and safety do not change because a layout changes. Unchanged: the summary-only queue (no prompt text in rows), the 100-row fingerprinted paging and 15-second poll in `loadInbox`/`Inbox`, `inboxSummaryOf` and the count rule (a count is a total only for a complete, successful read), the `CommandLifecycle` freeze, key reuse and receipt matching in `QuestionResponse.submit`, the unknown-outcome reconciliation, preserved drafts/selection/scroll/focus through `QuestionResponseStates` and `InboxState`, "a recommended or preselected option is not a submitted answer", and "answering clears no independent hold". Auto-selection and every display change send no command.
- Out of scope: any `src/**` change (no new field on `inboxItemSchema`, `questionReadSchema` or `taskSchema`); in-app approval decisions (see Planning decisions); short identifiers such as Q-204 or A-201 (U3 #837 owns them and the read model has none); the task detail page and its `QuestionResponse` call site in `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` (U5 #839 and #828 own that file); sign-in, account menu and not found (U2 #836); settings (U6); project setup (U7); the retained HTML operator, which stays reachable through contextual "Advanced …" / "Open existing …" links per the #835 agreement.
- Two kinds of repair, kept separate. (1) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (a named symbol, prop, route, test seam or data field does not behave as this plan says) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; after that, stop and re-plan. (2) Ordinary implementation defects belong to the ticket owner and do not count against that budget: integration breakage, flaky or failing tests and fixtures, selector migration, type and lint errors, formatting, docs, CI and screenshot-journey repairs. Investigate unknown overlap with #828/#836 before continuing. Stop for a material design or contract change or exhausted grants. Return human-required only if the accepted contract itself must change.
- If a frame contradicts the issue Scope, follow the frame where repository evidence supports it and record the choice in the PR (the choices already made are in Planning decisions). Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews; use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption.

### Planning decisions

- **Frames over Scope wording for the phone back control.** The issue says "Back to queue" appears on phone only. Frames 10, 21, 27–30 draw the designed phone detail header (Back "Inbox", title "Question · 3 of 5", subtitle, one "Open task" action), and `PageHeader` already has that detail variant from #835. So the in-body "Back to queue" button is removed and the phone Back is the header's link (`aria-label` "Back to Inbox"); after a recorded answer the confirmation card's button reads "Back to Inbox". Desktop has no back control. Record this in the PR.
- **Approvals: designed pane and hold in the Inbox, decisions stay at the exact destination.** Frames 07, 32 and 33 draw Approve/Deny in the Inbox. The decision control is inventoried at `/coordination/task/:id#<interaction>` (`docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` control crosswalk, `test/operator-control-inventory.test.ts`; the React app has no `approval.decide` caller), the acceptance criteria name no approval-decision test, and an in-app decision would be a new authority surface binding action, target and material. So T4 shows the exact action, target, revision, requester and the independent hold (frames 07, 33) with one "Review material & decide" link to the retained destination, in line with the agreed fallback. Frame 32's post-decision state cannot occur in the app and is not built. If the lead wants in-app decisions, that is a separate scope decision, not an implementation choice.
- **Evidence stays the task history link.** Frame 27 draws an in-pane excerpt. The question read has no excerpt field, so the existing "Question evidence" / "Task evidence" links remain; "inspect evidence and return" is met by browser Back or the header Back restoring selection, scroll position and the invoking link's focus (T5 records link focus in `QuestionResponseState.focusId`).
- **Single-question choice cards are not pinned.** Frame 06 puts the cards in the sticky reply area. A pinned option list is unbounded (up to 100 options), would need a nested scroll (`web/src/styles.css` already warns that a nested bound traps scrolling) and #800 recorded a pinned footer covering the last field. The cards stay in the reading flow; only the submit area is sticky, inside the single scroll owner `.inbox-detail`, so it occupies its own space at the end and cannot cover a field.
- **Queue rows use read-model facts only.** `InboxItem` has no request title, short ID or intervention subtype. A row shows the label "PROJECT / KIND" (kind: Question, Approval, Intervention), the task title as the bold line, the existing `reason`, the action text ("Answer question", "Review material & decide", "Inspect execution", the wording the Overview and task detail already use) and "Requester · HH:MM · age". The action is a styled span inside the row button, not a nested anchor. "Execution uncertain" vs "Intervention problems" (frame 11) is not derivable and stays one "Interventions" option.
- **Kept or omitted on purpose.** The shell Refresh stays on the Inbox (recovery path for a failed or stale read, driven by many existing tests); the frame's "Today · 11:00" fixture clock and the phone "Search" header action are not built (Search is in the drawer; header actions belong to #835/#836); frames 07 and 08 draw an older large "Inbox" title, and 06, 19 and #835 use 18/600, so 18/600 stands.
- **Auto-selection.** On a wide layout (`min-width: 761px`, the complement of the existing single-column rule at `max-width: 760px`) the first filtered row is selected once, when the first fresh read arrives for a mount that has no `request` URL parameter and no `InboxState.selected`. It uses no history entry (selection state, not navigation), never re-runs on polls or filter changes, and never runs on phone. After a recorded answer the detail stays on the confirmation; "Back to Inbox" clears the selection for that visit without opening another request (frame 11 rule 03).
- **Header seam.** `Inbox` gets an `onHeader` callback beside `onSummary`; it reports `{subtitle?, detail?}` and `null` on unmount. `app.tsx` only merges it into `PageHeader` props. `detail` is reported only on the single-column layout with a selected request, so desktop and tablet keep the top-level header. Subtitle variants: "N unresolved across M projects" (unchanged), "0 unresolved across your projects", "N unresolved · confirmation retained" while a recorded detail is held.
- **Assumption with a gate.** Two-column grouped questions rely on CSS multi-column inside a container-query container in Chromium and WebKit (both run in `operator-question-browser`). T5 asserts the columns in both engines; if WebKit differs, fall back to a viewport media query for the same breakpoint rather than a script. This is a bounded check inside T5, not a separate proof.

| Empty and filtered-empty states (frames 08, 11) | 2 | `operator-inbox-browser` (d), (e) |
| Existing tests pass; changed selectors updated, not deleted | 2–6 | migrated suites in each slice; full `npm run check` |
| Desktop and phone screenshots match the frames | 6 | screenshots and difference list in the PR body |

### Final validation

- From the repo root, after `npm ci` on Node 24.21.0, run `npm run check`; expect type checking, lint (warnings are errors), format, build and the full test suite to pass with 0 failures.
- Exercise the real production bundle in the browser suites only; no live model or runtime attempt is required because no runtime, command or contract changes. State that in the PR.

### Review focus

- Overlap with #836 and #828, as the implementer must handle it. #836 (plan 6088157840) edits `web/src/app.tsx` (`Login` removal, `AccountFooter`, `expired()`/`logout()`, the final fallback ternary and the now-dead `description`/`destination`, the header `action`/`ownsRefresh`), `web/src/components.tsx` (`PageHeader` divider option), `web/src/styles.css` (`.login*`, `.account-footer`, the ≤1120px drawer rules at ≈L688–765, directly beside `.page-inbox` at ≈L768), the two docs files in T6, and the sign-out selectors in `test/operator-question-browser.test.ts` (≈L260), `operator-web-browser`, `operator-ux800-shell-browser`, `operator-foundation-browser` and `operator-search-browser`. This plan's only `app.tsx` edits are the `onHeader` state, prop and `PageHeader` merge in T3; do not touch the dead `/app/inbox` fallback strings. Fetch and rebase before opening the PR and rerun T3's command if #836 merged first. #828 edits `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`, `web/src/local-review.tsx`, new `web/src/lead-feedback.ts`, `src/core/coordination.ts`, `src/core/local-review.ts`, `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` and `src/operator/contracts.ts` (additive `leadFeedback` and `resumedLead`). This plan edits none of them, and its published plan does not change `readInbox` or `inboxItemSchema`; T4 only reads the existing `taskSchema` fields. If #828 later adds an Inbox kind, `requestKindLabel` must stay exhaustive over the enum so the type check fails, not the UI.
- Data and privacy: the queue stays summary-only; the approval pane reads only the existing task read the task page already uses; nothing here sends or stores a command.
- Selection, focus and scroll: auto-selection must not repeat on polls, must not select on phone, and must not open the next request after a recorded answer; the header seam must reset on unmount, route change and sign-out.
- The submit label rename ("Submit answers" for several questions) and the removal of "Back to queue" are intentional selector migrations.

### Allowed deviations (when task-specific)

- Fixture and selector changes, class renames (with the test selectors updated), copy that differs only in punctuation, and CSS values that differ from the frames within the shared tokens are routine. A different seam for the phone header or approval hold than this plan names is a plan mismatch and uses the diagnosis and repair budget.

content.title: U3: Match Overview, task list and Board to the design

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/837
**Planned against:** `main` at `116f12e039482f24aa8be16454254452a964c7e3`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Seven sequential slices on one branch (`cb/issue-837-overview-task-list-board`), then one PR, with no `src/**`, contract or API change. T1 adds the pure model (column order, the Active/All state filter, next-actor wording, request wording, safe source links, subtitles) and repairs a red base test. T2 builds the one-row toolbar (inline Project and State dropdowns, List/Board switch, count, Refresh tasks) and the new header subtitles, and flips the default view to Active tasks. T3 rebuilds the task row (Overview and List) as the two-line row with state, next actor and lead. T4 rebuilds Overview attention as request rows read from the Inbox, and adds the completed-work line. T5 rebuilds the Board: link bar with every count, collapsed empty columns, the drawn card, and phone column tabs. T6 adds the persistent attention summary above List and Board. T7 records docs, deletes superseded CSS and compares screenshots with the frames. New React goes in new files and new CSS in `web/src/work.css`, so `app.tsx`, `styles.css` and `inbox.tsx` change in small, separate regions; U2 #836 and U4 #838 edit them too.

Source contract (retrievable, not restated): issue #837 Scope and Acceptance; epic #834 Boundaries; `design/DESIGN.md` (Screen reference map, "Interaction guidance", the Board notes in frame `e839O`); `docs/SPEC.md` "Everyday navigation and attention" and "Kanban board"; `docs/acceptance.md` UI03; PR #851's body ("Deferred", "Residual risks"). A conflict between this plan and those sources is a re-plan trigger.

Frames (read through Pen MCP on 9 October 2026, exported at scale 1; re-export them, do not parse `design/design.pen`): Overview `N9G11A`; List `nD0nh`; cross-project Board `E7qC9` and later columns `x9cPnW`; project Board `MUFPD`; phone Waiting `GWXOi` and Uncertain `CTUzI`; card `cjNBk` (its spec panel `jXyBK`); outcomes comparison `zeoGi` (Done and Cancelled rows, the "All tasks" dropdown option); link-bar items `Q5GVK` (desktop) and `kZTPH` (phone, 44px); compact progress `cIimt` and `L2aXf` (not built here, see Planning decisions); Board notes `e839O`; review notes `DuF5u` (section 6). Export with `Export(["N9G11A","nD0nh","E7qC9","x9cPnW","MUFPD","GWXOi","CTUzI","cjNBk","Q5GVK","kZTPH"],"png",<scratch dir>,{scale:1})`. There is no phone Overview and no phone List frame (the canvas index `H7aUq1` lists none); those two phone layouts are composed from the shell frames (`U3RAH`, `KthOL`) and the desktop frames and are compared by judgement.

### Guardrails

- Behaviour, contracts and safety do not change because the layout changes. Unchanged: `loadTaskList` paging and its catalog-fingerprint, order and cursor checks; `taskColumn`'s state mapping and `taskReasons`; the `data-task-id` attribute on exactly one element per task (the List, Board and Overview selectors count them); the URL filter parameters `project`, `state`, `source`, `ready`, `q` and `view` and their back/forward and reload restoration; List and Board show the same filtered task set and switching sends no command (the existing `commandPosts === 0` assertions stay); Board selection and scroll restoration through `history.state.board`; the stale/failed read semantics of `ResourceStatus`; the Inbox count rule `inboxSummaryOf` (a count is a total only for a complete, successful read); "unknown responsibility stays explicit"; no drag and drop and no status mutation; the retained HTML operator stays reachable through the contextual "Open existing …" / "Project settings" links.
- Out of scope: any `src/**` change (no field on `taskListSummarySchema` or `inboxItemSchema`, no new endpoint); a cross-task "Recent results" read; new identifier schemes (see Planning decisions); `web/src/inbox.tsx`, `web/src/question-response*.ts*`, `.inbox-*`/`.question-*` styles and the Inbox header seam (U4 #838); `Login`, `AccountFooter`, the account menu and not-found (U2 #836); `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`, `web/src/local-review.tsx`, `web/src/lead-feedback.ts` (#828 and U5 #839); settings, profiles, routing, runtime, recovery and project setup (U6 #840, U7 #841); `design/design.pen`; the shared `.task-actions` rule in `web/src/styles.css`, which task detail, search, composer, files and review also use.
- Two kinds of repair, kept separate. (1) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (a named symbol, prop, route, read-model field or shell resource does not behave as this plan says) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; after that, stop and re-plan. The assumptions that count are: the shell's whole-Inbox read (`inboxSummary` in `App`) is available on `/app`, `/app/tasks` and project routes and is re-read by the page-owned refresh; `InboxItem.destination` values are as `readInbox` builds them (question `/app/tasks/:id?request=…`, approval `/coordination/task/:id#…`, intervention `/app/tasks/:id`) and `/app/inbox?task=…&request=…` still selects a request; `TaskListSummary` carries no timestamp, counter or result text; `source.url` is an `https:` URL for imported tasks. (2) Ordinary implementation defects belong to the ticket owner and do not count against that budget: integration breakage, flaky or failing tests and fixtures, selector migration, type and lint errors, formatting, docs, CI and screenshot repairs, and the base `ux800-matrix` repair in T1. Investigate unknown overlap with #828, #836 and #838 before continuing. Stop for a material design or contract change or exhausted grants. Return human-required only if the accepted contract itself must change.
- If a frame contradicts the issue Scope, follow the frame where repository evidence supports it and record the choice in the PR (the choices already made are in Planning decisions).
- `npm run lint` fails on warnings (#850). New markup must pass `biome lint --error-on-warnings`; prefer semantic elements, and use a targeted `biome-ignore` with a reason only as `web/src/app.tsx` already does.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Frames versus Scope, and what is not built as drawn.**
  - *Page titles stay.* Frames 01, 24, 18 and 18b title the Overview and Tasks screens "Your workspace", and the phone Tasks header reads "Tasks". The issue Scope names no title change, #835 left titles to this slice, and several things depend on the current ones: U2's published tests assert h1 "Overview" after sign-in, about twenty existing assertions use "Overview" and "All tasks", and a shared title would make the two sidebar destinations indistinguishable to a screen-reader heading list. The route title is kept ("Overview", "All tasks", the project name); the frame's second line becomes the subtitle (below). Recorded as a deliberate deviation.
  - *Phone header action.* Frame `GWXOi` shows a "Search" action on the phone Tasks header. #835 chose one "New task" action on these routes at every width, Search is in the drawer, and `New task` has no other phone entry. Kept as is.
  - *Recent results strip (Scope bullet 1) cannot be built as drawn.* The strip shows "Completed · Delivery audit … result R-88 …" with a result excerpt. `TaskListSummary` has no result, timestamp or counter, no endpoint lists results across tasks (`/api/operator/search` needs a query), and fanning out one task read per Done task cannot order them by recency. The epic bars contract changes made for layout. Instead the Overview ends with one honest "Completed work" line, derived from the task list: "N completed task(s) · no decision needed" and a "View completed" link to `/app/tasks?state=Done` (needed anyway because Active tasks hides Done). It keeps SPEC's "recent results shown separately" intent and its label does not claim recency. A real strip needs a separate read-model slice with Chris's go-ahead; that is not created here and is listed in the PR as a gap.
  - *Short identifiers (Scope bullet 4).* AT-142, A-104, Q-204 and R2 are per-project, per-task and per-result counters that exist only in the fixtures: no read model carries them (`projectSummarySchema`, `taskListSummarySchema`, `assignmentSchema`, `result` have none), `docs/SPEC.md` and CONTEXT.md define no scheme, and a UUID-derived handle would look sequential and is not. The three screens in this slice show no raw UUID today (UUIDs appear only in `data-task-id` and hrefs). So this slice adds none: imported tasks show `repository#number` (the identity the frames draw as `acme/atlas#142`), local tasks show "Local task" as most frames do, and a browser assertion proves no UUID-shaped text appears on Overview, List and Board at both viewports. Q-, A- and R- identifiers belong to the request and result screens (U4, U5) and need counters the read model lacks. Recorded for the PR.
- **Active tasks is the default state view.** Scope names the dropdowns "All projects" and "Active tasks"; frames list six columns (Ready, Running, Waiting, Paused, Stopping, Uncertain) and "8 active tasks". `state` gets three meanings: absent = Active tasks (every column except Done and Cancelled, so Draft stays visible and no unfinished work disappears), `all` = All tasks, or one column name. A specific Done or Cancelled filter adds that column to the Board. The State dropdown's options are "Active tasks" (value empty), "All tasks" (`all`) and each column in the new order Ready, Running, Waiting, Paused, Stopping, Uncertain, Draft, Done, Cancelled (frame order for the six drawn, Draft after them, terminal states last). Old `?state=Done` style links still work. UI03 "all states remain reachable" holds through the dropdown and the Completed-work link.
- **Overview attention reads the Inbox, not the task list.** Frame 01 draws one row per request ("Intervention · Jonas · 10:59", "Question · 09:14", "Approval · Mira · 10:52"), with project/task, a message and one action. Today the Overview previews tasks with `attention.count > 0`. `InboxItem` has exactly those facts (`kind`, `projectName`, `taskTitle`, `requesterName`, `createdAt`, `reason`, `destination`), the shell already reads the whole Inbox off the Inbox route for the sidebar count, and the page-owned refresh already re-reads it. `TaskViews` gets one new prop, `requests: ResourceState<InboxRead>` (the type derived locally from `ReturnType<typeof loadInbox>`, so `inbox.tsx` is not edited). Rows come from `requests.data.items` in server order (urgency, then oldest), capped at three with "N more in the Inbox" below; the "N unresolved" badge uses `inboxSummaryOf` so it equals the sidebar count and is omitted when the read is partial or failed. The action wording is shared with U4 and the task views: question "Answer question", approval "Review material & decide", intervention "Inspect execution". The frame's "Choose audience" is the question's prompt, which the summary-only queue does not carry. Targets: question `/app/inbox?task=<taskId>&request=<id>` (the Inbox's own `choose()` URL), approval and intervention `item.destination`. Time is "HH:MM" local from `createdAt`; a missing time reads "Age unknown" and a missing requester "Responsibility unknown", the Inbox's existing strings. The frame's relative age ("1h 46m ago") appears on one row only and needs a clock tick, so it is omitted. Failure states: `ResourceStatus` with label "Requests" (loading, stale with a retry, error with "Try again"); an incomplete read adds the Inbox's own notice "Queue coverage is incomplete. Unavailable requests may remain." The attention rows carry `data-request-id`, never `data-task-id`, and the action link's accessible name is only the action (the task is attached by `aria-describedby`), so existing `getByRole("link", { name: <task title> }).first()` journeys still reach the task row.
- **Overview work list shows every active task.** Frame 01 lists tasks that also appear in attention ("Restore webhook delivery"), so the attention-free filter on `work` is dropped.
- **Task row (Overview compact and List table) from recorded facts only.** One markup, two CSS layouts, class names `task-row`, `task-title`, `task-status`, `task-lead` kept for the existing selectors and the `.task-title` wait in the `ux800-matrix` journey. Line one is the title link (the whole row is clickable through a stretched pseudo-element on the link) and the meta "Project · Local task" or "Project · acme/atlas#142"; the state is an icon plus the word `taskColumn`; the next actor is derived, not guessed: any `attention.codes` gives "Next: you · <action>" with the action wording by code (`execution-uncertain` "inspect execution", `approval` "review material & decide", `question` "answer question", `unresolved-result`, `completion-rejected`, `lead-review` "review task"); a Done task reads "Next: none · no decision" and a Cancelled one "Next: none · history retained" (frame `zeoGi`, derived from `taskColumn` alone, never read as success for cancellation); everything else reads "No operator decision"; each `taskReasons` string stays its own element so exact-text selectors still match; the lead reads "Mira · lead" or "No lead configured". Not derivable and not shown: "check failed", "repair assignment A-108", "Repair owner unknown" (they need assignment and check records the list summary lacks). A closed or unavailable GitHub issue keeps its `GitHub source: closed` text; an `open` one shows nothing extra (the frames draw none).
- **Filters.** The frames draw two inline dropdowns and the switch on one row, replacing the stacked labelled selects. The accessible names stay "Project" and "State" so `getByLabel` and `test/ui07/runtime-contract.mjs` still work; the visible text is the selected option. The existing "Search tasks" text filter and the Source and Readiness selects are not drawn but are existing capabilities with URL parameters and tests, so they move into a native `<details>` "More filters" below the row: closed by default, open when any of `q`, `source`, `ready` is set, never closed by the component itself. Row order follows the frames: on Overview dropdowns then switch with no count; on `/app/tasks` and project routes switch, dropdowns, then "N tasks". On phone the dropdowns and count come first, the switch below.
- **Refresh tasks, observation and project links.** "Refresh tasks" is the page-owned refresh U1 introduced and many tests click; the frames draw none. It stays, as a small ghost button at the end of the toolbar, and its accessible name is unchanged. The "Task states read hh:mm–hh:mm." line stays as muted text under the list or board (SPEC keeps known/stale state legible) and no test asserts it. On project routes "Project settings" and "Open existing project controls" stay as a muted link row directly under the page header (the #835 fallback agreement); the paused notice stays above them.
- **Board.** Link bar: one toolbar named "Board columns" with a ghost button per visible column labelled "Ready · 0" with the column name first, `aria-pressed` on the selected one; every count shows. The frame bolds the columns currently in view; here only the selected one is emphasised (recorded). Empty columns collapse to a 150px strip (`data-empty="true"`) whose text is "None ready. Held Ready work is in Waiting." for Ready and "No tasks" for the rest; non-empty columns are flexible with a 360px minimum; the area scrolls horizontally on desktop and shows one selected column on phone. Each column keeps `aria-label="<Column> tasks"` and an `h2` "Ready · 0". Selected-column state clamps to the visible column count because `history.state.board.selected` is an index and the column list changed. Phone: tabs in a 3-column grid, 44px high (`kZTPH`); previous and next move to the neighbouring column, are labelled "← Running" and "Paused →", carry `aria-label` "Previous column: Running" and "Next column: Paused", and the disabled end shows "1 of 7" style text; they sit below the column as in frame `GWXOi`. The frame's "task 1 of 3" and "N more waiting tasks" are static-frame artefacts (a column scrolls vertically, per `e839O`), the per-card readiness footnote under the phone card needs recorded text the summary lacks, and the footer "Columns 1–3 of 6" needs scroll maths; the footer reads "Scroll horizontally or choose a column above. Empty columns are collapsed." and the rest is recorded as not built.
- **Card as drawn (`cjNBk`).** Title link; "Project · acme/atlas#142 ↗" where the identity is an external link only when `source.url` parses as `https:` (otherwise plain text; zod's `url()` also accepts `javascript:`), with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; state icon and word; each reason; the next-actor line; for a task with attention and a known request, one action link ("Answer question →", "Review material & decide →", "Inspect execution →") built from `requests.data.items` grouped by `taskId` (first item), nothing when the Inbox read is unavailable; a footer with the lead's initial in a 22px circle, "Mira · accountable lead" and a decorative ↗. Padding is the frame-measured 12px (the unlayered `.task-card` padding rule already outranks the Card primitive's layered p-4 from #835; the browser test asserts the computed value, so a regression shows). Icons: Ready `CircleDot`, Running `LoaderCircle`, Waiting `Clock`, Paused `Pause`, Stopping `Square`, Uncertain `CircleQuestionMark`, Draft `FilePen`, Done `CircleCheck`, Cancelled `CircleX`; request kinds `CircleAlert` (intervention and approval) and `CircleQuestionMark` (question). All verified to exist in `lucide-react` 1.54.
- **Attention summary above List and Board (T6).** Frames 24, 18, 18b, 23 and 25 all draw a persistent bar, and the Board note `e839O` makes it part of the contract ("Stopping and Uncertain remain named tabs with counts, plus the persistent attention summary and Inbox link"). It is derived from the task list in scope (all tasks, or the project's): the first active task with the `execution-uncertain` attention code, else the first in the Stopping column. Uncertain: "Inspect execution · <title>", "<lead or Responsibility unknown> · execution may still be active; ownership stays held.", action "Inspect execution". Stopping: "Stopping · <title>", "Next: runtime · confirm execution ended. No operator request recorded.", action "Open task". Both link to `/app/tasks/:id`. At the right, "Inbox · N" (N from `inboxSummaryOf`, plain "Inbox" when unknown) links to `/app/inbox`. With none of those tasks the bar is absent. The phone frame draws a shorter two-line variant ("Uncertain 1 →"); the same bar reflows instead (recorded). The Overview keeps its own attention section and has no bar.
- **Styles live in `web/src/work.css`**, imported by `web/src/task-views.tsx`, so this slice does not append to `styles.css` where U2 and U4 also work; T7 only deletes the superseded `.task-filters`, `.task-row*`, `.task-card`, `.attention-preview`, `.column-*`, `.board-*` and `.phone-column-controls` rules from `styles.css` (and their copies in the `max-width: 760px` block). Frame measurements to match within 2px: attention row pitch 83px with a 34px tile (radius 10) and its action button right-aligned; Overview work-row pitch 69px; List row pitch 53px with columns title/meta, state, next and reasons, lead; board column radius 14 on `--card`, column gap 12, card padding 12, collapsed column 150px.
- **Baseline.** Trusted evidence at `116f12e0`: the push CI run `37977907208` passes install, typecheck, lint and format on both jobs and runs 1213 tests with 1211 passing and exactly one failure per job, `operator-ux800-browser` "finite Chromium and WebKit matrix" (the Node 26 job also marks one test cancelled behind it). Locally, in a scratch clone of `116f12e0` after `npm ci` and `npm run build` on Node v26.9.0, `dist/test/operator-task-list.test.js` passes 12 of 12. The planner's browser-suite run was not completed because the host load average was above 50 (U1 recorded the same load-flake pattern); the browser baseline therefore rests on the CI run above and the green PR run of #851. The one failure is a test-harness defect, not a product regression: its error `browser.launch.webkit: dependency-skipped after 0 ms` is `BrowserJourney.start` refusing a launch once the 15s `startupMs` window is spent. That window opens at the first `journey.start` (fixture creation) and so also covers the whole Chromium pass; the test never calls `journey.restart()` before the WebKit launch. The PR run of #851 passed because the Chromium pass just fit. Every slice here adds work to that route matrix, so T1 repairs it first, with the one-line `journey.restart()` the other browser suites already use.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/tasks.ts` — `columns` (L8, current order Stopping…Ready), `taskColumn` (L67), `TaskFilters` / `parseTaskFilters` / `taskFiltersUrl` / `filterTasks` (L82–L128), `reasonLabels`, `taskReasons` (L130–L170). Unit-tested by `test/operator-task-list.test.ts` (≈L296–L370: `parseTaskFilters("?…state=bad…")` returns `state: ""`; `filterTasks` with `state=Paused`).
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-views.tsx` (390 lines) — `TaskContents`, `TaskRow`, `TaskCard`, `TaskBoard` (button toolbar "Board columns", `column-tab`, `phone-column-controls`, `board-columns` scroller, `history.state.board`), `TaskViews` (props `state, refresh, workspace, path, navigate, projectId, overview`; the `.task-actions` row with "Refresh tasks", the "Task states read" line, the `attention-preview` Card, the stacked `.task-filters` fields, the `.view-toggle` buttons "List" / "Board"). Only `App` renders `TaskViews`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/app.tsx` — `inboxSummary` (`useOperatorResource(scope, inboxLoader, !onInboxRoute)`), `refreshAll` (workspace and, off the Inbox route, `inboxSummary.refresh()`), `taskRoute`, `headerSubtitle` (static intro strings for task routes), the `<TaskViews …>` call at the end of the route chain, `ownsRefresh`. `web/src/inbox.tsx` exports `loadInbox`, `inboxSummaryOf`, `InboxState`. `web/src/components.tsx` has `StatusBadge`, `ResourceStatus`, `ActionLink`, `PageHeader`; `web/src/ui/{button,card,native-select,badge}.tsx` are the primitives (`NativeSelect` wraps the select in a full-width span; style it from `work.css`, do not edit the primitive).
- **Existing contract facts:** `taskListSummarySchema` (`src/operator/contracts.ts` ≈L888) has `project`, `lead {profileId,name}|null`, `execution`, `admission.reasons`, `source {repositoryName, number, url, state}|null`, `attention {codes, count}`; `workspaceSchema` carries `projects` (with `leadProfileId`) and `profiles`. `InboxItem` (≈L2224) as in Planning decisions; `readInbox` (`src/standalone/operator-api.ts` ≈L2165) builds interventions with `requesterName: null`, `createdAt: null`.
- **Existing tests touched:** `test/operator-task-browser.test.ts` (`seedCatalog` ≈L793, `until` ≈L765; List/Board journey; `.task-list .task-row`, `.task-lead`, `.task-status`, `.task-project-metadata`, `.task-source-state` at ≈L1100–L1145; Overview regions ≈L1349–L1400; board loop ≈L1440–L1550; "Search tasks" ≈L74, L126, L1667), `test/operator-ux800-browser.test.ts` (`layoutProblems` squeezed-fact check on `.task-row > *`; WebKit launch ≈L92), `test/operator-ux800-shell-browser.test.ts` (focus journey with "Search tasks" ≈L273–L300; subtitle ≈L441; `New task` link counts ≈L444–L458; refresh ownership ≈L513), `test/operator-delivery-integration-browser.test.ts` (≈L255–L295: State "Done", "Board columns" button text `/\(1\)/`, `GitHub org/repo #1`, `/GitHub source:/`), `test/operator-foundation-browser.test.ts` (≈L383 `.column-tab` 32px/radius 10), `test/operator-web-browser.test.ts` (clicks "Refresh tasks"; unchanged), `test/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.ts` (≈L173–L198: `getByRole("link", { name: /Origin inspection/ }).first()` from Overview and project routes). Browser suites use `browserSuite(name)`, `createOperatorFixture`, `f.startWeb()`, `captureBrowserEvidence`, `seedOwnQuestion` (`test/fixtures/questions.ts`).
- **New:** `web/src/request-presentation.ts` — pure `requestKindLabel`, `requestActionLabel`, `requestHref`, `requestTime`, `requestMeta`. #838's plan names `requestKindLabel`, `requestActionLabel`, `ageLabel` and `clockLabel` in `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts`; whichever issue merges second imports the first's module and deletes its duplicate (same strings, kept by the pure test), recorded in the PR.
- **New:** `web/src/task-filters.tsx` — `TaskToolbar`; `web/src/task-attention.tsx` — `AttentionSection`, `AttentionBar`, `CompletedWork`; `web/src/work.css`; `test/operator-work-presentation.test.ts` (pure); `test/operator-work-browser.test.ts` (`browserSuite("ui08-work")`); `test/fixtures/operator-work.ts` (`seedCatalog` and `until` moved verbatim out of `operator-task-browser.test.ts`, plus `openMoreFilters(page)`).

### Review focus

- Overlap, as the implementer must handle it. **#836 (U2, plan 6088157840)** edits `web/src/app.tsx` (`Login` removal, `AccountFooter`, `expired()`/`logout()`, the final fallback ternary, header `action`/`ownsRefresh`), `web/src/components.tsx` (`PageHeader` divider option), `web/src/styles.css` (`.login*`, `.account-footer` ≈L215, `.logout-notice` ≈L295, the ≤1120px drawer rules ≈L688–L765), `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` and `design/DESIGN.md`, and the Sign out selectors in `operator-web-browser`, `operator-ux800-shell-browser`, `operator-foundation-browser`, `operator-search-browser`, `operator-question-browser`, `operator-comments-browser`, `operator-local-review-browser` and `operator-settings-browser`. This plan's only `app.tsx` edits are the `taskRoute` branch of `headerSubtitle` and one `requests` prop on `<TaskViews>`; its `styles.css` change is deletion of the `.task-filters`…`.phone-column-controls` blocks (≈L307–L450 and their copies in the 760px block), directly after `.logout-notice`, so expect a trivial adjacent-hunk conflict. Both plans edit `operator-ux800-shell-browser.test.ts` (this one at ≈L273–L300, ≈L441) and the docs. **#838 (U4, plan 6088510318)** edits `web/src/inbox.tsx`, `question-response*.ts*`, `.page-inbox` (≈L246 and ≈L768 inside the 760px block), `.inbox-*` and `.question-*`, an `onHeader` prop on `<Inbox>` and the `headerSubtitle`/`PageHeader` merge in `app.tsx` right beside this plan's `taskRoute` branch, `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` and the same two docs. This plan edits none of its files, and its `requestKindLabel`/`requestActionLabel` strings must equal #838's. **#828** edits `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`, `local-review.tsx`, `lead-feedback.ts`, `src/core/coordination.ts`, `src/core/local-review.ts`, `src/standalone/coordination-view.ts`, `operator-api.ts` and `src/operator/contracts.ts` (additive `leadFeedback`, `resumedLead`); this plan reads `taskListSummarySchema` and `inboxItemSchema` only and edits none of those files. If #828 adds an Inbox kind, `requestKindLabel` and `requestActionLabel` must stay exhaustive over the enum so the type check fails, not the UI. If either sibling merges first, fetch and rebase before each slice's validation and re-run its command.
- Privacy and safety: no command is sent from these screens; the external source link is built only from an `https:` URL with `noopener noreferrer`; attention rows show only summary-queue facts and no prompt text.
- The default flip: Done and Cancelled leave the default views. Check every consumer of `filterTasks` and every test that expects a completed task without an explicit state; the Completed-work link and the State dropdown are the way back.
- The `ux800-matrix` route journey visits `/app`, `/app/tasks` and project routes at many sizes in two engines; row and toolbar changes must not add squeezed facts, clipped controls or page overflow there, and `.task-title` must still exist on those routes.
- Accessibility: keyboard order (toolbar, More filters, rows or cards), visible focus on stretched row links, labels containing the visible text on the previous/next buttons, state shown by word as well as icon and colour.

### Allowed deviations (when task-specific)

- Fixture and selector changes, class renames (with test selectors updated), icon substitutions from `lucide-react`, copy that differs only in punctuation, and CSS values within 2px of the exported frames or within the shared tokens are routine. A different seam than this plan names for the shell's Inbox read, the Inbox selection URL, the source URL or the `TaskListSummary` fields is a plan mismatch and uses the diagnosis and repair budget.
- If the "More filters" disclosure proves unworkable for the existing "Search tasks" journeys, an always-visible compact text input at the end of the toolbar is allowed, with the same label and URL parameter; record it.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- A decision to build the Recent results strip with real data, a short-identifier scheme, or any other field on `taskListSummarySchema` or `inboxItemSchema`: those are server read-model changes outside this slice.
- Evidence that the shell's whole-Inbox read cannot be made available to `TaskViews` without changing `inbox.tsx` or the Inbox route's resource ownership, or a #838 change to the `/app/inbox?task=…&request=…` selection URL.
- Chris changing the page titles, the phone header action, or the Active-tasks default.

content.title: U5: Match task detail, composer and Stop confirmation to the design

nodes.body:
**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/839 **Planned against:** `main` at `bcf658f2ae722e061fe771cefc65fca671f6e819` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach Six slices on one branch (`cb/issue-839-task-detail-composer-stop`), then one PR, with no `src/**`, contract or API change. **Implementation starts only after #828 (PR #855) has merged**, because it rewrites the Reply composer, the "Ask lead about …" drafts and the resumed receipts in `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`; this plan is written on top of those seams (see Planning decisions, "#828"). T1 adds pure presentation helpers with unit tests. T2 replaces the in-body button stack with the designed header (task title, status line, **Execution** and **Stop…**) and builds the Stop confirmation. T3 recomposes the task page: the persistent decision card, then two columns (Shared brief on the left; Latest result with C1/C2 criteria rows, entry links and Assignments rows on the right), with the deeper inspection sections kept below under their current ids. T4 restyles the Reply card through `web/src/lead-feedback.ts` and wires `requesterName` into the task-page question. T5 rebuilds the composer (right-hand "Inherited from" panel, one Optional settings row with a summary and error count, fixed actions, phone states 34/35/35b). T6 records docs and the frame comparison and runs the full check. New React code goes in new files so the existing 2,000-line `task-workspace.tsx` and the shared `styles.css` change in small, separate regions; U2 #836 (PR #857), U3 #837 and U4 #838 edit the same shell files. Source contract (retrievable, not restated): the issue's Scope and Acceptance; epic #834 Boundaries; `design/DESIGN.md` ("Reviewed task overview design", "Layout and responsive composition", "Interaction guidance", "Screen reference map"); `docs/SPEC.md` "Execution and recovery", "Task overview and evidence", "Task detail", "Task creation and project setup"; `docs/acceptance.md` "Task overview and evidence design review"; PR #851's Deferrals. A conflict between this plan and those sources is a re-plan trigger. Frames (read through Pen MCP on 10 October 2026, exported at scale 1; re-export them, never parse `design/design.pen`): task detail desktop `MRbe2` (46a) and full-content `TG3LC` (46), result and entry links `gAT6T` (57), phone task `YFLwX` (47), phone empty/failed/parallel `Crq7h`, `F2OKCj`, `qCkVq`, expanded brief `vesIN`, earlier references `RyH7J` (03a), `oipj4`, `Q24BPH`, `kiPK9`, `biA7p` (12); Stop confirmation `uQrNE` (132); composer `Z315o` (02a), `MhM7z` (02), notes `s34356`, phone `i3glx` (34), `wXiWx` (35), `JX4dm` (35b). Export with `Export([...ids],"png",,{scale:1})` after `get_app_state` in the same invocation (the first call can take about 60s and may say "wrong .pen file"). ### Guardrails - Behaviour, contracts and safety do not change because a layout changes. Unchanged: every command, receipt and key in `task-workspace.tsx` (`send`, `command`, frozen operations, `ask`), the exact-reference drafts, the unknown-outcome reconciliation, `LocalReviewProvider`/`LocalReviewPanel`, `TaskFiles`, `Changes`, `RetainedResultEvidence`, history paging and its anchors, the `?section=`, `record=`, `request=`, `result=`, `source=` deep links and their section ids (`brief`, `files`, `review`, `context`, `changes`, `local-review`, `history`, `reply`), and "viewing is not approval". The document stays the single scroll owner (no nested scroller), because reading-position restoration uses `window` scroll and `[data-record-id]` anchors. - Authority: Stop in the app is a confirmation in front of the **existing** retained `POST /runtime/control/stop` form, not a new command (see Planning decisions). Nothing here adds an `OperatorCommand`, a route, a read field or a write path. #828 compatibility: `web/src/lead-feedback.ts` stays the single source of lead-feedback copy; its three exports (`leadFeedbackMode`, `leadResumeNotice`, `leadAwaitingRecoveryNotice`) keep their text; the #828 tests (`operator-task-workspace-browser`, `operator-local-review-browser`, `operator-review-browser`, `operator-follow-up`, `operator-contracts`) must not regress. - Out of scope: `src/**`; `web/src/local-review.tsx`; the internals of `task-files.tsx`, `inspection-changes.tsx`, `retained-evidence.tsx` (workspace inspection shipped with #782); sign-in, account menu and not found (U2); Overview, List and Board bodies and `web/src/work.css` (U3); Inbox and the `QuestionResponse` internals (U4); settings and profiles (U6); project setup (U7); `design/design.pen`; a task-level Pause (no command exists; project pause stays in settings); an in-app Resume; the paused X01–X08 work. The shared `.task-actions` rule in `web/src/styles.css` stays (search, files, review, composer still use it). - Two kinds of repair, kept separate. (1) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (a named symbol, prop, route, id, field or test seam does not behave as this plan says; for example the retained Stop route rejects the app's form post, or the `criteria[].position` rule below is wrong) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; after that, stop and re-plan. (2) Ordinary implementation defects belong to the ticket owner and do not count against that budget: integration breakage, failing or flaky tests and fixtures, selector and copy migration, type, lint and format errors, CSS, docs, CI and screenshot-journey repairs. Investigate unknown overlap with #828, #836, #837 and #838 before continuing. Stop for a material design or contract change or exhausted grants. Return human-required only if the accepted contract itself must change: a new authority surface (an in-app Stop or Resume command, a Stop with its own receipt), a new read field (project instruction text, repository access, short IDs) or a changed Stop guarantee. - If a frame contradicts the issue Scope, follow the frame where repository evidence supports it and record the choice in the PR (the choices already made are in Planning decisions). Frames that the repository cannot support (no read field, no command) are recorded as gaps, not built. - Browser tests wait deterministically. After `goto`, wait for `main.page h1` and then for the specific element under test before reading anything; `evaluateAll`, `count()`, `isVisible()` and `textContent()` do not wait (the 9 and 10 October CI flakes were exactly this, plus a shared startup window). Use locator `waitFor`, `page.waitForURL`, `page.waitForFunction` or an awaited response, and assert "does not happen" (no POST after Keep running) only after awaiting a positive signal that the interaction finished. When an engine loop is needed, run each engine as its own test or call `journey.restart()` before each launch (#853), and keep each journey under the 45s execution limit by splitting concerns. Do not add `--test-timeout=0` or any unbounded wait; any `page.route` that holds a request is released and unrouted in `finally`. - Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews; use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. - `npm run lint` fails on warnings. New role/ARIA markup must pass `biome lint --error-on-warnings`. ### Planning decisions - **Frames over Scope wording, and which frames.** The issue lists frames 02, 02a, 03, 03a, 12–15, 34–55 and 132. Two generations disagree: 03a (`RyH7J`), 12 (`biA7p`) and 36/37/45 draw "Pause task" and "Stop…" with a "Current holds" side panel (and 12 draws source and execution panes), while the 3 October task overview (46/46a `MRbe2`/`TG3LC`, 47, 57 `gAT6T`) draws **Execution** and **Stop…**, a decision card, "Shared brief" beside "Latest result", and Assignments rows. The issue Scope ("two columns… Execution, Stop…") matches the second set, DESIGN.md calls it the reviewed shared task experience and says frame 54 "specifies the shared change rather than duplicating every screen", so 46/46a/57 govern the layout for every task. No task-level Pause exists in the read or command contracts, so "Pause task" is not built. Imported tasks keep their source/execution separation through provenance labels ("REQUIREMENTS · GITHUB"), the source line with "View source" and the hold alert, not through separate panes. Record this in the PR. - **Stop confirms in the app, then uses the retained form.** `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` (the control table `test/operator-control-inventory.test.ts` reads) and `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` retain `/runtime/control/stop` (fields `taskId`, `csrfToken`; no key) at `/runtime/task/:id`, and `OperatorCommand` has no stop. So the confirm button is a native `
` with hidden `csrfToken` (the app's `session.csrfToken`, the same value `OperatorAuth.validateCsrf` checks) and `taskId`. The server answers 303 to `/runtime/task/`, where the retained page shows the Stop observation and Resume. **Evidence (planner, executed):** in a scratch clone at this SHA, a throwaway browser test signed in, opened `/app/tasks/`, submitted exactly that form from the React page and, in Chromium and WebKit, the request carried `Origin: `, the browser landed on `/runtime/task/`, and a following `GET /api/operator/tasks/` read `execution.state: "stopping"`, `holds.stop: true`. `authorizeWrite` only checks session and `Origin`, and the app CSP has `form-action 'self'`. T2's Stop test repeats this as a permanent check; if the retained route ever rejects the app's post, that is a seam mismatch (budget), and an in-app fetch Stop would be a human decision. Consequence recorded in the PR: Stop leaves the SPA (as the existing "Runtime / Stop / Resume" link already does), so unsent text in this page's reply box is not carried across it; Keep running, Escape and the overlay keep everything. - **Stop counterpart.** The designed rule is that Stop confirms first and reversible states show their counterpart. Resume exists only at `/runtime/task/:id`, which the **Execution** link opens. While `execution.holds.stop` is true the header shows a disabled "Stop requested" in place of "Stop…" and the status line says "Stopping; effects may continue"; **Execution** stays. No Resume button is added here (new write path, a gap recorded for the PR). - **Dialog copy (frame 132, `uQrNE`).** Title "Stop ?". Body: " (lead) and N delegated assignments are affected." (N counts assignments other than the lead that are not completed or cancelled; singular "1 delegated assignment is affected"; no lead: "This task's assignments are affected."), then the three consequence lines and the footnote exactly as drawn: "Holds queued and new turns for the lead and every delegated assignment." / "Requests cancellation of active turns. Effects may continue after the observation window." / "Stop, writer and capacity holds stay until termination is verified. Resume clears only Stop." / "Stop is not cancellation or completion. Files, history and results are kept." Buttons "Stop task" (destructive) and "Keep running" (outline). It uses `role="alertdialog"` on the existing `@radix-ui/react-dialog` (no new dependency), initial focus on **Keep running**, Escape and overlay press cancel, and focus returns to the trigger. The wording matches SPEC "Execution and recovery". - **Header seam carries data, not elements.** `TaskWorkspace` reports plain data to `app.tsx` (`TaskHeaderReport`: `title`, `subtitle`, `back {href, label, history?}`, `stop {taskId, title, lead, delegated, held}` or null, `executionHref`) from an effect keyed on its JSON, and clears it on unmount; `app.tsx` renders `TaskHeaderActions` from it. That keeps the dialog's state in one place, avoids render loops, and lets sign-out and expiry reset it (`expired()`, `logout()` and `taskStates.purge()` are the existing reset points). If #838 has merged its `onHeader` state, extend that state with a second variant instead of adding a parallel one; the two routes are mutually exclusive. - **One back control.** The in-body "Back to originating view" / "Back to project" row is removed (U1's deferral: on phone it duplicated the header Back). The header Back replaces it on every width: with an in-session `history.state.origin` it renders as a link named "Back to originating view" that calls `history.back()` (and `preventDefault()` so the app's document click handler does not push a new entry); otherwise a link named "Back to " to `/app/projects/`. `PageHeader` gains optional `back.history`/`back.ariaLabel` and a `desktopBack` flag (the base CSS hides the Back on desktop); #857 adds `plain` to the same props. - **No short identifiers.** AT-142, A-104, R2 and V-22 are not in any read model, and U3 #837 recorded the same decision. Local tasks show "Local task"; imported tasks show `repository#number`; assignments show profile name plus a responsibility excerpt with the first eight characters of the assignment id as 12px muted metadata (two assignments on one profile stay distinguishable); results keep "Result N". The frames' breadcrumb ("Atlas / List · Waiting · AT-142") becomes a Back link labelled by the origin view or project name, with the status line carrying state. - **C1/C2 come from the existing criteria records.** `src/core/task-review.ts` creates `criteria[]` from literal checklist lines (`/^\s*[-*+]\s+\[[ xX]\]\s+(.+)$/`) with `position` equal to the line index in `body`, capped at 128 with `criteriaOmittedCount` for the rest. So the brief prose is `body` minus the lines whose index is a retained criterion's `position`, with blank runs collapsed; omitted overflow lines stay as literal text, and a null `body` shows the existing coverage gap. Labels are `C`. The full literal brief stays one click away in the existing `Disclosure` ("read supplied text"), so `- [ ]` still appears there and only there. Criterion outcome rows use the recorded `outcome` per criterion ("Supported by recorded evidence", "Failed recorded check", "Unverified"), keep "stale source revision" and the duplicate-identity warning, and show scope and provenance as 12px metadata. **No overall pass is derived** from agent claims, missing checks or a count of supported rows (SPEC). - **Not built because nothing records it.** The frames' "Approach · Mira / A-104" (no recorded approach field; the lead's own assignment appears in Assignments), short IDs, "Compare screenshots" as a separate control (recorded before/after pairs already render under Latest result in `ReviewEvidence`), "Today · 11:00" clocks, and phone drill-in subviews (frames 47/48/51/55 push "Result & evidence" and "Assignments" screens). The phone keeps one reading column and the same in-place disclosures, because drill-in screens would need new history entries and would put reading position, expanded groups and unsent replies (DESIGN "Updates") at risk. "Message lead" is a link to the Reply section; Stop and Execution stay in the header at every width so Stop is never below the fold. - **The section-button row is replaced by contextual entries.** The `nav aria-label="Task sections"` row (eight section links) is removed as the issue says. Frame 57 draws the contextual entries that replace it under the latest result: **Files**, **Changes**, **Review (n)**, "Assignment context & identifiers" and "Changes & delivery →". They are in-page anchors to `#files`, `#changes`, `#local-review`, `#context` and `#history`, using the existing `showSection` (no history entry), and they are the only visible way to reach Files and Changes, so they are not optional. "Review (n)" counts local-review draft comments when the draft is known, otherwise it reads "Review". - **Retained controls stay reachable.** "Advanced task controls" (`/task/:id`, the only edit path for a local task's title and outcome), "Requests and coordination" (`/coordination/task/:id`) and "Open GitHub to edit source" remain visible links in the source line and decision card; "Runtime / Stop / Resume" becomes the header's **Execution**. - **Composer panel contents.** Frame 02a's right panel shows the lead, the instruction text and repository access. `composerOptionsSchema` carries the lead (`name`), capacity, `paused` and `routingEnabled`; project instructions are write-only private values (`ui06`) and no read exposes repository access. So the panel, titled "Inherited from ", shows Accountable lead (name or "Unconfigured"), the lead profile's public `summary` when `Workspace.profiles` lists it, routing mode, the existing paused, no-lead and "Capacity: a/b project · c/d global…" lines (kept verbatim, tests match them), a "View project instructions" link to `/app/projects//settings`, and the drawn "Created ≠ running" note. Instruction text and repository access are recorded gaps; adding either read is a human decision. - **Optional settings is one disclosure.** Replace the four `.composer-disclosure` blocks with one `details.composer-disclosure` holding the same four fields (ids `composer-context`, `composer-links`, `composer-profileId`, `composer-blockerTaskIds` and labels unchanged, so `getByLabel` selectors keep working). Summary: "Optional settings · none supplied", "· N supplied" or "· N error(s)" (errors win); below it, while collapsed, two lines of supplied values ("Context: …", "Reference: …", "Assignee: Eli (permitted)", "Depends on: …"). The error reveal logic (`reveal`, `sectionOf`, the `unavailable` effect) keeps working with one section id. "Unfinished input saved on this device" is shown only after a successful `writeRecovery` (`ComposerState.savedOnDevice`), never when storage failed, so the existing "Recovery unavailable…" notice is the only claim in that case. - **Composer heading.** One `h1` per route is a #835 invariant (tests count it). The h1 for `/app/tasks/new` becomes "Create a task" with the drawn subtitle on desktop; frame 34's phone header "New task" plus an in-body "Create a task" is not duplicated. Recorded difference. - **#828 (PR #855), as the implementer must handle it.** After merge, `task-workspace.tsx` holds `leadName`, `leadMode = leadFeedbackMode(data, lead?.state)`, the Reply line `{state.destination === "lead" && lead && leadMode === "resumes" &&

{leadResumeNotice(leadName)}

}`, the unavailable paragraph guarded by `leadMode === "unavailable"`, the Send `disabled` predicate using `leadMode`, the "Receipt recorded. resumed with this feedback." notice, and message rows `{m.requester ? " · requested by …"}`. T3 and T4 move or restyle these without changing their text, conditions or `role="status"`; new lead-delivery copy goes into `lead-feedback.ts` (one added export), never inline. `taskSchema.leadFeedback` is optional, so keep working when it is absent. - **Assumption with a gate.** The two-column CSS grid and the document scroll must keep `showSection`, `scrollTo(0, state.scrollY)` and the `[data-record-id]` anchor restore (`useLayoutEffect` near the `first.current` branch) correct. T3's journey asserts that a poll refresh with an expanded assignment and a typed reply moves the scroll anchor by at most 1px; if the grid breaks anchoring, switch the columns to a flow layout (CSS multi-column is not used) rather than adding a scroller. - **Baseline.** At `bcf658f2` (CI `check` green, run 38030086226), on Node v26.9.0 after `npm ci` and `npm run build` in a scratch clone, `operator-task-workspace-browser`, `operator-task-browser`, `operator-task-composer` and `operator-foundation-browser` pass (28 tests, 0 failures). The planner did not rerun the full suite. ### Implementation context - **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` — `TaskWorkspace({client, session, taskId, path, state, questionStates, onRefresh})` reads `taskSchema`, owns `command`, `send`, `ask`, history loading and scroll restoration, and renders one `article.task-workspace[aria-label="Task workspace"]`: an in-body `.task-actions` row (back, Refresh task, Advanced task controls, Runtime / Stop / Resume, Requests and coordination), `ResourceStatus`, a `header` (h2 title, badge, lead and execution text), `section.workspace-attention[aria-label="Pending requests and holds"]` (hold paragraphs, `QuestionResponse` for `?request=`, one block per open request with `data-record-id`, completion and unresolved-result links), `nav.task-actions[aria-label="Task sections"]` over `sectionIds`, the "New updates" button, `section#brief` (source line, `Disclosure`, `ChecklistCoverage`, `.literal-preview`, "Ask lead about brief", "Retained source revision" select, GitHub source block with "Open GitHub to edit source" and "Refresh source observation", native and local dependencies), `TaskFiles`, `section#review` ("Evidence review": viewing reference, "Result revision" select, the selected result, "Ask lead about result", `ReviewEvidence`, `RetainedResultEvidence`), `section#context`, `Changes` (`section#changes`), `LocalReviewPanel`, `section#history` and `section#reply`. `ReviewEvidence` renders criteria rows (with "Ask lead about criterion"), decisions, validation records and artifact pairs. - **Existing:** `web/src/app.tsx` — `title` (the `"Task workspace"` branch), `headerSubtitle`, `ownsRefresh` (true for the task route), `parentRoute` (static `/app/tasks` "Tasks" for task detail and a project Back for `/app/tasks/new`), the document click handler that pushes `history.state.origin` for every `/app…` anchor, `expired()`/`logout()` purge points, the `` and `` mounts, and `PageHeader` props. `web/src/components.tsx` — `Button` (`primary`|`secondary` only), `ActionLink`, `PageHeader({title, subtitle, action, badge, menu, back})`, `StatusBadge`. `web/src/ui/button.tsx` already declares a tinted `destructive` variant (`--nova-destructive-bg/-fg`); no route renders it yet (`test/operator-foundation-browser.test.ts` measures the declared classes for that reason). - **Existing:** `web/src/task-composer.tsx` — `TaskComposer` (fields, four `disclosure(...)` calls with `sectionOf`, `reveal`, `.composer-policy`, `.composer-actions`), `web/src/composer-state.ts` — `ComposerState` (`edit`, `discard`, `submit`, `recovered`, `notice`, `errors`, `writeRecovery`), `web/src/styles.css` `.composer*` (≈L452–540, sticky `.composer-actions` with safe-area padding), `.task-workspace*` (≈L853–935, ≈L1580–1660), `.workspace-attention`, `.task-workspace nav.task-actions`. - **Existing:** `src/core/task-review.ts` (≈L335–345: criteria and `position`), `src/core/task-review-contracts.ts` (`reviewMetadataSchema`: criteria outcomes `supported|failed|unverified`, `decisions`, `validations`, `artifacts`), `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`taskSchema`, `assignmentSchema` with `requesterAssignmentId`, `resultDestination`, `waitReason`, `brief`; `executionSchema.holds.stop`; `composerOptionsSchema`), `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` (`/runtime/control/stop`, `/runtime/control/resume`, `operationForm`), `src/standalone/operator.ts` (`authorizeWrite` Origin check, `validateCsrf`). - **New:** `web/src/task-overview.ts` — pure `criterionLabel`, `briefParts`, `criterionRows`, `taskStatusLine`, `stopConsequences`, `assignmentRow`, `originLabel`; `web/src/composer-summary.ts` — pure `optionalSummary`; `web/src/task-header.tsx` — `TaskHeaderReport`, `taskHeaderReport(...)`, `TaskHeaderActions` (Execution link and Stop); `web/src/stop-task.tsx` — `StopTask`; `web/src/ui/dialog.tsx` — shadcn-style wrapper over `@radix-ui/react-dialog`; `web/src/task-detail.tsx` — `SourceLine`, `DecisionCard`, `SharedBrief`, `CriteriaRows`, `EntryLinks`, `AssignmentRows`; `web/src/task-detail.css` and `web/src/composer.css` (imported by their components); `test/operator-task-overview.test.ts`, `test/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-composer-layout-browser.test.ts`. - **Follow:** `test/operator-ux800-shell-browser.test.ts` for `main.page h1` waits, viewport and one-`h1` journeys and the #854 wait; `test/operator-question-browser.test.ts` (engine list) and `test/operator-ux800-browser.test.ts` (`journey.restart()` per engine, #853); `test/fixtures/task-review.ts` `seedReviewTask` (lead "Task lead", body `- [ ] Restore focus\n- [ ] Retain drafts`, `delegatedResult(summary, metadata)`) for criteria and results; `web/src/ui/sheet.tsx` for the Radix Dialog wrapper pattern; `web/src/lead-feedback.ts` (after #828) for single-source copy. ### Implementation slices **Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 and T1 → T5; T6 depends on T4 and T5.
