this plan never edits those files and wires `requesterName` only if U4 has added it. - The `?section=`, `record=` and `request=` deep links, the `showSection` anchors (no history entry), scroll and anchor restoration, expanded assignment groups and unsent replies across refresh (T3 (c), (d)); nothing a test clicks may sit in a closed `<details>`. - Header report equality (no render loop), reset on sign-out, expiry and route change (T2 (e)); the Back handler against the app's document click interception. - Stop: the form posts only to `/runtime/control/stop` with `csrfToken` and `taskId`; a single request on double click; Keep running, Escape and the overlay send nothing; "Stop requested" shows while the hold is recorded; the copy matches SPEC "Execution and recovery" (best effort, effects may continue, Resume clears only Stop, not cancellation). - Honesty: no overall pass from criteria, no "saved on this device" unless the write succeeded, no instruction text or repository access shown, no invented identifiers or approach. - Selector migrations are intentional: "Evidence review" → "Latest result", "Back to originating view" button → link, "Runtime / Stop / Resume" → "Execution", four composer disclosures → one. ### Allowed deviations (when task-specific) - Fixture and selector changes, class renames (with test selectors updated), copy that differs only in punctuation, and spacing, radius and colour values within 2px or the shared tokens are routine. Moving a control within its column or a retained link to a different quiet row is routine if its accessible name and destination are unchanged. Using a different seam for the header report, the Stop transport or the criteria derivation than this plan names is a plan mismatch and uses the diagnosis and repair budget. ### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific) - #828 merges in a shape that no longer provides the `leadFeedbackMode` / `leadResumeNotice` / `leadAwaitingRecoveryNotice` seams, or changes `section#reply` so T4 cannot restyle it without altering its text or conditions. - The retained `POST /runtime/control/stop` rejects the app's form post, requires a key or a new header, or its redirect no longer lands on `/runtime/task/<id>`; or the operator decides Stop must complete inside the app (a new command, a receipt, an in-app Resume). - A requirement for project instruction text, repository access, short identifiers, a recorded approach, a task-level Pause or an overall pass in the UI (each needs a new read or command). - The two-column layout cannot keep scroll-anchor restoration and deep-link behaviour within one document scroller without a nested scroller.

content.title: U6: Match settings, profiles, routing, runtime and recovery to the design

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/840
**Planned against:** `main` at `bcf658f2ae722e061fe771cefc65fca671f6e819`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Planned implementation branch: `cb/issue-840-settings-profiles-routing-runtime-recovery`, one PR closing #840. Start it after #857 (U2) has merged, because both rewrite the same `web/src/app.tsx` title and route region (see T3 Prerequisites). #855 (#828) shares no file with this plan.

### Approach

Ten slices on one branch, no new `OperatorCommand`, route, read field or write authority. T1 adds the pure model (change lists, source rows, headers, summaries) and a "last saved" memory on the draft store. T2 is the only `src/**` change: optional guidance on `routing.configure` and keep markers on `github.configure`, so the forms can edit in place. T3 rebuilds the Settings index (114). T4 adds the settings header seam (titles, breadcrumb trail, sidebar highlight) and rebuilds the two profile pages (122, 123). T5 builds the project configuration shell, the General tab (118) and the phone state cards (121). T6 is the Routing tab (124, 125), T7 the GitHub source tab (119) and T8 the Sync & placement tab (120). T9 rebuilds Runtime (126) and assignment recovery (127, 128). T10 records docs and the frame comparison. `web/src/settings.tsx` keeps only the shared draft controls and `ProjectSetup` (U7 #841 owns it); each screen moves to a new file and new CSS goes in `web/src/settings.css`, so `app.tsx` and `styles.css` change in small regions that U2–U5 also touch.

Source contract (retrievable, not restated): issue #840 Scope and Acceptance; epic #834 Boundaries; `docs/SPEC.md` "Task creation and project setup" (configuration rules, profile summary) and "Assignment routing and accountability"; `design/DESIGN.md` (Screen reference map, "Rules from the 9 October pass"); review notes 130 sections 3, 4 and 6; `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md`; ADR-1009 (the U7 boundary); PR #851's body ("Not changed", "Deferrals"). A conflict between this plan and those sources is a re-plan trigger.

Frames (read through Pen MCP on 10 October 2026, exported at scale 1; re-export them, never parse `design/design.pen`): Settings `vEr15` (114); project General `gi83t` (118), GitHub source `w0ozf` (119), Sync & placement `SBB7W` (120), phone project `Pwzju` (121); profile create `F6d3SQ` (122), configure `O96oS` (123); routing `Z8uZnh` (124), after save `c8af5` (125); runtime `AqYk0` (126), recovery `iEF1o` (127), phone recovery `ur1mr` (128); notes `DuF5u` (130); account menu `DhtZq` (113, U2). Export with `Export(["vEr15","gi83t","w0ozf","SBB7W","Pwzju","F6d3SQ","O96oS","Z8uZnh","c8af5","AqYk0","iEF1o","ur1mr","DuF5u"],"png",<scratch dir>,{scale:1})` after `get_app_state` in the same invocation (the first call can take about 60s). There are no phone frames for the Settings index, profiles, routing or runtime; those layouts are composed from the shell frames and compared by judgement.

### Guardrails

- Behaviour, contracts and safety do not change because a layout changes. Unchanged: the session/CSRF contract; keyed commands with `expectedVersion` per section; draft semantics in `web/src/settings-state.ts` (a conflict keeps input and needs explicit adoption, an unknown outcome freezes edits until `reconcile`, expiry and sign-out purge drafts); private values (project, profile and routing text, search queries, Project filters, repository paths, credential references) are never loaded, echoed or placed in a URL, receipt or evidence file; Settings never resumes work, clears holds or grants repository access; the retained HTML editors (`/project/:id`, `/profile/:id`, `/task/:id`, `/runtime*`, `/coordination*`) stay served and linked. Per the agreed fallback (#835 option (a)), every control this plan does not match keeps its contextual "Advanced …" / "Open existing …" link.
- Out of scope: `ProjectSetup`, `/app/settings/projects/new` and the discovery credential row (U7 #841); sign-in, account menu and not found (U2); task views, Inbox, task detail, composer and Stop (U3–U5); `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`, `local-review.tsx`, `lead-feedback.ts` (#828); `design/design.pen`; any new command type, endpoint, read-model field, persisted timestamp, discovery or picker read; Claude-harness work (#822–#827, which will later add a runtime field to profiles).
- Two kinds of repair, kept separate. (1) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; then stop and re-plan. The assumptions that count: `ConfigurationDrafts` can hold a per-section "last saved" record and re-initialise a recorded draft without changing `CommandLifecycle` behaviour (T1); `DomainStore` can resolve keep markers inside `configureGitHub` before verification and inside `apply` without breaking command-hash replay (T2); the existing read endpoints (project configuration, source observations, runtime, assignment recovery) carry every fact the frames need that this plan marks derivable; `?tab=` on `/app/projects/:id/settings` reaches the client under U2's strict `knownRoute` and the service's path-based `shell()` match (T5); `profile.configure` accepts the partial bodies the forms send (T4). (2) Ordinary implementation defects belong to the ticket owner and never consume that budget: integration breakage, selector migrations, test and fixture repairs (including the baseline flake named below), CSS and layout, docs, CI and screenshot repairs. Investigate unknown overlap with #836–#841 before continuing. Return human-required only if the accepted contract itself must change: a new authority, a persisted "last saved" time or any other new read field, a discovery or picker read for readiness names, a new command type, relaxed repository verification, or removing phone editing.
- Follow the frames over the issue Scope where repository evidence supports it, and record each choice in the PR (the choices made are in Planning decisions).
- Browser tests: after `goto` wait for the signed-in `h1` or a named landmark with a web-first `locator.waitFor()` before any read; no `evaluateAll`, `count()` or `isVisible()` reads on a page that is not ready; poll focus and layout with `waitForFunction`. A journey that launches two engines calls `journey.restart()` before each engine's launch. Keep every journey under the 45s execution limit (split journeys; Chromium for behaviour, one WebKit smoke on the Settings index and project configuration). Release held routes in `finally`. Never pass `--test-timeout=0`. Baseline flake: at `bcf658f2`, "configuration inline validation stale revision and revoked lead failures retain editable input" failed once in a sequential run and passed alone three times, because it reads `document.activeElement` straight after the error text appears while `submitDraft` focuses in `requestAnimationFrame`; T5 repairs it with a polled wait.
- `npm run lint` fails on warnings (#850): new markup must pass `biome lint --error-on-warnings`; use semantic elements.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **In-place editing needs two API changes, and no more (T2).** SPEC "Configuration forms edit current values in place" and the issue ("Add API support where the build still requires complete replacement") are authoritative; `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` still documents routing and source writes as complete replacements. `project.configure` and `profile.configure` already omit what is unchanged, and the capacity form is fully public. Two commands still force a complete replacement: `routing.configure` (guidance is required, so a save without guidance clears it) and `github.configure` (every selection and repository link, with private queries, filters and paths, must be re-sent). Decision: `guidance` becomes optional on `routing.configure` (omitted keeps the saved text, an explicit empty string still clears it); in `github.configure` a selection may be `{id, keep: true}` and a repository link may omit `path`, both resolved by the service from the configuration at the fenced `expectedVersion`. Same command types, actor, version fence, receipt shape and verification; the legacy HTML editors keep sending complete bodies. No read field is added. This is a new input shape of an existing write, not a new authority; it amends the UI06 doc's "complete explicit replacement" paragraph, which T10 rewrites.
- **Add and Remove only for sources.** Existing selection rows are shown read-only (kind, owner/name or Project node id, active or inactive; "Private query kept" for a search) and can be removed; a changed definition is a Remove plus an Add. New selections get a generated id `S-<n>` above every id saved or in the draft, so a new definition never reuses a removed id. That matters: `DomainStore.apply("github.configure")` keeps `project_github_active` rows for ids that stay in the list, so a same-id replacement would keep a stale activation. That is existing server behaviour the UI never triggers; it is listed for the owner as a follow-up, not changed here. New sources are therefore inactive until previewed in Sync & placement, as SPEC and frame 119 say.
- **Frames versus Scope, and what is not built as drawn.**
  - *Last saved (Scope: "the header shows when it was last saved").* No table stores a configuration timestamp (`domain_projects`, `project_routing`, `project_github_sources`, `profiles` carry only `version`). Persisting one is a schema and read-model change. Decision: each section's header shows its version and, for a save this browser session recorded, "saved HH:MM" from the receipt; after a reload only the version shows, never an invented time. A durable time is listed as a judgment call.
  - *Phone frames 121 and 128 are read-only fixtures.* Removing phone editing would change behaviour (a project can be paused from a phone today), and SPEC only says complex configuration is desktop-first. Decision: the forms stay usable on phone; a "Current state" and "Next step" card pair (derived from the configuration read, source observations, placements and unsettled placement drafts) leads the project page on phone as frame 121 draws, and recovery (already read-only) follows 128.
  - *Phone headers.* Frames 121 and 128 draw the menu header; DESIGN.md's 9 October rule and U1's all-routes test (`operator-ux800-shell-browser`) make project settings, profile pages, Runtime and recovery detail headers with Back to the static parent. Kept; recorded.
  - *"Copy desktop link" (121, 128) is not built.* Note 130 and the issue mark it "needs review" and no decision is recorded. The phone states explain the state and next step without it. It is one clipboard button if Chris approves.
  - *Readiness Project-field conditions keep node-ID inputs.* Note 130 section 3 says names need a picker and "needs review"; ADR-1009 and U7 own discovery. Label conditions are edited in place as drawn.
  - *The Project filter stays private.* Frame 119 prints "Atlas roadmap · status:Next", but UI06 and SPEC treat filters like search queries; the row shows the Project node id and "Filter kept · private". The discovery credential row of frame 114 belongs to U7.
  - *Short identifiers (RL-31, A-203, AT-151) are not built*, as U3 and U5 recorded: no read model carries them. Rows use titles and profile names. "Last observed 10:59" and "requested by Jonas → A-202" in frame 127 are not in the recovery read and are omitted.
  - *Titles follow the frames*: h1 "Atlas · project configuration", "Reviewer · profile configuration", "Create profile", "Runtime capacity and recovery"; recovery reads "Assignment recovery evidence" on desktop and "Recovery" in the phone header (frame 128) through one `h1` with two spans, one hidden by CSS. The breadcrumb trail of recovery is the static "Settings / Runtime / Assignment recovery" because task and assignment names are not available to the shell.
  - *Refresh stays on every settings route*: U1 made it the header action on routes without a page-owned refresh and left removal to the screen slices; frames 114 and 118–127 draw it (122 does not; it keeps one consistent action). The header Refresh also re-reads the open page's own resources, so the in-page "Reload project configuration" / "Reload profile configuration" buttons go. U2's header-divider option (`plain`) is used on settings routes if #857 has merged, since the frames draw no divider.
  - *Switches* are a native checkbox styled as a switch in `settings.css`; there is no Switch primitive and `check()` keeps working.
- **Save is a change list, not a blind submit.** Every form computes "Changes to save" with the pure functions from T1 (each name, lead, pause, candidate, selection, readiness, repository, reference and private replacement, one line each), shows it beside the form (frame 119's panel), disables Save until it is non-empty, and offers "Discard changes". After a recorded save the draft is purged and re-initialised from the refreshed read (guidance and instructions return to replace-only, Save is disabled until something changes: note 130 section 4), and a persistent "Saved …" alert and the section's saved line come from the `saved` record, not from the receipt. Conflict, rejected and unknown behave as today.
- **Removing all repository access** (note 130: "not drawn") adds a required checkbox "Remove all repository access" and a warning inside the change panel; Save stays disabled until it is checked and the checkbox resets when the list is no longer empty. No dialog, so nothing depends on U5's `ui/dialog.tsx`.
- **Profiles.** Name, summary and capabilities edit in place (capabilities are loaded text; if the read returns null they fall back to replace-only); instructions stay replace-only behind "Replace instructions". Revoke and Restore are one draft field `revoked` toggled by a button ("Revoke profile" when available, "Restore profile" when revoked, "Undo …" while unsaved) and saved by Save profile, so there is one version fence and a counterpart exists in both directions. The destructive tint uses `Button variant="destructive"` if U5 has merged it, else a `settings.css` class on the existing `--nova-destructive-*` tokens.
- **Routing.** Candidates start from the saved list (revoked profiles are listed disabled and unchecked and are dropped from the saved list by the next routing save, as `activeProfile` already rejects them); guidance is "Replace routing guidance" (replace-only); the credential reference keeps the Preserve / Set / Clear control with env names never shown.
- **Index data.** The index reads each project's configuration (at most four in flight), the source observations and the runtime overview, all existing endpoints; a failed read shows "Unavailable" with Retry for that row only, never "None" or "Disabled".
- **Tabs are links, not ARIA tabs.** `?tab=general|routing|github|sync` on `/app/projects/:id/settings` (default General); the four items are `<a>` in a `nav` named "Project configuration sections" with `aria-current="page"`, so history, reload and deep links work and U2's `knownRoute` and the service's path-based shell need no change. Each tab keeps its own draft in `ConfigurationDrafts`, so unsaved edits survive tab changes.
- **Runtime and recovery.** Capacity keeps its keyed command (no version fence, as SPEC and UI06 say) with the change list and Save disabled until a change. Recovery shows the five independent holds as pills (stop "Active"/"Not active", task hold "Active"/"Not recorded", writer and capacity "Held"/"None reported", uncertainty "Active"/"None reported"; never "released"), the destructive "Execution may still be active" alert only when `holds.uncertainty`, and "Inspect execution" to the existing Task detail destination `/app/tasks/:taskId?assignment=:assignmentId`. The destination badges and the six advanced links keep their current derivation, targets and names.
- **Baseline.** At `bcf658f2`, in a scratch clone on Node v26.9.0 after `npm ci` and `npm run build`: `operator-configuration`, `operator-settings-state`, `operator-runtime` and `operator-control-inventory` pass 28 of 28; `operator-settings-browser` passes 18 of 19, the one failure being the flake above (it passed 3 of 3 alone). The CI run on `main` at this SHA completed with success. #851 recorded the same class of load flake in browser suites. `.node-version` is 24.21.0; the implementer uses it.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/settings.tsx` — `SettingsWorkspace` (index), `ProjectSetup`, `ProfileConfiguration` (create and edit), `ProjectConfiguration` (General form, then `RoutingConfiguration`, `SourceConfiguration` with preview, `SourceObservations`, `PlacementConfiguration`, `UnsettledPlacement`), and the shared `useDraft`, `DraftField`, `DraftCheck`, `DraftOutcome`, `submitDraft`, `SettingsProps`. Today the routing candidate list, the source selection list and the repository list start empty and readiness starts as one default label row, which is why every save is a complete replacement.
- **Existing:** `web/src/settings-state.ts` — `ConfigurationDraft` (`set`, `initialize`, `adoptVersion`, `startOperation`, `purge`, `submit`, `reconcile`; phases editing, pending, recorded, rejected, conflict, unknown) over `CommandLifecycle`; `ConfigurationDrafts` (`get`, `purge`, placement receipts). `web/src/recovery.tsx` — `RuntimeSettings`, `AssignmentRecovery`. `web/src/app.tsx` — `ProjectNavigation` (`link(...)`, project `current`), `title`, `headerSubtitle`, `ownsRefresh`, `refreshAll`, the settings, profile, project and recovery route branches (`key={pathname}`), `drafts`. `web/src/components.tsx` — `PageHeader`, `ActionLink`, `Button`, `StatusBadge`, `ResourceStatus`; `web/src/ui/{card,alert,badge,input,native-select,textarea}.tsx`.
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `operatorCommandSchema` (`routing.configure` L1810, `github.configure` L1828), `projectConfigurationSchema`, `profileConfigurationSchema`, `runtimeSettingsSchema`, `assignmentRecoverySchema`. `src/core/domain.ts` — `commandSchema` (L118–L139), `parseCommand`, `DomainStore.configureGitHub` (verifies every link before `executeParsed`), `apply` cases `routing.configure` (L1538) and `github.configure` (L1580), `DomainCommands.execute` (≈L2112; it routes `github.configure` with links to `configureGitHub`). `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` — `selectionSchema`, `repositoryLinkSchema`, `githubConfigurationSchema`. `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `readProjectConfiguration` (L3245: selections carry `id`, `kind`, `descriptor`, `active`; repositories carry `repositoryId` and `ref`, never `path`), `readRuntimeSettings`, and `execute`, which forwards configuration commands to the domain unchanged.
- **New:** `web/src/settings-changes.ts` (pure: `projectChanges`, `profileChanges`, `routingChanges`, `sourceChanges`, `sourceRowsFrom`, `sourceCommand`, `nextSelectionId`, `removesAllAccess`, `capacityChanges`); `web/src/settings-view.ts` (pure: `settingsHeader`, `indexSummary`, `projectStateSummary`, `savedLine`, `holdPills`); `web/src/settings-index.tsx`, `profile-config.tsx`, `project-config.tsx`, `routing-config.tsx`, `source-config.tsx`, `sync-placement.tsx`; `web/src/settings.css`; `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts` (`seedSettingsWorld`, `createCheckout`); `test/operator-settings-presentation.test.ts` (pure); browser suites `operator-settings-layout-browser.test.ts`, `operator-profile-config-browser.test.ts`, `operator-project-config-browser.test.ts`, `operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.ts` (each `browserSuite("ui08-settings-…")`).
- **Follow:** `web/src/tasks.ts` + `test/operator-task-list.test.ts` for pure web modules tested from Node; `test/operator-configuration.test.ts` (`OperatorApi.execute`, restart replay) for T2; `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts` `seedSettings`, the Git checkout setup (≈L634–L660) and `seedOperatorRecovery` (`test/fixtures/operator-web.ts`) for fixtures; `test/operator-ux800-shell-browser.test.ts` all-routes journey for viewport and `h1` checks.
- **Selector migrations (update, never delete):** "Settings home" → breadcrumb or Back link "Settings"; "Reload project/profile configuration" → "Refresh"; h2 "Project configuration" waits → the h1 or the tab nav; "Runtime and recovery" link → "Open runtime"; "Replace routing" → "Save routing"; "Replace source configuration" → "Save changes"; "Add selection"/"Remove selection n" → "Add source"/"Remove <id>"; "Add linked repository"/"Remove repository n" → "Add repository"/"Remove repository <id>"; create-profile "New instructions" → "Instructions" (edit keeps "Replace instructions" then "New instructions"); "Open exact private …/exact … editor" → "Open advanced … editor" (frame wording); "Open delivery policy and authority editor" → "Open advanced editor" inside "Credential and environment references"; "Stop, Resume, dependencies and Apply" → "Task controls". Labels of controls that still exist (Project name, Lead profile, Replace instructions, Credential reference change, Linked repository ID, New local repository path, Linked repository ref, Review latest … revision, Reconcile exact submission) keep their text. `operator-settings-browser.test.ts` is split by slice: move each migrated journey into the slice's new suite or edit it in place, keeping its intent assertions (no diagnostic echo, private values absent, receipts original, focus on the exact invalid row).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** acyclic. T1 and T2 have no dependency and touch disjoint files (`web/src/settings-*.ts` and tests versus `src/**`), so they may run concurrently. T3 depends on T1; T4 on T1, T3; T5 on T1, T3, T4; T6 and T7 on T2, T5; T8 on T5; T9 on T3, T4; T10 on all. T3–T10 share `web/src/app.tsx`, `web/src/settings.css` and the new browser suites, and T5–T8 share `project-config.tsx`; one owner runs them in order. T9 touches only `recovery.tsx`, `settings.css` and its own suite after T4, so a second owner could run it beside T5–T8 if `app.tsx` edits are serialised; the default is sequential.

#### 1. Pure settings model and "last saved" memory

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** new `web/src/settings-changes.ts`, `web/src/settings-view.ts`, `test/operator-settings-presentation.test.ts`; `web/src/settings-state.ts` (`ConfigurationDrafts` gains `saved(key)` and a private map, cleared by `purge()`; `ConfigurationDraft` gets a bound `onSaved` callback that `send()` calls on a `recorded` disposition with `{at: Date.now(), version}`); `test/operator-settings-state.test.ts`. No React, CSS or `src/**`; Node imports the pure modules and only types from `src/operator/contracts.js`.
**Test:** Pure Node tests. `projectChanges`: loaded Atlas, lead Mira, enabled, against values (name "Atlas II", lead Jonas, paused, replace instructions) returns four lines, including "Pause project" and "Instructions replaced (private, not shown after saving)"; identical values return `[]`. `profileChanges`: capabilities edited and `revoked` flipped true then false gives "Revoke <name>" then "Restore <name>". `routingChanges`: adding Worker, enabling, replacing guidance and a reference set give one line each; a saved revoked candidate is not a change. `sourceRowsFrom`/`sourceChanges`: the saved source yields kept selection rows (`keep: true`) and kept link rows with no path; removing S-3, adding a search source, a ref edit, a path replacement, a readiness mode change and a reference clear each give one line, and a new search row reads "+ S-4 · Search (query private) · added inactive". `sourceCommand` serialises kept selections as `{id, keep: true}` and kept links as `{repositoryId, ref}` with no `path`, and a replaced path includes it. `removesAllAccess` is true only when the saved list is non-empty and the draft list is empty. `nextSelectionId(["S-1","S-3","Literal <x>"],["S-4"])` is `"S-5"` and `nextSelectionId([],[])` is `"S-1"`. `settingsHeader` returns titles and trails for the seven settings routes (project tab "github" adds "GitHub source"; recovery has `shortTitle` "Recovery"; unknown names fall back to "Project"/"Profile"). `holdPills` maps the five booleans to the words in Planning decisions. State: a fake client returning a matching receipt leaves `drafts.saved(key)` with a numeric `at`; `startOperation` after `recorded` keeps it; store `purge()` clears it; after an unknown outcome `saved` is unset, `set()` returns false and `startOperation` does nothing.
**Implementation:** Write the functions with the signatures above over plain data (the loaded read model plus draft `values`); each returns `string[]` or the structure named. No wording lives in components.
**Validate:** From the repo root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-settings-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-state.test.js`; expect 0 failures.
**Complete when:** the pure and state tests pass and no existing `operator-settings-state` test changed meaning.

#### 2. In-place API: optional routing guidance and source keep markers

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none. This slice establishes the private-value persistence boundary; T6 and T7 start only when its replay and redaction tests pass.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` (new `selectionKeepSchema` `{id, keep: z.literal(true)}` strict, `repositoryLinkInputSchema` with optional `path`, and `githubConfigurationCommandSchema`: selections `union(selectionSchema, keep)` max 30 with unique ids, repositories max 20 with unique `repositoryId`; `githubConfigurationSchema` and its stored shapes stay unchanged); `src/core/domain.ts` (`commandSchema` `routing.configure` with `guidance: prose.optional()` and `github.configure` using the command schema; `configureGitHub` resolves link rows without `path` from `githubConfiguration(projectId).repositories` before `verifyRepository`, failing with `DomainPolicyError("invalid-input", "Repository verification failed")` when no saved link has that `repositoryId`; the `github.configure` apply case resolves keep selections from the current stored selections, throwing `DomainConflictError("Unknown GitHub selection")` for an unknown id, then stores resolved values only; `routing.configure` apply uses `command.guidance ?? present(current, "guidance")`); `src/operator/contracts.ts` (the two operator command variants use the same schemas); `test/operator-configuration.test.ts`.

| Profile revoke and Restore | 4 | T4 (b) |
| Routing save and reload with guidance replace-only | 6 | T6 save and reload |
| Settings index: repository access and discovery separate, profile summaries, routing, runtime, Refresh kept | 3 | T3 (a), (b) |
| Project tabs; each section saves on its own; header shows version and session save time | 5, 6, 7, 8 | T5 (a), (b); T6; T7 (b); T8 status line |
| New sources added inactive; Add and Remove | 2, 7 | T2 (b); T7 (b) |
| Runtime capacity, task recovery destinations, read-only recovery | 9 | T9 (a), (b) |
| Desktop screenshots match the frames | 3–9, 10 | captures in each slice; T10 comparison table |
| Phone shows state and next step | 3, 5, 9 | T3 (c); T5 (d); T9 (c) |
| Copy desktop link reviewed | 10 | recorded as not built, with the reason (PR gap list) |

### Final validation

- From the repo root on Node.js from `.node-version`, run `npm ci && npm run check`; expect typecheck, lint (no warnings), format, build and the full suite to pass. If a browser file fails only under heavy host load, rerun it with `node --test --test-concurrency=1` and confirm each journey stays under its 45s limit.
- `EVID=$(mktemp -d) && ENSEMBLE_TEST_EVIDENCE_DIR=$EVID node --test dist/test/operator-settings-layout-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-profile-config-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-project-config-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.js` (a directory outside the worktree) to collect the 1366×900 and 390×844 captures named in T3–T9 for the T10 comparison. No live runtime or provider attempt is required: no runtime, execution or provider behaviour changes; state that in the PR.

### Review focus

- T2 is the only server change: markers must resolve from the version the operator saw (the fence), idempotent replay must hold across restart with markers in the hash, and nothing private may reach a read, receipt or error body.
- The reload-after-record step must never discard input typed after a save settled (`initialize` already refuses dirty or frozen drafts) and must not mask an unknown outcome.
- Privacy on every new surface: change-list lines, status text, `aria-describedby`, evidence screenshots and error copy must not contain private text, paths or reference names.
- Phone: forms stay editable at 390px with 44px targets; the state cards must say only what the reads support.
- Selector migrations must keep each case's original intent assertions, not only its names.
- Overlap, as the implementer must handle it. #857 (U2, in CI) edits `web/src/app.tsx` (title ternary, `knownRoute`, account menu), `PageHeader.plain`, the sign-out selectors in `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts` (≈L2134–L2286) and the two design docs: this plan starts after it merges and edits the settings branches of the same ternary and route chain. #837, #838 and #839 add small header seams and props to `app.tsx` and `PageHeader` (`onHeader`, `back.history`, `desktopBack`, `Button` destructive): `trail` and `shortTitle` are additive; rebase, never reformat. #837 keeps the "Project settings" link to `/app/projects/:id/settings`, which this plan keeps valid. #839 leaves the UI06 control table alone; T10 edits only the `routing.configure`, `github.configure` and `profile.configure` capabilities rows. #828 (PR #855) touches `src/core/coordination.ts`, `local-review.ts` and the task schema region of `src/operator/contracts.ts`, not the command schemas T2 edits. #841 (U7) owns `ProjectSetup`, `/app/settings/projects/new` and the discovery credential row, which it adds to `settings-index.tsx` after T3.

### Allowed deviations

- Adjust spacing, radius and colour within 2px of the exported frames; rename a control only where this plan or the frames name it. If U5 has merged `Button variant="destructive"`, use it for Revoke profile; if #857 has not added `PageHeader.plain`, skip the divider option.

### Re-plan triggers

- The in-place semantics need a new command type, a new read field, a persisted timestamp, relaxed repository verification or exposure of a private value.
- `ConfigurationDraft` cannot be re-initialised after `recorded` without weakening conflict or unknown-outcome behaviour.
- #857 or #855 merge in a shape that removes the seams named above (`knownRoute`, `plain`, account-menu routes), or U7 moves `ProjectSetup` or the Settings index contract in a way that changes T3.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/841
**Planned against:** `main` at `c3070786bb14e869519ef937afb84b043fcefdf7`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

Planned implementation branch: `cb/issue-841-project-setup-discovery`, one PR closing #841. Start it after #857 (U2) has merged, because both edit `web/src/app.tsx` (title ternary, route chain) and `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts`. #840 (U6) is independent in order but shares seams (see Overlap in Review focus). #855 (#828) is already in the baseline and shares no file with this plan.

### Approach

Nine slices on one branch. The accepted contract (ADR-1009, SPEC "Task creation and project setup", frames 115–117b and 131) already covers every new read and write surface, so nothing here needs a human decision before work starts; the choices that are mine are listed in Planning decisions. T1 extends `project.create` into the one atomic "Create paused project" command (optional instructions, verified repositories, one inactive GitHub Project source) and adds the origin check to the existing repository verifier. T2 adds the installation-level discovery credential reference (a keyed `discovery.configure` command, a status read). T3 adds a read-only GitHub discovery reader and three authenticated reads (repositories, branches, Projects). T4 adds the two authenticated POST routes that list home-folder subfolders and verify a checkout. T5 adds the pure web model, client methods and a Dialog primitive. T6 rebuilds `ProjectSetup` (frames 115, 116, 117, 117b). T7 adds the folder picker dialog (131). T8 adds the credential row to Settings (the row in frame 114). T9 records docs, resolves ADR-1009's open item and runs the full check with screenshots.

Source contract (retrievable, not restated): the issue's Scope and Acceptance; epic #834 Boundaries; [ADR-1009](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/main/docs/adr/1009-project-setup-discovery.md); `docs/SPEC.md` "Task creation and project setup" and "Workspaces and execution access"; `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md`; `design/DESIGN.md` "Screen reference map"; review notes 130 section 2. A conflict between this plan and those is a re-plan trigger.

Frames (read through Pen MCP on 10 October 2026, exported at scale 1; re-export them, never parse `design/design.pen`): setup `wk678` (115), error `q6ZqlW` (116), first run `bkNmZ` (117), discovery unavailable `T6VX5` (117b), folder picker `M6N2BQ` (131), the credential row in Settings `vEr15` (114), notes `DuF5u` (130). Export with `Export([...ids],"png",<scratch dir>,{scale:1})` after `get_app_state` in the same invocation (the first call can take about 60s). No phone frame exists for setup or the picker (notes 130 section 5).

### Guardrails

- Authority is exactly ADR-1009. Discovery, a chosen folder and a linked GitHub Project grant no repository access; access is exactly the repositories the operator adds. The discovery credential is read-only by construction: the reader issues only GETs and one fixed GraphQL query, no mutation, and no discovered list is stored. The folder routes list subfolder names and Git status only, never file contents or file names, only under the operator's home folder, only for an authenticated operator session; no agent tool, model tool or extension route exposes them. Unchanged: paused-on-create, readiness and admission rules, repository verification at `github.configure`, delivery policy, the retained HTML editors (`/` keeps its name-and-lead create form).
- Private values never leave the write path: instructions, local paths, the credential reference (name and value) are never loaded into a read, receipt, error, URL, query string, `aria` text or evidence file. Paths travel only in POST bodies (home-relative `~/…` or typed absolute), and the folder listing displays home-relative paths. Origin URLs are parsed server-side and only `owner/name` for `github.com` is returned, never the URL (it can carry credentials).
- Out of scope: project configuration tabs, source preview/activation, readiness names and the Settings index layout (U6 #840); Overview and its empty state (U3); sign-in, account menu and not found (U2); any GitHub write; storing discovered lists; inheriting the discovery credential into a project's source credential; stripping the discovery variable from the Codex spawn environment (see Planning decisions); `design/design.pen`; paused X01–X08 work.
- Two kinds of repair, kept separate. (1) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; then stop and re-plan. The assumptions that count: `DomainStore` can create the project, its first instruction revision, the GitHub source row and the linked repositories in one `executeParsed` transaction after asynchronous verification, without changing existing command hashes (T1); `git -C <dir> remote get-url origin` and `symbolic-ref` give the origin and branch for plain, worktree and `.git`-file checkouts (T1, T4); the existing `ConfigurationDraft`/`CommandLifecycle` and `matchesConfigurationReceipt` settle the extended `project.create` unchanged (T6); GitHub's `/user/repos`, branches and `projectsV2` GraphQL shapes are as T3 states, confirmed by T3's live probe; `handleWeb` and `OperatorWebBoundary.knownApi` accept the new paths (T3, T4). (2) Ordinary implementation defects belong to the ticket owner and never consume that budget: integration breakage, selector and fixture migrations, test and flake repairs, CSS and layout, docs, CI and screenshot repairs. Investigate unknown overlap with #840 and #857 before continuing. Return human-required only if the accepted contract itself must change: browsing outside the home folder, returning file contents, agent access to the folder routes, storing discovered lists, a GitHub write, a project inheriting the discovery credential, or relaxed repository verification.
- If a frame contradicts the issue Scope, follow the frame where repository evidence supports it and record the choice in the PR (made so far: Planning decisions, "Frames over Scope"). Frame details the repository cannot support are recorded as gaps, not built.
- Browser tests wait deterministically. After `goto`, wait for `main.page h1` and then for the specific element under test before reading anything; `count()`, `isVisible()`, `textContent()` and `evaluateAll` do not wait. Use locator `waitFor`, `page.waitForURL`, `page.waitForFunction` or an awaited `waitForRequest`/`waitForResponse`, and assert "does not happen" (no POST after a client-side rejection) only after awaiting a positive signal that the interaction finished. Run each engine as its own test or call `journey.restart()` before each launch (#853); keep every journey under the 45s execution limit by splitting concerns; never add `--test-timeout=0` or an unbounded wait; any `page.route` that holds or aborts a request is released and unrouted in `finally`.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews; use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption.
- `npm run lint` fails on warnings; new role/ARIA markup must pass `biome lint --error-on-warnings`.

### Planning decisions

- **One command, not chained commands (settles ADR-1009 "Open").** `project.create` gains optional `instructions`, `repositories` and `githubProject`; the service verifies every repository first, then one SQLite transaction records the project, instruction revision 1, the linked repositories and the inactive source under one keyed receipt. Evidence: frame 116 reads "Project not created. Fix the highlighted field. Every other value is kept", which a chain cannot honour (a recorded create cannot be unwound); `DomainStore.executeParsed` already runs one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction with a project-scoped receipt, and `configureGitHub` already shows the verify-then-transact pattern; `ConfigurationDraft` freezes exactly one key and payload and reconciles by replaying them, so one command reuses the unknown-outcome and conflict behaviour with no multi-step lifecycle; optional fields are omitted before canonical hashing, so existing `project.create` hashes and receipts stay valid. Consequence: there is no partially recorded setup. "Partial-failure reporting" is the all-or-nothing report (which field failed, nothing recorded, every value kept) plus the existing unknown-outcome report. Record the choice in ADR-1009 (T9).
- **Origin check lives in the shared verifier, scoped to setup.** `verifiedRepository(input, expectedOrigin?)` in `src/core/github-source.ts` gains an optional origin check (`git remote get-url origin`, `github.com` only, case-insensitive `owner/name`, userinfo and a `.git` suffix ignored, forms `https://`, `ssh://git@`, `git@host:` and `git://`). `github.configure` and the admission re-check call it without an origin and are unchanged, so U6's repository editing and existing fixtures (checkouts with no remote) keep working. The verifier throws a typed `RepositoryVerificationError(reason)`; the folder verify route returns the reason, and `project.create` maps it to a fixed field path. Provider instance is the host (`github.com` only; `IssueSnapshot.providerInstance` is that literal today), so a `github.example.com` origin is rejected with "origin-provider".
- **Recorded repository identity.** A discovered repository is recorded with its GitHub `node_id` (what `readSelection` and delivery compare). A typed `owner/name` (discovery unavailable) is recorded as `github.com/<owner>/<name>` lower-cased, because no node ID can be read without a credential. Evidence that this is safe: `repositoryId` is an opaque per-project key in `workspaces.ts`, `provisionTask` and the retained-evidence policy, and only delivery grants and imported issues compare it with GitHub node IDs (`github-delivery.ts`), where a non-matching id fails closed. Judgment call (see report): the typed id is provisional and a later U6 edit can replace it with a node ID.
- **Credential is a keyed command, not a CLI-only setting.** Frame 114 ("Change") and 117b ("Set discovery credential") and the issue Scope ("set … in Settings") require a UI write. `discovery.configure {credentialRef: env:NAME | null}` follows `capacity.configure` (installation-scoped singleton, receipt scope `system:discovery`, no expected version, set and clear). Only the reference is stored; the value is read from the service environment at read time and, like every other credential, never returned.
- **Reads are GET, filesystem and verification are POST.** Discovery lists (`/api/operator/discovery`, `…/repositories`, `…/branches?repository=owner/name`, `…/projects?repository=owner/name`) carry no private input, so they are authenticated GETs through the existing `OperatorWebBoundary.read`. The folder listing and checkout verification carry local paths, so they are POSTs (`/api/operator/setup/folders`, `/api/operator/setup/verify-checkout`) with the existing session, `Origin` and CSRF checks and a body limit, keeping paths out of URLs.
- **Home scope.** The service resolves `~` against `os.homedir()` (injectable). A listing request is `~` or `~/a/b`: each segment must be non-empty and not `.`/`..`; the target is `realpath`-ed and must equal or sit under `realpath(home)` (macOS `/var` → `/private/var` makes comparing real paths on both sides mandatory). Dot-folders and symlinks are not listed; a symlink that resolves outside home is refused when requested (403). A typed absolute path outside home stays accepted for verification, as typed paths are today.
- **Frame 131 row detail is kept.** Rows show "Git checkout · origin acme/atlas · main" (normalized `github.com` origin and current branch via `git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD`) and a "Matches acme/atlas" badge, which is slightly more than "Git status". Bounded: at most 200 entries, four concurrent git probes, 2s each, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, no `status`/hook-running commands.
- **Frames over Scope, recorded.** (a) Frame 115 shows a Project count "owned by acme" with no repository chosen; ADR-1009 derives Projects only from chosen repositories ("linked … then other Projects owned by the same owner"), so the Project control is disabled with "Choose a repository to list its GitHub Projects" until a repository is chosen. (b) Frame 117 preselects the single linked Project ("Found automatically"), frame 116 shows None; follow 117 and let the operator pick None (116 reads as that choice). (c) Frame copy says "on this Mac" where the ADR says "the host"; keep the frame copy (the service is the macOS LaunchAgent). (d) Added and not drawn: Remove on additional repository rows, Retry on a failed discovery read, an inline credential form in Settings with Clear, phone layout (single column, 44px targets). (e) Breadcrumb "Overview → New project" on first run, "Settings / Projects / Create project" otherwise, as drawn.
- **Discovery credential and the agent environment.** The Codex child inherits the service environment minus delivery credentials (`deliveryRuntimeEnvironment`), exactly as it does for source credentials. This plan does not strip the discovery variable: a name or value match would also remove a token operators deliberately share with agents (for example `GH_TOKEN`), a behaviour change outside the issue. The Settings row tells the operator to use a dedicated read-only token, and the docs record the limit. Judgment call (see report).
- **Bounded baseline evidence (10 October 2026, scratch clone at `c3070786`, Node 26.9.0 against `.node-version` 24.21.0, which #848 qualifies):** `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass; `node --test --test-concurrency=1 dist/test/operator-configuration.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/operator-settings-state.test.js dist/test/github-source-config.test.js` passes (40 tests); `node --test --test-name-pattern="Settings guides empty workspace" dist/test/operator-settings-browser.test.js` passes in about 0.9s. The full `npm run check` was not repeated at planning time; T9 owns it.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `commandSchema` (`project.create` ≈L37), `DomainStore.execute` (≈L502, throws for `github.configure` with links), `configureGitHub` (≈L530, verifies then `executeParsed`), `recordedCommand` (≈L564), `executeParsed` (≈L588, one transaction plus receipt), `apply` cases `project.create` (≈L1362; inserts the project, instruction revision 1 `''`, routing and a GitHub row with the default `label ready` readiness) and `github.configure` (≈L1580), `DomainStore` constructor's injected `verifyRepository: typeof verifiedRepository` (≈L302), `DomainCommands.execute` (≈L2096; routes `github.configure` with links to `configureGitHub`), three inline `projectId`/`profileId`/`"system:capacity"` scope ternaries (≈L576, L600, L2116), `scheduler_capacity_limits` singleton table (≈L387) as the precedent for T2.
- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source.ts` — `verifiedRepository` (≈L81; absolute path, `realpath`, `rev-parse --git-common-dir`, `rev-parse --verify <ref>`, returns `{...input, path, gitCommonDirectory}`), `linkedRepositorySchema`. `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` — `repositoryLinkSchema`, `selectionSchema` (project selections need `projectNodeId` and a `filter` string), `readinessSchema`, `githubConfigurationSchema` (≤20 repositories, unique `repositoryId`).
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `operatorCommandSchema` (`project.create` ≈L1776, `capacity.configure`), `configurationReceiptSchema` (≈L1912), `commandReceiptSchema` (≈L2282), `apiErrorSchema` (closed code enum, fixed messages, optional `fieldPaths`), the `envelope` helper. `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `OperatorApi` constructor (≈L301; 4th parameter `previewReader` is the injection precedent), `exclusions` (≈L360; adds every credential reference, env key and value), `executeDomain` (≈L3618; maps `Repository verification failed` to `["repositories"]` for `github.configure`), `execute` (≈L4248; the `project.create`/`github.configure` group builds the configuration receipt, `capacity.configure` is the installation-scoped precedent). `src/standalone/operator-web.ts` — `OperatorWebBoundary.shell`, `read` (query keys are rejected after the early branches), `knownApi`. `src/standalone/operator.ts` — `handleWeb` (≈L1249): `expected` method list for POST paths, session, `Origin` and CSRF checks, `readJson` (64 KiB), `OperatorApiError` → status/code/fieldPaths. `src/standalone/github-http.ts` — `githubFetch`, `nextPageLink`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/settings.tsx` — `ProjectSetup` (name, lead, `Create paused project`, recorded alert, "Create another project"), `useDraft`, `DraftField`, `DraftOutcome`, `submitDraft`, `SettingsWorkspace`. `web/src/settings-state.ts` — `ConfigurationDraft` (scalar and `string[]` values only, `submit`, `reconcile`, `startOperation`, `purge`), `matchesConfigurationReceipt`. `web/src/api.ts` — `OperatorClient` (`read`, `command`, `refreshSources` is the only non-command POST). `web/src/app.tsx` — route chain (`/app/settings/projects/new` → `ProjectSetup`), sidebar "New project", `knownRoute` (after #857). `web/src/ui/sheet.tsx` — Radix Dialog wrapper pattern; `web/src/components.tsx` — `PageHeader`, `ActionLink`, `StatusBadge`, `Button`.
- **New:** `src/standalone/github-discovery.ts` — `GitHubDiscoveryReader` (`repositories()`, `branches(owner, name)`, `projects(owner, name)`), `DiscoveryFailure(reason)`. `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts` — `OperatorSetupSeams` (`home?`, `discovery?`), `resolveHomePath`, `listHomeFolders`, `verifyCheckout`. `web/src/setup-model.ts` (pure), `web/src/project-setup.tsx`, `web/src/folder-picker.tsx`, `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx`, `web/src/ui/dialog.tsx`, `web/src/setup.css`. Tests: `test/project-setup.test.ts`, `test/github-discovery.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-model.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-setup-picker-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.ts`, fixture `test/fixtures/setup-home.ts`.
- **Follow:** `test/operator-configuration.test.ts` (real SQLite through `new OperatorApi(f.service, [f.directory])`, replay across `service.stop()/start()`, post-commit notification failure stays unknown ≈L373) for T1/T2; `test/operator-web-http.test.ts` for the authenticated HTTP cases; `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts` (real temporary Git checkout ≈L673; `browserSuite`, `journey.start`, `captureBrowserEvidence`) and `test/operator-ux800-browser.test.ts` (`journey.restart()` per engine) for browser tests.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** acyclic: T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 → T5 → T6 → T7; T2, T6 → T8; T7, T8 → T9. T1–T4 all edit `src/operator/contracts.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-web.ts` and `src/core/domain.ts` (T1, T2), and T6, T7 and T8 share `web/src/app.tsx`/`web/src/settings.tsx`, so no two tasks are safe to run concurrently; run them in order T1 … T9 on one branch.

#### 1. Atomic setup command and origin-aware repository verification

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** #857 merged (only for the later web slices; T1 is server-only). Baseline green as recorded in Planning decisions.
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` (new `setupRepositorySchema` = `repositoryLinkSchema` extended with `owner`, `name`, and a ref that cannot start with `-` or contain whitespace/control characters); `src/core/github-source.ts` (new `parseGitHubOrigin(url)`, `RepositoryVerificationError` with `reason` in `path-invalid | not-checkout | origin-missing | origin-provider | origin-mismatch | ref-unavailable` and the actual `owner/name` on `origin-mismatch`, `verifiedRepository(input, expectedOrigin?)`); `src/core/domain.ts` (`commandSchema` `project.create` gains optional `instructions` (`prose`), `repositories` (≤20, unique `repositoryId`) and `githubProject` (`{projectNodeId}`); `DomainPolicyError` gains optional `fieldPaths`; `DomainStore.execute` throws for `project.create` with repositories as it does for `github.configure`; new `DomainStore.createProject` replaying a prior receipt, verifying each repository in order, then `executeParsed`; `apply("project.create")` writes revision 1 = `instructions ?? ""`, the verified links as `{repositoryId, path, ref, gitCommonDirectory}` (never `owner`/`name`), and `selections = githubProject ? [{id:"S-1", kind:"project", projectNodeId, filter:""}] : []`, leaving the default readiness, `project_github_active` empty and every version at 1; `DomainCommands.execute` routes `project.create` with repositories to `createProject`); `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`operatorCommandSchema` `project.create` gains the same optional fields, `path` up to 4096 characters); `src/standalone/operator-setup.ts` (new; `OperatorSetupSeams {home?: string}` and `resolveHomePath(input, home)`: `~` and `~/…` expand against `home ?? os.homedir()`, absolute paths pass through, anything else is `path-invalid`; T3 adds `discovery`, T4 the listing functions); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (constructor 5th parameter `setup?: OperatorSetupSeams`; `execute` expands `repositories[].path` with `resolveHomePath` before `executeDomain`; `executeDomain` returns `error.fieldPaths` when present); `test/fixtures/operator-web.ts` (`startWeb(controlPaths?, setup?)` passes the seams to `OperatorApi`).
**Test:** New `test/project-setup.test.ts` (real SQLite and real temporary Git checkouts built with `git init -b main`, a commit and `git remote add origin …`; `DomainStore` through `DomainCommands`) and additions to `test/operator-configuration.test.ts` (through `OperatorApi.execute`). (a) Success: a command with instructions `PRIVATE SETUP SENTINEL`, one repository `{repositoryId:"R_atlas", owner:"acme", name:"atlas", path, ref:"main"}` whose origin is `https://github.com/acme/atlas.git`, and `githubProject.projectNodeId:"PVT_1"` records one paused project at version 1; `project(id).instructions` is the sentinel at revision 1; `githubConfiguration(id)` has `repositories` equal to `[{repositoryId:"R_atlas", path:<realpath>, ref:"main", gitCommonDirectory:<realpath>}]` (no `owner`/`name` keys), `selections` equal to the one `S-1` project selection with `filter:""`, version 1, default `label ready` readiness, `project_github_active` empty; routing unchanged. The receipt JSON lacks the sentinel and the path. Replaying the identical body after `service.stop()/start()` returns the original receipt; the same key with a changed instruction returns the conflict. (b) Origin matrix, each as its own assertion with nothing created (`domain_projects`, `project_instruction_revisions`, `command_receipts` unchanged): `https://user:SECRETPASS@github.com/Acme/Atlas` (no `.git`) and `git@github.com:acme/atlas.git` and `ssh://git@github.com/acme/atlas.git` and `git://github.com/acme/atlas` all verify (case-insensitive) and `SECRETPASS` appears in no error, receipt or stored row; `https://github.com/acme/relay.git` → `origin-mismatch` with actual `acme/relay` and `fieldPaths ["repositories.0.path"]`; `https://gitlab.com/acme/atlas` and `https://github.example.com/acme/atlas` → `origin-provider`; no origin remote → `origin-missing`; a plain folder → `not-checkout`; a relative path and a missing folder → `path-invalid`; ref `nope` → `ref-unavailable` with `repositories.0.ref`; ref `--help` rejected by the schema before any git process (use the injected `verifyRepository` spy to prove zero calls). (c) With two repositories where the second fails, the error names `repositories.1.path` and nothing is recorded (all-or-nothing). (d) `actor: "agent"` is `forbidden`. (e) A `project.create` without the new fields still uses the synchronous path and its existing receipt hash is unchanged (the existing replay test stays green). (f) Post-commit notification failure of the extended command stays unknown and an exact replay applies once (follow ≈L373 and ≈L601 of `operator-configuration.test.ts`).
**Implementation:** Verify before the transaction, as `configureGitHub` does, so a failed check records nothing; the receipt scope remains the project id. **Complete when:** the credential can be set, shown only as configured or unconfigured, and cleared from Settings, and setup reflects it.

#### 9. Docs, ADR resolution, screenshots and full check

**Task ID:** `T9`
**Depends on:** `T7, T8`
**Prerequisites:** T1–T8 merged on the branch.
**Files and symbols:** `docs/adr/1009-project-setup-discovery.md` (replace "Open" with the decision: one atomic `project.create`, no partial states, unknown outcome reconciled by key; record the typed-fallback identity and the folder-row detail); `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` (first paragraph and control table: `project.create` now carries instructions, repositories and one inactive Project source; add rows for `discovery.configure`, the four discovery reads and the two setup POST routes with their dispositions; remove "optional project instructions are saved later through project configuration" for setup); `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` (crosswalk rows for the same controls and the `/app/settings/projects/new` surface row); `docs/SPEC.md` ("Task creation and project setup": one sentence that the service enforces home-folder scope and that typed fallback records a provisional repository identity; no behaviour change to the rest); `docs/acceptance.md` (an "Operator UI additions" entry for #841 naming the tests above and the limits); `README.md` (UI06 line mentions guided setup, GitHub discovery and the folder picker; native structured input and live provider qualification remain separate). The PR body lists entry points and counterparts and attaches the frame-versus-screenshot table.
**Test:** Not applicable (documentation); screenshots come from the browser suites.
**Implementation:** In the PR body list entry points: sidebar "New project" and the first-run route (frames 115/117), Settings index "Create project", the deep link `/app/settings/projects/new`, "Set discovery credential" from setup to Settings, project configuration after create; the retained `/` HTML create form is unchanged (name and lead only; remains the fallback); gaps: Overview empty state (U3), the typed identity being provisional, the discovery token being ambient to the runtime (limit), no project delete or archive (an accepted, irreversible create; recovery is editing in project configuration), phone frames not drawn. List counterparts: Clear credential, Remove repository row, Cancel, Create another, Retry, folder Cancel. Record the Pen frame ids and a table (frame, screenshot, difference, reason).
**Validate:** From the repo root on Node.js from `.node-version`, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check`; expect typecheck, lint (no warnings), format, build and the full suite to pass. Then `EVID=$(mktemp -d) && ENSEMBLE_TEST_EVIDENCE_DIR=$EVID node --test --test-concurrency=1 dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-picker-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.js`, a directory outside the worktree, to collect the 1366×900 and 390×844 captures for the comparison.

### Acceptance coverage

### Final validation

- From the repo root on Node.js from `.node-version`, run `npm ci && npm run check`; expect typecheck, lint (no warnings), format, build and the full suite to pass. If a browser file fails only under heavy host load, rerun it with `node --test --test-concurrency=1` and confirm each journey stays under 45s.
- Live evidence is bounded: T3's discovery probe against api.github.com with a read-only token and T4's real-home listing, both recorded as pass/fail and counts only. No Codex runtime, execution or delivery behaviour changes, so no runtime journey is required; say so in the PR.

### Review focus

- `project.create`: all-or-nothing recording, no private value or origin URL in any receipt, error or evidence, existing command hashes untouched, and `github.configure`/admission verification unchanged (no origin check added there).

- Frame fidelity versus the choices recorded in Planning decisions; the selector migrations in `test/operator-settings-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-ux800-shell-browser.test.ts` (≈L367, L643) and `test/operator-web-browser.test.ts` (≈L230) keep their intent assertions.

U6 also changes `github.configure` (keep markers, optional `path`) in `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts` and `src/core/domain.ts`; T1 only adds a new schema beside it and a `project.create` branch, so rebase, never reformat. #837–#839 add small header props to `app.tsx`/`PageHeader`; rebase, never reformat. #828 (PR #855) is merged and unrelated.
