content.title: Claude harness C1: Remove Codex assumptions outside the Codex runtime

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/823
**Planned against:** `main` at `36938df0965ac59fbaf953761298cc53f131abc8`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Introduce a closed `ExecutionHarness` identifier (only `"codex"` for now) and thread it through the
existing seams instead of adding a new abstraction layer: the service's runtime factory takes a
harness, the runtime safety port the service builds stamps that harness onto runtime evidence, and
`ExecutionState` persists it on execution bindings and the two `runtime_*` evidence tables using the
repository's add-column-if-missing migration pattern (existing rows default to `codex`). Failure
evidence crossing the `Runtime` boundary becomes harness-neutral; `CodexRuntime` keeps its
`codexErrorInfo` classification and maps it into the neutral shape. The pinned Codex CLI version
moves from core native-input validation into the Codex runtime. Power supervision keys off "a real
harness runtime is configured" instead of `instanceof CodexRuntime`. Deliver as one PR from
`cb/823-harness-neutral-runtime`.

### Guardrails

- Codex behaviour is unchanged: same App Server policy, classification codes, retry budget
  (`ensemble + harness retries <= 2`), recovery holds, power assertion timing and operator-visible
  output. No change under `src/operator/**`, `web/src/**`, `src/standalone/operator*.ts`, or
  `src/core/domain.ts`; no operator API/contract field is added (C2 #824 owns exposing the runtime).
- Out of scope: agent-profile harness selection, per-binding runtime routing and multiple runtimes
  per service (#824 C2); any Claude runtime, SDK dependency or `"claude"` harness value (#825 C3,
  which depends on C0 #822 evidence that this ticket does not need); native Codex visibility
  (paused X01–X08). Do not neutralise other Codex-shaped facts the issue does not name (for example
  `execution_intents.accountType`, `sandbox`, `approval`, `runtime_thread_qualification.codexVersion`).
- No SQL column renames or table rebuilds. Existing `codexRetries`/`codexRetriesUsed` columns and the
  `failureSource = 'codexErrorInfo'` CHECK on `execution_retry_attempts`/`execution_retry_resolutions`
  stay as stored representation; only TypeScript names and `runtime_terminal_evidence.failureEvidence`
  JSON written for new rows change. Unknown persisted harness values fail closed (zod parse throws on
  read); there is no fallback to another harness.
- Existing Codex tests change only for the renamed neutral fields listed in T3 (and the extra
  `harness: "codex"` field on direct `resolveFailedGeneration` proofs). Any other existing-test edit is
  a sign the change altered behaviour; investigate rather than adjust the assertion.
- Plan-mismatch budget versus ordinary repairs: if an approved-plan seam or repository assumption is
  factually wrong (for example a named symbol/seam does not own the behaviour described, the
  add-column migration cannot express the default, or a renamed field is consumed somewhere this
  plan says it is not), spend at most one focused diagnosis and two repair cycles under that
  allowance, recording each in the delivery record; stop and return for replanning if it is still
  wrong or the fix needs a material design/contract change. Ordinary implementation defects —
  integration wiring, type errors, failing tests, fixtures, documentation, lint/format and CI
  repairs within the unchanged design — stay with the ticket owner, are fixed as normal work and do
  not consume that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage,
  architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate
  unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for
  a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets
  and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Harness type.** `executionHarnessSchema = z.enum(["codex"])` in a new
  `src/standalone/execution-harness.ts`, with `type ExecutionHarness` and
  `defaultExecutionHarness: ExecutionHarness = "codex"`. Keeping the enum closed until C3 means any
  harness-specific mapping written as `Record<ExecutionHarness, …>` or an exhaustive `switch` fails to
  compile when `"claude"` is added, forcing that ticket to decide each mapping. SQL columns use
  `harness TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'codex' CHECK(length(harness) BETWEEN 1 AND 64)` (no value list), so
  adding a harness later needs no table rebuild; value validation is zod-on-read.
- **Where harness is decided.** The service knows which harness it asked the factory for, so it binds
  the harness into the `RuntimeSafetyPort` closures and into `bindTask`; `Runtime` implementations do
  not report their own harness to persistence. `ExecutionState` methods take a trailing
  `harness: ExecutionHarness = defaultExecutionHarness` parameter so existing direct test callers
  (`test/fixtures/runtime-safety.ts`, ~15 `bindTask` call sites) stay unchanged; production service
  code always passes it explicitly.
- **Power gate.** Today `powerEnabled = power?.enabled ?? (power?.eventSource !== undefined ||
  runtime instanceof CodexRuntime)`. Fake runtimes across the suite rely on being unsupervised (power
  start polls `/usr/bin/pmset` immediately and CI runs on `ubuntu-latest`), while
  `test/s03b/live-runtime.mjs` relies on an injected `CodexRuntime` being supervised. Replace the
  `instanceof` with an optional `readonly harness?: ExecutionHarness` on the `Runtime` interface that
  real harness runtimes declare (`CodexRuntime.harness = "codex"`): supervision starts for any harness
  runtime, and `ExecutionPower` already holds the caffeinate assertion only while executions are
  active. Fakes omit `harness` and keep today's behaviour. Put the decision in an exported pure
  `powerSupervisionEnabled(power, runtime)` so it is testable without pmset.
- **Neutral failure evidence.** `RuntimeTerminalFailureEvidence` (runtime-retention.ts) becomes
  `{ classification; reasonCode: string; source: "harness" | "missing"; harnessRetries: number | null }`;
  `FailureEvidence`/`parseFailureEvidence` stay in `codex.ts` beside the `Runtime` interface (so
  existing imports keep working) but become that plus `threadId`, `turnId`, `status: "failed"`, optional `retryAfterMs`, with `reasonCode` a bounded
  string (`min(1).max(64)`) instead of `CodexErrorInfo`. The service retry gate becomes
  `source === "harness" && harnessRetries !== null` with the same transient reason codes
  (`serverOverloaded`, `rateLimitExceeded`), which is equivalent for Codex because Codex only emits
  `codexErrorInfo|missing`. `FailureResolutionEvidence` gains required `harness` and uses
  `source: "harness"`, `harnessRetries`; `FailedGenerationResolution.codexRetriesUsed` becomes
  `harnessRetriesUsed`. `state.ts` maps `harness` to the retry tables' stored `failureSource` through
  `const retryFailureSource: Record<ExecutionHarness, "codexErrorInfo"> = { codex: "codexErrorInfo" }`
  for both inserts and the committed-row equality checks. Known follow-on, not C1 scope: recording a
  Claude transient retry will need C3 to relax that CHECK.
- **Legacy failure JSON.** New `runtime_terminal_evidence.failureEvidence` rows store the neutral
  JSON (well under the 256-byte CHECK). The reader accepts either the neutral strict schema or the
  current legacy strict schema (`source: "codexErrorInfo"|"missing"`, `codexRetries`, Codex reason
  enum) and maps legacy to neutral; legacy rows carry the column default `harness = 'codex'`.
- **Native input literal.** `nativeInputQualificationSchema` in `src/core/structured-questions.ts`
  keeps its fields (persisted `qualificationJson` rows stay valid) but `codexVersion` becomes
  `z.string().min(1).max(128)`. `src/standalone/codex.ts` defines and exports
  `codexNativeInputQualificationSchema = nativeInputQualificationSchema.extend({ codexVersion:
  z.literal("codex-cli 0.159.0") })` and uses it where it qualifies a thread (currently
  `nativeInputQualificationSchema.safeParse` near codex.ts:843), so only the Codex runtime pins the
  version. Native input is Codex-only per ADR-1008 (Claude disables `AskUserQuestion`).
- No documentation edit is required: the change is internal, `docs/`, `README.md` and `CONTEXT.md`
  do not mention the renamed fields, and the "Execution binding" term already covers the harness.
- No proof task is needed: every assumption is settled by repository evidence above, and C1 needs no
  Claude SDK behaviour, so C0 #822 is not a prerequisite.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `RuntimeSpawnContext` (l.159); `StandaloneServiceOptions.power`
  (l.178); constructor default `runtimeFactory = (context) => new CodexRuntime("codex", context)`
  (l.297–299); `start()` builds `runtimeSafety: RuntimeSafetyPort` (l.416–431), calls
  `this.runtimeFactory(context)` (l.536) and computes `powerEnabled` with `instanceof CodexRuntime`
  (l.637–642); `state.bindTask(request.workId, context)` (l.3422); failed-turn retry branch using
  `parseFailureEvidence`, `source === "codexErrorInfo"` and `codexRetries` (l.3850–3895). Only
  production caller: `src/standalone/cli.ts:57` `new StandaloneService(dataDir)`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/codex.ts` — `codexErrorInfoSchema`/`CodexErrorInfo` (l.68, l.114);
  `FailureEvidence`, `failureEvidenceSchema`, `parseFailureEvidence` (l.306–343);
  `makeFailureClassification` (l.345–365, returns `source: "codexErrorInfo"|"missing"`,
  `codexRetries: null`); `Runtime` interface (l.433); `CodexRuntime` (l.516); native thread
  qualification (l.794–870); `failureEvidence()` (l.1697–1724). `src/standalone/index.ts` re-exports
  `CodexRuntime` and `Runtime` only.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/runtime-retention.ts` — `RuntimeTerminalEvidence`,
  `RuntimeTerminalFailureEvidence` (l.19–24), `RuntimeThreadQualification`, `RuntimeSafetyPort`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `runtimeTerminalFailureEvidenceSchema` (l.157),
  `runtimeTerminalEvidenceRowSchema` (strict, parses `SELECT *`, l.182), `parseRuntimeTerminalEvidence`
  (l.199), `runtimeThreadQualificationSchema` (l.213), `FailureResolutionEvidence`,
  `FailedGenerationResolution`, `failureResolutionSchema` (l.270–313); DDL in the `ExecutionState`
  constructor (l.364–560) followed by the `PRAGMA table_info` + `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` pattern
  (l.564–579); `bindTask`/`taskBinding` (`SELECT *`, l.974–1076); `recordRuntimeTerminal` (insert
  l.1770); `registerRuntimeThreadTools` (l.1839); `runtimeThreadQualification` (explicit column list,
  l.1857); `recordRuntimeThreadQualification` (`JSON.stringify(after)` equality, l.1870–1935);
  `resolveFailedGeneration` and retry inserts (l.4109–4515).
- **Existing:** `src/core/structured-questions.ts` — `nativeInputQualificationSchema` with
  `codexVersion: z.literal("codex-cli 0.159.0")` (l.120–133), re-validated on read by
  `parseNativeInputRequest` and `CoordinationStore.parseRuntimeQuestion`.
- **New:** `src/standalone/execution-harness.ts` — `executionHarnessSchema`, `ExecutionHarness`,
  `defaultExecutionHarness` only. It must not import `codex.ts`, `state.ts` or `service.ts`, so
  those modules can import it without a cycle.
- **New:** `test/execution-harness.test.ts` — factory, power-gate and migration tests.
- **Follow:** `test/fixtures/coordination.ts:29–39` / `test/retained-evidence-store.test.ts:37–47` for
  opening a file-backed SQLite DB with `Store`, `DomainStore` and `ExecutionState`;
  `test/standalone.test.ts:1265–1300` for hand-written legacy DDL in a migration test;
  `test/background-service.test.ts` `FixtureRuntime` for a minimal fake `Runtime`.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → {T2, T4} → T3; acyclic. T2 (service.ts, state.ts) and T4
(structured-questions.ts, codex.ts native-qualification region, native-input test) may run
concurrently after T1. T3 edits codex.ts, service.ts and state.ts, so it waits for both. All slices
land in one PR. No overlap with the concurrently queued UI tickets' files (#839–#841, #860:
`web/src/**`, `src/operator/contracts.ts`, `src/standalone/operator*.ts`, `src/core/domain.ts`,
`src/core/github-source-contracts.ts`).

#### 1. Harness identifier, factory and power gate

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** new `src/standalone/execution-harness.ts` (`executionHarnessSchema`,
`ExecutionHarness`, `defaultExecutionHarness`); `src/standalone/codex.ts` (`Runtime` gains optional
`readonly harness?: ExecutionHarness`; `CodexRuntime` declares `readonly harness = "codex" as const`);
`src/standalone/service.ts` (new exported `createRuntime(context, harness)`; constructor
`runtimeFactory: (context: RuntimeSpawnContext, harness: ExecutionHarness) => Runtime = createRuntime`;
private `runtimeHarness`; new exported `powerSupervisionEnabled`); new `test/execution-harness.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/execution-harness.test.ts`: (a) `createRuntime(context, "codex")` with a context built
from `test/fixtures/runtime-safety.ts` returns an instance of `CodexRuntime` whose `harness` is
`"codex"` (constructor only; do not call `start()`); (b) `createRuntime(context, "claude" as
ExecutionHarness)` throws `/Unsupported execution harness/`; (c) `powerSupervisionEnabled`: `undefined`
options with `{ harness: "codex" }` runtime → `true`; with a runtime lacking `harness` → `false`;
`{ enabled: false }` with a harness runtime → `false`; `{ eventSource }` with a runtime lacking
`harness` → `true`; `{ enabled: true }` → `true`.
**Implementation:** `createRuntime` validates with `executionHarnessSchema.safeParse` and switches
exhaustively (`never` default) — `"codex"` → `new CodexRuntime("codex", context)`. `start()` calls
`this.runtimeFactory(context, defaultExecutionHarness)` and stores that harness in `runtimeHarness`
for T2/T3. Replace the `instanceof CodexRuntime` power expression with
`powerSupervisionEnabled(this.options.power, runtime)` implementing
`power?.enabled ?? (power?.eventSource !== undefined || runtime.harness !== undefined)`. Existing
single-argument injected factories remain assignable; do not edit them.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/execution-harness.test.js dist/test/background-service.test.js dist/test/s05-runtime-integration.test.js`;
expect all tests pass, and `rg -n "instanceof CodexRuntime" src` prints nothing.
**Complete when:** the factory and power gate are harness-keyed, tests above pass, and no
`instanceof CodexRuntime` remains in `src`.

#### 2. Persist harness on execution bindings and runtime evidence

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the branch (`ExecutionHarness`, `runtimeHarness`).
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/state.ts` (DDL for `task_execution_bindings`,
`runtime_terminal_evidence`, `runtime_thread_qualification`; add-column-if-missing migration;
`bindTask`, `taskBinding`, `runtimeTerminalEvidenceRowSchema`, `parseRuntimeTerminalEvidence`,
`recordRuntimeTerminal`, `registerRuntimeThreadTools`, `runtimeThreadQualificationSchema`,
`runtimeThreadQualification`, `recordRuntimeThreadQualification`); `src/standalone/runtime-retention.ts`
(`RuntimeTerminalEvidence.harness`, `RuntimeThreadQualification.harness`); `src/standalone/service.ts`
(`runtimeSafety` closures, `bindTask` call); `test/execution-harness.test.ts`.
**Test:** Migration test in `test/execution-harness.test.ts`: open a temp file DB, run `new Store(db)`
and `new DomainStore(db)`, then create the three tables with their exact pre-change DDL from
`state.ts` at `36938df0` (no `harness` column) and insert: one `execution_intents` row plus a
`task_execution_bindings` row for it; one `runtime_terminal_evidence` row with `workId` NULL,
`firstStatus = 'failed'`, generation/timestamp columns set and legacy `failureEvidence`
`{"classification":"transient","reasonCode":"serverOverloaded","source":"codexErrorInfo","codexRetries":null}`;
one `runtime_thread_qualification` row. Construct `new ExecutionState(db)` twice (idempotent
reopen). Assert `taskBinding(workId)?.harness === "codex"`,
`runtimeTerminal(threadId, turnId, generation)?.harness === "codex"`,
`runtimeThreadQualification(threadId)?.harness === "codex"`, and `PRAGMA table_info` shows
`harness` with default `'codex'` on all three tables. Add a fresh-DB case: `bindTask` and
`recordRuntimeTerminal` with no harness argument store `codex`; re-binding the same work ID with a
different harness value (cast) throws the existing mismatch error. (The legacy failure JSON
assertion is added in T3.)
**Implementation:** Add `harness TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'codex' CHECK(length(harness) BETWEEN 1 AND 64)`
to the three `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` statements and, after them, add the column when
`PRAGMA table_info` lacks it (same pattern as `runtimeGeneration`). Add `harness` to
`runtimeTerminalEvidenceRowSchema` and `runtimeThreadQualificationSchema` as
`executionHarnessSchema`, include it in `runtimeThreadQualification`'s column list and in the
`recordRuntimeThreadQualification` expected object. `taskBinding()`/`bindTask()` return
`TaskExecutionBinding & { harness: ExecutionHarness }` (export as `TaskExecutionBindingRecord`),
parsing `harness` with `executionHarnessSchema`; leave `TaskExecutionBinding` and its derived
interfaces unchanged. `bindTask`, `recordRuntimeTerminal` and `registerRuntimeThreadTools` take a
trailing `harness = defaultExecutionHarness`, write it on insert, and throw on an existing row whose
harness differs (binding mismatch joins the existing "Work ID already bound…" check). In
`service.ts`, the `runtimeSafety` closures and `state.bindTask(...)` pass `this.runtimeHarness`.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/execution-harness.test.js dist/test/runtime-retention.test.js dist/test/task-writer.test.js dist/test/coordination.test.js dist/test/runtime-question-store.test.js`;
expect all pass with no edits to those existing test files.
**Complete when:** legacy rows read as Codex, new rows persist the service's harness, and the
listed existing suites pass unchanged.

#### 3. Harness-neutral failure evidence

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`, `T4`
**Prerequisites:** T2 (harness column on terminal evidence) and T4 (codex.ts sequencing).
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/runtime-retention.ts` (`RuntimeTerminalFailureEvidence`);
`src/standalone/codex.ts` (`FailureEvidence`, `failureEvidenceSchema`, `parseFailureEvidence` made
neutral in place; `makeFailureClassification` returns neutral fields; `codexErrorInfoSchema` and
`CodexErrorInfo` remain only for Codex classification); `src/standalone/state.ts` (`runtimeTerminalFailureEvidenceSchema`
neutral + legacy reader, `recordRuntimeTerminal` default failure JSON,
`FailureResolutionEvidence`, `FailedGenerationResolution`, `failureResolutionSchema`,
`retryFailureSource` map, `resolveFailedGeneration` SQL parameter/compare mapping);
`src/standalone/service.ts` (retry gate and `resolveFailedGeneration` call with
`harness: this.runtimeHarness`); tests `test/retry.test.ts`, `test/codex-runtime.test.ts`,
`test/runtime-retention.test.ts` (renames only), `test/execution-harness.test.ts`.
**Test:** Extend the T2 migration test: the legacy terminal row's `failure` reads as
`{ classification: "transient", reasonCode: "serverOverloaded", source: "harness", harnessRetries: null }`;
a freshly recorded failed terminal stores JSON containing `"source":"harness"` and
`"harnessRetries"` and no `codex` key. Rename in existing tests only: `source: "codexErrorInfo"` →
`"harness"` and `codexRetries` → `harnessRetries` in failure-evidence values and expectations, and add
`harness: "codex"` to the direct `resolveFailedGeneration` proof in `test/retry.test.ts` (~l.539–552).
`retry.test.ts` must still show: transient `serverOverloaded`/`rateLimitExceeded` with numeric
harness retries queues one bounded retry; `null`, negative and fractional retries do not; budget
exhaustion at 2 is unchanged.
**Implementation:** As settled in Planning decisions. The service gate keeps every other existing
condition (thread/turn identity, callbacks ended, no known risk, no stop target, safe timestamps).
`resolveFailedGeneration` writes `retryFailureSource[value.harness]` into `failureSource` and the
`harnessRetries`/`harnessRetriesUsed` values into the existing `codexRetries`/`codexRetriesUsed`
columns, and compares committed rows against those mapped values.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/execution-harness.test.js dist/test/retry.test.js dist/test/codex-runtime.test.js dist/test/runtime-retention.test.js dist/test/background-service.test.js`;
expect all pass. Then `rg -n "CodexErrorInfo|codexErrorInfo" src --glob '!src/standalone/codex.ts'`
prints only the `retryFailureSource` map and the legacy-JSON reader/DDL CHECK lines in
`state.ts`, and `rg -n "codexRetries" src --glob '!src/standalone/state.ts'` prints nothing.
**Complete when:** no type outside the Codex runtime references `CodexErrorInfo` or a `codexRetries`
property, Codex classification is unchanged, and the retry suites pass with only the listed renames.

#### 4. Scope the Codex CLI version pin to the Codex runtime

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 (shared `codex.ts`).
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/structured-questions.ts` (`nativeInputQualificationSchema.codexVersion`);
`src/standalone/codex.ts` (new exported `codexNativeInputQualificationSchema`, used in native thread
qualification); `test/native-input.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/native-input.test.ts`, using the existing `qualification` fixture: core
`parseNativeInputRequest(request, { ...qualification, codexVersion: "codex-cli 0.160.0" })` succeeds;
`codexNativeInputQualificationSchema.safeParse({ ...qualification, codexVersion: "codex-cli 0.160.0" })`
fails while the unmodified fixture passes. Existing runtime-question tests stay unchanged.
**Implementation:** As settled in Planning decisions; the Codex runtime's qualification path must
use the Codex schema so an unqualified executable still yields no qualification.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/native-input.test.js dist/test/runtime-question-store.test.js dist/test/runtime-question-service.test.js dist/test/runtime-retention.test.js`;
expect all pass, and `rg -n "codex-cli 0\.159\.0" src` prints only `src/standalone/codex.ts`.
**Complete when:** core no longer pins a Codex version and the Codex runtime still enforces it.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Harness identifier persisted on execution bindings and runtime evidence; existing rows read as Codex | 2, 3 | Migration test in `test/execution-harness.test.ts` (T2, extended in T3) |
| Power supervision no longer depends on `instanceof CodexRuntime`; enabled for any harness runtime, assertion follows active execution | 1 | `powerSupervisionEnabled` cases; `rg "instanceof CodexRuntime" src` empty (T1) |
| Failure evidence outside the Codex runtime not typed by `CodexErrorInfo`/`codexRetries`; Codex keeps its classification | 3 | `retry.test.ts`, `codex-runtime.test.ts`, `rg` checks (T3) |
| `codexVersion` literal scoped to the Codex runtime | 4 | `native-input.test.ts` cases and `rg` check (T4) |
| Runtime factory constructs a runtime for a given harness | 1 | `createRuntime` tests (T1) |
| `npm run check` passes; existing Codex tests pass unchanged except renamed types | all | Final validation; T2/T3 rename-only rule |
| A migration test shows existing bindings and evidence read as Codex | 2, 3 | Migration test (T2, T3) |
| No user-visible behaviour changes | all | Final validation diff check; Guardrails path exclusions |

### Final validation

- From the repository root with Node from `.node-version` (24.21.0), run `npm ci && npm run check`;
  expect exit 0 (typecheck, lint, format check, build and full test suite).
- Run `git diff --stat origin/main -- src/operator web/src src/standalone/operator*.ts src/core/domain.ts docs/SPEC.md`;
  expect no output. Run `git diff origin/main --stat -- test` and confirm every pre-existing test file
  change is limited to the T3 renames (new file `test/execution-harness.test.ts` aside).
- No live-runtime run is required: behaviour is unchanged and CI evidence covers the fake and
  fixture-executable Codex paths; `test/s03b/live-runtime.mjs` keeps power supervision via
  `CodexRuntime.harness`.

### Review focus

- The legacy/neutral failure-evidence reader and the `retryFailureSource` mapping: confirm a legacy
  row and a new row yield the same retry decision, and that committed retry rows written before the
  change still compare equal on replay.
- That production code passes `this.runtimeHarness` explicitly everywhere a defaulted `harness`
  parameter exists.

content.title: Claude harness C2: Select the execution runtime per agent profile

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/824
**Planned against:** `main` at `ecb4c2eb186381077561d3820dd2b70acac161bc`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Widen the C1 harness identifier to `"codex" | "claude"` and move it into core so agent profiles can
carry it. Each profile (and each immutable profile revision) stores a harness-discriminated
`runtime` object: Codex has no settings, Claude has `model` and `reasoningEffort`. `ExecutionState.bindTask`
owns the selection rule: the first binding of an assignment conversation takes the harness of its
captured profile revision, and every later binding in the same conversation inherits it. The service
replaces its single `runtime` with one runtime per configured harness. Admission, Stop, start-up
recovery inspection, native input, runtime anomalies and retry all resolve the runtime through the
work's persisted binding. A harness with no configured or available runtime leaves the work waiting
with a visible reason and never falls back. Production configures only Codex until C3 #825 adds the
Claude runtime. Deterministic tests use fake runtimes keyed by harness. The operator API returns the
profile runtime and the binding harness through runtime-validated contracts. Deliver as one PR from
`cb/824-per-profile-runtime`.

### Guardrails

- Codex behaviour is unchanged: the same admission, wait/hold reasons (including
  `Codex runtime unavailable; restart the service`), retry budget, recovery holds, power supervision,
  Stop observation and `runtimeStatus()` output. Existing Codex tests keep their assertions. The only
  permitted existing-test edits add the new required response fields to strict-schema fixtures
  (`runtime` on profile configuration reads, `harness` on `executionGeneration`). Any other
  existing-test change means behaviour has changed: investigate it rather than adjust the assertion.
- No fallback between harnesses. A persisted binding harness is never rewritten. An unknown stored
  harness or profile runtime fails closed when read (zod parse throws).
- Out of scope:
  - `ClaudeRuntime`, the Agent SDK dependency, tokens and secrets, and passing model/effort into a
    runtime. These belong to C3 #825, which uses the C0 #822 evidence that this ticket does not need.
  - Relaxing the retry tables' `failureSource = 'codexErrorInfo'` and `reasonCode IN (...)` CHECKs.
    This is the #868 follow-on assigned to C3.
  - Operator UI for the runtime selector, harness display, token status and unavailable-harness
    recovery (C4 #826). Changes to `web/src/**` are limited to type/fixture compile repairs.
  - Per-harness `runtimeStatus` and capacity limits. Capacity stays shared and harness-neutral.
  - Native Codex X01–X08 work, which remains paused.
- Plan-mismatch budget versus ordinary repairs. The budget covers a wrong approved-plan seam or
  repository assumption. Examples: a named symbol does not own the behaviour described; the
  conversation-inheritance rule cannot be expressed in `bindTask` without breaking its existing
  rebind/consistency check; a runtime use outside the listed call sites cannot be routed by binding;
  or a fake runtime cannot drive the listed scenarios through the production service. For such a
  mismatch, spend at most one focused diagnosis and two repair cycles and record each in the delivery
  record. Stop and return for replanning if the plan is still wrong, or if the fix needs a material
  design or contract change. Ordinary implementation defects do not consume that budget: integration
  wiring, type errors, failing tests, fixtures, documentation, lint/format and CI repairs within the
  unchanged design. The ticket owner fixes them as normal work.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage,
  architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate
  unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for
  a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets
  and grants.
- Concurrent #841 (U7 project setup) also edits `src/core/domain.ts`, `src/operator/contracts.ts` and
  `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`. C2's hunks are confined to profile commands/DDL/snapshots, the
  profile configuration read and assignment `executionGeneration`. Do not touch project-setup,
  GitHub discovery or `web/src/**` settings code. Rebase onto whichever lands first and resolve
  textual conflicts without changing #841 behaviour.

### Planning decisions

- **C2 adds `"claude"`.** The issue requires a selectable second harness with Claude-validated
  settings and mixed-task tests. C1's plan deferred the value to C3, but #824's accepted scope
  governs. `createRuntime(context, "claude")` still throws `Unsupported execution harness: claude`,
  so the existing factory test stays unchanged. C3 replaces that branch.
- **Harness schema moves to core.** `test/core-boundary.test.ts` forbids `src/core` importing
  `src/standalone`, and `DomainStore` must validate profile runtimes. A new `src/core/execution-runtime.ts`
  owns `executionHarnessSchema`, `ExecutionHarness`, `defaultExecutionHarness` and
  `profileRuntimeSchema`. `src/standalone/execution-harness.ts` re-exports them so C1 imports stay
  unchanged.
- **Profile runtime shape.** `profileRuntimeSchema` is a strict discriminated union on `harness`:
  `{ harness: "codex" }` or `{ harness: "claude", model: Token | null, reasoningEffort: Token | null }`,
  where `Token` is a trimmed string of 1–128 characters with no whitespace and `null` means the
  harness default. Each strict variant rejects the other harness's settings, so Codex rejects
  `model`. ADR-1008 requires validation against the values the installed integration supports.
  No Claude integration is installed before C3, so C2 validates shape only. C3 narrows the Claude
  variant using C0 evidence. Until then no Claude turn can run, so no unsupported value reaches a
  runtime.
- **Storage.** `profiles` and `profile_revisions` each gain
  `runtime TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{"harness":"codex"}'` through the existing add-column-if-missing
  block in `DomainStore.migrate()` (the `summary` precedent). Existing profiles and revisions read
  as Codex. The value is canonical JSON parsed with `profileRuntimeSchema` on every read.
- **Commands.** `profile.create` and `profile.configure` accept an optional `runtime`. Create
  defaults it to `{ harness: "codex" }`. Configure replaces the whole object, bumps the version and
  snapshots the revision like the other fields. Existing assignments keep their captured
  `profileRevision` until `assignment.apply`.
- **Conversation-start rule lives in `bindTask`.** The service passes the harness of the captured
  profile revision (`request.profileRevision` of the assignment's `profileId`). `bindTask` uses the
  first match from this list:
  1. the existing binding for this `workId`;
  2. the earliest binding (lowest rowid) for the same `(assignmentId, conversationRevision)`;
  3. the passed harness.
  The existing consistency check then compares against that effective harness. After
  `assignment.apply`, a turn in a live conversation therefore stays on the conversation's harness.
  A new conversation (`replaceConversation`) or a new assignment uses the current profile revision's
  harness. Requests without an assignment (direct workspace work) use `defaultExecutionHarness`.
- **Configured runtimes.** `StandaloneServiceOptions.runtimeHarnesses?: readonly ExecutionHarness[]`
  defaults to `[defaultExecutionHarness]`. It must contain the default harness and no duplicates.
  `start()` calls the runtime factory once per configured harness. Each call gets its own
  `RuntimeSafetyPort`, which stamps that harness on `recordRuntimeTerminal`/`registerRuntimeThreadTools`.
  The service keys each runtime by the requested harness, not by `runtime.harness`, because test
  fakes omit it. Existing factories such as `() => runtime` are therefore called once, as today.
  Default-harness factory or start failures keep today's abort-and-hold start-up path. A non-default
  harness whose factory or `start()` fails is recorded as unavailable and Codex continues.
- **Visible waiting.** Follow the existing `runtimeUnavailableSince` pattern: before `state.begin`,
  with no capacity reservation and no admission, the intent and scheduler request wait with a reason.
  An unconfigured harness waits with `<Label> runtime is not configured`. A failed or lost runtime
  waits with `<Label> runtime unavailable; restart the service`. Labels are Codex and Claude, so the
  Codex string is unchanged. Already-admitted turns on a failed runtime follow the existing
  failure/uncertainty holds.
- **Routing by binding.** `runtimeForWork(workId)` returns the runtime registered for
  `state.taskBinding(workId)?.harness ?? defaultExecutionHarness`, or `undefined`.
  `ExecutionSupervisor` receives `runtimeFor: (workId: string) => Runtime | undefined` instead of one
  runtime. `ExecutionSupervisor` is constructed only in `service.ts`, and tests use the service.
  Start-up inspection with no runtime records `unknown`, so existing uncertainty holds are retained.
  Stop interrupt with no runtime records `failed`, keeping its current reason string.
- **Per-runtime listeners.** Each runtime's listeners close over that runtime and its harness.
  - `onUnexpectedRequest` and `onTerminalAnomaly` keep matching exact identities. Their "affect
    everything active" fallbacks (`state.activeExecutions()`, `state.activeOrLastCompleted(...)`)
    are filtered to executions whose binding harness matches the emitting runtime, so a Codex
    anomaly cannot hold Claude-bound work.
  - `onFailure` marks only that runtime unavailable.
  - Native input (`stopTask` cancellation, `handleUserInputRequest`, `runtimeAnswerEligibility`,
    `flushRuntimeAnswers`) uses the runtime that owns the question's binding/generation, iterating
    runtimes where the code iterates today.
- **Retry harness from the failed binding.** This is #868 follow-on 1. The `resolveFailedGeneration`
  call in `executeAdmitted` passes the failed work's binding harness instead of the service's single
  harness. `retryFailureSource` becomes `Record<ExecutionHarness, "codexErrorInfo" | null>` with
  `claude: null`. A new exported `harnessRetrySupported(harness)` in `state.ts` gates that call, so
  a Claude transient failure stays held without retry. C3 maps Claude and relaxes the CHECKs
  (#868 follow-on 2).
- **Operator API.** Runtime validation uses the existing strict zod contracts.
  `profileConfigurationSchema.data` gains `runtime: profileRuntimeSchema`, read by
  `readProfileConfiguration`. `profileSummarySchema` stays unchanged to limit list/fixture churn,
  and C4 may add it there. `assignmentSchema.executionGeneration` gains
  `harness: executionHarnessSchema.nullable()`, which is the persisted binding harness, or `null`
  before binding. It is read through a new `StandaloneService.bindingHarness(workId)`.
  The operator command schemas accept the optional `runtime`. `operator-api.ts` already forwards
  `{ ...c }` to `executeDomain`.
- **No C0 dependency.** All acceptance uses fake runtimes. #822 blocks only C3, not this ticket.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/execution-harness.ts` — closed `executionHarnessSchema` (`"codex"`),
  `defaultExecutionHarness`; imported by `service.ts`, `state.ts`, `codex.ts`, `runtime-retention.ts`.
- **Existing:** `src/core/domain.ts` — `profile.create`/`profile.configure` command schemas (≈L92–115),
  `profiles`/`profile_revisions` DDL (≈L326–336), add-column migration block (≈L430–437),
  `profile()`/`profileRevision()` reads (≈L901–931), command handlers (≈L1512–1548),
  `snapshotProfile` (≈L2060), `assignment.apply` (≈L1889).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/state.ts` — `bindTask` (≈L1030–1135, `INSERT OR IGNORE` + consistency
  throw), `taskBinding`, `replaceConversation` (≈L2698), `retryFailureSource` (≈L331),
  `activeExecutions`/`activeOrLastCompleted` (≈L2922–2930).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `createRuntime` (L168), `powerSupervisionEnabled`
  (L183), the single `runtime`/`runtimeUnavailableSince`/`runtimeHarness` fields (L298, L316). Its
  uses are `start()` wiring and listeners (L446–665), start-up cleanup and `stopOwned` (L735–965),
  `runtimeStatus` (L1111), `stopTask` (L2018), native input (L2101–2360), `attemptRequest` binding
  and admission (L3300–3520), `executeAdmitted` (L3583+), the retry call (L3887–3931) and
  `requireRuntime` (L4190).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/supervisor.ts` — `ExecutionSupervisor(state, runtime, …)`. It uses
  `runtime.inspectExecution` in `reconcileOnStart` and `runtime.interruptTurn` in `interrupt`.
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `profileConfigurationSchema` (≈L2140), `generation`
  within `assignmentSchema` (≈L977–1003), `profile.create`/`profile.configure` operator commands
  (≈L1793–1818). The consumers are `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` `readProfileConfiguration`
  (≈L3225) and the assignment mapping (≈L2494), and `web/src/profile-config.tsx`/`settings-changes.ts`
  (type consumers only).
- **New:** `src/core/execution-runtime.ts` — harness enum, default, `profileRuntimeSchema` and the
  `ProfileRuntime` type.
- **New:** `test/execution-harness-routing.test.ts` — service-level mixed, profile-change and
  unavailable-harness scenarios.
- **Follow:** `test/s05-assignment-prompts.test.ts` (`JourneyRuntime`, `command(...)` helper,
  `assignment.create` with `resultDestination`) for fake-runtime service journeys. Follow
  `test/execution-harness.test.ts` for migration-from-exact-DDL and fresh-row persistence tests.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 (acyclic, linear). T1 widens the shared enum that
T2–T4 compile against. T2 and T3 both edit `state.ts`/`service.ts`, and T4 needs T2's binding read
plus T1's contracts. No two tasks are safe to run concurrently.

#### 1. Profiles carry a validated execution runtime

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- New `src/core/execution-runtime.ts`.
- `src/standalone/execution-harness.ts`: re-export only.
- `src/core/domain.ts`:
  - command schemas;
  - DDL and migration for `runtime` on `profiles` and `profile_revisions`;
  - `snapshotProfile` copies `runtime`;
  - a parsed `profileRuntime(profileId, revision?)` read;
  - create/configure handlers.
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: operator profile commands and `profileConfigurationSchema.runtime`.
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`: `readProfileConfiguration`.
- `src/standalone/service.ts`: add a `case "claude"` to `createRuntime` that throws
  `Unsupported execution harness: claude`.
- `src/standalone/state.ts`: `retryFailureSource` with `claude: null`, plus the exported
  `harnessRetrySupported`.
- `docs/SPEC.md`: profile paragraph (≈L480). Add one sentence saying that a profile selects its
  execution runtime (Codex by default) with harness-specific settings, and that the Claude runtime
  is planned, not implemented.
**Test:**
- `test/domain.test.ts`:
  - `profile.create` without `runtime` reads `{harness:"codex"}`.
  - Create with `{harness:"claude", model:"opus", reasoningEffort:"high"}` round-trips.
  - `{harness:"codex", model:"x"}`, `{harness:"claude", model:"has space"}` and an unknown harness
    are rejected with no row or version change.
  - `profile.configure` from Codex to Claude bumps the version. `profileRuntime(id, 1)` stays Codex
    and `profileRuntime(id, 2)` is Claude.
- `test/execution-harness.test.ts`: a migration test creates the exact pre-change `profiles` and
  `profile_revisions` DDL with a row, runs `DomainStore.migrate()` twice, and reads Codex. A stored
  unknown runtime JSON throws on read.
- `test/operator-api.test.ts`:
  - The profile configuration read returns `runtime`.
  - An operator `profile.configure` with a Claude runtime succeeds.
  - One with Codex plus `model` is rejected as invalid input.
**Implementation:** as in Planning decisions (harness move, shape, storage, commands). Update
strict-schema fixtures that build profile configuration reads (for example
`test/operator-settings-presentation.test.ts`) only by adding `runtime`.
**Validate:** From the repository root on Node 24.21.0, after `npm ci`, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/domain.test.js dist/test/execution-harness.test.js dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/core-boundary.test.js`.
Expect all to pass, including the new cases, and the existing factory test unchanged.
**Complete when:** profiles persist and return a validated runtime, old databases read as Codex,
and `npm run typecheck` passes.

#### 2. Bindings persist the conversation's harness

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the branch (`"claude"` is a valid harness).
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/state.ts` `bindTask` (effective-harness resolution before
the insert, and the consistency check against it).
**Test:** Add to `test/execution-harness.test.ts`, using an `ExecutionState` fixture like the
existing fresh-row test:
1. The first binding for assignment A, conversation 1, with harness `"claude"` stores Claude.
2. A second workId for A in conversation 1, passed `"codex"`, stores Claude.
3. Rebinding the same workId with a different passed harness keeps Claude and does not throw.
4. After `replaceConversation(A)`, a new workId passed `"codex"` stores Codex.
5. A different assignment B, passed `"codex"`, stores Codex.
**Implementation:** as in Planning decisions (conversation-start rule).
**Validate:** From the repository root, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/execution-harness.test.js dist/test/retry.test.js dist/test/s05-assignment-prompts.test.js`.
Expect all to pass.
**Complete when:** the five assertions pass and existing binding tests are unchanged.

#### 3. The service routes each binding to its harness runtime

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2's binding rule passes its focused check.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/standalone/service.ts`:
  - replace `runtime`/`runtimeUnavailableSince`/`runtimeHarness` with a per-harness map;
  - add `runtimeForWork`;
  - add the `runtimeHarnesses` option;
  - harness-bound safety ports;
  - per-runtime listeners;
  - `attemptRequest`, which resolves the profile-revision harness, binds it, then gates on that
    runtime;
  - `executeAdmitted`, stop/cleanup, native input and the retry call;
  - power gate over any configured runtime.
- `src/standalone/supervisor.ts`: the `runtimeFor` constructor parameter.
**Test:** new `test/execution-harness-routing.test.ts`. Use two `JourneyRuntime`-style fakes that
record `startThread`/`resumeThread`/`startTurn`/`interruptTurn`/`inspectExecution` calls. The
factory is `(_, harness) => fakes[harness]` with `runtimeHarnesses: ["codex","claude"]`,
`power: { enabled: false }` and `routingClient: null`.
- **Mixed task.** Use a Codex lead profile and a Claude worker profile, with one task holding the
  lead plus an `assignment.create` worker.
  - The Codex fake receives only the lead's thread/turns and the Claude fake only the worker's.
  - `state.taskBinding` reports `codex`/`claude`.
  - With both turns held open, `stopTask` interrupts each turn once, on its own fake only.
  - A Codex `onUnexpectedRequest` without identity holds the Codex execution but not the Claude one.
  - A Claude transient failure with `failureEvidence` (`serverOverloaded`) is held with no
    `execution_retry_resolutions` row.
- **Profile change during a live conversation.**
  1. The first turn of a Codex-profile assignment completes.
  2. Then: `profile.configure` sets `runtime` to Claude, and `assignment.apply` follows.
  3. An operator message triggers the next turn. It runs `resumeThread` on the Codex fake and the
     binding stays Codex.
  4. A new assignment with the same profile starts on the Claude fake.
- **Unavailable harness.**
  1. Start with `runtimeHarnesses: ["codex"]`. A Claude-profile assignment's request waits with
     `Claude runtime is not configured` and holds no capacity reservation. Neither fake starts it,
     and a Codex assignment in the same project is still admitted.
  2. Restart the service with both harnesses. The waiting work is admitted on the Claude fake, and
     its binding stays Claude.
  3. Separately, firing the Claude fake's `onFailure` makes the next Claude request wait with
     `Claude runtime unavailable; restart the service`. `runtimeStatus()` stays `available` and
     Codex work continues.
- **Recovery.** Restart while Claude-bound work is admitted and running, with Claude unconfigured.
  The supervisor records `unknown` for it, the Codex fake's `inspectExecution` is not called for it,
  and its uncertainty, writer and capacity holds remain.
**Implementation:** as in Planning decisions (configured runtimes, visible waiting, routing,
listeners, retry).
**Validate:** From the repository root, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/execution-harness-routing.test.js dist/test/execution-harness.test.js dist/test/supervisor.test.js dist/test/standalone.test.js dist/test/retry.test.js dist/test/recovery.test.js dist/test/power-service.test.js dist/test/runtime-question-service.test.js dist/test/s05-assignment-prompts.test.js`.
Expect all to pass with the existing files unmodified.
**Complete when:** the four scenarios pass, no reference to a single service runtime remains, and
the existing Codex service tests pass unchanged.

#### 4. The operator API returns the binding harness

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T1`, `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 complete (the `StandaloneService.bindingHarness(workId)` read exists or is
added here).
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: `generation.harness`.
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`: the assignment mapping (≈L2494).
- `src/standalone/service.ts`: `bindingHarness(workId): ExecutionHarness | null`.
**Test:** `test/operator-api.test.ts`. An admitted Codex assignment's task read has
`executionGeneration.harness === "codex"`. A Claude-profile assignment waiting on an unconfigured
harness reads `"claude"` once bound. Its `waitReason` contains `Claude runtime is not configured`.
Existing `deepEqual` comparisons of `executionGeneration` across reads keep passing. Update any
strict `assignmentSchema` fixtures in `test/operator-contracts.test.ts` only by adding `harness`.
**Implementation:** as in Planning decisions (operator API).
**Validate:** From the repository root, run
`npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-contracts.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime.test.js`.
Expect all to pass.
**Complete when:** the operator API returns runtime-validated profile runtimes (T1) and binding
harnesses.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Mixed task (Codex lead, second-harness worker) with fake runtimes | 3 | `execution-harness-routing.test.ts` mixed-task case |
| Profile change during a live conversation affects only new conversations | 2, 3 | T2 binding-rule cases; routing test profile-change case |
| Unavailable/unconfigured harness holds work visibly without fallback | 3, 4 | Routing test unavailable and recovery cases; T4 `waitReason`/harness read |
| Runtime field on profiles, default Codex, per-harness settings validation | 1 | T1 domain and operator-api cases |
| Operator API returns runtime on profiles and bindings, validated at runtime | 1, 4 | T1 profile configuration read; T4 `executionGeneration.harness` |
| Service holds one runtime per harness; admission, Stop, recovery, capacity act on the binding's runtime | 3 | Routing test mixed (Stop, anomaly), unavailable (no capacity reservation) and recovery cases |
| Codex behaviour and tests unchanged | 1–4 | Existing suites pass with only the Guardrail-listed fixture additions; final `npm run check` |

### Final validation

- From the repository root on Node 24.21.0 (`.node-version`), run `npm ci && npm run check`. Expect
  exit 0 with typecheck, lint, format, build and every test passing. The count is the baseline 1309
  plus the new cases.
- Run `git diff --stat main -- test/`. Expect existing test files to change only for the new cases
  and the Guardrail-listed fixture field additions.
- Baseline evidence:
  - Node 24.21.0 at the planned SHA.
  - `npm run build:service` passed.
  - `node --test` passed 55/55 over `execution-harness`, `domain`, `supervisor`,
    `s05-assignment-prompts`, `retry` and `operator-api`.
  - #868 reported `npm run check` passing with 1309/1309 at its head.
  - CI run 38102292309 on the planned SHA was in progress at planning time.

### Review focus

- `bindTask` effective-harness resolution against its existing rebind `UPDATE` and the consistency
  throw. A ready, never-admitted binding must not change harness.
- Every former `this.runtime` use is routed by binding. Check especially the anomaly fallbacks,
  native-input generation checks and the generation/identity guards in `executeAdmitted` (formerly
  `this.runtime !== runtime`).
- Non-default harness start-up failure must not abort the service or alter Codex start-up failure
  handling.

nodes.body:
<!-- run-github-project:authority-pause:v1 -->
**Planning paused: ADR-1008 decisions needed**

- Repository: `chrisbanes/ensemble`; issue #825; Project item `PVTI_lAHOAAN4ns4BatgHzg_hBSs`
- Configuration digest: `sha256:d397f661efe931ee747a5bfa66dcdccf32900dacb662235eea215bb9b7526ff8`; base `main@1dbcd712d6ebe8e7505a9ffcc2974033d118ff75`
- Current state: Status `Todo`, assigned `chrisbanes`. No plan, branch, worktree or PR exists.
- Blocked operation: implementation planning (`to-plan --auto`), which returned `human-required`.

The C0 probe evidence (#822, `docs/evidence/issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-2026-10-11.md`) contradicts two ADR-1008 guarantees. The token mechanism is undefined.

**D1. Shared, writable sandbox temp directory (F6.1).** The Claude sandbox's `TMPDIR` is `/tmp/claude-<uid>`, which is writable and shared across tasks. ADR-1008 promises workspace-only writes, and #777 promises a sandbox equivalent to Codex's (Codex excludes `/tmp` and `TMPDIR`).
- **A (recommended):** make a bounded proof the first task: can the temp directory be redirected per task, or `/tmp/claude-<uid>` be denied? If not, amend ADR-1008 and #777 to accept the shared directory as a disclosed limit.
- **B:** accept it as a disclosed limit now.
- **C:** hold the harness until it is fixed upstream.

**D2. An unusable sandbox does not fail the turn (F6.4).** Commands fail with exit 126 and nothing runs unsandboxed, but the query ends in `success`. ADR-1008 says "failure if the sandbox is unavailable".
- **A (recommended):** amend the guarantee to "commands never run unsandboxed", add an Ensemble sandbox self-test before each turn that fails the turn as runtime-unavailable, and disclose that a sandbox breaking mid-turn shows up only as failed commands.
- **B:** accept per-command failure as a disclosed limit.
- **C:** detect exit 126 in the event stream (fragile).

**D3. Token storage and ownership.** This is shared with #826 (https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/826#issuecomment-6110987141). No "secret store" exists.
- **A (recommended):** reuse the `env:NAME` reference. #825 resolves it and passes the token only into the Claude subprocess environment, never into the Codex spawn environment.

F5.5 and F6.3 (untested) are not blocking: ADR-1008 already discloses untested surfaces as limits.

**Resume condition:** D1–D3 are recorded in ADR-1008 (with matching wording in #777), the #825 body and the #826 body; then `to-plan --auto` runs again on #825.

**Overlap:** PR #905 (#894) changes the runtime spawn environment in `src/standalone/service.ts` `start()`, the seam #825 would use. Whichever PR merges second rebases onto it.

<!-- run-github-project:authority-resume:v1 -->
**Planning resumed**

- Pause record: https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/825#issuecomment-6111443663
- Decision evidence: Chris chose the recommended options (A for D1–D3) in the run controller chat. They are recorded in ADR-1008 by PR #907 (merged as `777cde3ae796a6bd51d264c32c9e1234b6705b7e`), with matching updates to the #777, #825 and #826 bodies.
- Current state: Status `Todo`, assigned `chrisbanes`; configuration digest `sha256:d397f661efe931ee747a5bfa66dcdccf32900dacb662235eea215bb9b7526ff8`; base `main@777cde3a`. No plan, branch or PR exists yet.
- Next: `to-plan --auto` against the updated contract.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/825
**Planned against:** `main` at `777cde3ae796a6bd51d264c32c9e1234b6705b7e`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add `src/standalone/claude.ts` with a `ClaudeRuntime` that implements the existing `Runtime` interface (`src/standalone/codex.ts`). It uses `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, pinned to the C0-qualified `0.3.296`. Each Ensemble turn is one `query()`. The first turn uses a runtime-minted `sessionId`, and later turns `resume` it. The policy, credential and recovery contract is [ADR-1008](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/777cde3ae796a6bd51d264c32c9e1234b6705b7e/docs/adr/1008-claude-code-execution-harness.md) as merged by #907. Settled SDK behaviour comes from `docs/evidence/issue-822-claude-sdk-probes-2026-10-11.md` (C0).

The `Runtime` interface is generalised only where Claude needs it, and every addition is optional, so Codex is unchanged:
1. A pre-admission turn check that can make work wait.
2. Per-turn model and effort.
3. A per-turn process identity recorded through the safety port.

The service gains a stored Claude token reference, excludes it from every spawn environment, and builds the Claude per-turn environment. The first task is a bounded live proof that selects how the shared sandbox `TMPDIR` is handled. All three possible outcomes are already decided by ADR-1008.

### Guardrails

- ADR-1008 and the #825 body are authoritative. Do not reopen the token, sandbox self-test or `TMPDIR` decisions. If a decision proves unimplementable, stop and return evidence.
- Codex behaviour is unchanged. New `Runtime` members and arguments are optional, and `CodexRuntime` ignores them. Existing Codex tests must pass unmodified, except for mechanical type updates.
- The production service keeps `runtimeHarnesses` defaulting to `["codex"]`. Enabling and advertising Claude, README/SPEC/acceptance text, and live journeys belong to #827. Token set/clear HTTP, UI, status and the profile model/effort UI belong to #826. This ticket provides only the domain command, the read seams and the runtime.
- Claude transient-failure retry stays unsupported: `harnessRetrySupported("claude")` stays false. Failures are classified and recorded, but there is no retry-table migration.
- No fallback to another harness. Nothing silently retries or releases writer or capacity ownership. Crash, process loss, a malformed stream, unverified exit or an unverified Stop leaves the existing uncertainty, writer and capacity holds.
- The token is never logged, persisted or rendered. It never appears in hold or wait reasons, errors, conversation events, evidence files or test output. Reads of `~/.env` and live turns happen only inside T1 under its budget and Chris's per-ticket authorization.
- Tests never spawn the real Claude CLI or need credentials. CI runs on ubuntu with Node 24 and Node 26. The SDK is injected as a fake, and any sandbox or process boundary is injectable.
- **Plan-mismatch budget vs ordinary repairs.**
  - (a) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping. Examples: a named symbol or seam doesn't exist or behaves differently, an SDK option name or behaviour contradicts the C0 evidence, or `recordTurnProcess` cannot bind without changing Codex admission.
  - (b) Ordinary in-scope work stays with the ticket owner and does **not** consume that allowance: implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, lint, format and CI repairs, including Node 26 or npm 12.2.0 lockfile fixes. Record (b) corrections briefly in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks or reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption, and preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Token reference storage.** Follow the `installation_discovery` / `discovery.configure` pattern in `src/core/domain.ts`:
  - Add a singleton `claude_runtime_credentials(singleton, credentialRef)` table, seeded with `NULL`.
  - Add a `claude-token.configure` operator command (`credentialRef: env:NAME | null`, same regex as delivery). Its receipt is `{configured}` only.
  - Add `claudeTokenReference()`.
  - #826 builds HTTP and UI on these.
- **Spawn environment and inheritance.** The `start()` closure in `service.ts` also excludes the configured Claude reference and every nonempty exact-value alias of it. To do this, generalise the body of `deliveryRuntimeEnvironment` into `credentialFreeEnvironment(env, names)` and keep the wrapper.
  - `runtimeSpawnSnapshot` keeps its meaning: what the long-lived runtime inherited at start. Claude never calls `spawnEnvironment()`, so the snapshot is never refreshed.
  - The per-turn Claude base environment is `credentialFreeEnvironment(snapshot, current delivery refs ∪ {Claude ref})`. It is therefore never wider than what started, and delivery credentials stay excluded.
  - If the reference name or its value is present in the snapshot, the work waits with "Claude token reference was configured after the service started; restart the service". This mirrors delivery `activationAllowed` and `test/delivery-service.test.ts:558`.
- **Missing token.** An unconfigured or empty token, an inheritance hold, an unsupported model or effort, or a failed sandbox self-test means the turn does not start. These outcomes come from the new pre-admission check: the work waits via `state.wait`/`store.wait` with a reason prefixed `Claude runtime unavailable:`, so it is not held and gets no uncertainty hold. The check runs again on the next scheduler wake, so no restart is needed once the condition clears.
- **Invalid token.** The CLI emits `init` and then returns `subtype: "success"`, `is_error: true`, `terminal_reason: "api_error"` (C0 F7.1). This fails the turn visibly with `classification: "permanent"`, `reasonCode: "unauthorized"`.
- **Claude turn environment.** Base environment, then:
  - Remove any inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, because API-key billing is deferred.
  - Add `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<resolved>`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dataDir>/claude/config` (created mode 0700) and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1`.
  - Add the `TMPDIR` handling selected by T1.
  - Query options: `settingSources: []` and `strictMcpConfig: true`.
- **Process identity per turn.** Each turn has its own CLI, so `ClaudeRuntime.processIdentity()` returns `null` at admission. The turn sequence is:
  1. `startTurn` mints the turn ID.
  2. It calls `query()` with a **gated streaming-input prompt**.
  3. The custom `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` wraps `node:child_process.spawn`, passes `SpawnOptions.signal` (needed for abort, per C0 F2) and captures the identity.
  4. A new optional `RuntimeSafetyPort.recordTurnProcess({threadId, turnId, processIdentity})` synchronously sets the process columns on the single `execution_recovery_identities` row. That row's intent must be `submitting`, bound to `threadId`, with `turnId` and `processId` still `NULL`.
  5. Only then does the runtime yield the prompt.

  If the record fails, the turn aborts, exit is verified and `startTurn` rejects through the existing submission-failure path. A crash before the record leaves a `NULL` identity, so the work fails closed into the existing held/no-proof path; the CLI has no prompt yet. `inspectExecution` returns `unknown`, as Codex does.
- **Settings.** Add `RuntimeTurnSettings = {model, reasoningEffort}`, passed as an optional fourth argument to `startTurn` and to the pre-admission check. The service derives it from `domain.profileRuntime(profileId, profileRevision)` for Claude bindings.
  - `ClaudeRuntime.start()` performs one model-free `query()` with a never-released gated prompt. It reads `supportedModels()` and the init `claude_code_version`, then aborts and verifies exit.
  - It caches these and exposes `supportedSettings()` for #826.
  - The pre-admission check rejects unsupported values by waiting with a reason.
  - If T1 shows `supportedModels()` cannot be read before a prompt, use the C0 F7.6 set (`default|sonnet|opus|haiku|fable`; efforts `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`), pinned to SDK `0.3.296` by a test that asserts the installed version.
- **Coordination tools.** Serve `coordinationTools` via `createSdkMcpServer({name: "ensemble"})` and `tool()`, with the shape from `z.fromJSONSchema(inputSchema)` (available in zod 4.6.5).
  - The `PreToolUse` hook precedes the MCP handler (C0 F5.1). It queues `tool_use_id` by `(tool name, canonical input digest)`, and the handler takes the oldest matching ID as `RuntimeToolCall.callId`, so coordination receipts keep their `(threadId, turnId, callId)` idempotency.
  - If there is no match, the call is refused with an `isError` result and never dispatched.
  - `dispatchCoordinationTool` remains the authoritative argument validator.
- **Tool policy.**
  - `permissionMode: "dontAsk"`.
  - `tools` / `allowedTools`: `Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, Bash` plus `mcp__ensemble__*`.
  - `disallowedTools`: `AskUserQuestion, WebFetch, WebSearch, Agent, Task, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode` (the C0 P5 policy).
  - No `canUseTool` grant. A `canUseTool` callback, if ever invoked, denies the call and emits `onUnexpectedRequest({method: "claude/canUseTool:<tool>", threadId, turnId})`, so the existing service hold path applies.
  - The hook records `{toolUseId, toolName, decision}` in a per-turn ledger capped at 256 entries, with names only and no inputs. It denies:
    - any tool outside the allowlist;
    - `Write`/`Edit` whose resolved `file_path` is outside the writable roots;
    - `Bash` with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`.
- **Sandbox.** `{enabled: true, failIfUnavailable: true, allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true, network: {allowedDomains: []}, filesystem: {allowWrite: [workspace, ...T1 per-task root if redirected]}}`, plus a T1 `denyWrite` if that is the selected outcome.
  - **Self-test.** This is model-free and runs in the turn's spawn context (same environment without the token, `cwd` = workspace): `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)' /usr/bin/true`, with a 5 s timeout and exit 0 required. A non-darwin platform fails it.
  - It is injectable for tests. Its limit (it proves that Seatbelt can start, not the CLI's exact profile) and the mid-turn exit-126 limit are disclosed.
- **Effective policy.** `ClaudeRuntime.effectivePolicy(workspace)` returns a validated object: writable roots, shared write roots (`/tmp/claude-<uid>` unless T1 redirected or denied it), `network: "denied"`, `fileToolConfinement: "hook"` and a `limits` list.
  - `limits` covers: hook-enforced (not OS) file confinement; a mid-turn sandbox failure shows only as failed commands; the untested C0 surfaces F5.5, F6.3 and F6.4 (missing binary); the shared temp root if applicable; and the self-test scope.
  - #826 renders it.
- **Repository instructions.** `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are read from the workspace root and from each first-level `repo-*` directory (regular files only via `lstat`, 32 KiB each and 128 KiB total, truncated with a marker, labelled by relative path). They go into `systemPrompt: {type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", append}` and are never loaded through setting sources.
- **Message validation and failure mapping.** Zod schemas cover the consumed subset: `system/init`, `assistant` text blocks and `result`. Other message types are ignored.
  - A known type that fails validation aborts the query and emits `onTerminalAnomaly` for that turn.
  - A `result` maps as follows:
    - `success` with `!is_error` → `completed`.
    - `success` with `is_error` and `terminal_reason: "api_error"` → `failed`, `permanent`/`unauthorized` when the error text matches the not-logged-in/401 shape, otherwise `unknown`/`api_error`.
    - `error_during_execution` → `unknown`/`error_during_execution`.
    - `error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd` and `error_max_structured_output_retries` → `permanent` with the subtype as the reason code.

  - The CLI1 spawn wrapping (`managedAssignmentEnvironment(deliveryRuntimeEnvironment(...))`) is already in the baseline, and T2 extends it.
  - #826 consumes `claude-token.configure`, `claudeTokenReference()`, `supportedSettings()` and `effectivePolicy()`.

### Review focus

- Ordering of `recordTurnProcess` before prompt release, and fail-closed handling of every abort or exit path (no unverified survivor reported as completed).
- No token exposure across any of: Codex env, alias values, Claude MCP/Bash/hook children (scrub), errors, waits, events, evidence and test output.
- Preflight waits never pass through `state.begin` or create uncertainty records, and they never block Codex work.
- Hook correlation for coordination `callId` idempotency.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- SDK `0.3.296` cannot be installed or pinned, or its `query`/hook/MCP/sandbox option names or behaviour contradict the C0 evidence in a way that removes a planned seam.
- The `PreToolUse` hook does not precede the SDK MCP handler for the same call, which leaves `callId` correlation impossible.
- `recordTurnProcess` cannot be implemented without changing Codex admission or recovery semantics.

- Repository: `chrisbanes/ensemble`; issue #826; Project item `PVTI_lAHOAAN4ns4BatgHzg_hBTQ`

**Decision needed:** how the Claude subscription token is stored, and whether #825 or #826 owns that. ADR-1008 and #825 say the token lives in "Ensemble's secret store", but no secret store exists (`docs/design/standalone.md` lists secret handling as still to be defined). The only credential mechanism today is the `env:NAME` reference used for discovery and delivery credentials. Whether the token may be ambient in the service environment that Codex agents also inherit is a security-policy question.

Options found during planning:
- **A (recommended by the planner).** Use the existing `env:NAME` reference pattern. #826 owns the set/clear command, a configured/available status read and the UI. #825 owns resolving the reference, passing it only to the SDK subprocess and keeping it out of the Codex spawn environment. Invalid-token detection stays at turn start in #825.
- **B.** Add a native blocker #825 → #826 so #825 defines the mechanism first. This serialises C4 behind C3.
- **C.** Split token setup/status into a separate slice blocked by #825, and narrow #826's acceptance.

Everything else in #826 can be delivered on current main: the profile runtime selector with model and effort, harness and execution identity display, per-harness status and holds, and the static policy disclosure.

**Resume condition:** the decision is recorded in the #826/#825 bodies or an ADR-1008 note. Coordinate with #887 (Backlog), which rewrites the same runtime-unavailable copy.
