<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/826
**Planned against:** `main` at `777cde3ae796a6bd51d264c32c9e1234b6705b7e`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Extend the existing React operator UI and operator API so an operator can choose a profile's harness, see which harness and execution identity each assignment ran on, read the effective execution policy and its disclosed limits, see an unavailable harness with a recovery route, and set or clear the Claude token reference. The contract is [ADR-1008](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/blob/777cde3ae796a6bd51d264c32c9e1234b6705b7e/docs/adr/1008-claude-code-execution-harness.md) as merged by #907 and the #826 body. Every piece reuses an existing pattern: `Panel`, `Aside`, `DraftField`/`NativeSelect`, `DiscoveryCredentialRow`, `ChangeList`, assignment row metadata and the retained server-rendered pages.

The work is ordered by dependency on [#825](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/825) (plan: https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/825#issuecomment-6111943992):

- **T1–T5 need nothing from #825** and start from current `main`: per-harness status, the profile runtime selector (model and effort, shape-validated), harness/model/effort/execution identity on task and assignment views, recovery routes for unavailable-harness waits and failed Claude turns, and the policy-disclosure surfaces (Codex content now).
- **T6–T8 consume #825's seams and need #825 merged to `main`** (exact seams listed under Planning decisions): token set/clear/status (#825 T2), supported model/effort values (#825 T4), and the Claude effective policy (#825 T5).

**Ordering constraint for the controller.** #826 cannot reach its acceptance until #825 is merged. Either admit #826 after #825 merges (one PR), or admit it now and hold the implementation at the T5/T6 boundary; do not stub or duplicate #825's seams. Before T6 the implementer checks `gh issue view 825 --json state` and `git log origin/main`, rebases onto `main`, and verifies each named seam in code. No live Claude turn, credential or `~/.env` read is needed anywhere in this ticket.

### Guardrails

- ADR-1008 and the #826 body are authoritative. The token is an `env:NAME` reference; #826 owns operator set/clear and configured/available status and never displays the value or the reference name; #825 resolves it and an invalid token fails the turn. A failed per-turn sandbox self-test or missing token is a visible wait for an unavailable runtime, never a hold and never a fallback. Do not reopen these decisions.
- Codex behaviour and copy stay identical: `Codex runtime unavailable — restart the service`, the retained "Effective execution policy" heading and its current Codex statements, retry and recovery. Existing Codex tests pass unmodified except mechanical fixture/type updates for the new strict fields.
- Do not enable or advertise Claude. `runtimeHarnesses` keeps defaulting to `["codex"]`. README, `docs/acceptance.md` and "Claude is supported" claims belong to #827; `docs/SPEC.md` keeps saying the Claude runtime is planned, not implemented.
- `workspace.runtime` (`{state}` for the default harness) keeps its shape: CLI2 (#895, draft PR #908) consumes it. New contract fields are additive. `profileSummarySchema` is not changed.
- No new layout. Use only the patterns named in Approach. If a piece cannot be built from existing components, return to design review instead of inventing one. Edit `design/DESIGN.md` text only; do not touch `design/design.pen`.
- Each slice that adds a surface updates, in place and without dated sections, the `design/DESIGN.md` differences bullet, the `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` control dispositions and the `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` row it touches.
- A live conversation is never moved between harnesses. The UI says a runtime change saves a new profile revision and affects new conversations only.
- No secret appears in status reads, receipts, errors, waits, DOM text, logs or test output: status reads carry booleans and closed enums only.
- **Plan-mismatch budget vs ordinary repairs.**
  - (a) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping. Examples: a named #825 seam is absent or lacks a fact this plan needs (`claude-token.configure`, `claudeTokenReference()`, `RuntimeSpawnContext.claude.turnEnvironment()`, `supportedSettings()`, `effectivePolicy()`); `workspace.runtime` cannot stay compatible with CLI2; a named existing symbol or route list behaves differently from this plan.
  - (b) Ordinary in-scope work stays with the owner and does **not** consume that allowance: implementation, integration, test, fixture and stub updates for the new strict fields, documentation, lint, format and CI repairs, including Node 26 or npm 12.2.0 lockfile fixes, and mechanical field-name adaptation of the T7/T8 adapters to #825's merged shapes. Record (b) corrections briefly in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks or reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption, and preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Status contract.** The service reports one status per harness: `available`, `not-configured` (not in `runtimeHarnesses`) or `unavailable` with `since`. It is added as `workspace.harnesses`, an additive array in the read the shell and Settings already poll. `workspace.runtime` stays. Production today is Codex-only, so Claude reads `not-configured`.
- **Selecting a harness that is not enabled is allowed**, with a warning beside the selector. `docs/SPEC.md` (profile paragraph) already says work for an unconfigured or unavailable runtime waits visibly and never falls back, and the domain accepts it (#869). Blocking would contradict that.
- **Assignment runtime facts.** `assignmentSchema` gains `runtime` (the `profileRuntimeSchema` of the assignment's captured `profileRevision`, `domain.profileRuntime(profileId, revision)`). The displayed harness is the persisted binding harness (`executionGeneration.harness`) when bound, else `runtime.harness`. Model and effort are shown only when they belong to the displayed harness. `profile_revisions` always carries a row per revision (`snapshotProfile`).
- **Validation is pre-submit and keyed to the server's field paths** (`runtime.model`, `runtime.reasoningEffort`). A pure `runtimeErrors(values, supported)` returns specific messages. A new `ConfigurationDraft.reject(errors)` (settings-state.ts) sets `errors`, `phase = "rejected"` and the notice without sending, and `submitDraft` accepts an optional `errors` argument and focuses the first invalid field exactly as it does after a rejected send. Server-side supported-value rejection (T7) uses `OperatorApiError(400, "invalid-input", ["runtime.model"])`.
- **Recovery route classification.** Waits created by the service are `<Label> runtime is not configured`, `<Label> runtime unavailable; restart the service` (#869) and, from #825, `Claude runtime unavailable: <detail>`. One pure presenter classifies a wait by the `^<Label> runtime ` prefix of `waitReason` and returns the explanation and ordered routes. Unknown wording falls back to showing the reason verbatim. A failed Claude turn is held (`state.hold("Bound turn failed or was interrupted")`); its failure facts come from `runtime_terminal_evidence` (`classification`, `reasonCode`, already bounded to 64 characters), exposed as `executionGeneration.failure`. Only a `claude` binding renders a failure notice, so Codex presentation is unchanged. #869 recorded "in-product recovery for Claude work while Claude is unconfigured" as owned by this ticket: the routes are explanation, Stop (existing), edit the profile for new conversations, Runtime status, and Recovery for held executions. The UI offers no force-resume and no harness migration.
- **Token status mirrors discovery.** `GET /api/operator/claude-token` returns `{configured, available, state}`; the set/clear command is `claude-token.configure` with `credentialRef: env:NAME | null` (same regex as discovery). `available` means the variable has a non-empty value in the service environment; `restart-required` reports #825's inheritance hold. The row sits in the existing Settings "Runtime and recovery" panel as children, as the discovery row sits in "Projects". Validity is not probed; the row says it is checked when a Claude turn starts, and an invalid token appears as the T4/T6 failure notice. The Claude reference and its resolved value join the operator-api redaction exclusions and the reference fence, as the discovery reference does.
- **#825 seams consumed (from its approved plan, not yet in code).** Verify each at the T6 gate; adapters validate with zod and are duck-typed so no `Runtime` interface edit is needed here:
  - T6: domain command `claude-token.configure` (`credentialRef`, receipt `{configured}` only), `claudeTokenReference()`, and `RuntimeSpawnContext.claude.turnEnvironment(): {env, token} | {unavailable: string}`. If its unavailable result has no machine-readable code, add an additive `code: "not-configured" | "empty" | "restart-required"` to it (the string stays) so the status read needs no string matching.
  - T7: `ClaudeRuntime.supportedSettings()` (supported model values and reasoning efforts, cached at `start()`).
  - T8: `ClaudeRuntime.effectivePolicy(workspace)` (writable roots, shared write roots, `network`, `fileToolConfinement: "hook"`, `limits`).
- **Policy disclosure model.** `policy: {lines: string[], limits: string[]} | null` per harness. Codex content is the current retained text, moved to `src/standalone/execution-policy.ts` and guarded by a test that reads `executionPolicy("/w")` (workspace-only writes, no network, `/tmp` and `TMPDIR` excluded). A Claude policy is built from `effectivePolicy()` with raw paths mapped to category labels (task workspace, per-task temporary directory, shared sandbox directory) so no private data-directory path is rendered. `null` means not yet disclosable and renders as such.
- **Entry points** (named gaps are intentional):

  | Surface | Disposition |
  | --- | --- |
  | React profile create and configure | T2 selector, T5 policy, T7 supported values |
  | Retained `/profile/:id` | Read-only runtime line; its save keeps the stored runtime (T2) |
  | Retained `/` profile create form | Unchanged: creates a Codex profile; choosing a runtime is a Settings action (T2) |
  | Settings index (profile rows, Runtime and recovery panel) | T2, T1, T6 |
  | Shell alert and Runtime page | T1, T5 |
  | Task rows, assignment details, `/app/assignments/:id/recovery` | T3, T4, T5, T6, T8 |
  | Retained `/runtime`, `/runtime/task|assignment/:id`, `/assignment/:id` | T1, T3, T5 |
  | Inbox, composer, project lead and routing candidate pickers | Show no execution settings or holds today; unchanged (gap: harness not shown while picking a lead or candidate) |
  | CLI | Reads share the contracts; runtime facts and commands belong to #895/#896; no CLI controls here |
  | Context menus, extensions, notifications | None exist for these surfaces; the `/app/profiles/:id/settings` and recovery deep links are retained |

  Counterparts: token Set ↔ Clear (and Cancel); a harness change is reversed by another save (new revision); Stop and Recovery are the existing counterparts for waiting and held work.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:**
  - `src/core/execution-runtime.ts` — `executionHarnessSchema` (`codex`, `claude`), `profileRuntimeSchema` (strict; Claude `model` and `reasoningEffort` are tokens or `null`).
  - `src/standalone/service.ts` — private `harnessLabel` (216); `runtimeWaitReason` (1094); `bindingHarness` (1431); `runtimeStatus()` (1436, default harness only, `ponytail: ... C4`); `runtimeUnavailableSince`; `runtimeHarnesses` option; non-default construction or start failure marks that harness unavailable.
  - `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `readWorkspace` (1707) and `profiles()` (1696); `readTask` assignment mapping with `waitReason` and `executionGeneration` (2583; the recovery read reuses it); `readProfileConfiguration` (3315, returns `runtime`); `readDiscoveryStatus` (3703); `exclusions()` (419) and `referenceFence()` (371) which include the discovery reference and value; the `discovery.configure` branch (4586); `executeDomain` maps `DomainPolicyError` and `OperatorApiError` field paths.
  - `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `workspaceSchema` (75), `generation` (984), `assignmentSchema` (994), `operatorCommandSchema` (1597; `discovery.configure` at 1889), the receipt union (`discovery.configure` at 2011), `discoveryStatusSchema` (2510), `profileConfigurationSchema` (2191).
  - `src/standalone/operator-web.ts` and `operator-credentials.ts` — `knownApi`, the GET dispatch and `operatorRouteAuthority` list the discovery route; `test/operator-cli-http.test.ts` ("every known API route has an explicit authority") enumerates them.
  - `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts` — retained Runtime overview: alert (98), "Effective execution policy" section (128), task and assignment pages (`taskPage`, `statusForAssignment`, `selectAssignmentExecution`). `src/standalone/operator.ts` — retained `profile()` and `assignment()` pages.
  - `src/standalone/state.ts` — `runtime_terminal_evidence` (has `workId`, `firstStatus`, bounded `failureEvidence`); `harnessRetrySupported`.
  - `web/src/` — `app.tsx` (alert at 827; `SettingsProps.workspace` carries the workspace read), `profile-config.tsx`, `settings.tsx` (`submitDraft`, `ReceiptText`, `Panel`, `Aside`, `DraftField`), `settings-state.ts` (`ConfigurationDraft`, `matchesConfigurationReceipt`), `settings-changes.ts` (`profileChanges`), `settings-index.tsx`, `discovery-credential.tsx`, `recovery.tsx` ("Revisions and actual admitted generation" panel, 296), `task-detail.tsx` (`AssignmentRows`), `task-overview.ts` (`assignmentRow`), `task-workspace.tsx` (assignment `<details>`, "Recorded wait / execution reason", ~1515).

- **New:**
  - `web/src/execution-runtime.ts` — pure presenters: harness labels, `runtimeSummary`, `runtimeErrors`, `harnessNote`, `executionSummary`, `waitRoute`, `failureNotice`. `web/src/execution-notice.tsx` — `ExecutionNotice` (text plus `ActionLink` routes).
  - `src/standalone/execution-policy.ts` — `codexPolicyDisclosure()`, later `claudePolicyDisclosure()`.

  - Tests: `test/operator-execution-runtime.test.ts` (unit), `test/operator-harness-status-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-harness-assignment-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.ts`, and a fake Claude-shaped runtime in `test/fixtures/operator-web.ts` (T7/T8).
- **Follow:**

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic, one chain: T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 → T5 → T6 → T7 → T8. Every task edits `src/operator/contracts.ts`, `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` and shared `web/src` files, so none may run concurrently. External gate **#825-merged** applies to T6, T7 and T8 (below). T1–T5 are mergeable from current `main`.

#### 1. Per-harness runtime status and shell alerts

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/core/execution-runtime.ts`: new `executionHarnessLabels`; re-exported from `src/operator/contracts.ts` for the web.
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: `harnessStatusSchema` (discriminated on `state`; `unavailable` carries `since`; a shared base object so T5 and T7 extend it once); `workspaceSchema.harnesses`.
- `src/standalone/service.ts`: replace `harnessLabel` with the shared map; add `harnessStatuses()` beside `runtimeStatus()` (which is unchanged; remove the stale C4 `ponytail:` note).
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` `readWorkspace`: add `harnesses`.
- `src/standalone/operator-runtime.ts`: `RuntimeOperatorApi.harnessStatuses`; the overview alert loops over unavailable harnesses.
- `web/src/app.tsx`: one `Alert` per unavailable harness. `web/src/recovery.tsx` `RuntimeSettings`: an "Execution runtimes" Panel with one row per harness and a `StatusBadge` (Available, Not enabled, Unavailable), the destination the T4 "Runtime status" route opens.
- Fixtures: `createOperatorFixture` forwards `harness` to `runtimeFactory(context, harness)`; `startSettings` takes an optional `{runtimeFactory, serviceOptions}`.
- Stubs and fixtures for the new strict field: `test/operator-api.test.ts` (the two `runtimeStatus` stubs near 969 and 997), `test/operator-client.test.ts:7` (typed `Workspace`) and `test/operator-contracts.test.ts` (workspace parse cases).
**Test:**
- `test/operator-api.test.ts` "workspace reads report every harness's status":
  - default fixture → `harnesses` deep-equals `[{harness:"codex",state:"available"},{harness:"claude",state:"not-configured"}]` and `data.runtime` is still `{state:"available"}`;
  - `runtimeHarnesses: ["codex","claude"]` with a factory that throws for `claude` → claude `unavailable` with a numeric `since`, codex `available`; then `f.runtime.crash()` → codex `unavailable`.

The existing `test/operator-web-browser.test.ts` banner tests still pass unmodified.
**Implementation:** `harnessStatuses()` returns one entry per `executionHarnessSchema.options` in order: `not-configured` when absent from `runtimeHarnesses`, `unavailable` with `since` from `runtimeUnavailableSince`, else `available`. Alerts keep the exact `<Label> runtime unavailable — restart the service` format. `not-configured` is the normal Codex-only state and raises no shell alert; it surfaces on the profile selector (T2) and on affected work (T4).
**Validate:** From the implementation worktree root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/operator-contracts.test.js dist/test/operator-client.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime.test.js dist/test/operator-harness-status-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-web-browser.test.js dist/test/execution-harness-routing.test.js`; expect exit 0 and no failures.

#### 2. Profile pages choose and show the runtime

**Implementation:** Selecting Claude reveals the two inputs and a `harnessNote` sourced from `workspace.harnesses` (`not-configured`: "The Claude runtime is not enabled on this service. Assignments using this profile wait until it is; they never fall back to Codex."; `unavailable`: restart note; `available`: none). A short Aside item says a runtime change saves a new profile revision and affects new conversations only. Do not add model or effort for Codex.

content.title: Claude harness C5: Qualify Claude journeys and document limits

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/827
**Planned against:** `main` at `899fecd22f502b7ab1127940183e233413126c66`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Build one guarded live-journey driver (Claude-only, mixed Codex + Claude, Stop, crash mid-turn, plus the token subprocess-scrub facet) on the real `StandaloneService` with the real `ClaudeRuntime` and the approved ChatGPT.app Codex launcher, and cover its refusals, budget, redaction and cleanup with deterministic tests. Draft the README/SPEC/acceptance/development text in parallel. Run the live qualification only after Chris grants it (T3). Then, only if every journey passes and the terms recheck finds no material change, enable Claude in the production service and change the docs from "implemented, not enabled" to "qualified, with limits" (T4). The branch is `cb/827-claude-qualification`, with one PR.

### Guardrails

- **Live checkpoint.** T3 is the only task that runs live turns or touches the Claude token. It needs Chris's explicit grant in chat for this ticket covering (a) reading only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `~/.env` (line `export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=...`), by name, inside the driver process through `loadToken()` in `test/claude-c0/harness.mjs`, never echoed, logged or read by the agent, and (b) the live-turn budget below. Without that grant, T1, T2 and their checks still run, the draft PR may open, and work stops at T3 with the status "awaiting live grant". A drain must not treat a plan, issue or controller message as the grant.
- **Live-turn budget (hard caps, enforced by the driver's ledger).** Claude profiles use `model: "haiku"`, `reasoningEffort: "low"`. Allow at most 2 attempts per facet. Per-attempt `startTurn` caps: scrub 1 Claude; J1 Claude-only 8 Claude; J2 mixed 4 Codex + 3 Claude; J3a Stop 1 Claude; J3b crash 2 Claude (the killed turn plus the recovered turn). Global caps: 30 Claude and 10 Codex `startTurn` calls. Each turn gets 4 min, after which the driver issues Stop and records a failure. Each facet attempt gets 20 min of wall time, and the whole session gets 2 h. One escalation to `sonnet`/`low` per journey is allowed only after a haiku attempt fails for a recorded model-compliance reason (for example, the wrong tool or argument) and never for a harness defect. It counts against the same caps. Exhausting a cap stops that facet as `failed (budget)`.
- **Isolation.** Use disposable roots (`mkdtemp` under `test/temp.js` `tmpdir()`, mode 0700) and temporary SQLite only. Never use the real Ensemble data directory, operator projects, launchd agent, `~/.codex` state edits or the installed Haze prototype. Git fixtures are local throwaway repositories with no remote. Codex uses the existing ChatGPT.app launcher login (`/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex`), read-only, as CLI7 did.
- **Process termination.** Signal only exact PIDs that the driver created or recorded (the child service `child.pid` and recorded Claude/Codex process identities). Verify each exit with `MacProcessTerminationVerifier`. Escalate SIGTERM then SIGKILL only after re-verifying identity. Never use name or command-line matching such as `pkill`.
- **Evidence hygiene.** Redact at write time with `redact`/`redactionContext` from `test/claude-c0/harness.mjs`. Before committing, scan every new evidence file for the token value (in memory), `sk-ant-`, `Bearer `, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=` followed by a value, the disposable-root paths and the home path. Any hit blocks the commit.
- **Enablement gate.** T4 enables and advertises Claude only if J1, J2, J3a and J3b pass, the scrub facet has a recorded disposition, and the terms recheck finds no material change. Otherwise production keeps `runtimeHarnesses` at `["codex"]`, the docs keep "implemented, not enabled", the evidence records the failure, and work stops for Chris.
- **Out of scope.** No new runtime features, no operator route for bound-turn recovery (#899 records it as a gap), no OpenCode/Pi, no API-key billing, no launchd plist changes for token provisioning (document the requirement instead), and no change to Codex behaviour or the profile default (Codex).
- **Plan mismatch vs ordinary repair.** (a) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example, `resolveHeldExecution` bound-turn recovery cannot resume the Claude session, the child-process service cannot share the data directory after SIGKILL, or the token reference cannot be set before start) gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. After that, stop and report. (b) Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, CI and rebase repairs (including adapting to #899/#929 moving recovery types) are the owner's work and consume no allowance. A Claude runtime defect found live is fixed in scope with a deterministic regression test in `test/claude-runtime*.test.ts`, and the facet is rerun within its attempt cap.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record each correction and renew the affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles, as in (a); ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap, and stop for material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Enablement and advertising follow ADR-1008 and the approved C3/C4 plans; no new stakeholder decision is needed.** ADR-1008 makes the runtime a per-profile setting with Codex as the default, and says Claude may be advertised once these journeys pass and the terms have been rechecked. The approved #825 plan and #826 assign "enabling and advertising Claude, README/SPEC/acceptance text and live journeys" to #827. The ADR defines no service-level enable flag, so T4 enables Claude unconditionally in the production CLI: exported `productionRuntimeHarnesses = ["codex", "claude"]` in `src/standalone/cli.ts`, passed by `main`'s default factory. Profiles still default to Codex, and `ClaudeRuntime.start()` only creates the config directory and imports the bundled SDK. Existing Codex work is therefore unaffected, and a Claude profile without a token waits visibly as `not-configured`. No env opt-in flag is added, because nothing requires one. The terms recheck fetches the URL cited in the ADR and records the date and a paraphrase. A material change, such as an explicit prohibition covering a self-hosted single-operator service, is a re-plan trigger that returns to Chris.
- **Recovery path.** The crash journey uses the service seam that the deterministic tests use (`StandaloneService.resolveHeldExecution` with a `bound-turn` receipt built from `recoveryView()`, then a new operator message, as `test/recovery-continuation.test.ts` does). The bound-turn route has no operator HTTP or CLI route (#899/PR #929 records this as a gap), and the evidence states that. "Resumes the session" means the post-recovery Claude turn runs on the same `threadId` (the SDK session ID).
- **Crash method.** The service runs in a child Node process (`test/c5/service-child.mjs`, following `test/ui01/runtime-contract.mjs`'s spawn/SIGKILL pattern), so SIGKILL of that exact PID is a real service crash. After the kill, the driver checks whether the recorded Claude CLI process exits by itself within 10 s. It records that observation either way and stops a survivor only by exact verified PID. A restart is a new child on the same data directory.
- **Scrub qualification.** In one Claude turn, the agent runs sandboxed Bash that writes `env | cut -d= -f1` to `env-names.txt`, writes `env` to `env-full.txt`, and writes `ps -E -o command= -p $PPID` output (or an error) to `ps-parent.txt`, all in the workspace. The driver reads the files in memory and records only booleans: token variable name present, token value present in `env`, token value visible in the parent's environment through `ps`, and `ENSEMBLE_C5_CONTROL` present. `ENSEMBLE_C5_CONTROL` is a non-secret positive control set in the service environment, which shows the probe really reads Bash's environment. The driver deletes the files before any evidence is written. Outcomes:
  - Name and value absent, control present: scrub qualified for Bash.
  - Value visible: disclosed residual-exposure limit (enablement may still proceed, as ADR-1008 allows).
  - Control absent: probe inconclusive, so the scrub stays "not qualified".
  - Hooks and stdio MCP children: not applicable. The hook runs in-process, and strict MCP config allows no stdio servers. Recorded as such.
- **Token reference.** The driver sets the token in the service process env under `ENSEMBLE_C5_CLAUDE_TOKEN`, configures `claude-token.configure` with `env:ENSEMBLE_C5_CLAUDE_TOKEN`, then stops and restarts the service before any Claude turn. This follows `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` "inherited by the running runtime waits until restart". The test exercises the real reference path, not just the SDK variable.
- **No new deterministic runtime tests are planned.** Fault, rejection, Stop and restart holds are already covered by `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` (for example "losing the Claude process mid-tool…", "a restart with a running Claude execution holds it as unknown"). Tests are added only for the new driver and for the T4 production default, or as regressions for defects found live.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts`
  - `StandaloneServiceOptions.runtimeHarnesses` defaults to `[defaultExecutionHarness]`.
  - `createRuntime(context, harness)` builds `ClaudeRuntime`.
  - `claudeContext.turnEnvironment()` resolves the `env:` token reference and requires a restart after the reference is configured.
  - Other members used: `stopTask`, `recoveryView`, `resolveHeldExecution`, `claudeTokenStatus`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/claude.ts`
  - `ClaudeRuntime` (per-turn `query()`, sandbox self-test, `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR` per-task base).
  - `claudeTurnEnvironment` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1`.
  - `claudePolicyLimits` line 327 states that the scrub is not yet qualified. It is surfaced through `effectivePolicy()` and mirrored in `test/fixtures/operator-web.ts`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/cli.ts` — `main(commandLine, serviceFactory)` constructs the production `StandaloneService` without `runtimeHarnesses` (Codex only).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/coordination-tools.ts` — tools `ensemble_delegate`, `ensemble_ask_question`, `ensemble_report_result`, `ensemble_request_completion`.
- **Existing:** `docs/SPEC.md:537-547` (profile runtime paragraph; "The Claude runtime is planned, not implemented."), `README.md` "Where it stands", `docs/acceptance.md` scenarios and required-evidence areas, and `docs/development.md` (operator setup).
- **New:**
  - `test/c5/live-journeys.mjs`: guarded driver. It accepts exactly `--live --facet scrub|claude-only|mixed|stop|crash`; anything else exits 2 and creates nothing. It imports from `dist/`, keeps the budget ledger, writes redacted JSON to stdout, and cleans up its disposable root by exact path.
  - `test/c5/service-child.mjs`: child service for the crash facet. It talks to the parent over IPC and reports the recovery identity and turn counts.
  - `test/c5-live-harness.test.ts`: deterministic tests for the driver.
  - `npm` script `"c5:live": "node test/c5/live-journeys.mjs"`.
  - `docs/evidence/issue-827-claude-journeys-<date>.md` plus `.json`.
- **Follow:**
  - `test/cli7/live-diagnostics.mjs` for the guard, launcher check, real service/runtime factory with a wrapped `startTurn` budget, and evidence/cleanup shape.
  - `test/s04b/live-runtime.mjs` for lead/worker prompts, `waitForTool` and completion assertions.
  - `test/claude-c0/harness.mjs` for `loadToken`/`redact`.
  - `test/s05-live-harness.test.ts` for refusal tests.
  - `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` for Claude profile, task and token setup.
  - `docs/evidence/issue-825-claude-tmpdir-proof-2026-10-11.md` for the evidence format (facet table, budgets used, attempts, untested, method and cleanup).

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 and T2 are roots, T3 depends on T1, and T4 depends on T2 and T3. T1 (`test/c5/*`, `test/c5-live-harness.test.ts`, `package.json`) and T2 (`README.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/acceptance.md`, `docs/development.md`) share no files and may run concurrently. T3 is the isolated live task behind Chris's grant. T4 edits T2's files and `src/standalone/cli.ts`/`claude.ts`. `README.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/acceptance.md`, `pre-turn-recovery.ts` and `service.ts` overlap open PR #929 (#899 CLI6). Whichever lands second rebases; that is an ordinary repair. #901 (CLI8) is blocked by #899 and shares no planned file.

#### 1. Guarded live-journey driver and deterministic harness tests

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `test/c5/live-journeys.mjs` (entry only), `test/c5/harness.mjs` (pure helpers: grammar parse, budget ledger, redaction scan, exact-path cleanup; no side effects on import), `test/c5/service-child.mjs`, `test/c5-live-harness.test.ts`, `package.json` (`c5:live`). Reuses `test/claude-c0/harness.mjs` (`loadToken`, `redact`, `redactionContext`), `dist/src/standalone/{service,claude,codex,termination,operator-api}.js`.
**Test:** `test/c5-live-harness.test.ts`, spawning the driver with `execFileSync`/`spawnSync` and a sentinel token in env:
- No args, `--live` alone, an unknown facet, or a facet without `--live` → exit 2, stderr matches `/Refusing/`, no `ensemble-c5-` root created, sentinel never in output.
- With `--live --facet scrub` and `HOME` pointed at an empty temp dir and no token env → exit 2 with `/token unavailable/`, no SDK call, no root left behind.
- The ledger from `test/c5/harness.mjs` (imported via `pathToFileURL`, as `test/claude-c0-harness.test.ts` imports its harness) refuses the (cap+1)th `startTurn` per facet and the 31st Claude / 11th Codex globally.
- The redaction scan helper flags a string containing the sentinel token, `sk-ant-x`, `Bearer abc`, the disposable root path or `$HOME`, and passes a clean sample.

**Implementation:**
1. Driver gates: exact grammar, then the ChatGPT.app launcher present, then the token from `loadToken()`, before any root is created.
2. Per facet:
   - Create a 0700 root with a local git repo fixture.
   - Construct `StandaloneService` with `runtimeHarnesses: ["codex","claude"]`, `power: {enabled:false}`, `routingClient: null` and a factory where `codex` → `new CodexRuntime(launcher, ctx)` and `claude` → `createRuntime(ctx, "claude")`, each with `startTurn` wrapped by the ledger.
   - Set up the token reference, then restart (Planning decisions).
   - Create lead/worker profiles via domain commands with the facet's runtimes (Claude: haiku/low).
   - Run the facet:
     - `scrub`: one Claude worker turn running the env probe (Planning decisions).
     - `claude-only`: a Claude lead `ensemble_delegate`s to a Claude worker. The worker calls `ensemble_ask_question`; the driver answers through the domain answer command; the worker calls `ensemble_report_result` with a nonce; the lead calls `ensemble_request_completion` with that result ID; the task finalizes.
     - `mixed`: as `claude-only`, but with a Codex lead and no question.
     - `stop`: a Claude turn told to run `sleep 120` in Bash. After the turn is running with a recorded process identity, call `service.stopTask(taskId)`. Assert the interrupt is acknowledged and the terminal is observed. Otherwise assert the hold is visible with the writer hold retained. Assert no further `startTurn`.
     - `crash`: in `service-child.mjs`, a Claude turn running `sleep 120`. Once it is running with a process identity, SIGKILL the child PID. Observe the Claude CLI exit (exact PID). Restart the child on the same data dir. Assert `held`, observation `unknown`, writer/capacity/uncertainty holds all true, the hold visible through the operator API read with `execution.read` scope, and 0 `startTurn` over a 30 s quiet window. Then `resolveHeldExecution(bound-turn receipt)` and one operator message. Assert exactly one new Claude turn on the same `threadId` that completes, a `startTurn` total of 2, and holds released only after that.
3. Each facet emits JSON: Node/SDK `0.3.296`, CLI version (`initializationResult`), Codex launcher version and SHA-256, model/effort, `startTurn` counts, outcome and failure stage, process identities with verified exits, and cleanup.
4. A `finally` stops the service, verifies exits, and removes the root and the `/tmp/ens-*` temporary base through `releaseClaudeTemporaryBase`, all by exact path.

**Validate:** From the worktree root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/c5-live-harness.test.js dist/test/claude-c0-harness.test.js`. Expect all tests to pass with 0 failures and no live call made (no launcher or token needed except the refusal cases).
**Complete when:** The driver and child exist, refuse unsafe invocations, enforce the ledger, and their deterministic tests pass. No live turn has run.

#### 2. Pre-qualification documentation of Claude support, policy differences, limits and terms caveat

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `docs/SPEC.md` (profile runtime paragraph near line 547), `README.md` ("Where it stands"), `docs/acceptance.md` (new "Claude execution harness" scenario rows C5-1..C5-4 plus a required-evidence area marked **Unproved**), `docs/development.md` (Claude token setup).
**Implementation:** Replace "The Claude runtime is planned, not implemented" with text that the Claude runtime is implemented and selectable per profile, but not enabled in the production service until the #827 journeys qualify it. State the execution-policy differences from Codex, sourced from ADR-1008 and `claudePolicyLimits`:
- `dontAsk` with an allowlist and a `PreToolUse` hook.
- Seatbelt sandbox with no unsandboxed retry.
- A per-turn self-test, with work waiting when the self-test fails.
- A per-task `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR`.
- Hook (not OS) confinement of edit tools.
- Isolated configuration, with repository instructions passed as text.
- Questions only through `ensemble_ask_question`.

Also cover:
- The terms caveat, linking the ADR and the terms URL.
- The disclosed limits, and that untested surfaces stay limits.
- Setup: `claude setup-token`, then an `env:NAME` reference that must be in the service process environment at start. The launchd agent does not set it, so the operator adds it to the service environment. Configuring it after start needs a restart.

The acceptance rows are C5-1 Claude-only, C5-2 mixed, C5-3 Stop + crash recovery, and C5-4 scrub qualification. Distinguish implemented from planned throughout, revising docs in place without dated sections.
**Validate:** From the worktree root, run `npx prettier --check README.md docs/SPEC.md docs/acceptance.md docs/development.md && rg -n "planned, not implemented" docs/SPEC.md`. Expect prettier to pass and `rg` to find no match for the Claude runtime sentence.

#### 3. LIVE qualification run and evidence record (authorization checkpoint)

Also: `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on PATH, `npm run build` fresh at the T1 head, the ChatGPT.app launcher present, and no other live harness running.

**Implementation:**
1. Recheck the terms page cited in ADR-1008 and record the date and a ≤2-sentence paraphrase. A material change is a re-plan trigger.
2. Run `npm run c5:live -- --live --facet <f>` for `scrub`, `stop`, `crash`, `claude-only` and `mixed`, in that order (cheapest first), within the caps.
3. Write the evidence record in the #825 format:
   - Versions: Node, SDK, CLI, Codex launcher, candidate SHA.

   - Per-facet disposition table: passed/failed/inconclusive with attempt number and observations.
   - Budget used against the caps.
   - Attempts and corrections.
   - The scrub result and its mapping to the limit text.
   - The crash observation of whether the Claude CLI exited on its own.
   - Recovery via the service seam, with no operator route.
   - An "Untested", limits-only list, including at least:
     - stdio MCP and hook children (not applicable);

**Validate:** From the worktree root, run each facet command above and expect exit 0 with `"outcome":"passed"` for `claude-only`, `mixed`, `stop` and `crash`, and a recorded disposition for `scrub`. Then run `node --input-type=module -e` with the `test/c5/harness.mjs` scan helper over `docs/evidence/issue-827-*` and expect no findings. Then `git status --short` should show only the evidence files and any regression fix.
**Complete when:** The evidence is committed, every facet has a disposition within budget, all exact-PID exits are verified, no disposable roots or `/tmp/ens-*` bases remain, and the scan is clean.

#### 4. Enable and advertise the qualified Claude harness

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T2`, `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 passed under the Guardrails enablement gate. Otherwise skip T4, keep the T2 wording, and report.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/cli.ts` (new exported `productionRuntimeHarnesses`, passed in `main`'s default factory); `src/standalone/claude.ts` `claudePolicyLimits` (rewrite the scrub line, and any "Untested" line that T3 now covers, per the evidence); `test/background-service.test.ts` (already imports `main` from `src/standalone/cli.js`); the four docs from T2.
**Test:** In `test/background-service.test.ts`, assert `productionRuntimeHarnesses` deep-equals `["codex","claude"]`, and that `main`'s default factory passes it (a `StandaloneService` built with `{runtimeHarnesses: productionRuntimeHarnesses}` and a fake runtime factory, after `start()`, reports Claude `available`, not `not-configured`, in its harness statuses, while a default-runtime profile still routes to Codex). Existing `operator-web`/policy browser tests must still pass with the updated `claudePolicyLimits`.
**Implementation:**
- Pass `runtimeHarnesses: productionRuntimeHarnesses` in the default factory.
- Update the scrub limit text to the T3 outcome. For example, "Bash children do not see the token (#827 evidence); …", or the residual-exposure wording if T3 found exposure.

**Validate:** From the worktree root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/background-service.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime-service.test.js dist/test/operator-harness-status-browser.test.js`. Expect 0 failures.
**Complete when:** Production starts both runtimes, the docs and limits match the evidence, and the focused tests pass.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Claude-only journey (lead + worker, coordination tools, question, result, completion) on a disposable repo | 1, 3 | T1 driver tests; T3 `--facet claude-only` passed |
| Mixed journey: Codex lead delegates to Claude worker | 1, 3 | T3 `--facet mixed` passed |

| README, SPEC and acceptance distinguish implemented from planned and state policy differences and the terms caveat | 2, 4 | T2 prettier and `rg` check; T4 doc review against evidence |
| Journeys run under a scoped grant against disposable projects only, never touching the prototype or operator projects | 1, 3 | T1 refusal/cleanup tests; T3 grant recorded in evidence; exact-path cleanup check |

### Final validation

- From the worktree root, at the integrated delivery candidate (after T4, or after T3 if enablement is withheld), run `npm ci && npm run check` with Node 24.21.0 first on PATH. <!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/904
**Planned against:** `main` at `eb03ca244167d2caeacffafff7adb44fc4a3143d`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Design-only change on a ticket branch (suggested `cb/904-cli-credentials-design`): through the Pen MCP server, add the CLI credentials Settings frames (desktop and phone) to `design/design.pen`, copying the existing Settings index (`vEr15`), Profiles rows (`gBpa3`) and Stop dialog (`uQrNE`) patterns and starting from the shipped #894/#905 copy and structure. Then reconcile the drawn design against the shipped section and `docs/design/operator-cli.md`, refresh `design/DESIGN.md` (screen map, notes, implemented differences) with the node ids read back from MCP, and return a reconciliation report. No code, docs under `docs/`, issues or labels change; the controller files any follow-up issues from the report.

### Guardrails

- `design/design.pen` is edited and read ONLY through the Pen MCP tools (`mcp__pencil__execute`, `get_app_state`, `read_skill`); never Read, Grep, `cat`, `sed` or parse it. Shell use is limited to `shasum`, `git status` and `git diff --stat`/`--check`, which do not open its content.
- Scope is exactly: new frames in the "09 / Settings, sign-in & recovery" area, the canvas-contents and review-notes text updates (T4), and `design/DESIGN.md`. Do not edit web code, `docs/design/operator-cli.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/acceptance.md` or existing frames' content (other than the specific text/index additions named in T4). Do not restyle or re-layout existing frames.
- Fixture token values are obviously fictional placeholders, never a real or locally issued token (DESIGN.md: all names, identifiers and captures are fictional fixtures). Phone and desktop frames are static: they prove no focus, keyboard, clipboard or screen-reader behaviour (DESIGN.md "Design limits").
- DESIGN.md is revised in place to the current contract (AGENTS.md): no dated sections, amendment logs or approval narration; differences are stated factually without issue numbers (the controller files issues afterwards).
- Differences between design and shipped UI are reported, not fixed in code here. Do not file issues, labels, assignees or Project status; the controller does.
- Plan-seam failures (a): the assumptions that the Pen MCP can open, write and persist the ticket worktree's `design/design.pen` (T1), that the shipped section is as read in Implementation context, or that frames can be added without disturbing existing ones. If one is wrong, allow one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, then stop and return to the controller for a replan. Do not consume this allowance for ordinary repairs.
- Ordinary in-scope implementation, documentation and CI repairs (b) are owned by the implementer with no allowance cap: layout or clipping fixes, copy and token changes, node-reference corrections, DESIGN.md wording, format/lint, a CI rerun, re-applying additive frames onto a newer base. Record the correction briefly in the delivery record and renew affected evidence.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews; use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes.

### Planning decisions

- **Draw from the shipped section.** #894 followed existing Settings patterns because no frame existed; the least-risk design starts from that structure and copy and deviates only for a stated design reason against the issue's state list or `docs/design/operator-cli.md` (lines 22-29, 159-170, 183-184). Every deviation or gap becomes a reconciliation-report row; this keeps the diff small and the report meaningful.

Intended node ids are read back, never predicted.

There is no deep link, context menu, extension or notification surface, and the legacy HTML UI has no credential controls (docs/evidence/issue-894-cli1-2026-10-11.md). Counterparts: create → revoke (irreversible by design: recovery is issue or rotate a replacement); rotate → revoke the old one afterwards; lost token → rotate or issue new. The main checkout (at `111f46d7`) and `origin/main` (`eb03ca24`) hold the byte-identical `design.pen` (same SHA-256). Write persistence to a worktree copy is untested and is the T1 proof.

### Implementation context

Each is shown once, expires, and can be rotated or revoked."); inline create form (Credential name `TextField`, Scope native select Read-only/Read-write default Read-only, Lifetime native select 7/30/60/90 days default 90, "Create credential"); name error "Name must be 1 to 64 characters without control characters."; request failure "The request failed. Check the list below before retrying." / "The outcome is unknown. Check the list below before retrying."; list-unavailable "Credentials are unavailable." + Retry; empty "No CLI credentials."; no loading state.

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `design.pen` contains the credentials section for desktop (empty, list with scope/expiry/last-use, create with scope and lifetime, one-time reveal, rotation, revocation confirmation, expired/revoked) | 2 | T2 id-map, text-inventory, structure readbacks and screenshots for 133-138 |

### Final validation

- From the ticket worktree root, with Node from `.node-version` (24.21.0; the planning host has v26.9.0, so select the pinned version) after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` at the integrated delivery candidate (before PR; CI runs the same); expect exit 0 (typecheck, lint, format, build, tests pass). The change touches no code, so if one timing-sensitive test fails under host load, rerun its file and rely on the PR's CI as authoritative, as in the #894 evidence.

content.title: Scope the 128-row exclusions bound to the task being read

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/917
**Planned against:** `main` at `e0979727bf15d8d167e06bb7e345496b23cd7a19`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Replace the installation-wide `retainedRowsExceed(128)` gate in `OperatorApi.exclusions()` with a per-task gate over the task's own `turn_requests` and recovery identities, using the same capped-count technique and fail-closed result as #875. Implementation branch: `cb/917-task-scoped-exclusions-bound`, from `main` at or after the planned SHA. One PR, three observable slices.

1. **Store and service reads (T1).** Two indexed, capped per-task counts and one service method replace the global count; the global `retainedRowsExceed` is deleted (its only production caller is `exclusions()`).
2. **Exclusions gate (T2).** `exclusions()` calls the per-task method before reading any row; the privacy-boundary tests are rewritten for the new scope and both directions (unrelated rows no longer withhold; the task's own excess still does).
3. **Docs (T3).** State the task-scoped bound in `docs/SPEC.md` and `docs/design/ui03-tasks.md`.

### Guardrails

- Decision (Chris, 2026-10-12, recorded in #917): the bound is scoped to the task being read. No retention, pruning or schema change. The 128 limit keeps applying per kind (turn requests and recovery identities are each compared with 128, as today, not summed).
- Unchanged: fail-closed (`exclusions()` returns `undefined`, prose withheld) when the task's own rows exceed 128; the 128-assignment bound, the 400-binding bound, the combined 128 profile/project revision budget, revision-coverage checks, unknown-assignment checks, and every other privacy check in `exclusions()`.
- The gate must still run before `turnRequestsForTask`, `recoveryForTask` or `assignments()` read any row, and must use indexed capped queries (`LIMIT`), never a history scan or a full-history store read.
- Out of scope: caching or once-per-request exclusion computation (#877), the Claude token reference (#936), conversation-history redaction (#918), recovery paging (#932).
- Failure classes. (a) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example the per-task recovery count not matching `recoveryForTask(taskId)` rows, or `exclusions()` having a task-scoped caller the plan missed): one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, then stop and return it for replanning. (b) Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs (type errors, fixture seeding, lint/format, assertion tuning, flaky timing such as #921): the owner repairs them directly with no allowance, recording the correction in the delivery record and renewing affected evidence. Stop for a material change to the accepted outcome, coverage, architecture or authority, or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews.

### Planning decisions

- Per-kind comparison, not a sum, matches the replaced behaviour (`countUpTo(limit+1) > limit || recoveryCountUpTo(limit+1) > limit`).
- Both counts use existing indexes: `turn_requests_taskId_sequence` (`src/standalone/scheduler.ts:53`) and `task_execution_bindings_task` (`src/standalone/state.ts:464`), joined to `execution_recovery_identities` by its `workId` primary key. The recovery count therefore equals the rows `recoveryForTask(taskId)` (no `alsoWorkId`, as `exclusions()` calls it) would load, so the gate bounds exactly what is subsequently read. Evidence: `ExecutionState.recoveryForTask` selects identities whose `workId` is in `task_execution_bindings WHERE taskId = ?`.
- Installed per-task cost: task list/Inbox reads call `exclusions(projectId, taskId)` once or twice per visible task, so each now issues two capped (<=129 index entries) counts instead of two global ones; this is bounded and acceptable. No batching (that is #877).
- The global methods are deleted (in T2, once `exclusions()` stops calling them) rather than kept: `rg retainedRowsExceed|countUpTo|recoveryCountUpTo src` finds no other production caller, so keeping them would leave dead global-scope reads.
- Boundary evidence lives in T2 (the slice that establishes the privacy boundary). T3 documents behaviour and may run in parallel.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `OperatorApi.exclusions(projectId?, taskId?, historyBindings, disclose)`; inside `if (taskId)` (about line 549) the comment "The 128-row bounds are installation-wide" and `if (this.service.retainedRowsExceed(128)) return undefined;` precede `d.assignments(taskId)`, `turnRequestsForTask`, `recoveryForTask`. All task-scoped reads reach it through `this.exclusions(projectId, taskId)`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts:1824` — `StandaloneService.retainedRowsExceed(limit)` calls `schedulerStore.countUpTo(limit + 1)` and `requireState().recoveryCountUpTo(limit + 1)`; `turnRequestsForTask` / `recoveryForTask` are its per-task row reads.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts:240` — `SchedulerStore.countUpTo(limit)` (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM turn_requests LIMIT ?)`); `forTask(taskId)` is the index-backed row read. `src/standalone/state.ts:3576` — `ExecutionState.recoveryCountUpTo(limit)` over `execution_recovery_identities`; `recoveryForTask` at 3563.
- **New:** `SchedulerStore.countForTaskUpTo(taskId, limit)` — `SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM (SELECT 1 FROM turn_requests WHERE taskId = ? LIMIT ?)`.
- **New:** `ExecutionState.recoveryCountForTaskUpTo(taskId, limit)` — `SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM (SELECT 1 FROM task_execution_bindings binding JOIN execution_recovery_identities identity ON identity.workId = binding.workId WHERE binding.taskId = ? LIMIT ?)`.
- **New:** `StandaloneService.taskRetainedRowsExceed(taskId, limit)` — same shape as the method it replaces, using the two new reads with `limit + 1`.
- **Follow:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` `countUpTo` and `state.ts` `recoveryCountUpTo` for the capped-count form and doc comments; `test/targeted-read-stores.test.ts` parity tests for store tests; `test/operator-targeted-exclusions.test.ts` for the task-scoped privacy tests.
- **Test fixtures:** `test/fixtures/read-guards.ts` — `seedOrphanHistory(f, count, kinds)` seeds rows bound to random tasks/assignments; `forbid(target, names)` and `historyRowCounter(t)` guard full-history reads and count history rows returned to operator read code.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic: T1 (root) -> T2; T3 has no dependency. T1 and T2 share the `retainedRowsExceed` seam and test fixtures, so they are sequential. T3 touches only `docs/SPEC.md` and `docs/design/ui03-tasks.md` and may run concurrently with T1/T2, but one implementer on one branch is expected; if split, keep SPEC.md edits to one added sentence to limit conflict with the in-flight #827 PR (#933 also edits `docs/SPEC.md`).

Overlap: #827 (PR #933: `test/c5` harness, docs including `docs/SPEC.md`, `src/standalone/cli.ts`, `claude.ts`) shares only `docs/SPEC.md`, so rebase the T3 sentence if it merges first. #936 (queued, Claude token file reference) edits the Claude-token exclusion at the top of `exclusions()` in `operator-api.ts`, adjacent to but outside the `if (taskId)` block T2 edits: textual conflict possible, no semantic dependency; whichever merges second rebases. #877 (exclusions computed once per request, open and ready) rewrites the same function and should not run concurrently with T2; sequence it after this PR (its plan must treat the per-task gate as part of the task-specific exclusions).

#### 1. Per-task capped counts

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/scheduler.ts` (new `SchedulerStore.countForTaskUpTo`); `src/standalone/state.ts` (new `ExecutionState.recoveryCountForTaskUpTo`); `src/standalone/service.ts` (new `StandaloneService.taskRetainedRowsExceed`); `test/fixtures/read-guards.ts` (`seedOrphanHistory` gains an optional fourth argument `owner: { taskId, projectId, assignmentId }`: when given, seeded turn requests and recovery bindings use the owner's identifiers with `assignmentVersion` 1 and revisions 1/1, so they pass the unknown-assignment and revision-coverage checks and only the count bound can reject them); `test/targeted-read-stores.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/targeted-read-stores.test.ts`: (1) extend the store parity test next to the existing `recoveryCountUpTo`/`countUpTo` assertions (about line 179): for every task in `tasks` and `n` in `[1, 5, ownCount, ownCount + 1]`, assert `scheduler.countForTaskUpTo(taskId, n) === Math.min(n, requests.filter(r => r.taskId === taskId).length)` and `state.recoveryCountForTaskUpTo(taskId, n) === Math.min(n, view.filter(r => r.binding?.taskId === taskId).length)`; an unknown task id gives 0. (2) Add a service test: with an owner task from the operator fixture, seed `128 - ownCount` owned rows per kind (requests-only, then recovery-only) and assert `taskRetainedRowsExceed(taskId, 128)` is `false`; seed one more and assert `true`; seed 129 unowned orphan rows on a fresh fixture and assert `false`. content.title: Retained recovery page can hide an assignment's held generation behind newer sibling generations

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Keep assignment recovery evidence visible when sibling assignments have newer generations.

**Approved behavior:** Make recovery records assignment-specific before applying the existing display cap, while preserving task-wide hold visibility. The operator's selected assignment determines the record list; sibling generations must not consume its limit or inflate its omitted count.

**Current behavior and evidence:** At e6bf9d21, readAssignmentRecoveryOnce defaults to task-wide records and slices the last 20. The React assignment recovery endpoint uses that default; recovery-options filters to the selected assignment first. Redundancy checks covered both API paths, React recovery rendering and existing sibling-generation fixtures. The CLI fix exists, but the retained page fix does not.

**Key interfaces:** Assignment recovery read/projection, recovery-options, assignment/task bindings, recovery record limits and hold aggregation, and React recovery/advanced recovery navigation.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] With an older held generation on A and 21 newer generations on sibling B, A's recovery read and page expose A's record; B's records do not consume A's cap.
- [ ] Omitted-count and evidence-availability descriptions match the assignment-specific list.
- [ ] Task-wide holds remain visible even when caused only by sibling or omitted records; the UI clearly distinguishes that aggregate from the selected assignment's records.
- [ ] Recovery/advanced-recovery links and controls retain correct assignment/work identity; cross-assignment actions remain refused.
- [ ] Existing authorization, exact-evidence checks, bounded reads and recovery ownership rules remain intact.
- [ ] API regression fixtures and relevant browser tests cover assignment selection, sibling holds and navigation from task and assignment recovery entry points.

**Validation:** A bounded fake-runtime/real-SQLite probe on Node 24.21.0 reproduced the defect: the retained endpoint returned 20 sibling records, omitted 2 records including A's held generation, and kept held=true. recovery-options returned A's single record with omittedCount=0. This is API evidence, not browser validation. Implementation runs pinned npm ci and npm run check plus the regression/browser coverage above.

**Out of scope:** Automatically releasing holds, changing recovery eligibility, unbounded history, changing the 20-record cap, or adding new recovery actions.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/932
**Planned against:** `main` at `e21abd499cf95f4c35a89942fc577eec19ac2786`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Make the retained React recovery read project recovery records for the selected assignment before applying the existing 20-record cap. Compute task-associated holds from the complete verified task record set before that projection, then make the React page identify those holds as task-wide and its evidence list and omission count as assignment-specific. Preserve the existing recovery-options projection and all current recovery action routes.

### Guardrails

- Preserve the 20-record cap, bounded task-scoped recovery read, verified task/assignment binding checks, exact selected-request handling for unbound rows, workspace/instruction fences, and existing redaction and runtime schemas.
- Task Stop and task holds, plus writer, capacity and uncertainty holds found on any verified task recovery record, remain visible on every assignment recovery page. Only the selected assignment's records determine `records`, `evidenceAvailable`, and `omittedCount`.
- Preserve assignment/work identity in task-detail and advanced-recovery destinations; do not add recovery actions or change the existing cross-assignment refusal.
- Do not add automatic hold release, alter recovery eligibility, raise the history limit, or introduce an unbounded history read.
- Before T1 admission, the controller must screen the current candidate against the overlapping #873 and #881 edits: start from the controller-provided clean implementation worktree after those changes are integrated or released, inspect the committed delta in `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`, `src/standalone/service.ts` and their tests for compatible ownership, and renew the focused baseline checks if the planned base moved. Unknown overlap blocks admission pending investigation.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- Use the assignment-specific filter already established by `readRecoveryOptions` (`own = true`) as the read-model precedent. The React assignment endpoint currently takes the default task-wide list and slices it, while `recovery-options` selects one assignment before the same cap; the current main baseline contains the CLI sibling-generation regression in `test/operator-recovery-options.test.ts`.
- Keep two views over one already-loaded, verified task-scoped record set: aggregate task-associated holds from that full set, then derive the selected assignment's visible records and omitted count. This retains sibling/omitted hold visibility without including sibling records or counts in the selected list.
- The triage comment at issue comment 6130130824 resolves the body's earlier choice. The accepted result is assignment-specific records plus task-wide hold visibility; no further product decision is needed.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `OperatorApi.readAssignmentRecovery` calls `readAssignmentRecoveryOnce`; that method loads `service.recoveryForTask`, validates bound records against the task's known assignments and exact selected identity for unbound rows, aggregates holds, and currently applies `slice(-20)` to the task-wide list. `readRecoveryOptions` calls the same method with `own = true`.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-recovery.ts` — `recoveryOptions` enriches the already-selected bounded assignment list with exact evidence and action eligibility; retain its current contract.
- **Existing:** `web/src/recovery.tsx` — `AssignmentRecovery` reads `/api/operator/assignments/:id/recovery`, renders `data.holds` in the task-associated hold panel and `data.records`/`omittedCount` in Recorded evidence, and builds task and advanced destinations from the selected assignment and task IDs.
- **Follow:** `test/operator-recovery-options.test.ts` — its sibling-generation test creates a held generation for A followed by 21 verified sibling B generations and proves selected records, zero A omissions, and cross-assignment command refusal. Extend this fixture to exercise `/recovery` and the B read as well.
- **Follow:** `test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.ts` — existing desktop and phone coverage checks the React recovery route, task-wide hold panel, omitted-record explanation, read-only page and exact task/assignment destinations.
- **Follow:** `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` — revise its current React recovery behavior in place to state that the visible records and omission count are selected-assignment scoped while holds aggregate across verified task records.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 → T2. T1 and T2 are sequential because the page contract depends on the API's distinct assignment-record and task-hold projections. There are no safe parallel tasks within this issue. The controller's compatible-base admission gate in Guardrails applies before T1.

#### 1. Scope the recovery API records to the selected assignment

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** The compatible-base admission screen in Guardrails passes. After any base movement, confirm the relevant API files and rerun this slice's focused checks against that clean candidate.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `readAssignmentRecoveryOnce`, `readAssignmentRecovery`, `readRecoveryOptions`; `test/operator-recovery-options.test.ts` — the existing sibling-generation fixture and both recovery reads.
**Test:** Extend the sibling fixture with one older held A generation, then seed 21 later verified B generations bound to the same task, with no holds of their own. Read `/api/operator/assignments/A/recovery`: assert its records contain only A's held work, `evidenceAvailable === true`, and `omittedCount === 0`. Read B: assert at most 20 B records, `omittedCount === 1` for B's own history, no A work in its list, and task-wide writer/capacity/held flags remain true because A's held generation is omitted from B's list. Keep the existing assertion that an action naming B work under A is refused.
**Implementation:** Derive a verified task-wide record set using the existing binding, known-assignment, UUID, and exact unbound-selected-request predicates. Aggregate task-wide Stop/task/writer/capacity/uncertainty holds from that set and current task state. Before `slice(-20)`, select only records bound to the requested assignment (or the exact selected unbound request). Derive `evidenceAvailable` and `omittedCount` from that assignment list. Keep `readRecoveryOptions` on the same assignment-scoped projection and preserve its exact-evidence enrichment and action guards.
**Validate:** From the controller-provided implementation worktree root, after the shared pinned install, run `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run build && PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH node --test dist/test/operator-recovery-options.test.js dist/test/operator-configuration.test.js dist/test/operator-recovery-commands.test.js`; expect the service and web builds to pass and all three suites to pass, including assignment selection, the 20-row bound and cross-assignment recovery refusal.
**Complete when:** Both assignment reads return their own bounded record lists and accurate omission/evidence fields, while every read retains the task-wide hold aggregate; existing recovery options, ownership checks and action refusal remain green.

#### 2. Distinguish task-wide holds from selected-assignment evidence in the React page

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's API regression and focused checks pass.
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/recovery.tsx` — `AssignmentRecovery` hold and evidence panels; `test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.ts` — Runtime Settings and assignment recovery journeys; `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` — Source observations and execution recovery contract.
**Test:** Exercise the real browser fixture with A's older held record and 21 later B records. Open each assignment from the task's recovery destinations in Runtime Settings and open A again from its Task detail `ExecutionNotices` recovery link. Assert A's page shows its held record and no B records; B's page shows only B records with its own omission count while still showing the task-wide hold caused by omitted A. Assert the task-wide label/description and selected-assignment evidence label are distinct, and inspect/advanced recovery links preserve the expected task and assignment IDs. Keep the page read-only and verify no recovery/release controls appear.
**Implementation:** Label the hold panel as task-wide and the records panel as belonging to the selected assignment; clarify that omissions count only this assignment's records while the aggregate holds above include verified sibling and omitted generations. Keep existing task detail and advanced links keyed to `data.taskId` and `p.assignmentId`. Update the UI06 contract in place to describe the implemented filter-before-cap behavior and task-wide hold aggregate.
**Validate:** From the controller-provided implementation worktree root, after T1 and the shared pinned install, run `PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH npm run build && PATH=/private/tmp/ensemble-drain-20261012/toolchain/bin:$PATH node --test dist/test/operator-runtime-recovery-browser.test.js`; expect desktop and phone browser journeys to pass with the assignment-specific records, cross-assignment navigation and task-wide holds visible. The browser fixture needs localhost access; if the sandbox returns `listen EPERM` or a process-access denial, rerun this exact command using the controller's authorized escalation path rather than treating it as a pass or omitting it.
**Complete when:** The page identifies its selected-assignment evidence and task-wide holds, both task and assignment entry routes retain exact IDs, the UI06 contract matches, and the focused browser journey passes.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
