content.title: Resolve the Claude subscription token from an owner-only file reference

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/936
**Planned against:** `main` at `e0979727bf15d8d167e06bb7e345496b23cd7a19`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Add `file:/absolute/path` as a second accepted form of the Claude token reference, **alongside** `env:NAME`. One new resolver module turns either form into the token value or a fixed, value-free problem string. Every place that currently does `claudeTokenReference()?.slice(4)` / `process.env[...]` goes through it: turn environment, Codex spawn snapshot, helper-child exclusions, history redaction, operator-read exclusions and the reference fence. The token stays stored only as a reference in `claude_runtime_credentials`, so the LaunchAgent renderer and plist stay unchanged and carry no secret. Settings copy and docs describe both forms. Planned branch: `cb/936-claude-token-file`.

### Guardrails

- Keep every existing ADR-1008 guarantee unchanged for both forms. The token is set only as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the Claude subprocess environment (`claudeTurnEnvironment` in `src/standalone/claude.ts`, unchanged). It is never in the Codex, delivery or helper spawn environments, together with any env variable holding the same nonempty value (exact-value alias). It never appears in operator reads, history, logs, wait reasons or receipts. `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1` is unchanged. A value already inherited by the running runtimes holds as `restart-required`.
- `env:NAME` keeps its exact current behaviour, including restart-hold. Other credential references (discovery, routing, GitHub source, delivery) stay `env:NAME`-only. Out of scope: the LaunchAgent renderer (`src/standalone/launchd.ts`), #919 diagnostics env, a CLI for `claude-token.configure` (React-only per `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md`), new status states or UI layout, token expiry, live/real-token runs, and reading `~/.env`.
- Tests use temp files, synthetic canary values and the fake SDK only. Use no real token and no live turns. Never print a token value in test output or evidence.
- Repair classes:
  - (a) A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption: a named file, symbol, seam or behaviour that does not exist or behaves materially differently from **Implementation context**. This gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; then stop and report for replan.
  - (b) Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, formatting and CI repairs, including rebase conflicts with #917/#933 and Node 26 timing flakes (#921). These stay with the owner, consume no allowance and are recorded briefly in the delivery record.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record each correction and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **`file:` is added alongside `env:`, not instead of it.** The issue delegates this choice ("alongside or instead of `env:NAME` (decide during planning; record the choice)"). Evidence:
  - The installed-service problem (#931) is solved by `file:` alone. Removing `env:` gains no guarantee, because the env path's exclusion and restart-hold rules stay correct.
  - Removing it would regress current users and evidence paths: `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts`, `test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.ts`, the #827 journey driver in PR #933 (configures an `env:` reference), and foreground/dev runs from a shell.
  - It keeps the one-column `claude_runtime_credentials.credentialRef` storage (no migration) and the existing reference-row UI.
  - Recorded in ADR-1008 by T4.
- **Reference grammar** (identical in `src/operator/contracts.ts` and `src/core/domain.ts`): `^(?:env:[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*|file:(?:\/(?!\.{1,2}(?:\/|$))[^/\0\r\n]+)+)$`, max length 1024. This means an absolute path with no empty, `.` or `..` segments and no trailing slash. Configure only checks syntax; the file need not exist yet, so the operator can configure it first and create the file later.
- **File validation at read time** (`readClaudeToken`, fails closed, never throws):
  1. `openSync(path, O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK)`. `ENOENT` gives "missing", `ELOOP` gives "a symbolic link", any other error gives "unreadable".
  2. Run `fstatSync(fd)` checks in this order, before any read: `!isFile()` gives "not a regular file"; `uid !== process.getuid()` gives "not owned by the service user"; `(mode & 0o077) !== 0` gives "permits group or other access"; `size > 4096` gives "larger than 4096 bytes".
  3. Read at most 4097 bytes; more than 4096 is the same size problem. Close the fd in `finally`.
  4. Strip trailing whitespace/newlines and decode as UTF-8. Empty gives "empty". Any character outside `\x21-\x7e` gives "does not hold a single token".

  The checks run on the opened descriptor (no lstat-then-open race). `O_NOFOLLOW` covers only the final component: intermediate symlinks such as macOS `/var` → `/private/var` are allowed, and parent-directory ownership is not checked. That is a disclosed limit; the ops doc recommends a private real directory. Each problem becomes the wait reason `Claude runtime unavailable: subscription token file is <problem>` with `code: "empty"`, so the status read maps it to `missing-value`. Reasons never contain the path or contents. A sync read of at most 4 KiB is accepted, like the existing sync `lstatSync`/`existsSync` use in `service.ts`.
- **Read timing, rotation and restart.**
  - `env:` is unchanged.
  - `file:` is read on every `turnEnvironment()` call: Claude preflight, turn start and the status read. It is also read when the Codex spawn snapshot is taken at runtime start, and on helper-child spawns, operator-read exclusions and history redaction. Never cache it.
  - Rotation: atomically replace the file (write a new 0600 file in the same directory, then `mv`). The new value applies from the next turn without a restart. A running turn keeps its spawned value.
  - Changing or clearing the reference applies at the next turn.
  - `restart-required` applies to a file value only when it equals a value in the running runtimes' spawn snapshot, meaning the same token is also in the service environment and Codex inherited it. This is the existing alias rule.
  - An unsafe or missing file is never read, so its contents are not excluded. Nothing can leak them, because Ensemble never obtains them.
- **Exclusion and redaction values per form.**
  - `env:NAME` keeps the current values: ref, `NAME`, and the value of `process.env[NAME]`.
  - `file:PATH` adds the ref, `PATH` and the resolved value when valid.
  - Env-variable aliases holding the file value are removed from the Codex snapshot and helper-child environments by value.
  - The fence digest covers the resolved value, or the problem text when there is no value, so a read fences when the file content changes.
- **Settings UI** changes copy only, inside the existing `ReferenceRow` (no new layout, no `design/design.pen` change). The note becomes "Use file:/absolute/path to an owner-only (chmod 600) file, or env:NAME. The value is passed only to the Claude process and is never shown. Create it with claude setup-token. Validity is checked when a Claude turn starts." The `missing-value` line becomes "reference configured · token unavailable". The specific cause is the work's visible wait reason.
- **Acceptance 1 verification.**
  - The plist side is already pinned. `test/launchd.test.ts` asserts that the rendered `EnvironmentVariables` are exactly `PATH`, `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_AUTH_FILE` and `ENSEMBLE_OPERATOR_ORIGIN`, and `test/termination.test.ts` asserts the exact keys. The renderer is unchanged.
  - The turn side is a fake-SDK Claude assignment turn (T1) whose `process.env` holds no variable with the token value.
  - A live launchd-installed Claude turn with a real token is excluded by the run constraints. It stays the untested surface already recorded by #827, and T4 keeps it disclosed.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:**
  - `src/core/domain.ts` — the `claude-token.configure` command schema (~L291–300, `env:`-only regex), `claudeTokenReference()` (L749) and the executor (L2239). Storage is `claude_runtime_credentials.credentialRef TEXT`, with no constraint.
  - `src/operator/contracts.ts` — the operator command schema (~L1996–2002, `env:`-only regex, also used by web client validation) and `claudeTokenStatusSchema` (L2838, unchanged).
  - `src/standalone/service.ts` — inside runtime start (~L760–825): `claudeTokenName()`, `setChildCredentialExclusions` (names only), `spawnEnvironment` (Codex snapshot via `credentialFreeEnvironment`), and `claude.turnEnvironment()` (restart-hold, `not-configured`/`empty`/`restart-required`). Also `claudeTokenStatus()` (L1647) and the history redaction value list (~L5234, `ref.slice(4)`). `ClaudeTurnEnvironment` is at L201.
  - `src/core/child-environment.ts` — `credentialFreeEnvironment(env, keys, current)` removes names and alias values of those names. `setChildCredentialExclusions(() => names)` and `childProcessEnvironment()` (used by `gitEnvironment()` and helpers) cache the last exclusions.
  - `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `referenceFence()` (~L417, `ref.slice(4)`) and `exclusions()` (~L485–505, a discovery+claude loop with `slice(4)`).
  - `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx` — `ClaudeTokenRow` (L171), with note and `configuredLine` copy.
  - `src/standalone/claude.ts` — `claudeTurnEnvironment` and `preflightTurn`/`startTurn` call `turnEnvironment()`. No change is needed.
- **New:** `src/standalone/claude-token.ts`:
  - `claudeTokenSource(ref)` returns `{kind:"env",name} | {kind:"file",path}`.
  - `readClaudeToken(source, env = process.env, uid = process.getuid())` returns `{value} | {problem}` (validation above). The `uid` parameter is the test seam for wrong-owner checks.
  - `claudeTokenExclusions(ref, env)` returns `{ names: string[]; values: string[] }`. `names` is the env name or empty; `values` is ref, name/path and the resolved value if any.
- **Follow:** `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` `harnessFixture`/`withEnvironment`/`claudeServiceRun` for service-level tests; `test/operator-api.test.ts` "task reads redact the Claude token reference and its value"; `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts` "the Claude token reference and value are redacted when history is captured"; `test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.ts` for the Settings journey.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 → {T2, T3} → T4. T2 and T3 may run concurrently after T1: T2 owns `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`, the history-redaction hunk of `service.ts` and tests; T3 owns `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx` and the browser test. They share no files. T4 also has an external prerequisite: PR #933 (#827) must be merged and the branch rebased, because #933 rewrites the same ADR-1008, `docs/SPEC.md` (~L550), `docs/development.md`, `README.md`, `docs/design/standalone.md` and `docs/acceptance.md` paragraphs. T1–T3 do not touch #933's code files (`src/standalone/cli.ts`, `src/standalone/claude.ts`). #917 edits the `if (taskId)` block of `exclusions()` and scheduler/state per-task counts. T2 edits only the credential loop at the top of `exclusions()` and `referenceFence()`, separate hunks; whichever merges second rebases and reruns the T2 validation (class (b) repair).

#### 1. Resolve a `file:` token into the Claude turn only

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/operator/contracts.ts` and `src/core/domain.ts`: the shared grammar for `claude-token.configure`, and the doc comment on `claudeTokenReference()`.
- New `src/standalone/claude-token.ts`.
- `src/core/child-environment.ts`:
  - `credentialFreeEnvironment(environment, keys, current = environment, values: readonly string[] = [])` also removes any variable whose value is in `values`.
  - `setChildCredentialExclusions` takes `() => { names; values }`, and `childProcessEnvironment` passes both.
- `src/standalone/service.ts`:
  - Replace `claudeTokenName()` with the resolver.
  - The Codex `spawnEnvironment` excludes the env name or file value.
  - `turnEnvironment()`:
    - **not configured:** unchanged.
    - **env:** the current logic.
    - **file:** a problem gives unavailable with the file reason and `code: "empty"`; a value in the snapshot gives `restart-required`; otherwise `{ env: credentialFreeEnvironment(snapshot, deliveryNames, process.env, [value]), token: value }`.
**Test:**
- New `test/claude-token-file.test.ts` covers the resolver, using a `realpathSync(mkdtempSync(...))` root with mode 0700:
  - A 0600 file `"canary-file-token-3381\n"` resolves to `canary-file-token-3381`.
  - A symlink to that valid file gives "symbolic link".
  - Mode 0640 and mode 0604 each give "group or other access".
  - 4097 bytes gives "larger than 4096 bytes".
  - A missing file gives "missing".
  - A directory gives "not a regular file".
  - An empty file or only `"\n"` gives "empty".
  - `"a b"` gives "does not hold a single token".
  - The valid file with `uid = process.getuid()! + 1` gives "not owned by the service user".
  - Every problem string excludes the path and the canary.
- `claudeTokenSource` parses both forms. `claudeTokenExclusions` returns `{names:[NAME], values:[ref, NAME, value]}` for env and `{names:[], values:[ref, path, value]}` for a valid file. For an unsafe file it returns values without the contents.
- `test/domain.test.ts` "Claude token reference configures…":
  - Accepts and persists `file:/private/claude/token`.
  - The invalid list drops `file:/x`. It adds `file:relative`, `file:/a/../b`, `file:/a/./b`, `file:/a/`, `file:/a//b`, `file:` and `file:/a\nb`, plus a 1025-character ref.
- `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` adds:
  - **Isolation:** with `file:` ref, `ALIAS` env = file value and `NAME` unset, then restart. Codex `spawnEnvironment()` and `gitEnvironment()` contain neither the value nor `ALIAS`. `turnEnvironment()` token = file value, and its `env` lacks the value.
  - **Restart hold:** with `ALIAS` = value already in the running snapshot, configuring `file:` gives `restart-required`, and it is available after restart.
  - **Fail closed:** chmod 0644 gives unavailable `code:"empty"`. The reason matches "permits group or other access", contains neither path nor value, and `claudeTokenStatus().state === "missing-value"`.
  - **Rotation:** an atomic rename of a new 0600 file with a different value; the next `turnEnvironment()` returns the new value with no restart.
  - **Full turn:** a `claudeServiceRun` variant with `file:` ref and no env variable holding the token. The turn completes, `sessions[0].options.env.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` = file value, and no `process.env` value equals it.
- All existing env tests stay green.
**Implementation:** As above. Leave `claudeTurnEnvironment` unchanged.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci` and Node 24.21.0 first on `PATH`, run `npm run -s build:service && node --test dist/test/claude-token-file.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime-service.test.js dist/test/domain.test.js`; expect 0 failures.
**Complete when:** Both forms are accepted, unsafe files fail closed with value-free reasons, and the token reaches only the Claude turn. The T1 boundary tests pass. T2/T3 must not start until they do.

#### 2. Redact and fence the file-sourced value in operator reads and history

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 tests green.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`:
  - `exclusions()`: discovery stays on `slice(4)`; Claude uses `claudeTokenExclusions(ref).values`.
  - `referenceFence()`: for the Claude ref, hash the resolved value or the problem text.
- `src/standalone/service.ts` history-redaction value list (~L5234): the Claude ref uses `claudeTokenExclusions(ref).values`; discovery is unchanged.
**Test:**
- `test/operator-api.test.ts`: a new test, "task reads redact a file-sourced Claude token value and path". Configure `file:<tmp>/token` (0600, canary `claude-file-redaction-canary-6610`, no env variable). Put the canary and the path in the task outcome. `readTask` JSON contains neither.
- `test/s05-conversation-history.test.ts`: a file-form twin of the existing history-redaction test. The emitted text includes the file value and path, and the stored `conversation_history_items` contain neither.
- `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` "operator token status…": add a `file:` case. Status is `available` for a valid file and `missing-value` for an unsafe one, and the JSON contains neither the path nor the value.
**Implementation:** As above.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run -s build:service && node --test --test-name-pattern="Claude" dist/test/operator-api.test.js dist/test/s05-conversation-history.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime-service.test.js`; expect 0 failures, including the new tests.
**Complete when:** The file-sourced value and path are redacted from operator reads and history, and the fence changes with file content.

#### 3. Settings token row accepts and explains `file:`

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 tests green.
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx` `ClaudeTokenRow`: the note and the `missing-value` line copy from Planning decisions. `test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- Update the existing assertions to the new `missing-value` line.
- Add the test "Settings sets a file: Claude token reference and shows it unavailable when unsafe":
  1. Write a 0600 temp file with a canary value.
  2. Set → `file:<path>` → Save. The request body has `credentialRef` = that ref, and the row shows "reference configured · available".
  3. chmod 0644 → Refresh. The row shows "reference configured · token unavailable".
  4. `GET /api/operator/claude-token` and the page `innerText` contain neither the path nor the canary.
  5. `file:relative` shows "Check this field." with no command sent.
- The phone-width no-overflow check is unchanged.
**Implementation:** Copy only, inside the existing row.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run -s build && node --test dist/test/operator-claude-token-browser.test.js`; expect 0 failures.
**Complete when:** The Settings row accepts `file:`, shows the available/unavailable state, and never displays the path or value.

#### 4. Update ADR-1008 and operator docs in place

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T2`, `T3`
**Prerequisites:** PR #933 merged into `main` and this branch rebased onto it (external). T2 and T3 green.
**Files and symbols:**
- `docs/adr/1008-claude-code-execution-harness.md` Authentication: both forms; the add-alongside decision; the file validation rules; read timing, rotation and restart; the intermediate-symlink and parent-directory limit; the env-alias exclusion. Note that the installed LaunchAgent uses `file:` with no secret in the plist.
- `docs/SPEC.md` (the token sentence near L550).
- `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` "Runtime and authentication": create a private real directory with mode 0700, then run `install -m 600 /dev/null <dir>/claude-token`. Paste the `claude setup-token` output into it without shell history or argv, for example `pbpaste > <dir>/claude-token`. Verify `stat -f '%Su %Lp' <dir>/claude-token` shows the service user and `600`. Configure `file:<dir>/claude-token` in Settings. Rotate by atomic replace; no restart is needed. State that the plist needs no Claude variable.
- `docs/design/ui06-configuration.md` row (L38).
- Every Claude-token `env:NAME` mention that #933 left in `README.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/design/standalone.md` and `docs/acceptance.md`.
- Revise in place, with no dated or amendment sections.
**Implementation:** Docs only. The launchd-installed live Claude turn stays a disclosed untested surface.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run -s format:check` and `rg -n "Claude.{0,80}env:NAME|env:NAME.{0,80}Claude" README.md docs --glob '!docs/evidence/**'`. Expect format to pass, and every remaining hit to also name `file:`.
**Complete when:** All four acceptance criteria have matching docs, and ADR-1008 records the decision.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| An installed (LaunchAgent) service with a `file:` reference runs a Claude turn with no token in its environment or plist | 1 (+ unchanged renderer) | T1 full fake-SDK turn with no env holding the token; existing `launchd.test.ts`/`termination.test.ts` exact plist env keys |
| Unsafe files (symlink, wrong owner, group/other readable, oversized, missing) give a visible unavailable state and never a token read | 1, 2, 3 | T1 resolver and fail-closed service tests; T2 status test; T3 browser unsafe-file journey |
| Token value never in Codex or helper spawn environments, operator reads, logs or evidence; redaction tests cover the file-sourced value | 1, 2 | T1 isolation test (Codex snapshot, `gitEnvironment`, alias); T2 operator-read and history redaction tests |
| ADR-1008 and operations docs updated in place | 4 | T4 format check and `rg` sweep |

### Final validation

- On the integrated candidate, with Node 24.21.0 (`~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin` first on `PATH`), run `npm ci && npm run check` from the repository root; expect typecheck, lint, format, build and all tests to pass. Run the full check through `npm` and not `node --test` directly: `launchd.test.ts` asserts it runs from npm, and at baseline its CLI test fails only under bare `node --test`. The local npm is 11.19.0 while `packageManager` pins 12.2.0; CI's pinned npm and Node 26 run is authoritative. A Node 26 timing flake matching #921 is a class (b) rerun, not a plan mismatch.

### Review focus

- Every remaining `slice(4)` on the Claude ref (`rg -n "claudeTokenReference\(\)" src` must show only resolver-mediated uses).

content.title: Use the GitHub CLI login as the discovery credential

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/942
**Planned against:** `main` at `e6bf9d219f2c03073807502e64e6ad3a44e327a7`
**Publication mode:** Reviewed
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Prove first that a launchd GUI-domain job can read the keychain-backed `gh` login
without prompting (T1). Then add one credential-reference parser, a bounded `gh`
resolver and the new reads and command grammar (T2). Route every exclusion and
redaction site through one discovery-exclusion helper (T3). Design frames 114 and 116
in Pen (T4), then implement the Settings row and setup alert against a fake `gh`
(T5). Revise the docs (T6) and finish with bounded live validation through a launchd
job (T7).

### Guardrails

- Delivery, routing and project-source credentials keep `env:NAME` only. Their
  schemas, parsers and `ref.slice(4)` call sites do not change, apart from where a
  shared read site also handles the discovery reference.
- `gh:github.com` is the only `gh:` form. No other host, no token caching for reads,
  no prompts and no implicit fallback: Ensemble reads with a `gh` login only when the
  operator chose it.
- The token value never appears in a response, receipt, log, error message, evidence
  or test output. `gh` stderr is never surfaced. Status reports only the state and the
  account login.
- Claude token, delivery exclusions and existing discovery reasons keep working
  unchanged. The Claude subscription row (`ClaudeTokenRow`) keeps its current UI.
- Do not install, migrate or modify the Haze prototype. Do not touch launchd's shared
  environment. Every live launchd job is disposable, uses a unique label and is
  booted out with absence verified.
- Disclosed limit: if the Codex sandbox can reach the keychain, an agent could run
  `gh` itself. Ensemble neither enforces nor claims to prevent this.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged
  requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and
  renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two
  repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown
  overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration
  amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable
  consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Feasibility proof first (T1).** The keychain assumption can only be tested in the
  target runtime. T1 gates every other slice. On failure, the issue returns for a
  scope decision before any UI work, as the issue states.
- **Live target.** No Ensemble LaunchAgent is installed on this host
  (`~/Library/LaunchAgents` has none; `launchctl list` shows none). "Installed
  LaunchAgent" is therefore satisfied by a disposable per-user LaunchAgent. T1 uses a
  minimal probe job and T7 uses the documented renderer and a disposable data
  directory, both in `gui/$(id -u)` with the renderer's fixed `PATH`
  (`src/standalone/launchd.ts` `LAUNCHD_PATH`). These are the same domain and `PATH`
  that an installed service gets.
- **Grammar.** A new `src/core/credential-reference.ts` exports the `env:NAME`
  pattern, the `gh:github.com` literal and a `discoveryCredentialReference` schema
  (their union). `commandSchema` in `src/core/domain.ts` and the operator command in
  `src/operator/contracts.ts` use that schema for `discovery.configure`. A project
  source credential can later adopt the `gh:` member without a new parser.
- **Resolution.** A new `src/standalone/gh-credential.ts` runs `gh` through async
  `execFile` with `stdin` ignored, a 10 s timeout, a 64 KiB `maxBuffer`, and
  `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` and `GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1`. The child environment drops
  the Claude and delivery credentials but keeps the discovery credential, because
  `gh` may legitimately read `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
  - `detect()` runs `gh auth status --active --hostname github.com --json hosts`
    (verified locally with gh 2.102.0: it reports `state`, `login` and `tokenSource`,
    with no token) and zod-validates the output.
  - `token()` runs `gh auth token --hostname github.com` and accepts one line
    matching `^[\x21-\x7e]{1,512}$`.
  - Mapping: spawn `ENOENT` → `not-installed`; no `github.com` account →
    `not-signed-in`; any other failure (non-success state, non-zero exit, timeout,
    invalid output) → `unreadable`.
  - The executable defaults to `gh` on the service `PATH`. A `ghExecutable` option on
    the operator API setup (beside the existing `discovery` reader injection) is the
    test seam.
- **Per-read resolution.** For `gh:`, the default reader factory in `discoveryRead`
  (`src/standalone/operator-api.ts`) awaits `token()` on every read and passes the
  value to `GitHubDiscoveryReader`. Failures map to `DiscoveryFailure` reasons
  `gh-not-installed`, `gh-not-signed-in` and `gh-unreadable`. These are added to
  `DiscoveryFailureReason` (`src/standalone/github-discovery.ts`) and
  `discoveryUnavailableReasons` (`src/operator/contracts.ts`). The discovery fence
  for `gh:` is the reference alone. A gh account switch during one read is not
  detected; that limit is accepted.
- **Status read.** `discoveryStatusSchema` becomes:

  ```
  { configured, available, source: "env" | "gh" | null,
    gh: { state: "signed-in", login } | { state: "not-installed" | "not-signed-in" | "unreadable" } }
  ```

  `login` is validated as a GitHub login. `readDiscoveryStatus` becomes async and runs
  `detect()` on every read, so the UI can offer the gh option even when unconfigured.
  For `gh:`, `available` means `signed-in`.
- **Exclusion helper.** `discoveryCredentialExclusions(ref)`, in the new standalone
  module, returns `{names, values, redactions}`, mirroring `claudeTokenExclusions`:
  - `env:NAME`: name `NAME`, value `process.env[NAME]`.
  - `gh:github.com`: names `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` (gh's own env token sources
    for github.com), plus every token value this process has resolved.
  - Resolved values live in a bounded (8) in-memory set used only for exclusion and
    redaction. They are never persisted, returned or used for reads.
  - `StandaloneService.start()` awaits one bounded `token()` before building the
    runtime spawn snapshot when the reference is `gh:`. A failure there does not block
    start.
- **Exclusion sites.** These sites use the helper instead of `discovery.slice(4)`:
  - the runtime spawn snapshot and both Claude turn environments in
    `src/standalone/service.ts` (~L776–L850);
  - helper children, via `setChildCredentialExclusions` (combined with the Claude
    exclusions);
  - `exclusions()` and the fence JSON in `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (~L425–L510);
  - the conversation-history redactions in `src/standalone/service.ts` (~L5236).

  A long-lived Codex runtime keeps the environment it inherited at spawn. A discovery
  reference set later applies to Claude turns and helpers immediately and to Codex
  after a restart. The docs disclose this, as they already do for Claude `env:`
  references.
- **UI.** A dedicated `DiscoveryCredentialRow` replaces the generic `ReferenceRow` use
  for discovery. It offers a radio choice: GitHub CLI (recommended) or Environment
  variable (advanced, name only, `env:` implied, validated with the same pattern).
  - Commands: `gh:github.com` or `env:NAME`. Clear sends `null` (the reverse path).
  - Configured line: `GitHub CLI · @login · read-only use`, or the existing env lines.
  - The setup alert in `web/src/project-setup.tsx` offers **Use GitHub CLI login
    (@login)** only when the discovery reason is `unconfigured` and status reports
    `signed-in`. That one `discovery.configure` command is followed by the existing
    retry path. The other cases keep **Set discovery credential**, with gh-specific
    copy in `discoveryReasonCopy`.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:**
  - `src/core/domain.ts` — `discovery.configure` (L284 schema, L2233 execution, L745
    `discoveryCredentialReference()`).
  - `src/operator/contracts.ts` — L1987 command, L2857 `discoveryStatusSchema`, L2860
    reasons.
  - `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `readDiscoveryStatus`, `discoveryFence` and
    `discoveryRead` (~L4710–L4770), `exclusions()` (~L499), task-read fence (~L442).
  - `src/standalone/service.ts` — spawn snapshot and Claude `turnEnvironment`
    (L766–L857), history redactions (L5236).
  - `src/core/child-environment.ts` — `credentialFreeEnvironment`,
    `setChildCredentialExclusions`, `childProcessEnvironment`.
  - `src/standalone/github-discovery.ts` — `GitHubDiscoveryReader(token)`,
    `DiscoveryFailure`.
  - `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx` — `ReferenceRow` and `DiscoveryCredentialRow`
    (frame 114).
  - `web/src/project-setup.tsx` — L436 alert (frame 116).
  - `design/DESIGN.md` — L397/L398 frame references: 114 `vEr15`, 116 `q6ZqlW`.
- **New:**
  - `src/core/credential-reference.ts` — reference grammar (see Planning decisions).
  - `src/standalone/gh-credential.ts` — `detect`, `token`,
    `discoveryCredentialExclusions` and the resolved-value set.
  - `test/gh-credential.test.ts`.
  - `test/fixtures/fake-gh.ts` — writes an executable fake `gh` into a temporary
    directory, with its state driven by a sibling file.
- **Follow:**
  - `src/standalone/claude-token.ts:claudeTokenExclusions` for the
    names/values/redactions shape.
  - `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts:112` for spawn, turn and helper exclusion
    assertions.
  - `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts:89` for command-boundary rejection.
  - `test/fixtures/setup-browser.ts` `setupJourney` for browser journeys.
  - `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` § "Generate and review a per-user
    LaunchAgent" for launchd steps.
  - `docs/evidence/s08a-operations-2026-09-30.md` for the launchd evidence form.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic:

```
T1 → {T2, T4}
T2 → T3
{T2, T4} → T5
{T3, T5} → T6
T6 → T7
```

T2 and T3 share `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` and `src/standalone/service.ts`, so
they are sequential. T4 (Pen and `design/DESIGN.md` only) may run concurrently with
T2 and T3. T5 needs T2's status schema and T4's frames. Pen edits go through the Pen
MCP only. Pen MCP cannot save, so open `design/design.pen` in Pen and save it there,
then refresh `DESIGN.md` through MCP.

#### 1. Feasibility: gh login readable from a launchd job

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** New `docs/evidence/942-gh-discovery-credential-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`.
The probe script and plist live in a private scratch directory and are not committed.
**Implementation:**
- Write a probe script and a plist for a unique label `dev.ensemble.probe942.<rand>`.
  The plist sets `RunAtLoad=true` and `PATH` equal to `LAUNCHD_PATH`, and has no other
  environment variables.
- The script runs, with stdin from `/dev/null` and a 10 s timeout:
  - `gh auth status --active --hostname github.com --json hosts`;
  - `gh auth token --hostname github.com`.
- It records each exit code, the `state`, `login` and `tokenSource` fields, and
  whether the token is non-empty and matches the token pattern. It records the
  token's length only, never its value, and writes the result to an owner-only
  output file.
- `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u)`, wait for exit, read the result, then
  `launchctl bootout` and confirm `launchctl print` fails.
- Record the host, gh version, commands, results and cleanup readback, with no token.
**Validate:** From the worktree, after the job exits, the output file shows status
exit 0 with `state: success` for `github.com`, and token exit 0 with a non-empty
valid token. No keychain prompt appears during the run. `launchctl print
gui/$(id -u)/<label>` exits non-zero after bootout.
**Complete when:** The evidence file records pass, or a failure. On failure, stop
and post the scope-decision question to #942 with the evidence; do not start T4 or T5.

#### 2. `gh:github.com` reference, per-read resolution and status

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 passed.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/core/credential-reference.ts` (new);
- `src/core/domain.ts` (`discovery.configure` schema);
- `src/operator/contracts.ts` (command, `discoveryStatusSchema`,
  `discoveryUnavailableReasons`);

- `src/standalone/github-discovery.ts` (`DiscoveryFailureReason`);
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`: `readDiscoveryStatus` (now async, plus its route

- `test/fixtures/fake-gh.ts` (new);
- `test/gh-credential.test.ts` (new);
- `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts`.

**Test:**
- `test/gh-credential.test.ts`, using a fake `gh` whose state file selects one of:
  - signed-in (status JSON with `login: "octo"`, token `gho_fake-canary-942`);
  - not signed in (`{"hosts":{}}`, token exit 1);
  - unreadable (status `state: "error"`);
  - hang (sleeps beyond a test timeout override);
  - invalid token output;
  - plus a missing executable path.

- `test/operator-setup-api.test.ts`:
  - `discovery.configure` accepts `gh:github.com` and rejects `gh:`,

    alongside the existing env cases.

    `{configured: true, available: true, source: "gh", gh: {state: "signed-in",
    login: "octo"}}`, and the body lacks the canary.
  - The repositories read reaches the injected reader with the canary token. Use a
    reader factory that records the token it received; the test checks this, not the
    response.
  - Each gh failure state yields the matching `gh-*` unavailable reason.
  - Unconfigured status still reports the detected gh state.
  - A routing, delivery or GitHub source configure command with `gh:github.com` is
    still rejected.

**Implementation:** As settled in Planning decisions (Grammar, Resolution,
Per-read resolution, Status read).
**Validate:** From the worktree, run `npm run build && node --test
dist/test/gh-credential.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-api.test.js`. Expect
0 failures and the new cases listed as passing. Also run `npm run typecheck`; expect
exit 0.
**Complete when:** The command boundary, reads and status behave as tested, and no
token appears in outputs.

#### 3. Exclude the discovery credential from children and redactions

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 integrated.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/standalone/gh-credential.ts` (`discoveryCredentialExclusions` and the
  resolved-value set);
- `src/standalone/service.ts`: `start()` resolves once for `gh:`; spawn snapshot,

- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`: `exclusions()` and the task-read fence;
- new `test/discovery-credential-exclusion.test.ts`, following
  `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts`.

**Test:** For each of `env:FIXTURE_DISCOVERY` and `gh:github.com`:
- The service environment holds the credential value under the configured name, or
  under `GH_TOKEN`, plus an alias variable carrying the same value.
- After service start, assert that none of the following has the name or the value:
  the runtime spawn snapshot, the Claude turn `env`, and
  `childProcessEnvironment()`.
- Assert that task-text redaction covers the reference, the name and the value
  (follow the existing "task text holding the discovery credential is never captured"

- Sensitivity check: with the helper bypassed, at least one assertion fails. Report
  the order it was observed in.
- Also assert that the `gh` resolver child still receives `GH_TOKEN`, so gh can use

**Implementation:** As settled in Planning decisions (Exclusion helper, Exclusion
sites).
**Validate:** From the worktree, run `npm run build && node --test
dist/test/discovery-credential-exclusion.test.js
dist/test/claude-runtime-service.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-api.test.js
dist/test/delivery-service.test.js`. Expect 0 failures.

child and redaction site, and the existing Claude and delivery exclusion tests pass.

#### 4. Design frames 114 and 116

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 passed.
**Files and symbols:** `design/design.pen` frames 114 `vEr15` and 116 `q6ZqlW`
(edited only through the Pen MCP), and `design/DESIGN.md`.
**Implementation:**
- Frame 114, discovery row: the source choice, with GitHub CLI marked recommended

- Detection states:
  - `Signed in to github.com as @account` with **Use this login**;
  - `gh not installed`;
  - `gh not signed in · run gh auth login`;
  - `gh login unreadable from the service`.
- The environment-variable name field, with `env:` implied.
- Configured state: `GitHub CLI · @account · read-only use` with Change and Clear,
  plus Cancel in the open form.
- Frame 116, discovery-unavailable alert: **Use GitHub CLI login (@account)**

- Save in Pen, then refresh the `DESIGN.md` snapshot sections that reference

**Validate:** Re-read both frames through the Pen MCP and confirm the strings above
are present. Run `git diff --stat design/` and expect changes in both `design.pen`
and `DESIGN.md`.
**Complete when:** Both frames and `DESIGN.md` show every state above.

#### 5. Settings row and setup alert

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T2`, `T4`
**Prerequisites:** T2 status schema; T4 frames.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx` (new `DiscoveryCredentialRow`; `ReferenceRow`

- `web/src/project-setup.tsx` (alert action and `discoveryReasonCopy`);

- `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`.

**Test:** Chromium journeys with the fake `gh`:
1. **Settings, signed in.** The row shows `Signed in to github.com as @octo`. Click

   row then reads `GitHub CLI · @octo · read-only use`. Clear sends `null` and the row
   returns to not configured. Cancel closes without a command.
2. **Settings detection states.** For each of the three gh failure states, the exact

3. **Environment variable.** Typing `FIXTURE_DISCOVERY` sends `env:FIXTURE_DISCOVERY`.
   An invalid name such as `lower` is blocked with a field error and sends nothing.
4. **Setup alert.** Unconfigured and signed in: **Use GitHub CLI login (@octo)** sends
   one `discovery.configure` command, then the repository list loads from the fake
   reader. Unconfigured and not signed in: only **Set discovery credential** appears.

No assertion may contain the token. Update the existing discovery-unavailable copy
assertions (L254–L340) only where the alert legitimately changes.
**Validate:** From the worktree, run `npm run build && node --test
dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js`. Expect 0 failures. Also run `npm run
typecheck && npm run lint`; expect exit 0.
**Complete when:** All states, Clear and Cancel are covered by passing browser
journeys.

#### 6. Docs

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T3`, `T5`
**Prerequisites:** Final contract from T2, T3 and T5.
**Files and symbols:**
- `docs/adr/1009-project-setup-discovery.md` (replace the "inherits … dedicated
  read-only token" guidance with the exclusion contract, the `gh:` reference and the
  disclosed keychain limit);
- `docs/SPEC.md` (project-setup discovery section ~L529–L536, and any credential
  inheritance statement);
- `CONTEXT.md` (add **Credential reference**);
- `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` (gh login for the LaunchAgent, and Codex
  applying a later env reference after restart).

All revisions are in place, with no dated sections.
**Validate:** From the worktree, run `rg -n "dedicated read-only token|agents may
inherit" docs CONTEXT.md web/src` and expect no matches. Run `npm run format:check`;
expect exit 0.
**Complete when:** The docs describe the implemented contract and its limits.

#### 7. Bounded live validation

**Task ID:** `T7`
**Depends on:** `T6`
**Prerequisites:** The integrated candidate builds. T1 passed.
**Files and symbols:** Append a live section to the T1 evidence file.
**Implementation:**
- Render a disposable LaunchAgent through the documented renderer, with a disposable
  private data directory, unique label and loopback port.
- Bootstrap it, sign in as operator through the CLI or API, and run
  `discovery.configure` with `gh:github.com`.
- Read `/api/operator/discovery`; expect `source: "gh"` and `state: "signed-in"`
  with the host login.
- Read `/api/operator/discovery/repositories`; expect `state: "ready"` and a
  non-empty list. Record only the count and whether one known repository
  (`chrisbanes/ensemble`) is present.
- Bootout, verify the label is absent and remove only the disposable data directory.
- No Codex or Claude turns are run.

**Validate:** The evidence records the commands, the HTTP status and state fields,
the repository count and the cleanup readback, and contains no token. Run
`rg -n "gh[opsu]_" docs/evidence/942-*` and expect no matches.
**Complete when:** Live discovery lists repositories via the gh login under launchd,
and cleanup is verified.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `discovery.configure` accepts `gh:github.com`; invalid references rejected at the command boundary | 2 | `operator-setup-api.test.ts` boundary cases |
| Per-read gh resolution; failures map to reasons without naming the token | 2 | `gh-credential.test.ts` and `operator-setup-api.test.ts` status and read cases |
| Runtime and helper child environments exclude the credential by name and value (env and gh) | 3 | `discovery-credential-exclusion.test.ts` |
| Settings row and setup alert states, Clear and Cancel, browser-tested against a fake gh | 5 | `operator-setup-browser.test.ts` journeys 1–4 |
| Pen 114 and 116, DESIGN.md, ADR-1009, SPEC and CONTEXT updated in place | 4, 6 | MCP re-read; `rg` check for the stale guidance |
| `npm run check` passes; live launchd discovery lists repositories via gh | 7, Final | Final validation; T7 evidence |
| Feasibility recorded in `docs/evidence/` | 1 | T1 evidence file |

### Final validation

- From the worktree, using Node from `.node-version` and `npm@12.2.0`, after
  `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate. Expect exit 0
  with typecheck, lint, format and the full suite (including Chromium and WebKit
  journeys) passing.
- T7 live evidence must be bound to the same candidate head, or re-run if the T7
  head and the final head differ in `src/` or `web/`.

### Review focus

- The token must not leak through status, errors, receipts, logs, test output or
  evidence. The `gh` stderr must not be propagated.
- Every former `discovery.slice(4)` site must handle `gh:`. A missed site would read
  `process.env["ithub.com"]` and silently skip exclusion.
- The resolver child keeps `GH_TOKEN` while helper and runtime children drop it.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- T1 fails or prompts: stop and return to #942 for a scope decision.
- `gh auth status --json` output differs materially under launchd from the locally
  verified shape.

content.title: Let project GitHub sources use the GitHub CLI login

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement  
**Summary:** Let an operator explicitly choose the GitHub CLI login for a project's GitHub source, with usable credential settings, visible blocked states and credential exclusion from children.

**Current behaviour and verified evidence:**

At `8a86bd6505967829aa9d8969252207b9c0a8c6bc`, #943 supports `gh:github.com` for installation discovery only. Source configuration and CLI source edits still accept only `env:NAME`. A linked GitHub Project starts inactive; discovery authentication does not configure its source.

An isolated reproduction using Node 24.21.0, npm 12.2.0, the real service/domain/API, real SQLite and a fake provider confirmed:
- With discovery configured as `gh:github.com` and a project selection `S-1` with no source credential, refresh performs zero provider reads, imports zero tasks and records no sync row. The selection remains inactive.
- The source observation is `never`, with null attempt/success timestamps and no missing-credential explanation.
- JSON API preview fails with a 409 conflict (the implementation uses “Preview configuration conflict”); the advanced HTML preview fails with “GitHub credential reference required”.
- Source configuration rejects `gh:github.com` at schema validation. The existing test that routing, delivery and source credentials accept only env references passes (1/1).
- The reproduction starts zero runtime turns and removes its fixture data on completion.

Dependency installation and the service TypeScript build passed. This verifies the application behaviour in a controlled fixture; it does not independently verify the reported installed Haze state, browser presentation, live gh source access or a completed fix. No full check or live runtime qualification was run during triage.

**Desired behaviour:**

Project GitHub sources accept `env:NAME` and exactly `gh:github.com`. Choosing either is explicit for that project source. Detection offers an identity; it grants no source configuration, activation or repository access. Never fall back to the installation discovery credential.

All source reads resolve the selected credential per read: selection sync, preview, issue status and blockers. Reuse the existing bounded, non-interactive gh resolver and reference validation. Report `gh-not-installed`, `gh-not-signed-in` or `gh-unreadable` without exposing tokens or child stderr. Credential failure leaves source/dependency knowledge incomplete or unknown, preserving admission safety and existing configuration fences.

Source settings offer GitHub CLI with detected `@account`, or Environment variable. Configured state offers Change and Clear; editing offers Cancel. A source with selections and no usable credential shows the reason and a route to its credential setting in source settings and Sync & placement. Preview uses the same actionable explanation. Cover the JSON API, React UI, advanced HTML editor and operator CLI.

Source credentials are excluded by name and value from Codex spawn environments, both Claude turn environments and helper children, independently of whether discovery has a credential. Keep resolved token values out of public output, receipts and captured evidence. Preserve the documented runtime limits: an existing Codex spawn environment needs restart to apply changed exclusions, and Ensemble does not prevent an agent reaching the host gh keychain through its runtime permissions.

**Key interfaces:**

- Credential-reference schemas and `github.configure`: extend source references without widening delivery, routing or Claude token references.
- `GitHubReaderFactory` / `GitHubSourceReader`: per-read credential resolution for `readSelection`, `readBlockers` and `readIssueStatus`, including every preview consumer.
- Credential exclusion/redaction functions and runtime/helper environment construction: include every configured project source; do not treat a `gh:` reference as an environment-variable suffix.
- Project configuration and source-observation contracts: expose safe credential kind, usability and reason needed by settings and CLI, without revealing private reference names or values.
- CLI source edit/prepare/apply and preview commands: accept the same source references and give consistent actionable failures.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Runtime validation accepts `env:NAME`, `gh:github.com` and explicit Clear for source configuration; invalid references are rejected. Existing omitted-reference semantics remain intact. Delivery and routing remain env-only.
- [ ] Sync, both preview paths, issue status and blocker reads use per-read gh resolution without token caching for reads. Fake-gh tests prove changed tokens are used on later reads and cover all three failure reasons.
- [ ] Missing/unresolvable credentials produce visible, actionable source and sync states and consistent preview errors. Existing imported tasks and blockers fail closed rather than retaining stale admission evidence.
- [ ] Detection alone does not select a source identity. Tests cover source gh with discovery unset or configured differently, and prove there is no discovery fallback.
- [ ] Codex, Claude and helper environments exclude env-source names/values and gh token variables/resolved values, including aliases holding those values. Tests cover source-only configuration and redaction from operator output and captured evidence.
- [ ] Browser tests against fake gh cover choice, detected account, configured state, Change, Cancel, Clear and missing/unusable states. Failed or uncertain saves/Clear retain drafts and support existing keyed outcome reconciliation.
- [ ] Credential Change/Clear follows existing source-save rules: retained/new selections require preview at the new source version, provider observations become incomplete and imported blockers unknown. Clear preserves the source definition and imported task history; reconfigure and preview restore the workflow.
- [ ] CLI edit/prepare/apply/preview and advanced HTML source configuration support the same reference choices and errors as the React UI.
- [ ] Update source settings and blocked-state Pen frames through Pen MCP first, then refresh `design/DESIGN.md`; revise ADR-1009, SPEC and CONTEXT's Credential reference in place.
- [ ] With the pinned toolchain, `npm ci` and `npm run check` pass. Record bounded live validation against the installed dev service: an explicitly chosen `gh:github.com` source successfully previews/activates a GitHub Project and then imports matching `ready` issues. Record preview, activation and successful import separately, preserving the installed prototype and existing execution policy.

**Out of scope:**

- Delivery or routing credentials accepting `gh:`.
- Hosts other than github.com, implicit discovery fallback, or automatically activating sources.
- Changes to readiness, dependency, repository-access or scheduling policy.
- An independent Ensemble sandbox, universal containment of host gh/keychain access, or reopening paused native Codex/ChatGPT work.

**Context:** #942 and merged PR #943 supply the discovery implementation and accepted limits. Redundancy searches covered credential schemas/resolvers, source sync/preview/status/blockers, child environments/redaction, source settings, Sync & placement and CLI edits. Source gh support is absent. No `.out-of-scope/` knowledge base exists in this checkout; ADR-1009's discovery-only boundary and #942's explicit allowance for later source support are the relevant prior decisions.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/944
**Planned against:** `main` at `e21abd499cf95f4c35a89942fc577eec19ac2786` (clean detached planning checkout)
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Extend the existing project source contract to explicitly accept the github.com gh login. Resolve credentials at each public source read, centralize safe status/reason presentation, and apply source exclusions to runtime/helper environments independently of discovery. Keep credential edits inside the existing keyed, versioned source-save workflow. Update Pen before implementation; qualify the complete preview/activation/import path on one isolated disposable development LaunchAgent after offline boundary evidence passes.

The authoritative requirements are the issue and [accepted agent brief](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/944#issuecomment-6132148462). This is one coherent delivery candidate, not one PR per slice.

### Guardrails

- Source references accept `env:NAME` and exactly `gh:github.com`; nullable Clear and omitted-reference preservation remain distinct. Delivery/routing stay env-only; Claude references retain their existing contract. No discovery fallback or automatic source activation, repository grant, readiness change, scheduling change, provider mutation or reopened native work.
- Detection offers an account, never selects a source identity. gh stdin remains closed, prompts disabled, stderr suppressed and each subprocess bounded by the existing 10-second timeout. No token read cache; values retained solely for exclusion/redaction must never become read credentials or persisted evidence.
- Preserve current source-version/configuration fences, keyed receipt replay, unknown outcomes, drafts, task history, and independent holds. Clear leaves source definitions/history intact; Change/Clear invalidate activation and provider/dependency completeness through the existing source-save transaction. Failed reads make knowledge incomplete/unknown and cannot leave stale admission evidence trusted.
- Exclude every configured source credential by names and values, including aliases, from Codex spawn, both Claude turn branches and helper children, whether discovery is unset or different. Preserve the disclosed Codex restart requirement and the limitation that runtime permissions may still allow direct host gh/keychain access.
- All delivery commands below run from the controller-provided implementation worktree root, never this planning checkout. Root supplies an available slot, verified compatible base and shared-file/canvas grants before implementation; root owns remote writes and publication. Preserve other owners' changes.
- Live grant: one attempt, at most 300 seconds, zero model turns and zero GitHub writes. Root's durable checkpoint owns consumption; consume immediately before bootstrap, never automatically reset after failure or uncertain outcome. Production/Haze state remains untouched. Offline harness evidence is mandatory before consumption.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. A factual plan mismatch allows one diagnosis and two repair cycles; ordinary repairs do not consume that budget. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- Use a credential-resolving `GitHubSourceReader` wrapper around `GitHubHttpSourceReader`, with a service-owned factory shared by synchronizer and both preview consumers. Its `readSelection`, `readBlockers` and `readIssueStatus` each resolve the selected reference immediately before delegating. Within one blocker read, existing nested HTTP status requests use that read's token; later public reads resolve again. Keep injectable reader/fetch/gh seams for tests.
- Credential status reports configured, kind (`env`, `gh`, or null), usable, safe reason and detected gh account/state. Do not return reference names, tokens or provider/child stderr. Add explicit safe credential reason to observations, including inactive selections with no sync row, without fabricating an attempt/success timestamp. Credential usability means successful resolution, not merely signed-in detection. A separate detected account never proves the chosen env identity.
- Reuse `github.configure`, `selectionKeepSchema`, source draft `referenceMode`, and `DraftOutcome` reconciliation. Source credential controls set/clear the reference in the full source change document; Cancel abandons only credential editing and keeps unrelated source draft edits. There is no new credential mutation route or alternate activation path.
- Existing `ghEnvironment(domain)` is discovery-centric. Generalize its explicit purpose/reference input so an explicitly chosen source gh resolver does not accidentally lose gh token variables because discovery uses env, and unrelated env-source, delivery and Claude credentials/aliases are removed. Do not derive its source choice from discovery. Generalize exclusion naming while keeping discovery callers compatible.
- Successfully resolved gh values must remain excluded/redacted for process lifetime, including after source Clear or token rotation. The existing eight-value eviction can otherwise expose an old resolved alias. The retained set is exclusion-only memory, never a credential read cache or durable secret store. Each token remains bounded to 512 bytes by the resolver, but retained memory grows with distinct successfully resolved rotations until service restart; disclose that operational tradeoff. Lead accepted this central privacy correction, including the >8 rotations regression.
- Existing `github.configure` invalidates sync and imported blocker state and deletes activations at the new source version. Reuse that transaction, augment only if boundary tests expose a missing affected dependency path. Missing/unusable active reads must invalidate blocker knowledge even when an incomplete selection causes the current loop to skip `readBlockers`.
- Qualification uses the macOS runbook and #942 disposable LaunchAgent precedent because fresh lead probes found no installed Ensemble service/job/listener. Use a new paused local project, no repositories/delivery policy/routing, and the smallest currently readable real GitHub Project filter matching an existing open ready-labelled issue. Project 6 is already readable; metadata may be read, but fixture visibility/labels/project membership must not be changed. A project-wide import is unnecessary.

### Implementation context

- `src/core/credential-reference.ts`: shared env/discovery validation; `src/core/github-source-contracts.ts:githubConfigurationSchema` is currently env-only and supplies `DomainCommand` source validation. `src/cli/source.ts:editSchema` repeats the env-only source rule.
- `src/standalone/gh-credential.ts`: `detectGh`, `ghToken`, `ghEnvironment`, `discoveryCredentialExclusions` provide bounded resolution and safe failures. `ghToken` runs status then token, each at most 10 seconds, and remembers resolved values only for exclusion.
- `src/standalone/github-source.ts:GitHubSourceReader` / `GitHubHttpSourceReader`: public selection/blocker/status reads, 15-second HTTP timeout and safe incomplete reasons; `readProject` handles filtered ProjectV2 pagination. Preserve provider host/origin checks and current finite pagination limits.
- `src/standalone/github-sync.ts:GitHubSynchronizer`: default factory currently slices `env:`, missing refs silently skip project selections, incomplete selections skip blockers; retained local-blocker status already becomes unknown. Reconciliation captures project/config version/reference identities.
- `src/core/domain.ts:github.configure` and `src/core/github-source.ts:GitHubSourceStore`: real SQLite configuration, activation, sync/dependency reconciliation and history. `test/github-sync-race.test.ts` proves stale selection, native blocker and retained-status responses cannot commit after reconfiguration.
- `src/standalone/service.ts`: synchronizer construction, runtime `spawnEnvironment`, both `claude.turnEnvironment` branches, `setChildCredentialExclusions`, `capturedEvidenceExclusions`; currently these gh exclusions depend on discovery only. `src/core/child-environment.ts:credentialFreeEnvironment` removes aliases by value.
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts:OperatorApi` default preview factory, `previewGitHubSelection`, `readProjectConfiguration`, `readSourceObservations`, `exclusions`; `src/standalone/operator.ts:LocalOperatorUi` default preview and advanced HTML project/source editor; `src/standalone/cli.ts` wires both surfaces.
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: project source configuration and source-observation schemas; `web/src/project-config.tsx`, `source-config.tsx`, `sync-placement.tsx`, `settings-changes.ts`, `settings-view.ts`, `settings.tsx`: settings/status/draft wiring. `web/src/discovery-credential.tsx` supplies choice/account/Change/Cancel/Clear precedent.
- `test/fixtures/fake-gh.ts` supplies signed-in/missing/unreadable/hanging states; extend it with controlled changing token values. `test/discovery-credential-exclusion.test.ts` captures runtime environments with zero turns, both Claude branches, helpers and operator redaction. Browser precedent is `test/operator-discovery-credential-browser.test.ts`; source/receipt fixtures are in `test/fixtures/operator-settings.ts` and `operator-cli.ts`.

#### 6. Offline qualification and one development LaunchAgent import

**Task ID:** `T6`
**Depends on:** `T4, T5`
**Prerequisites:** all focused privacy/persistence/recovery checks; integrated `npm run check`; root confirms remaining grant = 1 and hands over exact private qualification paths/label.
**Files and symbols:** new `test/944/live-source-credential.mjs`, new `test/source-credential-qualification.test.ts` (offline harness test), dated `docs/evidence/944-gh-source-credential-<date>.md`; update `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` source guidance in place.

Offline mode injects fake gh/provider/runtime, exercises failure/persistence/recovery and the same sequence, proves zero turns/writes, and validates timeout/unknown cleanup behavior before any real attempt. Live mode uses one rendered disposable per-user LaunchAgent with a new private data/auth/log/plist root, the pinned absolute Node/compiled CLI, fixed non-secret renderer PATH and fresh loopback port. Initialize operator auth via existing protected verifier helpers; never put password/token/cookie in argv/plist/logs. Render/lint/read exact plist, then bootstrap exact label. Record filter/readiness label and immutable candidate SHA. If no matching issue or readable Project exists, stop unspent and report the specific precondition. Harness must validate filter bounds offline and confirm complete one-page metadata before choosing it; avoid a broad Project import. Default service sync interval is 300 seconds, so execute one explicit operator refresh after activation rather than wait for the interval.

1. Root records the attempt consumed immediately before `launchctl bootstrap`. Start an absolute monotonic 300-second deadline. Bootstrap/readiness/authentication must complete within 60 seconds; `/login`/operator requests use at most 5 seconds except credential/source requests below. Fresh project is paused, no lead/runtime work is requested, routing/delivery/repository grants remain absent.
2. Create one paused project and configure the captured Project selection/readiness with explicit `gh:github.com`. Record receipt/source version and verify inactive state. Source resolution is at most two existing 10-second gh subprocesses per read; each HTTP request retains its 15-second production timeout.
3. Call JSON `github.preview` once under a stored key and expected source version; allow at most 60 seconds. Capture separately the complete preview result, activation receipt and readback of the exact selection/version. If response is lost, reconcile the same key/payload once (at most 30 seconds, within the outer deadline); do not create a replacement operation.
4. Call source refresh once (at most 90 seconds); no retry of a failed provider read. Read source/task observations and exact imported external identity once. Pass requires successful source completeness/import, matching label readiness, correct project/selection membership, and paused project with zero runtime turns/provider writes. Capture import separately from activation. Preserve any receipt/outcome uncertainty; no inference of success from preview alone.
5. Reserve the final 30 seconds for `launchctl bootout` of the exact created label and reconciliation: bounded label/PID/loopback checks prove absence and owned process exit. Verify PID ownership against the recorded job before graceful signal fallback; never kill by name. Delete only the exact disposable paths after absence/exit proof. Otherwise retain private fixture state and record ownership/unknown outcome hold; no second attempt or automatic grant reset. The hard outer 300-second deadline stops actions even if nested source pagination could take longer; cancellation/bootout owns the service, never an assumption that `GitHubSynchronizer.stop()` instantly ends pending HTTP reads.

**Test:** offline production-SQLite harness proves complete success sequence, gh timeout/not-signed-in/unreadable, failed preview/no activation, lost keyed reply, Clear/reconfigure/new preview recovery, retained history and blockers unknown, read deadline cleanup/uncertain process ownership, and zero model/provider mutations. Fake runtime throws if a turn is attempted; guarded fake provider permits only GET/fixed GraphQL queries. Live records only safe identities/counts/status/timestamps; sanitize private logs and assert canary/gh token patterns absent before writing evidence.
**Validate:** after S/build, `node --test dist/test/source-credential-qualification.test.js`; then `node test/944/live-source-credential.mjs --live --one-attempt --max-seconds 300` from implementation root, after root's fresh grant/path handoff. CLI flags are the new harness interface to implement. Expect offline checks pass first, live preview/activation/import each independently proven, zero turns/writes, and exact LaunchAgent cleanup proved. Failure is recorded, not retried under this grant.
**Complete when:** sanitized bounded real-provider evidence and cleanup/hold disposition are committed; live success is required for issue completion. A failed/exhausted live attempt keeps the task blocked for a specific decision, while independent repairs/evidence work can continue.

### Acceptance coverage

| Accepted brief criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source env/gh/Clear runtime validation; omitted semantics; other credentials env-only | T2, T3, T5 | resolver/schema and CLI/domain configuration matrix |
| Per-read gh for sync, JSON/HTML previews, status and blockers; rotation and safe failure reasons | T2, T3 | changing-token fake-gh and production-path reader tests |

| Codex/Claude/helpers/aliases and evidence exclusion for both credential kinds | T2, T3 | source exclusion captures, >8 rotation and safe output assertions |
| Browser choice/account/Change/Cancel/Clear, failed/unknown draft recovery | T4 | fake-gh browser journeys and keyed outcome tests |
| Change/Clear version fences, preserved history, incomplete blockers, restoration | T3–T6 | real SQLite race/restart and UI/CLI recovery matrix |
| CLI and advanced HTML parity | T3, T5 | integrated HTML/API refusal and CLI source journeys |
| Pen first, DESIGN/ADR1009/SPEC/CONTEXT in-place | T1 | MCP readback/screenshots and diff review |
| Pinned ci/check, installed dev preview/activation/import | T6 | integrated check, offline harness, one real LaunchAgent attempt |

### Final validation

- From implementation root with S, run `npm run check` on the integrated candidate before live qualification; expect typecheck/lint/format/build/tests pass. CI runs the same check; root retains final-head provider gate ownership.
- Independent review of the integrated candidate against the original issue/brief and this plan, with `ship`, `fix-first` or `rethink` verdict and concrete evidence. Review privacy/fences and qualification safety before accepting issue completion; repair with original owner and renew affected evidence.
- Confirm all entry points applied: source settings, Sync & placement, project configuration summary/phone next step, JSON API, advanced HTML source/preview, operator CLI prepare/apply/preview and source observations. No extension/context-menu/notification source-credential mutation exists in the inspected implementation; investigate any added entry point before handback.
- Root verifies live grant consumption, successful import/cleanup or remaining hold, final HEAD/checks/review, and permitted publication/merge. Discovery evidence alone does not prove source support.

- Failure after a formerly complete selection must invalidate dependency knowledge even when no blocker read runs, and stale old-version responses must not restore it.
- Credential status detection/resolution and draft conflict handling must not override keyed replay or expose tokens in operator errors, browser diagnostics or evidence.
