content.title: Package Ensemble as a versioned self-contained release
P1: Build the release tarball with bundled Node and a tag-triggered CI release

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Build a self-contained `darwin-arm64` release tarball with bundled Node, produced by one script used both locally and by a tag-triggered CI release.

**Current behavior:**
Ensemble runs only from a checkout built in place with nvm-managed Node. A local script builds a commit into an immutable directory, but it relies on the host's nvm and keeps the full dev dependency tree. `package.json`'s `files` ships only the compiled service, not the built operator web UI. CI has a check workflow and no release workflow.

**Desired behavior:**
- One packaging script turns a commit into `ensemble-<version>-darwin-arm64/` (and a `.tar.gz` of it): compiled service and operator UI, production dependencies only, the exact Node from `.node-version` downloaded for darwin-arm64 and verified against nodejs.org's published checksum, and a `bin/ensemble` launcher that runs the bundled Node. The release must run with no repository, nvm or system Node present.
- The release excludes the Claude Agent SDK's platform binary packages (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-*`); `claude` comes from the host (see #981).
- A release manifest records version, commit, Node version and a deterministic tree digest; the manifest digest verifies against the unpacked tree.
- A GitHub Actions workflow on `v*` tags runs the existing check, packages on a macOS arm64 runner and attaches the tarball, `SHA256SUMS` and manifest to a GitHub Release. It refuses a tag that differs from `package.json`'s version. It also supports a manual run that uploads the same files as a workflow artifact without creating a release.
- The script replaces the existing local stable build script; update the "Local stable build" operations docs to use it.

**Key interfaces:**
- Release layout: `bin/ensemble`, the bundled Node runtime, the compiled tree and production `node_modules`, `manifest.json`.
- `package.json` `files`/`bin` must include the operator UI build so the same build also serves the later npm channel.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The script produces the tarball locally from a named commit and refuses to overwrite an existing output.
- [ ] Unpacked into a fresh directory with an empty `PATH` apart from system directories, `bin/ensemble --version` works and the service starts against a fresh private data directory and serves the operator UI.
- [ ] The tarball contains no `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-*` platform package and no dev dependencies.
- [ ] The manifest's tree digest matches a recomputation over the unpacked tree.
- [ ] A manual workflow run on the PR branch produces the artifact and `SHA256SUMS`; the downloaded artifact passes the unpacked-start check above.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes.

**Out of scope:**
- Pushing a real `v*` tag or creating a GitHub Release: Chris pushes the first tag.
- Signing, notarization, npm publish, Homebrew, other platforms, self-update.
- Merging the CLIs into one executable or installing a LaunchAgent (#980).
- Renaming the product.

Decisions: ADR-1011. Parent: #978.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/979
**Planned against:** `main` at `043b634003ef9e8dc058d8c6d8709e16f64e6adc`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Replace `scripts/local-build.sh` with one Node packaging script, `scripts/package-release.mjs`, used both locally and by CI. It archives a named commit and downloads the exact `.node-version` Node for darwin-arm64, rejecting it unless it matches nodejs.org's `SHASUMS256.txt`. The downloaded Node and the pinned npm run `npm ci`, the build and `npm prune --omit=dev`. The script then removes the Claude Agent SDK platform packages and lays out `ensemble-<version>-darwin-arm64/` with `bin/ensemble`, a tree-digest manifest, a `.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS`. The same script has a `verify` command that unpacks a tarball into a fresh directory, recomputes the digest and starts the release with a minimal `PATH`. A new `release.yml` workflow runs the existing check, packages and verifies on macOS arm64, and creates a GitHub Release only on a matching `v*` tag push. The operator CLI gains `--version`, and `package.json` `files` gains `dist/operator`.

### Guardrails

- Never push a tag, create a GitHub Release or run the tag-triggered release job during implementation or validation. Chris pushes the first tag. Workflow evidence comes only from pull-request or manual (`workflow_dispatch`) runs, which upload a workflow artifact and nothing else.
- Node download verification fails closed. A non-200 response, a missing or duplicated `SHASUMS256.txt` entry for the exact file name, or a hash mismatch aborts the build before extraction and leaves no completed output. There is no bypass flag or environment override for checksum verification.
- The release job is the only job with `contents: write`. It runs only for `push` events on `refs/tags/v*` after the check, package and verify jobs succeed. Pull-request runs, including runs from forks, and manual runs keep `contents: read` and never reach release creation.
- The build never overwrites output. It refuses an existing release directory, tarball or partial directory.
- Out of scope: subcommand unification and LaunchAgent install, upgrade or uninstall (#980); resolving `claude` from `PATH` and Claude readiness (#981, PR #985); signing, notarization, npm publish, Homebrew, other platforms, self-update and renaming the product. Keep `serve`, `operator`, `operations-cli` and `operator-auth-cli` working under their current paths; #980 adds `ensemble` subcommands for them.
- Do not change service startup, readiness or the Codex runtime contract. The release depends on `codex` from `PATH` in the same way as the current checkout build.
- Keep the existing `check` job name and behaviour in `ci.yml`. The only allowed edit there is the `workflow_call` trigger.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume the plan-mismatch budget. Only a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption gets one diagnosis plus at most two repair cycles before the owner stops and returns a replan request. Examples are `workflow_call` being unable to reuse `ci.yml`, the service failing to start without the SDK platform package, or `npm prune --omit=dev` removing a runtime dependency. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Node orchestrator, downloaded build Node.** The script runs under any host Node 24 or later; locally that can be any Node, and in CI it comes from `setup-node`. It builds with the downloaded and verified Node by putting that Node's `bin` first on `PATH` and running `npx --yes --package <packageManager pin> -c 'npm ci && npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev'` with `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=/dev/null`. This reuses `local-build.sh`'s npm pattern. It drops nvm and guarantees that the build Node is the shipped Node. A Node script keeps the checksum and digest logic importable by the existing `node:test` suite, following the precedent of `test/test-runner.test.ts` importing `scripts/run-tests.mjs`.
- **SDK platform packages removed explicitly.** Remove them after the prune and fail the build if any `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-*` remains. Do not use `--omit=optional`, because `@napi-rs/canvas` (through `pdfjs-dist`) is also an optional production dependency and must not be dropped silently. The lockfile shows no production package with an install script. #979 owns this exclusion; #981 lists it too, but only #979 creates a release tree. Until #981 lands, a release has no `claude` binary and Claude turns fail. Codex remains the default harness (ADR-1008). The operations docs disclose this limit.
- **Release layout.** `ensemble-<version>-darwin-arm64/` contains:
  - `bin/ensemble`
  - `node/bin/node` and `node/LICENSE` (only the binary and licence from the official tarball; no bundled npm)
  - `dist/src` and `dist/operator`
  - the production `node_modules`
  - `package.json`, which is required for `"type": "module"`
  - `LICENSE`
  - `manifest.json`

  `bin/ensemble` is a POSIX `sh` launcher. It resolves its root with `cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd -P` and runs `exec "$root/node/bin/node" "$root/dist/src/cli/main.js" "$@"`. Quote every path, because the ADR-1011 install path contains spaces. Until #980, the service starts through the bundled Node directly: `node/bin/node dist/src/standalone/cli.js operator DATA PORT`.
- **Manifest and digest.** `manifest.json` has this shape:

  ```json
  {"schema":"ensemble.release/v1","name":"…","version":"…","platform":"darwin-arm64","commit":"<full sha>","node":{"version":"…","sha256":"<official tarball sha256>"},"tree":{"algorithm":"ensemble-tree-sha256/v1","digest":"<hex>"}}
  ```

  `ensemble-tree-sha256/v1` walks the release root and excludes the root `manifest.json`. It sorts relative POSIX paths by byte order. Each regular file contributes the line `file <0755|0644> <sha256> <path>\n`, where the mode is `0755` when any execute bit is set. Each symlink contributes `link <target> <path>\n`. Any other entry type fails. The digest is the SHA-256 of the concatenated lines. Document the algorithm in the operations docs so the digest can be recomputed outside the artifact. `SHA256SUMS` uses `shasum -a 256` format for the tarball and `manifest.json`, so `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` verifies them. A copy of `manifest.json` sits beside the tarball.
- **Output locations.** `build COMMIT` defaults to `~/.config/ensemble-dev/builds/<sha>/`, which keeps the per-commit immutable directory of `local-build.sh`. It also keeps that script's creation of private `data/`, `auth/` and `snapshots/` directories and its refusal of symlinks. `--out DIR` is used by CI and writes only the outputs. The script stages work in `<out>.partial` and renames it on success.
- **Tag guard.** `check-tag TAG` exits non-zero unless `TAG === "v" + package.json version`. CI runs it on tag pushes before packaging. The tag-push trigger and release creation are tested through this command and a static review of the workflow, never by a real tag.
- **PR-branch workflow evidence.** GitHub dispatches `workflow_dispatch` only for workflows already on the default branch. To get a PR-branch run, `release.yml` also runs on `pull_request` for the packaging paths: `scripts/package-release.mjs`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `.node-version`. That run is the same non-release package-and-verify path that a manual run uses, so it satisfies the brief's "manual workflow run on the PR branch" criterion. After merge, verify the dispatch trigger with `gh workflow run release.yml --ref main`, which uploads an artifact only. On pull requests the reused `check` job is skipped, because `ci.yml` already runs it there. The package job runs when `check` succeeded or was skipped.
- **Startup needs `codex` (measured during planning).** On this Mac, the built service at `b67ebff0` exits with `spawn codex ENOENT` when `PATH` holds only system directories. With a private directory holding only a fake Codex app-server stub, it starts under that minimal `PATH` and a temporary `HOME`. The stub answers `initialize`, `account/read` (`{account:{type:"chatgpt"}}`) and `config/read`. The service then serves `/app` with HTTP 200, but it took more than 10 s. The stub pattern follows `test/codex-runtime.test.ts`. Therefore `verify` sets `PATH=<private codex dir>:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` and `HOME=<fresh dir>`. The private directory holds only a generated stub whose shebang is the release's bundled Node, and `verify` asserts that `command -v node` fails in that environment. Use a 120 s startup deadline. This is the acceptance criterion's "empty PATH apart from system directories" plus the `codex` that ADR-1011 already requires from `PATH`. A real Codex login is not exercised; #980's live install run owns that.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `scripts/local-build.sh` builds one commit into `~/.config/ensemble-dev/builds/<sha>` with nvm and the full dev tree. Its only reference is the "Local stable build" section of `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`, lines 405–457.
- **Existing:** `package.json` has `files: ["dist/src"]` and `bin.ensemble: dist/src/cli/main.js`, which is the operator CLI. `npm run build` runs `tsc`, which writes to `dist/src` and `dist/test`, and then Vite, which writes to `dist/operator` (`web/vite.config.ts`). `src/standalone/cli.ts:138` loads the UI from `new URL("../../operator", import.meta.url)`. Nothing in `src` reads files outside `dist/`.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/main.ts` `main(argv, deps)` uses `parseArgs` in strict mode with a `help` boolean and writes `USAGE` (line 66). There is no `--version`. Tests call `main` through `test/fixtures/cli-harness.ts` `harness()` in `test/operator-cli.test.ts`. `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts` uses `test/fixtures/packed-cli.js` `installPacked` to `npm pack` and install the package.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-auth-cli.ts init` needs a TTY. Tests initialize auth non-interactively with `OperatorAuth.initialize(authFile, password)` from `dist/src/standalone/operator-auth.js`. An unauthenticated `GET /app` returns 200 with the shell (`test/operator-web-http.test.ts:64`).
- **Existing:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on push to `main` and on `pull_request`, using `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, a global install of the pinned npm, `npm ci`, a Playwright install, `npm run test:fixture-preflight`, `npm run check` and `actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2`. There is no release workflow.
- **Existing:** `package-lock.json` has optional, OS-filtered `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-<platform>` packages; the darwin-arm64 package is 230 MB. `@napi-rs/canvas*` are optional production packages, and `@types/react-dom` is `devOptional`.
- **New:** `scripts/package-release.mjs` exports these pure or injectable functions:
  - `nodeChecksum(shasumsText, fileName)` returns the single expected hex or throws.
  - `downloadVerifiedNode({ version, directory, fetch })` downloads, verifies, then extracts, and returns `{ nodeDirectory, sha256 }`.
  - `treeDigest(root)`.
  - `checkTag(tag, version)`.

  Its CLI commands are `build COMMIT [--out DIR]`, `verify TARBALL` and `check-tag TAG`. A main-module guard runs the CLI only when the file is executed directly.
- **New:** `.github/workflows/release.yml` has these jobs:
  - `check`: `uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml`; skipped on `pull_request`.
  - `package`: `macos-15` (arm64). Runs `check-tag` on tag pushes, then `build HEAD --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release"`, then `verify` the tarball, then uploads the tarball, `SHA256SUMS` and `manifest.json` as one artifact.
  - `release`: `ubuntu-latest`, `permissions: contents: write`, only on tag push. Downloads the artifact and runs `gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" <files> --verify-tag`.

  The workflow default is `permissions: contents: read`.
- **Follow:** `test/test-runner.test.ts:21` for importing an `.mjs` script with `pathToFileURL(resolve("scripts/…"))`. Follow `test/codex-runtime.test.ts:575-600` for the fake Codex app-server stub, and `scripts/local-build.sh` for private-directory, symlink-refusal and npm-isolation behaviour.
- **Overlap:** open PR #983 (#950) edits `src/cli/main.ts`. Open PR #973 edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `package.json` and `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`. Resolve either as a routine rebase. PR #985 changes only ADR-1011 text about `claude` version gating, and this plan neither depends on nor contradicts it.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is T1 → T3, T2 → T3 and T3 → T4, and it is acyclic. T1 and T2 can run in parallel because they share no files. T3 extends T2's `scripts/package-release.mjs`, and T4 needs T3's commands.

#### 1. Operator CLI reports its version; the npm package ships the operator UI

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `src/cli/main.ts` (`main`, `USAGE`), `package.json` (`files`), `test/operator-cli.test.ts`, `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- In `test/operator-cli.test.ts`, `main(["--version"])` through `harness()` exits 0 and writes exactly `ensemble <package.json version>\n`, with the version read from the repo's `package.json`. `--help` output lists `--version`.
- In `test/operator-cli-packed.test.ts`, the installed package contains `dist/operator/index.html`, still has no `dist/test`, and the installed `.bin/ensemble --version` exits 0 with the same line.
**Implementation:** Add a `version` boolean option. When it is set, read `version` from `new URL("../../../package.json", import.meta.url)`, write the line and return 0 before `run`. That path resolves from `dist/src/cli/main.js` in a checkout, an npm install and the release. Add `"dist/operator"` to `files`.
**Validate:** From the repo root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-cli.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-packed.test.js`. Expect all tests to pass.
**Complete when:** `--version` works in the checkout and in the packed install, and the packed install contains the operator UI.

#### 2. Fail-closed Node download and the release tree digest

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** new `scripts/package-release.mjs` (`nodeChecksum`, `downloadVerifiedNode`, `treeDigest`, `checkTag`) and new `test/package-release.test.ts`, which imports the script as in `test/test-runner.test.ts`.
**Test:** In `test/package-release.test.ts`, with temporary directories and an injected fake `fetch`:
- `nodeChecksum` returns the hex for an exact single match. It throws on a missing entry, on a duplicate entry, and on a near-miss name such as `node-v24.21.0-darwin-arm64.tar.xz` when the request is for `.tar.gz`.
- `downloadVerifiedNode` throws when the tarball bytes do not match the published hash, and leaves no extracted directory. It throws on a non-200 response for `SHASUMS256.txt` or for the tarball. With a fixture tarball (`tar -czf` of `node-v<ver>-darwin-arm64/bin/node` and `LICENSE`) and a matching `SHASUMS256.txt`, it extracts and returns the hash.
- `treeDigest`:
  - is identical for two trees created in different orders;
  - changes when any of these change: a file's content, the execute bit, a rename, an added file or a symlink target;
  - ignores the root `manifest.json` and does not ignore a nested `manifest.json`;
  - throws on a FIFO.
- `checkTag("v0.1.0", "0.1.0")` passes, and `checkTag("v0.1.1", "0.1.0")` and `checkTag("0.1.0", "0.1.0")` throw.
**Implementation:** Implement the four functions as described in Planning decisions, using `node:crypto`, `node:fs/promises` and `tar` through `execFile`. Download only from `https://nodejs.org/dist/v<version>/`. Hash the downloaded file before calling `tar`, and remove the download on any failure.
**Validate:** From the repo root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/package-release.test.js` and expect all tests to pass. Then run `npx biome lint --error-on-warnings scripts/package-release.mjs test/package-release.test.ts` and expect no findings.
**Complete when:** Every fail-closed branch has a passing test and the digest tests pass.

#### 3. The packaging and verification commands replace the local build script

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1, T2`
**Prerequisites:** T1's `--version` and T2's functions.
**Files and symbols:**
- `scripts/package-release.mjs`: the `build`, `verify` and `check-tag` commands, the launcher text and the manifest writer.
- Delete `scripts/local-build.sh`.
- `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`: rewrite "Local stable build" (lines 405–457).
- `README.md`: the "Packaging" bullet near line 154 says that the packaging script and release workflow exist and that no release has been published.
- `test/package-release.test.ts`: add a launcher test.
**Test:** In `test/package-release.test.ts`, write the launcher into a temporary root whose path contains a space, with a stub `node/bin/node` shell script that prints its arguments. Run `bin/ensemble --version` through a symlink-free absolute path and assert that the stub received `<root>/dist/src/cli/main.js --version`.
**Implementation:**
- `build COMMIT [--out DIR]`:
  1. Resolve `git rev-parse --verify COMMIT^{commit}`, then read `package.json` and `.node-version` with `git show`.
  2. Refuse any existing output or `.partial`, and handle the default-location private directories.
  3. Run `git archive | tar -x` into a source directory, call `downloadVerifiedNode`, then run the build, prune and SDK removal with the downloaded Node.
  4. Assert that no `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-*` directory remains and that no lockfile entry with `dev: true` exists in `node_modules`.
  5. Copy the layout, write `bin/ensemble` with mode 0755, write `manifest.json` with `treeDigest`, create the tarball and `SHA256SUMS`, and rename the partial directory.
  6. Print the output paths and the start commands.
- `verify TARBALL`:
  1. Check `SHA256SUMS` in the tarball's directory when it is present.
  2. Unpack into a fresh `mkdtemp` directory and recompute `treeDigest` against `manifest.json`.
  3. Repeat the forbidden-package and dev-package scan.
  4. In the minimal environment from Planning decisions, assert that `command -v node` fails and that `bin/ensemble --version` prints `ensemble <manifest version>`.
  5. Initialize auth with the release's bundled Node importing the release's `operator-auth.js` and a random password.
  6. Start `node/bin/node dist/src/standalone/cli.js operator <fresh data> <free port>`. Within 120 s, expect `GET /app` to return 200 and one `/assets/` URL from the shell to return 200.
  7. Send SIGTERM to that exact child PID, wait for exit, and remove the temporary directory.
- Update the docs with the new commands and layout, the start command with `"$RELEASE/node/bin/node"`, the digest algorithm, and the Claude-unavailable-until-#981 limit. Keep the upgrade, snapshot and rollback text.
**Validate:** From the repo root, after committing T1–T3 on the branch, run each step below with any host Node 24 and expect the stated result.
1. Run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/package-release.test.js`; expect all tests to pass.
2. Run `node scripts/package-release.mjs build HEAD --out "$TMPDIR/rel979"`; expect exit 0 and the files `ensemble-0.1.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz`, `SHA256SUMS` and `manifest.json`.
3. Run the same command again; expect a non-zero exit with a refusal message and unchanged `shasum -a 256 "$TMPDIR/rel979"/*`.
4. Run `node scripts/package-release.mjs verify "$TMPDIR/rel979/ensemble-0.1.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz"`; expect exit 0 after the digest, package-scan, `--version` and `/app` steps.
5. Run `tar -tzf <tarball> | grep -E 'claude-agent-sdk-|/node_modules/(typescript|vite|playwright|@biomejs)/'`; expect no output.
6. Run `node scripts/package-release.mjs check-tag v9.9.9`; expect a non-zero exit.

Record the commit SHA and the command outputs in the PR.
**Complete when:** A local tarball from a named commit verifies in a fresh directory, a second build refuses, `local-build.sh` is gone, and the docs describe the new procedure.

#### 4. Tag-triggered release workflow with artifact-only PR and manual runs

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3's `build`, `verify` and `check-tag` commands.
**Files and symbols:** new `.github/workflows/release.yml`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (add `workflow_call:` to `on:` only).
**Implementation:**
- `on`: `push: tags: ['v*']`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `pull_request` with the packaging paths. The workflow default is `permissions: contents: read`.
- Job `check` reuses `ci.yml` and has `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`.
- Job `package` runs on `macos-15` with `needs: check` and `if: ${{ !cancelled() && (needs.check.result == 'success' || needs.check.result == 'skipped') }}`. Its steps are:
  1. Check out the repository and set up Node from `.node-version`.
  2. On tag pushes, run `node scripts/package-release.mjs check-tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`.
  3. Run `build HEAD --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release"`, then `verify`.
  4. Upload the three files with `actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2` as `ensemble-release-${{ github.sha }}`.
- Job `release` runs only when `github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`. It needs `[check, package]`, has `permissions: contents: write`, uses the `actions/download-artifact` major that pairs with upload v7, and runs `gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" … --verify-tag` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`.
**Validate:**
1. From the repo root, run `npx --yes actionlint@<current> .github/workflows/release.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml`, or the `rhysd/actionlint` binary; expect no findings.
2. Push the PR branch and confirm with `gh run list --workflow release.yml --branch <branch>` that a `pull_request` run ran. In that run, `package` succeeded, `check` and `release` were skipped, and no release exists (`gh release list` is unchanged and empty).
3. Run `gh run download <run-id> -n ensemble-release-<sha> -D "$TMPDIR/dl979"`, then `(cd "$TMPDIR/dl979" && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS)` and `node scripts/package-release.mjs verify "$TMPDIR/dl979/ensemble-0.1.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz"`. Expect both to exit 0.
4. Run `gh api repos/chrisbanes/ensemble/tags --jq '.[].name'` and confirm that no new tag exists.
**Complete when:** The PR-branch workflow run produced the artifact and `SHA256SUMS`, the downloaded artifact passes `verify`, and the release job is statically restricted to tag pushes.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| The script produces the tarball locally from a named commit and refuses to overwrite an existing output | 3 | T3 Validate steps 2 and 3 |
| Unpacked into a fresh directory with a minimal `PATH` (system directories plus `codex` only, no Node), `bin/ensemble --version` works and the service starts against fresh private data and serves the operator UI | 1, 3 | T1 `--version` tests; T3 `verify` (Validate step 4) |
| No `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-*` platform package and no dev dependencies | 3 | `build` assertions plus T3 Validate steps 4 and 5 |
| The manifest's tree digest matches a recomputation over the unpacked tree (also in the issue body) | 2, 3 | T2 `treeDigest` tests; T3 `verify` digest step |
| A manual or PR-branch non-release workflow run produces the artifact and `SHA256SUMS`, and the downloaded artifact passes the unpacked-start check | 4 | T4 Validate steps 2 and 3 |
| Node is the exact `.node-version` build for darwin-arm64, verified against the published checksum and failing closed | 2, 3 | T2 checksum and download tests; `manifest.node.sha256` from T3 |
| `dist/operator` ships in `files` and in the release | 1, 3 | T1 packed test; T3 `verify` asset request |
| Release manifest records commit, version, Node version and tree digest | 3 | T3 `verify` reads and checks `manifest.json` |
| The workflow refuses a tag that differs from `package.json` version | 2, 4 | T2 `checkTag` tests; T4 `check-tag` step; T3 Validate step 6 |
| A `v*` tag runs the check, packages on macOS arm64 and attaches the tarball, `SHA256SUMS` and manifest to a Release | 4 | Static review and actionlint only; the tag path is unproven until Chris pushes the first tag (see Final validation) |
| `scripts/local-build.sh` is replaced and the "Local stable build" docs are updated | 3 | Diff review of the T3 deliverable |
| `npm run check` passes | all | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repo root, on the integrated delivery candidate, run `npm ci && npm run check`. Expect exit 0. The `check` CI job runs the same command on the PR.
- On the PR head, expect the `release.yml` `pull_request` run to show the `package` job succeeding, with `check` and `release` skipped. Rerun T4 Validate step 3 if the PR head changed after it last passed.
- After merge, not as a delivery gate: run `gh workflow run release.yml --ref main` and confirm that only an artifact is produced and no release or tag is created.
- Unproven until Chris pushes the first real `v*` tag:
  - that the `push: tags` trigger fires;
  - that the reused `check` job runs under `workflow_call` on a tag ref;
  - that the `release` job's `contents: write` token can create the release;
  - that `gh release create --verify-tag` attaches all three files;
  - the end-to-end refusal of a mismatched real tag, which is tested only through `check-tag`.

  These are also unproven: Gatekeeper behaviour for a tarball downloaded through a browser, which gains a quarantine attribute (signing and notarization are out of scope); a real Codex login and runtime under the release, which #980's live install run owns; and the Claude harness in a release before #981 lands.

### Review focus

- The fail-closed order: hash, then extract. Check that no code path can use an unverified Node or leave a completed output after a failure.
- The workflow privilege boundary. Check that `contents: write` appears only on the tag-gated `release` job, and that `pull_request` (including from forks) and `workflow_dispatch` cannot reach it.
- Launcher path handling with spaces, and whether `verify` truly runs without any host Node or nvm on `PATH`.
- Digest determinism: byte-order sorting, the execute-bit rule, and symlinks in production `node_modules/.bin`.

content.title: P2: Unify ensemble subcommands and add service install, upgrade and uninstall

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** One `ensemble` executable with service/admin subcommands, and `ensemble service install | upgrade | uninstall` owning the per-user LaunchAgent. Blocked by #979.

**Current behavior:**
The service, offline operations (backup/verify/restore, LaunchAgent rendering), operator auth init and the operator CLI are separate entry points. The operations CLI renders and writes a plist, but bootstrapping, upgrading and removing the job are manual `launchctl` steps documented in the macOS operations guide.

**Desired behavior:**
- `ensemble` exposes the service, offline operations, operator auth init and the existing operator CLI commands. Existing entry points keep working until docs move off them.
- `ensemble service install` renders, lints and bootstraps a LaunchAgent bound to the exact versioned executable of the running release (never a symlink), with default state under `~/Library/Application Support/Ensemble/` (data, auth, snapshots beside `versions/`) and logs under `~/Library/Logs/Ensemble/`. It keeps the existing path validation (absolute, canonical, private, no symlinks), fixed `PATH` and no secrets in the plist.
- `ensemble service upgrade <version directory>` stops the exact job and confirms its process exited, takes and verifies an offline snapshot, re-renders the plist for the new version, bootstraps it and runs the readiness checks. On any failure it leaves the job stopped and reports the snapshot and log paths. There is no rollback command.
- `ensemble service uninstall` removes the job and keeps data, auth, snapshots and version directories.
- Rewrite the macOS operations guide around these commands, keeping snapshot/restore as disaster recovery.

**Key interfaces:**
- The existing LaunchAgent configuration renderer and offline snapshot operations are reused, not reimplemented.
- `launchctl` access goes through a seam that tests can replace with a fake.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Automated tests with a fake `launchctl` cover install, successful upgrade, upgrade failing at start and at readiness (job left stopped, snapshot verified and reported), and uninstall preserving state.
- [ ] Upgrade refuses when the exact job's process cannot be confirmed exited.
- [ ] Bounded live run on this Mac with a throwaway label and private paths: install release A, upgrade to release B, readiness passes, snapshot verifies; then boot the job out and confirm the label and process are absent.
- [ ] The live run never touches the Haze prototype, its data or any existing LaunchAgent.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes.

**Out of scope:**
- Version rollback, self-update, pruning old version directories, desktop app.
- The S08c cutover itself (#761).
- Claude CLI resolution (#981).

Decisions: ADR-1011. Parent: #978.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/980
**Planned against:** `main` at `24237649629873fde685bf78d4a3c89cc1b27806`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

`src/cli/main.ts` gains two local command areas that it routes before its operator-CLI argument parsing. `ensemble service serve|operator|run|list …` delegates to the existing standalone `main`, and `ensemble service init-auth` and `ensemble snapshot create|verify|restore` call the existing auth and snapshot functions. `ensemble service install|upgrade|uninstall` live in a new `src/cli/service.ts`. That module reuses `writeLaunchAgent`, `createSnapshot`/`verifySnapshot`, the process-identity verifier and the operator CLI's `doctor` readiness read. `launchctl`, `plutil`, process-exit confirmation, the health probe and readiness all reach it through one injected host seam. A private JSON install record holds the configuration and plist digest. The activation plist sits in the LaunchAgents directory, and log files are named per generation. Tests drive every lifecycle path with a fake `launchctl` in temporary directories. A guarded live harness then runs install A → upgrade B → uninstall on this Mac with a throwaway label and private paths. The operations guide is rewritten around the commands.

### Guardrails

- Implementation and validation never touch the real `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, the real `~/Library/Application Support/Ensemble` (which already holds files from the earlier pipeline implementation), the real `~/Library/Logs`, the Haze prototype, any existing launchd job or any running service. Automated tests use only temporary directories and the fake `launchctl`. Only T4's guarded live run calls the real `/bin/launchctl`. It may do so only for its own `local.ensemble.validation-<random>` label, with the plist in a temporary agents directory, and only after an ownership check. It never stops a process by name or by command-line match.
- Keep `npm run service`, `npm run operations` (including `render-launch-agent`), `npm run operator-auth`, `dist/src/standalone/*-cli.js` and their outputs working unchanged. The new commands are added alongside them. Removing them is out of scope.
- Keep `renderLaunchAgent`'s validation and plist contents unchanged: absolute canonical paths, no symlinks, private directories, new log files, the fixed `PATH`, `RunAtLoad=true`, `KeepAlive=false` and no secrets. Service commands report only paths they own and fixed stage names, never raw error causes or secret values.

### Planning decisions

- **Command surface.** The new commands are:
  - `ensemble service <serve|operator|run|list> ARGS…`, which passes `argv.slice(1)` unchanged to `src/standalone/cli.ts` `main`;
  - `ensemble service init-auth [AUTH_FILE]`, which defaults to `<state>/auth/operator-auth.json` and creates `<state>/auth` with mode 0700, and which needs a TTY just as `operator-auth-cli` does;
  - `ensemble snapshot create SOURCE SNAPSHOT | verify SNAPSHOT | restore SNAPSHOT DESTINATION`, which uses the same functions and the same `{ok, operation, manifest}` JSON as `operations-cli`;
  - `ensemble service install|upgrade VERSION_DIR|uninstall`.

  The `snapshot` area avoids colliding with the operator CLI's `operation get`. `render-launch-agent` is not exposed, because `service install` replaces it. Usage errors exit 2 and failures exit 1.
- **Paths and options.** The defaults derive from `deps.env.HOME`, not `os.homedir()`, so tests can supply a temporary HOME:
  - state `S = $HOME/Library/Application Support/Ensemble`, holding `data/`, `auth/operator-auth.json`, `snapshots/`, `launchd/` and `versions/<version>/`;
  - logs `L = $HOME/Library/Logs/Ensemble`;
  - agents `A = $HOME/Library/LaunchAgents`.

  The options `--state-dir`, `--log-dir`, `--launch-agents-dir`, `--label` (default `local.ensemble.service`) and `--port` (default 8787; the origin is `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) exist for tests and the live run. `S` and `A` must be real, canonical, user-owned directories with no group or world write bit. The real `S` and `A` on this Mac are 0755. They are created with mode 0700 if missing. `data/`, `snapshots/`, `launchd/` and `L` are created with mode 0700 if missing and must be private. Other entries in `S` are never read or changed. ADR-1011 already treats the label as persisted surface that will be renamed with the product before any public release.
- **Bound executable.** The plist binds `S/versions/<v>/node/bin/node` and `S/versions/<v>/dist/src/standalone/cli.js operator S/data PORT` through the unchanged renderer. Both paths are exact and versioned, with no symlink and no `bin/ensemble` shell hop. `install` uses the running release, found at `new URL("../../..", import.meta.url)` from `dist/src/cli/service.js` (tests inject it). It refuses unless that root is canonical, its parent is `realpath(S/versions)`, and it holds a `manifest.json` with zod-validated `schema: "ensemble.release/v1"`, `platform: "darwin-arm64"` and `version === basename(root)`. A checkout therefore cannot install. `upgrade VERSION_DIR` applies the same check to the target. It accepts the currently installed version, which lets an operator re-run a failed upgrade with a fresh snapshot.
- **Install record and activation.** The record is `S/launchd/<label>.json`, mode 0600, written to a temporary file and then renamed into place. It holds `{schema:"ensemble.service/v1", label, plistSha256, configuration: LaunchAgentConfiguration}`, and every read validates it with zod. The plist is written by `writeLaunchAgent` into a fresh `mkdtemp` 0700 staging directory under `S/launchd/`, linted with `/usr/bin/plutil -lint`, and renamed to `A/<label>.plist`, replacing any earlier copy. The record is written before that rename. Direct writes to `A` are impossible because `writeLaunchAgent` requires a private parent and the real `A` is 0755. Each generation's logs are `L/<label>.<version>.<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>.{out,err}.log`, because the renderer refuses existing log files. The activation copy is what makes launchd start the job at login, while the record is what `upgrade` and `uninstall` work from.
- **Ownership before any bootout.** A loaded job is ours only when `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>` reports `path = A/<label>.plist` and that file's SHA-256 equals `record.plistSha256`. Exit code 113 (measured during planning for an absent label) means not loaded. Any other `print` failure refuses. Before the bootout, the command captures the job's `pid` with `captureProcessIdentity`. If a pid is present but cannot be captured, the command refuses without stopping anything. After `bootout`, it polls for up to 30 s until `print` reports the label absent and `MacProcessTerminationVerifier.verify` returns `verified`. Otherwise it stops at stage `stop` with "process exit unconfirmed".
- **Install.** The preflight runs in this order:
  1. Check the release root.
  2. Require that the label is not loaded and that neither the record nor the activation file exists.
  3. Require the auth file. If it is missing, report "run `ensemble service init-auth`".
  4. Probe that the loopback port is free by listening on `127.0.0.1:<port>` and then closing.

  Install then creates the directories, renders and lints, writes the record and activation, and calls `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> A/<label>.plist`. It waits up to 120 s for `GET <origin>/app` to return 200. If bootstrap or the health wait fails, install undoes itself. It boots out the job only if it is owned (with exit confirmed), removes the activation file and the record, keeps the data, auth and logs, reports the log paths and exits 1. It then leaves no installed state, so install can simply be re-run.
- **Upgrade.** The upgrade proceeds in stages:
  1. Preflight with no state change. Read the record, validate the target, and resolve the readiness connection: `--connection`, `ENSEMBLE_CONNECTION` or the default connection, with its token loadable and its URL equal to the record's origin.
  2. Stop the job. This step is skipped when the job is not loaded, for example after a failed upgrade.
  3. Snapshot to `S/snapshots/<label>.<from>-to-<to>.<stamp>` with `createSnapshot` and then `verifySnapshot`. The data owner lock refuses independently if any process still holds the data directory.
  4. Re-render, lint, write the record and activation.
  5. Bootstrap.
  6. Wait for `/app`.
  7. Read readiness through the connection until it passes or the 120 s deadline expires. The identity check must confirm the same installation and origin. Readiness passes when no check has status `fail`; `not-configured` is accepted. This stays correct when #988 adds `claude-executable`, which reports `not-configured` while Claude is unused.

  Any failure from step 2 onward leaves the job stopped. If the new job was loaded, the command boots it out only after the ownership check and confirmed exit. It removes the activation file so that nothing starts at login, and keeps the record so that `upgrade <fixed release>` or `uninstall` can recover. On stderr it writes `{"ok":false,"operation":"upgrade","stage","jobStopped","snapshot","logs"}`, and it exits 1. On success it writes `{"ok":true,"operation":"upgrade","label","version","snapshot","logs","readiness"}`, where `readiness` lists the check ids and statuses. Recovery is a fixed release and another upgrade, or `ensemble snapshot restore` into a new data directory (ADR-1011).
- **Uninstall.** With no record, no activation file and an unloaded label, uninstall prints "not installed" and exits 0. It refuses, changing nothing, when a loaded job or the activation file is not owned. Otherwise it boots out the owned job and confirms the exit. If the exit is unconfirmed, it removes the activation file, keeps the record, exits 1 and says to re-run. Finally it removes the activation file and the record. Data, auth, snapshots, versions and logs remain. Install after uninstall reuses the data and auth.
- **Readiness credential.** Readiness is reachable only through the authenticated `/api/operator/readiness` route. Upgrade therefore reuses the operator CLI's `connect` with `["cli.identity","diagnostics.read"]` and `doctor`'s `readinessSchema` read. The connection is the operator's existing `ensemble auth login` connection with a `read` credential, which `test/operator-cli-doctor.test.ts:46` shows is sufficient. It is wired in `main.ts` as an injected `readiness(connection)` function. This makes a logged-in CLI connection a documented upgrade precondition. It is checked before anything stops.
- **Host seam.** `ServiceHost = {uid, launchctl(args) → {status, stdout}, lint(path), captureIdentity(pid), exited(identity), fetch, now, sleep}`. Production values come from `execFile("/bin/launchctl" | "/usr/bin/plutil")` with a 20 s timeout and `childProcessEnvironment()`, `captureProcessIdentity` and `MacProcessTerminationVerifier`. CI runs on `ubuntu-latest`, so automated tests use a fake. The fake is a label map that renders `print` text containing `path =`, `state =` and `pid =` lines, returns 113 when the label is absent, and records every call. Only a darwin-guarded test calls the real `plutil`. That guard follows `test/launchd.test.ts` `lintPlistIfAvailable`.

| `service uninstall` removes the job and keeps data, auth, snapshots and version directories | 2 | Uninstall preservation test |
| No rollback command; failed upgrade reports snapshot and logs | 3 | Failure JSON assertions; `--help` has no rollback |
| Bounded live run: install A, upgrade to B, readiness passes, snapshot verifies; bootout leaves label and process absent | 4 | `node test/980/live-service-lifecycle.mjs --live` plus the evidence record |
| The live run never touches the Haze prototype, its data or any existing LaunchAgent | 4 | Baseline-equality steps 1 and 8, and the throwaway label and paths |
| The operations guide is rewritten around these commands, keeping snapshot and restore as disaster recovery | 5 | T5 search and format check plus diff review |
| `npm run check` passes | all | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the repo root, on the integrated delivery candidate, run `npm ci && npm run check`. Expect exit 0. The CI `check` job runs the same command on the PR.
- Baseline: CI run 38570918701 at the planned SHA passed `check` on Node 24. `check-node-26` failed one timing test, "a stalled web startup retains its resources while an independent listener closes" (`auth-1.initialize: timed-out after 87 ms`). That test is outside this plan's files, and the five previous `main` runs passed. If it fails again on the PR, treat it as a pre-existing flake to report, not as a defect in this ticket.
- Re-run T4 only if `src/cli/service.ts`, `src/cli/main.ts` routing or `src/standalone/launchd.ts` changed after the recorded live run.
- These remain unproven and need the maintainer; record them in the guide and the evidence:
  - the first install with the default label `local.ensemble.service` into the real `~/Library/LaunchAgents` and the real `~/Library/Application Support/Ensemble`, beside the earlier pipeline files;
  - launchd starting the job at login from the activation plist after a logout or reboot;
  - an upgrade over a real data directory with projects, workspaces or a running turn, where bootout interrupts work and recovery holds apply;
  - installing from a CI-built tagged release (#979's tag path), or from a browser-downloaded tarball with quarantine attributes;
  - Claude turns under launchd (#981);
  - the #761 cutover.

### Review focus

- Every `bootout` is preceded by the ownership check, and no failure path deletes data, auth, snapshots, versions or logs, or leaves an activation plist that would start a failed upgrade at login.
- Upgrade order: the preflight makes no state change; the exit is confirmed before the snapshot; the snapshot is verified before re-rendering.
- Record validation on read and the handling of torn writes: record before activation, staging cleanup, and `rename` within `S` and `A`.
- The live harness's cleanup scope: it never bootouts outside the throwaway label and never acts on any process except a recorded owned pid.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- Readiness can reach a pass on this Mac only by accepting a check that reports `fail`, for example Codex login. That changes the readiness-pass contract and needs a decision; it is not a harness repair.

content.title: P3: Resolve claude from PATH instead of redistributing the SDK binary

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Run the Claude harness with the `claude` CLI found on the service's `PATH` instead of the Agent SDK's bundled platform binary, and report its version in readiness without gating it.

**Current behavior:**
The Claude runtime loads the Agent SDK without `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`, so each turn runs the platform binary package the SDK pulls in. Readiness checks the Claude token but not the CLI.

**Desired behavior:**
- The Claude runtime resolves `claude` by name from the service's fixed `PATH` (the same way Codex is resolved) and passes that absolute path to the SDK.
- Readiness reports whether `claude` was found and its version. Ensemble does not judge compatibility; an incompatible CLI surfaces as the SDK's turn-start failure.
- A missing `claude` makes only the Claude harness unavailable, with a clear readiness fix line; Codex and the service are unaffected.
- Qualification evidence records the `claude` version used.

**Key interfaces:**
- The Claude runtime's SDK `query()` options gain `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`.
- The readiness check set reports the Claude CLI alongside the existing Claude token check, following the existing Pass / Fail / Not configured shape with no paths or secrets in output.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Tests cover `claude` found (version reported, path passed to the SDK) and missing (Claude harness unavailable, readiness explains the fix, Codex unaffected).
- [ ] No version comparison or minimum is enforced.
- [ ] One bounded live Claude turn runs with the PATH-resolved `claude`, and its evidence records the version.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes.

**Out of scope:**
- Excluding the SDK platform packages from the release (#979).
- Installing, pinning or updating `claude`.
- API-key billing or other harness changes.

Decisions: ADR-1011. Parent: #978.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/981
**Planned against:** `main` at `a704f38fbadfcab2d04a93a03bf4f8a1a3503d90`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

One shared PATH resolver, `resolveOnPath`, replaces readiness's private `onPath` and also serves `ClaudeRuntime`. `ClaudeRuntime.start()` resolves `claude` once from the service `PATH`, rejects when it is absent, and passes the absolute path as `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` on both SDK `query()` calls. The existing secondary-runtime failure path then marks only the Claude harness unavailable. Readiness gains a `claude-executable` check, placed before `claude-token`, that runs `claude --version` and shows the version without comparing it. The ready-check and Getting started consumers, the docs and one disclosed limit follow. One bounded live turn uses the existing `scrub` facet of the `c5` harness, extended to record which `claude` it spawned and its version.

This plan implements the ADR-1011 contract as merged by #985 (`a704f38f`, which is `043b6340` plus that docs-only change; CI passed on it): Ensemble does not gate the CLI version, only the SDK's declared `claudeCodeVersion` is qualified, another version is a disclosed limit, and evidence records the version used.

### Guardrails

- No `claude` version comparison, minimum, allowlist or `claudeCodeVersion` read anywhere in `src/`. The only version logic is parse-and-display. A `claude` that cannot run `--version` is a runnable-ness failure, not a compatibility verdict.
- Never fall back to the SDK's bundled binary: both `sdk.query` call sites in `src/standalone/claude.ts` always carry `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`.
- A missing `claude` affects only the Claude harness. Codex and service start-up are unaffected. Claude stays optional (ADR-1008), so a Codex-only host must not show a red readiness row.
- Readiness output stays fixed literals with no paths and no secrets. The only dynamic text is the parsed version token in the Pass label. The version child gets `PATH` only as its environment. `src/standalone/readiness.ts` keeps no `*Sync(` call, which `test/readiness.test.ts` enforces by reading its source.
- Out of scope: excluding `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-*` from the release tree, `scripts/package-release.mjs`, `release.yml` and `package.json` `files` (#979 owns them; the issue body's third scope bullet is assigned to #979 by the Agent Brief); installing, pinning or updating `claude`; API-key billing; editing ADR-1011; a new `detail` field or any other change to `readinessCheckSchema`'s shape; Pen frames and `design/DESIGN.md`.
- Live validation is the one bounded Claude turn in T5: the `c5` `scrub` facet only, at most the harness's two attempts, one Claude turn each, no Codex turn. If the ledger refuses, stop and report. Never delete or edit the ledger, and never print the token.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs, including rebasing over #983 or #979, stay with the ticket owner and do not consume the plan-mismatch budget. Only a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption gets one diagnosis plus at most two repair cycles before the owner stops and returns a replan request. The seam and assumption claims in this plan are:
  - the SDK uses a supplied `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` and never resolves the bundled package;
  - a rejected `ClaudeRuntime.start()` leaves Codex and the service running with only Claude unavailable;
  - `claude --version` is a fast, model-free, credential-free probe;
  - the Homebrew `claude` behaves under SDK `0.3.296` as the bundled binary did.

  A failure of one of these four is a mismatch. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design or contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Resolve once per runtime start, not per turn.** `ClaudeRuntime` already reads the CLI's supported models once per start (`supported`, in `readSettings`), so a changed `claude` already needs a restart. A start-time rejection also gives the acceptance wording literally: `src/standalone/service.ts` (~1034–1052) turns a rejected non-default `start()` into `runtimeUnavailableSince`, so `harnessStatuses()` reports Claude `unavailable`, Codex stays `available`, and #983's `runtime-unavailable` wait and the Runtime harness readiness check follow without new code. Recovery is to install `claude` into the fixed PATH and restart the service, as for any unavailable runtime.
- **Pass the PATH entry, not its `realpath`.** `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` is a symlink into `Caskroom/claude-code@latest/<version>/claude`. A Homebrew upgrade changes the target directory, and the PATH entry stays valid.
- **The SDK honours the path (read in `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs` at 0.3.296).** It resolves the bundled platform package only when `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` is falsy. For a path not ending in `.js/.mjs/.ts/.tsx/.jsx` it hands that path to `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` as `options.command`, which is what `ClaudeRuntime.spawnChild` spawns.
- **Version shown in the Pass label, no schema change.** A Pass row cannot carry a reason or fix, and a `detail` field would change the strict operator contract, `web/src/readiness.tsx`, `src/cli/doctor.ts`, the Pen frames and surfaces #983 is editing. The label is rendered verbatim by Settings → Readiness and by `ensemble doctor`: `Claude executable (2.1.296)`. Fail and Not configured keep the stable label `Claude executable`. Measured at planning: `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin /opt/homebrew/bin/claude --version` exits 0 in about 15 ms, prints `2.1.296 (Claude Code)` and writes no files, even without `HOME`.
- **Not configured vs Fail.** A missing `claude` is `not-configured` when Claude is unused (no token reference and no active Claude profile) and `fail` otherwise, mirroring `claude-token`. A `profiles()` that throws counts as in use. A `claude` that is found but whose `--version` fails, times out or prints no version token is `fail`: found must mean runnable.
- **Check order and counts.** `claude-executable` goes immediately before `claude-token`, as Codex's executable precedes its login. The check count becomes eight, which changes the count asserted in `test/readiness.test.ts` (the title and two assertions) and `test/operator-readiness-browser.test.ts`.
- **Disclosed limit.** ADR-1011 says another version is a disclosed limit, so `claudePolicyLimits` gains one line. `src/operator/contracts.ts` `policyDisclosure.limits` allows 12 strings of at most 300 characters, and the list has 10 now.
- **Live turn through the existing harness.** `test/c5/live-journeys.mjs --facet scrub` is the repository's guarded one-Claude-turn harness (turn cap 4 min, attempt cap 20 min, ledger in the tmpdir, token from `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `~/.env`). On a dev tree the bundled binary is still installed, so absence cannot prove the PATH `claude` ran. `service-child.mjs` therefore wraps the SDK to record the `command` passed to `spawnClaudeCodeProcess`.
- **Only a live turn can test one assumption:** the Homebrew `claude` (here `2.1.296`, equal to the SDK's declared version) behaves under SDK `0.3.296` like the bundled binary, including the sandbox and the token scrub. T5 is the proof and the scrub disposition is the pass condition. A `residual-exposure` or `inconclusive` disposition on the PATH binary is a finding to return to the controller, not something to loosen or gate by version.
- **Entry points checked.** Settings → Readiness and `ensemble doctor` render any check (no edit). Project setup ready check: T3 (its `own` list is hard-coded). Getting started "Claude (optional)" row: T3, which needs #983. Task detail, Inbox and the CLI task waits: the unavailable harness yields #983's `runtime-unavailable` wait with the Open readiness check Fix (no edit). Add Claude and its `/api/operator/readiness/claude-token` read stay token-only (intentional gap). Pen frames and `design/DESIGN.md` list readiness rows as sample data and are not edited (gap, reported to the lead).

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/claude.ts` — `ClaudeRuntime.start()` imports the SDK and creates the generation. `readSettings()` (model-free settings read) and `startTurn()` are the only two `sdk.query` call sites and set no `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`. `spawnChild(options)` spawns `options.command`. `claudePolicyLimits` is the disclosed-limits list.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `createRuntime` builds `ClaudeRuntime`; the start loop (~1034) handles a rejected non-default `start()`; `harnessStatuses()` reports it.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/readiness.ts` — private `onPath(name, env)` returns a boolean (absolute PATH entries only, executable regular file, follows symlinks). `Readiness.check` is an exhaustive switch over `ReadinessCheckId`; `labels` and `fixes` are literals; `claudeTokenCheck` is the sibling to follow. `src/operator/readiness.ts` holds `readinessCheckIds`; `readinessSchema` requires `checks.length === readinessCheckIds.length` in that order.
- **Existing:** `web/src/setup-model.ts` `readyCheckItems` lists the Claude lead's readiness items from a hard-coded `own = ["claude-token"]`.
- **Existing (from open PR #983, absent from this base):** `web/src/getting-started-model.ts` `checklistRows` derives the "Claude (optional)" row from the `claude-token` check only. `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` needs no edit.
- **Existing tests:** `test/fixtures/claude-sdk.ts` `fakeSdk` records `queries` names only; `test/claude-runtime.test.ts` `fixture()` and `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts` (the `new ClaudeRuntime` at ~568 and `harnessFixture` at ~74) construct runtimes; `test/readiness.test.ts` `fixture()`/`deps()`/`check()`; `test/c5/service-child.mjs` `startJourneyService`; `test/c5/live-journeys.mjs`.
- **New:** `src/standalone/executable-path.ts` — `resolveOnPath(name, env): Promise<string | null>`, `onPath`'s body returning the candidate path (not `realpath`).
- **New:** `ClaudeRuntimeOptions.resolveExecutable?: () => Promise<string | null>` in `src/standalone/claude.ts`, defaulting to `resolveOnPath("claude", process.env)`; the runtime keeps the result in a private `executable`.
- **New:** `Readiness.claudeExecutable()` and `ReadinessDeps.versionTimeoutMs?` (default 5000) in `src/standalone/readiness.ts`.
- **Follow:** `sandboxSelfTest` and `captureProcessIdentity` in `ClaudeRuntimeOptions` for an injectable seam; `claudeTokenCheck` for the check's shape; `test/readiness.test.ts` for PATH fixtures.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3, T2 → T4, and T1, T3, T4 → T5. The graph is acyclic. T2 imports T1's new module, so T1 and T2 run in order. After T2, T3 and T4 touch disjoint files (T3: `web/`, the web tests and `docs/user-flows/getting-started.md`; T4: all other docs) and may run concurrently. T5 runs last, on the integrated candidate. The only shared-file overlap with other work is with #979 and #983 (see Review focus).

#### 1. ClaudeRuntime runs the PATH-resolved `claude`; a missing one fails start

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** new `src/standalone/executable-path.ts` (`resolveOnPath`); `src/standalone/claude.ts` (`ClaudeRuntimeOptions.resolveExecutable`, private `executable`, `start()`, `stop()`, `readSettings()`, `startTurn()` options, `claudePolicyLimits`); `test/fixtures/claude-sdk.ts` (`fakeSdk` also returns every query's `options` as `optionsSeen`); new `test/executable-path.test.ts`; `test/claude-runtime.test.ts`; `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- `test/executable-path.test.ts`, with temp directories `a` (non-executable `claude`, mode 0644), `b` (a `claude` symlink to an executable file in `c`) and `c`:
  - `PATH=a:b:c` returns the `b/claude` symlink path itself, not its target.
  - A directory named `claude`, a relative entry and an empty entry are skipped.
  - `{}` returns `null`.
- `test/claude-runtime.test.ts`: `fixture()` passes `resolveExecutable: async () => "/fixture/bin/claude"` by default and exposes `optionsSeen`.
  - After `start()` and one turn, the model-free settings read's options and the turn's options both have `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable === "/fixture/bin/claude"`. The resolver ran once across two turns.
  - `resolveExecutable: async () => null` makes `start()` reject with `Claude executable is not on the service PATH`.
  - The policy-limits test adds the pattern `/version the pinned SDK declares/`.
- `test/claude-runtime-service.test.ts`: a service whose factory returns a fake Codex runtime for `codex` and `new ClaudeRuntime({ ..., sdk, resolveExecutable: async () => null })` for `claude` (follow `harnessFixture`). `service.start()` resolves; `harnessStatuses()` gives `codex: available` and `claude: unavailable`. A control with `async () => "/fixture/bin/claude"` gives both `available`.
- Update the other `new ClaudeRuntime` call at ~568 of `claude-runtime-service.test.ts` to pass the fixture resolver, so CI hosts without `claude` still start it.
**Implementation:**
- `resolveOnPath` is `onPath`'s loop (absolute entries only, `stat().isFile()`, `access(X_OK)`) returning `join(directory, name)` or `null`.
- `start()` first runs `const executable = await (this.options.resolveExecutable ?? (() => resolveOnPath("claude", process.env)))()`. It throws `new Error("Claude executable is not on the service PATH")` when that is `null`, before the config directory is created, and stores the path. `stop()` clears it.
- `readSettings()` and `startTurn()` read `this.executable` beside `this.sdk`, throw `Runtime stopped` when it is unset (`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` forbids passing `undefined`), and add `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable: executable` to their `Options`.
- Append to `claudePolicyLimits`: `Only the Claude Code version the pinned SDK declares was qualified. The installed claude is not version-checked, and another version may enforce the sandbox, tool and permission controls differently.` (under 300 characters).
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/executable-path.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime.test.js dist/test/claude-runtime-service.test.js dist/test/execution-harness.test.js`; expect all tests to pass. At planning, these three existing files plus `readiness.test.js` passed 63 tests on the base.
**Complete when:** Both queries carry the path, a null resolver rejects `start()`, a service with a null resolver starts with Claude unavailable and Codex available, and `rg -n "claudeCodeVersion" src` has no match.

#### 2. Readiness reports the `claude` found and its version, without gating

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1's `resolveOnPath`.
**Files and symbols:** `src/operator/readiness.ts` (`readinessCheckIds` gains `"claude-executable"` before `"claude-token"`; the "seven" comment becomes "eight"); `src/standalone/readiness.ts` (import `resolveOnPath`, delete `onPath`, use it in `executable()`; `labels`, `fixes`, `check()` switch, new `claudeExecutable()`, `ReadinessDeps.versionTimeoutMs`, class comment); `test/readiness.test.ts`; `test/operator-readiness-browser.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- `test/readiness.test.ts`: `fixture()` stays without `claude`; a helper writes `bin/claude` as `#!/bin/sh` with a chosen body. The `7` becomes `8` at the test title ~452, ~494 and ~503, and in `test/operator-readiness-browser.test.ts` ~84. `claude-executable` is immediately before `claude-token` in the order assertion.
- New cases:
  - **Found:** the body echoes `2.1.296 (Claude Code)`. Status is `pass`, reason and fix are `null`, label is `Claude executable (2.1.296)`, and the serialized result contains no path (not `f.bin`).
  - **No gate:** bodies echoing `0.0.1 (Claude Code)` and `99.9.9` both pass with that version in the label.
  - **Missing, unused:** default deps give `not-configured`, label `Claude executable`, reason `Claude Code is not on the service PATH`, fix `Install Claude Code into the fixed PATH, then restart the service`.
  - **Missing, in use:** each of `claudeTokenReference: () => "file:/x"` and `profiles(claudeProfile)` gives `fail` with the same strings. A throwing `profiles()` also gives `fail`.
  - **Unrunnable:** bodies that print `hello`, exit 1, or `exec sleep 30` with `versionTimeoutMs: 200` all give `fail`, reason `Claude Code did not report a version`, fix ``Run `claude --version` as the service user, or reinstall Claude Code, then restart the service``.
  - **Environment:** with `env: { PATH: f.bin, CANARY_READINESS_VARIABLE_4417: "x" }`, the body writes `${CANARY_READINESS_VARIABLE_4417-unset}` to a file whose path is baked into the script. The file reads `unset`.
- The existing "running the checks changes nothing on disk and leaks no canary" and "a throwing dependency fails that check only" tests must still pass.
**Implementation:** `claudeExecutable()`:
1. `const path = await resolveOnPath("claude", env)`.
2. Compute in-use as `claudeTokenReference() !== null` or any non-revoked `claude` profile (a `profiles()` that throws counts as in use).
3. When `path` is null, return `outcome(id, inUse ? "fail" : "not-configured", ...)` with the strings above.
4. Otherwise run `execFile(path, ["--version"], { env: { PATH: env.PATH ?? "" }, timeout: versionTimeoutMs ?? 5000, maxBuffer: 4096 })` through `util.promisify` or a callback wrapper. Take the first whitespace token of the first stdout line and require `/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+[0-9A-Za-z.+-]{0,32}$/`.
5. On success return `{ ...pass(id), label: `${labels[id]} (${version})` }`; on any failure return the unrunnable `fail`.

Never spread the service environment into the child. Update the class comment: no model turn, and the only spawn is the bounded `--version` probe.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/readiness.test.js dist/test/readiness-http.test.js dist/test/operator-cli-doctor.test.js`; expect all tests to pass. Then run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-readiness-browser.test.js`; expect it to pass (needs `npx playwright install chromium webkit`, as in CI).
**Complete when:** All eight checks parse with the shared schema, the found, no-gate, missing (both statuses) and unrunnable cases pass, and no output carries a path or the canary.

#### 3. Project setup and Getting started surface the check

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2's check id. Part B also needs #983 merged into the branch base (see Review focus).
**Files and symbols:**
- Part A: `web/src/setup-model.ts` (`readyCheckItems`, the Claude branch of `own`); `test/operator-setup-model.test.ts`; `test/operator-setup-browser.test.ts`.
- Part B: `web/src/getting-started-model.ts` (`checklistRows`, the `claude` row); `test/operator-getting-started-model.test.ts`; `docs/user-flows/getting-started.md`.

**Test:**
- Part A, `operator-setup-model.test.ts`: a Claude lead with `claude-executable` failing yields `{ text: "claude-executable reason", fix: "claude-executable fix" }` with no link, and the `claude-token` item keeps its Add Claude link. A Codex lead ignores `claude-executable`. Follow the existing `claude-token` cases at ~368–390.
- Part A, `operator-setup-browser.test.ts`: `stubReadiness(page, { "claude-executable": "fail" })` for a Claude lead shows `claude-executable fix` in the ready check. Follow the `claude-token` case at ~965–975.
- Part B, `operator-getting-started-model.test.ts`: `claude-executable: fail` makes the Claude row `attention` with that check's reason, even when `claude-token` passes. With the token not configured and the executable `not-configured` the row stays `optional`. With both passing it stays `done`.

**Implementation:**
- Part A: `own` becomes `["claude-executable", "claude-token"]` for a Claude lead, keeping the Add Claude link only on `claude-token`.
- Part B: in the `claude` row, if either check has `status === "fail"` the row is `attention` with that check's `reason` as detail; otherwise the existing token logic is unchanged.
- Part B row description in `getting-started.md`: "A Claude token reference is readable and `claude` is on the service PATH".

**Validate:** From the repository root, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator-setup-model.test.js dist/test/operator-setup-browser.test.js dist/test/operator-getting-started-model.test.js`; expect all tests to pass.
**Complete when:** A failing `claude-executable` appears in the project-setup ready check for a Claude lead and turns the Getting started Claude row to attention.

#### 4. Documentation

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2's strings and behaviour.
**Files and symbols:**
- `docs/user-flows/readiness-check.md`: a Claude executable row before Claude token; Pass is "`claude` resolves on the service `PATH`; the label shows its version"; Not configured when Claude is unused; the fix line; a note that the version is reported and never compared.
- `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md`: the fixed-PATH paragraph (~75–82) says `ClaudeRuntime` resolves `claude` from the same `PATH` once at start. A host whose Claude is outside it, such as the native installer's `~/.local/bin`, needs Homebrew or a reviewed renderer change. The readiness list (~86) adds the Claude executable. The Claude section (~224–258) says to install `claude` and restart the service after installing or upgrading it. It states that readiness reports the version but does not gate it, that only the SDK-declared `claudeCodeVersion` is qualified, and that any other version is a disclosed limit.
- `docs/SPEC.md`: one sentence in the Claude runtime paragraph (~585–600) with the same contract.
- `docs/user-flows/project-setup.md` (~35): the ready check also lists "`claude` not found for a Claude lead".
- `README.md`: the Claude runtime bullet notes that it runs the `claude` on the service PATH.
- If #979's text is already on main, remove its "Claude is unavailable until #981" disclosure from `standalone-macos.md`. If it is absent, add nothing.

Do not edit `docs/adr/1011-*`, which #985 settled, `docs/user-flows/getting-started.md` (T3), or `design/DESIGN.md`. Revise in place; no dated sections.
**Validate:** From the repository root, run `rg -n "Claude executable" docs README.md --glob '!docs/evidence/**'`, which must match `readiness-check.md`, `standalone-macos.md` and `project-setup.md`. Run `rg -n "exact CLI version|claude-agent-sdk" docs README.md --glob '!docs/evidence/**' --glob '!docs/adr/1011*'`, which must match nothing unless #979's release text is already on main.
**Complete when:** The docs describe the PATH-resolved, ungated `claude` as the current contract, with the restart and fixed-PATH requirements.

#### 5. One bounded live Claude turn with the PATH-resolved `claude`

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T1, T3, T4`
**Prerequisites:** `npm run build:service` done; `claude` on PATH (this Mac: `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude`, `2.1.296`); a Claude token in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `~/.env`; the Codex launcher at `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex` (present at planning). Run on the integrated candidate.
**Files and symbols:** `test/c5/service-child.mjs` (export `recordClaudeSpawns(sdk, observed)` and build the Claude runtime with it in `startJourneyService`); `test/c5/live-journeys.mjs` (`evidence.claudeCli`); `test/c5-live-harness.test.ts`; new `docs/evidence/981-claude-path-<run date>.md` plus the redacted stdout JSON beside it, following `docs/evidence/issue-827-claude-journeys-2026-10-12.md`.
**Test:** In `test/c5-live-harness.test.ts`, a fake SDK driven through the new wrapper records the `command` passed to `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` and the `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` it received. It also shows that the wrapper forwards the original callback unchanged.
**Implementation:**
- In `startJourneyService`, for `harness === "claude"` construct `new ClaudeRuntime({ safety: context.safety, claude: context.claude, sdk })` from `dist/src/standalone/claude.js`. `recordClaudeSpawns` returns the real SDK with a `query` that replaces `options.spawnClaudeCodeProcess` by a function that pushes `o.command` onto `observed.claudeSpawns` and then calls the original.
- Before the attempt opens, `live-journeys.mjs` refuses when `resolveOnPath("claude", process.env)` (from `dist/src/standalone/executable-path.js`) is null. In `inProcess`, after `run(...)` returns, it records `evidence.claudeCli`:
  - `version`: the first line of `<spawned command> --version`;
  - `sdkDeclared`: `sdkPackage.claudeCodeVersion`;
  - `fromPath`: the spawned command equals `resolveOnPath("claude", process.env)`, using `dist/src/standalone/executable-path.js`;
  - `bundled`: the command contains `claude-agent-sdk-`;
  - the executable directory with `homedir()` replaced by `~`, because the harness leak scan rejects the home path.
- Fail the attempt as a harness failure unless `fromPath` is true, `bundled` is false and at least one spawn was recorded.
- Run once, then at most once more only for a harness defect: `npm run c5:live -- --live --facet scrub > <scratch>/981-scrub.json`.
- Write the evidence document: candidate SHA, `claude` and SDK versions, the command's PATH provenance, the scrub disposition, ledger totals, and the leak-scan result. Include the limit that only a live scrub run on `2.1.296` is evidence for that version.

**Validate:** From the repository root: `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/c5-live-harness.test.js`, then the live command above. Expect exit 0, `outcome: "passed"`, `observations.disposition: "qualified"`, `startTurn.turns: 1`, `claudeCli.fromPath: true`, `claudeCli.bundled: false`, `claudeCli.version` starting `2.1.296`, a clean leak scan and every `processes[].verification` equal to `verified`.
**Complete when:** The evidence file records the PATH-resolved `claude` version for a passed one-turn run.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `claude` found: version reported | 2 | T2 found case, label `Claude executable (2.1.296)` |
| `claude` found: path passed to the SDK | 1 | T1 asserts `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` on the settings read and on the turn |
| `claude` missing: Claude harness unavailable, Codex unaffected | 1 | T1 service test: `claude: unavailable`, `codex: available`, service started |
| `claude` missing: readiness explains the fix | 2 | T2 missing cases, reason and fix strings; Not configured when unused, Fail when in use |
| No version comparison or minimum | 1, 2 | T2 `0.0.1` and `99.9.9` pass; T1 `rg "claudeCodeVersion" src` empty |
| One bounded live turn with the PATH-resolved `claude`, evidence records the version | 5 | T5 live run and `docs/evidence/981-claude-path-*.md` |
| Other versions are a disclosed limit (ADR-1011) | 1, 4 | T1 policy-limits pattern; T4 docs |
| Entry points: setup ready check and Getting started | 3 | T3 model and browser tests |
| `npm run check` passes | all | Final validation |
| Excluding SDK platform packages from the release | not in scope | #979 |

### Final validation

- From the repository root, on the integrated delivery candidate (after rebasing onto current `origin/main`, with #983 merged first), run `npm ci && npm run check`; expect exit 0. The `check` and `check-node-26` CI jobs run the same command on the PR.
- The T5 live run is one-shot. If later commits change `src/standalone/claude.ts`, `src/standalone/executable-path.ts` or the c5 files, rerun only if the harness allowance remains; otherwise record the drift in the evidence file and delivery record.
- Not claimed: a launchd-installed Claude turn with the PATH `claude` (the live run is outside launchd, as in the #827 evidence), and any `claude` version other than the one recorded in T5.

### Review focus

- Both `sdk.query` sites pass the path, and nothing can reach the bundled binary.
- The readiness output: literal strings only, the parsed version token as the sole dynamic text, a `PATH`-only child environment, and no `*Sync(` call.
- No version comparison anywhere, and Not configured vs Fail for a missing `claude` on a Codex-only host.
- Overlap, resolved as routine rebases:
  - #983 adds `web/src/getting-started-model.ts` and edits `docs/SPEC.md` and the user-flow docs. It does not touch `src/standalone/readiness.ts` or `src/operator/readiness.ts`. Merge #983 before this PR. If it has not merged when the other slices are done, hold T3 Part B and tell the controller rather than editing #983's branch.
  - #979 edits `docs/operations/standalone-macos.md` (the "Local stable build" section and a Claude-unavailable limit) and `README.md`'s Packaging bullet. Hunks are disjoint. Whichever PR merges second removes that limit sentence.
  - #985 is merged (`a704f38f`). The ADR text this plan consumes is on main.
