content.title: Power admission can still be held when reading the pmset log takes longer than 10 s

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Keep power admission working when `pmset -g log` takes longer than the 10 s read timeout, without weakening completeness or cursor guarantees.

**Current behavior and verification:** `MacPowerEventSource` (`src/standalone/power.ts`) runs `pmset -g log` and kills it after `timeoutMs` (default 10 000). A killed read is incomplete, so `ExecutionPower` holds admission. On this macOS 27.0.1 host the log is ~41 MB; bounded live reads during #1000 took 9.1–9.8 s idle and timed out at 10.0 s under load, completing in 9.4–13.4 s with `PMSET_TIMEOUT_MS=60000` (PR #1011 body). The parser fix from #1000/#1011 is on main at 325304ce.

**Desired behavior:** A baseline and follow-up read complete on a loaded Mac with a large log. Prefer reducing the work (e.g. reading only output after the persisted cursor) over simply raising the timeout; if the timeout changes, keep it bounded and justified by measurement. Keep reads off the coordinating event loop as today.

**Key interfaces:** `MacPowerEventSource` read options and streaming parser, persisted cursor format (`pmset-time`/`pmset-event` with whole-output line indices, including the legacy-cursor fallback from PR #1011), `ExecutionPower` hold reasons.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Bounded live check on macOS 27 with a ~40 MB log under concurrent load: baseline and follow-up reads complete; record timings in the PR.
- [ ] Existing cursors (including pre-27 legacy cursors) still resolve; unknown/missing cursors still fail closed.
- [ ] A timed-out read is distinguishable from a parse failure in the hold reason or diagnostics.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the new read path; run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing power-supervision policy, persisting state across a missing event cursor (no re-baseline path today), non-macOS power sources.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1022
**Planned against:** `main` at `93b52c00b9f208c75120de0629da5f2556ff4b78`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null
**Planned branch:** `cb/issue-1022-pmset-read-timeout`

### Approach

Replace the single 10 s wall-clock kill in `spawnPowerLogReader` with a **progress-based streaming deadline**: kill `pmset` only when stdout makes no progress for 10 s (idle bound) or the whole read exceeds a hard 60 s ceiling, and surface either as a typed `PowerLogReadTimeout` error. `ExecutionPower` maps that error to its own hold reasons, so a slow or stalled read is distinguishable from a parse failure ("incomplete or ambiguous"). Admission freshness (`observedForAdmission`) is measured from poll completion instead of poll start, so a read longer than 15 s does not leave admission permanently unobserved. Parsing, cursor format and whole-output line-index semantics are unchanged.

### Guardrails

- Cursor contract unchanged: `pmset-time:<ms>` and `pmset-event:<ms>:<lineIndex>:<hash>` with whole-output line indices, the PR #1011 legacy (pre-macOS 27) cursor fallback, and fail-closed rejection of unknown/missing/unusable cursors. `createPmsetParser` and `parsePmsetPowerLog` are not edited.
- Completeness guarantee unchanged: any killed, over-long-line, non-zero-exit or reader-error read never yields `complete: true`; the child is always killed on early exit. Reads stay in a child process streamed off the event loop.
- Both read bounds stay finite positive integers validated in the `MacPowerEventSource` constructor (idle ≤ total).
- `observedForAdmission` keeps its safety condition: only a poll that *started* after the last execution ended counts; a failed poll never refreshes it.
- Out of scope: power-supervision policy changes beyond the freshness anchor below, re-baselining after a lost cursor, non-macOS sources, reading only output after the cursor, committing a live harness.
- **Plan-mismatch budget:** a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (e.g. `pmset` does not stream progressively, `observedForAdmission` is not the only freshness consumer, the persisted cursor contract differs from `src/standalone/power.ts` at the base) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before stopping for a replan. Ordinary implementation, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs (type errors, failing assertions, flaky timing margins in new tests, lint/format, updating the existing "10 second timeout" and "timeout makes the batch incomplete" tests) stay with the ticket owner and do not count against that budget.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Chosen approach: progress-based streaming deadline (idle 10 s, ceiling 60 s).** Evidence from one timed read during planning (2026-10-16 12:12 BST, this macOS 27.0.1 host, 1-min load average 6.33): `/usr/bin/pmset -g log | wc -lc` took **12.14 s real / 11.28 s user / 0.72 s sys** for **239,355 lines / 54,976,963 bytes**; the log has grown from ~41 MB at #1000. A preceding planning read was terminated by SIGPIPE at 1.05 s after its consumer had already received the first line, so `pmset` emits output early rather than only at exit.
  - *Tail-after-cursor rejected:* `pmset -g log` has no since/offset option and the cost is `pmset`'s own CPU (11.3 s user) generating the full output, not Ensemble's parsing; line-index cursors also require counting every line from the start. Skipping lines Ensemble-side saves nothing measurable.
  - *Raised fixed timeout rejected as the sole fix:* the log grows (~41 → ~55 MB) and load varies, so any fixed wall-clock budget is a moving target; a stall is indistinguishable from slow progress.
  - *Progress deadline:* a live but slow `pmset` keeps resetting the 10 s idle bound; a hung one is killed within 10 s of its last output. The 60 s ceiling equals the maximum allowed power poll interval (`service.ts` rejects >60 000 ms), keeps the read bounded, and is ~5x the measured loaded read.
- **Proof gate T1:** progressive streaming under load is only partly evidenced (first-line-early). T1 measures the maximum stdout inter-chunk gap on this host under load before dependent code relies on it.
- **Distinguishable slow read:** `spawnPowerLogReader` throws an exported `PowerLogReadTimeout` (with `kind: "idle" | "total"`) when it kills on either bound; `MacPowerEventSource.readSince` rethrows it (all other failures still return `complete: false`). `ExecutionPower` maps it to `"Power-event history read timed out"` (initial read) and `"Power-event advancement read timed out"` (post-reconciliation re-read); other thrown errors keep `"…is unavailable"`, invalid/incomplete batches keep `"…incomplete or ambiguous"`. The operator UI already shows the supervisor's hold reason verbatim (docs/SPEC.md power-hold wait), so no UI mapping change is needed.
- **Freshness anchor:** today `observedForAdmission` requires `now - pollStartedAt < 15 s`; a read of 15 s or more would make every admission attempt re-poll (`service.ts` `pollPowerThenWake`) without ever being observed — a livelock that defeats acceptance criterion 1 on this host. Record completion time and require `now - pollCompletedAt < 15 s` while keeping `pollStartedAt > lastEndedAt`. This preserves the R03 contract (a sleep/wake during a finished turn is observed before more admission) and only changes the staleness clock.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/power.ts` — `spawnPowerLogReader(command, args, { timeoutMs, maxLineBytes })` kills the child with one `setTimeout(..., timeoutMs)`; a kill surfaces as a generic `"exited (SIGKILL)"` rejection. `MacPowerEventSource(readLog = spawnPowerLogReader, timeoutMs = 10_000, maxLineBytes = 64 KiB, now)` streams lines into `createPmsetParser` and catches every error into `{ complete: false }`. `ExecutionPower.pollUnlocked` holds with "Power-event history is unavailable" on throw and "…incomplete or ambiguous" on invalid/incomplete batch; the advancement loop uses "Power-event advancement is unavailable"/"…incomplete or ambiguous". `ExecutionPower.poll` records `observedPollStartedAt`; `observedForAdmission(now)` checks start-after-end and 15 s age from start.
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — constructs `new MacPowerEventSource()` with defaults (line ~1108), awaits one poll at startup, polls every ≤60 s, and gates admission on `power.observedForAdmission()` (line ~4802) with `pollPowerThenWake`.
- **Existing tests:** `test/operations/power.test.ts` — `PowerLogReader` type mirror (line ~68), "admission observation needs a completed poll started after the last execution ended" (227), the legacy-cursor test (1008), streamed-parity tests (901, 980), "an over-long line, a timeout, a failing exit or a reader error…" (1198), "the pmset source defaults to a 10 second timeout and 64 KiB lines" (1249). `test/operations/power-service.test.ts` covers service admission waits.
- **New:** `PowerLogReadTimeout` (exported from `src/standalone/power.ts`); reader options gain `idleTimeoutMs`; `ExecutionPower` gains a completion timestamp.
- **Follow:** `test/operations/power.test.ts` `printLines` + `spawnPowerLogReader(process.execPath, …)` for child-process reader tests, and the pid-file liveness check in the 1198 test for "child stopped".

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 → T4, acyclic. T2 and T3 both edit `src/standalone/power.ts` and `test/operations/power.test.ts`, so they are sequential; T4 needs the integrated build. No tasks run concurrently.

#### 1. Proof: `pmset` streams progressively under load

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:** none committed. A scratch Node script outside the repository (session scratchpad) that spawns `/usr/bin/pmset -g log` with stdout piped and records time to first byte, maximum gap between stdout chunks, total time, bytes and lines; started while CPU load runs (see Live qualification setup).
**Implementation:** Hypothesis: under concurrent load `pmset` writes stdout continuously, with every inter-chunk gap well under the 10 s idle bound. Pass: the read exits 0 and the maximum inter-chunk gap is ≤ 2.5 s. Fail: any gap > 2.5 s, or output arrives only at exit → stop dependent work and request a replan (the progress deadline would not protect against a slow-but-healthy read). This counts as live read 1 of the budget below.
**Validate:** From the session scratchpad, run `node pmset-progress.mjs` under load; expect JSON with `exitCode: 0`, `maxGapMs ≤ 2500`, `bytes ≥ 40_000_000`, recorded `firstByteMs`, `totalMs`, `loadavg`.
**Complete when:** The JSON result is recorded in the delivery record (PR body) and passes.

#### 2. Progress-based reader with typed timeout

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 passed.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/power.ts` — `PowerLogReader` options `{ timeoutMs, idleTimeoutMs, maxLineBytes }`, `spawnPowerLogReader`, new exported `PowerLogReadTimeout`, `MacPowerEventSource` constructor and `readSince`. `test/operations/power.test.ts` — `PowerLogReader` type mirror and module exports.
**Test:** In `test/operations/power.test.ts`, using `spawnPowerLogReader(process.execPath, ["-e", script], options)`:
- *Slow but progressing:* child writes `pmsetRows` one line every 300 ms (total > idle bound) with `idleTimeoutMs: 1000, timeoutMs: 10_000`; `readSince(null)` then `readSince(baseline.cursor)` are `complete: true` and deep-equal `parsePmsetPowerLog(text, baseline.cursor)`; a legacy cursor from the existing 1008 fixture resolves through the same slow reader to the same events as the exact cursor.
- *Stalled:* child writes one row then idles (the existing `hang` script) with `idleTimeoutMs: 500`; `readSince` rejects with `PowerLogReadTimeout` `kind: "idle"` and the pid-file child is gone (ESRCH).
- *Ceiling:* child writes a valid row every 50 ms forever with `idleTimeoutMs: 500, timeoutMs: 1000`; rejects with `kind: "total"`, child stopped.
- Update the 1198 test: the timeout case now expects `PowerLogReadTimeout`; over-long line, non-zero exit and reader error still return `complete: false` (no throw). An unusable or unknown cursor and a malformed log still return `complete: false`.
- Update the 1249 defaults test to `{ timeoutMs: 60_000, idleTimeoutMs: 10_000, maxLineBytes: 65_536 }`; constructor rejects non-positive/non-integer bounds and `idleTimeoutMs > timeoutMs`.
**Implementation:** Reset an idle timer on each stdout chunk; a separate total timer. On either firing, record the kind and `SIGKILL` the child; after the stream ends, throw `PowerLogReadTimeout(kind)` instead of the generic exit error. Keep the existing `finally` kill and line-limit checks. In `readSince`, rethrow `PowerLogReadTimeout`; keep returning `{ complete: false }` for every other error.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operations/power.test.js`; expect all tests pass, including the new slow/stalled/ceiling cases and the unchanged legacy-cursor and parity tests.
**Complete when:** The reader enforces both bounds, timeouts are typed, and the focused suite passes.

#### 3. Distinct hold reasons and completion-anchored freshness

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 complete.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/power.ts` — `ExecutionPower.pollUnlocked` catch blocks (initial read and advancement loop), `poll`, `observedForAdmission` and its doc comment. `test/operations/power.test.ts`.
**Test:**
- `FakePowerEvents.readSince` throwing `new PowerLogReadTimeout("idle")` → after `poll()`, `status().admissionReason === "Power-event history read timed out"` and admission is held; a generic thrown `Error` still gives "Power-event history is unavailable"; `complete: false` still gives "Power-event history is incomplete or ambiguous". The same split for the advancement re-read after a sleep/wake ("Power-event advancement read timed out" vs "…unavailable").
- Update the 227 test: a poll whose read takes 20 000 ms of mocked clock (gate the fake read, advance `clock`) is observed immediately after completion, still observed at `completedAt + 14_999`, stale at `completedAt + 15_000`; a poll started before the last execution ended is still not observed; a failed poll still does not refresh; a backwards clock is stale.
**Implementation:** Add the `instanceof PowerLogReadTimeout` branches. Record `observedPollCompletedAt` alongside the existing start time on successful completion and measure age from it.
**Validate:** From the repository root run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/operations/power.test.js dist/test/operations/power-service.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Slow-read holds are distinguishable from parse failures and freshness is anchored on completion, with focused tests green.

#### 4. Live qualification on this host

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 complete; `npm run build:service` from the branch head.
**Files and symbols:** none committed. Scratch harness outside the repository importing the built `dist/src/standalone/power.js` `MacPowerEventSource` with **production defaults** (no overrides).
**Implementation:** Under load, call `readSince(null)` (baseline) then `readSince(baseline.cursor)` (follow-up), timing each with `performance.now()`; record results as JSON in the PR body. See Live qualification contract.
**Validate:** From the session scratchpad run `node pmset-qualify.mjs`; expect the pass conditions below.
**Complete when:** A passing JSON record with timings is in the PR body.

### Live qualification contract

- **Host and setup:** this Mac, `sw_vers -productVersion` 27.x, `pmset -g log` ≥ 40 MB (bytes measured by T1). Load: the harness starts one busy-loop Node child per logical CPU (`os.availableParallelism()`), records their PIDs, starts reads after 3 s, and terminates exactly those PIDs (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) in `finally`. Record 1-minute load average before the first read and after the last. Reading `pmset -g log` is read-only; no `pmset` setting is changed and no sleep is forced.
- **Pass (acceptance criterion 1):** baseline returns `complete: true` with a `pmset-time:` cursor; the follow-up from that cursor returns `complete: true`, `fromCursor` equal to the baseline cursor and a valid event chain; neither throws; each read's seconds, the load averages, macOS version and log size are recorded. A read over 10 s that completes is a pass (that is the regression being fixed).
- **Read budget:** at most **6** live `pmset -g log` reads for the whole delivery: T1 uses 1 (one repeat only if the harness itself failed before `pmset` finished); T4 uses 2 per attempt, with one repeat attempt allowed only for a harness/setup defect. A `PowerLogReadTimeout` or `complete: false` from T4 under production defaults is a demonstrated failure: record it, stop, and report a replan trigger — do not tune bounds and re-run.
- Legacy-cursor resolution is covered by unit tests only (this host has no pre-27 layout or persisted event cursor), as in PR #1011.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Baseline and follow-up reads complete on macOS 27 with a ~40 MB log under concurrent load, timings recorded | 1, 4 | T1 progress JSON; T4 qualification JSON in PR body |
| Persisted cursors (including pre-27 legacy) still resolve; missing/unknown cursor fails closed | 2 | Legacy cursor through slow reader; unchanged 1008/980/901 tests; unusable cursor → `complete: false` |
| A slow read is distinguishable from a parse failure in the hold reason or logs | 2, 3 | `PowerLogReadTimeout` kinds; "read timed out" vs "incomplete or ambiguous" hold-reason tests |
| Unit tests cover the new read path; pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check` | 2, 3 | Focused suites; Final validation |

content.title: Treat a later closure as provider closure after an Ensemble-closed issue reopens

nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Decision

Recorded by the maintainer during triage: **once an issue that Ensemble closed through its own delivery is reopened, Ensemble's own-closure record is superseded; a later closure of that issue is a provider (GitHub) closure.** SPEC must be updated to say so.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug  
**Summary:** Supersede Ensemble's own-closure record when the issue reopens, and stop misclassifying later closures.

**Current behavior and verification:** `github_delivery_closures` keeps one row per node that nothing invalidates (`src/core/github-source.ts`). `reconcileOwnDeliveryClosures` (`src/standalone/service.ts`) runs before every GitHub sync for every task whose delivery owns a confirmed closure: while reopened, `inspectOwnClosure` fails and `recordDeliveryClosureUnavailable` sets a `closure-read-unavailable` hold; a PR-merge own closure followed by an independent re-close yields `provider-closure-attribution-unproved`, handled as a transient read failure; an `issue.close` own closure followed by an independent re-close is re-recorded as Ensemble's own because `inspectClosedIssue` (`src/standalone/github-delivery.ts`) doesn't check attribution. Under "Treat closure as Done" (#1006) such tasks never complete. All paths currently fail safe. Evidence: PR #1016 threads 4277278316 and 4277188259.

**Desired behavior:** When reconciliation observes the issue open after Ensemble's own closure, mark that own-closure record superseded (keep audit history). Superseded records are ignored by own-closure reconciliation, `hasOwnDeliveryClosure`, the closure-hold branch in `updateReadiness` and the Done-mode finalizer. A later closure is provider closure. A deterministic attribution-unproved result gets an explained state instead of the transient `closure-read-unavailable` hold. `issue.close` reconciliation never re-attributes a closure it didn't make.

**Key interfaces:** `github_delivery_closures`, `recordDeliveryClosure`, `recordDeliveryClosureUnavailable`, `hasOwnDeliveryClosure`, `reconcileOwnDeliveryClosures`, `inspectOwnClosure`/`inspectClosedIssue`, `providerClosure`, `completeFromProviderClosure`, SPEC closure sections (~195, 219–221, 501–502).

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Own closure → reopen → independent close: treated as provider closure; under Done mode completes once settled; under Skip keeps a `closed` hold.
- [ ] Own closure with no reopen never becomes provider-completed.
- [ ] Attribution-unproved is not a transient read failure and shows an explained state on web, HTML and CLI.
- [ ] `issue.close` own-closure reconciliation does not re-attribute an independent re-close.
- [ ] Migration keeps existing records valid; no audit history deleted. SPEC documents the rule. Run pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check`.

**Out of scope:** Changing Skip/Done mode semantics beyond this rule, delivery action history, PR completion detection.

<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1023
**Planned against:** `main` at `93b52c00b9f208c75120de0629da5f2556ff4b78`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null
**Planned branch:** `cb/issue-1023-reopened-closure-attribution`

### Approach

Record supersession of an own-delivery closure append-only, keyed by the closing delivery operation, and make every own-closure predicate ignore superseded operations so a later closure follows the existing provider-closure path (closure hold, then Done-mode completion once settled). Reconciliation classifies each fresh provider inspection as reopened (supersede), proved (record and pin the GitHub ClosedEvent), attribution-unproved (new explained hold `closure-attribution-unproved`, surfaced as closure state `unattributed`) or a read failure (the existing transient `closure-read-unavailable`).

### Guardrails

- Source authority: the maintainer Decision and Agent Brief on #1023 (https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1023#issuecomment-6188924750). Once an issue Ensemble closed through its own delivery is reopened, that own-closure record is superseded; a later closure is provider closure.
- Persistence is additive only. Never delete or rewrite `delivery_actions`, existing `github_delivery_closures` rows or supersession rows. Existing closure rows stay valid as effective (unsuperseded) own closures.
- Fail safe as today: an own closure that is not superseded is never provider-completed; a read failure keeps `closure-read-unavailable`; supersession never clears `changed-text`, `readiness-lost` or `withdrawn` holds, and never resolves uncertain execution.
- Out of scope (from the brief): Skip/Done mode semantics beyond this rule, delivery action history and its receipts, PR completion detection, the explicit-close read/write race already documented in SPEC.
- Ownership: no edits to `src/standalone/power.ts` or power supervision (#1022 owns them).
- Repair budget. A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (a named symbol, table, call flow, fixture seam or command in this plan proves false) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; record the finding in the delivery record, then stop and request a replan if unresolved. Ordinary implementation, test, fixture, documentation, formatting and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume that budget. Continue routine corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap; stop for material design/contract changes or exhausted grants.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Supersession persistence (no maintainer decision needed).** Add `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS github_delivery_closure_supersessions (nodeId TEXT NOT NULL, operationId TEXT NOT NULL, supersededAt TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(nodeId, operationId))` and a guarded nullable `ALTER TABLE github_delivery_closures ADD COLUMN closedEventId TEXT` in `GitHubSourceStore.migrate`, following the existing `skippedClosedNodeIds` guard. Both are additive; no row is rewritten or deleted, legacy rows keep `closedEventId` NULL and remain effective, which satisfies the brief's "migration keeps existing records valid; no audit history deleted". Keying by `operationId` (not only `nodeId`) keeps a later genuine Ensemble re-close (a new confirmed operation) effective. A separate table rather than a flag on `github_delivery_closures` is chosen because a reopen can be observed before any closure row exists (proof never succeeded) and because `recordDeliveryClosure` upserts by `nodeId`, which would erase the audit fact.
- **Effective own closure.** An own closure is effective only for a confirmed closing operation with no supersession row. One predicate in `DeliveryStore` (`src/core/delivery.ts`) selects that operation (`ownClosureOperation(taskId, nodeId)`, using the existing `ownsConfirmedClosure` receipt rules and excluding superseded operation IDs, guarded by a `sqlite_master` check as `DomainStore.hasOwnDeliveryClosure` does); `ownsConfirmedClosure` becomes `!!ownClosureOperation(...)` and `DeliveryCoordinator.inspectOwnClosure` uses the same selection instead of its looser `.find`. SQL that tests `github_delivery_closures` presence (`completeFromProviderClosure`, the closure-hold branch in `updateReadiness`, `hasOwnDeliveryClosure`) counts only rows whose `operationId` has no supersession row. `src/core/delivery.ts` already reads `github_*` tables, so this cross-table read follows precedent.
- **Reopen evidence.** A fresh provider read showing the issue open supersedes. A fresh read showing it closed with a ClosedEvent id different from the id pinned for the same operation also supersedes: a second ClosedEvent can exist only after a reopen. This covers a reopen and independent re-close between two reconciliation passes for both `pr.merge` and `issue.close` closures.
- **Attribution.** With no pin (first proof, or a legacy row), `pr.merge` requires GitHub's latest ClosedEvent closer to be the merged PR (existing rule); `issue.close` requires a latest ClosedEvent with a null closer (an explicit close has no closer). A mismatch, or a closed issue with no ClosedEvent, is deterministic `attribution-unproved`, never the transient read failure. Residual limit, documented in SPEC beside the existing explicit-close race: a reopen plus a manual re-close that both happen before the first proof of an `issue.close` closure, with no PR or commit closer, is indistinguishable and is pinned as own.
- **Explained state.** New source-hold reason `closure-attribution-unproved`; `DomainStore.providerClosure` returns a new value `"unattributed"` while that hold is active on an open task. Views explain it as held, closed on GitHub, not provably closed by Ensemble, with recovery "reopen the issue on GitHub, then resolve the source hold". It is never completed by the Done-mode finalizer (which requires hold reason `closed`). Reopening proves supersession on the next reconciliation.
- **Holds on supersession.** `supersedeDeliveryClosure` converts an active `closure-read-unavailable` or `closure-attribution-unproved` hold to `closed`; other active holds are untouched. This matches SPEC "reopening grants no readiness and keeps any closure hold": the operator resumes after reopen, and a later independent closure is already under the `closed` hold that `completeFromProviderClosure` requires.
- **Classification owner.** Provider returns facts; `DeliveryCoordinator.inspectOwnClosure` classifies; `StandaloneService.reconcileOwnDeliveryClosures` persists via `GitHubSourceStore`. No new proof task is needed: every assumption is exercised by deterministic fixtures, and the GitHub GraphQL `ClosedEvent.id` field is a standard Node id.
- **#1022 overlap.** None in planned files beyond `src/standalone/service.ts`, where #1022 may wire power supervision near startup (lines ~129–270); this plan edits only `reconcileOwnDeliveryClosures` (~2687–2735). Rebase conflicts there are an ordinary repair.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/core/github-source.ts` — `GitHubSourceStore.migrate` (table DDL ~235, guarded ALTER pattern ~246), `recordDeliveryClosure` (~886, positional `INSERT INTO github_delivery_closures VALUES (?,?,?,?)` ~987, sets hold `closed`/`readiness-lost`), `recordDeliveryClosureUnavailable` (~998), `updateReadiness` closure-hold branch (~1046–1065), `completeFromProviderClosure` (~299, `NOT EXISTS github_delivery_closures`), `setSourceHold` (~1291).
- **Existing:** `src/core/delivery.ts` — `DeliveryStore.ownsConfirmedClosure` (~1232); `src/core/domain.ts` — `hasOwnDeliveryClosure` (~1550), `providerClosure` (~1574) and its callers `admission` (~1617) and `src/standalone/github-sync.ts:readsBlockers` (~89).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/delivery.ts` — `DeliveryCoordinator.inspectOwnClosure` (~242) returns `{snapshot, operationId, closerPrNodeId}`; `src/standalone/github-delivery.ts` — `GitHubDeliveryProvider.inspectClosedIssue` interface (~31) and `GitHubHttpDeliveryProvider.inspectClosedIssue` (~268, throws `provider-own-closure-unproved` when open and `provider-closure-attribution-unproved` on closer mismatch), `deliveryDocuments.EnsembleDeliveryClosure` (~55, `timelineItems(last:1,itemTypes:[CLOSED_EVENT])`).
- **Existing:** `src/standalone/service.ts` — `reconcileOwnDeliveryClosures` (~2687; called at start-up ~1075 and before every GitHub refresh ~2509, ~2679) catches every error into `recordDeliveryClosureUnavailable`; `completeSettledProviderClosures` (~2737).
- **Existing views:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` `sourceClosure` enum (~812); `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (~2427, ~4066) passes `providerClosure` through; `src/cli/task-write.ts:closureSuffix` (used by `src/cli/main.ts:449`, `src/cli/browse-workspace.ts:253`); `src/standalone/operator.ts` `closureText` (~89) and task detail (~411); `web/src/tasks.ts` `taskColumn`/`taskReasons`; `web/src/task-overview.ts` `taskReadiness`/`taskColumnOf`; `test/fixtures/task-summary.ts` closure type.
- **New:** `GitHubSourceStore.supersedeDeliveryClosure(nodeId, operationId)`, `GitHubSourceStore.recordDeliveryClosureAttributionUnproved(nodeId)`, `GitHubSourceStore.deliveryClosure(nodeId)` (row incl. `operationId`, `closedEventId`), `DeliveryStore.ownClosureOperation(taskId, nodeId)`, a provider result type `ClosedIssueInspection = {state:"open"} | {state:"closed"; snapshot; closedEvent: {id; closerKind: "none"|"pull-request"|"other"; closerPrNodeId: string|null} | null}`, and a coordinator outcome `{kind:"reopened"|"proved"|"attribution-unproved"; operationId; ...}`.
- **Follow:** `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts` `closedIssueWorld` and the migration test "migration adds the skipped closed issues to existing sync state rows"; `test/delivery/pr-completion.test.ts` service tests on `deliveryFixture` (`test/fixtures/delivery-fixture.ts`); `test/coordination/operator-cli-task.test.ts` "a pending own-delivery closure proof is not shown as GitHub closure on any task view".

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** Acyclic: T1 → T2, T1 → T3. T2 and T3 may run concurrently after T1; they share no source file (`test/fixtures/task-summary.ts` and `test/fixtures/delivery-fixture.ts` are each touched by one task only). T4 depends on T2 and T3. T1 establishes the persistence boundary; T2 and T3 must not start until T1's focused check passes.

#### 1. Supersession persistence and effective own-closure predicates

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `src/core/github-source.ts` (`migrate`, `recordDeliveryClosure` gains a `closedEventId: string | null` argument and an explicit column list, new `supersedeDeliveryClosure`, `recordDeliveryClosureAttributionUnproved`, `deliveryClosure`, effective-row filter in `updateReadiness` and `completeFromProviderClosure`; `recordDeliveryClosure`'s accepted prior-hold list adds `closure-attribution-unproved`); `src/core/delivery.ts` (`ownClosureOperation`, `ownsConfirmedClosure`); `src/core/domain.ts` (`hasOwnDeliveryClosure` effective-row filter, `providerClosure` returns `"unattributed"` and keeps `null` for `closure-read-unavailable`). Update existing `recordDeliveryClosure` callers in tests (`test/sources/github-service.test.ts`, `test/delivery/pr-completion.test.ts`) and the positional insert in `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts` (~724).
**Test:** In `test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.ts`, using `closedIssueWorld` plus a confirmed `issue.close` and a `pr.merge`-style operation seeded through `DeliveryStore` as `test/sources/github-service.test.ts` (~1055–1092) does:
- "a superseded own closure lets a later closure complete under Done mode": record own closure, assert `hasOwnDeliveryClosure` true and `completeFromProviderClosure(...)` false; `supersedeDeliveryClosure`; observe open, observe closed; assert `hasOwnDeliveryClosure` false, `providerClosure` `"held"`, hold `closed`, `completeFromProviderClosure(taskId, () => true)` true and `providerCompletion` set. Repeat under Skip: hold `closed`, state open, no completion.
- "an own closure without supersession is never provider-completed": closed own closure under Done mode with hold `closed`; finalizer returns false, `providerClosure` null.
- "a later Ensemble closure after supersession is own again": supersede op A, confirm op B; `hasOwnDeliveryClosure` true.
- "attribution-unproved is an explained hold, not a pending read": `recordDeliveryClosureAttributionUnproved` replaces `closure-read-unavailable`/`closed`, `providerClosure` `"unattributed"`, finalizer false; `supersedeDeliveryClosure` converts it to `closed`.
- "migration adds supersession storage and keeps delivery closures": create the old 4-column `github_delivery_closures` with a row, run `migrate`; row intact with `closedEventId` NULL, supersession table empty, migrate is idempotent; supersession rows are never deleted by `recordDeliveryClosure` for a new operation.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Supersession inserts `INSERT OR IGNORE`, converts only `closure-read-unavailable`/`closure-attribution-unproved` to `closed`, bumps the task version, and runs in one `transaction`. `recordDeliveryClosure` stores `closedEventId` and must not be called for a superseded operation (asserted by T2's caller, not re-checked here).
**Validate:** From the checkout root with Node 24 (`.node-version`) after `npm ci`, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/sources/github-reconciliation.test.js dist/test/sources/github-service.test.js dist/test/delivery/pr-completion.test.js`; expect all pass including the new cases.
**Complete when:** New store behaviour and migration tests pass and existing closure tests still pass.

#### 2. Fresh inspection classification and reconciliation wiring

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 focused check green.
**Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/github-delivery.ts` (`EnsembleDeliveryClosure` adds `id` to `ClosedEvent`; `inspectClosedIssue` always queries it and returns `ClosedIssueInspection`; drops the `expectedCloserPrNodeId` parameter and both attribution throws; node/repository identity mismatch still throws); `src/standalone/delivery.ts` (`inspectOwnClosure(taskId, target, pinned)` classifies per Planning decisions using `ownClosureOperation`); `src/standalone/service.ts` (`reconcileOwnDeliveryClosures`: reopened → `supersedeDeliveryClosure` then `updateReadiness` via existing source paths; proved → `recordDeliveryClosure(..., closedEventId)`; attribution-unproved → `recordDeliveryClosureAttributionUnproved`; thrown error → `recordDeliveryClosureUnavailable`). Fixtures: `test/fixtures/delivery-fixture.ts` (controllable inspection: open/closed, ClosedEvent id and closer), `test/fixtures/delivery-integration.ts` and `test/delivery/github-qualification/fixture.ts` (ClosedEvent `id` in scripted responses).
**Test:**
- `test/delivery/github-delivery-provider.test.ts`: replace the attribution-unproved rejection case with facts: open REST state → `{state:"open"}`; closed with PR closer → `closerKind "pull-request"` and `closerPrNodeId`; null closer → `"none"`; commit closer → `"other"`; empty timeline → `closedEvent: null`; node/repo mismatch still rejects.
- `test/delivery/pr-completion.test.ts` (service on `deliveryFixture("through-merge", true)` with the source reconfigured to `closedIssues: "done"` as `test/coordination/operator-cli-task.test.ts` does):
  - "own merge, reopen, then independent closure completes under Done mode once settled": merge P7 (ClosedEvent `CE1` closer P7) → refresh, own closure recorded with pin `CE1`; inspection open + reader open → refresh → supersession row exists, hold `closed`; inspection closed `CE2` closer null + reader closed → refresh; after the lead turn settles, task `done` with provider completion. Skip variant: stays open with hold `closed`.
  - "an own closure that is never reopened is not provider-completed": merge, settle, repeated refreshes under Done mode; no provider completion row.
  - "a reopen and independent re-close between passes is not re-attributed" for `issue.close` and `pr.merge`: pinned `CE1`, next inspection closed with `CE2` → superseded, provider closure.
  - "unproved merge attribution gets an explained hold": first inspection closed with closer `P9` → hold `closure-attribution-unproved`, `providerClosure` `"unattributed"`, not `closure-read-unavailable`; a thrown read still yields `closure-read-unavailable`.
  - "issue.close attribution without a pin requires a null closer": first inspection with PR closer → `closure-attribution-unproved`.
**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Pinned comparison applies only when the stored row's `operationId` equals the selected operation; a legacy NULL pin uses the no-pin rules and is pinned on success.
**Validate:** From the checkout root after T1, run `npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/delivery/github-delivery-provider.test.js dist/test/delivery/pr-completion.test.js dist/test/sources/github-service.test.js dist/test/delivery/delivery-service.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Service-level reopen, re-close and attribution paths pass with deterministic fixtures and existing delivery tests remain green.

#### 3. Explained `unattributed` closure on web, HTML and CLI

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 focused check green.
**Files and symbols:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`sourceClosure` adds `"unattributed"`); `src/cli/task-write.ts:closureSuffix` → ` (closed on GitHub; closure not attributed to Ensemble; held)`; `src/standalone/operator.ts` `closureText` and task-detail paragraph ("Held · closed on GitHub; Ensemble could not prove its delivery closed it. Reopen the issue on GitHub, then resolve the source hold."); `web/src/tasks.ts` (`taskColumn` Paused, `taskReasons` unshifts "Held · closure not attributed to Ensemble", task-unready filter as for `held`); `web/src/task-overview.ts` (`taskReadiness` "Held · closure not attributed to Ensemble", `taskColumnOf` Paused); `test/fixtures/task-summary.ts` type; `design/DESIGN.md` closure-hold sentence (~180) names the variant (text variant of artboard `42-phone-provider-closed`; no new artboard).
**Test:**
- `test/coordination/operator-cli-task.test.ts`: new "an unproved own-delivery closure attribution is explained on every task view", modelled on the pending-proof test: `recordDeliveryClosureAttributionUnproved("I1")` then a closed observation; assert API `readTask`/`readTaskListPage` `source.closure === "unattributed"`, `task get`/`task list` output contains "closure not attributed to Ensemble", HTML `ui.task` contains "could not prove" and "Source hold: closure-attribution-unproved".
- `test/operator/operator-work-presentation.test.ts` and `test/operator/operator-task-overview.test.ts`: `taskReasons`, `taskColumn`, `taskReadiness`, `taskColumnOf` for `closure: "unattributed"` (Paused; explained text; not Draft).
**Implementation:** Text and enum additions only; existing `held`/`completed` presentation unchanged.
**Validate:** From the checkout root after T1, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build:service && node --test dist/test/coordination/operator-cli-task.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-work-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-task-overview.test.js`; expect all pass.
**Complete when:** Each surface shows the explained state and the typecheck covers the web project.

#### 4. SPEC and glossary

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T2`, `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T2 and T3 complete.
**Files and symbols:** `docs/SPEC.md` closure paragraph beginning "Losing readiness, leaving all selections or external closure…" (~235–247): add the supersession rule (reopen after own closure supersedes it; a later closure is provider closure in both modes; supersession keeps audit history and any closure hold) and the `closure-attribution-unproved` explained hold with its reopen recovery. Own-closure paragraph "Only proven own closure permits…" (~1407–1414): ClosedEvent pinning, a different later ClosedEvent proves a reopen, explicit-close attribution requires a null closer, and the first-proof residual limit. `CONTEXT.md` **Closure hold** entry: one sentence that a superseded own closure no longer exempts the task.
**Implementation:** Revise in place; no dated sections or amendment notes (AGENTS.md).
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run format:check`; expect success, and `rg -n "superseded|closure-attribution-unproved" docs/SPEC.md` shows both paragraphs.
**Complete when:** SPEC documents the rule and the explained hold consistently with the implementation.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Own closure → reopen → independent close is provider closure; Done completes once settled; Skip keeps a `closed` hold | 1, 2 | T1 "superseded own closure…" (Done and Skip); T2 "own merge, reopen, then independent closure…" (Done and Skip) |
| Own closure without a reopen never becomes provider-completed | 1, 2 | T1 "own closure without supersession…"; T2 "never reopened is not provider-completed" |
| Attribution-unproved is not a transient read failure and is explained on web, HTML and CLI | 2, 3 | T2 "unproved merge attribution gets an explained hold"; T3 operator-cli-task and presentation tests |
| `issue.close` reconciliation does not re-attribute an independent re-close | 2 | T2 "reopen and independent re-close between passes…" (`issue.close`) and "issue.close attribution without a pin requires a null closer" |
| Migration keeps existing records valid; no audit history deleted | 1 | T1 "migration adds supersession storage and keeps delivery closures" |
| SPEC documents the rule; tests cover each path | 4, 1–3 | T4 validation; slice tests above |
| Pinned `npm ci` and `npm run check` | Final | Final validation |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root on Node 24.21.0 with npm 12.2.0, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate; expect typecheck, lint, format, build and all tests (including both browser engines locally) to pass.
- CI on the pull request must pass its documented profiles (`docs/development.md`). Base `93b52c00` CI run 38887407918 passed `quality`, all service/operator/execution/workspaces/integrations shards and `check`; focused baseline tests for the touched files were also run locally green (78 + 28 tests).
- The live GitHub delivery qualification (`test/delivery/github-qualification/live-delivery.mjs`) is not required for acceptance; keep its fixture compiling with the new `ClosedEvent.id` field.

### Review focus

- Every own-closure consumer (`admission`, `readsBlockers`, `updateReadiness`, `completeFromProviderClosure`, `providerClosure`, `inspectOwnClosure`) uses the effective (unsuperseded) predicate; none still reads raw `github_delivery_closures` presence.
- A stale or eventually consistent provider read must not supersede incorrectly: supersession needs a fresh open state or a different ClosedEvent id for the same operation, never `observedState` from the last sync.
- `supersedeDeliveryClosure` and hold conversion are one transaction, and supersession rows are never deleted.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- GitHub's `ClosedEvent.id` proves unavailable or unstable through the existing GraphQL path, or an `issue.close` ClosedEvent carries a non-null closer: the pinning or null-closer attribution design no longer holds.

nodes.body:
## Slice plan

Each slice is one reviewable PR. Slice 1 lands first; slices 2–6 depend only on it and can run in parallel, except that 4 and 5 both touch `task-views.tsx`/`work.css` and should not run at the same time.

1. **Tokens, state badges and shell** — #1036. Canvas tokens mapped onto the shadcn layer; state badges with symbol + word; 232px sidebar (Search work field with ⌘K, project activity, capacity meter); 48px top bar (breadcrumb, connection status, New task). Reference: `Sidebar`, `TopBar`, `Main`.
2. **Overview** (`01-attention-overview`) — stat strip (Needs you, Uncertain, Active tasks, Running turns); Needs you as cards (uncertainty first, then questions and approvals oldest first) with inline evidence and in-card single-choice answers; dashed overflow row to the Inbox; work table beside a Projects panel and Recent results.
3. **Inbox** (`02-inbox-approval`) — three panes: grouped queue, request pane with sticky response bar, task-context inspector. Queue selection as `--overlay` fill plus a 2px indigo left edge. The Inbox still never approves or denies; an approval links to exact material.
4. **Task detail** (`03-task-detail`) — header (ID, source chip, title, outcome, Execution and Stop…), status strip, tabs (Overview, Files, Changes, Review, History), decision card first, inspector (source sync, holds, dependencies, execution facts, results).
5. **Board** (`04-tasks-board`) — all columns on one screen at 1366, equal width, an empty Ready column as a narrow labelled rail; cards with reason, next actor (amber when you) and lead; phone column tabs.
6. **Composer** (`05-composer`) — "If you create it now" prediction panel (Starts now / Will wait with numbered reasons and their Fix), inherited project facts, collapsed optional sections as chips with error counts, sticky draft/create bar.

Follow-ups noted in slice 1, to fold into the slices above: the sidebar Paused project badge still uses the attention tone where the canvas uses idle; the capacity meter reads usage from the task list (absent with no tasks); remaining legacy `Badge` uses outside `StatusBadge` should adopt symbols as each surface is redone.

**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1040 **Planned against:** `main` at `1da07083a8b826c93d786d5923366930a54d9023` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach Implementation starts from a base that includes #1047 (merged to `main` as `34f8f519`; it adds the exported seams below). Restyle and restructure the existing Inbox in place; no endpoint, read-model, command or SPEC change. Five increments: (T1) pure presentation helpers; (T2) grouped queue and the three-column workbench layout, with the queue pane owning the `h1` on the sidebar shell; (T3) the request pane, with one task read lifted above it; (T4) the task-context inspector; (T5) `design/DESIGN.md` Implementation status, the Inbox deviations and screenshot evidence. ### Guardrails - Behaviour stays as SPEC.md and the existing tests define it: the Inbox never approves or denies (an approval ends with the statement of what a decision covers and one "Review material & decide" link to `item.destination`); answering, drafts, failed/stale/conflict/unknown outcomes, holds that "answering/approval does not clear", return-to-queue anchoring, the 15-second poll, filters and sign-out clearing stay unchanged. `QuestionResponse` and `ApprovalFacts` are shared with `/app/tasks/:id?request=` and the Overview cards (#1047); change them only through Inbox-scoped CSS or backward-compatible props. - Update selectors that change instead of deleting tests; add browser tests for what changes. Keep class names the tests use (`.action-inbox`, `.inbox-queue`, `.inbox-rows`, `.inbox-row`, `.inbox-row-label`, `.inbox-row-meta`, `.inbox-detail`, `.inbox-detail-header`, `.question-submit`) and the region names "Action Inbox" and "Selected request". - Use only read-model facts (`InboxItem`, `TaskRead`); do not invent contracts, short identifiers or request text. Settings, task detail, Board, composer, Overview, `task-views.tsx`, `work.css`, the Haze prototype and the canvas itself are out of scope. - Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, CSS, documentation and CI repairs stay with the ticket owner and do not consume the plan-mismatch budget. Only a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption (for example an exported seam below that does not exist or behaves differently) allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles; stop and re-plan beyond that, for a material design/contract change, or when grants are exhausted. Investigate unknown overlap. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews; this plan needs no integration amendment. ### Planning decisions - **Evidence and base.** Artboards read through the Artifact tool: `02-inbox-approval` (desktop), `09-phone-inbox-queue`, `10-phone-question`, `31-phone-inbox-anchored-return`, `800b-tablet-inbox-question`, `06`, `32`. Baseline at `1da07083`: CI `quality` (typecheck, lint, format, build) and `node24-operator-1/2` passed; the aggregate `check` is red only because Node 26 `service-2` failed in `test/coordination/task-writer.test.ts` ("uncertain archive status keeps its archival hold across restart", child-exit timing), which this web/test/docs change cannot reach. Main has since advanced only by #1047 (`34f8f519`); its delta to the Inbox seams is exactly what is listed below, so the plan holds on `34f8f519` or later. Verified locally: `node --test dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.js` runs a single compiled test file (10 pass). - **Layout.** Queue 340px, request pane flexible, inspector 280px from 1280px viewport width (`@media (min-width: 1280px)` in CSS and `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1280px)")` in code); 761–1279px shows queue 300px + request pane only (frame `800b` draws no inspector); at or below 760px the existing single column queue → detail → queue is unchanged. The inspector is conditionally rendered, not CSS-hidden, so no hidden duplicate content exists. - **Heading ownership.** At the sidebar shell (>= 1121px) the panes run edge to edge under the top bar and the queue pane header holds the single `h1` "Inbox", the existing subtitle ("N unresolved across M projects", "… · confirmation retained") and a "Refresh" button; `app.tsx` then does not render `PageHeader` for the Inbox route and passes `Inbox` a `chrome` prop (`{ onRefresh, refreshing }`) that replaces the page-header Refresh (`refreshAll()` plus `tasks.refresh()`, disabled while `workspace.state.pending`). At <= 1120px `PageHeader` (menu, title, count badge, Refresh, phone detail header) is unchanged. This keeps exactly one `h1` per route. Selectors on `.page-header-title p` / `.page-header-count` for the Inbox at 1366px change to the queue header (`.inbox-heading`, `.inbox-summary`). - **One task read.** `Inbox` calls `useInboxTask` once per selected task (`taskId` becomes `string | null`; null disables the read; add scope `"request"`) and passes the result to the request pane, the holds and the inspector. This replaces the per-kind reads inside `ApprovalDetail` and the Inbox's use of `InboxQuestion`; the Overview card keeps `InboxQuestion` unchanged. Loading or a failed read still shows no hold, never blocks answering, and never hides evidence links. - **Recorded gaps (compose from nearest frames, no new contract).** The read model has no short identifiers (AP-17, A-104, C-104, Q-204, AT-142): the identity line is "requester · version N · HH:MM" and the chain uses assignment names ("Operator → Mira → Jonas"). The request headline stays the task title (an approval's `prompt` is system-composed "Approval requested for …" and `reason` is generic; the question text is the form's own legends). There is no material excerpt or tabs, no "Version N is out of date" note and no Approved/"Return to task" state (the Inbox never decides): the exact action, target and version facts and the one Review link stand in. The breadcrumb stays "Inbox"; the kind label stays "Intervention" (no execution-uncertain subtype in the Inbox read); the frame's "Today · HH:MM" clock stays unbuilt. Frame 02's Previous/Next request buttons are built (pure navigation through the existing `choose`). - **Evidence links appear once.** Tests query "Task evidence" and "Requesting conversation" at page level. With the inspector (>= 1280px) they move there from the request intro; below it they stay in the intro. - **Entry points and counterparts.** Applies to: Inbox desktop three-pane, tablet two-pane and phone; the `/app/inbox?task=&request=` deep link (opens the pane and inspector). Unchanged: `/app/tasks/:id?request=`, Overview cards (share `InboxQuestion`, `ApprovalFacts`, `useInboxTask`, `QuestionHolds`), the retained coordination page. No new state-changing action; Previous/Next and Refresh are navigation and existing reads (reverse of Next is Previous). ### Implementation context - **Existing, shared with #1047 (merged):** `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx` — exports `useInboxTask(client, session, taskId, observedAt, scope)`, `InboxQuestion` (reads holds via `holdNotices(task, "answer")`), `ApprovalFacts({ task, item })`, `ApprovalDetail` (calls `useInboxTask` itself; only `inbox.tsx` uses it), `InterventionDetail`. `web/src/question-response.tsx` — `QuestionResponse` (`holds`, `compactContext`, `onBack`), exported `QuestionHolds`; `.question-submit` is sticky inside `.inbox-detail`. `web/src/request-presentation.ts` — now holds `inboxSummaryOf` (moved from `inbox.tsx`; `inbox.tsx` and `app.tsx` import it from there). `web/src/overview-attention.tsx` — consumer of the four seams and owner of a private `icons` map (question `CircleQuestionMark`, approval `Diamond`, intervention `TriangleAlert`). - **Existing:** `web/src/inbox.tsx` — `Inbox`, `InboxState`, `InboxHeader`, `loadInbox`; `single = useMediaQuery("(max-width: 760px)")`, `choose`, `back`, the selection/`implicit`/`leftQueue` logic, the `onHeader` effect for the phone detail header, `.inbox-filters` as a grid area above queue and detail. `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` — `requestKindLabel`, `requestActionLabel`, `ageLabel`, `clockLabel`, `filterCounts`, `holdNotices`. `web/src/app.tsx` — `onInboxRoute`, `inboxHeader`/`inboxHeaderProps`, `` (about lines 967–1011, with `ownsRefresh` and `refreshAll`), `` (about line 1115). `web/src/styles.css` — inbox block from `.action-inbox` (about line 1991) to `.inbox-empty` and its two media blocks (about line 2290), plus shell rules `.page-inbox` (about lines 316, 537, 944); `.question-*` rules are shared and stay. `web/src/tokens.css` — `--surface`, `--raised`, `--overlay`, `--line`, `--line-strong`, `--accent-edge`, `--focus`, `--attn*`, `--risk*`, `--fg-2`, `--fg-3`. `web/src/components.tsx` — `Button`, `ActionLink`, `ResourceStatus`, `PageHeader`, `TopBar`; `web/src/ui/badge.tsx` variants `attention` and `destructive`. Contracts: `InboxItem` (`kind`, `createdAt`, `revision`, `requesterName`, `requestingAssignmentId`, `evidence`, `conversation`, `destination`, `reason`) and `TaskRead` (`lead`, `leadAssignmentId`, `assignments[].requesterAssignmentId`, `source.repositoryName`/`number`, `waits`, `admission`, `approvals`). - **New:** `web/src/inbox.css` (imported by `inbox.tsx`, as `task-detail.tsx` imports `task-detail.css`) takes the inbox block moved out of `styles.css`. `web/src/inbox-context.tsx` — `InboxContext` (the inspector). `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` — `queueGroups`, `requestIdentity`, `assignmentChain`, `taskContext`. `web/src/request-presentation.ts` — `requestKindIcons` (moved from `overview-attention.tsx`, which imports it). - **Follow:** `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts` `openInbox`/`settle` helpers and `captureBrowserEvidence`; `test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts` for unit style; `docs/evidence/ui-workbench-shell.md` for the evidence record. ### Implementation slices **Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 → T5; acyclic. T2–T4 all edit `web/src/inbox.tsx`, `web/src/inbox.css` and `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts`, and T3/T4 need the previous layout, so no two tasks run concurrently. Files shared with merged #1047: `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx`, `web/src/inbox.tsx`, `web/src/app.tsx`, `web/src/request-presentation.ts`, `web/src/question-response.tsx` (read only), `web/src/overview-attention.tsx` (T2 swaps its private icon map for the shared export), `design/DESIGN.md`, `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md`, `test/operator/operator-responsive-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-web-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.ts` (read; `.inbox-row[aria-pressed]` at its line ~370), `test/operator/operator-task-browser.test.ts` (no planned edit). Not touched by #1040 and owned by in-flight work: #1030 (`task-header.tsx`, `operator-runtime.ts`, `state.ts`, `operator-api.ts`), #1032 (`source-config.tsx`, `github-discovery.ts`, `operator-api.ts`), #1043 (`task-composer.tsx`, `composer.css`, `wait-reasons.tsx`, composer rules in `styles.css`; T2's deletion of the inbox block and edits to `.page-inbox` rules in `styles.css` are different regions, so expect at most a trivial textual merge). Run the slices in one implementation branch cut from `main` at or after `34f8f519`. #### 1. Queue, identity and context presentation helpers **Task ID:** `T1` **Depends on:** `none` **Prerequisites:** none. **Files and symbols:** `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` (add `queueGroups`, `requestIdentity`, `assignmentChain`, `taskContext`); `test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts`. **Test:** extend `operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts` (no browser). Add `three panes: a grouped queue under its filters, with the overlay and indigo-edge selection, and a page that does not scroll (1366)`: seed two questions and one intervention (`seedOwnQuestion`, `seedOwnIntervention`) plus an approval, open at 1366×900, assert the `.inbox-group` headings read "Intervention · 1" then "Questions & approvals · oldest first" and precede their rows, the selected row has computed background `rgb(30, 34, 53)` and a 2px left border `rgb(99, 102, 241)`, `.inbox-queue` is 340px wide with `--surface` background, `document.documentElement.scrollHeight <= innerHeight`, queue and detail scroll independently (reuse the wheel pattern of the existing scroll test), "Refresh" still rereads the Inbox, and no `.page-header` exists. Add a 1024×768 step: two panes, `.page-header` present with the menu and one `h1`, no horizontal overflow. **Implementation:** (1) Inbox markup: `.inbox-queue` becomes a flex column with `.inbox-queue-head` (when `chrome`: `h1.inbox-heading` "Inbox", `p.inbox-summary` with the existing `subtitle`, Refresh button named exactly "Refresh" that calls `chrome.onRefresh` and is disabled while `chrome.refreshing`; then `.inbox-filters` with the two existing selects and their options unchanged), `ResourceStatus` and the coverage alert, `.inbox-rows` containing `

Design record and screenshot evidence **Task ID:** `T5` **Depends on:** `T2`, `T3`, `T4` **Prerequisites:** the integrated Inbox from T2–T4. **Files and symbols:** `design/DESIGN.md`; `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` (the "Inbox and structured questions" row, and the shell row's header sentence); `docs/evidence/ui-workbench-inbox.md` (new, dated) and `docs/evidence/ui-workbench/` PNGs (new names only; keep `1366-inbox.png`); `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts` (capture names). **Implementation:** (1) `design/DESIGN.md` Implementation status: remove "the three-pane Inbox" from "Not yet adopted" (that line was also edited by #1047) and add an "Implemented Inbox" item: queue 340px / request / inspector 280px from 1280px, two panes 761–1279px, phone single column unchanged; heading, subtitle and Refresh in the queue header at >= 1121px; grouping; selection style; the inspector's facts; Previous/Next. In "Inbox and structured questions" list the recorded gaps from Planning decisions and update "Entry points that apply" (inspector, Overview cards share the seams).
