content.title: Shell rough edges: Refresh on forms, three search entry points, duplicate Runtime menu item, read-time line

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1083
**Planned against:** `main` at `4da7e94e13eec90817aaa7cff7339880d1da9fd2`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Four small UI changes, each with its own browser or unit check. All use rules and frames that are already in the base.

1. The shell's page-header Refresh is hidden on the three create routes.
2. The desktop sidebar loses its Search nav link, so the Search work field (⌘K) is the one desktop entry point. The task table's "Search tasks" becomes "Filter tasks".
3. The account menu and the phone drawer rows drop Runtime.
4. The work-table read line becomes "Updated HH:MM" through a new `presentation.ts` helper, with a range only when the two clock labels differ.

`design/DESIGN.md` and `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` are revised in place where they still describe the old shell. No design-canvas edit is needed: the `Sidebar` component already draws only the field, and `113-account-menu` already draws Settings, Getting started, Approval and delivery forms, Sign out.

### Guardrails

- Read views keep exactly one page-level Refresh, and page-owned refreshes stay as they are: Refresh tasks, Refresh task, Refresh results, and the Inbox queue header's Refresh. The following controls are out of scope and stay: Refresh execution in the composer's post-create outcome (a read of the created task), Refresh source / Refresh delivery status / Refresh captured history in the task workspace, and Refresh sources in sync placement.
- `/app/settings/runtime` keeps its route, its breadcrumb and its Settings entry (`settings-index.tsx` "Runtime and recovery" panel → Open runtime link). Assignment recovery keeps Back to Runtime (`parentRoute`). Only the account-menu and drawer entries go.
- The Getting started / Show getting started behaviour (#1111 decision, already built in `account-menu.tsx`/`AccountRows`) and the Approval and delivery forms entry (#1087) stay unchanged, in frame order. Don't change `configureGettingStarted` or the `/coordination` anchor.
- ⌘K/Ctrl+K behaviour, Search origin/history state (`pushAppEntry`) and `/app/search` routing are unchanged. The field's submit already goes through `navigate()` → `pushAppEntry`, the same path as the removed link.
- The task filter keeps the URL parameter `q`, its matching (`filterTasks`: title, project, lead, repository over the loaded list) and its place under More filters. Only the visible/accessible label changes.
- Times use `clockLabel` from `web/src/presentation.ts` (#1085 rule 4). Don't add local time formatting.
- No server, API, schema or persisted-state change.
- Out of scope: a phone-header Search action (DESIGN.md Search section, not built), clearing the sidebar field after submit, and anything in #1084 (Inbox request pane / "Refresh request") or #1095.
- Ordinary implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the implementer. They don't count against any budget: updating existing assertions that name "Search tasks", "Runtime", "Task states read", the Search nav link or the menu item count; selector changes; lint/format fixes; flaky-wait fixes. Record each briefly in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence.
- A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption is a mechanical plan mismatch. Examples: `ownsRefresh` is not what renders the header Refresh; `ProjectNavigation` is not shared by sidebar and drawer; `AccountRows` is not the drawer account group; the work-table read line is not in `task-views.tsx`. A mismatch gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Stop and return it if it is still unresolved, or if fixing it would change acceptance, architecture or authority. Investigate unknown overlap with concurrent work before proceeding.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Create forms are three routes:** `/app/tasks/new` (with or without `?project=`), `/app/settings/projects/new` and `/app/settings/profiles/new`. They are the only routes with a page Refresh that create a record. `/app/getting-started`, settings, recovery and runtime are read views and keep Refresh. The route check lives with the existing `ownsRefresh` predicate in `App` (rename it if that reads better, for example `noShellRefresh`). It hides the header button at every width, because the same `PageHeader` serves desktop and the drawer shell.
- **One search entry per layout.** At >1120px the sidebar field is the shell's only Search entry, so the `Search` link is removed from the desktop `ProjectNavigation`. The drawer shell (≤1120px) hides the whole sidebar, including the field, and has no other Search entry. So `ProjectNavigation` keeps the Search row only when `row` is true, which keeps the drawer at one entry. This satisfies "one search entry point in the shell" without removing phone access.
- **The field takes over Search's current-page cue.** On `/app/search` the `.search-work` form gets the current navigation treatment, which `Sidebar.dc.html` draws as `searchStyle` when `active === 'search'`. Use a `data-current` attribute plus a CSS rule in `web/src/styles.css` that reuses the existing current nav-link tokens. Without it, no sidebar item is current on Search.
- **The filter label is "Filter tasks".** The filter matches only the loaded list (`filterTasks` in `web/src/tasks.ts`), so the ticket's "different label" condition applies. Keep `id="task-search"` / `q` so the URL and saved filters are unaffected.
- **Read line format.** Add `updatedLabel(first: number, last: number)` in `web/src/presentation.ts`. It returns `Updated ${clockLabel(first)}` when the two clock labels are equal, otherwise `Updated ${a}–${b}`. "Reads differ" is judged at the displayed precision, so two reads in the same minute show one time. Following rule 4, the app clock is 24-hour HH:MM ("Updated 16:48"). The ticket's "4:48 PM" is an illustration of the same rule in DESIGN.md. No trailing period.
- **Docs revised in place:**
  - `design/DESIGN.md` line 120, "Settings, Runtime and Sign out live in the account menu" → "Settings, Getting started, Approval and delivery forms and Sign out live in the account menu".
  - The Search section's "Discoverable entry" bullet: the desktop entry is the sidebar Search work field above Overview, Inbox and Tasks, and the drawer keeps a Search row.
  - The Implemented shell bullet: replace "The Search link stays in the navigation beside the field."
  - `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md` row for the `/app` shell: sidebar entries, the menu entries, and "Refresh elsewhere" → "Refresh on read views; create forms have none".
  - Each doc edit belongs to the slice whose behaviour it describes.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/app.tsx`
  - `App`: `ownsRefresh` (~L812) gates the `PageHeader` `action` Refresh button (~L1007), which calls `refreshAll()` (~L806). `taskRoute` already replaces it with New task on the Overview, Tasks and project routes.
  - `ProjectNavigation` (L132) renders Overview, Inbox, Tasks, Search (~L206) and projects. It is used by `navigation(row)` for both the sidebar (`row=false`) and the drawer (`row=true`).
  - `SearchWorkField` (L252) is the sidebar form. It is rendered once in `<aside className="sidebar">` (~L948), and its ⌘K listener falls back to `/app/search` when the field is hidden.
  - `AccountRows` (L330) is the drawer account group, with Settings, Runtime (L366), Getting started / Show getting started, Approval and delivery forms, and Sign out.
- **Existing:** `web/src/account-menu.tsx` — `AccountMenu` renders the desktop popup items via `link()`, with Runtime at L187–191. The doc comment at L25 names Settings and Runtime. The `Gauge` import is used only by Runtime (also in `app.tsx`'s import list, used only at L370). Remove the unused imports.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-filters.tsx` — the "Search tasks" label (L109–116) is under `<details className="work-more">`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-views.tsx` — the work section footer (L471–477) prints `Task states read {toLocaleTimeString()}–{toLocaleTimeString()}` from `state.data.firstObservedAt/lastObservedAt`. These come from `loadTaskList` (`web/src/tasks.ts` L49–89): first page and last page `observedAt`. On a failed refresh, `useOperatorResource` keeps the last `state.data` (status `stale`), so the line keeps the last successful read.
- **Existing tests that assert the old shell** (update them in the owning slice):
  - `test/operator/operator-shell-browser.test.ts`: "desktop shell lists the designed destinations…" L384–389, which expects Search 4th; "production shell keeps direct task links usable…" L214, a drawer Search click that stays valid; "page-owned refresh replaces the shell Refresh…" L552–639.
  - `test/operator/operator-account-browser.test.ts`: "desktop account menu: pointer, keyboard…" L325–567 (Runtime item, count 5, keyboard order, Enter on Runtime → `/app/settings/runtime`); "phone drawer shows the account group with Settings, Runtime and Sign out" L569–611.
  - `test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.ts` L41, 152, 182, 301, 438, 516 and `test/workspaces/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.ts` L66: desktop clicks on link "Search" at 1366px.
  - `test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.ts` L172–180 ("Search tasks") and L244 (`/^Task states read /`).
  - `test/operator/operator-task-browser.test.ts` L80, 132, 1546 ("Search tasks").
- **Follow:** `test/operator/operator-presentation.test.ts` for pure-helper unit tests (local `Date` construction). Follow the `page-owned refresh` test in `operator-shell-browser.test.ts` for counting `getByRole("button", { name: "Refresh", exact: true })` per route.
- **New:** `web/src/presentation.ts` — `updatedLabel(first, last)` (see Planning decisions), used only by `task-views.tsx`.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** acyclic, with two chains.

- **Chain A:** T1 → T2 → T4. All three edit `web/src/app.tsx` and `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md`. T2 and T4 also edit `design/DESIGN.md`, in different bullets.
- **Chain B:** T3 → T5. Both edit `test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.ts`.

Chain A and chain B share no files, so T1 and T3 may start concurrently. One PR delivers all five slices. Shared setup for every slice: from the checkout root, run `npm ci` with Node from `.node-version`. Browser commands below use `ENSEMBLE_TEST_PROFILE=chromium ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=chromium` (abbreviated **CHROMIUM**).

#### 1. Refresh hidden on create forms

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/app.tsx`: `App` → `ownsRefresh` (or its renamed predicate).
- `test/operator/operator-shell-browser.test.ts`: the page-owned refresh test, or a new sibling case.
- `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md`: `/app` shell row, "Refresh elsewhere".

**Test:** a desktop (1366×900) browser case using `createOperatorFixture` with one project (as in the existing page-owned refresh test).
- For each of `/app/tasks/new`, `/app/tasks/new?project=<projectId>`, `/app/settings/projects/new` and `/app/settings/profiles/new`, after `main.page h1` renders, assert that the count of buttons named exactly "Refresh" is 0.
- For `/app/settings`, `/app/getting-started`, `/app/settings/runtime` and `/app/inbox`, assert exactly 1. The existing loop covers `/app/inbox` and `/app/settings`; extend it.
- Stale-state/remount: start on `/app/settings` (1 Refresh), click the sidebar link "New project" (client navigation, no reload), and assert 0. Then `page.goBack()` and assert 1 again on `/app/settings`. Then navigate client-side from `/app/tasks/new` to a read view through the account menu Settings item, and assert 1.
- Phone (390×844): `/app/tasks/new` and `/app/settings/projects/new` have 0 Refresh buttons in the drawer-shell header.

**Implementation:** add the three create routes to the predicate that suppresses the header Refresh. Do not change `refreshAll` or any form's own controls. Update the ui08 doc row wording.
**Validate:** from the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && CHROMIUM node --test dist/test/operator/operator-shell-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass, including the new create-route assertions.
**Complete when:** the create routes render no page Refresh at desktop and phone widths, read views keep one, and the shell test passes.

#### 2. One shell search entry (sidebar field)

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the working branch (shared `app.tsx`).
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/app.tsx`: `ProjectNavigation` (Search link only when `row`), `SearchWorkField` (accepts the current pathname and sets `data-current` on the form on `/app/search`), and the sidebar call site.
- `web/src/styles.css`: a `.search-work[data-current]` rule using the current nav-link tokens.
- `test/operator/operator-shell-browser.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.ts`, `test/workspaces/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.ts`.
- `design/DESIGN.md`: Search → Discoverable entry; Implemented shell bullet.
- `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md`: sidebar list.

**Test:**
- In the "desktop shell lists the designed destinations…" case, assert the first three nav labels are Overview, Inbox and Tasks, and that a link named exactly "Search" inside `.sidebar` has count 0. Assert `.sidebar` has exactly one `search` landmark with the "Search work" input.
- Submit behaviour: submitting the field empty lands on `/app/search`; submitting "Shared" lands on `/app/search?query=Shared`. ⌘K (`Meta+K`, and `Control+K`) at 1366px focuses the "Search work" input.
- On `/app/search` the form has `data-current`. After Back to `/app`, it no longer has it (stale-state).
- At ≤1120px (for example 1024 or 390): the drawer dialog still has exactly one link "Search" (the existing L214 click stays). ⌘K navigates to `/app/search` and focuses `#retained-query`.
- Replace each desktop `getByRole("link", { name: "Search", exact: true })` click in the search and inspection-navigation browser tests with field entry: focus the "Search work" input and press Enter with an empty value, or click the input then Enter. Keep their existing origin/Back/Forward assertions. Those assertions prove the origin state is unchanged.

**Implementation:** remove the desktop Search nav item, keep the drawer row, mark the field current on Search, and revise the DESIGN.md and ui08 bullets as listed in Planning decisions.
**Validate:** from the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && CHROMIUM node --test dist/test/operator/operator-shell-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass. `rg -n "Search link stays" design/DESIGN.md` prints nothing.
**Complete when:** desktop has only the field, the drawer has one Search row, the Search origin journeys pass through the field, and the docs match.

#### 3. In-table filter renamed

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/task-filters.tsx` (label text "Filter tasks"); `test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.ts` L172–180; `test/operator/operator-task-browser.test.ts` L80, 132, 1546.
**Test:** in the existing work/task browser cases, use `getByLabel("Filter tasks")`.
- Filling "Normal Stop" narrows the rows and clearing restores them (existing work test).
- After a reload or Back, the label's input keeps the `q` value "Literal" (existing task test L132, which keeps the stale-state guarantee).
- Add one assertion that `getByLabel("Search tasks")` has count 0.

**Implementation:** change the label text only.
**Validate:** from the checkout root, run `npm run build && CHROMIUM node --test dist/test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-task-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass. `rg -n "Search tasks" web/src test` prints nothing.
**Complete when:** the table's filter reads "Filter tasks" and filtering/URL retention tests pass.

#### 4. Account menu without Runtime

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 on the working branch (shared `app.tsx`, `DESIGN.md`, ui08 doc).
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/account-menu.tsx`: `AccountMenu` items, doc comment, `Gauge` import.
- `web/src/app.tsx`: `AccountRows` (remove the Runtime `RouteLink`; drop `Gauge` if unused).
- `test/operator/operator-account-browser.test.ts`: both menu cases; rename the phone case to "…with Settings, Getting started, Approval and delivery forms and Sign out".
- `design/DESIGN.md`: line 120 shell bullet.
- `docs/design/ui08-foundation.md`: menu entries.

**Test:**
- **Desktop popup:** the menuitems in order are Settings, Getting started, Approval and delivery forms, Sign out (count 4), and `menuitem` "Runtime" has count 0. Keyboard: Enter opens on Settings, ArrowDown walks Getting started → Approval and delivery forms → Sign out, and wraps to Settings. ArrowUp from Settings goes to Sign out. Replace the old "Enter on Runtime" step with Enter on Getting started → `/app/getting-started` and the menu detached.
- **Recovery path:** from `/app/settings`, the Runtime and recovery panel's link reaches `/app/settings/runtime`, and its breadcrumb or Back returns to Settings.
- **Dismissed state** (existing "Getting started: menu entry, Dismiss and its undo…" case): after Dismiss, the menu shows button menuitem "Show getting started" in second position and still 4 items. Activating it restores the card on `/app/getting-started` and the item reads Getting started again. If the existing case does not already assert the count and order, add those assertions.
- **Remount:** after `page.goBack()` the menu is closed (existing assertion), and reopening still lists 4 items.
- **Phone drawer (390):** rows Settings, Getting started, Approval and delivery forms, each ≥44px. The Sign out button is ≥44px. Link "Runtime" in the dialog has count 0. Replace the Runtime click with the Settings row → `/app/settings`, and keep the Sign out step.

**Implementation:** delete the Runtime entries from both surfaces, fix the doc comment, and update the docs.
**Validate:** from the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build && CHROMIUM node --test dist/test/operator/operator-account-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-shell-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-settings-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass. `rg -n '"Runtime"' web/src/account-menu.tsx` prints nothing.
**Complete when:** neither menu surface lists Runtime, the Runtime page is reachable from Settings, and the account tests pass.

#### 5. Read-time line shows one time or a real range

**Task ID:** `T5`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3 on the working branch (shared `operator-work-browser.test.ts`).
**Files and symbols:** `web/src/presentation.ts` (new `updatedLabel`); `web/src/task-views.tsx` work footer (L471–477); `test/operator/operator-presentation.test.ts`; `test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.ts` L244.
**Test:**
- **Unit** (`operator-presentation.test.ts`), with local `Date` construction:
  - `updatedLabel(16:48:07, 16:48:07)` is "Updated 16:48".
  - `updatedLabel(16:48:01, 16:48:59)` is "Updated 16:48", because it is the same minute.
  - `updatedLabel(16:47:59, 16:48:00)` is "Updated 16:47–16:48".
  - `updatedLabel(23:59:30, 00:00:10 next day)` is "Updated 23:59–00:00".
- **Browser** (work test at L244): wait for `/^Updated \d{2}:\d{2}$/`, and assert `getByText(/Task states read/)` has count 0. After Refresh tasks succeeds, the line still matches the pattern.
- **Stale-state:** route `/api/operator/task-list` to fail with 500 (`page.route`), click Refresh tasks, and wait for the Tasks `ResourceStatus` stale notice. Then assert the read line text equals the text captured before the failed refresh. Unroute, refresh again, and assert the stale notice clears.

**Implementation:** add the helper and replace the footer text with `{updatedLabel(state.data.firstObservedAt, state.data.lastObservedAt)}`. Add no local formatting.
**Validate:** from the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-presentation.test.js && CHROMIUM node --test dist/test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass. `rg -n "Task states read|toLocaleTimeString" web/src/task-views.tsx` prints nothing.
**Complete when:** the footer shows "Updated HH:MM", or a range only for differing labels, keeps the last successful time on a failed refresh, and the unit and browser tests pass.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Refresh hidden on create forms; stays on read views | 1 | T1 shell browser case: 0 on the three create routes (desktop and phone), 1 on read views, across client navigation and Back |
| One shell search entry: sidebar field with ⌘K opens Search | 2 | T2 shell/search browser cases: no desktop Search link, field submit and ⌘K, drawer keeps one row |
| Work table keeps its in-table filter under a different label (filters only the loaded list) | 3 | T3 work/task browser cases with "Filter tasks"; no "Search tasks" |
| Account menu lists Settings, Getting started, Approval and delivery forms, Sign out as in `113-account-menu`; dismissed → Show getting started restores it | 4 | T4 account browser cases: order, count 4, keyboard, dismissed state, phone rows, Runtime via Settings |
| Read-time line shows one time ("Updated …") or a range only when reads differ | 5 | T5 `updatedLabel` unit cases and work browser case, including the failed-refresh case |
| DESIGN.md / ui08 doc describe the current shell | 1, 2, 4 | `rg` checks in T2 and T4; final format check |

### Final validation

- From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate (typecheck, lint, format, build and the full test suite in both browsers). Expect success.
- Run `npm run test:built -- --suite=operator --profile=service` once to confirm discovery is unchanged: no new test file is added, and the operator suite runs without missing or duplicate files.
- PR CI (`quality`, `node24-operator-*`, `node24-workspaces-*`, `node26-service-*`) must pass on the PR head.

### Review focus

- The ⌘K handler at drawer widths still lands on `/app/search` with `#retained-query` focused, now that the drawer row is the only entry there.
- `data-current` on the search form is set from the shell's current `pathname`, not a mount-time value, so Back/Forward clears it.
- Overlap with concurrent tickets. None of these edit `web/src/app.tsx`, `account-menu.tsx`, `task-filters.tsx`, `task-views.tsx` or `styles.css` sections touched here.
  - **#1084** (in implementation): `design/DESIGN.md` (Inbox and structured questions bullets, a different section) and `web/src/presentation.ts` (reads helpers only; if it adds exports, merge alongside `updatedLabel`). Its "Refresh request" removal is in `inbox-detail.tsx`/`question-response.tsx` and does not touch the shell header Refresh. No overlap with T1.
  - **#1095** (ready): `design/DESIGN.md` (Implementation status → Settings/recovery bullet, a different bullet) and `test/operator/operator-task-browser.test.ts` (different cases from T3's three label lines).
  - **#1087** (merged): already placed Approval and delivery forms. T4 only removes Runtime, so the final order matches the frame.
  - **Exclusive resources:** none. Tests use per-fixture ports and temp data; there are no global ports, credentials, live runtimes or Project-board state.

content.title: Inbox: lead with the question, not the scaffolding around it

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1084
**Planned against:** `main` at `43d3b0c2e443e66441fd5c314927e9998fe07095`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Give each Inbox item a privacy-checked `headline` in the read model: the first question's label, or the approval's exact action. A 100-row queue cannot make one question read per row, which the Overview cards do today. The queue row and request pane then lead with that headline, with the task title and project beneath it. The scaffolding moves below the form: version line, conversation revision, evidence links and drafts note. The always-present "Refresh request" button is removed from the shared `QuestionResponse`. Its re-read is folded into the host page's refresh/poll. Stale-read recovery keeps the existing `ResourceStatus` "Try again".

### Guardrails

- Rules from #1085 apply. Use `web/src/presentation.ts` helpers (`clockLabel`, `shortId`, `codeSentence`) and add no local time or identifier formatting. A missing requester, time or evidence line is omitted, never printed as a placeholder. Add no sub-panel refresh.
- Privacy: `headline` follows exactly the same disclosure rule as the exact read it summarises. A question's headline is null unless `intactQuestion(form, excluded)` holds for the composed form. An approval's headline is null unless the approval's exact material is disclosable (`interaction(q, excluded).approvable`). Interventions have a null headline. When the headline is null, the UI falls back to the task title; it never shows "Unavailable" as a title.
- Leave the server `reason` field, the CLI `inbox list` table, the SPEC and the Overview cards unchanged. The web stops rendering the generic reasons ("Operator answer requested", "Review exact approval material"). It keeps the intervention reason and the native-delivery reason ("Answer recorded; native delivery remains unresolved", rows with an `attentionCode`).
- The Inbox still never approves or denies. The approval pane keeps its exact action/target/version facts, holds, bound-decision statement and one "Review material & decide" link.
- The task page (`/app/tasks/:id?request=`) and Overview question cards share `QuestionResponse`. Its layout changes (context block and drafts note below the form, no pending badge, no Refresh request) apply to all three hosts on purpose, so the shared behaviour stays consistent. Answer, retry, conflict ("Review current request"), offline ("Check connection") and recorded ("Back to Inbox") paths are unchanged.
- A background re-read of the question must not run while an answer is sending or its outcome is uncertain (`state.sending` / `state.lifecycle.uncertain`). It must not discard draft input; the existing `sameForm` check governs schema changes.
- Out of scope: Overview card headlines (#1098's Answer flow), the inspector's contents beyond what moves there today, the legacy-form links (#1087), and any canvas edit.
- Routine implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the implementer within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority. Record the correction in the PR/delivery record and renew the affected evidence. Those repairs do not consume the plan-mismatch budget.
- A wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption is different. Examples: `readInbox` cannot reach the composed question form or the `approvable` flag without a new domain read, or `QuestionResponse` cannot take a host `observedAt` without changing its draft/receipt state machine. That is a mechanical plan mismatch and allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Then stop and report the mismatch for replanning. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop on material design or contract changes, for example adding a new route, changing the question read, or changing who may approve.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption; preserve repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **Server headline instead of client fan-out.** The Overview reads each question to show `form.questions[0].label` (`web/src/overview-attention.tsx` `QuestionCard`). The Inbox queue holds up to 100 rows, so the read model carries `headline: safeText` (nullable, required key) on `inboxItemSchema`. Composition:
  - Own or native form: the composed form's first question `label`, which is the native `header` via `nativeQuestionForm`.
  - Plain question (no own or native form): `this.safe(interaction.prompt, excluded)`, because its synthetic form label is just "Answer".
  - Approval: the approval's exact `action`.
  - Intervention: `null`.
  
  The form composition moves out of `readQuestion` into one private helper, so the queue and the exact read cannot disagree. The issue example "Choose the guide's audience" is `choiceForm`'s label in `test/fixtures/question-data.ts`.
- **Row layout.** The acceptance criterion is authoritative over frame `02-inbox-approval`, which still draws "Review material & decide" as an approval row title. The label line keeps kind icon and kind. The title is `headline ?? taskTitle`. The subtitle is "Project / Task title" (project only when the title already is the task title). The intervention/delivery reason line, action and "requester · HH:MM · age" meta keep their current rules. One pure helper in `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` decides title, subtitle and shown reason, so it can be unit-tested.
- **Request pane.** The intro is "Project / Task title" (small), then `h2` = `headline ?? taskTitle`, then the intervention/delivery reason only. After the response component, a new below-form block holds:
  - the `requestIdentity` line ("requester · version N · HH:MM");
  - below 1280px only, the "Task evidence" and "Requesting conversation" links (they already live in the inspector from 1280px).
  
  Inside `QuestionResponse`, the "Conversation revision N." line, the "Requesting conversation" link (non-compact hosts) and "Question evidence" link, and the drafts hint move below the form/recorded card. The pending "Awaiting answer" badge is dropped. Non-pending status badges (recorded, stale, cancelled, offline, unsupported, unavailable) and the "N of M completed" progress stay above, because they change what the operator can do.
- **Refresh request.** It is removed entirely, not kept for the stale state. `ResourceStatus` at the top of `QuestionResponse` already shows "Refresh failed. Showing the last fetched data." with "Try again" for a stale read. #1085 rule 3 (DESIGN.md → Presentation) forbids sub-panel refresh. `QuestionResponse` gains an optional `observedAt?: number | null`. When it changes, it `poll()`s its read, following `useInboxTask`.
  - The Inbox passes `resource.state.fetchedAt`.
  - `InboxQuestion` forwards its existing `observedAt`, which covers Overview cards.
  - `TaskWorkspace` passes its task `resource.state.fetchedAt`.
  
  The page Refresh and existing polls therefore re-read the request. Frame `29-phone-question-stale-read` still draws a "Refresh request" button. DESIGN.md records the divergence instead of a canvas edit; the canvas is not changed.
- **Phone first view.** Once the scaffolding moves below the form, a single two-option question at 390 × 844 shows both options above the sticky `.question-submit`. If the browser assertion still fails, fix it in `web/src/inbox.css` (sticky area padding/gap at ≤760px) within the slice. Do not make the options sticky (DESIGN.md: only the submit area is sticky).

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`:
  - `readInbox` (about lines 2801–2940) builds `InboxItem`s from `taskSummaryRead`'s `view.questions`/`view.approvals`, with `excluded` in scope.
  - `readQuestion` (about 2704–2800) composes `own?.form ?? nativeQuestionForm(native.request.questions) ?? plain form` and gates on `intactQuestion`.
  - `interaction(i, excluded)` (about 2985) computes `action` and `approvable`.
  - The generic reasons are at about 2902–2905.
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `inboxItemSchema` (strict, about 2537) is parsed by the web client and by `src/cli/attention.ts` `inbox list`, whose human table is unchanged.
- **Existing:** `web/src/inbox.tsx`:
  - `row()` (about 304–337) renders the label, `taskTitle`, `reason`, action and meta.
  - The detail intro (about 518–559) renders project, `h2` task title, `requestIdentity`, reason and the below-1280 evidence links, then mounts `QuestionResponse` directly (`compactContext`, `holds={answerHolds(task.state)}`).
  - `resource.state.fetchedAt` is the Inbox read time, already fed to `useInboxTask`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/question-response.tsx` — `QuestionResponse`'s `.question-context` block (about 207–246), `.question-hint` (about 303) and the `Refresh request` button (about 491–503). `statusBadges.pending` reads "Awaiting answer".
- **Existing:** `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx` — `InboxQuestion` consumes `observedAt` for holds only. `ApprovalDetail`/`ApprovalFacts` are unchanged.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx:~1562` mounts `QuestionResponse` for `?request=`. `web/src/overview-attention.tsx` mounts `InboxQuestion`.
- **New:** `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` — `requestHeading(item: Pick<InboxItem, "kind" | "headline" | "taskTitle" | "projectName" | "reason" | "attentionCode">)` returns `{ title, subtitle, reason }`. `reason` is non-null only for interventions or rows with an `attentionCode`. It is used by the queue row and the pane intro.
- **Follow:** `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx:useInboxTask` for the observedAt-change → `poll()` pattern. Follow `test/operator/operator-inbox.test.ts` "privacy exclusions withhold an entire exact form…" for the exclusion assertion.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 → T4. The graph is acyclic and strictly sequential. T2 and T3 share `web/src/inbox.tsx`, `web/src/inbox.css`, `design/DESIGN.md` and `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts`. T3 and T4 share `web/src/question-response.tsx` and `test/coordination/operator-question-browser.test.ts`. No two tasks are safe to run concurrently. One PR delivers all four slices.

#### 1. Inbox read carries a privacy-checked headline

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none.
**Files and symbols:**
- `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`inboxItemSchema`: add `headline: safeText`).
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`: new private helper (e.g. `composedQuestionForm(view, taskView, interaction)` returning `{ form, source }`), used by `readQuestion` and `readInbox`. Set `headline` on question, approval and intervention items.
- `test/operator/operator-inbox.test.ts`.
- Typed `InboxItem` fixtures that `tsc` flags: at least `test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts` (~line 71) and `test/operator/operator-overview-model.test.ts` (~line 31), with `headline: null` or a value.

**Test:** In `test/operator/operator-inbox.test.ts`:
- In "action Inbox is cross-project summary-only…", assert:
  - the `seedOwnQuestion` item with `mixedForm` has `headline === mixedForm.questions[0].label`;
  - a `seedOwnApproval` item has `headline === "Create a pull request. No merge or deployment."`;
  - `JSON.stringify(queue).includes("options")` is still false.
- In "privacy exclusions withhold an entire exact form…" (exclusion `"Blue"`), assert `(await api.readInbox()).data.items[0].headline === null` and that the queue JSON does not include `"Blue"`.
- Add one plain-question case (no own form) where `headline` equals the interaction prompt, and one intervention with `headline === null`.

**Implementation:**
- Extract the form composition from `readQuestion` unchanged.
- In `readInbox`, for each listed question set `headline = intactQuestion(form, excluded) ? (source === "plain" ? safe(prompt) : form.questions[0]?.label ?? null) : null`.
- For approvals, set `headline = mapped.approvable ? mapped.action : null`, using `this.interaction(q, excluded)`.
- Interventions get `headline: null`.
- Leave `reason` unchanged.

**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && node --test dist/test/operator/operator-inbox.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-cli-http.test.js dist/test/coordination/operator-cli-attention.test.js`. Expect typecheck clean and all tests pass.
**Complete when:** the Inbox read returns `headline` for questions and approvals, null under exclusions, and the existing CLI/inbox tests still pass.

#### 2. Queue rows lead with the question or exact action

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the working branch.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts` (new `requestHeading`).
- `web/src/inbox.tsx` (`row()`).
- `web/src/inbox.css` (`.inbox-row*`; clamp the title to two lines with the full text in `title`).
- `test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts`.
- `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts`: "queue rows are request cards…" (line ~75) and the phone row test (~218).
- `design/DESIGN.md`: the Inbox and structured questions bullet "Queue rows use read-model facts only…".

**Test:**
- Unit tests in `operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts` for `requestHeading`:
  - question with headline → `{ title: headline, subtitle: "P / T", reason: null }`;
  - approval → title is the action, reason null;
  - delivery row (`attentionCode: "question-delivery"`) keeps its reason;
  - intervention → title is the task title, subtitle is the project, reason kept;
  - null headline → task-title fallback.
- Browser: seed `seedOwnQuestion(f, choiceForm, …)` plus `seedOwnApproval`. Assert:
  - the question row's `strong` text is "Choose the guide's audience";
  - the row contains "<project> / <task title>";
  - no row contains "Operator answer requested" or "Review exact approval material";
  - the approval row title is the exact action.

**Implementation:** The row renders `requestHeading(item)`: kind label line, title, subtitle, optional reason, action, then the existing meta. Update the DESIGN.md bullet to describe the new row and remove "the task title, the reason" from the row facts.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.js`. Expect all pass (Chromium).
**Complete when:** rows show headline-first with task and project as the subtitle, and the generic lines are gone, proven by the tests above.

#### 3. Request pane leads with the question; scaffolding moves below the form

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/inbox.tsx`: detail intro; new below-response block `.inbox-detail-meta` holding `requestIdentity` and the below-1280 evidence links.
- `web/src/question-response.tsx`:
  - move `.question-context`'s revision line and evidence links, and `.question-hint`, after the form/recorded card;
  - stop rendering the badge for `pending`;
  - keep the progress line and other status badges above.
- `web/src/inbox.css`, `web/src/styles.css` (`.question-context`, `.inbox-detail-intro`, `.inbox-identity`, `.inbox-detail-links`).
- Tests:
  - `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts`: "the request pane shows kind, position, identities…" (~1070), the paused-project question test (~797, which asserts "Awaiting answer" at ~812), and the phone tests (~468, ~903);
  - `test/coordination/operator-question-browser.test.ts` and `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (~567, "Question evidence"), where they assert order or position.
- `design/DESIGN.md`:
  - "Implemented Inbox (`02-inbox-approval`)" paragraph;
  - the "Three-pane workbench…" bullet, replacing "The request headline stays the task title, because…";
  - the "Evidence stays the existing … links" bullet.

**Test:**
- Desktop 1366 × 900: the selected question's `h2` is "Choose the guide's audience". The selected approval's `h2` is the exact action. The `.inbox-identity` line (`/^.+ · version \d+ · \d\d:\d\d$/`) and the "Conversation revision" text sit below the last `fieldset` (compare bounding boxes). "Awaiting answer" is absent for a pending question.
- New phone test at 390 × 844 (`openInbox(j, 0, …)` with a `choiceForm` question selected):
  - on first view, without scrolling, the bottom of each option label ("Every new member", "Team owners") is ≤ the top of `.inbox-detail .question-submit`;
  - the "Task evidence" and "Requesting conversation" links' tops are ≥ the bottom of the last `fieldset`.
  
  Capture `captureBrowserEvidence(page, "390-inbox-question-first-view")`.
- Task page `?request=` still shows "Question evidence", now below the form.

**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Use `requestHeading` for the intro. Keep the deep-link/no-`selected` path rendering `QuestionResponse` unchanged.
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.js dist/test/coordination/operator-question-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js`. Expect all pass.
**Complete when:** the pane heading is the question or action, the scaffolding sits below the form on desktop and phone, and the phone first-view assertion passes.

#### 4. Remove Refresh request; page refresh re-reads the request

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `T3`
**Prerequisites:** T3.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/question-response.tsx`: delete the `Refresh request` button; add the `observedAt` prop with change → `resource.poll()` unless sending or uncertain.
- `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx`: `InboxQuestion` passes `observedAt` through to `QuestionResponse`.
- `web/src/inbox.tsx`: passes `observedAt={resource.state.fetchedAt}`.
- `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`: passes `observedAt={resource.state.fetchedAt}` at the `QuestionResponse` mount.
- Tests: `test/coordination/operator-question-cards-browser.test.ts` (~342–380, ~532–545, ~572–585) and any `Refresh request` use in `test/coordination/operator-question-browser.test.ts` and `test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.ts`.
- `design/DESIGN.md`: the "Entry points that apply…" bullet's counterparts. "stale read, Refresh request" becomes "stale read, Try again (or the page Refresh)". Add one line noting that frame 29's "Refresh request" button is not built (DESIGN.md Presentation: one refresh per page).

**Test:**
- `rg -n "Refresh request" web/src` returns nothing.
- Cards test (f): with the question read routed to 503, trigger a re-read via the host's page refresh/poll (or "Try again"). Assert "Stale read · last read HH:MM", Submit disabled and draft retained. After unrouting, "Try again" restores Submit.
- New Inbox browser case at 1366 × 900: answer the selected question through the API (or a second session) so it is recorded elsewhere. Click the queue header "Refresh". Assert the pane shows the recorded or stale status without any in-pane refresh control.

**Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Do not change `statusNotice` actions ("Check connection", "Review current request").
**Validate:** From the repository root, after `npm run build`, run `node --test dist/test/coordination/operator-question-cards-browser.test.js dist/test/coordination/operator-question-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.js`. Expect all pass. Also run `rg -n "Refresh request" web/src` with no output.
**Complete when:** no Refresh request control remains, and the page refresh/poll and "Try again" cover the re-read and stale recovery on the Inbox, Overview cards and the task page.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Queue row title is the first question's label / approval's exact action, with task title and project as subtitle; generic lines go | 1, 2 | T1 `operator-inbox.test.ts` headline assertions; T2 `requestHeading` unit tests and the queue-row browser test |
| Request pane heading is the question or exact action; version, revision, evidence links and drafts note below the form or in the inspector | 3 | T3 desktop request-pane browser assertions |
| Phone: options not under the sticky bar on first view; evidence buttons below the form | 3 | T3 390 × 844 first-view browser test |
| Refresh request removed or folded into the page-level refresh | 4 | T4 `rg` check, cards stale-read test, Inbox page-Refresh re-read test |
| `inbox-presentation.ts`, `inbox-detail.tsx`, Inbox browser tests updated; DESIGN.md implementation status notes the change | 2, 3, 4 | Diff contains those files; DESIGN.md bullets updated in T2–T4 |

### Final validation

- From the repository root on the integrated candidate, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run format:check`. Expect all clean.
- From the repository root, after `npm run build`, rerun the four slices' focused `node --test` commands together. Expect all pass in Chromium.
- PR CI on the integrated head (`check`, `quality`, `node24-operator-1/2`, `node26-service-1/2` and the rest of the workflow's jobs) must pass. That is the full-suite trigger, and a local `npm run check` is not required. Baseline CI passed on `43d3b0c2` for all those jobs.
- `rg -n "Operator answer requested|Review exact approval material" web/src` returns nothing. The strings remain only in `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (server reason, CLI).

### Review focus

- The headline disclosure gate matches `readQuestion`/`interaction` exactly, with no path that exposes a label or action the exact read would withhold.
- The background question re-read never runs during send or an uncertain outcome, and never clears a draft.
- Shared `QuestionResponse` layout changes on the task page and Overview cards: no lost control or link, and focus restoration for the moved evidence links still works (DESIGN.md: returning from the task restores the link's focus).

### Conflict admission

- **Files touched:**
  - `src/operator/contracts.ts`
  - `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`
  - `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts`
  - `web/src/inbox.tsx`
  - `web/src/inbox-detail.tsx`
  - `web/src/question-response.tsx`
  - `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`
  - `web/src/inbox.css`
  - `web/src/styles.css`
  - `design/DESIGN.md`
  - `test/operator/operator-inbox.test.ts`

It gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. After that, stop and return a replan request. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for a material design or contract change, or when the grant is exhausted. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. ### Planning decisions - **Where capacity is stated.** It goes on one line in `TaskViews`'s work section, directly after ``, so it shows on Overview, `/app/tasks` and project routes, in List and Board, at every width. The sidebar meter is not used for three reasons: - it shows only global usage, not project limits; - it is hidden in the drawer shell below 1121px; - #1083 is changing `app.tsx`. content.title: Task detail: raw identifiers, literal tokens and GitHub-only controls on local tasks

nodes.body:
**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1088 **Planned against:** `main` at `dd448cf0331a7c2861a3deb717c73b76cf767f72` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach Fix the six listed task-detail problems on the Overview tab, the inspector and the Changes tab's delivery block, using the #1085 helpers (`shortId`, `codeSentence`) and the DESIGN.md Presentation rules. One server change is needed: the task read gains an optional `repositoryLinked` boolean. Today the web client cannot tell whether a local task's project has a linked repository. Everything else is web copy and conditional rendering. Ship it as one PR. ### Guardrails - Behaviour stays the same: command payloads (`message`, `comment.send/review/confirm`, `review.view`, `delivery.refresh`), the exact `reference` sent with a lead message, unknown-outcome reconciliation, `TaskWorkspaceState` persistence across tab switches and polls, and the server's `commentPolicy` gate. The CLI's output does not change (the new field is additive and optional; `src/cli/**` is not edited). - Out of scope: the #1008 layout and order; History, Files and Review tab copy; Changes tab copy other than hiding its delivery block; retained-evidence item-level gap reasons (`entry.reason`, `content.reason`); result timestamps (`date(...)`); the "No viewing baseline …" wording when results exist; the `Immutable reference:` JSON text, which only moves below the textarea and keeps its text because tests read it; `src/cli/**`; the design canvas. - Identifiers carry no secrets, so showing the full value in a `title` attribute is allowed. A redacted or null `task.outcome` gets no subtitle, no disclosure and no placeholder text. - Every new test must be runnable on its own with `--test-name-pattern`, must seed its own fixture, and must pass on macOS and ubuntu. Assert text with exact or anchored matchers. Do not depend on locale, timezone, fonts, test order or another test's state. - Routine implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the implementer under unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority, and do not use up the mismatch budget. Examples: updating existing assertions that quote changed copy, adjusting fixtures, fixing lint or format. Record each correction in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence. - A wrong seam or repository assumption in this plan is a mechanical plan mismatch. Examples: `domain().githubConfiguration(projectId).repositories` is not the linked-repository source, `TaskStrip` is not rendered under the shell header, or `MarkdownPreview` cannot be imported into `task-header.tsx`. It allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. After that, stop and report. Investigate any unknown overlap. Stop for any material change to design, contract or scope. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption. ### Planning decisions - **What counts as "GitHub source or repository".** The GitHub reply tab shows only when `data.source` exists, because the server's `commentPolicy` already requires a bound GitHub issue. Delivery lines show when `data.source`, `data.repositoryLinked` or `data.delivery?.binding` is truthy. When `repositoryLinked` is missing (hand-built test reads), it counts as false, so GitHub-only controls stay hidden unless proven. - Evidence: the task read has no repository fact today (`src/operator/contracts.ts` `taskSchema`). - `deliveryProjection` is returned for every task, so `Delivery: Reviewable PR · no PR yet` shows on repository-free tasks (`src/standalone/operator-api.ts:3362`, `:4449`). - Project linked repositories come from `this.domain().githubConfiguration(projectId).repositories` (`src/core/domain.ts:1042`; the same call is used in `retainedEvidencePolicy`, `operator-api.ts:730`). - Dropping `delivery` instead was rejected: `src/cli/delivery.ts:57,78` would print "not reported", which changes CLI output (#1107's area). - **Outcome under the title.** The shell subtitle becomes the first non-empty line of the outcome with heading, list and checklist markers removed, using the same regex as `search.tsx` `plainExcerpt`. When anything follows, the task strip shows a closed native `
` ("Full desired outcome") that renders the whole outcome with `MarkdownPreview` (inert, `skipHtml`). This meets the "first line with a disclosure" option without editing `app.tsx` or `PageHeader` (#1083 owns the shell). No canvas edit is needed: this is undrawn production detail, recorded in DESIGN.md Implementation status like the other "differ from the frames" notes. - **Identifiers.** Results are labelled `R`, where n is the 1-based position in `data.results` (oldest first). This is the numbering the inspector and the Result revision select already use as "Result n". Assignment, source and result ids show as `shortId` (8 characters) in mono. They render through a new shared `ShortId` component, `{shortId(full)}`, as separate metadata and never inside a sentence. Assignments keep 8 characters rather than `A-9bd4`, matching existing assignment rows (`task-overview.ts:271`) and the Presentation rule's "8 chars" example. - **Tokens.** - Criterion metadata reads `Source revision n`, then scope, then provenance, joined with " · ". A missing value is omitted, and neither "No supporting scope supplied" nor "provenance" appears. The duplicate-records literal follows the same rule. - Validation rows drop "checked head not supplied". Heads render as `ShortId`, and the comparison reads "Matches the current pull request head", "Checked an earlier head than the current pull request head" or "Head comparison unknown". - A result-level retained-evidence `unavailable` reason becomes a sentence via `codeSentence`, with the code inside a closed Details. <!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1089
**Planned against:** `main` at `ac84ed8ccf7527c93247e9deff49161d5f70b62f`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Change only the Search page (`web/src/search.tsx`, `web/src/search.css`). Three changes:

- Show Back only when the page was reached from a task or an Inbox item.
- Put the query form first, with the coverage note as one line beneath it.
- Move the Project, Type, date and history filters, plus Refresh results, into the results header beside the count. They render only when there is a query, and changing one re-runs the search.

Then adapt the browser tests that set filters before submitting a query. Rewrite the Search notes in `design/DESIGN.md` to match. The shell (`web/src/app.tsx`), the sidebar Search work field, the HTTP search read and the URL parameters stay unchanged.

### Guardrails

- **No contract change.**
  - `GET /api/operator/search`, `searchReadSchema`, the CLI search JSON and exit codes, and persisted data stay the same.
  - The `/app/search` URL parameters stay the same: `query`, `projectId`, `type`, `after`, `before`, `historical` and `cursor`.
  - The `history.state` fields written by `pushAppEntry` stay the same: `origin`, `workspaceOrigin`, `entryIndex`, `workspaceIndex`, `navKey` and `navigationScope`.
  - If the work seems to need any of these changed, stop and return it as a re-plan.
- **Restore behaviour stays.** Back/Forward and the return from an opened match must still restore the query, every filter, the selected match and the scroll position (`SearchState`).
  - The "Refresh failed. Showing the last matches" retained-results state stays, as do the omitted-count wording and the no-match wording.
  - The SPEC rule that Search never implies complete capture still holds. The visible one-line note must still say that Search does not cover full transcripts.
- **Out of scope:**
  - The sidebar `SearchWorkField`, the drawer Search row and ⌘K handling (`web/src/app.tsx`).
  - Phone headers (#1091) and the Files tab (#1094/PR #1130).
  - Search read-model fields such as short IDs and revisions.
  - Replacing From/Through with a single date select.
  - Editing the claude.ai Design canvas. Frame `73-search` already has no Back control. Where production differs from it (filters in the results header), record that in `design/DESIGN.md`; do not edit the frame.
  - Historical `docs/evidence/` records stay untouched.
- **Repairs.** Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs belong to the implementer and do not use the re-plan budget. That includes selector updates, wait fixes, new fixture helpers, formatting and lint. Record each correction and renew the affected evidence.
- **Re-plan budget.** A factual mismatch in this plan's seam or repository assumptions gets one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles before it is returned as a re-plan. Examples: `history.state.workspaceOrigin` does not carry the originating path, Search is not remounted per history entry, or other tests depend on the Back button from a non-task origin.
- **Stop conditions.** Investigate unknown overlap with concurrent work. Stop for any material design or contract change, or when grants are exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and any checks or reviews that are still valid.

### Planning decisions

- **When Back shows.** Back shows only when `history.state.workspaceOrigin` names one of these:
  - a task detail: pathname matches `^/app/tasks/[^/]+$` and is not `/app/tasks/new`;
  - an Inbox item: pathname is `/app/inbox` with a non-empty `request` parameter. This is the shape of the item link in `web/src/inbox.tsx:289`.

  Otherwise nothing is rendered: direct entry, reload with no state, entry after sign-out (`clearPrivateNavigation` drops the state), Overview, list, board, project or the Inbox list. Today the `ActionLink` fallback to `/app/tasks` renders in these cases; remove it.
  - Evidence: `pushAppEntry` keeps `workspaceOrigin` and `workspaceIndex` across search-to-search entries (`fromSearch`). Back therefore stays visible, and keeps returning in one click, across filter changes and across a round trip through an opened match.
  - When Back shows, keep the label "Back to originating workspace" and the existing `history.go(delta)`, falling back to `navigate(origin)`. Those tests already pass from task-detail origins.
- **How filters apply.**
  - Project, Type and Include historical records apply on change.
  - From and Through apply on blur, or on Enter in either date field, and only when the value differs from the URL. Keyboard edits of a native date field emit a value for every segment (for example the year 0002, then 0020), so applying on each input would push throwaway queries.
  - Applying re-runs the existing `submit()` route. It uses the field's current text, falling back to the URL `query` when the field is blank. It builds fresh parameters, so `cursor` is dropped, and it pushes a history entry the way a submit does.
  - Clearing a filter is its own counterpart: choose "All…", clear the date, or uncheck.
- **Where filters show.** The results header renders whenever the URL has a `query`, including while the read is loading or has failed with no data. The count text appears only when data exists, so a failed first read never strands the filters.
- **Coverage note.** One line under the query form reads "Searches saved excerpts, not full agent transcripts." Its `title` carries the detail: "Covers permitted retained task, decision and result excerpts, up to 16,000 characters each. Long source coverage is partial. It does not generate summaries." The essential no-complete-capture claim stays visible, so the tooltip only adds limits.
- **Empty state.** Without a query the page shows the form, the coverage line and "Enter a phrase to search across projects.", with no filters.
- **Search records button.** It stays, together with Enter submit. The issue does not ask for its removal.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `web/src/search.tsx`
  - `Search` reads the filters from `path` and holds local `useState` copies.
  - `SearchState` (`origin`, `selected`, `scrollY`, `data`, `dataPath`) is created per history entry in `app.tsx` (`searchState` map keyed by `navKey`). `<Search key={csrf:entryKey}>` remounts per entry, so the local filter state is always initialised from that entry's URL.
  - Today the `.search-nav` row renders Back unconditionally: a `Button` when `history.state.origin` exists, otherwise an `ActionLink` to `state.origin`, defaulting to `/app/tasks`. Refresh results sits in the same row.
  - The form holds the query row and the `.search-filters` row. The `.search-coverage` paragraph has three sentences. The results section starts with `h2#search-count`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/app.tsx`
  - `pushAppEntry` (around line 460) writes `workspaceOrigin` and `workspaceIndex`.
  - `navigate` (around line 715) pushes an entry.
  - `clearPrivateNavigation` (around line 485) clears state on sign-out.
  - None of this is edited.
- **Existing:** `web/src/search.css`. It styles `.search-nav`, `.search-query-row`, `.search-filters` (with a two-column phone grid at max-width 700px and 44px controls) and the `.search-results h2` padding.
- **Existing tests:**
  - **Set filters before submitting, so they must change:**
    - `test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.ts`. The first test sets historical, type and dates before "Search records". It also clicks Back from `/app/tasks?view=board&q=Shared` (line 143) and from the phone project origin (line 178); both are now absent by design.
    - `test/workspaces/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.ts:71` (historical).
    - `test/workspaces/operator-retention-access-browser.test.ts:201` (historical and type).
  - **Click Back from task-detail origins, so they should pass unchanged:**
    - `test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.ts:1011`
    - `test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.ts:310`
    - `test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.ts:655`
    - `test/workspaces/operator-local-review-browser.test.ts:1366`
    - `test/workspaces/operator-local-review-browser.test.ts:1384`
- **Existing fixtures:**
  - `test/fixtures/shell-search.ts` provides `openSearchFromSidebar`.
  - `test/fixtures/questions.ts` provides `seedOwnQuestion`, which creates an Inbox question item. The Inbox item URL shape is asserted in `test/operator/operator-work-browser.test.ts:849`.
  - `test/fixtures/task-review.ts` provides `seedReviewTask`.
- **New:** `test/fixtures/shell-search.ts`. `searchRecords(page, query, filters?)` will:
  1. fill the query and press Enter;
  2. wait for the URL `query` parameter;
  3. apply each requested filter (`historical`, `type`, `projectId`, `from`, `through`; dates are filled and then committed with Tab);
  4. after each filter, `page.waitForURL` for that exact parameter.

  It uses no timeouts or sleeps. The three tests that set filters use it.
- **Follow:** `browserSuite` from `test/fixtures/browser-diagnostics.js` for new cases. Follow the existing `page.route` barrier pattern (`operator-search-browser.test.ts:191`) for held reads.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:**
- The graph is acyclic: T1 → T2, with T3 independent.
- T1 and T2 both edit `web/src/search.tsx` and `test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.ts`, so they run sequentially in one worktree.
- T3 touches only `design/DESIGN.md`, so it may run alongside T1/T2. Deliver all three in one PR.

#### 1. Back only from a task or Inbox item

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/search.tsx`: `Search`'s `.search-nav` block, and a small module-level predicate on the origin path (for example `returnsToItem(origin)`). Set `SearchState.origin` to the item origin, or to `null` when the origin is not an item.
- `test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.ts`
**Test:** Add a new `browserSuite` case, "Search shows Back only after arriving from a task or Inbox item", at 1366×900. Use `seedReviewTask` plus `seedOwnQuestion` and assert each of these:
- **Direct entry:** `page.goto('/app/search')`, then sign in. The `Back to originating workspace` role count is 0. Also check `/app/search?query=Shared` directly and after `page.reload()`.
- **Non-item origins:** from the sidebar on Overview `/app`, the board `/app/tasks?view=board`, a project page and the Inbox list `/app/inbox`, the count is 0.
- **Task origin:** from task detail `/app/tasks/<id>`, the count is 1. Submit a query, change one filter (after T2; before that, submit a second query), open a match, then return with the task page's "Back to originating view". One click on Back to originating workspace then lands on exactly the task URL, with the task heading visible. This covers stale state across remounts and extra entries.
- **Inbox origin:** from an Inbox item `/app/inbox?task=…&request=…`, the count is 1. Clicking it returns to that exact URL with the item's question visible.
- **Signed out:** sign out from Search reached from a task, then sign in again. The count is 0.

Update the existing first test: replace its two Back clicks with absence assertions. Then return to the board with a bounded `page.goBack()` loop (at most 10 steps, ending when the pathname is `/app/tasks`). Assert the restored URL equals `/app/tasks?view=board&q=Shared`, so the view state is still restored by browser Back.
**Implementation:** Render `.search-nav` only when the predicate holds, and remove the `ActionLink` branch. Remove the `ActionLink` import if it becomes unused.
**Validate:** From `/` (repo root), after `npm ci && npm run build`, run `node --test --test-name-pattern="Search shows Back only" dist/test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.js`. Expect 1 pass. Then run `node --test dist/test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.js dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-local-review-browser.test.js`; expect 0 failures.
**Complete when:** Back renders only for task and Inbox-item origins, and every listed test passes.

#### 2. Box first, coverage line, filters beside the count

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1` (shared files)
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the working branch.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/search.tsx`: the form keeps only the query row; the `.search-coverage` one-line note goes under it. The `.search-filters` block and Refresh results move into a header `div` inside `section.search-results` with `h2#search-count`. Render that section whenever `query` is set, and render the count `h2` text only when `data` exists. Filters apply as described in Planning decisions.
- `web/src/search.css`: the results-header flex row (count left, filters and Refresh wrapping right). Keep the phone two-column 44px filter grid inside the header. Remove the now-unused `.search-nav` space-between styles only if they are unused.
- `test/fixtures/shell-search.ts`: new `searchRecords`.
- `test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.ts`
- `test/workspaces/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.ts`
- `test/workspaces/operator-retention-access-browser.test.ts`
**Test:** Add a new `browserSuite` case, "Search leads with the field and shows filters beside the result count once there is a query", in `operator-search-browser.test.ts`. Assert each of these:
- **Before a query:** `Record type`, `Project`, `From date`, `Through date` and `Include historical records` have count 0. The query field is the first form control in `.search-workspace`. `.search-coverage` has exactly the planned text and the planned `title`. At 1366 its rendered height is at most 1.5× its computed line-height, which proves one line.
- **After submitting:** all five filters are inside `section.search-results`, alongside `#search-count`.
- **Type change:** `selectOption('result')` updates the URL to `type=result` (`waitForURL`) and every rendered `[data-search-record]` is a Result. The assertion does not depend on result order.
- **Cursor dropped:** after following "Next retained matches" (seed enough matches for a cursor, or route-fulfil a response with `nextCursor`), a filter change removes `cursor` from the URL.
- **Dates apply on commit:** `fill` From date leaves the URL unchanged. Pressing Tab adds `after`, and pressing Enter in Through date adds `before`.
- **Failed first read:** route the first search read to 503 on direct `?query=` entry. The filters are still present, the status alert shows, and changing Type issues a new read with `type=` that renders results once the route is lifted.
- **In-flight read:** hold the first read behind a `page.route` barrier and change Type before releasing it. Only the new URL's results render, and the released stale response neither restores the old URL nor shows old results. Use outcome assertions, not timing.
- **Back/Forward:** after two filter changes, `goBack` restores the earlier filter values in the controls and URL, and `goForward` restores the later ones.
- **Phone:** at 390×844 the filter controls are at least 44px, the existing assertion.

Switch the three existing filter-before-query journeys to `searchRecords`, keeping their assertions.
**Implementation:** As in the Planning decisions and Files fields above.
**Validate:** From the repo root, after `npm run build`, run:
1. `node --test --test-name-pattern="Search leads with the field" dist/test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.js`; expect 1 pass.
2. `node --test --test-name-pattern="shared Search preserves" dist/test/operator/operator-search-browser.test.js`; expect 1 pass.
