content.title: Files tab: open on the changed files and trim the file header

nodes.body:
<!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1094
**Planned against:** `main` at `dba6cd00e70b468768fc9a0f327a7a4f4df36dd2`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

A web-only change to the Files tab (`web/src/task-files.tsx`), in three increments on one branch and one PR:

1. The explorer opens at a repository root, and its rows carry change markers. The markers come from the Branch comparison the Changes tab has already read for that repository (`TaskChangesState.comparisonReads`). Files never starts a comparison read of its own.
2. The open file gets a one-line header (path · type · size · observed time). Hash and read provenance move into a `Provenance & limits` disclosure. The same header is used for retained result files, so the two surfaces stay consistent.
3. The toolbar holds one `Refresh`. Show ignored files becomes a checkbox in the explorer footer and the ignore-status token goes. `Add review comment` becomes primary once a line is selected and sits in its own spaced action row.

No service, contract, SPEC or canvas change.

### Guardrails

- Service reads, scope/exclusion enforcement, `requestUrl` query shapes, `TaskFileTabState` selection and range semantics, review anchors (`workspaceFileAnchor`, `resultEvidenceAnchor`) and the `previewChange` "Changed since you last looked" notice all stay as they are.
- Files must not issue `/comparisons` requests or write `TaskChangesState`. It only reads `comparisonReads`. The Changes tab's fetch, validation, refresh notice and selection-retargeting logic stay untouched apart from using the extracted key helper.
- The first-open jump to a repository root never moves focus. It never overrides a direct `?path=` link or an open tab. It applies at most once per `TaskFilesState`, so going back to the workspace root, switching tabs or remounting does not jump again.
- Out of scope:
  - a nested or expandable tree explorer (frame 78 draws one; see Planning decisions);
  - the repository picker drawn in frame 78;
  - line count and "Wrap off" in the header;
  - restyling Set start / Set end;
  - Changes rail or diff visuals beyond the shared `CommentAction` variant;
  - any service or comparison caching change;
  - closing the sibling #1096 PR-line work.
- Exceptions to the presentation rules:
  - the mime essence is metadata, not a code to map;
  - existing reason sentences stay as they are.
- Plan mismatch vs ordinary repairs:
  - **Plan mismatch:** a factual seam or repository assumption in this plan turns out wrong. Examples: comparison entry `path` is not repository-relative; `comparisonReads` keys cannot be shared; the hidden Changes panel does not read Branch on mount; the fixture's `ref: "main"` repository does not yield an `available` default comparison. This allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. After that, stop and report for replanning.
  - **Ordinary repairs:** in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, selector, copy-assertion, documentation, formatting and CI repairs stay with the implementer and do not use that budget. Example: existing Files tests that click `Workspace root`, `Refresh selected file`, the `Show ignored files` button or the `Full path` summary must be updated to the new controls.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record each correction and renew the affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for material design or contract changes, or once grants are used up.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption; keep the repair budgets and grants.

### Planning decisions

- **"Opens expanded to the repository root" means the explorer opens at a repository's root listing, not the workspace row.** The explorer stays one level deep. Two marker rules keep changes visible from the root:
  - a directory row whose subtree contains changed paths gets a muted `•` marker, aria "contains changed files";
  - deleted files in the current directory are listed as non-interactive rows marked `D`, since they are no longer in the listing.

  Frame 78's expandable tree, and DESIGN.md's "Right/Left expand/collapse", are already unimplemented on main (Right/Left navigate into and out of folders). This issue's acceptance does not require a tree. DESIGN.md's Files paragraph gets one sentence recording this (T3).
- **Which repository opens first:** `state.changes.repositoryId` if the workspace listing contains it (set by `?repository=` links or by the Changes panel), otherwise the first `repository` entry in Files' own workspace listing. Changes picks `repositories[0]` from the same `files?scope=workspace&showIgnored=false` listing, so both tabs pick the same repository. With no repository entries, Files stays at the workspace root.
- **What "the same comparison the Changes tab uses" means:** the cached read under the key the Changes panel builds for `{target: "branch", repositoryId, baseBranch: changes.baseBranchByRepository[repositoryId] ?? null, changeSet: null}`.
  - The panel is always mounted (`TabPanel` only sets `hidden`) and reads Branch for its repository on mount, so the default repository gets markers without another request.
  - The key builder moves to a shared `comparisonReadKey(auth, taskId, expected)` in `web/src/comparison-read-match.ts`, so the two tabs cannot drift apart.
  - Markers render only when the read has `state === "available"` and `comparison.state === "available"`.
  - With no cached read, markers are omitted (presentation rule 1).
  - A cached read that is not available shows one muted explorer sentence: "Changed files aren't marked: the Changes tab has no complete Branch comparison for this repository."
  - Files Refresh does not recompute the comparison. Markers follow the Changes tab's Refresh, matching DESIGN "Current workspace snapshots stay fixed until Refresh".
- **Markers** map `added` A, `modified` M, `deleted` D, `renamed` R (on the new path) and `type-changed` T. The accessible label uses the word, for example "modified in Branch comparison". The letter is mono and colour is only supplemental.
- **Header line:** `<relative path> · <mime essence, parameters stripped> · <size.toLocaleString()> bytes[ · W × H px for raster] · <clockLabel(observedAt)>`. Missing parts are omitted.
  - The `Provenance & limits` `<details>` (collapsed by default, keyed per tab and content hash) lists:
    - Location (the full `pathLabel`)
    - Listing observed (`clockLabel`)
    - File read (`clockLabel`)
    - SHA-256 (full value)
    - any caller-supplied fields
  - Retained evidence passes its item path and no observed time.
  - The paragraphs for the `Full path` details, "Current workspace · as of", "Selected bytes · as of", "Source view · selectable lines" and the three `mime · bytes · SHA-256` / raster / PDF identity lines are removed.
- **One `Refresh` in the Files toolbar** re-reads the directory listing and, when a tab is open, the active preview. It is disabled while either read is pending, and the existing failure alerts stay.
  - `Workspace root` and `Repository root` leave the toolbar. The explorer's location line (`.file-current-location`) becomes compact breadcrumb buttons (Workspace › Repository *id* › dir…), built from `state.scope`/`state.path` in the same way as the reading-area `crumbs`.
- **Show ignored files** becomes `<label><input type="checkbox">Show ignored files</label>` in an explorer footer with the sentence "Sensitive exclusions still apply.". The existing "Ignore status is incomplete…" sentence moves into the same footer. The `StatusBadge` "… ignore status" is deleted.
- **`CommentAction` uses `variant={anchor ? "primary" : "secondary"}`.** This is shared with Changes, which is intended for consistency. In Files it sits with the selection sentence in a `task-actions` row, so buttons no longer run together.
- New presentation helpers stay in `task-files.tsx` or `file-change-markers.ts`, not `presentation.ts`, to avoid overlapping with #1083.
- Design canvas: **no canvas edit needed.** Frame `78-files-current-observation` (drawn by #1111/#1113) is the reference. Only `design/DESIGN.md` text changes (T3).

### Implementation context

- **Existing:**
  - `web/src/task-files.tsx`:
    - `TaskFiles` owns the explorer (`directoryResource`), the preview resource, `navigate`/`selectFile`/`openTab`/`closeTab`, the toolbar (lines ~1069–1103), the preview header (~1347–1364), the Refresh selected file button (~1414) and the ignore `StatusBadge` (~1429).
    - `FilePreviewBody` (~652) renders the identity lines and `CommentAction`/`ReviewComposer`; it is shared with `web/src/retained-evidence.tsx:385`.
  - `web/src/task-workspace-state.ts`: `TaskFilesState` (explorer state that persists across tab switches) and `TaskChangesState.comparisonReads`.
  - `web/src/inspection-changes.tsx`: `TaskWorkspaceChanges` builds `key = JSON.stringify({auth: session.csrfToken, taskId, ...expected})` (~297) and stores validated reads in `state.comparisonReads[key]`.
  - `web/src/task-workspace.tsx:~1924`: renders `<TaskFiles client session taskId state={state.files} />`. URL parsing (~334–358) already sets `state.changes.repositoryId` and `baseBranchByRepository` from `?repository=`/`?base=`.
  - `web/src/local-review.tsx:841`: `CommentAction`.
  - Comparison entries (`src/core/workspace-comparison-contracts.ts:105`) carry repository-relative `path`, optional `previousPath`, and `change` ∈ added|modified|deleted|renamed|type-changed.
- **New:**
  - `web/src/comparison-read-match.ts`: `comparisonReadKey(auth, taskId, expected)`. It returns exactly the string the Changes panel builds today, and both tabs use it.
  - `web/src/file-change-markers.ts`: a pure function `changeMarkers(read, path: readonly string[])`. It returns `{ files: Map<name, change>, directories: Set<name>, deleted: string[] } | null`, where `null` means not available. It is used by `TaskFiles`.
  - `TaskFilesState.defaultLocationApplied = false`.
  - `TaskFiles` gains a `changes: TaskChangesState` prop.
  - `FileHeader` in `task-files.tsx`.
- **Follow:**
  - `test/workspaces/comparison-read-match.test.ts` for unit-testing a web `.ts` module.
  - `startChangesJourney(…, { alphaRef: "main", beforeOpen })` in `test/workspaces/operator-changes-browser.test.ts` for a fixture whose default Branch comparison is `available`.
  - `sourceRepository`/`seedReviewTask` in `test/workspaces/operator-files-browser.test.ts`.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** T1 → T2 → T3 is an acyclic chain. All three edit `web/src/task-files.tsx` and `test/workspaces/operator-files-browser.test.ts`, so they run one after another in one worktree. Nothing can run in parallel.

#### 1. Explorer opens at the repository root with change markers

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/comparison-read-match.ts`: new `comparisonReadKey`.
- `web/src/inspection-changes.tsx`: use `comparisonReadKey` for `key`; no other change.
- `web/src/file-change-markers.ts`: new `changeMarkers`.
- `web/src/task-workspace-state.ts`: `TaskFilesState.defaultLocationApplied`.
- `web/src/task-files.tsx`:
  - `TaskFiles` gets the `changes` prop, the default-location effect and marker rendering in the entry rows;
  - deleted rows;
  - the "not marked" sentence;
  - `navigate`/`selectFile`/`openTab` set `defaultLocationApplied = true`.
- `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`: pass `changes={state.changes}` to `TaskFiles` (one line).
- `web/src/styles.css`: marker and deleted-row styles.

**Test:**
- (a) New `test/workspaces/file-change-markers.test.ts` covers `changeMarkers`:
  - nested modified path marks the top-level directory at `[]` and the file at `["src","components"]`;
  - added and deleted at the root;
  - renamed marks the new path only;
  - `type-changed` maps to T;
  - a non-available read (`state: "gap"`, `base-branch-required`, comparison `state: "gap"`) returns `null`;
  - an empty entries list returns empty sets.
- (b) `comparisonReadKey` equals the previous inline `JSON.stringify` for a branch and an uncommitted `expected` (add to `comparison-read-match.test.ts`).
- (c) New browser test in `operator-files-browser.test.ts`: `"Files opens at the repository root with changed files marked from the Branch comparison"`.
  - Setup: one repository `alpha` with `ref: "main"`. Commit on the task branch, before opening: modify `src/app/menu.ts`, add `added.md`, delete `gone.txt`.
  - Navigate to `?section=files`.
  - Assert, with no click: `alpha`'s root entries are listed; `added.md` shows A; `gone.txt` shows a non-button D row; the `src` directory shows the contains-changes marker; no "alpha, repository" workspace row is shown.
  - ArrowRight into `src/app` shows `menu.ts` with M.
  - Assert focus did not move on first open (`document.activeElement` is not a `.file-entry`).
- (d) New browser test: `"Files first-open location yields to links, persists, and ignores comparisons it cannot use"`. Assert each case:
  1. `?section=files&path=README.md&repository=alpha` opens that file's tab without the default jump overriding scope or tab.
  2. Navigate to the Workspace breadcrumb, switch to Changes and back to Files: still at the workspace root, no re-jump.
  3. Two repositories where `beta` (HEAD ref) is listed first: Files opens `beta`, shows the "aren't marked" sentence and no markers. Navigating to `alpha` shows alpha's markers only after the Changes tab has read alpha. Select `repo-alpha` in Changes, return to Files, and assert markers appear without a Files reload. No alpha marker is ever shown inside `beta`.
  4. Changes `Refresh comparison` after a new commit adding `late.md` makes `late.md` show A in Files, with no Files Refresh.
  5. A workspace task with no repositories stays at the workspace root without an alert.
  6. At a 390px viewport the first open shows the list view.
- (e) Sensitivity check: temporarily key markers on `target: "uncommitted"` and confirm (c) fails, then revert.
- Update the existing Files tests' navigation, which used to start from the `alpha` workspace row.

**Implementation:**
- The default-location effect runs when `directory` is ready at workspace scope, path `[]`, there is no `activeTab`, and `!state.defaultLocationApplied`. It sets the flag, picks the repository as decided above, and calls a navigate variant that leaves `focusAfterDirectoryKey` null. Any user navigation or tab open sets the flag first.
- Rows render `changeMarkers(changes.comparisonReads[comparisonReadKey(session.csrfToken, taskId, {target:"branch", repositoryId, baseBranch: changes.baseBranchByRepository[repositoryId] ?? null, changeSet:null})], state.path)` only when `state.scope.kind === "repository"`.
- Deleted rows sit after the entry list. They are `<li>` elements outside `explorerEntries` keyboard indexing.

**Validate:** From the checkout root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run build && node --test dist/test/workspaces/file-change-markers.test.js dist/test/workspaces/comparison-read-match.test.js && node --test dist/test/workspaces/operator-changes-browser.test.js && node --test --test-name-pattern="Files opens at the repository root|Files first-open location" dist/test/workspaces/operator-files-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass, with each new browser test passing when run alone by its pattern. Requires the repository's Playwright Chromium.
**Complete when:** the default open, markers and every stale case above pass, and the existing Changes tests stay green.

#### 2. One-line file header with a Provenance & limits disclosure

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the branch (shared files).
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/task-files.tsx`:
  - new `FileHeader({ path, data, observedAt, provenance })`;
  - `FilePreviewBody` drops its identity paragraphs and the "Source view · selectable lines" line;
  - `TaskFiles` replaces the `<h4>`, `Full path` details and the two observation paragraphs with `FileHeader`.
- `web/src/retained-evidence.tsx` (~385): render `FileHeader` with `content.item.path`, no observed time, `provenance: []` before `FilePreviewBody`.
- `web/src/styles.css`.

**Test:** New browser test `"Files shows a one-line file header with hash and read times under Provenance & limits"`.
- Open a text file: the header text matches `/^guide\.md · text\/markdown · [\d,]+ bytes · \d{2}:\d{2}$/` (an equivalent for the fixture file). It contains no `charset`, no `SHA-256` and no "as of".
- The `Provenance & limits` disclosure starts collapsed. Expanded, it shows the full 64-hex SHA-256, Location and File read.
- Stale cases:
  - Open a second tab: its disclosure starts collapsed and shows that file's hash.
  - Modify the first file and `Refresh`: the header time and the disclosure hash update, and the existing change notice still appears.
  - Raster and PDF headers include their type and size (raster adds `W × H px`).
  - "Source view · selectable lines" and the "Full path" summary are absent.
- Run `operator-retained-inspection-browser.test.js` and confirm the retained file header shows path · type · size and its hash only inside the disclosure.

**Implementation:** As decided in Planning decisions. Use `clockLabel` from `presentation.ts` (import only; do not edit that file).
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run build && node --test --test-name-pattern="one-line file header" dist/test/workspaces/operator-files-browser.test.js && node --test dist/test/workspaces/operator-retained-inspection-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-pdf-render-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass.
**Complete when:** both callers render the one-line header and the disclosure, and the focused tests pass.

#### 3. One toolbar Refresh, Show ignored checkbox, primary spaced Add review comment

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2`
**Prerequisites:** T2 on the branch.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/task-files.tsx`:
  - toolbar reduced to one `Refresh`;
  - explorer location breadcrumb buttons;
  - explorer footer with the Show ignored checkbox, "Sensitive exclusions still apply." and the incomplete sentence;
  - the `StatusBadge` ignore token and `file-refresh-preview` button deleted;
  - `CommentAction` wrapped with the selection sentence in a `task-actions` row.
- `web/src/local-review.tsx`: `CommentAction` variant.
- `web/src/styles.css`.
- `design/DESIGN.md`: one sentence in the "Files and diff editor" paragraph that starts "Screen 78 (`78-files-current-observation`) is drawn with…", recording the one-level explorer with markers, folder markers, deleted rows, toolbar Refresh and footer checkbox.

**Test:** New browser test `"Files keeps one toolbar Refresh, a reversible Show ignored checkbox and a primary Add review comment"`. Assert:
- The Files tabpanel has exactly one button named `Refresh` and no `Refresh files`, `Refresh selected file`, `Workspace root` or `Repository root` buttons.
- No text matching `/ignore status/`.
- The checkbox starts unchecked. Checking it lists `hidden.log`; unchecking hides it.
- Before a line is selected, `Add review comment` is disabled and not primary (button class or `data-variant`, whichever `Button` exposes). After clicking a line it is enabled and primary.
- Its bounding box does not overlap any sibling button.
- Stale and failure cases:
  - `Refresh` while a file is open re-reads both `/files` and `/preview`; assert both requests via `page.on("request")`.
  - With no tab open it re-reads only `/files`.
  - A routed 503 on `/preview` during `Refresh` keeps the last preview and shows the existing failure alert. A routed 503 on `/files` keeps the last listing and shows its alert.
  - `Refresh` is disabled while either read is pending.
  - After closing the last tab, `Refresh` still works.
  - Breadcrumb Workspace → Repository alpha navigates and keeps keyboard focus rules.
- Re-run the Changes and review browser tests, because `CommentAction` is shared.

**Implementation:** As decided. The `Refresh` handler calls `directoryResource.refresh()` and, if `activeTab`, `previewResource.refresh()`.
**Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run build && node --test --test-name-pattern="one toolbar Refresh" dist/test/workspaces/operator-files-browser.test.js && node --test dist/test/workspaces/operator-files-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-changes-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-review-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-local-review-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-inspection-navigation-browser.test.js`. Expect all to pass.
**Complete when:** the toolbar, footer, comment action and DESIGN.md sentence are in place and the focused tests pass.

### Acceptance coverage

| Explorer opens expanded to the repository root with changed files marked M/A/D from the Changes tab's comparison | 1 | T1 tests (a)–(d) |

| Action buttons spaced and ordered: Add review comment primary when a line is selected, Refresh in the toolbar | 3 | T3 test (single Refresh, primary/non-overlapping Add review comment) |

### Final validation

### Review focus

- Default-location races: the first listing arriving after a link or user navigation; double application across remounts; focus theft.
- Marker key parity with the Changes panel (auth, base branch); no markers across repositories or from a non-available read.
- `Refresh` pending, disabled and failure paths, with the existing `previewChange` notice preserved.

**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1095 **Planned against:** `main` at `409554769003821cc4713019406a61deb62c7014` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach Do four small things and ship them in one PR. 1. The task read gains the recorded reason of a non-Stop task hold. 2. The task's raw `"{k} hold — use exact recovery controls"` lines become 149c hold lines. Each line says what clears the hold and links Execution details to the task's Execution view (`/runtime/task/:id`). `WaitReasons` renders them beneath Fix: Resume project when the project is paused, and the Resume confirmation names them. 3. The Inbox intervention's Inspect execution opens the task with the decision card in view. 4. The assignment recovery page collapses runs of identical generations under "N older records, same state". The Resume rule matches #1090's plan: one `ResumeProjectFix`, one `project.configure {paused:false}`, and Resume never clears holds. The plan adds no new command. ### Guardrails - **Resume rule (shared with #1090).** Fix: Resume project stays the Fix for the `project-paused` wait (SPEC "Task creation and project setup"). It still sends only `project.configure {type, key, projectId, expectedVersion, paused:false}`. Holds are listed beneath it and are never a Fix, button or command. The new `holds` input on `ResumeProjectFix`/`WaitReasons` is optional and defaults to none. #1090's `ProjectPausedBanner`, `getting-started.tsx` and the composer (`task-composer.tsx`) pass none, so their dialog and output stay unchanged. Keep the draft key `project.resume-fix:`. - Task-wide holds (Stop, task, writer, capacity, uncertainty) link only to the task's Execution view `/runtime/task/:taskId`, never to an assignment recovery page. A wait that names its assignment keeps its existing recovery link (`assignment-recovery-unresolved` → `/app/assignments/:id/recovery`, unchanged). - The recovery page stays read-only. Keep the server read (`assignmentRecoverySchema`, 20 visible records plus `omittedCount`), the "Task-wide holds" panel, the omitted-count description, witnesses and Inspect execution. The collapse is client-side presentation only. Settings → Runtime → Task recovery destinations stays unchanged. - #1085 rule 1 applies: no raw tokens such as `stop`/`writer`/`task` keys, and no placeholder text as content. A withheld task-hold reason reads "No reason recorded." and never shows an empty string or "null". - Out of scope: - changing `execution.holds.*` semantics or `taskHold()` priority; - the operator CLI hold output; - the Overview inspector "Holds" group, which holds admission/approval notices, not execution holds; - the legacy `/runtime/task/:id` HTML; - the #1090 project banner and the legacy links that #1087 removed; - the design canvas. #1111/#1113 already drew `127-assignment-recovery-relay` and `149c-wait-reasons-specimen`, and `design/DESIGN.md` already carries the First run and Recovery notes, so no canvas edit is needed. - Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation and CI repairs stay with the implementer. They need no replan and do not consume the mismatch budget. Record each correction in the delivery record and renew the affected evidence. - A mechanical plan mismatch is a wrong approved-plan seam or repository assumption. Examples: - `?section=decisions` does not open Overview at `#decisions`; - `/runtime/task/:id` is not the task's Execution view (the header "Execution" link in `web/src/task-header.tsx:92`); - `state.taskHold`'s tables do not hold the non-Stop reasons; - the 21-generation recovery fixture does not produce identical sibling records; - `WaitReasons` is not where task-detail waits render. A mismatch allows one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Then stop and return a replan report. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for a material design or contract change or an exhausted grant. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks and reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that requires durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants. ### Planning decisions - **"Execution view" is `/runtime/task/:taskId`.** The task header's only "Execution" action links there (`web/src/task-header.tsx:92`). DESIGN.md ("Stop task … lands on the Execution page, where the Stop observation and Resume live") and #1117 ("links Execution (`/runtime/task/:id`)") say the same. That page renders the execution hold section, including the task hold reason (`operator-runtime.ts` `executionHoldSection`). The link text is "Execution details" (frame 149c). Use a plain ``, because the page is server-rendered outside the app shell. This follows the #1087 History-tab pattern. - **Hold lines cover all five truthy holds** (the current code lists every truthy hold). Labels reuse `holdPills` (`web/src/settings-view.ts:290`), so task and recovery wording stay aligned. "Clears" copy comes from 149c and the DESIGN "until we know it ended" rule: - `stop`: "Operator Stop", "Clears when the task's Stop is resumed." - `task`: "Task hold", ". Recovery stays blocked while it remains." The reason falls back to "No reason recorded." when withheld. - `writer`: "Writer ownership", "Clears when we know the execution ended." - `capacity`: "Capacity", "Clears when we know the execution ended." - `uncertainty`: "Uncertainty", "Clears when we know the execution ended." They are joined with `Intl.ListFormat("en", {type: "conjunction"})` as `The ${list} stay.`, which gives the frame's "The Operator Stop and writer ownership stay." - **Task hold reason contract.** `execution.holds.task` is `Boolean(taskHold())`, and `taskHold()` also returns the operator-Stop row (priority 2, `state.ts:1103`). content.title: Delivery panel: link the PR and say the state in words

nodes.body:
**Revision:** 1 **Supersedes:** none **Replan report:** none ## Implementation plan **Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1096 **Planned against:** `main` at `99c0454a65a6172f86e838c986d1e6219cc3c862` **Publication mode:** Autonomous **Local state:** Clean **Epoch closure:** null ### Approach Add two optional fields to the task read's delivery binding: `url`, a GitHub pull-request link the server builds only when it has a verified name for the PR's own repository, and `draft`. Then rewrite the bound-PR part of the Changes tab's delivery block so it shows: one linked PR line (repository, #number, state badge, short head SHA); the provider read time as a clock label; check rows in words; one line when no checks were observed; one line saying no repair owner is recorded; and each blocker as a sentence, with its code in Details. Unknown codes fall back to a generic sentence. The service still decides every blocker, and nothing in this change creates a new read, cache or command. ### Guardrails - **Contract change, additive and optional only.** `deliveryReadSchema.binding` (`src/operator/contracts.ts`) gains `url?: string` (https, `https://github.com/` prefix only) and `draft?: boolean`. These fields also appear in `GET /api/operator/tasks/:id` and in the `ensemble delivery` CLI JSON, which serialises the read's `delivery` object unchanged (`src/cli/delivery.ts` `deliveryView`). Nothing else changes: no existing field is renamed, retyped or removed, there is no new endpoint, persisted data and the `prObservationSchema` digest are untouched, and CLI human output and exit codes stay the same. `repositoryName` keeps its type. Only its source changes: it uses the source's name only when that source is the PR's own repository (Planning decisions). - Repair ownership is **not** added to the read model. The delivery observation carries no repair owner. The only recorded repair ownership, a review finding's `repairAssignmentId`, already renders in the same section and stays as it is. The block therefore always says no repair owner is recorded for the PR. It never infers ownership from checks, feedback or running work (`design/DESIGN.md` Visual direction; `docs/SPEC.md` "Recorded changes and delivery"). If a reviewer wants a recorded repair owner sourced into delivery, that is a new read-model contract: stop and return it as a decision, do not build it. - The service still decides every blocker (`src/core/delivery.ts` `completionBlockers`, `actionBlockers`). The web only maps codes to words. Don't change blocker codes, their order or their computation. - Out of scope: settlement controls (the legacy "Approval and delivery forms" page keeps them). Also out of scope: the delivery action-history rows (`{a.kind}: {a.state} · …`), the Overview inspector's "Pull request …" row (`web/src/task-inspector.tsx`, concurrent #1097), the delivery-mode chip (`web/src/task-overview.ts` `deliverySummary`), CLI human text, the canvas artboards (frames `69-changes-delivery` / `71-delivery-alternatives` already draw the target), and #1093's no-PR omission (already merged). - Provider-supplied strings (check names, feedback, `readError`) stay text. Only the server-built `url` becomes an `href`. The web never builds a URL from `repositoryName`. - Plan-mismatch budget: if a seam, path, symbol or fixture this plan names turns out to be wrong (a mechanical plan mismatch), do one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles, then stop and report. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, formatting and CI repairs stay with the implementer and don't count against that budget. Investigate unknown overlap with concurrent work. Stop for any material design or contract change beyond the additive fields above. - Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision requiring durable consumption. Preserve repair budgets and grants. - Every new or changed test must run alone with `--test-name-pattern` and pass on macOS and ubuntu. It must not depend on file-system listing order, wall-clock timezone (build expected clock labels with `clockLabel` from the same timestamp), full-file run order or fixed sleeps. Use Playwright auto-waiting locators, never scroll or layout timeouts. Register browser cases through the file's existing `browserSuite`. ### Planning decisions - **The server builds the PR link; the web never derives it.** The server already builds the source issue's link this way (`githubIssueUrl` in `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`), and the web never derives it either (`sourceUrl` in contracts: "The server only builds https GitHub URLs"). The PR observation has only `repositoryId`, and linked repositories persist no owner/name (`repositoryLinkSchema`). So the only verified name is the imported source's `repositoryName`, and it counts only when `identity(taskId).repositoryId === binding.observation.repositoryId`. Today `deliveryProjection` shows the source's name even when the ids differ, which would mislabel or mislink a PR from another repository. Fix that in the same place. Local tasks, mismatched repositories and excluded names therefore get no `url`, and the web says so in one sentence. - **The PR URL schema is stricter than `sourceUrl`.** Use `z.url().startsWith("https://github.com/")`. The web parses every read with the shared schema (`web/src/api.ts` `request`, which returns `invalid-response` on mismatch), so a bad value fails the read closed rather than rendering. The web still renders the anchor only from `binding.url` and only when `new URL(url)` has protocol `https:` and host `github.com`. That covers fixtures fulfilled by route in tests. - **`draft` is optional and defaults to false in the web.** It comes straight from `binding.observation.draft`. Optional keeps it additive for any reader that ignores it. - **Badge words.** `MERGED` → "Merged", `CLOSED` → "Closed", `OPEN` with `draft` → "Draft", `OPEN` → "Open", through `StatusBadge` with its symbol (Visual direction: never colour alone). - **Blocker sentences** live in a new web module that applies `codeSentence`. They cover every code `publicTask` can emit. The first is the issue's sentence: - `reviewable-pr-awaiting-current-settlement` → "Waiting for the current PR head to be settled." - `pr-not-confirmed-merged` → "Waiting for GitHub to confirm the PR merged." - `delivery-provider-read-unavailable` → "The last GitHub read failed, so delivery state may be out of date." - `delivery-mode-changed` → "The project's delivery mode changed after this PR was bound." - `external-action-prepared` → "A GitHub action is prepared and has not been attempted." - `external-action-attempting` → "A GitHub action is in progress." - `external-action-uncertain` → "A GitHub action's outcome is unknown; check it before retrying." - Any other code → "Delivery is waiting on a condition this version can't describe." Every blocker row carries `OutcomeDetails fields={[["Code", code]]}`, so the code appears only in Details (DESIGN.md Presentation rule 1). - **`codeSentence` must not read inherited keys.** `sentences[code]` on an object literal returns `Object.prototype` members for codes like `constructor` or `toString`. Fix it once in `web/src/presentation.ts` with `Object.hasOwn(sentences, code)`. This shared fix benefits the existing callers (`inspection-changes.tsx`, `retained-evidence.tsx`) without changing their mapped output. - **Checks: missing versus observed-empty.** The read always carries `checks` as an array. "Observed empty" means `checks.length === 0 && omittedCheckCount === 0`, and it renders one line: "No checks or repair owner were observed on this head." When checks exist, each row is `: Passed | Pending | Failed`. A check whose `sha` differs from the head appends "· on an earlier head ". Then comes one line: "No repair owner is recorded for this pull request." The existing partial-coverage sentence stays. With `readError` set, the provider line becomes "Last GitHub read failed; showing the read from .", with `readError` in Details. The checks shown are that read's checks, never "current". ### Implementation context - **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — `deliveryProjection(taskId, excluded)` (~4453) builds the delivery read from `service.delivery().publicTask(taskId)`. `repositoryName` is `sourceSummary(...)?.repositoryName ?? b.observation.repositoryId`. `sourceSummary` (~2442) already checks the name against `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` and `disclosable`. `identity(taskId)` (~2034) gives the imported source's `repositoryId`. `githubIssueUrl` (~431) is the URL-builder precedent. - **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts` — `deliveryReadSchema` (~1156), strict binding object; `sourceUrl` (~811). - **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` — the Changes and delivery section component (~2645–2830; the `{d?.binding && (...)}` block, blockers `d?.blockers.map(b =>

{b}

)`, local `date()` at ~166). It renders from props on every read; it holds no state of its own for the binding. - **Existing:** `web/src/presentation.ts` — `clockLabel`, `shortId`, `codeSentence`. `web/src/components.tsx` — `ShortId`, `StatusBadge`. `web/src/action-feedback.tsx` — `OutcomeDetails`. - **New:** `web/src/delivery-presentation.ts` — `deliveryBlockerSentence(code)`, `pullRequestStateLabel(state, draft)`, `checkStatusWord(status)` and `safePullRequestUrl(url)`, the last returning the URL or null after the protocol/host check. These are pure functions, so service-profile tests can cover them without a browser. - **New:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` — exported pure `githubPullUrl(repositoryName, sourceRepositoryId, prRepositoryId, number)`, next to `githubIssueUrl`. It returns `https://github.com//pull/` only when the ids are equal, the name matches the owner/name pattern and neither segment is `.` or `..`. Otherwise it returns null. - **Follow:** `web/src/retained-evidence.tsx` (~271) for codeSentence plus a Details code, and `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (~2686, `page.route` rewriting `json.data.delivery`) for read fixtures fulfilled by route. - Reason-code consumers of `src/core/delivery.ts:1157`: core and standalone completion paths (`coordination.ts`, `standalone/delivery.ts`, `domain.ts`, `service.ts`) and the web blocker list. Only the web list changes. ### Implementation slices **Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 and T2 are roots, and T3 depends on both. T1 and T2 touch disjoint files and may run concurrently. T3 integrates them and edits `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`, the browser tests and `design/DESIGN.md`. #### 1. Delivery read carries a verified PR link and draft flag **Task ID:** `T1` **Depends on:** `none` **Prerequisites:** none **Files and symbols:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`githubPullUrl` new and exported; `deliveryProjection` sets `url` when non-null, `draft`, and `repositoryName` from the source only when the ids match). `src/operator/contracts.ts` (`deliveryReadSchema.binding`: `url: z.url().startsWith("https://github.com/").optional()`, `draft: z.boolean().optional()`). `test/operator/operator-observation.test.ts`. `test/delivery/delivery-integration.test.ts`. **Test:** - In `operator-observation.test.ts`, add the service-profile test "the pull request link is built only for the source's own repository". It covers `githubPullUrl("org/repo","R1","R1",7)` returns `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/7`. It returns null for each of these: ids `R1`/`R2`, name `null`, `"../.."`, `"org/.."`, `"org"` and `"org/repo/x"`. It also covers the coverage fixture (`seedDeliveryCoverage`, a local task): `read.binding.url` is undefined, `read.binding.draft === false` and `repositoryName === "R1"`. Finally, `deliveryReadSchema.safeParse` with `binding.url` set to `"javascript:alert(1)"`, `"http://github.com/x/y/pull/1"` or `"https://evil.example/org/repo/pull/1"` each fails, and `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/7` passes. - In `delivery-integration.test.ts`, add "the delivery read links an imported task's pull request in its own repository". After `createReleaseDeliveryFixture("reviewable-pr")` and `register()`, `new OperatorApi(f.service,[f.directory]).readTask(f.taskId)` gives `binding.url === "https://github.com/org/repo/pull/7"`, `repositoryName === "org/repo"` and `draft === false`. **Implementation:** As in Planning decisions. Keep `repositoryName` non-null and the same type. **Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && ENSEMBLE_TEST_PROFILE=service ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=none node --test --test-name-pattern="pull request link is built only|links an imported task's pull request" dist/test/operator/operator-observation.test.js dist/test/delivery/delivery-integration.test.js`. Expect 2 tests to pass. Then run both files whole (same command without the pattern) and expect all to pass. **Complete when:** The read carries the verified `url` and `draft`, and both tests pass alone and in their files. #### 2. Delivery wording helpers and safe code lookup **Task ID:** `T2` **Depends on:** `none` **Prerequisites:** none **Files and symbols:** `web/src/presentation.ts` (`codeSentence` uses `Object.hasOwn`). `web/src/delivery-presentation.ts` (new; symbols as in Implementation context). `test/operator/operator-presentation.test.ts`. `test/operator/operator-delivery-presentation.test.ts` (new, service profile). **Test:** - In `operator-presentation.test.ts`, add "an inherited object key is not a mapped code". `codeSentence` returns the fallback for each of `"constructor"`, `"toString"`, `"__proto__"` and `"hasOwnProperty"`. - In the new file, add "delivery blockers read as sentences and unknown codes fall back". Each of the seven codes maps to its exact sentence. `"reviewable-pr-awaiting-current-settlement"` gives "Waiting for the current PR head to be settled." `"delivery-new-unknown-code"`, `"constructor"` and `""` give the fallback, and no output contains `-`-joined code text. - In the same file, add "pull request state labels cover open, draft, closed and merged". Check `("OPEN",false)` → Open, `("OPEN",true)` → Draft, `("OPEN",undefined)` → Open, `("CLOSED",true)` → Closed and `("MERGED",false)` → Merged. Also check `checkStatusWord` for success, pending and failure. - In the same file, add "only an https github.com pull request URL is linkable". `safePullRequestUrl` returns the input for `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/7`. It returns null for `javascript:alert(1)`, `data:text/html,x`, `http://github.com/...`, `https://github.com.evil.example/...`, `https://evil.example/...`, `""`, `"not a url"` and `undefined`. **Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run build && ENSEMBLE_TEST_PROFILE=service ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=none node --test dist/test/operator/operator-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-delivery-presentation.test.js`. Expect all to pass. Each new test also passes alone with `--test-name-pattern=""`. **Complete when:** The helpers exist with these outputs and the tests pass. #### 3. Changes and delivery block uses the link, words and not-observed lines **Task ID:** `T3` **Depends on:** `T1`, `T2` **Prerequisites:** T1 read fields; T2 helpers. **Files and symbols:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` (the Changes and delivery section's `d?.binding` block and blocker list only). `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (new browser case). `test/delivery/operator-delivery-integration-browser.test.ts` (update the exact-text assertions at ~58, ~66, ~107 and similar for the new PR and check lines). `design/DESIGN.md`. **Implementation:** - PR line: an anchor whose text is `#`, followed by a `StatusBadge` with `pullRequestStateLabel(state, draft)` and "head" ``. The anchor renders only when `safePullRequestUrl(binding.url)` is non-null, with `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Without a URL, the line is plain text "PR #" with the same badge and head, followed by the sentence "No GitHub link: this PR's repository name was not observed." (`repositoryName` is not shown, because it may be an id.) - Provider line: "GitHub read ". With `readError` set, use the stale sentence from Planning decisions, with `readError` in Details. `date()` is no longer used here. - Checks, empty-checks line, repair line and blocker sentences with a Details code: as in Planning decisions. - Keep the existing partial-coverage lines, feedback rows, merged sentence, Refresh delivery status, the refresh outcome and the unconfirmed check. - `design/DESIGN.md`, in Implementation status › Task detail (the "Changes and delivery" sentence, ~2063): describe the linked PR line, state badge, short head, clock-label read, check words, the not-observed line, blocker sentences with the code in Details, and the no-link sentence. Add one difference: "No repair owner is carried by the delivery read, so `71-delivery-alternatives` A's recorded repair assignment is not built; the block says none is recorded." **Test:** Add the new `operator-task-detail-browser` case "The delivery block links the PR, says its state and blockers in words, and says when checks were not observed". Set it up with `seedReviewTask` plus `setLinkedRepository(…, true)`, and use `page.route` on `/api/operator/tasks/` to replace `json.data.delivery`, following ~2686. Switch a closure variable between reloads or `refreshTask` calls, then assert each step with exact-text locators scoped to `#changes`: 1. OPEN with `url` `https://github.com/acme/app/pull/12`, `checks: []` and blockers `["reviewable-pr-awaiting-current-settlement","delivery-new-unknown-code"]`. The link `acme/app#12` has exactly that href and `rel` containing `noopener`. The badge says "Open". The head shows 8 characters with the full SHA in `title`. "No checks or repair owner were observed on this head." is visible. Both blocker sentences are visible. Neither code is visible until that row's Details is opened, and then the code is visible. `#changes` innerText contains no `reviewable-pr-awaiting` before Details opens. 2. Same, `draft: true` → badge "Draft". 3. `CLOSED` → "Closed". `MERGED` → "Merged", plus the existing merged sentence. 4. Checks `[{name:"build",sha:head,status:"failure"},{name:"lint",sha:"c".repeat(40),status:"success"}]`. Expect "build: Failed", "lint: Passed · on an earlier head" plus an 8-character ShortId, and "No repair owner is recorded for this pull request.". The not-observed line is absent. 5. `url` omitted and `repositoryName: "R_kgDOabc"` → plain "PR #12" (no anchor in `#changes` with `/pull/`), the no-link sentence, and no `R_kgDOabc` text. 6. `url: "javascript:alert(1)"` → the task read fails closed (the page's read-failure state; no anchor with a `javascript:` href anywhere on the page). 7. `readError: "provider-read-unavailable"` → the stale sentence with `clockLabel(observedAt)`, computed in the test from the same timestamp, and the code only in Details. 8. Stale state across navigation: from step 1, open a second seeded task with `delivery.binding: null` in the same page. The `acme/app#12` link and the badge are gone. Return to the first task, and its link is back with the current read's values (step 4's checks if the closure was switched), not the earlier ones. The updated `operator-delivery-integration-browser` assertions check the link `org/repo#7` with href `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/7`, "build: Passed"/"build: Failed" after Refresh, and, where that mode's read has blockers (check `readTask(...).data.delivery.blockers` at that point), each blocker's sentence with no raw code visible outside Details. **Validate:** From the checkout root, run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build`. Then run `ENSEMBLE_TEST_PROFILE=chromium ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=chromium node --test --test-name-pattern="The delivery block links the PR" dist/test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js` and expect 1 pass. Then run `ENSEMBLE_TEST_PROFILE=chromium ENSEMBLE_TEST_BROWSER_ENGINE=chromium node --test dist/test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js dist/test/delivery/operator-delivery-integration-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-observation-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-task-workspace-browser.test.js dist/test/workspaces/operator-review-browser.test.js dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js` and expect all to pass. These are the files that drive Refresh delivery status or the delivery block. Then run `npm run format:check` and expect it to pass. **Complete when:** The block renders per the AC, the new browser case passes alone and in its file, the updated integration assertions pass in both delivery modes, and DESIGN.md describes the built block. ### Acceptance coverage | Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification | | --- | ---: | --- | | PR line is a link (repository name, #number, state badge, short head SHA) | 1, 3 | T1 link tests; T3 browser steps 1–3 and 5–6; integration-browser link assertion | | Reason codes map to sentences ("Waiting for the current PR head to be settled"), code in Details | 2, 3 | T2 blocker test; T3 browser step 1 (Details) and step 7 | | Checks and recorded repair ownership appear when observed; otherwise one line says not observed | 3 | T3 browser steps 1 and 4 | ### Final validation - From the checkout root, on the integrated delivery candidate, run `npm run check`. Expect typecheck, lint, format, build and all tests (both browsers) to pass. A green PR CI on the candidate head (service, operator, integrations, workspaces, execution shards on Node 24 and service on Node 26, which covers ubuntu) satisfies this. The implementer runs the focused commands above on macOS. - Baseline: CI run 39002052888 on `99c0454a` passed every job except `node24-integrations-1`, where `operator-question-cards-browser`'s "requests that cannot take an answer … restores selection, scroll and focus" failed a scroll-position assertion (`[603,626]`). That file is outside this plan. It passed when run alone locally on the base (macOS, chromium), and the previous main run (`ac84ed8c`) was green, so treat it as a scroll flake unrelated to this change. If it fails on the candidate, rerun that job once. Do not change it here. Locally on the base, `npm run typecheck` passed, and so did `operator-presentation`, `operator-observation`, `operator-observation-browser` and `operator-delivery-integration-browser` (10/10). ### Review focus - The `url` is set only when the source repository id equals the PR repository id, and `repositoryName` no longer shows another repository's name. - No raw blocker or read-error code shows outside Details. Unmapped and inherited-key codes fall back. - An empty `checks` array is never presented as passing. Checks from a failed read are never called current. - The exact-text updates in the integration-browser test keep its provider-truth assertions (head SHA, failure after Refresh) rather than loosening them. ### Conflict admission - Files written: `src/operator/contracts.ts` (only `deliveryReadSchema.binding`), `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` (`githubPullUrl` near `githubIssueUrl`; `deliveryProjection`), `web/src/presentation.ts` (only `codeSentence`), `web/src/delivery-presentation.ts` (new), `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` (only the Changes and delivery section's binding block and blocker list), `design/DESIGN.md` (only Implementation status › Task detail), and the tests `test/operator/operator-observation.test.ts`, `test/delivery/delivery-integration.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-presentation.test.ts`, `test/operator/operator-delivery-presentation.test.ts` (new), `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` (one new case) and `test/delivery/operator-delivery-integration-browser.test.ts`. - Overlaps with concurrent work: - #1097 (imported-task inspector/reply) may edit `web/src/task-inspector.tsx`, `task-workspace.tsx` reply/inspector hunks and `operator-api.ts` `sourceSummary`. This plan reads `sourceSummary`/`identity` but does not edit them. It edits a different `task-workspace.tsx` hunk. - #1103 (source setup) may edit `src/operator/contracts.ts` setup schemas and the source-state vocabulary. These are different hunks. The blocker vocabulary here is delivery-only and lives in its own module. - #1091 (phone headers) touches `components.tsx`, `app.tsx`, task-filters/views and inbox. <!-- to-plan:implementation-plan:v2 -->

**Revision:** 1
**Supersedes:** none
**Replan report:** none

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1097
**Planned against:** `main` at `99c0454a65a6172f86e838c986d1e6219cc3c862`
**Publication mode:** Autonomous
**Local state:** Clean
**Epoch closure:** null

### Approach

Four observable fixes on task detail, all in one PR:

- The server adds a machine `reasonCode` to the task read's `commentPolicy`. A new shared module turns that code into one sentence.
- The inspector line and the "Post GitHub comment" reply tab both show that same sentence.
- The inspector shows the sync time as the app's clock label and shows exactly one Dependencies block.
- One web casing helper keeps proper nouns such as GitHub and Claude capitalised when a wait label appears mid-sentence.

### Guardrails

- **Contract.** The task read (`taskSchema` → `commentPolicy`) gains one optional field, `reasonCode`. Nothing else changes in the HTTP API.
  - `commentPolicy.available`, `.mode` and `.reason` keep their current values and text for every task.
  - CLI JSON stays byte-identical: `delivery get` projects `commentPolicy` without `reasonCode`. CLI human output and exit codes do not change.
  - `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` labels and codes do not change. Persisted data does not change. There is no migration.
- **Controller decision D28 (accepted by the controller; the user delegated blocker calls to it).** This deviates from the issue's third acceptance criterion.
  - Ensemble cannot detect "read-only credential" or "source not activated" for commenting. Comments use the project's delivery credential and grant, not the source credential, and the server knows nothing about token scopes.
  - Those two reasons are therefore dropped.
  - The reasons are the ones the server can actually decide:
    - `no-source-issue`
    - `no-comment-grant`
    - `held`
    - `no-delivery-credential` (new)
  - #1103 may later add sentences for source-credential states to the same module. This issue adds none.
- **Out of scope:**
  - Detecting credential scope.
  - Changing comment admission, grants or the send path.
  - `sourceLine` in `web/src/task-overview.ts`, which no production code calls.
  - Canvas artboard edits. `design/DESIGN.md` text is updated instead; if an artboard contradicts this plan, report it rather than editing the canvas.
  - The legacy header buttons (#1087, already done).
  - The phone headers (#1091), the Delivery panel (#1096) and Search (#1089).
- **Plan mismatch versus ordinary repair.** If a seam or repository fact stated in this plan is wrong (a file, symbol, fixture helper or command does not exist or behaves differently), allow one focused diagnosis and at most two repair cycles. Then stop and report. Ordinary in-scope implementation, integration, test, fixture, documentation, formatting and CI repairs stay with the implementer and do not use that budget.
  - Expected ordinary repairs include updating existing browser assertions that pin the old wording ("No project grant for issue comments.", "GitHub commenting (permitted|unavailable)", "Issue open · synced \S+").
  - They also include giving comment fixtures a delivery credential reference.
- Continue routine implementation and fixture corrections within unchanged requirements, coverage, architecture and authority; record the correction and renew affected evidence. Investigate unknown overlap. Stop for a material design or contract change, such as changing `available` semantics, rewording `reason`, adding CLI JSON fields or editing `wait-reasons.ts` labels, or when a grant is exhausted.
- Reuse the existing delivery record and valid checks/reviews. Use an integration amendment only for a changed published integration decision that needs durable consumption.
- **Every new or changed test:**
  - Asserts the outcome: the rendered text or attribute, or the read's JSON value.
  - Can be run alone with `node --test --test-name-pattern=...` on its built file.
  - Passes on macOS and ubuntu.
  - Uses no timezone-dependent literals: build local dates with `new Date(y, m, d, h, min)` or compute expectations in the page.
  - Does not depend on file-system listing order or fixed sleeps: wait on text or attributes, never on a timeout.
  - Register browser cases with the existing `browserSuite` `test` in the file.

### Planning decisions

- **Availability is unchanged when the delivery credential is missing.** Making `available` false would change existing behaviour beyond an additive field:
  - CLI `delivery get` JSON would change (`test/delivery/operator-cli-delivery.test.ts:18` asserts `available: true` on a world with `credentialRef: null`).
  - `send-comment` would fail earlier with a policy-denied exit.

  So the server keeps `available`, and the web treats a comment as postable only when `available && !reasonCode`. CLI and web may differ for an unconfigured credential, which the CLI already reports at send time. This is an accepted limit.
- **Reason precedence follows the existing `reason`:** `no-source-issue` → `no-comment-grant` → `held` → `no-delivery-credential`.
  - `no-delivery-credential` is reported only when the policy is otherwise available and `credentialRef === null`.
  - Invariant: when `available` is false, `reasonCode` is the code for `reason`. When `available` is true, `reasonCode` is `null` or `no-delivery-credential`.
- **Shared map location:** a new `src/operator/github-reasons.ts`. It follows the `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` precedent: shared by server contracts and the web, imported from `web/src`.
  - It exports `commentReasonCodes`, a `CommentReasonCode` type, `commentReasonSentences` (`Record<CommentReasonCode, string>`) and a pure `commentAvailability(policy)`.
  - The web renders through the existing `codeSentence` (`web/src/presentation.ts`).
  - #1103 adds source-state codes as a separate exported record in the same file. It does not widen `CommentReasonCode`.
- **Sentences:**
  - `no-source-issue`: "This task has no GitHub issue to comment on."
  - `no-comment-grant`: "This project doesn't permit GitHub issue comments."
  - `held`: "Comments wait while the task's admission or delivery is held."
  - `no-delivery-credential`: "This project has no GitHub delivery credential set."
  - Fallback when `reasonCode` is absent (an older read) or not recognised: `` `${reason}.` `` when `reason` is non-null, else "GitHub comments aren't available for this task." These are today's strings.
  - The schema uses `z.enum(commentReasonCodes).nullable().optional()`. An unknown code from a newer server fails strict parsing exactly as today's strict schema does, so the web fallback covers only an absent field.
- **Keyboard-reachable disabled tab:** when not postable, "Post GitHub comment" uses `aria-disabled="true"` instead of the native `disabled` attribute.
  - Its click is a no-op.
  - It has `title={sentence}` and `aria-describedby` pointing to an `sr-only` span holding the same sentence.
  - Precedent: `aria-disabled` in `web/src/account-menu.tsx:224` and `web/src/local-review.tsx:866`; the `sr-only` class is already used.
  - While a send is pending or uncertain, the tab keeps the native `disabled`, as today.
  - The tab stays hidden for a task without a source (#1088, `task-workspace.tsx:1381`). That rule is not reimplemented.
- **Mid-sentence casing:** a new `midSentence(label)` in `web/src/presentation.ts` lowercases the first character unless the label starts with a proper noun (`GitHub`, `Claude`, `Codex`, `Ensemble`).
  - It replaces both `lowerFirst` helpers: `web/src/task-overview.ts:79` (used at :135) and `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts:8` (used at :194 and :317).
  - CLI text uses labels at sentence start and is untouched.
- **One Dependencies block:** an imported task cannot own local dependency edges ("Imported dependent cannot own a local dependency edge", `src/core/domain.ts:2515`). So the inspector shows "Dependencies · managed in GitHub" when `data.source` is set and the Ensemble "Dependencies" group only when it is not. No dependency is ever hidden.

### Implementation context

- **Existing:** `src/standalone/operator-api.ts:4295` `commentPolicy(taskId)` returns `{available, mode, reason}`; it is used by the task read at :3363.
  - `this.service.delivery().configuration(projectId)` already carries `credentialRef` (`src/core/delivery.ts:1290-1316`).
- **Existing:** `src/operator/contracts.ts:1362`, the `commentPolicy` strict object in `taskSchema`.
- **Existing:** `src/cli/delivery.ts:38` `deliveryView` passes `commentPolicy` through. Change it to `{available, mode, reason}` so CLI JSON is unchanged. `commentGates` (:172) is unchanged.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-inspector.tsx`:
  - :56-110 GitHub group: raw `synced` at :72; "Dependencies · managed in GitHub" at :82; comment line at :105-108.
  - :142-160 Ensemble "Dependencies" group.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`:
  - :1279-1281 destination reset for a source-less task.
  - :1354-1367 `replyNote`.
  - :1381-1396 "Post GitHub comment" tab.
  - :1419 and :1466 `available` gates.

  Every `data.commentPolicy?.available` check here becomes `commentAvailability(data.commentPolicy).postable`.
- **Existing:** `web/src/task-overview.ts:194` `sourceFacts` returns the ISO `synced` value; `test/operator/operator-task-strip.test.ts:130` asserts it. Keep it ISO and format at render time with `clockLabel(Date.parse(synced))`.
- **Existing fixture:** `test/fixtures/task-review.ts:90` `seedImportedCommentTask(f, mode)` returns `setGrant`, which configures delivery with `credentialRef: null`.
- **Existing tests:** `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts`:
  - :1955 "An imported task separates read-only GitHub source from Ensemble execution".
  - :2232 local task without repository.
  - :2402 "The GitHub reply says what posting does in one sentence and keeps its draft when the policy changes".
  - :2872 / :2885 / :2925 further GitHub comment flows.

  Also `test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.ts` (delivery `credentialRef: null` at :172), `test/delivery/operator-cli-delivery.test.ts` (`deliveryWorld`, `w.task()`), `test/operator/operator-task-overview.test.ts:224-262` ("Ready · …") and `test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts`.
- **Follow:** `src/operator/wait-reasons.ts` for a shared code/label module imported by the web, and the `codeSentence` usage in `web/src/inspection-changes.tsx:461`.

### Implementation slices

**Task graph and parallelism:** The graph is acyclic: T1 → T2 → T3; T4 has no dependencies. T2 and T3 share `web/src/task-inspector.tsx`, `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` and `design/DESIGN.md`, so they run in order. T4 can run alongside T1–T3 except for one line in `design/DESIGN.md`. One implementer and one PR are expected.

#### 1. Comment policy carries a reason code from one shared map

**Task ID:** `T1`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:**
- New `src/operator/github-reasons.ts`: `commentReasonCodes`, `CommentReasonCode`, `commentReasonSentences`, and `commentAvailability(policy | undefined) → { postable: boolean; sentence: string | null }`.
  - `postable` is `available && !reasonCode`.
  - `sentence` is null when postable; otherwise it is `codeSentence`-style lookup with the fallback above.
  - It is pure, so the web can import it. `codeSentence` sits in `web/src/presentation.ts`; either inline the same `?? fallback` lookup or have the web caller apply `codeSentence`. Keep one lookup and do not duplicate the strings.
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: add `reasonCode` to `commentPolicy`.
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts`: `commentPolicy`.
- `src/cli/delivery.ts`: `deliveryView` projection.

**Test:** new `test/delivery/operator-comment-policy.test.ts` (no browser), using `deliveryWorld` from `test/fixtures/operator-cli.ts` and the task read via `w.task()` or its `/api/operator/tasks/:id` read. The cases:
- (a) local task, `deliveryWorld(t, "allow", true)`: `{available:false, reason:"Task has no bound GitHub issue", reasonCode:"no-source-issue"}`.
- (b) imported task with no grant: `no-comment-grant`, with the `reason` text unchanged.
- (c) held task (pause the project or place a task hold so admission is ineligible): `held`.
- (d) grant present and `credentialRef: null`: `{available:true, reason:null, reasonCode:"no-delivery-credential"}`.
- (e) grant present and delivery `credentialRef` set: `reasonCode: null`.
- (f) precedence: no grant and also held reports `no-comment-grant`.
- (g) `delivery get` JSON `commentPolicy` deep-equals `{available, mode, reason}` with no `reasonCode` key. The existing `operator-cli-delivery.test.ts` assertions also pass unchanged.

Unit cases for `commentAvailability`:
- Each code maps to its sentence.
- An `undefined` policy or a policy without `reasonCode` falls back to `` `${reason}.` ``, or to "GitHub comments aren't available for this task." when `reason` is null.
- An exhaustive `Record<CommentReasonCode, string>` in the test fails on a code added without a sentence.

**Implementation:** set the delivery credential reference for (e) without affecting `activationAllowed` (`src/standalone/service.ts:875`). An unset env var resolves to `""`, so set a unique non-empty fake value in the test, the same way other fixtures set `env:FIXTURE_*`.
**Validate:** From `/` of the worktree, run `npm run build && node --test --test-name-pattern="comment policy" dist/test/delivery/operator-comment-policy.test.js dist/test/delivery/operator-cli-delivery.test.js`; expect every case to pass and 0 failures. Also run `npm run typecheck`, which should exit 0.
**Complete when:** the task read carries the right `reasonCode` for every case and the CLI JSON is unchanged.

#### 2. The inspector and the reply tab say why GitHub commenting is unavailable

**Task ID:** `T2`
**Depends on:** `T1`
**Prerequisites:** T1 merged into the branch.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/task-inspector.tsx`, comment line.
- `web/src/task-workspace.tsx`: `replyNote`, the tab, and the gates at :1387, :1419 and :1466.
- `test/fixtures/task-review.ts`: extend `seedImportedCommentTask` so `setGrant` (or a sibling `setCredential`) can set a delivery credential reference, defaulting to set so existing flows stay postable.
- `test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.ts:172`, and any other comment-posting browser fixture with delivery `credentialRef: null`. Find them with `rg -n "credentialRef: null" test` next to an `issue.comment` grant, and set a credential reference so they stay postable.
- `design/DESIGN.md` around :2045-2075: the inspector comment line states the sentence; the disabled tab carries the same sentence.

**Implementation:**
- Inspector, postable: "GitHub commenting permitted".
- Inspector, not postable: "GitHub commenting unavailable" followed by the sentence as a muted line.
- Tab: not postable → `aria-disabled` / `title` / `aria-describedby` as in Planning decisions. The reply note keeps exactly one sentence above the box and shows the same `sentence` when GitHub is the destination.
- A policy that flips while the composer is open keeps the selected destination and the draft, and updates the sentence.
- A draft for the GitHub destination is never sent while not postable. The Post button stays disabled.

**Test:** in `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts`, change the :2402 test and add focused cases. Each one signs in to the imported comment task, then asserts:
- (a) grant `null`: inspector text contains "GitHub commenting unavailable" and "This project doesn't permit GitHub issue comments."; the tab has `aria-disabled="true"`, `title` equal to that sentence, and an `aria-describedby` target whose text equals it.
- (b) the tab is keyboard-focusable. Press Tab until `document.activeElement` is the tab, or call `locator.focus()` and assert it is focused. Pressing Enter does not change the destination.
- (c) credential unset (`available:true`, `no-delivery-credential`): the tab is not postable and shows "This project has no GitHub delivery credential set.".
- (d) held: the held sentence.
- (e) flip while the composer is open: select GitHub with an allow grant, type a draft, then `setGrant(null)` and `refreshTask`. The note becomes the grant sentence, the draft is kept, Post is disabled, the tab is aria-disabled, and `commands` is empty. Then restore the grant and refresh: the tab is postable again and the draft is still kept.
- (f) local task (existing :2232): there is no "Post GitHub comment" tab and no inspector GitHub group.
- (g) fallback: intercept the task read with `page.route`, removing `reasonCode` and keeping `reason: "No project grant for issue comments"`. The inspector and tab show "No project grant for issue comments.".

**Validate:** From the worktree root, run `npm run build && node --test --test-name-pattern="GitHub comment|GitHub reply|commenting" dist/test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js`, then `node --test --test-name-pattern="Post GitHub comment" dist/test/coordination/operator-comments-browser.test.js`; expect all to pass. Run each new test once alone by its exact name.
**Complete when:** the inspector and the tab show the same sentence for every code and for the fallback, and the existing comment flows still post.

#### 3. The inspector shows the clock label and one Dependencies block

**Task ID:** `T3`
**Depends on:** `T2` (shared files only)
**Prerequisites:** T2 complete.
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/task-inspector.tsx`:
  - :72 becomes `synced ${clockLabel(Date.parse(synced))}`, importing from `./presentation.js`.
  - The Ensemble "Dependencies" group (:142-160) renders only when `!source`.
- `design/DESIGN.md` :2045-2054: one Dependencies block per task kind, and the sync time as the clock label.

**Test:** in `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` :1955 (imported):
- Replace `/Issue open · (synced \S+|no successful sync)/` with an exact match against `synced HH:MM`. Compute the expected value in the page as `clockLabel` of the read's latest `memberships[].sync.lastSuccessfulAt`, using `new Date(iso).getHours()` and `getMinutes()` padded, so the browser's timezone is used. Also assert the text has no `T\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}` ISO fragment.
- Assert the inspector has exactly one heading whose text starts with "Dependencies" and that it reads "Dependencies · managed in GitHub". No `.inspector-group` has the label "Dependencies".
- For a local task (any existing local-task test, e.g. :2232 or seedReviewTask): exactly one "Dependencies" group, and no "managed in GitHub".

Unit check in `test/operator/operator-presentation.test.ts`: `clockLabel(new Date(2026, 9, 16, 23, 59).getTime())` equals `"23:59"` and `clockLabel(new Date(2026, 9, 17, 0, 0).getTime())` equals `"00:00"`. Both are timezone-independent day-boundary cases. Add them only if no equivalent test exists.
**Validate:** From the worktree root, run `npm run build && node --test --test-name-pattern="imported task separates|without a repository|clockLabel" dist/test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-presentation.test.js`; expect them to pass.
**Complete when:** an imported task shows "synced HH:MM" and one GitHub-managed Dependencies block, and a local task shows one Ensemble Dependencies block.

#### 4. Wait labels keep proper nouns mid-sentence

**Task ID:** `T4`
**Depends on:** `none`
**Prerequisites:** none
**Files and symbols:**
- `web/src/presentation.ts`: new `midSentence`.
- `web/src/task-overview.ts`: remove `lowerFirst` (:79) and use `midSentence` at :135.
- `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts`: remove `lowerFirst` (:8) and use `midSentence` at :194 and :317.
- `design/DESIGN.md` Presentation rules (~:1485): one line saying labels composed mid-sentence keep proper nouns.

**Test:**
- `test/operator/operator-presentation.test.ts`: iterate every `waitCodes` entry against an exhaustive `Record<WaitCode, string>` of expected mid-sentence forms. Examples:
  - "imported-blockers-unknown" → "GitHub dependencies unconfirmed"
  - "imported-blockers-blocked" → "blocked by a GitHub dependency"
  - "claude-token-unavailable" → "Claude token unavailable"
  - "project-paused" → "project paused"
- `test/operator/operator-task-overview.test.ts`: a `taskStatusLine` case with `imported-blockers-unknown` produces "Ready · GitHub dependencies unconfirmed / …".
- `test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.ts`: an "Execution held (…)" title for a code that has no `heldLabels` entry keeps the casing from the label.
- Existing "Ready · project paused" and "Ready · blocked by a task dependency" stay unchanged.
- `test/operator/operator-wait-reasons.test.ts` and the CLI `task-write` output stay unchanged.

**Validate:** From the worktree root, run `npm run build && node --test --test-name-pattern="midSentence|taskStatusLine|Execution held" dist/test/operator/operator-presentation.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-task-overview.test.js dist/test/operator/operator-inbox-presentation.test.js`; expect them to pass. `git diff --stat -- src/operator/wait-reasons.ts src/cli` should be empty.
**Complete when:** every wait label composes with the expected casing and `wait-reasons.ts` and the CLI are untouched.

### Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Slice | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Sync times use the app's clock label ("synced 17:50") | 3 | Imported-task browser test computes the expected HH:MM in the page; the clockLabel day-boundary unit cases |
| One Dependencies block, GitHub-managed for imported tasks, Ensemble for local ones | 3 | Imported and local browser assertions for heading count and labels |
| "GitHub commenting unavailable" states why, and the Post GitHub comment tab is hidden or disabled with the same reason. The reasons are per D28: no issue, no grant, held, no delivery credential; read-only credential and source not activated are dropped | 1, 2 | `operator-comment-policy.test.ts` cases (a)–(g); T2 browser cases (a)–(g) |
| Wait-reason labels keep their case when composed mid-sentence | 4 | Exhaustive `midSentence` table plus status-line and Inbox cases |
| Contract: one additive optional task-read field; CLI JSON and exit codes unchanged | 1 | T1 case (g); existing `operator-cli-delivery.test.ts` passes unmodified |

**Failure cases the tests must cover:**
- Imported versus local task.
- Each reason code: no bound issue, no grant, held, credential unconfigured.
- Precedence when there are two reasons.
- A reason that flips while the composer is open, and back again.
- The tab is aria-disabled, focusable and described by the same sentence.
- An older read without `reasonCode`, which falls back to `reason`.
- `reason: null` with no code.
- Mid-sentence casing for every wait code, including GitHub and Claude.
- Clock labels at 23:59 and 00:00 built from local dates.
- The browser expectation computed in the page's timezone.

### Final validation

- From the worktree root, after `npm ci`, run `npm run check` on the integrated delivery candidate; expect it to exit 0.
- CI on base `99c0454a` failed one unrelated test in `node24-integrations-1`, "chromium: requests that cannot take an answer show titled notices with the server reason, and evidence return restores selection, scroll and focus" (`test/coordination/operator-question-cards-browser.test.ts`, run 39002052888). That is a baseline scroll flake. Don't attribute it to this change; rerun it once if it recurs.
- PR CI must pass on both macOS (local) and ubuntu (CI) profiles.

### Review focus

- `available` versus `postable` divergence for an unconfigured credential. The web must never offer a send that the server's `available` would refuse. The CLI is unchanged by design.
- No CLI JSON key is added (the `deliveryView` projection).
- Stale composer state after a policy flip: the draft is kept, the frozen or uncertain send path is untouched, and the destination is not silently switched for an imported task.
- The `aria-disabled` tab must not become activatable by Enter or Space.

### Re-plan triggers (when task-specific)

- Stop if `reasonCode` cannot be added without changing `reason` or `available`.
- The CLI parses the task read with the strict `taskSchema` (`src/cli/delivery.ts:32`, `attention.ts:183`, `task-write.ts:54`, `source.ts`). CLI and service ship in the same package, so the schema change lands in both at once. If repository docs show a supported older-CLI-against-newer-service pairing, stop and report.

**File overlap and exclusive resources:**
- `web/src/task-inspector.tsx`, `web/src/task-workspace.tsx` (reply composer) and `web/src/task-overview.ts`: overlap with #1096 (Delivery panel), which is being planned concurrently.
- `web/src/inbox-presentation.ts`: overlap with #1091 (Board/Inbox headers).
- `design/DESIGN.md` Task detail and Presentation sections: overlap with #1089, #1091, #1096 and #1103.
- `src/operator/contracts.ts`: overlap with #1103 and #1096.
- New `src/operator/github-reasons.ts`: #1103 will extend it later.
- `test/operator/operator-task-detail-browser.test.ts` and `test/fixtures/task-review.ts`: overlap with #1096.
- `src/standalone/operator-api.ts` `commentPolicy` and `src/cli/delivery.ts` `deliveryView`: #1096 may touch delivery reads.
- No ports, databases or services are exclusive beyond each test's own temporary fixture.

## Implementation plan

**Issue:** https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/issues/1103
**Planned against:** `main` at `a49368f11f2ab0fe20a4150982da18102481c505`, plus open PR [#1137](https://github.com/chrisbanes/ensemble/pull/1137) (issue #1104, head `74cd6201` when planned), which must merge first
