nodes.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Human Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Run and record the multi-day unattended qualification described in this issue.

**Why it can't be delegated:** it needs explicit authorisation for the host, repositories, merge authority, run window and model usage, real issues labelled over at least three days, and an operator answering agent questions. Agents can help prepare and analyse the run, but they can't own or authorise it.

**Decisions from triage:**
- **Reboot:** the required reboot is one planned `fdesetup authrestart` (FileVault is on). It must recover with no intervention. If an unplanned reboot happens, the FileVault unlock counts as a recorded intervention, not a failure.
- **Mechanical stall:** a task that isn't finished, with no recorded progress event and no open attention item for **2 hours**, outside a recorded sleep or reboot window. Waiting on CI, capacity or a scheduled retry counts as progress only while it is actually pending. Any mechanical stall fails the run.
- **Native blockers:** #732 (physical sleep/wake), #1143 (runtime auto-restart), #1144 (daemon install mode) and #1149 (daemon install qualified on a real `authrestart`).
- #1145 (Web Push) stays recommended, not blocking.
- Claude profiles join only once the subscription terms are settled. Otherwise the run is Codex-only and the record says so.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The run meets the Pass criteria in the issue body, using the stall rule above.
- [ ] Every intervention and its cause is recorded, and the run is recorded in `docs/evidence/`.
- [ ] On pass: the AGENTS.md claim rule, README "Where it stands" and product copy claim exactly what the run demonstrated. On fail: each stall is filed as its own issue and the wording stays as it is.

**Out of scope:**
- Unattended recovery from a power cut with FileVault on.
- Independent-device access (#1150).

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Rename the product from Ensemble to `cab` everywhere outside historical evidence, with an explicit migration rule for each persisted or external contract.

**Why this is ready-for-human:** most of the code rename is mechanical, but several steps need Chris:
- a trademark check in classes 9 and 42 (USPTO, UKIPO) before the repository is renamed;
- renaming the GitHub repository, which is an external, owner-only change;
- the logo and hero (an amber taxi roof sign) on the Design canvas, which needs design judgment;
- agreeing the migration table, including whether the existing dev root is moved or discarded;
- timing relative to the #761 cutover and the first published release.

An agent can implement the code, test and docs rename once the migration table is agreed.

**Current behavior:**
Triage checks confirmed the scope in the body: 2,340 case-insensitive matches in 425 files (test 236, docs 109, src 49, web 19, scripts 4, CI 2). There are no existing `cab` references. The contracts the body lists all exist:
- the data-directory marker `STANDALONE_MARKER_NAME` / `STANDALONE_MARKER_CONTENTS` (`.ensemble-standalone`, `ensemble-standalone-v1`);
- the service CLI defaults `local.ensemble.service` and `~/Library/Logs/Ensemble`;
- the release manifest schema `ensemble.release/v1` and its `ensemble-tree-sha256/v1` digest;
- the dev root `~/.config/ensemble-dev`;
- the browser storage key prefix `ensemble:local-review-send:`;
- 44 `ENSEMBLE_*` environment variables.

A dev root already holds data. No Application Support install or LaunchAgent exists yet.

**Desired behavior:**
- The product, binary, `--version` output, package metadata, docs and operator UI all say `cab`, always lowercase. Any npm package is scoped (`@chrisbanes/cab`).
- Each contract in the body's table gets its new name and a stated rule: rename only (nothing is installed), or a one-time migration (move or read once). There is no permanent dual support.
- The branding from the body is applied: the tagline "Get your work from A to B.", the README opening, the "Where to?" composer placeholder, and the logo and hero.
- Domain terms in `CONTEXT.md` (Task, Assignment, Project lead, Inbox and so on) keep their plain names.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The migration table is recorded in the issue and implemented. Tests cover a fresh install and, for any retained migration, a source still using the old names.
- [ ] A repository-wide search for `ensemble` finds only `docs/evidence/`, explicitly retained fixture or grant identifiers, and documented migration code.
- [ ] `npm ci` and `npm run check` pass, and full-suite discovery runs every test exactly once.
- [ ] A packaged release builds, verifies its manifest and prints `cab <version>`.
- [ ] The design change goes through the Design canvas, with `design/DESIGN.md` updated in the same change.
- [ ] After the trademark check, the repository is `chrisbanes/cab` and local remotes and CI references point to it.

**Out of scope:**
- Rewriting `docs/evidence/` records or existing external fixture and grant identifiers.
- The installed Haze prototype, until its reviewed cutover.
- Theming domain terms ("fares", "dispatch") or changing existing CLI receipts.
- Claiming autonomous operation in copy before #1146 passes.
